sig_008fcbd451c57a3642ec.description: In compliance with the principles of necessity, suitability and efficiency established in Article 28 of the LCSP, the nature and extent of the needs intended to be covered by the conclusion of this contract fall within the scope of the functions and powers attributed to this Management Centre, determining with precision the suitability of the object and content of the contract in the Specifications of Technical Requirements. The contract aims to respond to the need to comply with the provisions of Article 3.2.a of Royal Decree 1046/2022, of 27 December, which regulates the governance of the Strategic Plan of the Common Agricultural Policy in Spain and of the European agricultural funds EAGF and EAFRD (hereinafter, Royal Decree 1046/2022), which stipulates that the regional Management Authorities, responsible for the management and execution of the CSP in their territorial scope, shall participate in relation to the evaluation plan and ex-post evaluation, in the establishment of the CSP evaluation plan and in the monitoring and evaluation tasks corresponding to their sphere of competence, reporting on their development and outcome to the Strategic Plan Management Authority. Such an evaluation must necessarily be carried out by functionally independent experts, as required by Article 140 of Regulation (EU) 2021/2115 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 2 December 2021 laying down rules on support for strategic plans to be drawn up by Member States under the common agricultural policy (CAP strategic plans) and financed by the European Agricultural Guarantee Fund (EAGF) and by the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development (EAFRD) and repealing Regulations (EU) No. 1305/2013 and (EU) No. 1307/2013. Therefore, the corresponding tender must be carried out by this Department so that a team of independent expert evaluators in the field—since the Department of Agriculture, Livestock and Rural Development currently lacks this type of human resource among its staff capable of carrying out the necessary functions to perform this type of work and with the necessary knowledge to be able to carry out thematic evaluations within the framework of the CSP Strategic Plan in the territorial scope of Castile and Leon—can carry it out. In compliance with the provisions of Article 3.2 of DECREE 23/2025, of 30 December, regulating the conditions for the extension of the General Budgets of the Community of Castile and Leon for 2024 in the 2026 financial year, it is noted that the contract proposed to be initiated is considered a continuation of the CAP Strategic Plan approved on 31 August 2022 by the European Commission.

sig_009721ae1d261a05ddf5.description: This document is not a contract notice or a call for tenders but an invitation to a market dialogue. The City of Helsinki's Urban Environment Division (hereinafter the contracting authority) is preparing the procurement of a traffic signal central control system. The City of Helsinki's Urban Environment Division is procuring a new traffic signal control and monitoring system as a service procurement. The new system to be procured is intended to replace the traffic signal control and monitoring system, which is at the end of its life cycle and covers approximately 200 control units. Helsinki currently has a total of approximately 500 traffic signal control units and uses several control and monitoring systems. In principle, only control units using the RSMP interface will be connected to the system to be procured. The contracting authority's inventory of units comprises devices of different models from different eras, and some of the current units do not support the RSMP interface. For a diverse inventory of units, the control and monitoring system is required to support not only the latest versions of the RSMP interface but also several older versions supported by the current control units. The city will renew older control units in the coming years as separate projects, and the renewed control units will be connected to the system to be procured in connection with the unit replacements. Further information on the subject of the procurement is described in the document Introduction to the Procurement, as well as in the appendix Technical Environment and Responsibility Limits. The purpose of this market dialogue is to explore the market for these services and to obtain information regarding the procurement so that the procurement can be carried out appropriately. The material obtained through the request for information may influence how the procurement criteria are set and which procurement procedure will be used. The contracting authority is not bound by the information provided in this notice or its appendices; as the preparation progresses, the subject and requirements of the procurement may change. We request that you notify us if, in your view, the response contains trade secrets or other confidential information. We request that you identify and mark this information clearly. The responses provided in the request for information are not binding on the supplier, and responding is not a prerequisite for participating in the actual call for tenders later. Responding or failing to respond to the request for information does not affect a potential supplier's position in the actual call for tenders. No compensation will be paid for responding to the request for information. We request that you answer the questions presented in the request for information Forms survey as comprehensively as possible. We request that the answers be written in the fields provided in connection with the questions. Registration for the market dialogue sessions takes place using the same aforementioned Forms survey, where the participant indicates the most suitable time for the market dialogue session. The language used in the market dialogue sessions is Finnish or English. Link: https://forms.office.com/e/sWs6DmPME6

sig_00cb4035c1e3f4f6e4ff.description: Background Innovate UK Business Connect brings together businesses, researchers, investors and partners to accelerate innovation across the UK. As part of UK Research and Innovation (UKRI), and a strategic delivery partner to Innovate UK, we connect organisations to funding opportunities, partnerships and expertise to help ideas move from concept to scale. One of the key tools for making these connections is events. We deliver a diverse portfolio of in-person, virtual and hybrid events, ranging from webinars and workshops to large-scale conferences and exhibitions. To support the effective planning, delivery and evaluation of these events, we are seeking proposals from suppliers who can provide a modern event management system that streamlines event operations, enhances the participant experience and supports data-driven decision-making. Description of work Innovate UK Business Connect is seeking tenders from providers who can supply a single event management system that supports the end-to-end event lifecycle, including event creation, registration management, attendee communications, speaker and exhibitor management, networking, reporting and post-event evaluation. The system should integrate with existing business systems where required and provide a single source of truth for event delivery teams. This aligns with the organisation's wider objective of ensuring events are outcome-led, measurable and supported by efficient registration, communication and reporting processes. The event management system should: • Deliver an intuitive and user-friendly delegate journey from registration through to post-event follow-up • Improve the event experience for speakers and exhibitors • Reduce manual administration and improve operational efficiency • Provide real-time visibility of registrations, attendance, engagement and event performance • Support both virtual and in-person event delivery models • Enable consistent data capture and reporting to demonstrate event impact and ROI • Support accessibility, compliance and data protection requirements The platform must support multiple user roles and permission levels to reflect different operational needs across the organisation. As a minimum, the system should accommodate the following user groups: • Event Managers o Full end-to-end event management capabilities o Creation, configuration and administration of events o Management of registrations, attendee communications, speakers and exhibitors o Access to event-level reporting, analytics and post-event evaluation data • Marketing Managers o Access to update and manage event webpages and associated content o Access to registration, engagement and performance reporting • Integrated Systems o Administration of integrations between the event management platform and our CRM system (Workbooks) o Management of data flows, field mapping, data quality and synchronisation processes o Access to reporting, data exports and system configuration relating to integrations • System Administrators o A small number of designated super users (typically two to three individuals) o Full platform administration rights, including user management, permissions, integrations, security settings and system configuration We deliver a large and diverse portfolio of business-to-business events. Historically, this has included more than 300 events per year and generating approximately 60,000 delegate registrations annually. The event management platform must be capable of supporting a range of event formats, scales and audience sizes, including: • In person events: We deliver approximately 100 in-person events each year, typically attracting between 30 and 2,000 delegates to each. Most events are free to attend and may span one or more days. We do not require onsite event delivery support from the appointment supplier; however the platform must provide the functionality and tools to enable our team to manage attendee registration and onsite event operations, and provide a seamless and efficient onsite experience for attendees • Online Events: We deliver close to 200 fully online events annually. The majority are webinars, including webinar series and interactive workshops. We also run a small number of larger-scale virtual conferences and exhibitions, some of which take place over multiple days. The platform should provide a seamless user experience for both organisers and attendees and support the delivery of events of varying size and complexity. • Hybrid: A smaller proportion of our events are hybrid, combining in-person and virtual attendance. The platform should support hybrid event delivery and provide a consistent registration, communication and reporting experience across both audience groups. The proposed solution must be capable of supporting this volume of activity while providing robust registration management, attendee communications, data integration, reporting and analytics across all event formats. Timings This is a two-stage evaluation process. We will do an initially score of each supplier bid with the top two or three scoring suppliers invited to provide a demonstration. This will be the opportunity for the selected suppliers to demonstrate the setup of an event using a given scenario. Anticipated timeline: • October: demo • November: final evaluation • November - December: Contract is awarded • 1 April 2027: Contract starts • April - September: Onboarding, training, templates created and integrations built • September onwards: Events start to be managed from the platform Cost The maximum value of this requirement over the three-year period is a maximum of £600,000.00 excluding VAT. This contract is structured as an initial two-year period with a maximum budget of £400,000.00 excluding VAT with an optional 12-month extension valued at maximum £200,000.00 excluding VAT. Submission In response to this tender, please provide the information listed below. • Short narrative describing your overall approach to working with Innovate UK Business Connect • Checklist against the requirements • Supporting information against the essential requirements • A rate card of costs associated with services you provide • A completed copy of the Pre-Qualification Questionnaire including: o A copy of your audited accounts for the most recent two years (or alternative means of demonstrating financial status if trading for less than a year) • Legal information i.e. Your standard T&Cs Please provide the information requested above to re.support@iukbc.org.uk by 17:00 10 October 2026 at the latest. IR35 will be assessed before the awarding of a successful contract. Submissions sent without relevant documents as listed above will be automatically rejected. Innovate UK Business Connect may require successful submissions to be subject to non-disclosure agreements. Evaluation structure Submissions will be scored against the following areas: • Value for money - 20% • Technical specification - 70% o alignment to objective 10% o essential requirements 40% o desirable requirements 20% • Demonstration - 10% Lot 1: .

sig_011055b01c4d88cc16cc.description: A national programme is being established to encourage increased levels of physical activity and sustained participation in movement across England. The programme comprises a number of complementary workstreams, including marketing and communications, partnerships and engagement, rewards and recognition, educational content, and a digital component intended to support participation, engagement and long-term habit formation. The contracting authority is considering the future procurement of a supplier to design, build, operate and support the digital elements of the programme. A digital discovery exercise is currently underway and will provide an evidence-based recommendation for the future digital service, including user needs, service design, delivery approach and implementation roadmap. Whilst the final solution has not yet been determined, the discovery is expected to narrow the scope significantly and provide sufficient detail to support rapid delivery. The digital service may comprise a digital product, web-based service, social and community capability, AI-enabled engagement service, integration with existing consumer platforms, or a combination of these approaches. The successful supplier will be expected to take the outputs of the discovery phase through detailed design, build, deployment and live operation. The appointed supplier will work alongside other specialist partners responsible for marketing, communications, partnerships, rewards and wider programme delivery. The role of the digital supplier will be to translate programme objectives into effective digital services and experiences rather than duplicate functions delivered elsewhere within the programme. The programme is operating to ambitious timescales, with an initial digital capability expected to be launched before the end of 2026 and subsequently enhanced through live operation. The authority is therefore interested in engaging with suppliers who can demonstrate experience of delivering, operating and evolving user-centred digital services at pace. You are also welcome to apply for any other Lots on our DPS that you feel are relevant to your organisation. Should we decide to proceed to procurement, we are expecting to publish the Invitation to Quote to our Lot 5 suppliers towards the end of July 2026. This timeline is subject to change. sig_014d6bb9ab68582a49aa.description: Kela is planning to replace its current HR service package based on the SAP ERP environment. The objective of the market dialogue is, among other things, to form an up-to-date overall picture of alternatives available on the market and to gather suppliers' views on the preparation of the procurement's content, implementation model and contract terms. The procurement is preliminarily aimed at the following software and related services: 1. HR system The HR system must support at least the following areas: - HR master data (organisation data management, personal data management, employment relationship and salary basis management) - Competence management (competence management, competence profile, learning and renewal) - Training management (training and other events) - Continuous coaching discussion / development discussions - Salary discussion - Onboarding - Offboarding - Time management: holidays and absences - HR analytics and reporting 2. Payroll system - E-payslip distribution service 3. Working time management system The working time management solution must include at least: - Working time clocking - Working time reporting (allocation of working time to activities and projects) - Possible shift planning for period-based work (preliminary need) The delivery of the solution preliminarily involves the following requirements: - The solution must meet the functional and non-functional requirements set by Kela - A delivery and deployment project led by the supplier - Necessary integration implementations into other systems - Necessary conversion and migration implementations - Necessary training and documentation - Expert services that may be ordered separately (e.g. system development and consulting) Number of users: There are estimated to be approximately 8 500 users of the system at Kela. The objective of the market dialogue is, among other things: - to form an objective and comprehensive picture of solutions and implementation models on the market - to receive feedback on the content of the procurement subject and service package - to gather views on contract terms - to obtain information on prices and pricing bases Registration for the market dialogue: Kela requests interested suppliers to register and submit a short preliminary presentation of their solution (1-3). The market dialogue can also be conducted as Teams discussions. Registrations are requested to be sent by email: - Address: it.tarjouskilpailut@kela.fi - Message subject: HR-järjestelmä, ilmoittautuminen (1-3) - Content: company's official name and contact person's email address - Deadline: 21.4.2026. We particularly welcome views on the following themes: - Description of how the proposed system package meets Kela's needs - Access rights management, information security and data protection - Customer-specific test environment and related pricing - Integrations into other systems (principles, technologies, interfaces) - Usability-supporting solutions The material to be delivered is expected to include at least: - basic information on the system and architecture - description of support and maintenance - development roadmap - information security and data protection practices (e.g. role assignment, logging, auditing, data location)
sig_014d6bb9ab68582a49aa.title: Invitation to market dialogue: HR system entity as a SaaS service

sig_01ec67e5684cc534c0b2.description: Arkham Special Mission Processor (SMP): The Government is conducting market research to identify potential sources that possess the expertise, capabilities, facilities, and experience to manufacture, assemble, test, and deliver a total of 94 Arkham SMP Production Kits and 55 Spares. The Arkham SMP is a mission processor utilizing Sensor Open System Architecture (SOSA) in support of AC/MC-130J system integration. The Arkham SMP is separated into two (2) major processing areas: Video Processing/General Processing and Safety Critical Processing. The Video Processing/General Processing is done on five (5) Intel based General Purpose Processor Modules. The Safety Critical Processing is done on two (2) ARM based Safety Critical Processor (SCP) modules. The network includes a red and an internal NextGen SMP gold (same classified level with different subnets), and two unclassified black for multiple levels of security. Safety Critical Processing is separated into Red/Gold and Black zones. The Arkham SMP must utilize LYNXOS and Red Hat Enterprise Linux as the operating system. The acquisition strategy is for the contractor to provide kit production with a period of performance of seven (7) Years. The kit will include the following: Two (2) Arkham Units, two (2) External Data Storage (EDS) Devices, two (2) one (1) TB Delkin Solid State Drives (SSD), and other hardware required for aircraft installation. This will provide the AC/MC-130J mission with enhanced abilities for search and rescue in increased threat environments. Potential Sources must be capable of developing prototype hardware, software, and all associated technical data necessary to be able to produce and deliver the Arkham Production Kit and Spares. The Potential Source must be able to fully test and evaluate the function and performance of the Arkham Production Kit and Spares. The Potential Source must be capable of developing and providing the source data necessary to update AFTO’s and TDPs.
sig_01ec67e5684cc534c0b2.title: AC/MC-130J Arkham SMP Production

sig_021d3e32b4f73b363049.description: Avfall Sør would like to invite the market to a dialogue on the future solution for weighing residual waste at the recycling stations. The aim is to find a system with a high degree of automation/self-service, user friendliness and effective customer flow. It must take care of HSE considerations and be adapted to both the current and future needs for effective resource utilisation and sustainable operation. Avfall Sør has three recycling stations with high availability and access control. The residue waste is collected in large containers with compression; either closed compressor containers or open containers with rolling compressors. This can be changed, but a compressor system is wanted and protection from weather and wind. Key figures are given in the annex. We would like to charge for residual waste based on the weighted amount per customer, in order to comply with the polluter-payer principle and to ensure that sorting pays off. Avfall Sør has examined known systems in the market, but not found satisfactory systems. We would therefore like to have a dialogue with a tenderer who believes that they can offer this. The system must handle weighing and payment of residue waste in an efficient and user friendly way, without a requirement for dedicated manpower. Integration to established systems is not required, but we would like to present the possibilities. Tenderers are invited to submit a solution proposal with a description of relevant systems and price estimates, as well as a reference system. Deadline: 10.12.25, 16.00.Solution proposal can be sent in communication module in Mercell. Deadline for this: 03.12.25, 16:00.
sig_021d3e32b4f73b363049.title: Market dialogue - solution for weighing residual waste at recycling stations for Avfall Sør AS

sig_023870867493cccf1f1e.description: The scope of this contract is to acquire the full range of technical, management and support services necessary to obtain and maintain access to US food and cosmetic products. The contract is divided into the following task areas: Project Management Data Access Data Collection Training Support 6.1 Technical Requirements 6.1.1 Datasets The processed food and cosmetic products and their package data (as well as menu data) shall be from a currently existing, commercially available database(s) that shall provide immediate automated access. The data shall include products from all regions of the US (Appendix B indicates the US Census regions) and be accurate, quality-assured, and easily-validated; well organized; stored as relationally searchable information for trend and other analyses; and fully exportable. The database(s) shall be regularly updated and maintained in a current state throughout the base and option periods. Information will be required for the following product types: Processed, and retail food products (e.g. foods, infant formula, etc.; minimum 400,000 products that are selling on the market in the contract year) and thus, over 2 million historical products; (Optional) Restaurant food products/menu items (minimum 50,000 products from top chains) Dietary supplements (minimum 100,000 products); shall be categorized according to the definition in Appendix A Cosmetics (minimum 300,000 products) The following attributes (as shown on the package) shall be required: Package images (legible images of all surfaces (e.g. sides, top, bottom) of product packaging, including internal and external packaging Count of available images per product Information contained on and in product packaging – shall include the following at minimum (each data entry line in the database must be quality assured and -controlled (QA/QC’d) for accuracy as the database is populated) GTIN/UPC/Barcode Nutrition Facts label, including single and dual columns and including multi-packs (shall be displayed in format according to 21 CFR 101.9) and Supplement Facts label (shall be displayed in format according to 21 CFR 101.36(e)(10) (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)) Additional nutrients presenting on package labels Indication of added sugars Ingredients list (e.g. food additives, active ingredients for dietary supplements) Allergen labeling information (Contains/may contain) and advisory statements Pack size and weight Number of servings per package Brand Manufacturer Location of manufacturer, packer, or distributor Written and/or pictorial statements signaling the presence of one or more allergens (according to the Food Allergen Labeling and Consumer Protection Act (FALCPA) of 2004; e.g. “Contains”) and/or caution statements about the product (e.g. “warning statements”) Insignificant amounts for certain nutrients Claims on package (e.g., regulated, health, nutrition, efficacy, marketing, and all other types) including indication of “healthy” on package Statements/icons/signages and similar information that features the nutrition, health, organoleptic, processing, suggested usages (e.g., recipes), and other properties of the product (e.g., written and/or pictorial statements that feature nutrient content claim languages, front-of-pack language/icons) Certifications on package GE/Bioengineered/GMO language on package Verbatim language of all text (e.g. product description, instructions, etc.) and icons from product packaging Product source where collected Product category Dates of when product information is a) released to the market and on shelf, b) collected, c) published, d) updated, and e) discontinued Indication of “previous” or “new” nutrition facts label FNDDS 8-digit and 7-digit food codes; SR 5-digit sub codes (8-digit food code shall be linked to food products and ingredients;7-digit food codes are mapped to 8-digit at the product level; 5-digit SR sub codes are mapped to 8-digit food codes at the ingredient level) through 2019 GSFA (General Standard for Food Additives) categories through 2019 Food packaging types (primary and secondary) and codes Food content type Moreover, the data shall provide additional valid and verifiable information on the product ingredients; at a minimum, the data shall provide all available synonym name(s), allergen status, and technical or functional effect descriptors in a usable format. Additionally, FDA shall have access to other Mintel products, such as Mintel Leap, Mintel Food & Drink, Mintel Reports, Mintel Trends, Comperemedia Direct, Market Dynamics, and Global Consumer Research. 6.1.2 Product Requirements Overarching product requirements: Unlimited access for up to 200 FDA personnel; Located external to FDA network (access via weblink); Universal access from any FDA computer hardware (desktops, laptops with docking stations and/or scientific workstations) using internet browsers compatible with FDA current standards; Product access shall not be restricted according to product price; Capability to perform relational searching and analyses of the food and cosmetic product labeling and packaging datasets and menu datasets in functional environments using appropriate methodologies, which shall be valid, reliable, and robust; Ability to support disclosure of scientific and technical articles, study results, presentations, public health advisories, and similar works involving aggregated data to entities outside the Agency including the general public; High resolution, readable images for all sides of the package labels (and optionally, menu images) for validation and other research purposes. Images shall be displayed with product data from all sides of the package so that information may be easily verifiable by the user. Accurate data reflective of verbatim language and icons of product labels (and menus). Verification that products are still being sold in the US marketplace. Users shall be able to analyze and summarize their searches into summary reports and all available data and search results and outputs shall be downloadable and exportable within an accepted timeframe into Microsoft Excel Spreadsheets and Access Data Base Software, SAS Business Analytics Software, and other common formats. Regular, updated, extracted bulk/batch raw data of the full dataset shall be available by API and in MS Excel compatible format (e.g. single pipe delimited txt, csv) and shall be accessible in a secure FTP or cloud service acceptable by FDA. In addition to the product label (and menu) database(s), all sales data, other accompanying databases, and market research reports, when available, shall be provided. This information shall apply to food, dietary supplement, restaurant, and cosmetic products when available Data and UI status updates shall be posted on the system website main page and identified users shall be notified via email System usage statistics (including statistics regarding individual login usage and length of time logged in) shall be available in monthly reports and upon request All data and files shall undergo quality control checks prior to accessibility/delivery to FDA. Documentation on quality control procedures shall be provided (at the onset and with any changes over time) for all data and image collection and data processes (e.g. ingestion of data, quality assurance of data in different formats, etc.) as noted below. Web Interface A user-friendly and data comprehensive interface that is transparent and flexible and allows both predefined (i.e., canned) and custom reports shall be provided. The user should be able to conduct a multi-variable search (i.e. searching a combination of factors concurrently). The user should be able to search and filter according to product category, year, product name, UPC, brand, company, claims, ingredients, allergens, other product attributes, and user-entered keywords in any and all fields. Raw Data Files Raw files (e.g. MS Excel compatible, single pipe-delimited txt, csv) for all data (food, supplements, cosmetics, etc.) shall be delivered a minimum of quarterly as defined by FDA or downable without file size restriction. The file sizes should be appropriate so that they can be opened and readily used. Files shall be accessible in a secure FTP or cloud service acceptable by FDA and organized based on FDA specifications. All files shall also be available by API with fields as specified by FDA. The database(s) shall be scientific based on FDA’s definition: able to verify the data entry line(s) via product images, and the product’s contents may be analyzed, if the user chooses to have the item purchased and analyzed, to verify the accuracy/truthfulness of the product label, the offeror(s) shall provide this as a purchasable service. System maintenance during the base and all option periods, if exercised, shall be provided. Maintenance shall include upgrades and updates to the software and data, continued use of and access to the database system and data, and updates to technical and analytical documentation. 6.1.3 Documentation The Contractor shall compile and submit full documentation to the Contracting Officer Representative (COR) and Project Officer (PO) within 14 days of the beginning of the contract as well as any updated documentation through the contract years. After approval by the COR, all documentation shall be available to access online in the database(s) system with downloadable format into MS Word. The Contractor shall provide documentation on the following: All data collection and acquisition processes so that the source data is clearly understood Documentation on the status of all products found in the databases relative to what is selling on the market each year of the contract (e.g., is the product verified as being available in retail for purchase and/or is it discontinued). The methodologies used for any data cleaning and ingestion processes and those used to develop the data as well as information on pertinent software used as part of the process Data dictionary and a code book defining all data elements/fields that are included in the data package, which includes information on how calculations are performed relative to certain data fields Documentation on the process of standardizing and cleaning data from different sources as well as information on UPCs that are duplicated (e.g. historical vs, duplicated) Any related technical specifications on the technologies or software that is used Information on how to access and use the data in all formats Written methodology regarding quality control procedures for all data and images collected, ingested into a database, exported, and categorized, including information on the oversight of quality control to ensure above 98% accuracy Interface documentation and user guides Any updates to general processes, methodologies, data sources, QC processes, Documentation on limitations of database, errors in the database, and plans for mitigation and/or resolution of issues Full-disclosure 6.1.4 Support / Training A. Support: Ongoing technical and analytical support by phone or by e-mail shall be provided to all certified users of the data during business hours (9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time) throughout the period of performance (POP) in accordance with the service levels established in the contract. The Contractor shall notify the COR regarding any issues as they relate to Acceptable Quality Level (AQL) standards. All technical related issues would need to be addressed and resolved in 5 business days or within a reasonable timeframe agreement upon with COR and TCOR. B. Training: The Contractor shall provide up to two (2) one-day training sessions per year (on-site or via web-based methods). This training can be divided into shorter time periods. Additional options for additional “on-demand” sessions either in person or via web-based methods shall be made available under the IDIQ portion of the award. 6.1.5 Data Disclosure Clearance As part of its regulatory activities, FDA shall, at times, require disclosure of scientific and technical articles, study results, presentations, public health advisories, and similar works involving aggregated data to entities outside the Agency including the general public. For activities that require disclosure of aggregated data the Contractor shall accept and adhere to the FDA Data Disclosure Clearance Procedures and form found in Appendices D. The FDA shall continue to require the ability to release aggregated data through the FDA Data Disclosure Clearance process for data obtained during the contract period for the period of all Option Periods. The FDA will require the services of processing clearance requests. As part of its regulatory activities, FDA shall, at times engage in collaborative research projects with third parties outside of FDA for specific research projects of public health importance that are initiated by and for the benefit of FDA. These collaborations shall require FDA to have the ability to share project specific aggregated or raw data with third parties for collaborative research projects. For these collaborations that require sharing of aggregated or raw data, the Contractor shall accept and adhere to the Data Disclosure Clearance Procedures and form to be found in Appendices D. These Procedures include terms and conditions for third party collaborations. 6.2 Project Management The Contractor shall be responsible for creating, managing and updating project plans, schedules and managing resources for the project. 6.2.1 Quality Control The Contractor shall ensure that quality control procedures are conducted prior to providing FDA access to data. The Contractor shall provide written methodology on quality control procedures for all data and images collected, ingested into a database, exported, and categorized, including information on the oversight of quality control to ensure above 98% accuracy. The Contractor shall notify the COR should any issues with the data be noticed and shall flag it in the interface. Should FDA notice issues with the data, the Contractor shall address and fix the issues immediately within an agreed upon timeframe with the COR. 6.2.2 Reporting The Contractor shall provide a brief work plan outlining the strategy for supporting each of the areas outlined in Section 4 of the SOW to the COR within 10 days of award. Each month the Contractor shall provide a status report giving brief descriptions of activities performed. The monthly status report shall, at minimum, contain the following: usage statistics for databases and other resources; usage statistics of technical support feature by FDA staff; technical issues reported by FDA staff; other technical issues (ex. log of times when database(s)/resources were inaccessible), data ingestion success and failure rates with mitigation plans should issues be present. The Contractor shall conduct yearly face-to-face presentation meetings with the COR and other FDA staff as well as deliver final written progress reports about contract performance for the preceding period of performance. The Contractor shall submit to the COR a final report which documents and summarizes the results of the contract work 10 days prior to the end of each period of performance. The final report shall include tables, graphs, diagrams, curves, sketches, photographs and drawings as necessary and in sufficient detail to comprehensively explain the results achieved under this contract. 6.3 Contract Services Requirements The Contractor shall perform the following types of tasks as needed: Contractor shall collect information for selected products. The list of products and data fields to be collected shall be defined by the COR. Contractor shall conduct search(es) for products using search criteria defined by the COR. The option shall be available to purchase identified products. Contractor shall conduct exports for products using search criteria defined by the COR as needed. sig_0273419f3619102cfe5e.description: Link Group, the Contracting Authority, is seeking to modernise its telephony and contact management environment as part of a wider customer experience transformation. The requirement is not limited to a like-for-like telephony replacement. Link is seeking to understand how the market can support a move from fragmented channels and siloed systems towards a single, integrated and insight-led contact management platform. The primary objective is to implement a modern, scalable, cloud-based Contact Centre as a Service (CCaaS) solution capable of supporting seamless multi-channel customer engagement across voice, live chat, messaging, social media and future digital channels. Link is particularly interested in solutions that can provide a single view of the customer, intelligent routing based on customer intent and need, real-time operational visibility, workforce engagement capability and data-driven insight across the end-to-end customer journey. This Prior Information Notice (PIN) is issued solely to initiate a Preliminary Market Consultation exercise. The purpose is to test market capability, understand available delivery models, inform Link’s emerging specification and procurement strategy, and explore how suppliers can support both technology replacement and service transformation outcomes, including automation, virtual assistants, AI-assisted colleague support, workforce management and customer journey-led redesign. Link’s emerging priorities include reducing repeat contact, redials, avoidable transfers and misdirected queries; improving colleague access to customer history and knowledge prompts; enabling real-time demand management and reporting; increasing digital adoption through automation and self-service; and ensuring that future technology is aligned to priority customer journeys rather than being designed around existing channel structures. Lot 1: . Link Group is a group of social enterprise companies and one of Scotland’s largest social landlords. Link Group provides affordable housing, property management, regeneration, advice, financial inclusion, employability, care and support services to a large and diverse customer base across Scotland. Link Group serves more than 20,000 customers and provides housing management services to circa 16,000 tenants in social rented accommodation, including general needs and sheltered housing. The Link Group structure includes a number of related organisations and service areas that collectively deliver housing, property, care, support and community-based services. These include Link Group Ltd, which provides core group functions; Link Group Housing Services, which delivers housing management services for social rented tenants; C~urb, which brings together development, property management, letting, factoring and property maintenance activities; Horizon Housing Association, which provides affordable housing and services that support people with impairments to live independently; Larkfield Housing Association, a community-based Registered Social Landlord in Greenock; LinkLiving, which provides person-centred care, housing support and wellbeing services, and West Highland Housing Association, which provides affordable housing, property management, and maintenance services across the Lorn area and the Inner Hebridean islands of Scotland. The proposed replacement of telephony and contact centre systems is intended to support the wider Link Group operating environment rather than a single isolated service area. The future solution may therefore need to support multiple customer-facing and colleague-facing functions across housing, repairs, property management, factoring, care and support, advice, employability, development and corporate services. The Customer Service Centre (CSC) acts as a primary customer contact function, managing enquiries across housing, repairs, income, complaints and related services. Link also operates specialist customer-facing teams, including services supporting housing applications, registrations, lettings, responsive repairs, planned maintenance, compliance activities and property-related enquiries. These teams collectively support high-volume contact across a broad range of customer journeys. For market-sizing purposes, Link currently anticipates a future licence requirement in the region of 250–500 user licences across the Group, subject to confirmation through future operating model development, service design and multi-skilling activity. Given the scale and breadth of these services, effective contact management is central to Link’s ability to provide responsive, accessible and joined-up services to tenants, owners, applicants, private rented sector customers, supported people, partners and other stakeholders. This group-wide context is important because suppliers may be required to demonstrate how their proposed solution can support different operating models, service hours, customer journeys, user groups, reporting requirements, call flows, contact channels and integration needs across Link Group. Link is therefore seeking market insight into solutions that can provide scalable, resilient and configurable contact management capability across the full breadth of the group, while enabling consistent customer experience, improved colleague access to information and better operational insight.. sig_04513333c2a298124a08.description: Network Rail is seeking to engage the market regarding the future procurement of a Certificate Lifecycle Management (CLM) solution. This project is driven by significant industry changes, including the CA/Browser Forum’s decision to reduce the maximum lifespan of public SSL/TLS certificates over the coming years. By 2029, certificates will require renewal as frequently as every 47 days, and domain validation reuse will be limited to just 10 days. These changes are intended to enhance security but will introduce substantial operational overhead, making manual certificate management impractical and automation essential. Network Rail operates across a complex landscape of on-premises, cloud, and supplier-managed environments. A key challenge is the fragmented ownership and lack of central visibility over certificates, particularly those issued and managed by third-party suppliers. This fragmentation increases the risk of outages due to expired or misconfigured certificates and limits Network Rail’s ability to monitor, renew, or enforce compliance directly. The CLM project aims to address these challenges by implementing a solution that enables the centralised, automated management of certificates throughout their lifecycle, regardless of where they are issued or managed. The solution must provide comprehensive visibility across all environments, support robust automation for renewal and validation, and enable clear supplier accountability through contractual mechanisms. This includes the ability to track certificates managed by third parties, enforce renewal responsibilities, and ensure that incidents caused by supplier failures can be managed contractually. Network Rail is inviting suppliers to demonstrate how their solutions can meet these requirements, including the ability to: Centrally track and manage certificates across all environments and suppliers. Automate certificate renewal, validation, and compliance processes. Provide visibility and control over third-party issued certificates. Support supplier accountability and contractual enforcement. Align with upcoming industry standards and security requirements. Deliver proven solutions at scale, with references from similar large infrastructure organisations. This market engagement will inform Network Rail’s approach to the procurement of a CLM solution that ensures security, operational resilience, and compliance in a rapidly evolving digital landscape. sig_04bd4dfefcc7481716c7.description: Provision of a marketplace platform The advertised online portal is to be connected to SAP SRM as a catalogue via an interface based on the Open Catalog Interface (OCI) standard. In the intended process, the catalogue is called up by the user via a link from SAP SRM; it opens in a new browser window and is displayed there in a frame. In this catalogue, the user compiles a shopping basket from the required items. In the supplier's catalogue application, the user then completes the shopping basket after a verification step and initiates the transfer of the catalogue shopping basket to SAP SRM via the OCI interface. All items, quantities, and prices are transferred to the SRM shopping cart via the interface. The order is then completed by the user within the university according to a specified approval process and transmitted to the supplier. Direct order triggering from the supplier's online portal must not take place. The catalogue solution offered must therefore meet the conditions for connection from Appendix 5 "OCI Catalogue Performance Requirements" and for order transmission from Appendix 4 "IDOC Interface". SAP SRM is expected to be replaced by a successor product in the year 2026. Any necessary system adjustments to the marketplace connection will be supported by the contractor.

sig_0582aba2ee02a37a2288.description:
Supply of a forest fire location system divided into two parts. Part No. 1 - Supply, installation and commissioning of a forest fire monitoring system based on long-range fire-fighting cameras together with software for automatic smoke detection. Part No. 2 - Supply, installation and commissioning of a complete unmanned aerial vehicle system with an automatic docking station for fire monitoring of forest areas. A detailed description can be found in the relevant parts of the contract. The subject of the contract consists of sets of equipment together with installation and commissioning, the task of which will be to enable automatic detection and location of forest fires, including long-range fire-fighting cameras mounted on observation towers together with necessary accessories and the equipment of the Inspectorate's Alarm and Dispatch Point (ADP). The purpose of the system will be to carry out continuous fire monitoring of forest areas. Fire-fighting cameras mounted on observation towers are to work with the supplied software for automatic fire detection, which is intended to increase the effectiveness of monitoring in the given area. The image from the cameras must be sent to the ADP via a radio link in the unlicensed band, supplied and installed under this contract. The transmission system must be designed in a way that enables the future change of the transmission medium from radio to fibre-optic without the need to replace cameras, software and active network devices, with the exception of terminal devices used for connecting the fibre optic.. The Baczków and Hysne towers should be retrofitted with an Off-Grid power supply installation, and the ADP with a UPS emergency power supply system. The power supply must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62040-5-3:2017-05 (UPS systems) or equivalent. The installation must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62446-1:2016-08 (Photovoltaic installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62446-1:2016-08/A1:2019-01 (Testing of PV installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62109-2:2011 (Inverter safety) or equivalent and PN-EN IEC 62619:2023-02 (Lithium battery safety) or equivalent. The contract includes: - dismantling of the existing fire monitoring system, - supply and installation of 3 cameras for observing forest areas on the Baczków, Hysne and Dąbrowa fire-fighting towers, - supply and installation of sprinklers together with a fluid tank for the mounted cameras, - supply and installation of an off-grid power supply on the Baczków and Hysne towers. The installation must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62548 (Photovoltaic installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62446 (Testing of PV installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62109 (Inverter safety) or equivalent and PN-EN IEC 62619 (Lithium battery safety) or equivalent. - supply and installation of an alarm system and anti-burglary cameras on the fire-fighting towers, - supply and installation of radio links establishing connections: ● Baczków tower – Hysne tower in the 5 GHz band, ● Hysne tower – Dąbrowa tower in the 5 GHz band, ● Dąbrowa tower – Church in the 60 GHZ band with a backup 5 GHz, ● Church – Inspectorate building in the 60 GHZ band with a backup 5 GHz, ● Baczków tower – Dąbrowa tower in the 5 GHz band (redundant connection), - supply and installation of devices to provide backup communication 5G/LTE, - supply and installation of ADP equipment: ● supply and installation of 3 televisions for observing images from fire-fighting cameras, ● supply and installation of a computer with two monitors, ● supply and installation of a control console, ● supply and installation of a UPS emergency power supply. The power supply must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62040 (UPS systems) or equivalent. - supply, installation and commissioning of an automatic smoke detection system, - training on system operation. The Contractor is obliged to execute a complete work from the point of view of the purpose it is to serve. The Contracting Authority permits the installation of additional devices not included in the specification if they are necessary to achieve the required functionalities. Other information can be found in the procurement documents - Appendix No. 2 to the ToR; Supply, installation and commissioning of a complete unmanned aerial vehicle system with an automatic docking station for fire monitoring of forest areas - equipment under the FEnIKS project entitled: Comprehensive project for the adaptation of forests and forestry to climate change - prevention, counteracting and limiting the effects of threats related to forest fires (FIRE 2). 1. Subject of the contract 1.1. The subject of the contract is the supply of one complete, factory-new and unused UAS system comprising an unmanned aerial vehicle, an automatic docking station, a multi-sensor observation head, a control device, software, accessories, installation, configuration, commissioning, training and warranty service. 1.2. The system will be intended primarily for: automatic and ad-hoc patrols of forest areas during the fire hazard period; remote verification of smoke or fire alarms, including alarms transmitted by the alarm and dispatch point, camera system or rescue services; locating heat sources and determining their coordinates; live transmission in the visible and thermal imaging band; monitoring fire development, access roads, endangered objects and control after extinguishing a fire. 1.3. The subject of the contract has been described through functional requirements and minimum performance parameters. The Contracting Authority does not require a product of a specific brand or a single manufacturer's solution. However, all elements must form one compatible system, for the correct operation of which the Contractor is responsible. 2. Basis and rules for describing the subject of the contract. The description was drawn up taking into account in particular Article 16, Article 99, Article 101 and Article 105–107 of the Act of 11 September 2019 on Public Procurement Law (unified text: Journal of Laws of 2026, item 793 as amended). References to standards are to be understood as references to the indicated standard or an equivalent standard.

• Each indicated parameter is a minimum parameter, unless expressly stated otherwise. • Structurally different technical solutions are permitted if they ensure at least the same functionality, level of security and performance parameters. • If meeting a requirement requires an additional module, licence, modem, antenna, service or accessory, this element must be included in the tender and price. • All costs necessary to use the full functionality of the system for the period indicated in the OPZ must be itemised in the price form. Other information can be found in the procurement documents - Appendix No. 2 to the ToR

sig_05f5a9e0264aff4765ba.description: Helse Nord-Trøndelag HF, St. Olavs Hospital HF and Helse Møre og Romsdal HF have, by their clinics for mental health care, drug treatment, rehabilitation and habilitation need to use digital, standardised and normed review and mapping tools. The tools shall be used in mapping, reviewing, diagnosing patients in all age groups. They shall be based on recognised, standardised and normed methods. For example, cognitive ability tests, mapping executive functions, symptom mapping, function mapping, mapping of quality of life and mapping of patient satisfaction. We would like the different tools to be included in a digital platform where we as a customer can choose between different tools. As a minimum the delivery must include cognitive ability tests. The ability tests ought to include an option to also map verbal and non-verbal abilities. We are also interested in deliveries that cover parts of the needs, if one delivery does not cover all of the needs described here. Requirements for a digital system. We need a digital system that covers the needs outlined above, which ensure uniform administration, automatic scoring and reporting, which provides safe processing of sensitive data. The solution must also provide an option to use the existing paper based test set where the scoring still occurs digitally.

sig_0667c6733ad6a0223604.description: This notice is a prior information notice concerning the procurement of Internet capacity. This notice does not constitute a request for tenders. The notice is accompanied by an invitation to a technical market dialogue, giving all suppliers interested in the procurement the opportunity to engage in dialogue regarding the procurement with Istekki Oy. The purpose of the notice is to survey the market regarding operators interested in the procurement and to initiate a dialogue with interested operators. The objective is to discuss the subject matter of the procurement and its specification at a general level, and to gather information concerning the subject matter of the procurement for future tendering. In particular, the aim is to examine the market situation of Internet capacity and telecommunications connections, functional and technical characteristics, suppliers' pricing principles and price level. Respondents to the notice will not be remunerated for participating in the technical market dialogue. Technical dialogue is not a prerequisite for participating in any subsequent tendering. Nor does the technical dialogue bind Istekki Oy to carry out the procurement. The technical dialogue will be conducted through commenting on draft versions of the tender documentation and answering questions from the Contracting Authority relating to the subject matter of the procurement. The subject matter of the dialogue and future procurement consists of telecommunications connections used to connect Istekki Oy's network to the public Internet. The overall scope consists of two redundant Internet capacity connections. The aim of the procurement is to ensure business continuity and efficiency for the organisation by procuring sufficient Internet capacity. The procurement is divided into two lots. The maximum number of lots awarded is restricted to one lot per tenderer. REGISTRATION: Suppliers must notify their interest in participating in the technical market dialogue no later than 19.01.2026 by 16:00 by sending an email to hankinnat@istekki.fi with the subject heading: "Internet capacity - registration for market dialogue". Suppliers are requested to provide the following information in the message: - supplier contact person's email address Istekki Oy reserves the right to invite registered suppliers also to bilateral negotiations, to organise an open market dialogue session with registered suppliers or to continue the technical dialogue in another manner specified separately. Participating companies will not be remunerated for responding or participating. The information provided will be treated confidentially.

sig_06e3026067216c0f322c.description: NEW mobil und aktiv Mönchengladbach GmbH and NEW mobil und aktiv Viersen GmbH are public undertakings responsible for transport and swimming pool operations in the cities of Mönchengladbach and Viersen. Furthermore, the companies hold line concessions in the Rhein-Kreis Neuss, the Kreis Viersen and the Kreis Heinsberg. In the following, NEW mobil und aktiv Mönchengladbach GmbH is named for both companies. The two transport companies of the NEW Group, NEW mobil und aktiv Mönchengladbach GmbH and NEW mobil und aktiv Viersen GmbH, intend to introduce an ID-based ticketing system (IDBT) for the digitalisation and modernisation of sales in local public passenger transport. The aim is to implement cash-free and paperless ticketing based on EMV-compatible bank cards (open loop) as well as supplementary closed-loop EMV credit cards for user groups without a bank account. The project comprises the creation of an overall system. The scope of supply and services is structured as follows: 1. contactless sales devices (validators), 2. software and interfaces (purchase licences via a one-off fee) as well as 3. supplementary services such as installation and commissioning in the vehicle, project management, documentation and training. Following overall system acceptance, the overall IDBT system is to be operated with the following services: 1. operation of hardware, software and interfaces, 2. operation of a cloud, 3. processing of the transit payment service as well as 4. provision of supplementary services such as system service, software maintenance and conclusion of mobile communications contracts. The aim is customer-friendly, rapid and cash-free sales within the vehicle, in which, after a tap with an open-loop EMV or closed-loop EMV card at the validator, the encrypted token identity serves as a digital ticket. Initially, predefined tariff products (KFT) will be offered at the validator, and check-in-check-out (MTT) will also be used from a prospective perspective. For the project tendered here, "Introduction of an ID-based ticketing system (IDBT) for the digitalisation and modernisation of sales in local public passenger transport", funding is being sought via the Verkehrsverbund Rhein-Ruhr (VRR) in order to finance the introduction and operation. NEW mobil und aktiv Mönchengladbach GmbH and NEW mobil und aktiv Viersen GmbH are each carrying out the project "Introduction of an ID-based ticketing system" as an independent funding measure in accordance with the scheduling notifications of the VRR (OM 2025 02116 or 2025 04166). The present project can only be implemented if funding is granted to the extent previously discussed with the funding body. There is currently no reason to fear that the envisaged funding notifications would not be issued. Nevertheless, it must be clearly stated that at the time of the commencement of this procurement procedure, no funding notification is available. Therefore, the explicit notice must be given here that, should it – for whatever reasons – not have happened by immediately prior to the award of contract of this procurement procedure that NEW mobil und aktiv Mönchengladbach GmbH or NEW mobil und aktiv Viersen GmbH have received funding notifications from the aforementioned funding programme in the extents previously discussed with the funding body, the contract cannot be awarded. Either the binding period must then be extended in agreement with the bidders or the procurement procedure must be terminated by cancellation, especially in the event that there is ultimately no prospect whatsoever of obtaining funding. Then the procurement procedure cannot be concluded by contract award. As the general contractor, the contractor assumes overall responsibility for the planning, delivery, integration, commissioning and stable operation of the ID-based overall ticketing solution ("NEW IDBT") including all hardware and software components as well as all interfaces and dependencies. It shall ensure that the overall solution is fully functional in accordance with the specification over the entire contract term and that the relevant requirements of the card schemes (inter alia transit/retail-like and PAYG/MTT transactions) are complied with. The EVB-IT contract underlying the tender shall begin with the award of contract and end upon the expiry of 120 months after overall system acceptance. The contract shall be extended after the expiry of 120 months three times by 24 months each under the same conditions, if it is not terminated by the contracting authority with a notice period of six months to its end. sig_070576f1552b42207971.description: Groupe E currently uses the ServiceNow platform as a central tool for several internal and customer-oriented processes. The instance, named "Nestor", has been progressively configured to meet the operational and organisational needs of the Group. ServiceNow is used in particular for business request management, offering a centralised portal and automated workflows to facilitate the processing and tracking of internal requests. The platform also constitutes an essential pillar of ITSM, covering incident, change, task and problem management. Beyond internal processes, ServiceNow is used for customer request management, allowing for better traceability, improved service quality and optimal management of commitments (SLAs). The solution also integrates a module dedicated to vehicle fleet management, ensuring the operational and administrative monitoring of the Group's mobility resources. The ServiceNow instance is currently maintained and evolved by an external partner, who provides application support, specific developments and technical integration, in collaboration with internal governance teams. As the ServiceNow licence contract and service contract with the integrator are expiring, Groupe E is launching this call for tenders to ensure the continuity of these services, optimise costs and guarantee consistent development of the platform for the coming years. This lot concerns the acquisition of licences necessary for the use of the ServiceNow solution; The purpose of this lot is the provision of support services related to our ServiceNow instances

sig_076d9e425446174684f7.description: External receipt and processing of documents for invoice verification processes in accordance with Section 302 of the Fifth Book of the Social Code (SGB V) and the Eleventh Book of the Social Code (SGB XI). Lot LOT-0001: Comprehensive scanning service with end-to-end overall responsibility. In order to achieve further efficiency gains in the processes, invoice processing is to be digitalised. This specifically affects billing processes pursuant to Section 302 SGB V and Section 105 SGB XI. The scope of incoming mail digitalisation covers the invoice processes for aids, remedial therapies, travel expenses, rehabilitative sport and functional training, midwifery/obstetric care, care benefits in kind, day and respite care, and advisory visits pursuant to Section 302 SGB V as well as Section 105 SGB XI. The contractor receives the unopened letter and parcel post of the contracting authority (e.g. invoices or invoice components) in paper form. The contractor must independently perform all preparatory work necessary for scanning the documents. This includes, for example, opening envelopes and dispatch material, documenting the date of receipt and, if necessary, removing staples or other materials such as adhesive tape. The incoming documents must be scanned by the contractor and provided as a PDF document of PDF version 1.7 in the PDF/A 1 format. The contracting parties shall jointly agree on deviating versions. Scanning must be carried out in colour and with a resolution of at least 200 DPI. Both the front and back of the documents must be scanned. Scanning also includes the digitalisation of accompanying attachments. The contractor must ensure that documents deemed irrelevant by the contracting authority can be subsequently deleted or redacted by the contracting authority. These may include, for example, medical records that should not normally have been made available to the health insurance fund for data protection reasons. Following digitalisation and provision of the documents to the contracting authority, they must be stored for 30 calendar days and subsequently destroyed by the contractor. The contracting authority is entitled to request the original documents (e.g. for auditing purposes) within 30 calendar days. The contractor shall ensure that the documents are transmitted to the contracting authority within 14 calendar days. The documents must be provided with a qualified electronic signature/seal by the contractor immediately after scanning.
sig_076d9e425446174684f7.title: external scanning services

sig_077ef83a016c7df29302.description: The Home Office seeks to engage suppliers for the provision of healthcare services at short-term holding facilities and ports of entry across the UK. These services will support individuals whilst detained for short periods of time including in, but not limited to, short-term holding facilities as defined under the Short-Term Holding Facilities Rules 2018 (as amended), where individuals can be held up to 24 hours. The Authority is seeking a flexible, responsive and value for money healthcare solution that meets the basic needs of individuals and can be flexible to different service environments; the short-term holding facilities are located at different location types across the UK which include Airports, Seaports, and Reporting Centres. Remote Healthcare Services: This market engagement aims to understand supplier capabilities and appetite, to further refine the Authority’s specification and gather feedback on the proposed approach of remote healthcare services. This includes gaining further understanding of both the provision of Clinicians to undertake remote consultations and the provision of IT infrastructure required to deliver a remote only healthcare service. The content of this Notice, including the nature of services and the start date of the contract, is subject to change. The contract is expected to commence in early 2028. sig_0791676438d5426f0c44.description: Framework agreement on the provision, implementation and operation of rostering software in the form of a software-as-a-service (SaaS) for UKHD and other authorised ordering parties. In order to ensure university medical care at the highest level under the economic conditions on the wards and departments, a new cloud-based solution (software as a service (SaaS)) is to be introduced for the following application areas, including upstream and downstream tasks, and operated by the contractor for UKHD and other authorised ordering parties: - Holiday and absence management/rostering - Time management - Employee Self Service (ESS) / Manager Self Service (MSS) - Reporting and statistics. The rostering solution is intended to enable more efficient planning and handling of processes relating to rostering, control and billing. Due to the very close interaction, both functionally and data-related, the aforementioned application areas/functional units are to be considered as a single unit. Standard software is being tendered (no custom development) that implements the client's requirements or is to be adapted through appropriate configuration/parametrisation. Furthermore, the consolidation and standardization of the processes supported by the offered rostering solution are the subject of the tendered service; this must take place in close coordination with the client. The procurement project comprises the provision of a software-as-a-service (SaaS) system that enables the client to use the application in accordance with the contractually agreed service level agreements (SLAs). The contractor shall ensure the proper operation as well as the care and maintenance of the SaaS system during the contract term to the extent necessary to comply with the agreed SLAs. The rostering solution must be seamlessly integrated into the IT environment of UKHD via interfaces. The solution to be provided must be integrated into the IT environment of UKHD via seamless interface integration. The integration of the rostering solution ensures smooth data exchange without media breaks. In addition, supplementary services listed in this specification (e.g. training) are an integral part of the bid and the total price. Functional additions or extensions that are not the subject of the requirements in the specification are excluded from this. sig_0897a4bf55bdb8b956cc.description: The subject of this tender comprises consultancy and support services for the CCoE SAP KTBE. The estimated total volume is approximately CHF 50,5 million (approx. 50’500 TCHF) over the next five years (from January 2027). sig_08fcc417ba7e7ee3891e.description: The Region of Southern Denmark is facing the procurement of a new regional IT solution for the imaging diagnostics areas (hereinafter the "Solution"). The Solution must encompass RIS, PACS, VNA, Clinical Viewer as well as support for breast cancer screening and constitutes the central clinical tool for radiological and nuclear medicine departments at the Region of Southern Denmark. The Solution must be put into operation at 4 hospital units distributed across 12 radiological departments, 3 nuclear medicine departments as well as the regional breast cancer screening. The Region of Southern Denmark has several hundred imaging modalities and performs over 1 million examinations annually. The Solution must support an efficient clinical workflow in a patient-safe and user-friendly manner, as well as ensure the coherent patient pathway across hospital units, departments and specialties. The Solution must be a robust, stable and well-functioning tool in the clinicians' daily work while simultaneously possessing the flexibility necessary to accommodate future improvement initiatives and changed needs. The tendered procurement is described in further detail in Appendix-03 with sub-appendices. The procurement itself encompasses functionality to support workflows within radiology, nuclear medicine and mammography screening, as well as the storage of imaging diagnostics examinations. The procurement furthermore encompasses the implementation and maintenance of the new solution. BDSYD principles: The procurement is made on the basis of four overarching principles, which the Parties must correspondingly use as fundamental principles for the Solution and the collaboration: • Efficient support of the patients' journey: The Solution is patient-safe, labour-saving, intuitive and user-friendly. • Stable operation: The large volume of imaging diagnostics examinations can take place securely, unperturbed by downtime and operational stoppages to the benefit of patients, employees and efficiency. • Performance: Short system response times in the solution and good performance, which is important for patients, employees and efficiency. • Standard solution: The Solution is well-functioning and well-tested in a comparable setup and has open and well-defined interfaces. There is an option for the Central Denmark Region and the North Denmark Region for the procurement of a corresponding solution, cf. Appendix-19 with sub-appendices. The Region of Southern Denmark is conducting the procurement on behalf of all the regions, and separate contracts will subsequently be concluded between the chosen Supplier and the individual region. It is noted that the Region of Southern Denmark has geoblocking in relation to a number of countries as listed in Appendix-02.A. The list can be requested by contacting via the communication tab on the Ethics tender site and can be received by interested suppliers upon a confidentiality declaration from the requesting party. This has been accounted for in the determined tender deadline.
sig_08fcc417ba7e7ee3891e.title: Procurement, implementation and maintenance of an imaging diagnostics solution

sig_091918c49ae03344e714.description: The NHS Counter Fraud Authority (NHSCFA) is a health authority charged with identifying, investigating and preventing fraud and other economic crime within the NHS and the wider health group. As a health authority focused entirely on counter fraud work, the NHSCFA is independent from other NHS bodies and directly accountable to the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC). THE NHSCFA currently operate two separate systems for the provision of an intelligence database and a case management system. The intention is to identify if there is a single solution that can replace the existing systems. If that is not possible then the aim would be to have two separate products that connect and align with each other to avoid duplication and operational inefficiencies. This market engagement exercise seeks the views and opinions of those organisations that may be interested in delivering the requirements. The scope of this market engagement covers is provided within the draft service specification. This exercise and any subsequent responses are in no way legally binding on any party. Participation in the engagement exercise is not a mandatory requirement for participating in any potential future procurement; however, responses received will assist to inform the Contracting Authority as to the level of interest from the market and will be used to evidence a decision as to whether or not to undertake a competitive procurement. The Market Engagement Questionnaire and current Service Specifications can be downloaded from SAP Ariba Portal at the below link: https://discovery.ariba.com/rfx/23496944 Please return your completed MEQ through the Portal no later than 5pm on 30 October 2025.
