sig_091adee7794510240399.description: The Contractor shall provide Think Trends Software as an Agentic AI and Document Intelligence solution capable of processing structured, semi-structured, and unstructured adverse event documents, including scanned PDFs, handwritten or machine-generated forms, narratives, attachments, medical records, product complaints, lab reports, follow-up submissions, and case correspondence. The solution shall support end-to-end adverse event document processing through the following capabilities: A. Agentic Document Intake and Classification Think Trends Software AI agents shall automatically receive, classify, and route adverse event documents by submission type, FDA Center, product category, source, urgency, and case-processing requirements. The intake agent shall identify whether a document relates to drugs, biologics, devices, veterinary products, tobacco products, combination products, or other FDA-regulated products. Key capabilities include: • Automated ingestion of scanned PDFs, forms, emails, images, attachments, and electronic documents. • Classification of documents by Center-specific workflow, product type, and reporting pathway. • Detection of new cases, follow-up cases, duplicate submissions, incomplete submissions, and supporting attachments. • Intelligent routing to appropriate review queues, case-processing teams, or downstream systems. B. Agentic OCR and Intelligent Data Extraction Think Trends Software Agentic OCR shall combine optical character recognition, computer vision, natural language processing, large language models, and rule-based validation agents to extract key adverse event data elements from complex documents. The platform shall extract and structure critical case information, including: • Reporter, patient, animal, subject, or consumer information. • Product information, including drug, biologic, device, tobacco, or veterinary product details. • Adverse event terms, symptoms, outcomes, seriousness, and event narratives. • Dates, timelines, exposure details, dose, route, duration, lot numbers, manufacturer information, and product identifiers. • Medical history, concomitant products, lab results, device problem codes, clinical narratives, and follow-up information. • Center-specific data elements required for CVM-Drugs and CVM-Food, CDRH, CTP, CDER, CBER and HFP. C. Center-Specific Adverse Event Processing Agents The Contractor shall configure specialized AI agents within Think Trends Software to support unique regulatory and operational needs across FDA Centers. Each agent shall apply Center-specific data models, validation logic, terminology, business rules, and review workflows. Examples include: • CVM Agent: Processes veterinary adverse event reports, animal species, breed, weight, product exposure, dosage, outcome, and veterinarian/reporter information. • CDRH Agent: Processes device-related adverse events, device identifiers, manufacturer information, malfunction details, patient impact, and device problem descriptions. • CTP Agent: Processes tobacco product adverse experiences, product use patterns, health effects, consumer narratives, and product category information. • HFP Agent: Processes HFP-specific adverse event reporting requirements and associated workflows. • CDER Agent: Process drug product adverse experiences, product use patterns, health effects, consumer narratives, and product category information. • CBER Agent: Processes biologics product adverse experiences, product use patterns, health effects, consumer narratives, and product category information. D. Case Validation, Quality Control, and Human-in-the-Loop Review Think Trends Software shall incorporate validation agents to compare extracted data against business rules, required fields, confidence thresholds, terminology standards, and case-processing logic. Records that meet defined thresholds may proceed automatically, while exceptions shall be routed for human review. Key quality-control features include: • Confidence scoring at field, document, and case levels. • Source traceability to page, section, table, and line references. • Automated flagging of missing, inconsistent, conflicting, or low-confidence data. • Human-in-the-loop review screens for case processors and safety reviewers. • Reviewer acceptance, correction, override, and approval workflows. • Full audit trail of AI extraction, human edits, and final approved values. E. Data Standardization and Regulatory Output Generation Think Trends Software shall transform extracted adverse event information into structured formats required for case management, analytics, and downstream regulatory processing. The platform shall support configurable mappings to FDA data standards, Center-specific systems, XML structures, APIs, and reporting formats. Capabilities include: • Normalization of adverse event terms, product names, dates, identifiers, and narrative fields. • Mapping to Center-specific safety data models and controlled terminology. • Generation of structured case records for downstream review and processing. • API-based integration with FDA systems, case-processing platforms, data lakes, document repositories, and workflow tools. • Export to XML, JSON, CSV, database tables, or other required formats. F. Agentic Workflow Automation and Triage Think Trends Software shall automate repetitive case-processing steps while maintaining reviewer control for regulatory decisions. The system shall support configurable AI agents capable of executing multi-step workflows, requesting missing information, summarizing case narratives, identifying seriousness indicators, detecting duplicates, and prioritizing work queues. Workflow automation shall include: • Case prioritization based on seriousness, product risk, event severity, due dates, and Center-defined rules. • Automated summarization of long adverse event narratives and supporting attachments. • Duplicate and follow-up detection across submissions. • Exception handling and escalation workflows. • Generation of reviewer-ready case summaries. • Dashboard visibility into case volumes, processing status, aging, backlog, error rates, and productivity metrics. G. AI-Enabled Redaction for FOIA Compliance ThinkTrends will provide AI-powered redaction capabilities to support FDA's obligations under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA). The platform will automatically identify and redact personally identifiable information (PII), protected health information (PHI), commercially confidential data, law-enforcement-sensitive content, and other exemption-covered materials from adverse event documents prior to public release or response to FOIA requests. Key capabilities include: • Automated detection and redaction of PII and PHI, including patient names, addresses, dates of birth, medical record numbers, Social Security numbers, and other personal identifiers. • Identification and suppression of trade secrets, proprietary formulations, manufacturing processes, and commercially confidential submitter information protected under FOIA Exemption. • Detection of law-enforcement-sensitive and inter-agency deliberative content subject to FOIA Exemptions. • Configurable exemption profiles aligned to FDA FOIA policy, Center-specific guidance, and applicable federal regulations. • Confidence-scored redaction recommendations with source traceability, enabling FOIA reviewers to accept, modify, or override AI-proposed redactions. • Human-in-the-loop review workflow allowing FOIA analysts to validate, annotate, and finalize redacted documents before release. • Generation of redacted PDF and document versions with visible redaction markers, exemption codes, and reviewer audit annotations. • Full audit trail recording every AI-proposed redaction, reviewer decision, exemption code applied, and final release determination. • Support for bulk redaction processing across large FOIA request batches, including multi-document packages and rolling requests. • Integration with FDA FOIA tracking systems, document repositories, and case management workflows. 1.3 SALIENT FEATURES OF THINK TRENDS SOFTWARE Think Trends Software provides the following differentiating capabilities relevant to FDA adverse event reporting modernization: 1. Agentic OCR Beyond Traditional OCR: Think Trends Software does not merely convert images to text. It applies AI agents that read, interpret, validate, cross-check, and structure regulatory information from complex adverse event documents. 2. Center-Agnostic Core with Center-Specific Configuration: The platform provides a common document intelligence foundation while allowing FDA Centers such as CVM, CDRH, CTP, and HFP to configure unique workflows, data models, rules, and outputs. 3. End-to-End Adverse Event Case Automation: Think Trends Software supports intake, classification, extraction, validation, triage, routing, human review, data transformation, and downstream submission/output generation. 4. Human-in-the-Loop Regulatory Control: The system keeps FDA reviewers in control by allowing them to review, correct, approve, or override AI-generated outputs before final case acceptance. 5. Explainability and Source Traceability: Each extracted field can be traced back to the original source document, page, section, and text reference, supporting transparency, auditability, and reviewer confidence. 6. Confidence-Based Processing: Think Trends Software assigns confidence scores to extracted data and automatically routes low-confidence or inconsistent records for human review. 7. Multi-Document and Multi-Format Processing: Think Trends Software shall process scanned PDFs, structured forms, unstructured narratives, tables, handwritten content where feasible, images, attachments, correspondence, and supporting records. 8. Duplicate and Follow-Up Detection: AI agents shall compare incoming submissions against existing records to identify potential duplicates, follow-ups, related cases, and case-history updates. 9. Reviewer-Ready Case Summaries: Think Trends Software shall generate concise adverse event summaries, chronology, product-event relationships, missing-field lists, and review-ready case packages. 10. Secure FDA-Aligned Deployment: Think Trends Software shall be deployable in secure government cloud, FDA-managed, or approved hosting environments with role-based access, audit logs, encryption, and integration with enterprise identity management. 1.4 TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS Implementation of Think Trends Software for adverse event document processing is expected to deliver the following outcomes: • Reduction in manual data entry and repetitive case-processing tasks. • Faster adverse event intake, triage, and reviewer preparation. • Improved data quality through AI-assisted validation and standardization. • Greater consistency across FDA Centers while preserving Center-specific workflows. • Enhanced traceability, auditability, and regulatory transparency. • Improved ability to manage high-volume document backlogs and surge workloads. • Increased reviewer productivity through AI-generated summaries and exception-based review. • Scalable platform foundation for future FDA adverse event modernization initiatives. Please view the attached Request for Quote (RFQ) RFQ FDA-SOL-75F40126Q00384 document for additional information.

sig_09cf39cca538396dd30e.description: The NSF FINDERS FOUNDRY program supports collaboration among K-12 educators, technologists, and researchers to develop innovative solutions to persistent challenges in learning and workforce development. These challenges are identified by K-12 students, families, and educators. The program aims to create and scale evidence-based practices, tools, and technologies that improve learning outcomes and prepare students for a digital, Artificial Intelligence (AI)-driven future. A key focus is early exposure to AI to build curiosity, understanding, and readiness for future careers. The program encourages partnerships across sectors - schools, universities, industry, government, and nonprofits - to co-design responsive, technology-based solutions. NSF FINDERS FOUNDRY program includes two phases: Planning and Development. Planning proposals help teams explore one of several focus areas. Only teams awarded Planning grants may submit Development proposals, which support the growth and implementation of promising ideas. The program aligns with national priorities, including the Executive Order 14277, “Advancing Artificial Intelligence Education for American Youth ” (April 23, 2025), and the CHIPS and Science Act of 2022, Public Law 117-167 , Sections 10381-10383 and 10395.

sig_0a036bc1542d0c97b215.description: The overarching goal of this notice of funding opportunity (NOFO) and its companion opportunities is to establish the Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) Program to support development of innovative, reliable, cost-effective, and sustainable multimodal AI-based clinical decision support (CDS) tools. PRIMED-AI CDS tools are based on the integration of clinical imaging with other types of multimodal health data to enhance care for patients with a wide range of health conditions. The PRIMED-AI Program seeks to catalyze the adoption of AI-based CDS tools into clinical workflows to enable novel personalized medicine strategies that address significant health challenges. The purpose of this NOFO is to solicit applications for the design, development, and preliminary validation of robust frameworks for the application of multimodal-artificial intelligence (AI) models for clinical use. Frameworks developed through these awards would populate a "playbook", defined as a collection of actionable guidelines, standardized protocols, and/or standard operating procedures (SOPs) for reliable and effective development and deployment of multimodal AI tools. It is expected that the frameworks delineated in this playbook will directly address PRIMED-AI objectives and needs, while also remaining flexible enough to enable sufficient extensibility and interoperability for use across a broad spectrum of multimodal biomedical AI applications, both internal and external to the PRIMED-AI Program.
sig_0a036bc1542d0c97b215.title: Development and Testing of a Multi-use Frameworks Playbook for Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) (U01 Clinical Trial Not Allowed)

sig_0a04296a220e598f302b.description: The subject of this public procurement includes the selection of a contractor to provide technical and logistical support for the organisation and conduct of specialised and public events, the development of professional communities, the conduct of information and advertising campaigns, the management of social media profiles, media planning, the provision of advertising materials and consumables for events, the creation of an online community and other related activities with the aim of promoting project No 101250707 BRAIN++, implemented under the Horizon Europe Programme. Within the scope of the procurement, it is envisaged to organise and conduct two types of events, provisionally called Type A events and Type B events: – Large Type A events (conferences, forums, hackathons) – approximately 11 in number, with a minimum of 100 participants per event, whereby by 30.11.2026 the goal is to conduct events for 600 participants, and for the entire period until 30.11.2028 – for no fewer than 5 000 participants. Type A events are organised and conducted entirely by the Contractor, following prior coordination with the Contracting Authority, including communication, media coverage, advertising materials, catering, provision of speakers and moderators, preparation of a list of suitable guests, filming, provision of technical equipment, logistics and installation of equipment, provision of a stage, sound reinforcement and other similar activities. – Small Type B events (conferences, forums, competitions, webinars, networking, seminars, discussions, etc.) – a minimum of 42 in number, with between 20 and 100 participants per event and a minimum of 3 000 participants in total for the duration of the procurement. For Type B events, the Contractor is a provider of specific services required by the Contracting Authority for the organisation and conduct of the respective event, including communication, media coverage, advertising materials, catering, provision of speakers and moderators, preparation of a list of suitable guests, filming, provision of technical equipment, logistics and installation of equipment, provision of a stage, sound reinforcement and other similar activities. For the Contracting Authority, the number of participants is a priority over the number of events conducted, and the contract shall be considered fulfilled upon achieving a minimum of 8 000 participants in total across both types of events. The execution of the procurement specifically includes: planning, organisation and coordination of events, including communication with participants, speakers, moderators, partners and other stakeholders; registration and management of participants, including through an electronic registration platform; technical provision and logistics for events, including the provision of the necessary audio-visual, presentation, lighting and other technical equipment according to the specific event; provision of speakers and moderators, filming and other organisational and technical services necessary for the conduct of the events; media planning and coverage of events, including the preparation and dissemination of information and advertising content; management and maintenance of social media profiles and the conduct of advertising campaigns; production and provision of advertising and information materials and consumables for events; creation and maintenance of an online community in connection with the project activities; provision of catering, where applicable for the specific event; provision of other organisational, technical and logistical support according to the specific requests of the Contracting Authority and the requirements of the Technical Specification. The events will be held on the territory of the Republic of Bulgaria, with over 80% of them expected to be held in the city of Sofia. The service of renting premises/halls is not included in the subject of the public procurement. The provision of premises/halls is paid for by the Contracting Authority according to the final choice of venue for the respective event and the number of participants, and the Contractor may assist with proposals for suitable halls/premises.

sig_0a5c83b7d683c744e649.description: The procurement is being carried out as a procurement consortium involving the City of Helsinki and DigiHelsinki Oy (hereinafter the "Client"). A framework arrangement will be formed from the procurement, from which three suppliers will be selected in order of priority. The tendering process will be carried out using an open procedure. Each participant in the procurement consortium will make its own procurement decision and contract with the tenderers selected for the framework arrangement. The maximum value of the procurement is nine (9) million euros (VAT 0 %). Based on the framework arrangement, the Client and the Client's sectors, agencies, public utility services, and DigiHelsinki Oy may procure the Services or Continuous services referred to in the framework arrangement through separate delivery contracts. Delivery contracts may also relate to Applications implemented by the Client itself or in cooperation with other contractual partners. If several suppliers participate in the implementation, maintenance, or further development of the same Application, the division of responsibilities and the suppliers' cooperation obligations will be defined in the delivery contract. Deliveries may also include components implemented with other technologies in connection with Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Power Platform implementations, such as integration into an external database, interface, or software component, etc. The subject and scope of the procurement are set out in more detail in the call for tenders and its appendices.

sig_0af15c6dca7c7933c989.description: The services requested under this procurement procedure are the continuation of Software Assurance as well as the acquisition of licences incl. Software Assurance for software products from Microsoft and / or the acquisition of online products from Microsoft that Microsoft offers via the corporate programme, in accordance with the terms of the framework agreement (corporate agreement) of the Federal Ministry of the Interior (BMI) and Microsoft via a corresponding commercial partner. The services requested in the context of this procurement procedure are described in the specification of services (Section 6 of the procurement documents) including the appendices listed therein. The technical, legal and organisational framework conditions are contained in Section 5. Westdeutscher Rundfunk Köln (WDR) is advertising a framework agreement on behalf of the following broadcasting corporations and institutions of the broadcasting corporations: ARD-Hauptstadtstudio (ARD-HSB, represented by rbb), ARD ZDF Deutschlandradio Beitragsservice (ZBS), Bayerischer Rundfunk (BR), Deutschlandradio (DLR), Deutsche Welle (DW), Hessischer Rundfunk (HR), Informationsverarbeitungszentrum (IVZ, represented by rbb), Mitteldeutscher Rundfunk (MDR), Norddeutscher Rundfunk (NDR), Radio Bremen (RB), Rundfunk Berlin-Brandenburg (rbb), Saarländischer Rundfunk (SR), Südwestrundfunk (SWR), Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR) and Zweites Deutsches Fernsehen (ZDF). Also eligible are all other companies affiliated with the aforementioned broadcasting corporations and institutions, provided that these are "Authorised Institutions" within the meaning of the opening clause of the BMI contract. Affiliated and authorised companies associated with the aforementioned broadcasting corporations and institutions that do not meet the minimum order quantity of 250 qualified devices or users intend, if required, to join together with the affiliated broadcasting corporations and institutions in accordance with the BMI contract, Appendix 1 Section 3, a., (iii) to form a joint accession in order to reach the minimum order quantity. The framework agreement shall enter into force upon the award of contract and shall end upon expiry of the BMI corporate agreement, which entered into force on 01.06.2025, on 31.05.2028 or, taking into account its extension option, on 31.05.2029. During the term of the framework agreement, eligible entities may make accessions to the BMI corporate agreement. In doing so, each eligible entity may, if required and where applicable, also make accessions on the basis of various enrolments (e.g. EA Enterprise, EA SCE, EA Subscription enrolment). The effective date of each accession shall mark the commencement of a separate framework agreement (see template agreement in the appendix) between the respective eligible entity as the client and the commercial partner as the contractor. These individual framework agreements have independent terms, which are presented below, and shall therefore also apply to the respective contracting parties beyond the aforementioned end of the term of the framework agreement where applicable. Each eligible entity that makes an accession / concludes a framework agreement acts under its own responsibility, places orders and pays at its own expense. Joint and several liability between the various eligible entities is excluded. Insofar as individual clients guarantee minimum purchase quantities, these result from the appendix Minimum Purchase Quantities.xlsx of these procurement documents. Purchase quantities going beyond this are not guaranteed. The respective framework agreement shall end after 36 months without the need for termination. The framework agreement partner grants the clients the right to extend the respective framework agreement once by one year under the same conditions. The respective client must declare the exercise of the option in writing to the framework agreement partner before the expiry of the contract. The subsequent further extension option shall serve in particular the purpose of ensuring the possibility of an interruption-free commissioning of Software Assurance as well as operation for the respective client if a procurement procedure for such commissioning cannot be carried out / completed in good time. The framework agreement partner therefore grants the clients the right in each case to extend the respective framework agreement once again by up to 6 further months. The conditions may change for this extension period. An adjustment of the dealer's mark-up or markdown on its purchase prices may be made by mutual agreement in this case. The dealer must explain the circumstances altering the calculation. Insofar as further adjustments to the framework agreement have to be made due to Microsoft licence programme changes, these shall likewise be coordinated by mutual agreement. If and to the extent that valid successor agreements already exist between the Federal Ministry of the Interior and Microsoft at the time the extension option for the further 6 months is exercised - where applicable also on the basis of a different Microsoft licence programme -, these may be selected as the basis. The framework agreement partner further agrees that during this extension term, any client may terminate the framework agreement at any time and without observing a notice period and carry out a change of commercial partner. The currently existing EA accessions expire for all eligible entities on 31.05.2026. It is intended to make accessions to the new BMI corporate agreement on the following dates: 01.06.2026 The clients will announce the products and quantities for their respective initial orders in good time. The contractor will then promptly provide the respective client with the prices valid for the initial order, taking into account the Microsoft price and the discount for the EA commercial partners in accordance with the BMI corporate agreement as well as the mark-up or markdown to be offered.

The subject of the tender is the renewal and modernisation of the automation, visualisation and network technology in two water treatment works and one elevated reservoir. The aim of the measure is to upgrade the systems to the state of the art, taking into account the requirements for cybersecurity, network segmentation, availability and operational reliability in the environment of NIS-2 requirements. The scope of services includes the planning, supply, installation, parametrisation, programming, migration, commissioning and documentation of the automation technology, including the replacement of existing PLC systems, decentralised automation components and the required communication and telecontrol interfaces. The replacement of the automation technology will take place on the basis of the Siemens system platform using current SIMATIC S7-1500 controllers, including engineering in the TIA Portal. The central process visualisation is to be supplied, configured and put into operation ready for use on the basis of Siemens WinCC Unified. The visualisation is to be integrated with the automation systems to be newly constructed and the existing technical equipment. Furthermore, the service includes the renewal and expansion of the industrial network infrastructure, including active network components, network segmentation, secure communication connections, remote access solutions and the components required to implement a modern IT/OT security concept. The service also includes the migration of existing functions and process data, the execution of factory, function and data point tests, commissioning during ongoing plant operation, training of operating personnel and the handover of complete as-built and inventory documentation. The specification of the Siemens system platform is intended to ensure a uniform system architecture within the client's facilities, guarantee compatibility with existing standards, secure the ability of operating personnel to perform their own maintenance, and avoid additional training, licensing and interface expenses. The targeted system continuity serves in particular to ensure long-term operational and investment security as well as the implementation of a consistent cybersecurity concept. Special requirements arise from the maintenance of the water supply during the conversion measures. The contractor must plan and execute the work in such a way that necessary operational interruptions are limited to the technically necessary minimum. Comparable references from water treatment works, wastewater facilities or other critical infrastructure facilities are required.
sig_0b0d93c7d1fd46b33203.title: NIS-2-compliant transformation of OT systems cooling supply area

sig_0b3b2603ff6a58a15a82.description: The ESG data management system serves as a centrally controlled, specialised Software-as-a-Service platform (SaaS platform) for the integrative procurement, processing, quality assurance and provision of external ESG data for the KfW Group. The external ESG data delivery route (hereinafter also referred to as "XEDALI") replaces the previous decentralised and heterogeneous procurement and connection of external ESG data sources through a standardised ETL process (Extract – Transform – Load). The application will regularly query ESG data at the software interfaces to various external data providers, transfer it into a uniform data model and provide it for use in subsequent processes. It thus provides users with a consistent data source for external ESG data. sig_0ba0f15daf63d69f0175.description: Die Landesmesse Stuttgart GmbH & Co. KG (LMS) is advertising services of an external Information Security Officer (ISO). The LMS intends to commission services of an external Information Security Officer (ISO) in order to improve the level of security comprehensively and sustainably. The implementation of an internationally recognised standard for information security management systems is envisaged. The security level of the LMS is intended to be aligned with ISO 27001. Certification is not currently planned, but could become relevant from a perspective standpoint (e.g. due to customer requirements). The external Information Security Officer shall be assigned the following tasks in particular: - Development and implementation of security strategies: Creation of security concepts, policies and guidelines tailored to the specific needs of the LMS. This includes the further development of the Information Security Management System (ISMS). - Risk management: Implementation and continuous updating of risk analyses and business impact analyses (BIA) to identify and assess potential threats. - Reporting: Establishment of reporting processes as well as regular evaluation and presentation of security-related information to the specialist departments and management. - Continuous monitoring: Monitoring the effectiveness of the implemented security measures and, as required, adjustment of the implemented measures. - Compliance with statutory requirements: Ensuring that the LMS complies with all relevant laws, regulations and industry standards in the field of information security. - Security incidents: Investigation, processing and risk assessment of security incidents incl. taking measures for damage limitation - Collaboration: Close cooperation with the internal "Information Security Manager" as well as the other specialist departments (especially IT) as well as the Security Operations Center (SOC), the Data Protection Officer and management - Internal and external audits: Support in preparation for internal and external audits on information security - Technical security measures: Involvement in the conception, evaluation and decision on the introduction or modernisation of technologies (e.g. new EDR solution, network segmentation), which is why corresponding IT and IT security architecture know-how should be available with the contractor. The contractor does not have to be responsible for the decisions, but must be able to advise accordingly in the sense of an advisory function in accordance with their role. The subject matter of the procedure is now the Europe-wide procurement of services of an external Information Security Officer (ISO) by means of a negotiated procedure with a preceding call for competition. Further information on the content of the tender will be made available to the bidders who are invited to submit tenders. The services are to be awarded for a period of 24 months (2 years), provisionally commencing on 1 April 2026.
sig_0ba0f15daf63d69f0175.title: Landesmesse Stuttgart GmbH & Co. KG - Europe-wide procurement of services of an external Information Security Officer (ISO)

sig_0c33f8ce5717cafc61b0.description: THIS IS NOT A CONTRACT NOTICE OR A CALL FOR TENDERS BUT AN INFORMATION REQUEST FOR MARKET RESEARCH AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE. This information request is used to survey the market and obtain information regarding the procurement. The contracting authority is not initiating a procurement procedure with the publication of the information request; rather, a potential contract notice and call for tenders will be published later. The information request does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Answering the information request is not a prerequisite for participating in any later procurement procedure that may be organised. Suppliers will not be paid compensation for answering the information request or participating in the market dialogue. The responses provided to this information request will be used in planning the procurement of a medical device processing RFID system and related supplies for the needs of HUS-yhtymä. The system and supplies to be procured must be suitable for use in hospital sterile services environments. The purpose of the information request is to survey suppliers on the market as well as their product and service ranges. The purpose is to ascertain technical solutions, pricing principles and the cost level for budgeting purposes. HUS-yhtymä requests your written comments in particular on the following questions: 1. Durability and lifecycle of tags in a hospital environment 1.1. How do the RFID tags you offer withstand medical device processing sterilisation and washing processes? State the maximum temperature resistance of the tags (e.g. autoclave +134 °C), pressure resistance, and chemical tolerance (such as alkaline detergents). 1.2. What is the estimated lifecycle of the tags you offer (measured as operational reliability in washing and sterilisation cycles)? Do you offer a warranty for the durability of the tags in a sterile services environment? 2. Compatibility with existing automation and standards 2.1. Another unit of ours already uses RFID-controlled automation. What frequency bands and standards (e.g. UHF / RAIN RFID, HF, ISO 18000-63) does your system support to ensure seamless compatibility with existing equipment? 2.2. Does your system and readers support general global identification and data standards (such as GS1/EPC)? 2.3. Is your system "vendor-independent" (open standard) with regard to tags? Can we in future freely purchase tags that meet the requirements from third parties, or does the system require your own identifiers? 3. Reliability in a metal environment (On-Metal) 3.1. Medical device processing handles almost exclusively metal (baskets, containers, instruments). How are your system's reader devices and so-called on-metal tags optimised to operate in this environment without dead zones or signal reflection interference? 3.2. How reliably does your system perform bulk reading (e.g. a situation where an entire trolley of overlapping steel baskets is pushed through the reading area at once)? What is the tested margin of error in this scenario? 4. Software integrations and interfaces 4.1. What ready-made integrations or interface solutions (API) does your system have? HUS Sterile Services uses the Gemini production control system supplied by CGI. 4.2. How is data transferred from RFID reading to the main system: does the data transfer take place in real time and does it require the maintenance of a separate middleware? 5. Cost structure and implementation 5.1. What is the preliminary cost structure of your solution (one-off equipment and installation costs vs. recurring licence, maintenance and tag costs)? 5.2. According to the plan, the system is being procured for two sterile services centres (Jorvi and Meilahti). What is your preliminary estimate of the duration of the implementation project in units of this type? On what kind of schedule after signing the agreement would you be capable of starting/executing the implementation project? 6. Other 6.1 Would you like to raise any other aspects related to the subject of the procurement or the solution you offer? HUS-yhtymä requests suppliers interested in the procurement described above to notify the contracting authority of their interest and answer the questions presented above, and to attach to the response a general description/brochure of the solutions you offer for the need described above. Please note that all material is intended solely for conducting this market dialogue. The contracting authority will treat your responses confidentially. Based on the responses to the information request, clarifying questions may be posed to the supplier and/or an opportunity may be offered to present their solutions in a manner to be announced later. Suppliers that have responded to the information request may potentially receive preliminary call for tender documents for comment. We kindly ask you to submit your responses to the information request and notify your interest no later than 23.9.2026 at 12:00 to the address kilpailutus.ict@hus.fi. The subject line of the message must mention "HUS 578-2025 - Medical Device Processing RFID System".
sig_0c33f8ce5717cafc61b0.title: Information request: Medical Device Processing RFID System

SUBJECT: Kela is preparing the procurement of an organisation-wide AI governance tool (AI Governance Tool), which provides a centralised solution for the registration, risk classification, lifecycle management, documentation of AI systems, and verification of compliance in accordance with the EU Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act). The subject of the procurement is an off-the-shelf software delivered as a cloud service, which brings together processes, workflows, monitoring and reporting, enabling transparent, auditable and efficient AI governance across Kela's operations. The solution supports the initial setup of the 20–50 system and will scale according to growing needs, providing comprehensive maintenance, information security and support services as well as role-based access control. The presentation material is expected to describe concisely the key features of the solution, the technical architecture, the implementation of AI Act requirements, and any experience of similar implementations. sig_0e3fc2ae6dd2f31dce3e.description: The aim of this procedure is to procure modern and autonomous mobile systems intended for monitoring fruit and vegetable crops. The Contracting Authority expects the delivery of three systems in identical hardware and functional configuration, enabling their parallel use in different locations or by different user teams. The subject of the contract is a complete, integrated system combining the functions of a mobile robotic platform, measurement, data acquisition and processing systems, and analytical software supporting plant condition assessment. The aim of the contract is to create a tool enabling repeatable, automated and spatially located measurements in actual agricultural and horticultural production conditions, in a more accurate and efficient manner than classical manual observations. The system is to support ongoing crop monitoring and provide data for the further development of analytical algorithms, including solutions based on artificial intelligence methods. The ordered robots are to act as mobile measurement platforms, capable of working in various agrotechnical conditions. The robots must be adapted to work in actual agricultural conditions, including variable ground, terrain unevenness, moisture, dust, mud, vegetation and farm infrastructure elements. Each system should also be adapted for transport between locations and include appropriate transport equipment enabling safe loading and unloading without the use of specialist lifting devices.

sig_0eae879ae512de7f35df.description: Tenderers are hereby invited to a market dialogue for the procurement of 2026/68199 for the procurement of an ID card for access and login to the health companies in Helse Vest. The market dialogue is a part of the preliminary work for the procurement and is being carried out as the Contracting Authority would like input for the procurement from possible suppliers and other interested parties. It will be central to identify, among other things, how the supplier market can cover the need and relevant environmental considerations. At the same time, the contracting authority would like to make the market aware that Helse Vest is looking into future possibilities for acquiring a regional access administration system that shall collect identity and access management in a common platform. This is seen to have close connections with cards that shall be procured and it will be important to clarify the dependencies and important requirements against this so that it works together. We would like, in this market dialogue, to respond in writing to concrete questions in order to map the supplier market, environmental impact and relevant areas for the requirement specifications. It is also of interest to gain insight into important links and possibilities toward a future regional access management system. In order to limit the use of resources in the further dialogue after written responses, the Contracting Authority reserves the right to limit the number of participants who will be invited to one-to-one meetings.

sig_0ecf3f0ae5930329bd86.description: UCLH wishes to procure a transformation partner to improve efficiency and productivity of the radiotherapy department, challenging current ways of working and offering new insights. Lot 1: . University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, "UCLH", is one of the largest NHS trusts in the United Kingdom and provides first-class acute and specialist services. UCLH comprises of the following hospitals: University College Hospital, Elizabeth Garrett Anderson Wing, MacMillan Cancer Centre, University College Hospital Grafton Way Building, University College Hospital at Westmoreland Street, Royal National ENT and Eastman Dental Hospitals, National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery, Hospital for Tropical Diseases, Royal London Hospital for Integrated Medicine, and the Institute of Sport, Exercise and Health. UCLH delivers world class cancer care to patients from across the country. Cancer at UCLH spans across multiple sites and departments within the Trust and has included the opening of the Grafton Way Building one of two national Proton Beam Therapy services in December 2021. UCLH is a lead provider within the North Central London Cancer Alliance, as well as providing tertiary services for wider patient populations in specialist services, such as sarcoma for patients from across South East England. In early 2020, UCLH was selected by NHS England as the preferred tertiary cancer provider to take over management of the Mount Vernon Cancer Centre. This transition is subject to a due diligence process during which UCLH are providing transitional support to the Mount Vernon Cancer Centre team, building upon a number of years of collaborative working between the two services. Our Radiotherapy department offers cutting edge and specialised therapy to adult and paediatric patients treating over 2400 new patients a year. UCLH Radiotherapy is a national leader in complex/highly technical radiotherapy in: • Brain and was recently designated a Tessa Jowell Brain Cancer Centre of Excellence • Paediatrics, with the largest paediatric radiotherapy unit in the UK • Sarcomas - one of Europe’s largest service • Head and Neck – (ENT) third largest in the UK • Stereotactic Ablative Radiotherapy (SABR) • Haematological including total body radiation • Brachytherapy • Molecular Radiotherapy - National Referral centre (Paediatric, TYA and adult). The department works closely with a number of specialist hospitals to support cancer pathways which span multiple centres including Great Ormond Street, St. Mary's, Oxford, Southampton and the Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital. The UCH radiotherapy department contains six bunkers with four Varian TrueBeams and one Varian Halcyon. There is a large difference between the national and UCLH complexity profile, 92% of the UCH workload is classed as complex and approximately 8% of the workload is paediatric. The radiotherapy service is delivered by a team of staff including clinical oncologists, radiotherapy physics and engineers, therapeutic radiographers, healthcare play specialists, admin and clerical staff and dedicated nurses. UCLH is also one of two national Proton Beam Therapy centres, providing services to patients from the south of the UK. The departments run an integrated workforce model, with physicists, dosimetrists and radiographers rotating across Radiotherapy and PBT. In total there are around 300 WT across both services. UCLH wishes to procure a transformation partner to improve efficiency and productivity of the radiotherapy department, challenging current ways of working and offering new insights. This could include but is not limited to: • Delivering Cancer Waiting Time Access standards. • Scheduling of patients. • Machine downtime. • Patient pathway and organisation of workflow. • Radiotherapy physics pathways. • Process for commissioning of new linacs. • Use of automation and AI. Expression of Interest The purpose of this preliminary market engagement is to engage with potential partners to gather information and insights from the market to aid the development of the requirements and scope of opportunities for efficiencies to inform the procurement of a transformation partner. Suppliers are requested to provide expressions of interest, including responses to the below questions by e-mail to steviejay.cavanagh@nhs.net by 15:00 on 26th September 2025. 1. What innovative or new ways of working are you currently seeing in the market that may benefit the NHS, and more specifically UCLH, including those that have been included in procurements over the past 12 months? 2. Please describe how you think this contract should be best structured to deliver an efficient Radiotherapy service? 3. Is there anything you think that the Trust should consider before going out to market for these services? 4. What would be your expectations from a partnership with an NHS organisation? This notice does not constitute a formal call for competition. sig_0ee3c5cbeb5360d3ded0.description: The project "Supporting a Just Transition in Mexico" aims to strengthen the capacities of key public, private and civil society actors to design and implement socially just decarbonization processes in strategic sectors of the Mexican economy, with a particular focus in key industrial (incl. industrial parks) and the energy sector. The project is commissioned by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and implemented by GIZ, with the Mexican Ministry of Economy (SE) as technical partner. It contributes to the BMZ core theme "Climate and energy", to Mexico's implementation of the Paris Agreement and Agenda 2030 SDGs 13, 9, 7, 5, 16 and 17. Mexico's export-oriented industrial model, the rapid expansion of industrial parks and rising energy demand create pressure and opportunities for low-carbon transformation. Building on the updated climate targets set out in Mexico's Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC), the country faces the challenge of turning these commitments into coherent implementation. Regulatory gaps, insufficient technical and financial capacities, and social and gender inequalities still limit progress towards a decarbonised economy. The project responds to these challenges by promoting an integrated approach that combines climate protection, industrial competitiveness and social justice. The overall objective is to strengthen the capacities of key actors to implement just transition processes in strategic sectors of the Mexican economy. To achieve this, the project supports the development of participatory governance frameworks for a just transition. Multistakeholder dialogue formats will foster coordination between federal and subnational authorities, the private sector, financial institutions, workers' representatives and civil society organisations. At the meso and micro levels, the project aims to improve the enabling conditions for the adoption of green technologies by companies and industrial parks in selected sectors. This includes technical and economic feasibility studies, advisory services on energy-efficient and renewable energy solutions, and targeted capacity development for park operators, firms and service providers, with special attention to SMEs and the qualification of women and groups in vulnerable situations for future-oriented jobs. In addition, the project works with public development banks and other financial institutions to align their product portfolios with the needs of companies and park operators investing in green technologies and sustainable infrastructure. Together with these actors, it promotes demand-oriented "just transition finance" instruments that are consistent with Mexico's emerging sustainable finance taxonomy and that can be deployed in and around industrial parks, among other industry sectors. The project also supports the design and implementation of social and gender justice strategies in at least one subnational context. Together with public institutions, private sector actors and social partners, it will pilot mechanisms to identify and mitigate negative social impacts of industrial transformation, and to ensure that women and other groups in vulnerable situations benefit from new economic opportunities. Lessons learned will be documented and shared with key institutions across the country to enable replication in additional industrial parks and regions. By 2028, the project expects that several just transition-oriented policy and regulatory instruments have been adopted; that industrial parks and companies in prioritised sectors have taken investment decisions leading to measurable GHG emission reductions; that financial institutions provide suitable financing instruments for such investments; and that institutions in other regions make use of the experience gained with social and gender justice approaches in the Mexican just transition. The project is implemented from October 2024 to September 2028. Lot LOT-0001: 10040388-Consulting Services for Fostering a Just Transition in the Mexican Industrial Sector. Under the framework of the bilateral technical cooperation project "Supporting a Just Transition in Mexico", GIZ intends to award a contract for consulting services to foster a just transition in the Mexican industrial sector. The assignment will provide technical advisory services to support the design and implementation of socially just decarbonisation processes in key industrial sectors, with a particular focus on industrial parks and their interaction with the energy sector. The contract is tendered through an international competitive procedure in line with GIZ rules and applicable EU public procurement regulations. In close coordination with GIZ, the contractor will support Mexican partner institutions and other stakeholders in translating just transition principles into concrete action in emissions-intensive industries. This includes promoting industrial decarbonisation, enabling the deployment of clean energy and circular economy solutions, and integrating social and gender considerations in industrial transformation processes. The assignment contributes directly to the achievement of the project's outcome and to four key result areas: strengthening governance frameworks for a just transition; improving enabling conditions for green technologies in industry and energy; advancing "just transition finance"; and piloting social and gender justice strategies at subnational level. A first core area of work is the provision of on-demand technical advice and specialised analysis on just transition in the industrial sector, including industrial parks. The contractor will support partners in assessing and designing regulatory and policy approaches to improve the business environment for low-carbon investments, and identifying opportunities where industrial decarbonisation can be aligned with energy transition planning, industrial policy, circular economy models and the use of green materials. All support is expected to systematically address social and gender dimensions, in line with the project's just transition approach. A second core area involves in-depth analytical work on mitigation potential and decarbonisation pathways for selected industrial parks and industrial clusters. This may include the development of emissions baselines and marginal abatement cost curves, scenario modelling for different technology and investment options, and the analysis of economic, social and environmental co-benefits under a just transition perspective. The contractor will work closely with GIZ and national partners to define the scope of these analyses and to translate findings into practical recommendations for policymakers, industrial park operators, companies and financial institutions. A third area of work is strategic communication and knowledge management. The contractor will support the development of narratives around just transition in the Mexican industrial sector and will produce communication and knowledge products such as policy briefs, reports, infographics, editorial and audiovisual materials. The services may also include conceptual and organisational support to events, dialogue formats and peer-learning activities, to disseminate lessons learned and good practices from pilot interventions in industrial parks and other industrial contexts. A fourth area focuses on capacity development. The contractor will design and implement training formats, workshops and other learning tools for key actors at national and subnational levels, including public institutions, industrial park operators, companies, financial institutions, academia and civil society. These activities aim to strengthen technical competencies and practical know-how on just transition, industrial decarbonisation, green and climate finance, circular economy and energy transition, with particular attention to the inclusion of women and groups in vulnerable situations. The contract is expected to run from February 2027 to August 2028. Primary target groups include key actors from the energy, industrial sectors and industrial park operators, as well as state-level economic and environmental authorities and relevant federal institutions. Secondary target groups comprise affected communities, labour representatives, civil society organisations and academic institutions. The assignment builds on and complements cooperation with national and international partners, including UNIDO, Mexican state-level associations such as AMSDE and ANAAE, and the Mexican Association of Private Industrial Parks (AMPIP). To deliver these services, the contractor is expected to provide a multidisciplinary expert team. This includes a team leader with strong experience in industrial decarbonisation and just transition, as well as experts in energy, industrial technologies and eco-industrial park developments, green and climate finance, social and gender impact analysis, strategic communication and capacity development. A pool of additional short-term specialists with national and international experience should be available to cover specific thematic and methodological needs. Bidders are expected to demonstrate substantial experience in climate change mitigation, industrial and energy transitions, and collaboration with public and private stakeholders, and previous work with international cooperation, preferably in Mexico or Latin America. The services will be delivered through a combination of on-demand support and the implementation of result-oriented activities and milestones agreed with GIZ. The assignment includes robust project and knowledge management, results-based monitoring and regular reporting, and must comply with GIZ requirements on data protection, information security, gender equality and environmental and climate safeguards.
sig_0ee3c5cbeb5360d3ded0.title: 10040388-Consulting Services for Fostering a Just Transition in the Mexican Industrial Sector

sig_0f15f690a6a1f19f021a.description: NHS Wales Shared Services Partnership (NWSSP), hosted by Velindre University NHS Trust, are issuing this Market Engagement Notice to engage with the suppliers to gather feedback on market capabilities and capacity for the provision of managed services to support the operation of a finance, procurement and warehouse management system. The Central Team eBusiness Services (CTeS), within NWSSP, manage and supervise several core national enterprise systems which are used by Health Boards, Trusts, Special Heath Authorities, and Hosted Organisations, in Wales. These systems are collectively known as the FMS Enterprise System and include: - An e-Business Application System, including auxiliary services, which is facilitated through the Oracle eBusiness suite. - A Business Intelligence (BI) reporting system, facilitated through Qlik Sense. - An OCR Intelligent Scanning Management System - A Warehouse Management System - Other BI Reporting Systems The purpose of this market engagement exercise is to gather greater insight into the market’s capacity and capabilities in relation to provision of managed services and NWSSP are specifically seeking engagement from suppliers who are e-Business Suite experts with supply chain capabilities specifically covering warehouse management and who can also support to roll out and further development of discrete manufacturing processes within a regulated environment. The analysis of feedback obtained from this exercise will allow NWSSP to further develop its strategy and refine its service delivery requirements ahead of any potential procurement. The main objectives of this exercise are to: - Assess the level of interest in the marketplace from suppliers who can support the Oracle eBusiness Suite (EBS), - Test market capability and capacity, - Validate the proposed scope and service model, - Understand delivery approaches, innovations and commercial models and indicative rates, and - Explore development and innovation in relation to AI and the benefits that may be realised with its deployment through the Oracle eBusiness Suite. The provision of the Oracle EBS is facilitated through existing perpetual licences, and the scope of this engagement exercise does not include migrating the e-Business Application System to a Software as a Service (SaaS) model. This exercise is not a formal procurement process, does not constitute a call for competition and does not commit NHS Wales to any future procurement. However, information gathered through this engagement will help inform the development, scope and future direction of the project. Suppliers can express their interest in this process and request a copy of the Market Engagement Briefing Document, which contains further details on the requirement and engagement process, by contacting Chris Squires (christopher.squires@wales.nhs.uk). When submitting an expression of interest, suppliers are requested to confirm that they acknowledge and understand that: - the proposed managed service requirement relates specifically to Oracle E-Business Suite (Oracle EBS) and does not include support for Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solutions; - they have the necessary supply chain capabilities to support the requirements of the service; and - they possess the capability and expertise to support the development of warehouse management systems within discrete manufacturing environments. Suppliers will have the opportunity to participate in a structured engagement session which are scheduled for the 5th, 8th and 14th October. There are 10 sessions available and these will be allocated on a first come first served basis. However, NWSSP reserves the right, at its sole discretion, to make additional sessions available should there be sufficient interest from the market. No guarantee is given that additional sessions will be offered. Lot 1: . None

sig_0f4c5d5d65aa6b4c1926.description: This competition replaces the previously announced competition 2026/2237, which was cancelled 14.08.2026. The system shall contribute to strengthening situational comprehension in Norwegian sea areas by using image forming sensors (optical and SAR – Synthetic Aperture Radar). This shall enable: verification of AIS data detection of vessels that do not send AIS (so-called "dark vessels") improved situation understanding and decision support in the operative contexts The coastal system has tested the use of non-cooperative sensor data from satellites in the summer and autumn 2025 through the company Vake AS's presentation and analysis system (vake.ai.). The testing of data in Vake is based on optical and SAR sensor data from Sentinel-1 and 2 satellites in the EU's Copernicus programme and on AIS data from the Norwegian Coastal Administration. Developments in this procurement cannot be included. Tenderers shall document that the offered system was established and operative at the tender deadline. The documentation shall, at a minimum, consist of: A technical description of the offered system, including main functionality, used data sources and central analysing functions. Screen images showing central functions in the system, including visualisation of satellite data, object detection and analysis functionality. Information on the date of production of the system to the customer. Description of the system's operative use for at least one customer or final user. Documentation that substantiates actual operative operations before the tender deadline expiry, e.g. customer confirmation, operational reports, uptime reports, user statistics or equivalent. The contract will be valid for one (1) year, with an option for an extension.
sig_0f4c5d5d65aa6b4c1926.title: The qualification phase - Procurement of satellite based and optical SAR (new competition).

sig_0f53a03dbad4c54b0407.description: The purpose of this contract is the SERVICES FOR THE ANALYSIS, DESIGN, DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A VIRTUAL AGENT COORDINATION SYSTEM (CoVA) APPLIED TO INTERGENERATIONAL ASSISTANCE FOR THE ADMINISTRATION OF THE PRINCIPALITY OF ASTURIAS which enables a proactive and efficient administration, covering both processes and people and the technology necessary for its proper use, security and management. This contract is part of Public Procurement of Innovative Technology (CPTI), its purpose has an innovative content and employs functional specifications, rather than technical requirements: It is aimed at the acquisition of a service that does not exist in the Principality of Asturias, but can be developed in a reasonable time, given that the technology is at a degree of development that allows it to do so. The main tasks included in this contract are the following: a. Implementation of a virtual agent coordination system based on artificial intelligence applied to intergenerational assistance for the Administration of the Principality of Asturias that allows the exploitation of the data generated and managed. b. All services necessary for the commissioning of the contracted elements, necessary subscriptions/licences, as well as their management and maintenance during the pilot demonstration phase. c. The exploitation of the potential of the data of the Administration of the Principality of Asturias (hereinafter, APA) to implement new forms of public management based on interoperability and data analytics. d. Establish the technological and procedural bases for the implementation of a proactive administration that allows the optimisation of public expenditure while maximising its performance. e. The development of techniques/rules for the automated management and classification of data, documents and files using advanced Artificial Intelligence techniques. f. The incorporation of deep learning techniques since these digitalisation processes can produce immense amounts of data for training and thus be able to provide processing that increases efficiency, effectiveness and intelligence in the processing of data in the processes of Public Administrations. g. The creation of a corporate data space that includes origin data, those that may have been inferred during the scope of use of the system, as well as facilitating interoperability and administrative processing circuits. h. Creation of a proactive care and assistance environment with citizens. i. Creation of a specialised sandbox that serves as an ideation and experimentation environment. j. sig_0f683c0f3f7996dd9f88.description: The Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development (NICHD) intends to publish a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) to solicit applications for research on the impact of technology and digital media on children and adolescents. Technology and digital media (TDM) encompasses social media, applications, websites, television, motion pictures, artificial intelligence, mobile devices, computers, video games, virtual and augmented reality, and other content, networks, or platforms disseminated through the internet, broadcasted, or other media technologies, as applicable. Collectively, they have become an integral part of our children’s and families’ daily lives. Most children and adolescents now engage with TDM starting from an early age, often with high levels of exposure across multiple devices and contexts and involving a wide range of content. There is therefore an urgent need to understand how TDM use and exposure impacts children’s health and development, as well as how it alters the very nature of interactions between children and their family members, peers, and society at large. As TDM has evolved with breathtaking speed, our understanding of its impacts – whether positive, neutral, or negative – on children’s health and development has not kept pace. This initiative intends to address this expanding gap by inviting research proposals on the impact of TDM on children and adolescents, including potential broader effects on their families and communities. Please note that applications are not being solicited at this time . This notice is being provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations and responsive projects. This NOFO will utilize a phased R61/R33 mechanism. Investigators with interests at the intersection of TDM and child/adolescent development are encouraged to apply. In addition, collaborative teams that combine expertise across domains such as behavioral sciences, cognition and learning, computational and statistical modeling, computer science, geographic information science, library and information sciences, neurodevelopment, pediatrics, social and affective development and social sciences will be encouraged, and these investigators should also consider applying for this opportunity.
sig_0f683c0f3f7996dd9f88.title: Notice of Intent to Publish a Funding Opportunity Announcement for Impact of Technology and Digital Media Exposure Usage on Child and Adolescent Development

sig_10a5fd60bbf1d7997fd5.description: Die Bäder, Sport und Freizeit Salzgitter GmbH (BSF) originated from Thermalsolbad Salzgitter GmbH and Sport und Freizeit Salzgitter GmbH. BSF is a subsidiary of the City of Salzgitter and performs numerous tasks, particularly in the field of public services of general economic interest. It operates the thermal brine baths in Salzgitter-Bad with their extensive offerings, the municipal pool in Salzgitter-Lebenstedt with attractive family offerings, and the ice sports centre at Salzgittersee with various leisure offerings. In addition, BSF is the point of contact for organised sport in Salzgitter provided by the district sports association (Kreissportbund) and its numerous sports clubs, as well as the primary contact address for all queries relating to Lake Salzgitter. The contracting authority is planning the introduction of a uniform, cloud-based point of sale and administration system for its three facilities - the Thermalsolbad Salzgitter-Bad, the Stadtbad Salzgitter-Lebenstedt, and the Eissporthalle am Salzgittersee. The aim is to optimise internal working processes and create a seamless, consistent customer experience across all premises. Currently existing, disparate software systems lead to significant organisational and technical challenges. Customers cannot use products (e.g. value cards or vouchers) across different premises, and support provided by various service providers complicates administration. A uniform system with central support by a single supplier is intended to solve these challenges, standardise technical operations, and improve customer service. A solution involving multiple different systems and subsequent connection to a common back-end system is not considered expedient from a technical and economic perspective. The subject matter of the contract comprises the following partial services: a. Upgrading the access hardware and providing the point of sale hardware for the Eissporthalle Salzgittersee b. Optional: Upgrading the access hardware and providing the point of sale hardware for the Stadtbad - Salzgitter-Lebenstedt c. Optional: Delivery of new access hardware and point of sale hardware for the Thermalsolbad Salzgitter-Bad d. Provision and operation of the SaaS-based back-end solution. The introduction is to take place in phases: - Eissporthalle Salzgittersee: after the season 2025/2026 from the 2. quarter 2026. Completion by no later than 15.09.2026 (season opening of the ice sports centre is on the last weekend of September). - Stadtbad Salzgitter-Lebenstedt: expected in the 4. quarter 2026 - Thermalsolbad Salzgitter-Bad: expected from the 1. quarter 2027.
sig_10a5fd60bbf1d7997fd5.title: Cloud-based point-of-sale and management system for the Salzgittersee ice rink, the Salzgitter-Lebenstedt municipal pool, and the Salzgitter-Bad thermal brine bath

sig_114957fe11a47c6380ea.description: Nordhessischer VerkehrsVerbund (NVV) has been 1995 the pace-setter for mobility in the North Hesse region. As a management level, we combine planning, financing and quality management for buses, trams and trains in the districts of Kassel, Hersfeld-Rotenburg, Werra-Meißner, Schwalm-Eder and Waldeck-Frankenberg as well as the city of Kassel. The subject of this tender is the commissioning of an agency or a service provider for the comprehensive support and strategic further development of our social media channels. The service contract is awarded for a fixed term of 3 years with options for the client to extend twice by one further year each time. The contractor must provide the following services: 1. The core task of the service provider consists in the long-term support of the existing social media channels of NVV. This includes the continuous adaptation of content and strategies to the changing dynamics of the respective platforms in order to ensure optimal reach and interaction with the target groups. The service provider creates a monthly editorial plan that prepares relevant topics of NVV, regional events (e.g. events with combo tickets such as ski jumping in Willingen or the Kassel Kulturzelt) and product presentations in a channel-specific manner. The plans are drawn up in close coordination with NVV and can be adapted at short notice if necessary. Furthermore, the service provider is responsible for planning and carrying out cross-platform campaigns (such as competitions etc.) taking data protection into account. Another important aspect is the maintenance of cooperations with regional providers and content creators. An advent calendar for one of the platforms is to be conceived and implemented annually, including the required photo production. In the field of photography and videography, the service provider is responsible for the needs-based creation and editing of image material. This includes at least one video shoot per month on site (A-content), the creation of at least two video contents with existing material (B-content) as well as at least two moving-image contents with animations (C-content). 2. The tasks of the contractor also include the strategic further development of the social media presence of NVV. 3. Furthermore, the contractor has to fulfil the task of community management including dialogue management. For this purpose, the necessary tools for processing social media activities must be provided and compliance with the community guidelines of NVV must be ensured. A prompt response to comments, fan posts, messages and reviews within eight hours during working hours (working days 8-17 o'clock) must be ensured. 4. The success of the social media activities is measured by quarterly reports from the contractor, which contain the most important key performance indicators (KPIs) of the platforms. The service provider interprets the statistics and derives recommendations for action. In addition, an annual report is produced. 5. For the fixed contract term of 3 years, a total budget of 400.000 euros net is available. This includes an annual advertising budget of 18.000 euros for all channels.
sig_114957fe11a47c6380ea.title: Social Media

sig_1173cc2bcae43e84bfd9.description: Holbæk Kommune invites you to a market dialogue ahead of an upcoming procurement for the purchase of safety-enhancing IT technology in connection with citizens requiring care. The upcoming procurement comprises the delivery of an integrated software and hardware solution intended to support staff at the municipality's care centres – and potentially other areas – in prioritising and making the best possible professional care decisions. Dialogue is requested regarding an IT solution that can translate data into actionable insights that strengthen the professional overview, improve the quality of care and increase safety for citizens through more targeted efforts and better use of resources. The procurement is expected to include installation and configuration of software and hardware, implementation, ongoing user training, maintenance and support, etc. The service thus comprises both the supply of software and hardware and other services intended to support Holbæk Kommune in using and optimally exploiting the IT technology. The market dialogue is conducted as individual meetings, which are expected to be held on 16 and 17 February 2026 at the Town Hall in Holbæk Kommune, Kanalstræde 2, 4300 Holbæk. Registration must be made by email to: birgn@holb.dk.
sig_1173cc2bcae43e84bfd9.title: Market dialogue on safety-enhancing IT technology for citizens requiring care

After completion of the market exploration, the results will be evaluated by the contracting authority and are expected to be incorporated neutrally into the tender documents of the intended award procedure. The market exploration is to be implemented as follows. Feedback from interested companies is requested by 20.04.2026 at the contact address: echtzeit@nasa.de. Step 1: To do this, please first send an email to the address: echtzeit@nasa.de, with which you declare your interest in the market exploration. With this query, please submit at least one reference intended to serve as proof that you have already implemented a similar project as a supplier in a company. The reference should contain: name of the contracting authority, specification of the implementation period, cost scope, brief description of the content. Step 2: If the required reference is available, you will then receive the URL for downloading the documents as well as the password required for this. Step 3: If there is still an interest in the market exploration, the interested parties are expected to present the offered system after viewing these documents available online. The contract documents are available in German. The procedural language is German. The feedback should include, alongside the details of NASA GmbH (technical requirements), the presentation of the product (presentation, promotional film or similar), completed questionnaire, expected cost framework (investment and ongoing), possible special features of the product, possible implementation periods to establish this product in the company, and an explanation of what steps would be necessary for this. The feedback from interested parties should be sent to echtzeit@nasa.de by 18.05.2026. In the next step, up to 5 interested parties will be invited by NASA GmbH to a virtual interview, on-site interview at NASA GmbH or an on-site interview at their company at the beginning of June. Participation is voluntary and has no connection with subsequent participation in any later award procedure. Participation is also not a prerequisite for a later commission. In a later procedure, NASA GmbH will ensure that participants in the market exploration do not have an information advantage. Any expenses incurred by the companies participating in this market exploration will generally not be reimbursed.

sig_12c02ab808cda33bc30f.description: HTE is a field of chemistry that expanded exponentially in the past five years, and most pharmaceutical companies are currently using it in their workflows. This methodology allows multi-parameter optimisation of chemical reactions but also synthesis of multiple compounds (96 to 384) on a small-scale using plate chemistry. Combined with the implementation of Direct-to-Biology (D2B) approaches, which involves the direct testing of non-purified mixtures, biological data is obtained faster. The combination of these methods greatly improves the Design, Make, Test, and Analyse (DMTA) cycle. Lot 1: . The option is a cloud-based design platform, accessible via a secure web interface, offering enhanced scalability and reduced infrastructure overhead. The solution will integrate with a University of Dundee-hosted virtual machine to enable secure data exchange and computational workflows. Installation of server-side components will be managed by the DDU Data Management and Computational Chemistry teams, with network provisioning supported by DTS. Ongoing maintenance and updates will be provided by the vendor.
