sig_13a32b2b94765d0369f0.description: I. INTRODUCTION This Special Notice announces the Department of Navy Rapid Capabilities Office (DONRCO) Disruptor Days. The purpose of this event is to provide industry access to unique Government assets (test ranges, Labs, equipment, data) to support the development of mission-critical solutions. This initiative explicitly highlights a strategic partnership between Portfolio Acquisition Executive Mission Systems (PAE MS) and Office of Naval Intelligence (ONI). PAE MS will serve as the primary evaluators, and the ONI will be actively involved throughout the planning, evaluation, and review process to ensure solutions meet rigorous operational demands. Disclaimer: This announcement does not constitute a solicitation and shall not be construed as a commitment by the Government. Responses in any form are not offers, and the Government is under no obligation to award a contract as a result of this announcement. Any submission of information is strictly voluntary. II. TOPIC DESCRIPTION Globally significant maritime chokepoints present dense, asymmetrical, and highly dynamic threat environments. To address these operational challenges, the DONRCO seeks to identify and evaluate commercial data and technologies capable of performing rapid data fusion and multi-sensor correlation to support real-time Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA). Technical Focus The Department of the Navy (DON) needs to detect, locate, identify, and track all maritime vessels. The DON needs data solutions that can follow all types of vessels, from cooperative ships that report their location (self-reporting vessels) to non-cooperative "dark targets" that try to hide their positions. Dark targets may be involved in illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing, illicit drug trafficking, illegal arms trafficking, terrorism activities, or piracy. The DON is interested in novel data sources and analytics tools that can plug into and enhance the DON’s unclassified MDA tool, called SeaVision (https://info.seavision.volpe.dot.gov/). This event will experiment with novel combinations of data and analytics tools to demonstrate improvements in analytical MDA results by showing: the direct output of vessel positions, types, and predicted tracks. For this Disruptor Day event, data provided by participants should be in GeoJSON format. Data provided to participants for analysis will also be in GeoJSON format. Innovative Industry Solutions Submissions and demonstrations will focus on the following key operational and analytical capability areas. Participants can demonstrate in one or both capability areas. 1. Novel Data Sources After registration, the DON will specify a preferred location and window of time for data collection so that different data sources can be most easily overlaid with baseline SeaVision data. Advanced Data Solutions: Participants could demonstrate novel, previously untapped information pipelines to feed MDA analytical tools. High-Granularity Insights: Participants could demonstrate precise entity resolution and deep tracking capability. Latency and Timing: Participants should provide information regarding latency of data collected as well as how often data can be collected. 2. Novel Analytics Tools Correlation Engines: Participants could demonstrate automated calculators or AI tools to rapidly identify and report hidden relationships across disparate datasets. Source Identification: Participants should include identification of all data sources used to generate analytical results (e.g., a specific Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image, Automatic Identification (AIS) data feed, or Radio Frequency (RF) signal). Methodology Description: Participants should provide a high-level description of the analytic process or algorithms used. This information must be sufficient for the DON to understand the methodology, verify its legitimacy, and assess effectiveness during operational use. In-Scope Data Sources for Both Capability Areas New data sources and platforms must be capable of supporting the possibility of ingestion, correlation, and analysis using a standardized GeoJSON format. In addition to the following data types, vendors are encouraged to propose data sources beyond this list and/or ways to enhance these data types with additional attributes or analytics provided in GeoJSON format: Electro-Optical (EO) imagery and intelligence data, Infrared (IR) data and thermal imaging feeds and RF data, including signal emissions, intercept feeds, and spectrum analysis tools. SAR imagery and processing tools. Commodities Data (e.g., cargo manifests, shipping declarations, port-of-origin records, global trade statistics). Other Data (social media, acoustics, etc.) III. EVENT DETAILS The Disruptor Days event will occur starting the Week of November 30, 2026 (with a planned 2-week testing window) at NIWC Pacific in San Diego, CA. The event will take place in a specialized laboratory environment that allows vendors to brief their products in a traditional industry day format and execute live analytical evaluations. The DON anticipates using Limited Purpose Cooperative Research and Development Agreements (LP-CRADAs) to support this effort. More detailed information to follow. Following the event, selected vendors will receive structured feedback and scoring performance summaries from the Government evaluation panel. IV. REGISTRATION To Register for the Maritime Domain Awareness Disruptor Days, interested vendors should submit their information here: https://forms.osi.apps.mil/r/PaVKy9YV3S Additionally, DONRCO will host a virtual Q&A session prior to the event to answer vendor questions. Attending the virtual Q&A Session is optional and not required for Disruptor Day registration. Registration via the above form also serves to sign up for the Virtual Q&A session. Virtual Q&A session will be held: 1300 EDT, Wednesday, September 30, 2026 Sign-up Deadline for the Virtual Q&A session: 1200 EDT, on September 29, 2026 Pre-registration is REQUIRED for both the virtual Q&A and the Disruptor Days event. No walk-ins will be permitted. A downs selection will occur depending on interest due to limitations of space and time constraints. Additional information will be required prior to final event registration. V. SIGNIFICANT DATES AND TIMES Event / Milestone Date & Time Special Notice Announcement Released 18 September 2026 Virtual Pre-Event Q&A Sign-Up Deadline 1200 EDT on 30 September 2026 Virtual Pre-Event Q&A Session 1300 EDT on 1 October 2026 Final Survey Submission Closes 1600 EDT on 9 October 2026 Attendance & Invitation Approvals Sent 16 October 2026 Technical Q&A Session (Data Sharing & Setup) 21 October 2026 Disruptor Week Event Begins (NIWC Pacific, San Diego, CA) Week of 30 November 2026 (2-Week Duration) Disruptor Day Distinguished Visitor Day (NIWC Pacific, San Diego, CA) 10 December 2026 VIII. POINTS OF CONTACT Any questions regarding this announcement, data integration requirements, or event logistics should be submitted via email to: DisruptorDay@us.navy.mil

The section of county road DJ 792C km 77+626 – 81+228 is classified as a road with a cobbled road surfacing and is in a poor technical condition. The road section exhibits degradations specific to cobbled roads in an advanced stage of wear, namely: disintegration and loss of stone material from the running layer; appearance of ruts and longitudinal and transverse unevenness; surfaces with local settlements and deformations; potholes and areas with water accumulations; degradation of verges; silting up or absence of rainwater drainage systems; pronounced dust generation during dry periods and mud formation during periods of precipitation; depletion of bearing capacity and of the uniformity of the running surface. The existing technical condition significantly affects traffic conditions and road safety, leading to:  reduction in travel speed;  increase in journey times;  discomfort for road users;  increase in motor vehicle operating costs;  difficulties in traffic flow under adverse weather conditions;  impairment of road connectivity to the Romanian-Hungarian border area. Considering the above, it is necessary to modernise the county road DJ 792C km 77+626 – 81+228 Dorobanți – RO/HU Border, following the drawing up of technical documentation: update of DALI+PT+DE+CS, DTAC, documentation for obtaining approvals and verification of the project. General objective: as a result of the implementation of the county road modernisation investment, which will be carried out in accordance with DALI+PT+DE+CS, the following will be facilitated:  development of regional and cross-border connectivity;  stimulation of the economic and social development of the area;  facilitation of access to the border crossing point with Hungary by ensuring optimal traffic conditions and increasing the operational lifespan of the road infrastructure;  rapid transport of residents. The specific objective is the provision of design services and technical assistance from the designer for the DALI+PT+DE+CS, DTAC phase, documentation for obtaining the Urbanism Certificate, approvals, verification of the project for the investment ''Modernisation of DJ 792C km 77+626 – 81+228 Dorobanți – RO/HU Border”. sig_153ea3d9b6ff8a68a631.description: Bergen vann constructs and operates the water and sewage plant in Bergen municipality and is an agency with approx. 270 employees. We shall procure a notification system that sends SMS, email and any voice messages to relevant recipients. The primary need is map based notification of inhabitants and entities during operational episodes. The notification shall be sent to those who have registered for national addresses, or operate business activities within a given area. Operational events can be planned measures that result in a break in the delivery for technical work on the pipeline network, or in the event of pipeline breaks, leaks and other non-planned situations. For such events Bergen vann needs to be able to gather data for later reporting and statistics. This applies to both event and notification, duration and number of persons affected. The system shall also be used for notifying other municipal departments than Bergen water.
sig_153ea3d9b6ff8a68a631.title: BV 2025-35 - Telephone notification system - prequalification

sig_15d3de0b21e21d2f3694.description:
The contracting authority intends to introduce enterprise-wide uniform, legally compliant and digital records management (e-file). The aim of this market consultation is to gain an overview of available solutions as well as established professional, technical and organisational implementation approaches. In particular, insights are to be gained into: - suitable solution architectures and implementation approaches - integration options into the existing system landscape - requirements for operation, support and governance - automation and AI functionalities - licence, operating and cost models - scalability and future-proofing of the solutions - procedural models for introduction, migration and rollout - experiences from comparable organisations, particularly in the public environment and among KRITIS operators 1. Initial situation The contracting authority currently has a heterogeneous system and information landscape with different storage locations, applications and forms of documentation. Information and documents are stored, among other things, in Microsoft 365 applications (e.g. Outlook, Teams and SharePoint), various document management systems, SAP applications and local storage structures. As an operator of Critical Infrastructures (KRITIS), the contracting authority is subject to special requirements regarding information security, compliance, traceability and the long-term availability of information. The aim is to introduce central and standardised digital records management. 2. Target vision (functional requirements) We are looking for a solution that supports the following requirements in particular: - Central management and provision of files, documents and information - Role- and permission-based access control - Mapping of filing plans, metadata and retention rules - Audit-proof documentation and traceability - Integration of relevant enterprise applications and specialist procedures - Support for automated filing, search and research functions - Scalability for enterprise-wide deployment The contracting authority is expressly interested in different solution approaches and technological implementation options. 3. Operation and support requirements In addition to the provision of the solution, support services for the operation and further development of digital records management are expected. The future solution is to be operated as a cloud-based service (SaaS). In particular, the contracting authority shall assume the professional management, governance and user and role management. The technical operation of the solution shall be provided by the vendor. Support is expected in the following areas in particular: - Maintenance and further development of the solution - Technical support and error analysis - Implementation of updates and release changes - Support for configurations and system adjustments - Support for operations, performance and interface management - Training and qualification offers for administrators and users Solutions with an established cloud operating model, transparent support services and clearly defined service level agreements (SLAs) are sought. 4. Questions for the market The contracting authority asks interested companies for feedback on the following points: Solution & architecture - What solution approaches do you offer for the introduction of digital records management? - How are file structures, metadata, retention periods and archiving mapped in your solution? - What integration options exist with Microsoft 365, SAP and other enterprise applications? - What automation and AI functions are available? Operation & organisation - How is user, role and permission management carried out? - How are traceability, audit-proofness and audibility ensured? - What governance and compliance functions does your solution offer? - What operating and support models do you offer (e.g. SaaS, on-premises or hybrid)? - What experience do you have regarding the operational effort before and after the introduction of your solution? Scaling & costs - How does your solution scale in terms of user numbers, file volumes and organisational units? - What licence and pricing models are used? - Is the solution multi-tenant capable? - What essential cost and effort factors must be taken into account? Introduction & implementation - How is the introduction of your solution typically carried out (e.g. project procedure and phased model)? - What timeframe can be expected from experience for the introduction of digital records management? - What success factors and typical challenges should be taken into account on the customer side? - What experience do you have in introducing comparable solutions in public sector companies or operators of critical infrastructures? The contracting authority is initially interested in the submission of company documents, presentations or comparable documents with which the above-mentioned questions are answered. On the basis of the incoming feedback, the contracting authority reserves the right to hold in-depth discussions as well as presentation or demonstration appointments with selected companies. In this case, the signing of an NDA is necessary. Lot PAR-0000: Market consultation for the introduction of digital records management (e-file) at HAMBURG WASSER. sig_16a29305aca3aa2c1ef0.description: The DOE Office of Science (SC), Office of Critical Minerals and Energy Innovation (CMEI), Office of Environmental Management (EM), Office of Nuclear Energy (NE), Office of Electricity (OE), and Hydrocarbons and Geothermal Office (HGEO) hereby announce interest in receiving applications from interdisciplinary teams addressing the Genesis Mission National Science and Technology Challenges to accelerate scientific discovery and research and development (R&D) workflows using novel artificial intelligence (AI) models and frameworks. By achieving AI advantage, these teams will advance the DOE's mission and ensure America’s security and prosperity by addressing energy, environmental, and nuclear challenges through science and technology. Teams are encouraged to leverage the extensive scientific and data resources of the DOE/National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA), the National Laboratories, U.S. industry, and academia. The resulting AI models and workflows, if successful, may be integrated into the American Science Cloud. DOE is soliciting new FY26 Phase I small team and Phase II large team applications in the following topic areas: advanced manufacturing, biotechnology, critical materials, nuclear fission, nuclear fusion, quantum information science, semiconductors and microelectronics, discovery science, and energy (see specific focus areas in Section III Program Descriptions). In addition, this RFA will remain available to allow the recipients of FY26 Phase I awards to apply for larger team Phase II awards. In a few weeks, DOE plans to amend the RFA to clarify the LOI and application guidelines for FY26 Phase II awards. In FY27, DOE plans to amend the RFA or to issue an alternative funding opportunity to update the topic and focus areas to allow a second competition of Phase I small team applications and Phase II large team applications.

sig_16a777e75b86af434518.description: The Ministry of Defence (MOD), through the Defence AI Accelerator Task Force (TF RAID), intends to procure a secure, scalable capability to support operational planning across Defence. TF RAID exists to accelerate the responsible adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) and data-enabled capabilities in support of Defence outcomes, working with users, technical specialists and industry to identify, test and transition operationally relevant solutions. This requirement is expected to support operational planners by improving access to authorised planning information, enabling reusable machine-readable planning knowledge, orchestrating analytical services, and supporting the modelling, testing and comparison of alternative Courses of Action (COAs). The procurement will be structured as a single competition with 2 Lots: - Lot 1 will focus on planning data, knowledge and analytical orchestration services; and - Lot 2 will focus on COA testing, evaluation and adaptation services. Suppliers are invited to bid for 1 or both lots. Together, the Lots are intended to improve the speed, quality, traceability and robustness of operational planning while maintaining appropriate human oversight, governance, transparency, security and interoperability within Authority-approved environments, including those handling information up to SECRET UK EYES ONLY where required. MOD will be seeking to compete this requirement through the Government Commercial Agency Artificial Intelligence Dynamic Purchasing System (AI DPS/RM6200). Participation in any subsequent competition will therefore be limited to suppliers appointed to the relevant Lots of the AIDPS Framework who pass the shortlist filter exercise. Lot 1: Planning Data, Knowledge and Analytical Orchestration Services (PDKAOS). The requirement is expected to support operational planning activities through the integration of planning data, machine-readable planning knowledge and advanced analytical services. The Authority seeks a capability that improves the speed, quality and scale of operational planning whilst maintaining appropriate human oversight, governance, transparency and security. Requirement Summary: The Authority requires an initial capability to support operational planners by enabling them to: • Discover, access and exploit authorised planning information from multiple sources. • Create and maintain reusable representations of planning knowledge, expertise, assumptions, dependencies and relationships. • Assemble, configure and reuse analytical services in support of operational planning tasks. • Improve traceability between planning inputs, analytical activities and planning outputs. • Reduce dependency on fragmented information sources, manual processes and specialist knowledge bottlenecks. The capability is expected to support planning activity across multiple domains, operational functions and echelons of command rather than providing a single-purpose planning application. Lot 2: COA Testing, Evaluation and Adaptation Services for Operational Planning. The requirement is expected to support operational planning activities through the representation of operational environments, modelling of Courses of Action (COAs), evaluation of alternative scenarios and adversary responses, and generation of evidence-based insights to support planning and decision-making. The Authority seeks a capability that improves the speed, quality and robustness of operational planning whilst maintaining appropriate human oversight, governance, transparency and security. The Authority requires an initial capability to support operational planners by enabling them to: • Represent operational environments, actors, assumptions, constraints and dependencies in reusable and machine-readable forms. • Model, test and compare alternative Courses of Action. • Explore multiple operational scenarios, environmental conditions, assumptions and adversary responses. • Generate evidence-based insights to support adaptation and refinement of operational plans. • Improve traceability between planning inputs, analytical activities and planning outputs. • Reduce reliance on manual wargaming, fragmented information sources and time-intensive analytical processes. The capability is expected to support planning activity across multiple domains, operational functions and echelons of command rather than providing a single-purpose planning application.

sig_176a5d3078f78a0949cf.description: The Scottish Government’s Directorate for Digital is seeking an innovative service management solution to support a growing portfolio of digital services, including ScotAccount, ScotPayments, mygov.scot, Cloud Platform Services, and more. As demand, complexity and user expectations increase, we require scalable, technology-enabled approaches that can grow as our services grow, while delivering value for money. A successful solution will help ensure resilient, secure and efficient service operations, reducing risks to service quality, productivity, revenue and public trust, while supporting the future development of Scotland’s digital public services. Lot 1: . CivTech’s mission is to drive daring and innovation in the public sector by collaboratively solving Challenges that make people’s lives better – and in doing so create generations of sustainable, high growth businesses. CivTech brings together public sector expertise and private sector innovation to solve real problems, develop new products, and deliver better, faster and easier services for everyone. Central to the approach is co-production with the citizen. Part of the Scottish Government’s Directorate for Digital, CivTech’s approach is helping transform public sector engagement with tech and innovation, delivering significant benefits to public services, producing genuine uplifts for the Scottish economy - and along the way, making lives better. Across the country there are problems public sector organisations would like to solve and in the current environment the need for smart, efficient and effective products has never been greater. The Scottish Government is aware innovation is a good way to create them and is committed to ensuring a large part of its tech spend goes to innovative businesses - whatever stage they’re at, or size they are. This is where CivTech comes in. The CivTech Innovation Flow is designed to create products as quickly and effectively as possible, and uses a true Accelerator model at the heart of its Innovation Flow model. For you – whether you’re an individual, team or company – it’s an opportunity to take on a Challenge, solve it, and win contracts with a blue-chip public sector organisation. You’ll build a product, and a business to take it as far as possible. Because here’s the kicker: the Challenges we issue aren’t ‘single organisation’ problems – most of the problems we are solving exist worldwide. In short: Open Challenges are set. Any organisation, team or individual can respond. Applications are assessed, and shortlisted proposals go into an Exploration Stage where they’re developed further together with the Challenge Sponsor and the CivTech [for which participating applicants are paid]. The best go through to the Accelerator – a period of intensive work to create the solution, and through CivTech’s unique business growth workshop system, a business capable of taking the product to the world. Please visit our website for information on CivTech and how to get involved https://www.civtech.scot/how-to-apply-civtech-12 https://www.civtech.scot/civtech-12-challenge-2-scaling-dynamically-service-management-capabilities

Through the procurement of specialised consultancy services for project management, the necessary framework will be ensured for the efficient implementation of the project "Consolidation and rehabilitation of the Dumbrăveni Chronic Psychiatric Hospital, Vrancea County", in compliance with the obligations assumed through the financing contract, the requirements of the financier and the applicable legislation. The consultancy services will aim to support the beneficiary in the general coordination of the project, monitoring physical and financial progress, tracking compliance with assumed deadlines, managing documents related to implementation, supporting the procurement process, monitoring contracts, verifying that expenses fall within the approved budget, as well as drafting the documentation and reports requested by the financier. Proper implementation of the project requires permanent monitoring of the degree of completion of activities, assumed indicators and proposed results, as well as the identification and management of any risks that may arise during the project. In this context, the experience and skills of an economic operator specialised in the management of projects with non-reimbursable financing represent an important element for ensuring efficient and compliant implementation. Thus, to achieve this objective, the bidder declared the winner of the award procedure will ensure at least the following categories of services: - Assistance and support for monitoring the financing contract and the attached documents, for compliance with the assumed terms and conditions; - Assistance in monitoring public procurement contracts concluded within the project; - Management of the MySMIS2021 platform dedicated to project implementation; - Assistance in the creation and monitoring of cash flow throughout the project implementation period; - Drafting and documentation of pre-financing/payment/reimbursement requests; - Assistance in the relationship between the contracting authority and the REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT AGENCY FOR THE SOUTH-EAST DEVELOPMENT REGION (ADR SE), in its capacity as Management Authority for the South-East Regional Programme 2021-2027, during project implementation; - assistance in monitoring compliance with the rules regarding the visibility of the European Union, in accordance with the visual identity manual applicable to the South-East Regional Programme 2021-2027; - drafting of activity reports, as well as those established by the application and the financing contract. Further details can be found in the Specifications. The number of days by which clarifications can be requested before the deadline for the submission of tenders is 20 days. The Contracting Authority will respond only once to requests for clarification on the 11 day before the deadline for the submission of tenders. The object of the contract to be awarded through this public procurement procedure consists of the purchase of consultancy services for the implementation of the project "Consolidation and rehabilitation of the Dumbrăveni Chronic Psychiatric Hospital, Vrancea County". The consultancy services will aim to support the beneficiary in the general coordination of the project, monitoring physical and financial progress, tracking compliance with assumed deadlines, managing documents related to implementation, supporting the procurement process, monitoring contracts, verifying that expenses fall within the approved budget, as well as drafting the documentation and reports requested by the financier. Proper implementation of the project requires permanent monitoring of the degree of completion of activities, assumed indicators and proposed results, as well as the identification and management of any risks that may arise during the project. In this context, the experience and skills of an economic operator specialised in the management of projects with non-reimbursable financing represent an important element for ensuring efficient and compliant implementation. Thus, to achieve this objective, the bidder declared the winner of the award procedure will ensure at least the following categories of services: - Assistance and support for monitoring the financing contract and the attached documents, for compliance with the assumed terms and conditions; - Assistance in monitoring public procurement contracts concluded within the project; - Management of the MySMIS2021 platform dedicated to project implementation; - Assistance in the creation and monitoring of cash flow throughout the project implementation period; - Drafting and documentation of pre-financing/payment/reimbursement requests; - Assistance in the relationship between the contracting authority and the REGIONAL DEVELOPMENT AGENCY FOR THE SOUTH-EAST DEVELOPMENT REGION (ADR SE), in its capacity as Management Authority for the South-East Regional Programme 2021-2027, during project implementation; - assistance in monitoring compliance with the rules regarding the visibility of the European Union, in accordance with the visual identity manual applicable to the South-East Regional Programme 2021-2027; - drafting of activity reports, as well as those established by the application and the financing contract. The main benefits resulting from meeting the need are: • ensuring efficient coordination of all project activities and integrated implementation of technical, financial and administrative components; • increasing the contracting authority's capacity to manage the investment by supporting the implementation team with specialised expertise; • permanent monitoring of project progress and early identification of potential risks, delays or non-conformities; • ensuring that activities fall within the implementation schedule and the approved budget;

• supporting the beneficiary in carrying out the procedures, documentation and reporting requested by the financier; • reducing the risk of financial corrections or ineligible expenses as a result of non-compliance with the rules for implementing projects financed from European funds; • ensuring good management of contractual relationships with contractors, suppliers and other participants involved in the investment; • contribution to achieving the specific objectives of the project, namely the consolidation and rehabilitation of hospital buildings, increasing user safety, improving energy efficiency and reducing the impact on the environment. By achieving these objectives, the existing deficiencies of the hospital infrastructure will be remedied, the technical condition of the buildings will be improved and adequate conditions will be created for carrying out medical activities in conditions of safety, comfort and efficiency. Meeting the identified need thus contributes to the successful completion of the investment, the efficient use of allocated funds and the achievement of the results assumed through the Financing Application.

Südwestrundfunk (SWR), as a public service broadcaster of the ARD, is strictly dependent on a functioning IT infrastructure to fulfil its tasks. In the age of digital communication, central elements are necessary for efficient process control in order to be able to plan, execute, and implement processes digitally, both internally and across the entire ARD. Different software solutions for network management are currently in use at Südwestrundfunk and the eligible state broadcasting corporations. The network management tool CheckMK is already in use across the board at a large number of the eligible entities and is deeply integrated into the system landscape. As part of the ARD structural reform, a holistic solution is to be established across the entire ARD. For this purpose, services for the Checkmk product are to be procured for Südwestrundfunk and other eligible state broadcasting corporations. Furthermore, the eligible entities require further services such as consulting and support in the area of network management and for the CheckMK product. Südwestrundfunk (SWR) as the contracting authority and the eligible broadcasting corporations therefore intended to procure in two lots: • Lot 1: Services for the Checkmk product incl. support • Lot 2: Development and consulting in the area of Checkmk The contracting authority (SWR) / eligible entities place the following essential requirements on the services to be provided by the contractor: Lot 1: - Contract Framework agreement for the basic term of 24 months - Delivery services Services of the Checkmk product incl. support for a limited period. - Optional additional services Extension of the framework agreement by 12 to then 36 months Extension of the framework agreement by a further 12 to a total of 48 months Advance payment guarantee Services in accordance with the requirements of the technical specifications (see contract documents and Annex 17 – Service and Price Sheet for Lot 1) The acceptance quantities for Lot 1 are shown in the procedural and contract documents, Chapter 5.6 Acceptance Quantities: Acceptance quantities Number of services in units for Checkmk incl. support: Minimum acceptance quantity: 1.000.000 units, Planned acceptance quantity: 1.400.000 units, Optional maximum acceptance quantity: 1.800.000 units Acceptance quantities Checkmk Synthetic Monitoring: Minimum acceptance quantity: 10 units, Planned acceptance quantity: 200 units, Optional maximum acceptance quantity: 500 units Acceptance quantities virtual appliances: Minimum acceptance quantity: 0 units, Planned acceptance quantity: 0 units, Optional maximum acceptance quantity: 1 units per licence scale up to 600.000 services Lot 2: - Contract Framework agreement for the basic term of 24 months - Services Consulting and support services for the Checkmk product from Lot 1 Development, migration, and integration services - Optional additional services Extension of the framework agreement by 12 to then 36 months Extension of the framework agreement by a further 12 to a total of 48 months Services in accordance with the requirements of the technical specifications (see contract documents and Annex 21 – Service and Price Sheet for Lot 2) The acceptance quantities for Lot 2 are shown in the procedural and contract documents, Chapter 6.8 Acceptance Quantities: Acceptance quantities Service in hours: Minimum acceptance quantity: 200 hours, Planned acceptance quantity: 400 hours, Optional maximum acceptance quantity: 600 hours Acceptance quantities Flat rate for incidental costs (incl. travel times) per on-site deployment: Minimum acceptance quantity: 0 hours, Planned acceptance quantity: 0 hours, Optional maximum acceptance quantity: 10 hours The start of the framework agreement for each lot is planned for 01.03.2027. sig_18bd21c33e6440c1ba3c.description: This Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) allows you to submit an offer to a large number of educational institutions in Ireland and the Netherlands, after completing a simple registration procedure. The DPS will give admittance to all interested parties that offer online collaboration tools in accordance with the requirements described in the Tender documents. The Participants of the DPS wish to purchase online collaboration tools on demand in three categories, which are (1) online whiteboarding tools, (2) Project, task & work (place) management tools, and (3) Online survey & polling tools. This means that each Participant individually purchases a online collaboration tool in a category of their interest as and when it requires that software. The Assignments for delivering these products must be awarded in a simple manner and within a short period of time. sig_18feeb0caa7b2dd2da0a.description:
The purpose of the contract is the provision of services relating to physico-chemical analyses in various environmental matrices such as: soils, sediments, water and fertilising materials. Description of the services to be performed: Analyses of pollutants and physico-chemical parameters on samples of soils, sediments, water and fertilising materials and transmission of a report detailing the analysis results. These services fall under the CPV code: 79311300-0. This is a framework agreement for services in a sector sensitive to fraud: NO. Lot(s): The contract is divided into lots. - Lot 1 : Determination of pollutants and physico-chemical parameters on soils and sediments. In accordance with Article 15 of the Law of 17 June 2016 on public procurement, this lot is reserved for social economy insertion enterprises: NO - Lot 2 : Determination of pollutants and physico-chemical parameters on groundwater, surface water or wastewater. In accordance with Article 15 of the Law of 17 June 2016 on public procurement, this lot is reserved for social economy insertion enterprises: NO - Lot 3 : Determination of pollutants and physico-chemical parameters on fertilising materials. In accordance with Article 15 of the Law of 17 June 2016 on public procurement, this lot is reserved for social economy insertion enterprises: NO You may submit an offer for several lots. You may propose discounts or improvements in the event of being awarded several lots: NO. The contracting authority reserves the right not to award one or more lots. It also reserves the right to relaunch a procurement procedure for any lot not awarded. Furthermore, the award of a lot does not entail any obligation to order on the part of the contracting authority, which reserves the right not to follow up, in whole or in part, on the needs covered by this contract. Variant(s): This contract does not include any authorised, required or free variants. You may not introduce a variant. Free variants are prohibited. Any variants that may be proposed will not be taken into account. Option(s): This contract does not include any authorised or free options. Free options are prohibited. This contract contains one or more required option(s): 'supplement linked to emergency analyses', detailed more precisely in the award criteria. You must introduce an option. If you do not introduce an option, this will result in the irregularity of your base offer. Ensure that you respect the following minimum and specific requirements: within the framework of the various analyses, the tenderer must offer the possibility of performing emergency analyses. Tranche(s): The contract is not divided into tranches. The analyses may, in particular, be carried out for soils and sediments on: 1) the PFAS listed in the technical protocol CMA/3/D in compliance with this technical protocol; 2) the leaching of PFAS in compliance with the technical protocol CMA/2/II/A.26 ; 3) the analysis on eluate of the PFAS listed in the technical protocol WAC/IV/A/025 in compliance with this technical protocol; 4) the analysis on eluate of Trifluoroacetic acid (TFA), CAS no. 76‐05‐1 in compliance with the technical protocol WAC/IV/A/026 ; 5) the pH-KCl acidity; 6) the organic matter content (by loss on ignition); 7) the particle size: 5 fractions (<2,<16,<45,<63 and<2000 μm); 8) the parameters included in Annex 1 of the Soil Decree of 01/03/2018 (with analysis of the phenol index rather than phenol). The referenced technical protocols are available via the following links: https://emis.vito.be/nl/erkende-laboratoria/bodem-en-afvalstoffen-ovam/compendium-cma https://emis.vito.be/nl/erkende-laboratoria/water/compendium-wac As these protocols may evolve during the contract, the successful tenderer must always ensure that they comply with the latest available version (list of parameters subject to change). At the time of submitting the offer, the tenderer specifies the limits of quantification for each parameter. As leaching is a pre-treatment operation, no limit of quantification is expected for this item. The results are transmitted to the ISSeP according to the formats and mode of communication set out in point 2 : Documentation. The samples are kept at the laboratory until receipt and validation of the results by the ISSeP. They are then disposed of by the laboratory. Random checks by the ISSeP of the transmitted results may be carried out on an ad hoc basis. As a required option, the tenderer must propose the performance of emergency analyses (within a period of 24 h, 48 h or 72 h) and specify, as a percentage of the price of the analysis, the amount of the corresponding applicable surcharge.; The analyses may, in particular, be carried out for groundwater, surface water or industrial wastewater on: 1) the PFAS listed in the technical protocol WAC/IV/A/025 in compliance with this technical protocol; 2) the PFAS 'FTOH and C6O4' as follows: o 2-(Perfluorohexyl)ethyl alcohol (6:2 FTOH), CAS no. 647-42-7 o 2-(Perfluorooctyl)ethanol (8:2 FTOH), CAS no. 678-39-7 o 2,2-difluoro-2-((2,2,4,5-tetrafluoro-5-(trifluoromethoxy) -1,3-dioxolan-4-yl) oxy) acetic acid (C6O4), CAS no. 1190931-41-9 3) Trifluoroacetic acid (TFA), CAS no. 76‐05‐1 in compliance with the technical protocol WAC/IV/A/026 ; 4) the parameters included in Annex 1 of the Soil Decree of 01/03/2018 (with analysis of the phenol index rather than phenol). The referenced technical protocols are available via the following link: https://emis.vito.be/nl/erkende-laboratoria/water/compendium-wac As these protocols may evolve during the contract, the successful tenderer must always ensure that they comply with the latest available version (list of parameters subject to change). At the time of submitting the offer, the tenderer specifies the limits of quantification for each parameter.

The results are transmitted to the ISSeP according to the formats and communication method set out in point 2 : Documentation. The samples are kept at the laboratory until receipt and validation of the results by the ISSeP. They are then disposed of by the laboratory. Random checks of the transmitted results by the ISSeP may be carried out on an ad hoc basis. As a required option, the tenderer must propose the performance of urgent analyses (within a period of 24 h, 48 h or 72 h) and specify, as a percentage of the analysis price, the amount of the corresponding applicable surcharge.; The analyses may, in particular, be carried out for fertilising materials on: 1) the PFAS listed in the technical protocol CMA/3/O in compliance with this technical protocol; 2) the leaching of PFAS in compliance with the technical protocol CMA/2/II/A.26; 3) the analysis on eluate of the PFAS listed in the technical protocol WAC/IV/A/025 in compliance with this technical protocol; 4) the analysis on eluate of Trifluoroacetic acid (TFA), CAS No. 76‐05‐1 in compliance with the technical protocol WAC/IV/A/026; 5) the Total Oxidizable Precursors (TOP Assay) according to the Houtz and Sedlak method; 6) the Extractable Organic Fluorine (EOF); 7) the pH-H2O acidity; 8) the organic matter content (by loss on ignition); 9) the impurity content by gravimetry (S-IV-1); 10) the parameters included in Annex 1 of the Soil Decree of 01/03/2018 (with analysis of the phenol index rather than phenol). The referenced technical protocols are available via the following links: https://emis.vito.be/nl/erkende-laboratoria/bodem-en-afvalstoffen-ovam/compendium-cma https://emis.vito.be/nl/erkende-laboratoria/water/compendium-wac https://cwea.issep.be/cwea/ As these protocols may evolve during the contract, the successful tenderer must always ensure compliance with the latest available version (list of parameters subject to change). At the time of submission of the tender, the tenderer shall specify the limits of quantification for each parameter. Note that as leaching is a pre-treatment, no limit of quantification is expected for this item. The results are transmitted to the ISSeP according to the formats and communication method set out in point 2 : Documentation. The samples are kept at the laboratory until receipt and validation of the results by the ISSeP. They are then disposed of by the laboratory. Random checks of the transmitted results by the ISSeP may be carried out on an ad hoc basis. As a required option, the tenderer must propose the performance of urgent analyses (within a period of 24 h, 48 h or 72 h) and specify, as a percentage of the analysis price, the amount of the corresponding applicable surcharge.

sig_1951d05192e6de448c03.description: CLARIFICATION: This is ONLY a market exploration procedure to determine whether and, if so, which companies can offer the service intended for procurement. This preliminary information does not serve the purposes of Section 38 of the Public Procurement Ordinance (VgV). ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The Munich Fire Department is planning, in a lead management capacity for a nationwide joint procurement on a framework agreement basis with purchasing authorization for all operators of control centres for fire and rescue services in Germany, to tender and introduce an interface management system (≠ interface modelling system, see below) named "RESQON". RESQON is intended to make it possible to network all Integrated Control Centres (ILS) nationwide with one another and exchange data amongst each other. In addition, the system is to be used to connect external services with partly proprietary protocols to the various computer-aided dispatch systems of the respective control centre. RESQON consists of local instances at the control centres, which are to be combined into a network. This network is referred to as RESQON Mesh. Participating control centres can exchange incident data via RESQON Mesh. Within the RESQON Mesh there is a central instance, the so-called RESQON Core. RESQON Core provides external connections to standardised services such as, for example, AML and the nora emergency call app. Furthermore, connections to statutory health insurance control centres, to TPS service providers for eCall and police control centres are to be possible in the future. An elementary component of RESQON is an interface modelling system which allows various protocols and data to be transformed and, if necessary, process logic to be mapped using it. The interface modelling system is a component of every local RESQON instance. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- PLEASE NOTE: The purpose of this market exploration is to evaluate the availability of such interface modelling systems. This is also in particular in preparation for a possible direct award - in a lead management capacity for a nationwide joint procurement on a framework agreement basis with purchasing authorization for all operators of control centres for fire and rescue services in Germany - in accordance with Section 14 Paragraph 4 No. 2 letter b) of the Public Procurement Ordinance (VgV), since the objective absence of competition for technical reasons must be demonstrated and, if necessary, proven by the contracting authority. This market exploration is therefore an essential part of the required comprehensive market analysis at European level. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- See additionally the document "2025-11-25_Markterkundung_Schnittstellenmodellierungssystem.pdf". This can be requested from the contact point via the e-tendering system. ======================================================== PROCEDURE FOR INTERESTED COMPANIES: Interested companies that consider themselves in a position to offer a corresponding product are requested to contact the contact point by email at: info@mayburg.de (providing contact details, at least email and telephone) by no later than Thu., 08.01.2025. The LH Munich - Fire Department - will then be informed accordingly and will seek further contact for the continuation of the market exploration or the market exploration procedure.

sig_1a09837a3d46dc7fd567.description: The Norwegian Defence Materiel Agency (FMA) is the contracting authority and responsible for implementing the procurement. FMA is a part of the defence sector, directly under the Ministry of Defence (FD). FMA shall ensure that the Norwegian Armed Forces and other entities in the defence sector have access to cost efficient and secure material and services in line with approved long-term plans. FMA ́s main assignments are planning, procurement, management and disposal of material for the Norwegian Armed Forces and other departments under FD. Organisational reasons can be required during the contract period to transfer the resource to Cyber Defence ́s IT Department (CIT) DRIV. DRIV is responsible for the technical operation and further development (DEVSECOPS) of the Joint Integrated Management System (FIF). FIF is a SAP ERP system integrated with a number of other different applications. Internal processes are based on flexible frameworks (Scrum, SAFE), the Security Act and different industry standards for safety and ITIL for operation. DRIV consists of approx. 150 persons, most of whom are located in Oslo. Both employees and consultants staff the organisation. The aim of this notice is to fill the role of test manager and teamlead within S/4HANA for a product team in project P1160 "Critical Upgrade of ERP". The consultant shall assist with test coordination for product teams, as well as follow-up of teams within logistics, for the purpose of removing obstacles and ensuring speed and flow. The consultant will work closely with the manager of Value Management Office, the solution architects and the various product teams. The role can involve cooperation with other departments and/or projects in the Norwegian Armed Forces.

sig_1a35f66b83334eac618f.description: Background Trøndelag county needs a modern and comprehensive system for electronic substance register, which can support the entity's work on health, safety and the environment. The procurement is being carried out in order to ensure easy access to updated chemical information, contribute to compliance with the current regulations and facilitate safe handling of chemical products throughout the entire organisation. The county has a compound entity with different user groups and work areas, including sixth form colleges, laboratories, operation and cleaning functions, workshops, dental health services, road operation, administration and teaching environments. This sets requirements for a system that is user friendly, accessible and suitable for both employees and pupils, while at the same time being managed in an efficient way across units and professional environments. The aim of the procurement is to establish a joint system that provides a better overview of chemicals, supports local needs and at the same time enables central management and follow-up. Tenderers must therefore understand that the system shall function in a large and varied organisation, with a need for both broad availability and appropriate administration. Description of the assignment Trøndelag county shall procure an electronic substance register that is delivered as a site license for approx. 5,000 employees and 20,000 students. The system shall cover the county ́s need for registration, disclosure and management of information on chemical products across the entity. The delivery includes a digital system with functionality for i.a. search and access to safety data sheets, an overview of chemicals, as well as support for the accompanying HSE work such as risk assessment, substitute and exposure register. The system shall be suitable for different types of users and it can be used in both teaching related and operational contexts. Furthermore, the system shall support secure and efficient access management, including log-on and user administration adapted to the county ́s established identity management. A system is requested that combines user friendliness for local units with the possibility for general administration and control across the organisation. The design of the tender Tenderers shall fill in and respond to all points in the ESPD form, requirement specifications and price form. Any documentation beyond replies directly to the requirement specification shall be uploaded as pdf files, unless otherwise specified. The following shall be completed and submitted with the tender: · Complete Annex 1 - Tender Form · Digital requirement specifications and price form with reference to any annexes. · Completed data processing agreement with annexes. · Censured version of the offer
sig_1a35f66b83334eac618f.title: Electronic substance register

sig_1a7ed3e9d28a3e919c24.description: This is not a procurement notice nor a call for tenders, but a request for information through which Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue is surveying system suppliers to register for a potential tendering procedure. The wellbeing services county is responsible for social welfare, healthcare and rescue services. It is the largest employer in the region, employing approximately 6 000 professionals from various fields. Our vision is to be a pioneering community where services are accessible, the wellbeing of our population is among the best in Finland, and the occupational wellbeing of our employees is high. Our mission is to increase the health, functional capacity and security of our residents throughout their lives. Our values are “Mie turvaan”, “Mie uskallan”, “Mie vastaan” and “Mie välitän”. Strategic priorities include investing in personnel, smooth processes and the gradation of services. The realisation of these requires efficient, safe and user-friendly digital solutions. The roster planning system plays a central role in supporting the smooth flow of everyday operations, the occupational wellbeing of the staff and cost-efficiency. The purpose of the market dialogue is to obtain a comprehensive overview of the roster planning systems and related services available on the market. The information obtained can be used to assess what kinds of solutions exist on the market, what benefits they generate and how they suit the needs of the wellbeing services county. Through the market dialogue, the wellbeing services county aims to: 1. Obtain information on the market offering and various suppliers' solutions 2. Understand the functionalities and key use cases of the systems 3. Explore integration possibilities with existing systems and platforms 4. Assess the implementation of information security and data protection 5. Gain an overview of pricing models and cost structures (no individual tenders) 6. Survey delivery and service models 7. Obtain concrete examples and demos from suppliers to illustrate the suitability of the solutions for the needs of the wellbeing services county. The market dialogue is open to all suppliers that can offer systems or services falling within the scope of this solution package. The focus of the dialogue is on solutions that are already in production or available on the market. Suppliers are requested to present systems and services that are available and where the key functionalities have already been implemented. The presentation of solutions under development or merely at the concept stage is not desired on this occasion. In connection with registration, suppliers are requested to briefly describe: • what ready-made solutions and services they offer • in what kinds of environments the solutions have been deployed (example descriptions, no mandatory references) • the key features of the solution that they wish to present in the market dialogue All participants are offered equal opportunities to obtain information regarding the market dialogue. The dialogue does not bind Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue to initiate a procurement, nor are procurement decisions made on the basis of it. If there is a large number of registered suppliers, the wellbeing services county may hold both a joint information session and a limited number of individual meetings. The market dialogue focuses in particular on how solutions can support the key operations of the wellbeing services county. These are not procurement requirements, but thematic areas intended as a basis for discussion and illustration: • User management and information security • Working hours and shift management • Consideration of collective agreements and local agreements • Competence, qualifications and occupational health management • Usability and multi-user support • Reporting and information-driven management • Integrations with other systems • Mobile usage and employee services • Main administration, maintenance and support services • Intelligence and automation Pricing models and lifecycle services Participating suppliers have the opportunity to illustrate their solutions also through a demo or practical example scenarios. The wellbeing services county will provide a set of questions in advance to guide the discussion and ensure that the presentations of different suppliers can be compared on an equal basis. The market dialogue will be conducted as supplier-specific meetings via remote connection (Teams). The duration of an individual meeting is approximately 60 to 90 minutes. The supplier will have the opportunity to present their solution and its key features. The wellbeing services county will also ask pre-defined questions that support the equality and comparability of the discussion. Meetings will be held on the following days: 21.10., 22.10., 27.10., 28.10. and 29.10.2025. The exact time will be agreed with the registered suppliers based on the order of registration and schedule coordination. The language of potential presentations/meetings is Finnish. Registrations are requested to be sent by 3.10.2025 at 12:00. This request for information / market survey does not request tenders to be submitted nor are tenders given in response to this request for information; it requests ONLY procurement-related information. Participating or refraining from participating in the market survey / request for information does not affect the tenderer's position in any potential tendering procedure. The market dialogue invitation does not bind the respondent (supplier) to participate in the tendering procedure, nor is responding to this notice a precondition for participating in the actual tendering procedure later. Those participating in the market survey have no right to compensation for participation. The contracting authority does not undertake to carry out the procurement in question. Decisions on launching a potential procurement process will be made after the market survey. The submitted material will be handled as confidential in accordance with section 24, subsection 1, point 20 of the Act on the Openness of Government Activities.
sig_1a7ed3e9d28a3e919c24.title: Request for Information/Market Survey: Work shift planning system and related services

sig_1ab06211e4c143eb8191.description: Hereon requires external support for the migration of its SAP ERP system to S/4. The brownfield approach is to be used. This is a technical migration; potential improvements or optimisations will be carried out subsequently, decoupled from the migration. The subject matter of Lot 1 is the provision of comprehensive consultancy services for the planning, execution and documentation of the migration of the existing SAP ERP system to SAP S/4HANA. The services shall be performed in close coordination with the client's specialist departments. The contractor shall assume the following tasks: 3.1. Project planning and design - Preparation of a project schedule and content plan in close coordination with Hereon - Development of a migration concept including test design, definition of responsibilities and accompanying documentation 3.2. System analysis and process evaluation - Review of the existing SAP ERP systems with regard to the S/4HANA migration - Identification and evaluation of correction requirements in the implemented business processes - Communication of correction requirements to the specialist departments and verification of implementation 3.3. Archiving and system preparation - Archiving of FI and MM documents from completed financial years 2014-2019 - Setup of a sandbox system - Execution of necessary system copies from production to test systems 3.4. Migration and customising - Execution of the necessary customising - Execution and testing of the S/4HANA migration on sandbox, test and production systems - Review and adjustment of structural authorisations in connection with the Cross-Application Time Sheet (CATS) - Analysis of existing roles and authorisations in the SAP ERP system as well as evaluation and application of new authorisation objects in the context of S/4HANA - Execution of the H4S4 conversion - Review and migration of the personnel cost commitment processor, ensuring functionality and data integrity in personnel cost planning - Connection of the SAP Enterprise Portal and support for the connection of the above-mentioned non-SAP products 3.5. Documentation and quality assurance - Preparation of audit-compliant final documentation of the migration - Support in the review of non-SAP software - Support during an internal security check (SAP Basis) 3.6. Training and hypercare - Preparation of (delta) training materials - Conducting training sessions for participating employees and key users - Provision of live support (hypercare) after the migration 3.7. Cooperation with the client - All services shall be provided in close coordination with the responsible specialist departments - Tasks that can sensibly be carried out by Hereon itself (e.g. non-SAP software, authorisation roles) shall be processed internally accordingly 3.8. Period and scope - The consultancy service is to be provided over a period from early 2026 to mid-2027.; As part of an ongoing SAP migration project, an external service provider is commissioned with Lot 2 to technically accompany and evaluate the project phases of concept review, test preparation and test execution as well as the final documentation. The objective is quality assurance and risk minimisation in the migration process, as well as ensuring audit-compliant documentation. The contract specifically comprises the following services: 4.1. Review of the migration concept - Analysis of the migration concept for completeness, consistency and feasibility - with a particular focus on ensuring that the planned documentation meets the requirements of an audit - Identification of potential risks and vulnerabilities, particularly with regard to the traceability and audibility of the migration steps - Preparation of an evaluation with recommended actions to ensure audit-compliant documentation 4.2. Support for test preparation and test execution - Advice on the planning and organisation of test activities (e.g. system, integration and acceptance tests) - Support in the definition of test cases and test data so that traceability and audibility for an audit are guaranteed at all times - Quality assurance during test execution with a particular focus on complete and audit-compliant logging - Evaluation of test results and derivation of measures 4.3. Review of the final documentation - Evaluation of project documentation regarding traceability, completeness and conformity with project objectives - Support in the preparation of handover documents so that all necessary evidence for a subsequent audit is available 4.4. Conditions of participation - Demonstrable experience in supporting SAP migration projects - Specialist knowledge of SAP ERP and SAP S/4HANA - Experience in test management and quality assurance - Knowledge of standard project management and IT service management standards (e.g. PRINCE2, ITIL) 4.5. Period and scope The consultancy service is to be provided alongside the project over a period from early 2026 to mid-2027. The exact scope will be agreed upon when the contract is awarded.
sig_1ab06211e4c143eb8191.title: Migration SAP S/4 HANA

sig_1b0fe10a953dcadcf693.description: The currently used consolidation solution SAP SEM-BCS for the preparation of the consolidated accounts (legal consolidation) as well as financial statistics (profit centre consolidation) and the reporting based on this in SAP BW will only be regularly maintained by the manufacturer until 31. December 2027. A chargeable extension of the maintenance period is only possible until the end of 2030. There is therefore a need to introduce a new consolidation solution using SAP, including reporting, and to integrate it unchanged via a standard interface into the financial reporting tool (SAP Disclosure Management). SAP Group Reporting is intended as the successor solution for the preparation of legal consolidation as well as financial statistics (profit centre consolidation). Furthermore, reporting is to be set up with SAP applications available in the Canton. The reports can be evaluated for analysis purposes with the SAP Analytics Cloud add-in for Microsoft Excel, and on the other hand, they are to be integrated into SAP Disclosure Management for the preparation of financial reporting. In addition, the solution includes the optional data migration of historical closing data from the current systems (SAP SEM-BCS, SAP BW). After the replacement of the current solution, it should again be possible to have media-break-free financial reporting. The subject of the submission is the commissioning of a provider who has the necessary professional and technical skills to introduce the new consolidation solution consisting of the components consolidation with SAP Group Reporting, reporting and integration into SAP Disclosure Management (hereinafter referred to as "new consolidation solution") in the Finanzverwaltung. In addition, data migration is to be provided for.
sig_1b0fe10a953dcadcf693.title: New consolidation solution using SAP

sig_1b14d8b0802608b4973d.description: Helse Nord IKT HF (Northern Norway Health ICT Trust) wants to investigate whether there are solutions in the market that can support management of vulnerabilities. Rapid changes in the digital landscape, combined with a continuous more complex threat landscape, require public sector organisations to maintain clear visibility into vulnerabilities across their systems, networks, and applications. Public digital infrastructure is built on intricate systems and interconnected environments that are constantly exposed to cyber risks. A vulnerability management service enables organisations to identify and assess these environments, detect security weaknesses, optimise remediation efforts, and optimise vulnerability management workflows. Conducting regular efforts to detect vulnerabilities reduces the likelihood of data breaches, service disruptions, and other expensive incidents, while supporting a more proactive and structured approach to information security.
sig_1b14d8b0802608b4973d.title: Prior information notice: Vulnerability management for Helse Nord IKT HF

sig_1b6ac88fe119166d1b1b.description: The objective of this procurement is to establish a multi-supplier framework agreement for the provision of software development expertise for the entire VR Group. The framework covers development needs arising across VR Group companies, including but not limited to passenger services, logistics operations, infrastructure-related systems, commercial platforms, customer-facing digital services, and internal operational systems. The procurement covers Web Development (e.g. web based technologies such as modern frontend frameworks and standards). Experts are assigned to VR’s agile development teams, who operate according to VR’s technology choices and established models where VR acts as the Product Owner and oversees overall project and development management. Work is carried out in a hybrid model, both on-site at VR’s premises in Helsinki and remotely in accordance with VR’s working guidelines. The service also includes a Supplier-appointed Service Manager (for reporting, invoicing etc.). In accordance with Section 45(2) of the Act on Procurement in the Utilities Sectors, the maximum total value of contracts awarded under this Framework Agreement during the entire contract period shall be EUR 20 000 000 (VAT 0%). Tenderers are requested to note that the value stated above does not constitute the estimated value of the procurement, but the statutory maximum value as referred to in the Act. The maximum value also includes possible option periods of the procurement. VR Group does not commit to any minimum purchase volumes. Actual resource needs may increase or decrease during the contract period based on business requirements, technological development, and the lifecycle of projects and systems. The initial contract period is two (2) years, after which the Customer may extend the Agreement with four (4) optional periods of one (1) year each. This procurement will be carried out using an open procedure. The Finnish Act on Procurements and Concession Contracts of Entities Operating in the Water and Energy Supply, Transport and Postal Services Sector (Act 1398/2016, “Act on Public Contracts in the Utilities Sector”) applies to this procurement. Tenders must meet all suitability requirements set out in this notice and its appendices. The subject of the procurement is described in more detail in Appendix 2 (Procurement Description) to the Invitation to Tender. The suitability requirements for Tenderers are set out in the ESPD form.

sig_1c0d2bf1cf4e03d6b7b2.description: Background and Objectives of the Pathfinder Project: The Public Sector AI (PSAI) Directorate within the Department of Science, Innovation and Technology (DSIT) exists to help the government make brilliant public services that empower people in the UK. We work at the very centre of government to drive digital transformation focused on user needs and to reimagine how government uses AI to deliver public services and initiatives. The newly established Government Efficiency Accelerator (GEA) programme is a flagship initiative aimed at driving operational efficiencies across some of the government's key enabling functions (Finance, Policy, HR) through the safe and responsible adoption of AI. The GEA is working in collaboration with the GCF Commercial Innovation Hub (CIH) to better understand the availability of AI based solutions that can be used by teams across government departments to drive efficiency and increase productivity. The goal of this Pathfinder Project is to engage with the market to understand current capabilities, initially focusing on three core business areas: Finance, HR and policy (more details on a specific problem area below). Applicants should note that this engagement is not intended to lead to the procurement of a particular solution for DSIT or any other UK Government Department. Rather, we are looking to build a catalogue of tested and "kitemarked" products that will be made available to public sector organisations to consider procuring them in the knowledge that they have been tested and will meet requirements such as security, usability, transparency etc. We are interested in hearing from all types of suppliers and would particularly encourage SMEs and VCSEs to submit proposals. Challenge Summary: As noted above, the GEA and CIH are engaging with the market to build a deeper understanding of how AI based solutions and products can help make government departments more efficient and productive. We appreciate there are a multitude of potential use cases so for this initial engagement we have chosen to focus on problems relating to budgeting and workforce forecasting. We are inviting suppliers to submit proposals outlining how their products could be used by finance teams across UK government departments in a safe, transparent and unbiased way. We are keen to explore solutions which can reduce the level of repetitive tasks required specifically when budgeting and conducting workforce forecasting. Submissions should demonstrate how the solution can streamline tasks, improve accuracy, and shorten time spent on repetitive work in order to free colleagues up to complete higher-value work. There is no fixed scope, as we aim for platform-agnostic, AI driven and innovative tools that adapt to various organisational needs. Solution should be accessible to organisations of all sizes and is not dependent on any specific ERP platform.
sig_1c0d2bf1cf4e03d6b7b2.title: GEA Pathfinder

sig_1ce7e51c86c3539cc86c.description: This is not a procurement notice or a call for tenders, but an information request with which Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue is surveying comprehensive digital solutions for the administration and implementation of surrogate payment for the personal assistance employer model, as well as the management of informal care, foster care and other fee-based contracts, and the payment of fees, other expenses, etc., and statutory official contributions. The aim of the survey is to find out what kind of comprehensive solutions containing the functionalities described below are available on the Finnish market. Through the market dialogue, the wellbeing services county aims to: 1. Obtain information on market supply and different suppliers' solutions 2. Potential implementation of integrations into various platforms or systems 3. Assess the implementation of information security and data protection 4. Obtain an overview of pricing models and cost structures (no individual tenders) 5. Survey delivery and service models The market dialogue is open to all suppliers that can offer comprehensive solutions falling within the scope of this solution package. The dialogue will focus on solutions that are already in production. Suppliers are requested to present services that are available and in which the key functionalities have already been implemented. The presentation of solutions under development or merely at the conceptual stage is not desired on this occasion. When registering, suppliers are requested to briefly describe: Intended use and environment The system must be suitable for use by the wellbeing services county to manage the following service forms: - Informal care support and contract management - Foster care assignment contracts - Surrogate payment for the personal assistance employer model - Management of contracts for support families and support persons - Other similar contractual relationships User groups are: - Wellbeing services county employees (contract management) - Informal and foster carers (data entry) - Personal assistants and their employers - Other persons in a contractual relationship Key functionalities Contract management: - Electronic drafting and maintenance of assignment contracts - Contract lifecycle management - Recording of care days and working hours - Management of statutory leave Fee and salary processing: - Calculation of fees in accordance with care intensity categories - Payroll processing for personal assistants - Statutory payments and deductions - Processing of substitute carers' fees - Automatic inclusion of index adjustments Payment transmission: - Payment transmission operations approved by the Financial Supervisory Authority - Automatic payment processing - Generation of payment data files Integrations: - Direct data transmission connection to the Tax Administration - Possibility of integration into the wellbeing services county's other systems, particularly an interface to the accounting system - Data export and reporting (Data lake) - User account management via Entra ID Technical requirements - Cloud-based SaaS solution - Information security-audited system - Finnish-language user interface - Implementation in accordance with the Accessibility Directive - Continuous maintenance and updates - User support in Finnish We kindly ask you to answer the following questions: General description of the solution - Do you offer a system solution containing the functionalities described above? - What is the name of your solution and a short description? - What are the key strengths of your solution? Functionalities - How does your solution meet the described contract management needs? - What kind of fee and salary calculation features does the system include? - Does your solution have a licence from the Financial Supervisory Authority for payment transmission? - How is the Tax Administration integration implemented? Technical features - What is the technical architecture of the solution? - How is information security ensured? - What language options does the system support? Experience and references - In which wellbeing services counties / municipalities is your solution in use? - How many users does the system have? - Can you provide reference information on similar deliveries? Additional information - What other essential features does your solution include? - How is the system implementation typically carried out? - What kind of support and training do you offer? Responses to the questions are requested to be sent by 1.12.2025 at 15:00. Responses should be brief and informative. Responses are requested to be sent to the address hankinnat@ekhva.fi. Subject of the message: "Markkinakartoitus - omais- ja perhehoidon sekä henkilökohtaisen avun hallintajärjestelmästä ja ym. palkkioperusteisten sopimusten hallinta ja maksatus" This information request / market survey does not request tenders to be submitted, nor are tenders submitted in response to it; it requests ONLY procurement-related information. Participation or non-participation in the market survey does not affect a tenderer's position in a potential tendering procedure. The market dialogue invitation does not bind the respondent (Supplier) to participate in a tendering procedure, and answering this notice is not a prerequisite for participating in the actual tendering procedure at a later stage. Participants in the market survey shall not be entitled to compensation for participation. The contracting authority does not commit to carrying out the procurement in question. Decisions on launching a potential procurement process will be made after the market survey. The supplied material will be treated as confidential in accordance with section 24, subsection 1, point 20 of the Act on the Openness of Government Activities. Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue thanks you in advance for your responses. They are valuable in defining our system needs and preparing for a potential procurement.
