The Fraport AG Frankfurt Airport Services Worldwide ("Fraport") operates Frankfurt/Main Airport and, in addition, alone or together with third parties, several other airports, terminals and service companies worldwide. The subject matter of this procurement is the following services: -Software & system integration -Fuel dispenser procurement & integration (operational filling station, public filling station, mobile refuelling services) -IT security & operations -Training and documentation -System tests & quality assurance -User & rights management The subject matter of this tender is the supply, installation, commissioning and integration of a modern hardware and software solution for stationary and mobile fuel supply at Frankfurt Airport. The service comprises the equipment of several stationary refuelling systems - consisting of fuel dispensing systems, fuel containers and a staff filling station - with new hardware and software including all necessary components for controlling, monitoring and processing refuelling operations. In addition, the corresponding hardware and software technology is to be provided for five mobile refuelling vehicles to ensure continuous mobile refuelling at Frankfurt Airport. The solution offered must enable the operation of the stationary and mobile refuelling infrastructure in an integrated overall system. In addition, the necessary interfaces for data collection, administration and evaluation of the refuelling operations must be provided.

sig_1d3ac604a526b988e9fa.description: By the present procurement procedure, the EIT KIC Urban Mobility S.L. hereby being referred to as “EIT UM” or the “Company” is aiming to identify a provider (hereinafter, referred to as “Provider”) to support the Digital Platform for EIT Urban Mobility community, presently known as “Mobility Innovators”. This document, along with its annexes, constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) issued by EIT Urban Mobility for a potential procurement of services in the field of online communities. EIT Urban Mobility community is made of over 270 partners and larger ecosystem of more than 1,200 stakeholders as we work together to make the transition to more sustainable urban mobility and liveable urban spaces. This community includes industry, including large enterprises, SMEs, and startups, universities and education institutions; students and alumni; research and technology organisations; governments at local, regional, national and EU-level; and non-governmental organisations (NGOs). Two years ago, EIT Urban Mobility launched its private digital community platform, Mobility Innovators, which brings together our vibrant community of innovators described above. The platform already has more than 1,500 active users and serves as the central platform for collaboration and engagement within our community. Mobility Innovators enables partners and stakeholders to access information, documents and opportunities shared by EIT Urban Mobility, register for events, and engage in discussions with peers across sectors. It connects organisations from industry, research, academia, and the public sector, fostering collaboration to advance the transition towards more sustainable and liveable urban mobility. Our goal in this next phase is to further grow and activate the community, expand platform functionalities, and enhance user experience to ensure Mobility Innovators continues to support EIT Urban Mobility’s role as Europe’s leading innovation community for urban mobility.
sig_1d3ac604a526b988e9fa.title: Rfp Digital & Private Platform for EIT Urban Mobility Community - “Mobility Innovators”, 26-28

sig_1e36e4da8b700c63d492.description: South of Scotland Enterprise (SOSE) are notifying the market of a potential market opportunity for a supplier to deliver a fully managed, end-to-end IT service for the Mountainbike Innovation Centre (MTBIC) facility. This is to include the design, supply, installation, configuration, and ongoing support and operation of all IT equipment, network infrastructure, and associated services. Lot 1: . South of Scotland Enterprise (SOSE) are notifying the market of a potential market opportunity for a supplier to deliver a fully managed, end-to-end IT service for the Mountainbike Innovation Centre (MTBIC) facility. This is to include the design, supply, installation, configuration, and ongoing support and operation of all IT equipment, network infrastructure, and associated services. The MTBIC is a new build, being built in partnership with Hub South East. Morrisons are the main contractor. The appointed supplier will need to source, provide and install all required equipment per an IT matrix that has been produced and will be issued as part of the tender documentation. They will also need to provide a managed service provision to the tenants and SOSE within the building. Key requirements will likely include but will not be limited to: - Full Wi-Fi network, both internal and external - EDUROM Network - Ability for segregation of network to tenants - Ability to link into fire alarm and CCTV systems where appropriate - Managed service provision - Ability to live stream from the building - Potential for 100 concurrent users at select times - IT security compliant with relevant statutory requirements - Managed and maintained equipment - Service desk provision SOSE will require a comprehensive service, from inception to completion. The MTBIC is a brand new building, and the contractor will provide the cable routes and CAT install but SOSE is required to undertake all other aspects. Any infrastructure required e.g. WAPs, cabinets will need to be costed and provided for as part of this tender. SOSE will not be seeking discrete components or partial delivery — the requirement is for a single, fully managed service covering all IT and network requirements for the building. The purpose of the MTBIC is to provide workshop space to companies interested in developing new and exciting technology, hot desk space and office space, events space both internal and external. This is to be a hub out of which businesses will operate.
sig_1e36e4da8b700c63d492.title: Fully managed IT service for the Mountainbike Innovation Centre (MTBIC), Innerleithen

sig_1ee047eb41c952cf8874.description: In the field of road safety, the Safe System approach, recognised internationally and included in the “European Union Road Safety Policy 2021-2030” and the European Commission’s “Strategic Action Plan on Road Safety”, suggests acquiring greater knowledge about the different variables that influence road accidents —beyond the usual indicators, such as the number of accidents, deaths and serious injuries—, recommending the acquisition of other indicators, called Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), directly related to the prevention of deaths and injuries in traffic accidents. Among these indicators are the use of seat belts and child restraint systems, the use of helmets, vehicles travelling within the speed limit, drivers travelling within the legal blood alcohol limit, driver distractions and vehicle safety. These indicators constitute the object of this tender. The object of this lot is the design of a sampling plan for lots 2 and 3 and for the alcohol indicator and EDAP Study, obtaining the KPIs (except for KPI 6, whose calculation work remains within the scope of lot 4), and preparation of the dashboard.; The objective of lot 2 consists of carrying out measurements of speed and other characteristics of vehicle flow in a sample of 150 sections of the Spanish road network, in order to serve as a basis for the preparation and acquisition of the KPI 1 indicator; Carrying out fieldwork for the collection of data on the use of seat belts, child restraint systems (CRS), helmets and driving using mobile devices, by conducting non-participatory surveys in a sample of urban and interurban road sections, which allow the successful bidder of lot 1 to obtain these indicators (KPI 2, 3 and 5).; The object of this lot is the acquisition of the vehicle safety indicator (KPI 6).; The object of this lot is the management and supervision of the work of lots 1,2,3 and 4.
sig_1ee047eb41c952cf8874.title: Service for the preparation of reports on key performance indicators in road safety. 5 lots.

sig_1f546ffb36a174b5d647.description: To ensure efficient, secure and appropriate use of social media, Myndigheten för civilt försvar (the Authority) needs appropriate tools that support planning, publication, coordination, monitoring and analysis of communication efforts. The requested tool must comply with the Authority's social media strategy, i.e., it must prioritise presence in the social media channels that are largest in Sweden. The presence in social media must function as an extended arm of the Authority's social media, in addition to the channels in which the Authority otherwise operates (websites, apps, tools/services, etc.). Through this, the tool must ensure that the Authority can: - Promote dialogue and participation with the target group and thereby reduce the distance between the Authority and its target groups. - Take part in discussions, views and comments as part of the Authority's horizon scanning. - Reach out to target groups that the Authority otherwise finds difficult to reach in other channels. - Be present where the target groups expect the Authority to be. - Manage and answer comments in the social media channels where they are made. - Increase awareness of the Authority's operations. - Maintain and increase trust in the Authority as a government agency. - Drive traffic to the Authority's own channels.

sig_1f78a83939231b7ec8b5.description: Award of services for the implementation of the Frankfurt Founders' Fund. We are looking for a contractor to take over the central management of the Frankfurt Founders' Fund and the numerous associated tasks. Background: The Founders' Fund, operated by Wirtschaftsförderung Frankfurt on behalf of the City of Frankfurt, has been a cornerstone of Frankfurt's start-up support since its introduction in 2010. The Frankfurt Founders' Fund has since established itself and is now an integral part of the start-up activities of the City of Frankfurt am Main, Wirtschaftsförderung Frankfurt and the Frankfurt-Rhine-Main ecosystem. In 2009, the foundation stone for the Frankfurt Founders' Fund was laid. The microfinance study commissioned at that time revealed that young companies were facing a financing gap for credit requirements. On this basis, the Frankfurt Founders' Fund was launched. The Frankfurt Founders' Fund project is currently being operated by an external contractor (hereinafter referred to as the Contractor) and is the responsibility of Wirtschaftsförderung Frankfurt GmbH as the contracting authority (hereinafter referred to as the Contracting Authority). In addition, professional administration is necessary to ensure transparency, efficiency and sustainability. The Contractor, who is commissioned with the administration and implementation of the fund, must therefore have sound experience in the field of start-up financing, project and portfolio management and, ideally, in working with public institutions. Furthermore, knowledge of risk management, supporting founders and developing suitable monitoring and evaluation instruments is required. The Contractor will work closely with the Bürgschaftsbank Hessen and partner banks and offer founders a proven financing and coaching model. An essential part of the success model is not just the financial support for start-ups, for which Wirtschaftsförderung Frankfurt assumes 80 % of the guarantee, but also extensive support included in the Founders' Fund programme in the form of coaching by the Contractor throughout the entire loan term. In summary, the Contracting Authority expects the following services from the new Contractor: - Organisational services - Information and enquiry management - Review and processing of financing enquiries - Support/accompaniment of financing projects - Measures for loan defaults, early warning system - Debt collection and processing - Reporting and monitoring - Marketing/communication - Cooperation and community network maintenance
sig_1f78a83939231b7ec8b5.title: Frankfurt Founders' Fund

Analysis and independent quality assurance The contractor analyses and understands the project documentation of the digital transformation programme. The contractor acquires high-level knowledge of the offered and/or selected solutions and the suppliers' implementation approach. Support for project management and programme control The contractor acts as an independent sounding board for the project management and those responsible for change management. The contractor supports the preparation, assessment and validation of project deliverables, including implementation plans, communication and adoption plans, process documentation, functional analyses and other project-related documentation. In addition, the contractor supports the monitoring of the alignment between project objectives, programme objectives and the decisions of the steering committee. 3. Independent assessment of supplier proposals The contractor carries out a critical and independent assessment of proposed solution directions, design choices, working methods and implementation proposals from suppliers. The contractor supports the client in carrying out fit-gap analyses and ensures that processes are aligned where possible with the capabilities of the selected platforms, without unnecessarily reproducing existing working methods one-to-one. The contractor advises on price, quality and risk aspects of proposed solutions and supports the client in decision-making. 5. Neutral advice and mediation The contractor acts as an independent and neutral advisor in substantive discussions or disagreements between involved suppliers, project teams and stakeholders. The contractor formulates objective recommendations from the perspective of the client's interests and supports decision-making based on facts, risk analyses and programme objectives. 6. Support for organisational change The contractor supports the organisation in managing the impact of the changes and contributes to a feasible and supported implementation approach. In this, particular attention is paid to phasing, change readiness, support, adoption and the operational burden on employees, so that the continuity of care and support processes is maximally safeguarded. 7. Knowledge transfer and strengthening of internal capacity The contractor actively contributes to knowledge building within the organisation. The contractor supports internal key users, project staff and involved teams through knowledge sharing, coaching and documentation, with the aim of strengthening internal expertise and gradually reducing dependence on external parties. The final responsibility, direction and decision-making always remain with the client. 8. Reporting and support for decision-making The contractor reports periodically on progress, risks, dependencies, bottlenecks and recommendations. The contractor supports the preparation of decision documents for the steering committee and substantiates proposals regarding prioritisation, phasing, risk management and programme steering. 9. Independent implementation guidance (optional) The contractor supports the client during the implementation phase of the selected solutions and monitors the quality, feasibility and coherence of the implementation approach. The contractor critically assesses the implementation plans, proposed configurations, migration strategies, test approaches, training plans and commissioning processes of the suppliers. In doing so, the contractor ensures that choices made align with the strategic objectives, architectural principles and operational needs of the client. The contractor supports the project teams in identifying and following up on risks, dependencies and bottlenecks during the execution of the implementation. He or she does not take over operational responsibility from the suppliers, but acts as an independent quality monitor and advisor. The contractor also supports the preparation and follow-up of workshops, design discussions, test activities, data migrations and commissioning, and ensures that the agreed scope, quality requirements and project objectives are realised. The contractor ensures that the implementation leads to sustainable process improvement and that standard functionalities are utilised to the maximum, unless deviations are demonstrably necessary for the client's operations. 10. sig_200ce3d85d4db0a3975c.description: Description of the Project: Local Governance Reform Programme (LGRP) III The "Multi-Donor Action (EU-BMZ) - Strengthening Capacities and Institutional Readiness of Reform Actors in Palestine" co-financed by the European Union (EU) and the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and implemented by Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH, aims to enhance the institutional capacity, operational effectiveness, and coordination functions of MoFP and PMO ERO as leading entities in national planning and reform management. The Action will support MoFP in its role as the central coordinating body for national planning by enhancing its capacity to embed data-driven policymaking, ensure coherent approaches across line ministries, and improve coordination across all levels of governance. The Palestinian Authority (PA) faces significant institutional and technical challenges in managing, measuring, and demonstrating public sector performance. Monitoring and evaluation (M&E) functions across line ministries and agencies (LMAs) are narrowly defined, fragmented, and largely disconnected from planning and budgeting decisions. Indicators are poorly formulated, feeder data is weak and uncoordinated, and M&E reporting serves administrative compliance rather than evidence-based management. The Strategic Results Framework (SRF), which is the principal instrument for measuring national results delivery, lacks a usable structure, theory of change, and coherent indicator set. No overarching national M&E strategy exists, and data management responsibilities across government institutions remain undefined and unanchored. Lot LOT-0001: 10037895-Development of a National M&E System in Palestine. Description of Work and Services to be Provided: structured around eight work packages (WPs) covering the full cycle from system design through operationalization, capacity development, and digital enablement. WP1: Inception, Alignment, and Mobilization. It establishes the analytical and operational foundation for the assignment. The contractor reviews and consolidates the OECD/Sigma diagnostic findings, conducts targeted design assessments to collect operational information required for subsequent WPs, including data feasibility mapping, institutional baseline mapping, planning-budgeting process validation, pilot site readiness assessment, and a digital systems inventory. The contractor establishes the governance and coordination arrangements, detailed workplan, stakeholder engagement plan, and risk register. The primary deliverable is a comprehensive Inception Report. WP2: National M&E System Framework and Governance. It produces the foundational design of the national M&E system, developed jointly with MoFP and key government stakeholders rather than as an externally designed product. It defines the system"s purpose, scope, institutional roles, governance mechanisms, core M&E processes, data governance principles, integration logic with planning and budgeting, evaluation framework, and system stewardship mandate. The deliverable is a government-endorsed National M&E Framework. WP3: Results and Measurement Architecture. It redesigns the Strategic Results Framework using a methodology-first, pilot-based approach that accounts for the current limitations of the national development plan. The contractor develops a comprehensive SRF methodology and standards framework designed for the next national planning cycle, conducts a participatory results clarification exercise with a pilot of sectors, and produces a transitional indicator set for the remaining current planning cycle to enable piloting. Deliverables include the revised SRF Methodology Document and the Updated SRF and Indicator Framework. WP4: Institutional and Functional Design. It defines the organizational arrangements required to anchor M&E and data management as permanent government functions. Through a participatory process with MoFP and LMAs, the contractor develops functional design models, organizational options with feasibility assessments against General Personnel Council (GCP) civil service frameworks, RACI matrices, workflow systems, and HR alignment proposals. The deliverable is an Institutional and Functional Design Report. WP5: Integration with Planning, Budgeting, and Oversight. It defines how M&E information can flow into and influences core government decision-making processes, including annual planning, budget preparation, and performance oversight at CoM level. The contractor maps actual planning and budgeting processes, assesses linkage feasibility, designs standard decision-informing M&E products, and proposes integration mechanisms. Deliverables include M&E Integration Framework and Updated Planning and Budgeting Guidance Notes. WP6: Operationalization and Piloting. It translates the system design into operational reality through co-developed SOPs, data collection instruments, reporting templates, and interim digital tools, tested with 3-5 pilot LMAs selected on the basis of a readiness assessment conducted in WP1. The pilot tests real workflows and data flows, generating feedback that is incorporated into system refinements. The deliverable is a Pilot Implementation Report. WP7: Capacity Development, Change Management, and Sustainability. It builds the professional and institutional capacities required for sustained system operation. The contractor develops competency frameworks, training programs, and materials; delivers training in two waves; designs and initiates change management and communication strategies; proposes institutionalization and incentive mechanisms in coordination with GPC; and, importantly, builds system stewardship capacity enabling MoFP and LMAs to maintain, update, and evolve the system independently after assignment conclusion. Deliverables include the Capacity Development and Change Management Strategy, Competency Frameworks and Training Roadmap, Training Modules and Materials, System Stewardship Package, and System Handover and Transition Protocol. WP8: Digital Enablement Design and Procurement-Ready Specifications. It produces the complete technical basis for procuring a digital M&E platform. The contractor defines functional requirements, designs the data architecture and interoperability framework, conducts a technology options assessment including AI and emerging technology analysis, designs a public results portal concept, and produces a vendor-neutral technical and procurement specifications package.

sig_22950ad748b46de96910.description: Forsvarsministeriets Materiel- og Indkøbsstyrelse (”FMI) wishes to enter into a contract regarding the delivery, operation, maintenance, support and further development of an internet-based booking system for the Danish Defence's pool vehicles. The existing system is intended to be replaced by a more modern, reliable and user-friendly solution that supports efficient booking, lending and return of pool vehicles as well as providing FMI with access to relevant operational and administrative data. The purpose of the contract is to ensure the Danish Defence a comprehensive solution that, with a minimum of resource consumption from FMI, enables secure, flexible and efficient management of pool vehicles across the organisation. The solution must support both open and closed vehicle pools, be able to handle a large number of users and vehicles, and contribute to high availability and continuity in the Danish Defence's transport solutions. The contract comprises the supplier's delivery, operation, maintenance, support and further development of the overall system, including both the application and the infrastructure necessary therefor, for use by the Danish Defence's pool vehicles, as well as the delivery, installation and operation of electronic car-sharing equipment in the vehicles. The contract includes a start-up period consisting of a development period and an implementation period, during which the system is adapted, developed and commissioned in accordance with FMI's requirements. The supplier is responsible for the delivery of the application and for the infrastructure necessary therefor, including hosting the system on servers located in Denmark. The system is delivered as an internet-based solution (SaaS), and the supplier is responsible for all operation of the underlying infrastructure. The supplier is responsible for the integration of existing data regarding users, pools, pool vehicles and bookings, as well as for any reuse of already installed electronic car-sharing equipment. The system must support self-service access for users, comprehensive administration and reporting functions for FMI, as well as technical support and a round-the-clock manned helpdesk. The contract runs for 72 months from signature. The contract may be extended on the same terms by up to 2 times 24 months. It is a requirement that the development period must have a maximum duration of 6 months and that the implementation period must have a maximum duration of 6 months. The current system handles approx. 25.000 users and 2.800 pool vehicles. During the contract period, the solution is as a starting point expected to be able to handle up to approx. 5.000 pool vehicles. In view of the uncertain international security policy situation, however, the Danish Defence has a need for an option to be able to scale the solution so that the application and the associated infrastructure can, upon the customer's request, be expanded to handle up to 10.000 pool vehicles without impairment of functionality, response times, availability or the other requirements and service levels set out in the contract. In addition, the contract includes an option regarding the choice of access technology for the pool vehicles, whereby the customer, instead of using the Danish Defence's existing access carriers (RFID etc.), can choose an access and locking system supplied by the supplier on the terms set out in the requirements specification and the contract.
sig_22950ad748b46de96910.title: Tender for a contract regarding the supply, operation, maintenance, support, and further development of an internet-based booking system for the Danish Defence's pool vehicles

sig_22ef79c3fb93659935ec.description: In order to protect Statens IT (Ordering Party) against current and future cyber threats, the Ordering Party uses a number of security technologies, including an Extended Detection and Response (XDR) platform. The XDR platform supports the collection, correlation and analysis of security-related incidents across the Ordering Party's IT environment in order to protect systems, services and data, as well as to ensure the confidentiality, integrity and availability of the data. In view of this, the Ordering Party is tendering a contract whose purpose is to support and strengthen the Ordering Party's own operational IT security through the provision of a Managed Detection and Response (MDR) service from a Security Operations Center (SOC). The MDR service must use and supplement the Ordering Party's XDR platform with round-the-clock monitoring, analysis, detection, validation, escalation and handling of security incidents. The service must be delivered 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, and contribute to the rapid identification, assessment and handling of cyber threats and security incidents. The services constitute an essential element in the Ordering Party's ongoing maturation and development process in the field of cybersecurity with a focus on technology, processes, competencies and collaboration across internal and external stakeholders. Through the procurement, the Ordering Party wishes to gain access to a professional MDR service that can meet the Ordering Party's high demands for quality, robustness and efficiency, as well as a supplier that can continuously engage in dialogue with the Ordering Party on developments within cybersecurity, including the threat picture, technological opportunities, automation, competence development and ongoing improvements to the security level. The supplier must carry out a technical, organisational and procedural Transition In, which ensures that the ongoing MDR services can be delivered from the transition to the operational phase. The Ordering Party draws attention to the fact that the Ordering Party has concluded a contract with two (2) suppliers to handle the Ordering Party's existing XDR platform, with whom the supplier must cooperate in connection with Transition In. As part of this, the supplier must establish and configure the necessary integrations between the Ordering Party's XDR platform and other relevant security sources, as well as the supplier's tools and platforms used for the fulfilment of the contract. The supplier must deliver Ongoing MDR Services; including continuous monitoring, analysis, correlation, validation and detection of alarms and security incidents. The supplier must carry out triage and qualification of alarms in order to identify actual security incidents and ensure timely escalation and notification in accordance with agreed processes and service levels. These ongoing MDR services include: • Continuous SOC monitoring of security-related incidents and alarms. • Analysis, correlation and qualification of incidents across relevant data sources. • Identification, detection and validation of security incidents. • Preparation, implementation and ongoing optimisation of detection rules, use cases and analysis models. • Application of relevant Threat Intelligence to support the detection and analysis work. • Ongoing assessment of the threat picture and its relevance to the Ordering Party's environment. • Proactive identification of potential security incidents and security risks, including through Threat Hunting activities. • Escalation, notification and reporting of security incidents in accordance with agreed processes and service levels. • Maintenance of existing integrations and establishment of new integrations as needed. • Optimisation and further development of the Ordering Party's XDR platform and other security solutions. • Advice regarding the development and maturation of the Ordering Party's security organisation, security processes and governance. • Execution of targeted Threat Hunting courses and analyses of suspicious activities. • Incident Response assistance in the event of security incidents upon requisition from the Ordering Party, including analysis, delimitation, handling, remediation and recovery. • Assistance during major security incidents, cyber crises and coordination with relevant stakeholders. • Security-related advice and strategic sparring on developments within cybersecurity. The contract also includes cross-cutting services, including documentation, reporting, governance, quality assurance and information security, which are delivered throughout the contract period. Furthermore, the contract includes obligations upon contract termination (Transition Out), which must ensure a controlled, secure and documented transfer of knowledge, data, processes, integrations and other contract-related deliverables to the Ordering Party or a subsequent supplier.

sig_2366bcd26f0a92db294b.description: HUS (hereinafter also referred to as the Contracting Authority or Client) requests to participate in the procurement of imaging solution and related services. The procurement will be carried out through a competitive dialogue procedure (see Annex 1 Description of the Procedure). The object of the procurement is imaging solution and related services. This procurement concerns the Picture Archiving and Communication System (PACS), which is intended to be replaced with a new solution. The solution entity may also include functionalities of a Radiology Information System (RIS), an artificial intelligence (AI) platform designed to support the achievement of the objectives, and functionalities related to appointment booking/scheduling, as well as a speech recognition solution. The objective is to ensure that the service path between appointment booking system, the radiological information system (RIS), and the picture archiving and communication system (PACS) operates optimally. The aim is to develop customer experience based on a unified service model. The objective is to provide patients with more efficient diagnostics and good care also in the future. In addition, the objective is to reduce the manual and overlapping work. The imaging solution must enable smooth workflows for all user groups and support the development of processes to improve productivity. The deployment project may include the migration of images, image metadata, and RIS data from the Client’s current PACS system. The service includes support and maintenance activities and may also include 1 level support provided by the Supplier. The objective is also to explore solutions for scalability regarding a joint archiving solution for digital pathology and imaging. A more detailed description of the current state, the solution to be procured, and the services included in the procurement can be found in Annex 2 Current and target state description of imaging systems. Please also take into account the other annexes to the request to participate (Annexes 2.1–2.6, and 4), which provide additional information on the current and target state. These annexes are not binding on the Contracting Authority in the later stages of the procurement procedure and may be subject to change during the negotiations. If the documents have been drawn up in both Finnish and English, in the event of conflict of interpretation, the Finnish text shall prevail. The request for participation, along with all related documentation and any clarifying questions, must be submitted in Finnish or English in accordance with the instructions provided in the request to participate. sig_23789b5d84af3c7a2046.description: SKI hereby offers a dynamic purchasing system (hereinafter the System) regarding the procurement of servers and storage. It is voluntary for all of SKI's customers, as listed in Annex B Customer List, to make use of the System when they need to procure servers and storage. The System comprises two procurement categories: • Category 1 Supplementary purchases • Category 2 Solution purchases The content of the categories is described in more detail in Annex C The System's subject matter. The System's subject matter, as defined via the product and service areas, cf. Annex C, is identical in both categories, which means that the same products and services can be procured in both category 1 and category 2. The categories differ by the nature of the need that a specific procurement must meet, and thus not necessarily by the subject of the procurement as such. Category 1 must be used when a Customer has a specific need to supplement or expand their existing solution. Category 2 must be used when a Customer has a need to procure a new overall solution that is not based on an existing installation. Category 1 must be used when a Customer has a specific need to supplement or expand their existing solution. If there is already an established solution, and the procurement must be adapted to this both functionally and technically, the need falls under category 1. It includes components or units that must function together with the existing solution, without changes occurring in the solution's overall architecture. This may, for example, be the purchase of more CPUs or more storage capacity of a technology that the Customer already has. Similarly for network equipment, where there may, for example, be the establishment of rack capacity, cooling, emergency power, licences, etc.; Category 2 must be used when a Customer has a need to procure a new overall solution that is not based on an existing installation. This applies to both simple and complex solutions, including the establishment of a data centre solution, regardless of whether the solution subsequently must function together with or be integrated into one or more existing solutions, and where the tenderer must design, describe and deliver the full solution. This may, for example, be an overall expansion of a data centre's capacity or an overall purchase to support a new specific task in the data centre, e.g. a particularly heavy calculation task (weather models) or a task that requires a special technology (e.g. AI, which requires large GPU capacity).

sig_23e920630a744f4942a8.description:
SKI hereby establishes a dynamic purchasing system for standard software and related services (02.06 Standard Software). The system comprises two purchasing categories: Category 1 – Simple Solution and Category 2 – Complex Solution. The system may be used to procure the following service areas: 1) Standard Software 2) Support and maintenance agreements 3) Installation/implementation and/or configuration 4) Training 5) Consultancy Standard software is defined as software that is prefabricated and commercially available. Standard software is also referred to as COTS (Commercial Off The Shelf). A more detailed definition of the nature of the software is set out in Appendix C, which also includes a more detailed description of the 5 service areas. All 5 service areas may be procured in both categories. The difference between the two categories lies in a differentiation in the customer's need for tenders for the solution. Category 1 is used when the customer has a precisely specified purchasing need / standard purchase, where the customer has defined the solution prior to the purchase and solely wishes to receive tenders for this solution from suppliers. The customer evaluates solely on price, cf. point 14.1 of the tendering conditions. Category 2 is used for specialised and complex solution purchases, where the customer has a need for the supplier to define the solution based on the customer's described needs, and where a need thereby arises to evaluate the quality of the suppliers' various offered solutions. In Category 2, evaluation is based on both price and the suppliers' offered solutions (quality), cf. point 14.2 of the tendering conditions. In both categories of the system, standard software and related services, as delimited by the 5 service areas above, may be procured within the following functional areas: 1. Applications - 1 Customer Experience and Relationship Management (CRM) - 2 Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) - 3 Supply Chain Management (SCM) - 4 Project and Portfolio Management - 5 E-mail and Authoring - 6 Content Services - 7 Other Application Software 2. Application Platforms - 1 Application Infrastructure and Middleware - 2 Data Management - 3 Analytics and Business Intelligence 3. Infrastructure Software - 1 Operating Systems - 2 Storage Management - 3 Virtualization Infrastructure - 4 Other Infrastructure Software 4. Development and Operations Tools - 1 Application Development - 2 IT Operations 5. IT Security Software - 1 Security Appendix D, Overview of functional standard software areas, describes in more detail which functional areas of software and services linked to these functional standard software areas are included in the service areas 1-5. It is voluntary for all SKI customers, as shown in the published customer list, to make use of the System when they are to procure standard software or related services. The customer list in Appendix B.1 specifies the customers and their organisations that are customers of SKI at the time of tender and can thus use the system. However, the dynamic purchasing system may, throughout the term of the system, be used by all contracting authorities that are customers of SKI at the time of publication of a specific purchase in the system. All parts of the Danish state, regions and municipalities – including public companies and publicly owned companies subject to the obligation to tender as a result of their public ownership – can become customers of SKI by taking out a subscription covering their organisation. When new contracting authorities become customers of SKI, SKI will update the customer list on SKI.dk and announce on SKI.dk that a change has been made to SKI's customer list, as well as which contracting authorities are new customers of SKI and from what date these can publish purchases in the system. The customer list in Appendix B.1 is not updated after the time of tender. Instead, SKI's customer list valid at any given time will be publicly available on SKI.dk. Special attention is drawn to the fact that KL and the Ministry of Finance in the "Agreement on municipal finances for 2026" have agreed that 4-5 inter-municipal IT service organisations are to be established, which are to handle various tasks and establish solutions in the IT field for the participating municipalities. It appears from the agreement: "There is [...] agreement that the municipalities will, no later than d. 1. January 2027, establish themselves in new inter-municipal partnerships in the form of 4-5 municipal IT service organisations with a geographical starting point in the four regions. The new IT service organisations will be established as municipal units and will before the end of 2027 take over the municipalities' operation of server and network infrastructure. The parties have a shared ambition that the units will subsequently also gradually take over the operation of user management and monitoring, PCs and other end-user equipment as well as service desk and support leading up to 2030 and will continuously discuss the progress of the work." These inter-municipal IT service organisations are to be considered customers of SKI from the time they are established as an independent legal entity and will thereafter be able to use the system for specific purchases published in the system after their establishment. At the time of tender, the inter-municipal IT service organisations appear in Appendix B.1 Customer List with the designations [It-Service Nord], [It-Service Midt], [It-Service Syd], [It-Service Øst] and [It-Service Hovedstaden]. These designations will be updated according to the process stated in the foregoing when the units have been established. Whether 4 or 5 IT service organisations are established does not affect the fact that the total group of participants across the IT service organisations, i.e. the municipalities, is the same. Like all the other customers in the system, the inter-municipal IT service organisations have a right – but not an obligation – to use the system. Category 1 - Simple Solution Is used when the customer has a precisely specified purchasing need / standard purchase, where the customer has defined the solution prior to the purchase and solely wishes to receive tenders for this solution from suppliers.;

Category 2 – Complex Solution Is used for specialised and complex solution purchases, where the customer has a need for the supplier to define the solution based on the customer's described needs, and where a need thereby arises to evaluate the quality of the suppliers' various offered solutions.

sig_2453dc705bb5a4bd32f4.description: The Urban Environment Division of the City of Helsinki (hereinafter "Contracting Authority") is requesting requests to participate in a dynamic purchasing system (DPS) to be established for the procurement of digital twin platforms. The Contracting Authority uses digital twin services to make official operations and citizens' participation more efficient. Digital twin platforms are used in use-case-specific pilot projects of agile development in the Urban Environment as well as in production solutions. The platforms are intended to be able to combine and visualise data from various sources, such as e.g. city information model data, building and infrastructure information models, point cloud data and basic data of the built environment. The objective is to utilise the industry's best platforms and resources in creating services. Digital twin services are being developed for internal use in the urban environment for stakeholders, for official use, and for citizens. Some of the services will probably contain confidential official information and will only be accessible by authorities, which must be taken into account in their implementation. This contract notice establishes a dynamic purchasing system. The dynamic purchasing system is in two stages. In the first stage, service providers apply to join the purchasing system by submitting a request to participate. All candidates fulfilling the suitability requirements will be admitted to the dynamic purchasing system. In the second stage, the contracting authority makes procurements as procurements internal to the established dynamic purchasing system and selects, on the basis of the internal competition, the platform solution best suited to each use case. Admission to the dynamic purchasing system is not binding on the candidate. The candidate may choose which competitions organised within the system it participates in. Requests to participate may be submitted to the dynamic purchasing system throughout its duration. The dynamic purchasing system is valid for eight (8) years. The content of the dynamic purchasing system and the implementation of procurements are described in more detail in the appendix documents. The estimated value of the dynamic purchasing system is a total of approximately 2,3 million euros.
sig_2453dc705bb5a4bd32f4.title: Dynamic purchasing system (DPS) for digital twin platforms

sig_25691773fadd0d99dd05.description: Gloucestershire ICB and Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire (BNSSG) ICB are merging to form a single integrated body in April 2027. Both organisations currently rely on external providers for the delivery of their IT services. A new, unified service model is required; one that supports the merged organisation from day one, is commercially sustainable, and is capable of evolving as the ICS matures. Six principles shape the design of the future service: 1. Cloud-first and 'secure by design'. All new and renewed services will be cloud-based wherever possible. On-premises infrastructure will be exited as part of transition. This is both a strategic choice and a compliance requirement under the Government Cloud First Policy and Technology Code of Practice. 2. Outcome-focused. The service is defined by what it must deliver, not how it must be delivered. The supplier is expected to bring expertise, innovation and accountability for outcomes, not simply execute a prescriptive technical specification. 3. Single point of accountability. The preferred model is a single managed service provider with end-to-end accountability for operational delivery. This avoids the fragmentation and unclear ownership that characterises the current multi-supplier landscape and reduces the management overhead on the ICB digital team. 4. Lean governance. The ICB digital team will provide strategic oversight, roadmap ownership and supplier governance. It will not carry operational delivery responsibilities. This reflects the lean, strategically focused character of the merged organisation and the direction set by the Model ICB Blueprint. 5. Interoperable by design. The service must integrate cleanly with nationally contracted NHS platforms, in particular NHS.net Connect, the Health and Social Care Network (HSCN) and NHS Secure Boundary Service, as well as local platforms, such as the Gloucestershire ICS WAN and into UHBW and Crown Datacentres in Corsham. Service interfaces with these platforms should be clearly defined before the procurement specification is finalised. 6. Sustainable. The ICB's carbon neutral commitments should be reflected in technology choices, including energy-efficient end-user devices, PoE-powered monitors and cloud-based infrastructure in preference to on-premises data centre equipment. The following service stacks are in scope for the new managed service, reflecting services currently provided across both incumbents, consolidated and extended to support the merged organisation: - Service desk. The primary user-facing support channel, available 08:00-18:00 Monday to Friday. - Desktop support. Onsite presence at both sites as and when required, including end-user support, moves, adds and changes to desktop arrangements, MFD, Audio Visual equipment, and Teams Room management. The onsite support model must include provision for routine physical tasks including WFH equipment management, peripheral replacement, cable and hardware swap-outs, and stock management. - End-user compute. Device lifecycle management including provisioning, refresh (five-year target cycle), configuration, and secure disposal. - Telephony and unified communications. Microsoft Teams Phone as the unified platform for the merged ICB. - Print. Cloud-managed secure print at both sites. - Meeting rooms. Physical teams Room management and audio-visual support at 2 locations with 15 meeting rooms at one and at Shire Hall, Gloucester and 9 at the second location. - Asset management. Asset tagging, recording, and lifecycle tracking for all ICB-owned IT equipment. - Supplier and procurement management. The supplier will assume management of all ongoing third-party technology relationships and will procure all IT equipment and recurring support contracts on behalf of the ICB. Licence management across the estate is required. - DSPT support. The supplier is expected to provide the ICB with the technical evidence and assurance data required to support annual DSPT submission, including patch management records, asset inventory, access control logs and incident reports. - Project, change and architecture. The supplier will own project and change management, problem management, and architecture design. - Digital signatures. Digital signature capability is required as part of the new service. Full details are provided in the service specification. The total maximum contract value for the initial 3-year Contract is £1,920,000 inclusive of VAT (where applicable). At the end of the initial contract term the Commissioner will have two, separate, consecutive one-year extension option periods that can be exercised at the discretion of the Commissioner, giving a maximum possible contract value of £2,700,000 inclusive of VAT (where applicable) over 5 years if the full contract term is fulfilled. The Commissioner is of the view that TUPE does not apply to this service. The Contracting Authority reserves the right to use the Direct Award procedure under the Procurement Act 2023 for any subsequent extensions or new contracts for similar requirements. The new contract will commence on 1st April 2027, although implementation of the services will start during January 2027. Lot 1: .

sig_267c5f44064b1be068ef.description: The purpose of this PIN is to inform market operators of a potential future exercise to procure services supporting the marketing and communications for a new nationwide programme to increase physical activity and reduce inactivity. Health Innovation North East and North Cumbria (HI NENC) is commissioning an agency partner to design and deliver the marketing, PR, and communications strategy for a national behaviour change programme designed to increase physical activity and reduce inactivity across England. The Programme responds directly to the Government's 10 Year Health Plan commitment to motivate millions to walk - and where possible run - regularly. Sir Brendan Foster has convened expert partners to support this. The Programme aims to reframe movement as personal, cumulative and achievable through the core proposition: The Programme is not a traditional sports campaign. It is a long-term national behaviour change movement designed to: - • Increase movement among inactive adults • Address health inequalities • Build a recognisable, inclusive national movement brand • Enable sustainable habit formation through digital tools and rewards • Advertising - including advertising investment to launch and sustain the campaign within the first year. The associated marketing campaign must inspire participation at scale, whilst remaining grounded in behavioural science and public health evidence. The appointed agency will be responsible for developing and delivering a full set of campaign materials, frameworks, strategies, activation plans, toolkits, digital assets, evaluation reports, and all content needed to deliver the programme end to end. This must be aligned to the overall narrative framework. This will include planning major PR and press moments, building momentum towards launch dates and engaging with key stakeholders to strengthen partnerships. Additional information: HI NENC would like to invite potential providers of Marketing and Communications services to apply to our Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) DN670401 as a supplier. You can do this by following this link: https://procontract.due-north.com/SupplierPostLoginHome/ActivityDashboard?projectId=c1881153-e6f3-ed11-8122-005056b64545&callingPage=Home This opportunity will be developed as a further competition under Lot 5 of our DPS. You should therefore ensure you apply to Lot 5 to be able to bid to provide this service. You are also welcome to apply for any other Lots on our DPS that you feel are relevant to your organisation. We are expecting to put out the Invitation to Quote (ITQ) to our Lot 5 suppliers by the end of March 2026. This timeline is subject to change. Interested suppliers are advised to apply to the DPS promptly to ensure they have been accepted to the framework and receive the competition notification. Failure to be accepted to the framework ahead of the ITQ publication will mean that you will be unable to bid to supply. This notice is for information and engaging with the supply market only. It is not a binding statement of intent or call for competition. HI NENC reserves the right not to enter a formal process and not award a contract. The information contained in this notice, including information relating to the nature and scope of the requirements, the service classification of this requirement from the list of CPV codes, is only indicative of the HI NENC's current thinking and is neither exhaustive nor binding. HI NENC reserves the right at its absolute discretion to amend it at the time of issue of any further notices or at any other time. HI NENC will not be liable for any bid cost, expenditure, work or effort incurred by a potential supplier in acting on the basis of this PIN

sig_26a98529eaa32684637e.description: The subject matter of this procurement comprises the procurement of a SaaS solution, which encompasses various functions and services. The focus is on the provision of an extensive digital communication solution based on OX 8. The MBJS is looking for an experienced contractor capable of providing a corresponding solution based on OX 8 while meeting the specific requirements and needs of a state-level solution for the State of Brandenburg regarding high security standards (BSI IT-Grundschutz), data protection compliance (GDPR), integrity, flexibility and scalability. Lot LOT-0001: Communication solution for 25.000 persons in the education sector (teacher mail). In the year 2019, on behalf of the Ministry for Education, Youth and Sport (hereinafter referred to as MBJS), a complex IT infrastructure was built based on the products Univention UCS and Univention UCS@School, consisting of a central identity management system, hereinafter referred to as IDM, and the groupware and email solution Open Xchange from the manufacturer of the same name, hereinafter referred to as OX. An extensive communication solution was created for 20.000 teaching staff at publicly maintained schools in the State of Brandenburg. The schools mapped in UCS and UCS@School in the form of separate school OUs form the basis for the contexts set up in OX. Each school is thus assigned to a separate context in OX. The creation, modification and deletion of accounts in the IDM are carried out via the specialist procedures developed by the MBJS. After several years of operation, due to the lifecycle of OX, it is necessary to transition to the current version 8. The transition to OX 8 requires extensive changes to the UCS OX connector and the IT infrastructure. The version OX 8 requires Docker runtime environments that are not provided by the existing IT infrastructure. It is not possible to simply update the software in the existing system. The MBJS therefore intends to have the groupware and email solution for teaching staff based on OX operated in future as a SaaS solution by a provider. In this context, the user accounts in the existing IDM shall continue to form the basis for the email mailboxes and the existing provisioning processes shall be retained. Only the mail stack of the existing IT infrastructure is to be replaced by a SaaS solution.
sig_26a98529eaa32684637e.title: Communication solution for 25.000 persons in the education sector (teacher mail)

sig_26e1b91d8504330c38df.description: This is not a contract notice or a call for tenders, but a request for information with which the contracting authority is conducting a market survey of potential tenderers and solutions available on the market for its procurement need. The information obtained through the market survey will be used in the preparation of the future procurement. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue (LUVN) has a need to procure technology to be taken home for the use of the wellbeing services county's residents, as well as an alarm system that receives the alarms produced by the aforementioned technology. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue is assembling and launching as its own operation a so-called Safety Assistance Service, the goal of which is to enable and support customers' independent coping in their own homes around the clock. A central element in the Safety Assistance Service is the technology utilised in it that is taken to homes or home-like services, and the receiving system for the alarms produced by them. With this request for information, LUVN wants to survey the technology solutions available on the market that are suitable for social and health care, that ensure the customer's safety at home, and solutions suitable for receiving alarms related to these. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue estimates that the procurement entity according to its needs will consist of the following parts, but changes may occur in the entity: - Technology installed at home for the customer's safety (e.g. sensors, detectors, wristbands) as well as their maintenance and backup device services - Safety alarm centre system and mobile software possibly related to it - Service implementation project - Continuous services, support, maintenance and service of the technology and alarm centre system - Expert services related to the aforementioned technology and its utilisation and use during the contract period according to the subscriber's need. To support the specification of its procurement needs, the planning of the procurement and the preparation of the tendering documents, Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue wants to engage in a market dialogue with suppliers offering solutions corresponding to the procurement need. Through the market dialogue, the wellbeing services county hopes to receive information generally about solutions on the market corresponding to the object of the procurement. We are interested in your solutions and services related to safety technology supporting living at home and how the solutions direct alarms to the safety alarm receiving system and what features the receiving system includes. We also want to know what kind of information your system produces to support the planning of services offered to the customer for the professional, in addition to alarm information. Suppliers are requested to register for the market dialogue by email to the address: hankinta@luvn.fi Registration is requested to be sent by 3.10.2025 at 12. The registration should be titled as follows: “Kodin turvapalvelulaitteet ja hälytysten vastaanottojärjestelmä” (Home safety service devices and alarm receiving system). The content of the email message is sufficient to be the supplier's name and the contact details of the supplier's contact person. LUVN will be in contact with the contact persons of the suppliers who have registered to agree on the implementation of the market dialogue. According to the wellbeing services county's plans, the market dialogue should include both discussion sessions and the exchange of written material, but the exact schedule of the dialogue will be specified later. sig_26fc285d05c35f03de8a.description: NHS Scotland intends to establish a national Framework Agreement for the provision of a Digital Diabetes Prevention and Primary Hypertension Programme. The programme will support individuals identified as being at risk of developing Type 2 Diabetes and/or those diagnosed with primary hypertension, through the delivery of evidence-based, digitally enabled lifestyle and behaviour change interventions. The Authority intends to appoint a single supplier to a national Framework Agreement. The procurement will be conducted using a Restricted Procedure, comprising a Selection Stage and an Invitation to Tender (ITT) stage. Suppliers will be shortlisted following evaluation of their suitability, technical and professional capability, capacity and relevant experience, with a maximum of five suppliers invited to submit a tender. Lot 1: . NHS Scotland intends to establish a national Framework Agreement for the provision of a Digital Diabetes Prevention and Primary Hypertension Programme. The Framework will support NHS Scotland's strategic objectives to improve population health outcomes, reduce health inequalities and support the prevention and management of long-term conditions through evidence-based, digitally enabled interventions. The requirement comprises a single integrated service with two pathways: - Digital Diabetes Prevention Programme (DDPP) for individuals identified as being at increased risk of developing Type 2 Diabetes; and - Primary Hypertension Programme (PHP) for individuals diagnosed with primary hypertension, supported through lifestyle and behaviour change interventions designed to improve health outcomes and reduce cardiovascular risk. The appointed Framework Participant will be required to deliver evidence-based, digitally enabled lifestyle and behaviour change interventions designed to support participants in achieving sustainable improvements in health behaviours and clinical outcomes. The service will utilise a digital platform/application supported by appropriately trained personnel, including health coaching and clinical governance arrangements, to facilitate participant engagement, self-management, education, monitoring and behaviour change. The service is expected to support a range of participant needs and will include, as appropriate, digital onboarding, risk assessment, lifestyle intervention, coaching support, educational resources, progress monitoring, outcome reporting and onward referral or escalation processes where clinically indicated. The Authority seeks a solution that is accessible, inclusive and capable of supporting diverse populations across Scotland, including individuals who may experience barriers to participation arising from geography, deprivation, language, disability or digital exclusion. The Framework Participant will be expected to work collaboratively with NHS Scotland, NHS Boards, Primary Care and other relevant stakeholders to support the promotion of the programme, participant recruitment and self-registration, service mobilisation, programme delivery, performance monitoring and continuous improvement. Current funding has been identified to support approximately 15,000 participants through the Diabetes Prevention pathway during the initial three-year term of the Framework Agreement. The Hypertension pathway is anticipated to support approximately 500 participants per annum. These figures are provided for information only and do not constitute a guarantee of volumes. The Authority reserves the right, subject to future funding availability and service requirements, to increase participant volumes and/or expand the scope of the Framework to include additional prevention cohorts, pathways, clinical indicators or service requirements that are closely aligned to the subject matter of the Framework Agreement. The Authority intends to appoint a single supplier to a national Framework Agreement. The procurement will be conducted using a Restricted Procedure. Suppliers will first be assessed at Selection Stage through completion of the Single Procurement Document (SPD) and Pre-Qualification Questionnaire (PQQ), which will assess suitability, technical and professional capability, capacity and relevant experience. A maximum of five suppliers will be shortlisted and invited to participate in the Invitation to Tender stage.
sig_26fc285d05c35f03de8a.title: Digital Diabetes Prevention and Primary Hypertension Programme

The Oslo School has participated in a R&D project together with KS since 2017. the R&D project ends in its current form in summer 2024. In order to achieve autonomy and freedom of methodology in the choice of teaching aids, a use-based payment model is required where schools have access to all products and pay in arrears in arrears in accordance with actual use. Digital teaching aids and teaching resources consist of a market that is constantly developing. To a small degree, traditional approaches cover the schools ́need for flexible access to a wide range of teaching aids. The aim is also that an overall ecosystem shall make the procurement process of digital teaching aids and learning resources easier for school owners and more in line with the needs of the schools and pupils. The dynamic procurement scheme is for continuous delivery of digital teaching aids (freestanding or as part of teaching aids/learning universe), teaching resources, resource banks (news, pictures, movies, audio, music, etc.), teacher guides, teacher resources, assignment/trial collections and mapping tool with accompanying teacher overview, glosses, etc. that are delivered over the internet ("Software-as-a-service") for teaching purposes. The agreement also includes digital books and installed apps with Feide sign-in for teaching purposes. The diagnostic tool, which requires special competence to use, is not included. Digital services, which only have a functionality for delivering teaching aids that shall be physically implemented, are also not included. The agreement does not include the purchase of services that do not have Feide sign-in, including apps for iPads that are purchased via the App Store/Apple School Manager.

sig_28949b4799d8edb1223e.description: Chiltern Railways is seeking to procure supplier-hosted software solutions and associated services to replace its existing Train Planning and Rostering systems. The procurement is divided into two Lots: Lot 1 - Train Planning System; and Lot 2 - Rostering System. Lot 1 is for the provision, implementation, hosting, support and maintenance of a Train Planning System. The solution is required to support train planning and diagramming activities, including the creation, import, editing, validation, management and publication of timetables, schedules, rolling stock diagrams and traincrew diagrams. The solution must support planning data management, timetable change management, scenario modelling, auditability, version control, reporting, user permissions and secure data exchange with relevant operational and business systems. Lot 2 is for the provision, implementation, hosting, support and maintenance of a Rostering System. The solution is required to support base, weekly and daily rostering for relevant staff groups, including traincrew, station staff and fleet/engineering staff. The solution must support roster creation, validation, publication and management, allocation of staff to duties, management of leave, overtime, shift swaps, fatigue and risk assessment, identification of uncovered turns and roster coverage gaps, employee self-service, reporting, auditability, user permissions and secure data exchange with relevant operational and business systems. For each Lot, the successful supplier will be required to provide a fully managed, vendor-hosted solution. This includes the software, hosting, configuration, implementation, data migration, integration, testing, training, change management, documentation, support, maintenance, updates, service management, information security, business continuity, disaster recovery, contract management and exit assistance required to deliver and operate the relevant solution. Bidders may participate in respect of Lot 1, Lot 2, or both Lots. Chiltern Railways may award Lot 1 and Lot 2 to different suppliers or may award both Lots to the same supplier in accordance with the procurement documents and award methodology. The estimated value of Lot 1 is £140,000 to £430,000 per annum and £1,000,000 to £3,000,000 over the full contract term, including any optional extension period. The estimated value of Lot 2 is £210,000 to £500,000 per annum and £1,500,000 to £3,500,000 over the full contract term, including any optional extension period. The estimated combined value of Lot 1 and Lot 2 is £2,500,000 to £6,500,000 excluding VAT over the full contract term, including any optional extension period. The estimated contract start date is 26 July 2027. The indicative operational go-live date is 1 March 2028, being the date from which the system is expected to start being rolled out and used by Chiltern Railways staff. The indicative implementation complete date is 30 June 2028, being the date by which the system is expected to be fully implemented, tested, accepted where applicable, ready for and/or used in live operational production, and to have completed dual running with the incumbent tools. The initial contract term is expected to be 60 months, with an option for Chiltern Railways to extend for a further period or periods of up to 24 months in total. Lot 1: Train Planning System. Configuration of workflows, roles, permissions, learning pathways, dashboards, notifications and branding. 3. Microsoft 365 integrations, including Microsoft Teams and Outlook calendar integration. 7. Administrator, manager and end-user training, including materials and train-the-trainer or digital resources. 8. Ongoing hosting, storage, backups, disaster recovery, support, service levels, maintenance, updates, escalation and account management. 10. Reporting, dashboards and scheduled reporting. Relevant experience implementing and supporting Learning Management Systems for a housing association, public sector organisation or similarly regulated environment. 2. The RFQ defines Most Advantageous Tender as the tender offering the optimum combination of quality, social value and price in accordance with the evaluation methodology. Particular emphasis is expected to be placed on: 1. Functional LMS capability and user experience. 2. Compliance training management and reporting. 3. sig_293d60a574586a8b78e6.description: AI infrastructure components are being procured to expand the contracting authority's existing structure due to increased requirements resulting from project participation. Lot LOT-0001: AI Existing Infrastructure Extension - Project Racoon. 2.1 NVIDIA Deep Learning System DGX B300 Cluster - Lot 1 Required procurement of four NVIDIA DGX B300 systems for the efficient processing of computationally intensive AI issues (e.g. medical imaging, digital pathology, omics, and NLP). The system serves as central infrastructure and enables the flexible provision of GPU workstation environments for university partners in the RACOON joint project via advanced virtualization with DGX OS / NVIDIA Enterprise AI. The new systems integrate seamlessly into the existing management infrastructure, which is based on the NVIDIA Base Command Manager and NVIDIA Mission Control. This ensures highly efficient, consistent administration without additional familiarisation or migration effort for the operations team. Since all algorithms and AI models are based on the proprietary NVIDIA CUDA architecture, the system has no technical alternative; a transition to other architectures or APIs would be associated with a disproportionately high and economically unjustifiable effort. In addition, the existing GPU cluster management is built natively on this software stack. The selected Blackwell generation (B300) offers the only adequate performance class with 8x NVIDIA B300 GPUs, 2304 GB total memory, and a 800 Gbit/s InfiniBand connection. Furthermore, the enormous power density (10 U in the rack at max. 15,1 kW per system) guarantees resource-saving integration into the capacity-limited data centre. Lot LOT-0002: AI Existing Infrastructure Extension - Projects Athene. 2.2 NVIDIA GPU servers, network, and Spark cluster - Lot 2 The procurement serves to expand and optimize the existing infrastructure of the Research Compute Cluster (RCC) to meet the growing demand for high-performance resources for AI and data-intensive research applications. The NVIDIA DGX Spark systems enable the development, testing, and inference of AI models in the same NVIDIA software environment as the central GPU servers of the RCC. As a result, developed applications can be transferred to the higher-performance RCC resources without fundamental adaptations. The additional GPU server expands the central computing capacity of the RCC and is used in particular for medical AI, image analysis, genomics/metagenomics, as well as the training and inference of large AI models. Integration takes place into the existing Slurm-based infrastructure. To connect the additional components, the existing management and BMC network infrastructure is also expanded by a technically identical SuperMicro SSE-G3748R-SONIC. This ensures a uniform and operationally consistent infrastructure without establishing a separate network solution.
sig_293d60a574586a8b78e6.title: AI Existing Infrastructure Extension - Projects Racoon & Athene

sig_29714e9c55d9c6aac73c.description: The subject matter of this contract is: "Implementation of integration of the Information System for Management and Maintenance of the Public Register under the Environmental Liability Prevention and Remedying Act (ISMMPR under ELPRA), including migration of existing data, with the identified information systems of bodies under Article 16, paragraph 1 of ELPRA" The main objective of the project is the integration of the ISMMPR under ELPRA with other information systems (IS), both within the Ministry of Environment and Water (MoEW) and with external systems maintained by other state bodies. Main aspects of the subject matter of the contract: Analysis of existing information systems: • The project includes validating the analysis of the designated information systems of executive power bodies under Article 16, paragraph 1 of ELPRA for their integration into the ISMMPR under ELPRA and their functionalities that can be integrated with the ISMMPR under ELPRA. This validation of the analysis aims to determine the electronic nomenclatures in these systems, as well as the possibilities for copy-pasting existing data. Integration requirements: • The contract covers the definition of architectural and functional requirements for the integration of the systems, including automated data exchange between the ISMMPR under ELPRA and other registers of administrative bodies, as well as the maintenance of compatibility with information systems outside the MoEW. • Integration of the ISMMPR under ELPRA with information systems of executive power bodies under Article 16 of ELPRA, in accordance with the Ordinance on the Public Register of Operators Performing Activities under Annex No 1 to Article 3, item 1 of the Environmental Liability Prevention and Remedying Act and Guidelines on the provision of information for entry in the public register of operators performing the activities under Annex No 1 to Article 3, item 1 of ELPRA, including: • Validating the identified information systems of the executive power bodies under Article 16, paragraph 1 of ELPRA and their integration into the ISMMPR under ELPRA for data, as well as providing new functionalities for connecting the systems. Improvement of the public register under ELPRA: • The project provides for the modernisation and upgrading of the ISMMPR under ELPRA with the aim of ensuring centralised access to data and greater interoperability with other systems, while maintaining high information security and eliminating duplicate data. Maintenance services: • Information on the maintenance services of the integrated systems will be provided, including updating and monitoring of their operation. Compliance with regulatory requirements: • The requirements of the contract are aligned with the regulatory framework of the Electronic Governance Act (EGA) and subordinate legislation, as well as with the business analysis that establishes additional requirements for the implementation of the project. The subject matter of the contract covers the development and deployment of effective integration of information systems, ensuring interoperability between registers and systems maintained by various state administration bodies, and guaranteeing the proper functioning of the ISMMPR under ELPRA, in accordance with the requirements of ELPRA. Scope: The described objectives are achieved through the implementation of the following main stages: 1. Data and requirements analysis; 2. Preparation of a system design; 3. Development of the software solution; 4. Testing; 5. Deployment; 6. Training; 7. Warranty support. Project activities: Activity 1: Design; Activity 2: Integration/Construction.
