sig_385fb26148b2325dfc3a.description: Open procedure, pursuant to Article 71 of Legislative Decree No 36/2023, for the award of development, maintenance and management services for the information system of Fondimpresa (FPF System). A contract concerning the following activities shall be concluded with the successful tenderer of this procedure: i) Software development and enhancement (MEV) ii) Corrective and adaptive maintenance (MAC/MAD) iii) Housing, operation and hardware/software maintenance iv) Helpdesk (hereinafter also referred to solely as "Service" or "Services"), as better defined, described and set out in the technical specification attached to the tender specifications. A handover period with the new successful tenderer taking over at the end of the contract must be guaranteed, lasting at least 2 (two) months. Regarding the procedures for executing the contractual relationship, please refer to the provisions in paragraph 9 of the technical specification, without prejudice to compliance with the service levels referred to in paragraph 10 of the technical specification, failing which the penalties established therein shall apply. In order to outline the background context, notwithstanding what is better established in the technical specification, it is specified that Fondimpresa has acquired an information system (named "FPF System") for managing the training plans of the Training Account and the System Account, for communication between Fondimpresa, its regional offices and the member companies, for acquiring and managing membership data and contributions transmitted by INPS, as well as monitoring information to be sent periodically to the Ministry of Labour and Social Policies and for registering state aid with the RNA. The development of the Fund's activities, the diversification of training financing measures made available to member companies (via public notices), the increase in financing granted and the number of training plans managed, the steady growth in memberships and the evolution of monitoring specifications required by the guidance and supervisory authority, entail the need to guarantee: • evolutionary maintenance (MEV) of the FPF system; • corrective and adaptive maintenance (MAC/MAD) of the FPF system; • management of housing and operation services with particular attention to system monitoring activities and security aspect verification (penetration tests, vulnerability assessments, etc.); • management of the first and second-level helpdesk service; • the development of new document flow management features with a view to continuous and progressive paperless operation of the Fund's activities; • the integration of new tools based on artificial intelligence to automate and optimise human operational workflows; • architectural developments and hardware/software infrastructure modernisation interventions to ensure appropriate levels of security, efficiency and service continuity; • application support for the disaster recovery system. The currently estimated user base is approximately 280.000 users against approximately 210.000 contributing positions affiliated with Fondimpresa. The contract shall have a duration of 60 natural and consecutive months, commencing from the start date of activities determined by the date of a specific record of commencement of activities. For all services described in the preceding article, no interfering risks are identifiable for which specific safety measures need to be adopted and, therefore, the preparation of the DUVRI is not required (pursuant to Article 26, paragraph 3-bis, of Legislative Decree No 81/2008). Consequently, there are no safety costs of an interfering nature, which are therefore quantified as € 0,00. Since the tender procedure has as its object services of an intellectual nature (as these primarily concern software development and the elaboration of customised solutions, functional analysis and governance of system evolution), tenderers are not required to indicate, pursuant to Article 108, paragraph 9, of the Code, the amount of labour costs and company costs for fulfilling provisions regarding health and safety in the workplace. Please refer to the Tender Specifications and its attached technical specification for tender particulars. The contract consists of a single lot as it is characterised by the functional unity of the service. Therefore, it is considered appropriate, both from the perspective of economic efficiency and optimal service execution, not to proceed with a division into lots. In any event, the tenderer's future bid shall be understood to refer overall to the entirety of the services forming the subject matter of the tender.
sig_385fb26148b2325dfc3a.title: Open procedure, pursuant to Article 71 of Legislative Decree No 36/2023, for the award of development, maintenance and management services for the information system of Fondimpresa (FPF System)

sig_3867dc5e562dbd296212.description: The scope of this contract is to acquire the full range of technical, management and support services necessary to obtain and maintain access to US food and cosmetic products. The contract is divided into the following task areas: Project Management Data Access Data Collection Training Support 6.1 Technical Requirements 6.1.1 Datasets The processed food and cosmetic products and their package data (as well as menu data) shall be from a currently existing, commercially available database(s) that shall provide immediate automated access. The data shall include products from all regions of the US (Appendix B indicates the US Census regions) and be accurate, quality-assured, and easily-validated; well organized; stored as relationally searchable information for trend and other analyses; and fully exportable. The database(s) shall be regularly updated and maintained in a current state throughout the base and option periods. Information will be required for the following product types: Processed, and retail food products (e.g. foods, infant formula, etc.; minimum 400,000 products that are selling on the market in the contract year) and thus, over 2 million historical products; (Optional) Restaurant food products/menu items (minimum 50,000 products from top chains) Dietary supplements (minimum 100,000 products); shall be categorized according to the definition in Appendix A Cosmetics (minimum 300,000 products) The following attributes (as shown on the package) shall be required: Package images (legible images of all surfaces (e.g. sides, top, bottom) of product packaging, including internal and external packaging Count of available images per product Information contained on and in product packaging – shall include the following at minimum (each data entry line in the database must be quality assured and -controlled (QA/QC’d) for accuracy as the database is populated) GTIN/UPC/Barcode Nutrition Facts label, including single and dual columns and including multi-packs (shall be displayed in format according to 21 CFR 101.9) and Supplement Facts label (shall be displayed in format according to 21 CFR 101.36(e)(10) (i), (ii), (iii), and (iv)) Additional nutrients presenting on package labels Indication of added sugars Ingredients list (e.g. food additives, active ingredients for dietary supplements) Allergen labeling information (Contains/may contain) and advisory statements Pack size and weight Number of servings per package Brand Manufacturer Location of manufacturer, packer, or distributor Written and/or pictorial statements signaling the presence of one or more allergens (according to the Food Allergen Labeling and Consumer Protection Act (FALCPA) of 2004; e.g. “Contains”) and/or caution statements about the product (e.g. “warning statements”) Insignificant amounts for certain nutrients Claims on package (e.g., regulated, health, nutrition, efficacy, marketing, and all other types) including indication of “healthy” on package Statements/icons/signages and similar information that features the nutrition, health, organoleptic, processing, suggested usages (e.g., recipes), and other properties of the product (e.g., written and/or pictorial statements that feature nutrient content claim languages, front-of-pack language/icons) Certifications on package GE/Bioengineered/GMO language on package Verbatim language of all text (e.g. product description, instructions, etc.) and icons from product packaging Product source where collected Product category Dates of when product information is a) released to the market and on shelf, b) collected, c) published, d) updated, and e) discontinued Indication of “previous” or “new” nutrition facts label FNDDS 8-digit and 7-digit food codes; SR 5-digit sub codes (8-digit food code shall be linked to food products and ingredients;7-digit food codes are mapped to 8-digit at the product level; 5-digit SR sub codes are mapped to 8-digit food codes at the ingredient level) through 2019 GSFA (General Standard for Food Additives) categories through 2019 Food packaging types (primary and secondary) and codes Food content type Moreover, the data shall provide additional valid and verifiable information on the product ingredients; at a minimum, the data shall provide all available synonym name(s), allergen status, and technical or functional effect descriptors in a usable format. Additionally, FDA shall have access to other Mintel products, such as Mintel Leap, Mintel Food & Drink, Mintel Reports, Mintel Trends, Comperemedia Direct, Market Dynamics, and Global Consumer Research. 6.1.2 Product Requirements Overarching product requirements: Unlimited access for up to 200 FDA personnel; Located external to FDA network (access via weblink); Universal access from any FDA computer hardware (desktops, laptops with docking stations and/or scientific workstations) using internet browsers compatible with FDA current standards; Product access shall not be restricted according to product price; Capability to perform relational searching and analyses of the food and cosmetic product labeling and packaging datasets and menu datasets in functional environments using appropriate methodologies, which shall be valid, reliable, and robust; Ability to support disclosure of scientific and technical articles, study results, presentations, public health advisories, and similar works involving aggregated data to entities outside the Agency including the general public; High resolution, readable images for all sides of the package labels (and optionally, menu images) for validation and other research purposes. Images shall be displayed with product data from all sides of the package so that information may be easily verifiable by the user. Accurate data reflective of verbatim language and icons of product labels (and menus). Verification that products are still being sold in the US marketplace. Users shall be able to analyze and summarize their searches into summary reports and all available data and search results and outputs shall be downloadable and exportable within an accepted timeframe into Microsoft Excel Spreadsheets and Access Data Base Software, SAS Business Analytics Software, and other common formats. Regular, updated, extracted bulk/batch raw data of the full dataset shall be available by API and in MS Excel compatible format (e.g. single pipe delimited txt, csv) and shall be accessible in a secure FTP or cloud service acceptable by FDA. In addition to the product label (and menu) database(s), all sales data, other accompanying databases, and market research reports, when available, shall be provided. This information shall apply to food, dietary supplement, restaurant, and cosmetic products when available Data and UI status updates shall be posted on the system website main page and identified users shall be notified via email System usage statistics (including statistics regarding individual login usage and length of time logged in) shall be available in monthly reports and upon request All data and files shall undergo quality control checks prior to accessibility/delivery to FDA. Documentation on quality control procedures shall be provided (at the onset and with any changes over time) for all data and image collection and data processes (e.g. ingestion of data, quality assurance of data in different formats, etc.) as noted below. Web Interface A user-friendly and data comprehensive interface that is transparent and flexible and allows both predefined (i.e., canned) and custom reports shall be provided. The user should be able to conduct a multi-variable search (i.e. searching a combination of factors concurrently). The user should be able to search and filter according to product category, year, product name, UPC, brand, company, claims, ingredients, allergens, other product attributes, and user-entered keywords in any and all fields. Raw Data Files Raw files (e.g. MS Excel compatible, single pipe-delimited txt, csv) for all data (food, supplements, cosmetics, etc.) shall be delivered a minimum of quarterly as defined by FDA or downable without file size restriction. The file sizes should be appropriate so that they can be opened and readily used. Files shall be accessible in a secure FTP or cloud service acceptable by FDA and organized based on FDA specifications. All files shall also be available by API with fields as specified by FDA. The database(s) shall be scientific based on FDA’s definition: able to verify the data entry line(s) via product images, and the product’s contents may be analyzed, if the user chooses to have the item purchased and analyzed, to verify the accuracy/truthfulness of the product label, the offeror(s) shall provide this as a purchasable service. System maintenance during the base and all option periods, if exercised, shall be provided. Maintenance shall include upgrades and updates to the software and data, continued use of and access to the database system and data, and updates to technical and analytical documentation. 6.1.3 Documentation The Contractor shall compile and submit full documentation to the Contracting Officer Representative (COR) and Project Officer (PO) within 14 days of the beginning of the contract as well as any updated documentation through the contract years. After approval by the COR, all documentation shall be available to access online in the database(s) system with downloadable format into MS Word. The Contractor shall provide documentation on the following: All data collection and acquisition processes so that the source data is clearly understood Documentation on the status of all products found in the databases relative to what is selling on the market each year of the contract (e.g., is the product verified as being available in retail for purchase and/or is it discontinued). The methodologies used for any data cleaning and ingestion processes and those used to develop the data as well as information on pertinent software used as part of the process Data dictionary and a code book defining all data elements/fields that are included in the data package, which includes information on how calculations are performed relative to certain data fields Documentation on the process of standardizing and cleaning data from different sources as well as information on UPCs that are duplicated (e.g. historical vs, duplicated) Any related technical specifications on the technologies or software that is used Information on how to access and use the data in all formats Written methodology regarding quality control procedures for all data and images collected, ingested into a database, exported, and categorized, including information on the oversight of quality control to ensure above 98% accuracy Interface documentation and user guides Any updates to general processes, methodologies, data sources, QC processes, Documentation on limitations of database, errors in the database, and plans for mitigation and/or resolution of issues Full-disclosure 6.1.4 Support / Training A. Support: Ongoing technical and analytical support by phone or by e-mail shall be provided to all certified users of the data during business hours (9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Eastern Time) throughout the period of performance (POP) in accordance with the service levels established in the contract. The Contractor shall notify the COR regarding any issues as they relate to Acceptable Quality Level (AQL) standards. All technical related issues would need to be addressed and resolved in 5 business days or within a reasonable timeframe agreement upon with COR and TCOR. B. Training: The Contractor shall provide up to two (2) one-day training sessions per year (on-site or via web-based methods). This training can be divided into shorter time periods. Additional options for additional “on-demand” sessions either in person or via web-based methods shall be made available under the IDIQ portion of the award. 6.1.5 Data Disclosure Clearance As part of its regulatory activities, FDA shall, at times, require disclosure of scientific and technical articles, study results, presentations, public health advisories, and similar works involving aggregated data to entities outside the Agency including the general public. For activities that require disclosure of aggregated data the Contractor shall accept and adhere to the FDA Data Disclosure Clearance Procedures and form found in Appendices D. The FDA shall continue to require the ability to release aggregated data through the FDA Data Disclosure Clearance process for data obtained during the contract period for the period of all Option Periods. The FDA will require the services of processing clearance requests. As part of its regulatory activities, FDA shall, at times engage in collaborative research projects with third parties outside of FDA for specific research projects of public health importance that are initiated by and for the benefit of FDA. These collaborations shall require FDA to have the ability to share project specific aggregated or raw data with third parties for collaborative research projects. For these collaborations that require sharing of aggregated or raw data, the Contractor shall accept and adhere to the Data Disclosure Clearance Procedures and form to be found in Appendices D. These Procedures include terms and conditions for third party collaborations. 6.2 Project Management The Contractor shall be responsible for creating, managing and updating project plans, schedules and managing resources for the project. 6.2.1 Quality Control The Contractor shall ensure that quality control procedures are conducted prior to providing FDA access to data. The Contractor shall provide written methodology on quality control procedures for all data and images collected, ingested into a database, exported, and categorized, including information on the oversight of quality control to ensure above 98% accuracy. The Contractor shall notify the COR should any issues with the data be noticed and shall flag it in the interface. Should FDA notice issues with the data, the Contractor shall address and fix the issues immediately within an agreed upon timeframe with the COR. 6.2.2 Reporting The Contractor shall provide a brief work plan outlining the strategy for supporting each of the areas outlined in Section 4 of the SOW to the COR within 10 days of award. Each month the Contractor shall provide a status report giving brief descriptions of activities performed. The monthly status report shall, at minimum, contain the following: usage statistics for databases and other resources; usage statistics of technical support feature by FDA staff; technical issues reported by FDA staff; other technical issues (ex. log of times when database(s)/resources were inaccessible), data ingestion success and failure rates with mitigation plans should issues be present. The Contractor shall conduct yearly face-to-face presentation meetings with the COR and other FDA staff as well as deliver final written progress reports about contract performance for the preceding period of performance. The Contractor shall submit to the COR a final report which documents and summarizes the results of the contract work 10 days prior to the end of each period of performance. The final report shall include tables, graphs, diagrams, curves, sketches, photographs and drawings as necessary and in sufficient detail to comprehensively explain the results achieved under this contract. 6.3 Contract Services Requirements The Contractor shall perform the following types of tasks as needed: Contractor shall collect information for selected products. The list of products and data fields to be collected shall be defined by the COR. Contractor shall conduct search(es) for products using search criteria defined by the COR. The option shall be available to purchase identified products. Contractor shall conduct exports for products using search criteria defined by the COR as needed. sig_386ca583829de162b3f9.buyer_name: German Federal Bank, Procurement Central Division
sig_386ca583829de162b3f9.description: Market exploration - voluntary prior information - no contract notice The Deutsche Bundesbank is conducting a market exploration pursuant to Section 28 of the VgV to gather information on potential providers for the provision of interest rate data for the banking and financial services sector. The market exploration is aimed at providers that are capable of providing high-quality and comprehensive interest rate data for the banking sector. The Bundesbank is seeking a long-term cooperation with a provider that, through the provision of this data, can make a significant contribution to the continuation and further development of the Bundesbank's statistics and analyses. Interested providers are requested to contact the Bundesbank with a brief description of their services and their suitability for fulfilling the aforementioned requirements. Responses are to be sent to efida-markterkundung@bundesbank.de by 09 October 2026 with the subject line "Market exploration pursuant to Section 28 VgV: Provision of interest rate data for the banking and financial services sector". The Deutsche Bundesbank reserves the right to use the results of the market exploration for the preparation of a procurement procedure and thanks you in advance for your responses and support in conducting this market exploration. Lot PAR-0001: Market exploration pursuant to Section 28 VgV - Provision of interest rate data for the banking and financial services sector. This market exploration serves exclusively to gather information and prepare a potential procurement procedure. It constitutes neither an invitation to submit a tender nor preliminary information within the meaning of public procurement law. A procurement procedure may be initiated at a later date if applicable. The aim of the market exploration is to gain an overview of data offerings available on the market regarding interest rate data for the banking and financial services sector. In particular, the data should contain information on deposit and credit products of supervised institutions and be usable for statistical, analytical and market monitoring purposes. Of particular interest are data offerings that enable the highest possible market coverage, timely provision and long-term historical evaluation capability. The data should be provided in such a way that it can be efficiently integrated into existing analysis and evaluation processes. The Bundesbank is particularly interested in data offerings that meet the following technical requirements: clear assignment of conditions to specific products, such as call money, fixed-term deposits, consumer loans and mortgage financing; indication of the offering institution; indication of the interest rate or respective condition; indication of the term or contractual maturity of the product; clear documentation of the publication or validity date; traceability of the source of the publication, e.g. website of the institution, online deposit platform or other publicly accessible source; as timely a provision of the data as possible after publication of the respective conditions, ideally within one to two days; availability of historical data for the formation and analysis of long-term time series; broadest possible and transparently documented coverage of the relevant banking market; possibility for legally secure internal storage, processing and evaluation of the data. Furthermore, providers are asked to explain within the scope of the market exploration the extent to which the offered data is historically available, how frequently it is updated and what delay typically exists between the publication of a product offering and provision in the data stock. The following requirements in particular are placed on technical provision: structured and machine-readable provision of the data; provision in common formats such as CSV, Excel, JSON, XML or comparable formats; possibility of automated data access, for example via an API, database interface, ODBC or comparable technical solutions; clear documentation of the data structure, data fields and update logic; lowest possible manual effort in retrieval, processing and integration of the data; comprehensible handling of corrections, data gaps or subsequent changes. Providers are requested to provide information within the scope of their response in particular on market coverage, data quality, timeliness, history, technical provision, licence and usage rights as well as potential cost and pricing models. Of particular interest is whether long-term internal storage and evaluation of the delivered data as well as use for internal analysis and reporting purposes are permissible. In addition, information is requested regarding which security measures are taken to protect the access and usage history.

sig_38986fa46939d895c50f.description: For this project We have 6 modules. Each module is made up of 3 stages. These stages are (1) an x-y stage, (2) a tilt goniometric stage, and (3) rotational stage. The links to these stages and the control box can be seen in the attached supporting document. The difference between our stages and the COTS stages is that each stage has a different motor to the COTS item (integrated 485 bus-type closed-loop stepper driver, IRS42E-K02, manual available). All modules are controlled via a single controller box. The controller box has power and user instructions from control software (via RS232 to USB cable) as inputs and has six output cables, each connected to one of the modules (RS232 to RS232). Each output cable is limited to 2m length. The cable from the controller connects to the bottom most stage of the module, that is the x-stage. The x-stage is then connected to the y-stage via a RS232 cable. The y-stage is connected to the goniometric stage via a RS232 cable. Finally, the goniometric stage is connected to the rotational stage via a RS232 cable. In this way, a controller with 6 outputs controls 6x4=24 motors. This setup is shown in the diagram and a picture of a single module is also provided on the attached supporting document. The control signal is sent via the control box to the desired module. If the control signal is not for the x-stage, the control signal is passed up the chain, and so on. We need the control software to interface with our existing hardware to control the 6 modules. The solution could interface with the existing control box, or alternatively provide a new controller to interface with the 6 modules. The requirements above are for the software/control of the 6 modules. Lot LOT-0000: . None

sig_38ff39f46aa4f8f627f0.description: Maintenance, support and expansion of CEFTA TRACES NT and related SPS digital systems. CEFTA TRACES NT is a digital platform supporting the electronic processing and exchange of phytosanitary certificates, veterinary health certificates, CHED-like documents, pharmaceutical permits and notifications on non-compliant consignments. The platform supports traceability, information exchange and risk management in the sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) area. The contract will also support interoperability with local systems and relevant international platforms, as well as gradual alignment with the EU IMSOC approach, including TRACES NT, RASFF/iRASFF, EUROPHYT and ADIS-related functionalities, where relevant. Maintenance, support, further development and expansion of CEFTA TRACES NT and related SPS digital systems. CEFTA TRACES NT is based on the TRACES NT source code provided by the European Commission’s DG SANTE to CEFTA and adapted to support SPS processes and information exchange within CEFTA. The platform supports the electronic processing, issuance and exchange of phytosanitary certificates, veterinary health certificates, CHED-like documents, pharmaceutical permits and other SPS-related documentation and data, as well as traceability, information exchange and risk management between competent administrations. A key objective of the contract is to further develop CEFTA TRACES NT towards fully electronic, end-to-end exchange of phytosanitary and veterinary certificates within CEFTA and, progressively, with the European Union, reducing and ultimately replacing paper-based exchanges where the necessary technical conditions are in place. This will include further development of electronic certification workflows, certificate models, validation mechanisms, electronic signatures and trust services, and the interfaces required for electronic data exchange. The contract will also support the completion, further development and operationalisation of the CEFTA Notification System for plant health and food and feed safety, including notifications concerning risks, non-compliant consignments, rejections and related follow-up information. The contract will cover continuous maintenance, security, performance and reliability of the platform, as well as upgrades and new functionalities required to respond to evolving operational needs. It will also support interoperability with local SPS systems of CEFTA Parties and relevant EU and international systems, including the further development of interfaces and automated data exchange to minimise duplicate data entry. Further development will seek to maintain close technical alignment with the EU IMSOC environment and TRACES NT, as well as relevant notification and information-exchange processes linked to RASFF/iRASFF, EUROPHYT and ADIS, where applicable. The overall objective is to establish a progressively integrated SPS digital environment enabling reliable electronic exchange of certificates, notifications and other SPS information within CEFTA and between CEFTA and the EU.
sig_38ff39f46aa4f8f627f0.title: CEFTA TRACES NT Maintenance, Expansion and SPS Digital Systems Support

sig_390b1259a85dd646febb.description: IFIRS is tendering on behalf of Business Academy Aarhus a framework agreement for the provision of services in relation to further and continuing education activities targeted at the employment sector, including identification of competence needs, development of educational activities and additional services for the unemployed targeted at employment. The tender is divided into sub-agreements within the following subject areas: Leadership, Communication, sales and customer experience, IT and digital marketing. The sub-agreement includes subjects within the Academy Profession Degree in Leadership (e.g. Leadership in practice 10 ECTS). This will only concern subjects from the relevant curricula that have a workload level of 5 and 10 ECTS, which corresponds to a course for the unemployed under the designation "6 weeks of self-selected education". The sub-agreement includes subjects within the Academy Profession Degree in Communication and Media (e.g. Social media 10 ECTS) and the Academy Profession Degree in Sales and Marketing (e.g. Sales and sales psychology 10 ECTS or Strategic sales and Key Account management 10 ECTS). This will only concern subjects from the relevant curricula that have a workload level of 5 and 10 ECTS, which corresponds to a course for the unemployed under the designation "6 weeks of self-selected education". The sub-agreement includes subjects within the Academy Profession Degree in Information Technology (e.g. Application of artificial intelligence 10 ECTS) and the Academy Profession Degree in Sales and Marketing (e.g. Digital Marketing 10 ECTS or E-commerce 10 ECTS). This will only concern subjects from the relevant curricula that have a workload level of 5 and 10 ECTS, which corresponds to a course for the unemployed under the designation "6 weeks of self-selected education".
sig_390b1259a85dd646febb.title: Provision of services in relation to further and continuing education activities-EA

sig_3992b8dde9210f30441e.description: Market dialogue for a new competition for a Logon System for the Health Companies in Helse Vest.Sykehusinnkjøp HF shall, on behalf of Helse Vest IKT, procure a quick, secure, seamless and user-friendly log-on system for PCs as well as central professional applications for the clinical environments. The system shall enable employees to log in quickly and ensure authentication. The reason for the need is due to a long log-on time with the current system and several professional applications to deal with in the daily work. Therefore there is a great need for a system that contributes to freeing up the time currently used for logging in. Imprivata ́s system has been tested in clinics and such a form of solution shows considerable time savings. Sykehusinnkjøp HF is now preparing to announce a competition and therefore wants to obtain information from relevant tenderers who can deliver equivalent systems and/or systems that fulfil the need. The contracting authority would like to obtain market information from relevant tenderers. See the attached document for further information.

sig_39daf211ccd08ff86d93.description: Bromford Flagship LiveWest (BFL) wants to procure a single, modern Learning Management System (LMS) to provide a unified learning and compliance platform across the organisation. The proposed solution will replace existing learning platforms and support the delivery, management and reporting of learning across the organisation. The LMS will serve a workforce of more than 6,000 colleagues across a geographically dispersed operating area, supporting a wide range of roles including housing, property maintenance, customer services, corporate services, leadership and specialist functions. BFL requires a scalable, cloud-based solution capable of managing mandatory, role-specific, compliance, onboarding and professional development learning through a single platform. The system must support both internal colleagues and external users, including contractors, suppliers and customers. The proposed contract is anticipated to be for an initial term of 3 years, with the option to extend for up to a further 2 years. The contract value stated within this notice is an estimate over the initial 3 year contract term. sig_39f2c23a14b1414a3519.description: The Welsh Government seeks to appoint a contractor to deliver and further develop a pan-Wales programme of business events industry engagement and lead generation activity over a two-year period. Building on the findings and recommendations of the Mid and West Wales Regional Engagement Pilot, the programme will support the development of stronger regional networks, increased industry collaboration, improved destination readiness and enhanced lead generation activity that aligns with the National Events Strategy for Wales, Tourism strategies and wider Welsh Government priorities. The programme is intended to build long-term industry capability and resilience, enabling stakeholders to take increasing ownership of engagement, collaboration and opportunity development activity beyond the life of the contract. The primary aims and objectives of the contract are to: • Strengthen engagement with business events stakeholders across Wales. • Increase industry awareness and understanding of business events opportunities and support available through Meet In Wales. • Develop stronger regional networks and improve collaboration between destinations, local authorities, venues, hotels and industry partners. • Support destinations and businesses to identify, develop and pursue business events opportunities. • Improve the quality and quantity of lead generation activity across Wales. • Facilitate engagement with key intermediaries including agencies, event organisers, trade organisations and relevant industry bodies. • Identify barriers to growth and provide recommendations to support the development of Wales' business events offer. • Create mechanisms for sharing market intelligence, opportunities, best practice and industry updates. • Support the North Wales educational project by encouraging relevant industry representatives from across Wales to attend, engage fully in the sessions, take learning from the programme and apply this throughout the lifetime of the project. • Ensure opportunities to engage industry are fully utilised, including encouraging businesses to meet current Visit Wales accreditation requirements, secure an appropriate product listing, and explore opportunities to be bookable online through the TXGB distribution channel where relevant. • Support the development of a sustainable pipeline of business events opportunities that can deliver economic and wider benefits to Wales. • Provide measurable outcomes, regular updates and reporting and recommendations that support future business events policy and industry development activity. • Build industry capability, knowledge and confidence to support a sustainable and increasingly industry-led approach to business events engagement and opportunity development across Wales. • Develop and implement a clear transition and exit plan that enables industry stakeholders to assume greater ownership of networks, engagement activity, intelligence sharing and opportunity development by the end of the contract period. Provision of server hosting services under a framework service agreement for a duration of 18 months. The winning tenderer's task is to provide server hosting services to the Contracting Authority for a duration of 18 months up to a net framework amount of 100.128.000 HUF, for which amount the Contracting Authority undertakes a call-off obligation of 100 percent. High-standard placement of the Contracting Authority's server machines and the provision of related technical and professional services. Ensuring smooth operating conditions, a high-quality technical environment and continuous high-bandwidth connection for servers and telecommunications equipment, while maintaining the services continuously. Data centre requirements The Contracting Authority's requirement regarding the data centre is that it must have a machine room with at least TIER III or equivalent certification*. Power supply for the area (hosting) For every rack cabinet, at least 2 independent power-supplying IEC320 electrical distribution strips and network connectors must be provided. Statics Provision of a ceiling/raised floor capable of bearing the total weight of a fully loaded (approx. 1360 kg) standard (19-inch, 42U high (1970x600x1200)) rack cabinet. Fire protection, air conditioning, power supply, utilities Fire protection Fire protection as prescribed for electrical rooms. Sensors and an automatic gas-based fire extinguishing system. Operational environment Ensuring a server room temperature in accordance with manufacturer specifications, which is a redundant air conditioning system maintaining a maximum of 22 ± 2°C, which performs cooling from under the raised floor through the rack cabinets. The maximum humidity can be 50% (MSZ EN 300 019-1-3:2003 3.1 class: Controlled temperature placement according to standard). Ensuring the intake of fresh, filtered, dust-free air. Ensuring protection against water damage for the machine room. The ceiling, floor and walls of the machine room must be free of water and gas pipes. Lighting Brightness as prescribed for office rooms. Power supply The electrical (high-voltage) and data communication (low-voltage) cabling of the rack cabinets takes place through the raised floor, with a full Cross Connect solution. Application of a cable management system A system that records cable routes and labels entering the building from the outside and running inside the building, which facilitates new installations and dismantling. Circuit breakers Individually and regularly interruptible (miniature circuit breaker or individual switch) high-voltage power supply per rack cabinet and per feed. Sub-meters Redundant, 3-phase high-voltage power supply provided with a separate sub-meter. The provision of power supply must be solved for the cabinets with a separate sub-meter. The Contracting Authority pays the electricity fee to the winning Tenderer monthly based on actual consumption. Calculation of the electricity consumption fee: Electricity consumption fee = Measured consumption * Electricity fee corrected by cooling factor a.) Measured consumption: monthly consumption measured based on an individual consumption meter b.) Electricity fee corrected by cooling factor (PUE - ratio of the data centre's total power consumption to the power consumption of IT equipment) Uninterruptible power supply Uninterruptible power supply system (understood together with generator and uninterruptible power source). Security • The machine room must have 0-24-hour live security service. • Every entry and exit must be logged, and it must ensure the object and machine room access protection requirements set by NIS2. • There must be a camera surveillance system in the machine room. Recordings of the camera surveillance system concerning the Contracting Authority's area must be kept for the maximum of 30 days determined in the relevant legislation and the possibility of viewing must be provided upon request. • Entry of only pre-registered persons is permitted alongside photographic and personal identification documents. • Independent entry of the Contracting Authority's staff takes place according to the defined security regulations. • Physical access to the machine room must be provided 7x24 hours per week. • A continuous monitoring system must be in operation. • Must have a valid and tested disaster recovery plan. Telecommunications DDoS network (Layer3, Layer4) level protection The DDoS network service must provide automatic or manual DDoS protection in case of bandwidth-consuming or connection-based (Layer3 (IP) or Layer4 (TCP/UDP) level) attacks. The DDoS protection service must have at least 100 Gbps attack handling capacity, or must be provenly capable of handling volumetric attacks hitting the Contracting Authority's internet connection. The solution must ensure a continuous monitoring interface, and must also be able to provide a reporting interface. sig_3a48dd21108b2e189500.description: In line with technological evolution and the principles established in the Digitalisation Plan for Public Administrations and the National Cybersecurity Strategy, the trend in public sector corporate networks is moving towards architectures based on separate and isolated networks, using protocols running over Layer-3, such as SD-WAN, to create convergent communications services that enable: - Operational efficiency to be increased and management costs to be reduced. - Intelligent and proactive traffic management to be incorporated, particularly through the application of advanced analytics and artificial intelligence techniques. - Native integration with perimeter security systems and operations centres (SOC) to be facilitated. - The use of hybrid links (fibre, 4G/5G, Internet, etc.) to be permitted, guaranteeing high availability of services. - Scalability and flexibility to be ensured when opening new offices or launching new municipal services. In the field of office interconnection, the City Council of Ávila aims for an even more advanced and robust approach, replacing SD-WAN-based networks with Layer-2 networks capable of transporting VLANs based on the 802.1Q protocol. One of the fundamentals of this requirement is not to lose performance, such as the extremely low latency currently enjoyed, which is characteristic of campus networks or metropolitan area networks, constituted by point-to-point circuits. The City Council of Ávila is promoting an evolution towards a communications model based on the principles of robustness, agility, security, integration and scalability, in order to guarantee a modern, efficient and resilient infrastructure that supports the institution's digital transformation and continuous improvement in the provision of services to citizens. Based on this, the telecommunications services of the City Council of Ávila are being tendered, covering the areas of fixed and mobile telephony, broadband Internet access, data transmission between offices and associated services, as well as the maintenance of the infrastructures necessary for their correct provision. The contract seeks the provision of the related services and the comprehensive maintenance of the equipment and infrastructures necessary to guarantee the correct provision of the services throughout their validity, including the essential LAN equipment to provide the VoIP service, understanding that these are essential services for the proper functioning of the City Council.
sig_3a48dd21108b2e189500.title: Telecommunications service for the City Council of Ávila (fixed telephony, mobile, data, internet and associated services) distributed in 3 lots

sig_3a776fefa39e632dc03f.description: The Public Diplomacy Section (PDS) at U.S. Embassy Tunis invites results-oriented proposals for programs that foster economic opportunities for U.S. businesses and investors, innovation collaboration, showcase American leadership and excellence in science, technology, culture, the arts, sports, education, and English language, and strengthen ties between the United States and Tunisia in ways that make America safer, stronger, and more prosperous as we commemorate the 250 th anniversary of U.S. independence (2026) and 230 years of U.S.-Tunisian friendship (2027). All proposed programs must include an American element or a connection with American expert(s), organization(s), or institutions in ways that promote increased understanding of U.S. policies, perspectives, and society and/or celebrate U.S. culture and values. Proposals that include programming outside Greater Tunis or across multiple governorates and/or promote increased collaboration and networking among alumni of U.S. government programs are encouraged. Examples of possible PD small grant proposals include, but are not limited to: • Subject-matter expert, academic, and professional lectures, seminars, and speaker programs that include U.S. speakers/experts. • Programs that connect U.S. companies with Tunisian partners, suppliers, and market opportunities, facilitate business-to-business networking and investment matchmaking, prepare Tunisian startups and established businesses to meet U.S. market standards, enter U.S. markets, and partner with U.S. investors. • Sports diplomacy, culinary diplomacy, art exhibitions, film festivals, theater, musical theater, musical performances and master classes. • Cultural heritage conservation and preservation programs, including through use of new and immersive technologies, such as virtual reality (VR) or augmented reality (AR) technology. • U.S.-Tunisian University-industry partnerships, including with research or technology parks, that generate mutually beneficial commercialization projects or that create opportunities for U.S. companies in STEM fields and emerging technologies and innovation. • Hackathons, STEM or Maker Space camps/competitions, or other related hands-on activities that showcase American leadership and excellence in innovation and STEM fields, including but not limited to space exploration, technologies with beneficial applications to daily life developed as a result of NASA initiatives, or that foster target audiences’ artificial intelligence (AI) adoption and readiness. • University and cultural institution linkages programs that include but are not limited to development and implementation of a course, joint PhD advising, or joint degree program, or the design and teaching of a jointly-led course that includes virtual or in-person instruction from a U.S. professor/expert in fields outlined under Excellence in Education and English Teaching priority outlined in this APS. • English language programs, including but not limited to teacher training and programs that share innovative American English teaching methodologies, specialized English courses to improve business opportunities and innovation collaboration with U.S. companies, investors, U.S.-Tunisian university-industry partnerships, and foster economic self-reliance among target audiences. • Podcasts. • Professional and academic exchanges and programs. (Note: This funding cannot be used to support construction-related activities. End note.) Priority Program Areas and Strategic Themes: Proposals must focus on one of the five priority areas outlined below: ECONOMIC PROSPERITY AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP: Initiatives that expand U.S. commercial and investment opportunities; strengthen U.S. ties with Tunisia’s entrepreneurship ecosystem; promote U.S. entrepreneurial values and practices; and/or share best practices of successful U.S. business partnerships, startups, and investors with the aim of creating economic opportunities for U.S. and Tunisian businesses and investors. CELEBRATING AMERICA’S 250thANNIVERSARY AND U.S.-TUNISIAN ENDURING PARTNERSHIP: Initiatives, including innovative, small-scale programming and programming at our American Corners, that: 1) celebrate U.S. scientific breakthroughs, innovation, economic dynamism, sport prowess, agricultural strength, national parks, tourism, public service, freedom of speech or press, and other ideas and partnerships that shaped America’s development during the 250th anniversary year of U.S. Independence (2026) and in honor of the 230th anniversary year of the 1797 treaty of friendship between the U.S. and Tunisia (2027); 2) showcase and share American excellence in visual and performing arts, music, theater, film, and cultural heritage protection, including through artistic and cultural workshops, performances, exhibitions, or other activities, including community service initiatives that bring together Americans and Tunisians during the 250th anniversary year of U.S. Independence (2026) and the 230th anniversary year of the 1797 treaty of friendship between the U.S. and Tunisia (2027); 3) leverage people-to-people or institutional ties through sports or cultural diplomacy initiatives to increase the Tunisian public’s awareness and understanding of the history and benefits of the over two centuries of U.S.-Tunisian friendship, trade, and security cooperation. INNOVATION AND COLLABORATION IN SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY: Initiatives that encourage artificial intelligence (AI) adoption and readiness in Tunisia through use of U.S. AI platforms and technologies; raise awareness and promote collaboration on projects related to the 2027 solar eclipse; and expand U.S. ties to Tunisia’s innovation ecosystem through research collaboration and university-industry partnerships, including research and technology parks, to generate mutually beneficial commercialization projects that create opportunities for U.S. companies in STEM fields (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics), including but not limited to cybersecurity, space, energy, water security, food security, smart agriculture, health technology, and AI. MEGA DECADE OF SPORTS: Initiatives that leverage the U.S.-hosted 2026 FIFA Men’s World Cup, 2028 Summer Olympics and Paralympics, and 2034 Winter Olympics and Paralympics, in ways that strengthen people-to-people ties between the United States and Tunisia, promote American values, and demonstrate U.S. economic strength, infrastructure, and excellence and leadership in sports and tourism. Excellence in EDUCATION AND ENGLISH TEACHING : Initiatives that showcase American leadership and excellence in education and English teaching in public or private institutions; provide specialized English courses to improve opportunities with U.S. companies/investors for target audiences; and foster innovative collaboration between U.S. and Tunisian higher education institutions to enhance Tunisian participants’ understanding of U.S. culture, values, history, and policies, including in American studies, culture, and literature, freedom of speech, the arts and creative industries (film, music, design thinking, and cultural entrepreneurship), cultural heritage preservation, tourism and hospitality, municipal management, water and/or waste management, urban design, and STEM fields. Program and application details are available in the TUNIS APS FY2026 Questions should be addressed to PASTunisSmallGrants@state.gov

sig_3ae9239d240fc8183d6d.description: This notice provides information on the process and characteristics of the open market consultation, as well as preliminary information on a potential procurement process for the solution. The purpose of this notice is to provide advance information on the holding of an open market consultation (or preliminary market consultation, PMC) to gather market availability, or the possibilities for the market to provide and systematically integrate AI-based solutions to support Catalonia's early breast cancer detection programme. Specifically, it is of primary interest that the application of AI tools makes it possible to optimise the resources of the early detection programme, facilitating the extension of the screening age range (from 45 to 74 years of age) while guaranteeing human supervision and service quality. Specifically, solutions that: • Have CE marking certification and comply with the applicable regulatory framework regarding the processing of personal health data (GDPR (Regulation (EU) 2016/679)), medical devices (MDR (Regulation (EU) 2017/745)) and AI systems and models (AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689)); • Are applicable to the use cases identified in the context of breast cancer screening: general use on the population currently invited to the programme (digital mammography in women aged 50 to 69 years); population in the lower extended age range (digital mammography in women aged 45 to 49 years); population in the upper extended age range (digital mammography in women aged 70 to 74 years); and dense breast cases (digital mammography in women aged 45 to 74 years with dense breasts (BI-RADS classification C or D) without a prior history). • Can be integrated into the care workflow established by Catalonia's early breast cancer detection programme, taking into account the current organisation and dynamics of the teams and also the ICT tools and infrastructures of the Catalan public healthcare system (SISCAT). The PMC is being carried out as a prior step to the preparation of a potential public procurement of innovation (PPI) and all interested economic operators are invited to participate. The PMC will offer an overview of the objectives of the potential PPI and of the procurement process, providing pre-market information to prepare for submitting bids for the future potential PPI. On the other hand, the PMC involves the analysis of existing technologies and an opportunity to formulate questions to economic operators and cross-check the results with the previous state-of-the-art analysis. Thus, the PMC must allow for: — Analysing whether the required technologies are commercially available and acquiring information on the advantages and disadvantages and the level of compliance with the desired functionalities; — Identifying market risks that may jeopardise commercial objectives and the supplier's task; — Enabling and increasing opportunities for industry to form suitable consortia to achieve the intended objectives of the contract. The PMC will begin with a public presentation event, open to all interested economic operators. In addition, a questionnaire will be provided via the website to gather information from suppliers and available solutions. Operators who respond to the questionnaire will also have the opportunity to conduct bilateral interviews, should they wish to provide additional and/or more detailed information. All detailed information and documentation regarding the execution of the PMC, deadlines and participation options, as well as the information provided during the consultation, will be duly published on the contracting entity's profile (https://contractaciopublica.gencat.cat/ecofin_pscp/AppJava/perfil/AQuAS) and additionally on the Salut/AI Programme website (https://iasalut.cat/reptes/).). This notice also provides early-stage information on the potential procurement process for the solution and the expected date for carrying out the PPI. The potential contracting process will be carried out using an open procedure for the public procurement of innovative services in which a single supplier will be contracted.
sig_3ae9239d240fc8183d6d.title: Preliminary market consultation for innovative solutions based on Artificial Intelligence (AI) to support Catalonia's early breast cancer detection programme

sig_3aea0b680baabbf79381.description: The ESM is launching a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) as defined in the ESM Procurement Policy for consultancy services. The ESM’s current Consultant Panel will expire on 30/04/2025 therefore it is necessary to have new Framework Agreements in place to replace the expiring ones. We encourage candidates to submit their application by the 23/01/25 to ensure sufficient time for the assessment and the contract signature process to have new Framework Agreements in place by 01/05/25. The consultancy services are grouped in four categories: CATEGORY 1 ­ Financial services, CATEGORY 2 ­ IT services, CATEGORY 3 ­ Corporate services, CATEGORY 4 ­ Banking and economic services. Each category is composed of various Disciplines. Candidates can bid for one or multiple Disciplines. All procurement documents are available on the ESM website and the ESM e-procurement tool (InTend).

The subject of the tender is the conclusion of a framework agreement for the provision, introduction, integration, support and further development of vulnerability management for the contracting authority's IT landscape. The goal of the procurement is the transition of an already existing basic technical structure into a stable, permanently operable and future-proof regular operation. For this purpose, a suitable software solution including the necessary licences or subscriptions as well as the services required for operation and further development must be provided. The solution should enable the structured identification, analysis, assessment, prioritisation and tracking of vulnerabilities within the contracting authority's IT landscape. The scope of services includes in particular the provision, setup, configuration, integration, optimisation and ongoing support of the solution. This includes integration into the contracting authority's existing system and process landscape, support in establishing and ensuring operational readiness, improvement of scan coverage, optimisation of data quality, and the provision of suitable reporting, analysis and control functions. Furthermore, existing IT service management processes are to be supported and suitable interfaces for the acquisition, processing and transfer of relevant information are to be provided. The framework agreement does not establish any minimum purchase obligation for the contracting authority. The quantities, hourly rates, reference quantities, demand values and maximum quantities specified in the tender documents serve exclusively to determine the contract value, the comparability of the tenders and the award evaluation. There is no entitlement to the actual call-off of these quantities or services.

sig_3c6906217ed34d1b7a09.description:
Väylävirasto is preparing a procurement, the subject of which is the operating services for the road information systems of Väylävirasto, which suppliers will produce with the help of expert teams. The expert service to be procured includes operator services for six different information systems of Väylävirasto. The procurement is divided into the following four sub-areas. - Sub-area 1 Operation of Tievelho; - Sub-area 2 Operation of the Structural Register; - Sub-area 3 Operation of maintenance and - Sub-area 4 Location reference operation. The goal of the procurement is to ensure the smooth use of information system data from the perspective of data utilisation and updating, and to support the development of information systems. The expert teams will consist of road data experts, structural experts, operators, and technical experts. The roles include both senior and junior-level professionals. The length of the contract has been tentatively set at three years, plus an option of up to two years. Companies interested in the procurement are requested to register for the market survey in accordance with the registration instructions presented below. In the call for tenders, the tenderer may submit a tender for one or more sub-areas. A tender may be submitted independently, together with subcontractors, or as a consortium. Companies interested in the market survey are requested to notify as soon as possible, but no later than 30.9.2026 at 23.00 by filling out the electronic registration form: https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/ErRyRq6yXZ The market survey consists of the opportunity to comment on the draft material of the tender before the publication of the call for tenders. Please note that this is a market survey notice and this notice does not yet request tenders. Failure to respond to the market survey notice does not prevent participation in a potential call for tenders. The information presented in this market survey notice and the estimated publication date of the call for tenders are preliminary and indicative advance information, which does not bind Väylävirasto to any kind of decision. The preliminary goal of Väylävirasto is to publish the contract notice in January 2027. The market survey notice does not oblige Väylävirasto to carry out the actual procurement procedure. The procurement will form an expert team to support system development, maintenance, and specification, which will be responsible for user support, training, supporting data production processes, data processing and updating, quality management, information services, and documentation and communication related to operation. The experts will identify development needs that arise during operation and convey them to the client and to the separately procured development task specification service. The experts will act at the interface between Väylävirasto, system users, data producers, and maintenance, specification, and further development suppliers. The planned expert team will consist of road data experts, operating service experts, technical data management experts, and project data management experts. The expert team will have both junior and senior-level professionals. A short description of the information system that the supplier's expert team will operate: Basic data repository for road information (Tievelho): Basic data repository for road network infrastructure, condition and measurement data, restrictions, decisions, and classification data.; The procurement will form an expert team, whose tasks include, among others, quality assurance of the Structural Register data, checking and updating data, checking data to correspond to prevailing guidelines, checking data content and quality assurance, checking and updating process diagrams, and specifying data content. The planned expert team will consist of structural experts who have experience in using the Structural Register. A security clearance will be conducted on the experts. A short description of the information system that the supplier's expert team will operate: Structural Register: The Structural Register is a basic data repository for structures and an asset management system. In addition to administrative and structural data, it contains, for example, damage and condition data on structures such as bridges, tunnels, and fixed sea marks. In addition to objects owned by Väylävirasto, the register also contains data on structures owned by municipalities and cities. The Structural Register serves, for example, the experts and service providers of Väylävirasto, Centres for Economic Development, Transport and the Environment, as well as municipalities and cities. The system is being developed and the data content is being expanded continuously.; The procurement will form an expert team, whose tasks include ensuring the smooth use of maintenance information system data from the perspective of data utilisation and updating. A key goal is to ensure that maintenance information systems contain and are provided with up-to-date, high-quality, and structurally uniform data. The background is an identified need to: • Develop and implement quality control of data in maintenance information systems. • Maintain data in maintenance systems. • Produce data and materials for the needs of experts. • Develop and implement a uniform way of data management • Support data production processes in the production and utilisation of road data and maintenance data. • Develop, support, and supervise the data management related to road maintenance of Väylävirasto and Centres for Economic Development, Transport and the Environment • Develop and maintain instructions and documentation related to the utilisation and updating of maintenance data • Support Väylävirasto in development projects related to maintenance and road data management. The planned expert team will consist of operating service experts. The expert team will have both junior and senior-level professionals. Short descriptions of the information systems that the supplier's expert team will operate: YHA: Repair management system YHA (formerly

maintenance management system) is used for programming repair sites (selection, prioritisation and timing of sites and measures), calculating the impact of the planned programme, reporting and monitoring condition data, and exporting contracts to the Harja system. The system is used to manage repair measures for existing paved roads, walking and cycling routes, and gravel roads. Harja: The Harja system is used to monitor, supervise and report on the financial, qualitative, temporal and quantitative execution of highway maintenance contracts, surfacing and road marking contracts, lighting contracts and waterway canalisation contracts. The content of different contract types varies. Harja is one of väylävirasto's largest information systems.; The procurement establishes an expert team whose tasks include supporting the operation, testing and definition of systems related to the Väylävirasto location referencing framework. Tasks include, among others, road addressing of roads related to the creation of the road address network in conjunction with the Centres for Economic Development, Transport and the Environment, work related to the maintenance of Suravage geometry, support for the testing and definition of Viite (Road Address System) and the Framework Converter, and tasks related to the maintenance of the road address network. The expert team will consist of road data experts. Brief descriptions of the information systems that the supplier's expert team will operate: Viite: Road address system maintenance application. There is a need to make changes to road addresses due to the completion of road projects or administrative decisions. There are three tasks in the maintenance of the road address system: Maintenance of road addresses (including carriageway data (but not lane data)), maintenance of road names, and maintenance of nodes and junctions. In Viite, road addresses are linked to the frozen road link geometry of the Centre Line Geometry Repository, and road address maintenance takes place in a map user interface based on road link geometry. When maintaining road addresses, road address history is also preserved in Viite. Road addresses are used to record the locations of data related to highways. The most significant system utilising road addresses is Tievelho. Framework Converter (Viitekehysmuunnin): A REST-type interface application used to convert road locations from one location referencing framework to another, for example to obtain coordinates for a road address. The data to be converted is sent to the Framework Converter using a GET/POST request, the application processes the data and returns the converted data to the calling application as a response. The interface service is publicly available on the internet. In addition, there are separate authorised interface addresses for the service.

sig_3c84a101b6a6579c69c9.description: The National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS), with other NIH Institutes and Centers (ICs), intends to publish a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) to investigate the mechanisms of action of therapeutic medical devices with the overall goal of improving clinical outcomes with device-based approaches. Medical devices are essential in managing health conditions, complementing drugs and behavioral interventions, and often offer unique benefits. Despite the commercial availability of numerous medical devices and ongoing development of new technologies, many have shown inconsistent results in preclinical studies, failed translation to humans, and exhibit varied patient outcomes. To overcome these challenges, it is crucial to understand the mechanisms by which medical devices produce a therapeutic effect, to identify physiological markers of neurological conditions, and to assess how device-based therapies influence these markers. Advancing this knowledge will improve device-based interventions, inspire new device designs, and optimize current clinical approaches. Applications will be invited from interdisciplinary teams pursuing innovative research on how medical devices produce a therapeutic effect. Applicant teams will likely exhibit expertise in areas such as engineering, biology, pathophysiology, surgery, clinical care, healthcare delivery, biostatistics, software development, computational modeling, artificial intelligence, regulatory science, and clinical trials. This program will accept projects on investigational devices and those already FDA-approved and in clinical use. Applications are expected to include strategies for developing or optimizing therapies that could significantly improve patient care. Supported research may include mechanistic clinical trials, animal studies, and computational modeling or simulation. Applications are not being solicited at this time. Notice is being provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations and responsive projects.
sig_3c84a101b6a6579c69c9.title: HEAL Initiative: Optimization of Therapeutic Medical Devices through Team Science Mechanistic Research (RM1)

About the work Why the work is being done The work is being done to support the growing demand for high-quality data both within the department and the wider sector. The work of the central data team support and range of activities across that provide data support across the department, ALBs and wider transport sector. This includes the delivery of the actions in the transport Data Action Plan (DAP) with an increased focus on how we can further support local authorities and transport organisations with greater devolution of the transport sector. This technical data work sits alongside research to support the DAP and our ambitious AI programme. The work is being specified as individual SOWs to ensure we align to the current priorities for government and to make the most of technology in a complex and evolving landscape. Problem to be solved Following on from the transport DAP we are looking to deliver improved capacity and maturity of data projects across the DfT and greater collaboration across the wider sector. With a focus on both enhanced governance and communication while continuing to innovate as new technology is developed. This contract is design to compliment some of the research being undertaken for the action plan and the AI Delivery, Development, Research and Evaluation Support contract. This contract is designed to allow us to move quickly when new areas of work are identified and to support data projects across the wider DfT. Who the users are and what they need to do The contract is to support analysts, engineers and data specialists in continuing to improve and modernise our internal data landscape. This is to support policy development, analysis and enhanced use of Google Cloud technology to meet our commitments in the transport Data Action Plan. Preliminary market engagement A pre-market engagement call took place on 26th August. The slides and Q&A document are attached. Work done so far We have existing data maturity assessments and governance but these need to evolve in light of changes in technology and the increased importance of data in the wider transport landscape. We have already undertaken a discovery on APIs for DfT which can be found here: Developing application programming interfaces at DfT - GOV.UK Following this, work has begun on building an API developer portal in Apigee to host and share the first wave of DfT APIs. Existing team The existing central data team sits with the Chief Data Office in the Analysis Directorate. The central data team (D:ETLA) is around 20 experts covering: data engineering, data policy (inc. governance, maturity and standards), data transformation (delivering on the data action plan) and a crisis data function. We sit alongside the advanced analytics team who lead our internal AI programme and data science functions and the central stats team who has responsibility for our geospatial data strategy. We work alongside colleagues in our digital service function on a range of technical projects using GCP. sig_3e158d950d7f50ced64b.description: Digital Care Hub is seeking an independent evaluation partner to assess the delivery, impact, sustainability and value for money of the Better Security, Better Care (BSBC) programme. Funded by the Department of Health and Social Care, BSBC supports approximately 28,000 CQC-registered adult social care locations in England to improve cyber security, data protection and information governance, including compliance with the Data Security and Protection Toolkit (DSPT). Delivery is led nationally by Digital Care Hub through more than 30 Local Support Organisations, combining central leadership, guidance, training, communications, data analysis and performance management with trusted local support. The supplier will design and deliver a proportionate mixed-method evaluation covering programme governance and delivery, stakeholder engagement, partner effectiveness, reach, changes in awareness and behaviour, adoption of good practice, DSPT outcomes, organisational resilience, wider benefits, cost effectiveness, return on investment and social and economic value. The work should identify lessons, good practice and evidence-based recommendations while providing ongoing insight to support continuous improvement. Key deliverables are an evaluation framework and inception report within three months; ongoing data collection, analysis and stakeholder engagement; monthly progress meetings; an interim report by September 2027; and a final evaluation report, shorter executive report, presentation and dissemination-ready outputs by October 2028. Close-down and dissemination support will continue to March 2029. The proposed contract runs from October 2026 to March 2029, with a maximum budget of £125,000 inclusive of VAT. Bidders must demonstrate strong experience in programme and economic evaluation, publicly funded programmes, mixed-method research, stakeholder engagement and report writing. Knowledge of adult social care, health and care systems, cyber security, digital transformation or information governance is required. Tender responses must include organisation and personnel details, methodology, data collection and analysis plans, delivery timetable, resourcing, quality assurance, risk management, up to three relevant examples, a full pricing schedule, assumptions and proposed social value. Evaluation weightings are: understanding 15%, methodology 35%, experience 20%, project management 10%, social value 10% and price 10%. The supplier must comply with UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018, confidentiality, insurance, procurement, equality and safeguarding requirements. Clarification questions are due by 14 October 2026 and tenders by 18 October 2026. Please see attachment for full specifications.
sig_3e158d950d7f50ced64b.title: Independent Evaluation of the Better Security, Better Care Programme (October 2025 to October 2028)

sig_3e73758e8dae6ea8c0b8.description: The Directorate of DigitalIsation (Digdir) invites tenderers to give input on collaboration models for issuing a digital wallet in Norway. This request for information is related to the ongoing work with a CONCEPT CHOICE assessment (KVU) for issuing a digital wallet in accordance with the eIDAS2.0 regulation. This has been efficient and given us rapid and high spreading of eID in the population, and thus contributed to the fact that public and private actors have been able to digitalise a great many services. The national eID strategy has, however, pointed to some challenges with the current model, i.a. connected to not everyone having access to eID "High" within the current market-based systems. The eIDAS2.0 Regulation requires Norway to offer inhabitants and residents a free digital wallet at a security level "High". The regulation also requires most social sectors, both public and private, to accept the wallet for log-in, identification and different areas of use. This also applies across EU/EEA countries, which means that Norway be required to accept the digital wallets of others in norway. In addition to this, we see the introduction of digital wallets in the work with the KVU in connection with the challenges and needs described in the national eID strategy. Reply This is an open invitation to market participants, and there are no special form requirements for the feedback. Each market participant is free to emphasise what they find most relevant in their responses. However, we have prepared an overview of questions that can function as a guide, which gives an indication of which areas we would like feedback on. Response to this RFI (both questions and input) is sent via the communication module in Mercell.Deadline for written responses: 18 December 2025Se attached documents for further information.
