sig_3ee832445041b66999b9.description: The Kölner Verkehrs-Betriebe AG (KVB) intends to publish one or, where applicable, several procurement procedures for the procurement of validators including a background system and relevant software interfaces, likely from the year 2026. In order to improve KVB's level of knowledge regarding the technical and commercial aspects of such a procedure, KVB is conducting a market consultation pursuant to Section 26 of the Sectoral Procurement Ordinance (SektVO) ("industry dialogue"). As part of the industry dialogue, KVB will inform itself about, inter alia, 1. Functionalities of validators (hardware, software) and background systems 2. implementation options for KVB 3. commercial aspects (pricing models, price range, cost factors). Subject of the industry dialogue: KVB intends to replace the mobile ticket vending machines in the trains and buses with validators. These are intended to function without paper and cash based on contactless EMV transactions and to be embedded in an ABT/IDBT-capable system. Travel entitlements are to be stored as encrypted tokens in a cloud-based background system, whereby both providers and cloud storage must at least have the necessary ISO 27001 certification. The operation of the background system in a cloud environment must be subject to the European General Data Protection Regulation. The validators must make it possible to purchase a specific, independently configurable range of tickets (pre-selection) and additionally support an interoperable check-in/check-out procedure with integrated best-price calculation for the customer. All physical and virtual payment instruments that comply with the EMV standard (EC card, credit card, Google Pay, Apple Pay, etc.) must be accepted; in addition, payment via a prepaid card (closed-loop) must be possible. KVB reserves the right to commission a financial/payment service provider with the processing of payments. Corresponding software interfaces/APIs must therefore be supported/addressed. The payment options are to be expandable in the future. The customer must be able to view and manage their travel entitlements (ABT) independently via an online portal (web portal). The web/online portal is to be provided in KVB's corporate design. In addition, further software interfaces to a central customer account, which is set up internally by KVB, are to be provided. It must be possible to use a token that is linked to another person's payment medium. The control of the issued travel entitlements must be ensured across transport associations (at least throughout NRW) and made possible by corresponding software interfaces from the provider. A control option must also be possible when the validator is offline. The regular processing of blacklists is supported. Current and future developments of VDV-KA and (((eTiCore must be taken into account. The background system must contain at least the following software interfaces: - Ticketing back office with payment gateway and connection to payment service provider - Device management - Key management - Customer management - Enterprise asset management system - Fault notification software interface The background system should promote interoperability and must be able to be integrated into an overarching system landscape. The accounting data from the validators must be able to be integrated from there into the sales accounting system PATRIS (LHIND). Participation in the industry dialogue / qualification criteria: If potential bidders are interested in participating in the industry dialogue, KVB requests notification by email by no later than 23.9.2025, 10:00 hours, to the contact point daniela.lehnert@kvb.koeln. The references must be submitted in full by this time. When expressing interest in participating in the industry dialogue, the following qualification criteria / capabilities of the bidders must be proven and submitted. KVB reserves the right to exclude bidders whose qualification is not proven or is not sufficient based on proven references / documents from the industry dialogue and not allow them to participate in the industry dialogue. Submission of 2 references regarding previously executed contracts / services that are comparable to the advertised service in terms of subject matter and scope. The comparability of a reference requires that the subject matter of the reference contract includes at least the successful implementation / introduction of an ABT/IDBT system including mobile validators and a background system in public transport. In one of the reference contracts, the system must have been implemented on the basis of contactless EMV transactions. The reference contracts must not date back more than 5 years. The reference projects must have been implemented in Europe. The relevant factor in this regard is the date of acceptance or complete performance of the service. The following details must be provided in the reference: a) Name and address of the respective reference client b) Brief description of the reference project c) Contractual role of one's own company in the reference project d) Meaningful description of the nature and scope of the service provided (by oneself) e) Details of any (own) subcontractors f) Description of the comparability of the project (essential overlaps / parallels to the present industry dialogue) g) Duration of the project h) Contact person (naming a contact person who can confirm the reference and is authorized to provide information to KVB regarding the quality of service provision)

sig_3f443255f38bcabd6daa.buyer_original: Bundesamt für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik
sig_3f443255f38bcabd6daa.description: Artificial Intelligence (AI) methods demonstrate astonishing performance in many application areas and are increasingly used in areas that affect daily life. The field of cybersecurity has not remained untouched by AI either. New AI tools are published almost daily in this context, and large AI language models (LLMs) in particular are already being used today for various application purposes. At the same time, the threat landscape is changing significantly as benignly intended models are misused for attack purposes (dual use). As a consequence, it must sometimes be assumed that vulnerabilities will be discovered and exploited ever faster in future with the increasing capabilities of AI. Against this background, the defensive side must also take action, which is why this project is intended to investigate how AI can be used profitably in the SSDLC and what effects ongoing developments have on the security of software. For this purpose, the project is divided into three parts, with related but distinct services: In work package 1-4 [HM1.1], a study on the current state of the art and science in the field of AI in the Secure Software Development Life Cycle is to be drawn up. In addition, best practices for the use of identified AI tools are to be developed. The results are to be published. In work package 5-6 [HM2.1], based on the study and in cooperation with the BSI, the contractor shall review the evaluation criteria for AVA scoring in Common Criteria certification and update them in view of new circumstances. In addition, an implementation plan for the use of AI tools for conformity assessment bodies is to be created. In work package 7, a reference architecture is created for the Open CoDE platform, which illustrates how AI tools can be integrated into the Secure Software Development Life Cycle and the software environment of Open CoDE. Suitable tools are to be proposed in this regard. Lot LOT-0000: KI im Secure Software Development Life Cycle (KISDL). sig_3f48acbeeee6adfeb946.description: The aim of the procurement is to establish a framework agreement for the delivery of equipment, consumables and production services for the production of standardised brands for locations and equipment in Helse Sør-Øst. The procurement shall support the implementation and use of uniform physical and digital identification of locations and equipment based on international GS1 standards. Locations shall be able to be identified by use of GS1 GLN and the equipment shall be able to be identified by use of GS1 GIAI, in the form of GS1 Digital Link and other standardised GS1 syntaxes. Through the use of international standards, marks shall be able to be used by digital systems in Helse Sør-Øst, e.g. systems for Facility Management (FM)/property management, clinical logistics, medical engineering, ERP, etc. The procurement shall result in: - Standardised types of brands for locations and equipment. - Support for multiple information carriers on brands - Support for local production of brands - Support for production of large volumes of brands as external services. - Standardised production basis. - Secure management of business critical information. The procurement includes systems for both local production of brands in the health companies, and production of large volumes of brands. The system for local production can include production equipment, necessary software and/or integration components, consumables, equipment for encoding/programming NFC and UHF RFID, training, support, maintenance and documentation. The contracting authority will, together with the chosen supplier, establish a set of standardised brand types that will be used for the production of labels for locations and equipment. A tag type is a documented specification that specifies how a brand should be designed and produced.

sig_401c9b3a1aeaaeac68f3.description: This is a Prior Information Notice (PIN) with the purpose of assisting the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA) in engaging the market by gathering information. This PIN has the purpose of a fact-finding exercise and only. Background Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA) are exploring options to digitalise payments out of the Agency in a bid to reduce payable orders. A specific user case includes invoice-based payments. Invoices are returned with information to support a customer's application. These applications, information and invoices are currently paper based which are scanned and digitalised in-house. On receipt of the information and sufficient checks, a payment is made by payable order to those named on the invoice. The payable order process is also managed in-house and posted from DVLA. Volumes In this example, for the financial year 2025-26, 221,406 individual payable orders were issued, with a net value of approximately £14.8M. Considerations - The payments are made to anyone qualified to complete the supporting evidence, so there is no static list of payees. There could be around 60,000 individual payees which fluctuates. Some are repeat payees and some are one off payees. - The payees include individuals and company accounts from across the UK. - The invoices (currently paper based) include the payee bank information (account number, sort code). - The invoices are then scanned and a digital copy held. - As a Government Agency we are required to follow all HM Treasury guidance outlined in the 'Managing Public Money' published documentation. - This includes not being able to use intermediary bank accounts outside of the Exchequer pyramid. - DVLA do not have an existing BACs business as usual process for payments out. - DVLA has explored Open Banking for this user case and feel that due to the considerations above it doesn't fully meet our requirements. Project aims - Digitalise movement of funds - Reduce/remove payable orders - Improve invoice management processes - Improve customer experience Information required - Potential solutions to support the project aims aligned to the considerations - Any costs associated with developing and implementing the solution including any licences or additional external costs. - Any ongoing costs associated with ongoing running of the solution. - Time taken to develop and implement the solution. - Any wider considerations, fees or any other supporting information. - Do you provide this type of service for any other large organisations? - How can DVLA procure from your organisation? e.g. Are they on a framework? If so which one? Do we need to go through any third parties to obtain their services? Please provide a response via email to the above question to Michelle Palmer - Michelle.Palmer@dvla.gov.uk by 5pm on May 13th 2026
sig_401c9b3a1aeaaeac68f3.title: DVLA Payments Out

This Pre-Market Engagement Notice is issued solely for the purposes of information gathering and engagement with the market. It does not constitute a call for competition and create any obligation on the Authority to proceed with a procurement exercise, or enter into any commercial arrangement. Please note the procurement route and anticipated publication date for this opportunity are yet to be determined. These elements will be confirmed following completion of the market engagement process and development of the Authority’s commercial strategy. Any learnings will be used to formulate the associated procurement strategy. BLC work in collaboration with blue light organisations to maximise commercial benefit to UK emergency services. The focus of this solution will be improving Victim & Citizen Engagement, building trust and confidence, reducing demand within control rooms, and reducing the costs of serving the public by using innovative software to keep both victims and citizens more engaged. The aim is to ensure all forces have access to the most effective, reliable, and innovative solutions available in the market. This Solution needs to facilitate the force contact engagement from first contact with a police force to final closure of the contact, and via integration with police systems, e.g. Command and Control, Records Management Systems providing contact and updates throughout the journey without the need to call the force contact centre. It seeks to further drive standardisation and consistency, whilst helping forces to develop capability and invest in technology which will not only improve the service at first point of contact but will improve the overall contact experience. This Solution must facilitate Victim & Citizen engagement to reduce failure demand whilst proactively engaging to ensure high levels of customer (internal and external) trust and confidence. The delivery of the desired solution may be considered to follow the same customer service path as an online application or ordering process. For example, acknowledgement of the initial contact, time appropriate follow up contacts at defined points within the communication journey, and a closure contact at the end of the process. All communication will be auditable and align with the Victims code as appropriate. We are looking for solutions that can meet individual force needs and achieve the following: *Improve experience of members of the public accessing the policing service *Provide the public with consistent updates in a timely manner, *Improve public trust, confidence, and satisfaction, *Reduce Contact Management demand, *Improve force's overall Contact Management performance. sig_418d8d9a6769dfce9ec2.description: As part of the FSA’s commitment to ensure food is safe and is what it says it is, the FSA undertakes food safety risk assessments which underpin these decisions in line with the internationally recognised ‘Codex Working Principles for Risk Analysis for Food Safety’. A key component of food safety risk assessment is exposure assessment, which estimates the amount of a hazard consumed through the diet. Exposure assessment combines food consumption data with information on the concentrations of substances such as contaminants, food additives or pesticide residues in food to estimate the levels consumers may be exposed to. To conduct UK dietary exposure assessments, the FSA uses consumption data in combination with occurrence data for hazards and other substances in food. UK consumption data is primarily obtained from the UK National Diet and Nutrition Survey (NDNS). The National Diet and Nutrition Survey (NDNS) is a co-funded programme between the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) Office for Health Improvement and Disparities (OHID) and FSA. NDNS is a rolling programme which assesses the diet, nutrient intake and nutritional status of the general population of the UK. Tenders are invited to carry out the recoding of NDNS consumption data to FoodEx2, a standardised system for classifying and describing food. Lot 1: . None
sig_418d8d9a6769dfce9ec2.title: Coding NDNS Consumption data into EFSA’s food classification+description -FoodEx

sig_4241ee1527fd0e26e35d.description: NHS Scotland intends to procure a National Digital Diabetes Prevention Programme to support individuals identified as being at risk of developing Type 2 Diabetes. The programme will deliver a structured, evidence-based lifestyle intervention through a digital platform, including access to health coaching, peer support, and tools to support behaviour change and self-management. The procurement is expected to be undertaken via a Restricted Procedure, with a single supplier appointed to a national framework. Lot 1: . This Prior Information Notice (PIN) relates to NHS Scotland’s intention to tender for a National Digital Diabetes Prevention Programme. The programme will identify individuals at risk of Type 2 Diabetes based on clinical indicators (including HbA1c and fasting plasma glucose levels) or a previous diagnosis of gestational diabetes. It will provide a tailored, nine-month, evidence-based lifestyle intervention aimed at reducing the risk of progression to Type 2 Diabetes. The digital service will support Service Users via an application-based platform, providing access to trained health coaches, online peer support communities, and functionality to set, track, and monitor personalised health goals. The successful bidder will be required to deliver the programme in a way that is inclusive and accessible to Service Users from diverse linguistic and cultural backgrounds. This will include ensuring the service is culturally sensitive to local populations and flexible enough to meet the needs of users with diverse requirements, including appropriate language support. Participants will be able to access the programme through multiple referral routes, including Primary Care (e.g. GP referral) and self-referral pathways. Current funding has been allocated to support up to 15,000 users over a three-year period. The proposed framework will operate as a single-supplier arrangement and will also include provision for the delivery of a Hypertension Pathway for approximately 500 users per annum. Eligibility for the hypertension pathway will be based on a confirmed diagnosis of primary hypertension alongside a BMI ≥25 (or BMI ≥23 for minority ethnic groups). Please Note: During the term of the Framework Agreement, NHS Scotland reserves the right, should funding become available, to increase the volume of service users (current estimate of 15000 over the initial 3-years of the Framework Agreement term) who may access the Programme. For example, additional purchases may be made which exceed the level of funding currently secured as a result of clinical and service outcomes and benefits which support wider adoption of the Programme. The Authority also reserves the right to expand the scope of the service to include additional cohorts, pathways, or clinical indicators (for example, the inclusion of further at-risk populations identified through screening), which may increase overall demand under the Framework. The procurement is expected to be conducted using a Restricted Procedure, comprising two stages: Stage 1 Selection Stage (SPD Assessment): Suppliers will be required to complete and submit a Single Procurement Document (SPD). This stage will assess bidders’ suitability to proceed and will include a combination of pass/fail criteria (e.g. mandatory and discretionary exclusion grounds, economic and financial standing) and scored evaluation. As part of the SPD, the Authority will assess technical and professional ability, including responses to scored questions and requests for relevant examples of previous experience. These responses will be weighted and scored to enable the Authority to evaluate capability and rank suppliers. A shortlist of the highest-ranking bidders will be invited to progress to Stage 2. Stage 2 – Invitation to Tender (ITT): Only suppliers shortlisted at Stage 1 will be invited to submit a full tender. Bidders will be required to respond to a Statement of Requirements (SoR), setting out how they will deliver the contract, including proposed methodology, service delivery model, and pricing. Tenders will be evaluated in accordance with the published award criteria, based on quality and price, to determine the Most Economically Advantageous Tender (MEAT). Stage 1 is expected to commence mid to late August 2026, with Stage 2 anticipated to commence in early October 2026.. This project is derived from the Accelerated National Innovation Adoption (ANIA) Pathway. This is an initiative focused on using technology to fast-track proven innovations into the healthcare frontline on a Once for Scotland basis. See link:https://www.nhscfsd.co.uk/our-work/innovation/accelerated-national-innovation-adoption-ania-pathway/

sig_42a2ad5cb89a181e57ba.description: The Stadt Münster - citeq is setting up a dynamic purchasing system with a time limit until 30.12.2025 for the digitisation of paper files. This is the publication of the extension of the dynamic purchasing system (pursuant to Section 23 paragraph 2 no. 1 of the German Public Procurement Ordinance (VgV)) initially until 30.12.2026. A dynamic purchasing system in accordance with Section 120 paragraph 1 of the German Act against Restraints of Competition (GWB) is a time-limited, exclusively electronic procedure for the procurement of standard market services where the characteristics generally available on the market meet the requirements of the contracting authority. An unlimited number of contractors are publicly invited to submit non-binding declarations for the provision of services, and all suitable contractors that have submitted admissible declarations for the provision of services are admitted to participate in the system for the entire duration of the system. An application to participate is possible at any time. Companies will be informed of their admission to the dynamic purchasing system via the communication area on the procurement marketplace. Following the publication of the dynamic purchasing system, an initial time limit of 30 days must be observed before opening applications to participate. Thereafter, no further time limits apply and new applications can be opened immediately. These applications will be evaluated within ten working days of receipt. If an individual award is pending, all admitted companies will be invited to submit a tender.

sig_43d2a12892c49a99bb9c.description: Høje-Taastrup Kommune is considering procuring the purchase and support of AV equipment as well as devices (PCs and tablets) for the schools sector as operational leasing. This means a solution where the supplier undertakes the delivery, assembly, operation, maintenance and support of equipment as a solution where the supplier owns the equipment and the municipality obtains the right of use via payment of an annual fee. Therefore, the municipality wishes to enter into a dialogue with 2 - 3 suppliers of such types of IT equipment to discuss what the municipality should pay attention to in connection with procurement. Some documents are enclosed that describe some of the intended content in a procurement (requirements, wishes, etc.). The dialogue will be based on these documents. Initially, the municipality wishes an indication of whether you will enter into a dialogue with the municipality regarding such a procurement, as well as a response with some initial thoughts that you as a supplier have regarding a procurement of this type of operational leasing. As inspiration for this, here are some initial questions: Is the best way to procure the goods and services via 2 procurement or can both types of services (AV and PC/tablets) advantageously be combined in one procurement? Is there anything we should be aware of that a contract must contain and/or absolutely not contain: e.g. breach of contract, penalty - how do we handle defects in the equipment? Will the fact that the supplier owns, assembles and services e.g. AV equipment provide an advantage e.g. via the supplier's strict control of drivers/software as well as versioning of these components in relation to a more stable, well-functioning and cohesive AV solution across the municipality? Are there other things we should be aware of? Here, consideration is given to advantages the municipality can achieve and the disadvantages that may lie in such a solution. The intention is that equipment is to be replaced in an ongoing process. This means the supplier will take over support on e.g. existing AV equipment. The dialogue is intended as an informal discussion of advantages and disadvantages/risks of establishing such solutions. It is not immediately intended that actual transfer of employees should take place; the intention is to establish another and more efficient way to operate and support the mentioned solution areas.
sig_43d2a12892c49a99bb9c.title: Consultation regarding the procurement of leasing for AV equipment and devices for the schools sector in Høje-Taastrup Kommune

sig_43e7d2d7b65e40a467aa.description: Provision, implementation and operation of a cloud-based, SaaS-based data-centric security platform (DSP) for the analysis, monitoring and protection of data and access permissions in a hybrid IT environment (on-premises and cloud) of the Stadtwerke Düsseldorf AG including affiliated companies. The aim of the procurement is to create transparency regarding data stocks, access authorizations and security-relevant activities, as well as to support measures to increase information security and comply with regulatory requirements in the KRITIS environment. In addition to the provision of the platform, the service also includes supportive services for the analysis, evaluation and prioritisation of security-relevant events as well as for the derivation of suitable measures. The processing of all data shall take place exclusively within the scope of the EU GDPR. An uninterrupted transition from existing near-production operations must be ensured. The aim is to conclude a contract for the provision, implementation and operation of a scalable, cloud-based data-centric security platform (DSP) for the analysis, monitoring and protection of data and access permissions in a hybrid IT environment (on-premises and cloud). The solution must cover the following functions and services in particular: - Analysis and evaluation of data stocks, data access and permission structures, including the identification of potential security and data protection risks, - The solution should have integrated functions for detecting anomalies in user and system behaviour (User and Entity Behavior Analytics) - Creation of transparency regarding effective accesses and permissions, - Detection and evaluation of conspicuous, risk-prone or security-relevant activities, - Provision of monitoring, reporting and verification functions to support audit, compliance and security requirements, particularly in the regulated KRITIS environment, - Support in deriving and implementing suitable measures for risk reduction (e.g. adjustment of permissions or restriction of access rights), - Integration into the client's existing hybrid system landscape (in particular identity services, file and cloud storage as well as collaboration platforms) via standardised interfaces, - Provision and operation of the solution including maintenance, ongoing development, updates and technical documentation in a SaaS model. In addition, services are to be provided that support continuous evaluation, assessment and prioritisation (managed detection and response) of security-relevant events and provide recommendations for action. If configured accordingly, these services may also include operational support services. Continued operation requirements: - Ensuring an uninterrupted transition from existing near-production operations, including a suitable migration and transition concept, - Taking over existing configurations, evaluations and settings as far as technically possible, - Guaranteeing compatibility with existing system landscapes, role and permission models, - Minimising migration, integration and training efforts while taking cost-effectiveness over the entire life cycle into account, - Ensuring continuous operational capability during the transition phase. All services relating to the client's data or metadata must be provided exclusively within the scope of the EU GDPR.
sig_43e7d2d7b65e40a467aa.title: Provision and operation of a SaaS-based data-centric security platform (DSP) for the analysis, monitoring and protection of data and access permissions

sig_45182218dce81071619d.description: The objective of the request is to establish a dynamic purchasing system (DPS), the preliminary subject of which is the security technologies and related services required for the implementation of technical information security and compliance. The DPS to be established would enable, among other things, the procurement of the following solutions, technologies and services as needed: - Security event management, analytics and response automation. Examples include SIEM, SOAR and other similar solutions, security alert enrichment, correlation, prioritisation, workflow automation, hyperautomation and AI agent-based automation. - Analytics and artificial intelligence solutions to support security monitoring and response. Examples include AI/ML-based solutions to support SOC operations, improving analyst efficiency, automation of threat hunting, and supporting anomaly detection and investigation. - Threat intelligence management and utilisation in security monitoring and response. Examples include the management, combination, automation, analysis and utilisation of threat intelligence collected from public, open, commercial and other sources in anomaly forecasting, enrichment and decision-making, including Threat Intelligence Platform (TIP) solutions. - Asset management for security monitoring needs. Examples include solutions that create and maintain up-to-date and unified visibility into environments containing IT, OT, IoT and medical devices, including devices, software, software versions, dependencies, integrations with existing asset management solutions, and the utilisation of SBOM data. - Third-party and supply chain risk management. Examples include automated solutions supporting supplier information security risk assessment, continuous monitoring and software supply chain risk management. - Network traffic security event detection and response. Examples include Network Detection and Response (NDR) and other similar solutions for analysing network traffic, identifying anomalies and supporting automated or guided response. - Safe utilisation of artificial intelligence and usage monitoring. Examples include solutions for managing, monitoring and protecting the use of artificial intelligence, generative artificial intelligence and AI agents in the organisation, as well as the risks associated with their use. - A system/solution intended for the handling of security incidents (case management), into which all data related to incident handling, such as memory dumps, log data, actions taken, evidence, etc., can be collected securely as part of the DFIR process. - SandBox tools for malware investigation and operational analysis. In addition, probable general requirements/boundary conditions concerning all potential procurement packages are: - Solutions should in principle support a multi-tenant model or otherwise be suitable for a multi-tenant environment. - Solutions should in principle be integrable with security event management and response automation solutions (e.g. SOAR) as well as log management solutions, and support the large-scale utilisation of artificial intelligence. - Procurements to be implemented may include, inter alia, the following: consulting, maintenance, development, deployment, integration and expert services. - Istekki may procure technologies for its own use, exclusively for customers' use, or for the use of both Istekki and customers. The objective is for the establishment phase of the dynamic purchasing system to commence in May-June 2026. Please note that this is a prior information notice (hereinafter referred to as the notice), and this notice does not yet constitute a request to participate. The information provided in this notice is preliminary and may change as preparation progresses. REGISTRATION. Companies interested in this dynamic purchasing system (DPS) are requested to register for the market dialogue by email at: hankinnat@istekki.fi no later than 17.4.2026 (with the subject "Tietoturvapalveluiden DPS"). The personal data of registered persons will be used solely for contacts related to the preparation of this dynamic purchasing system. MARKET DIALOGUE. Draft material related to the dynamic purchasing system under preparation will be sent to registered companies for comments, in a so-called market dialogue, during an estimated period of 05/2026. Registered companies will be given the opportunity to comment on the draft material in writing. The market dialogue and materials will be in Finnish. Participation or non-participation in the market dialogue does not preclude participation in a potential procurement procedure.

The contract is divided into lots as follows: • Lot 1 "Audit Consultancy"; • Lot 2 "Finance Consultancy"; • Lot 3 "Internal Control Consultancy". The exact nature and characteristics of each lot are defined in Part III of these special tender conditions, "Technical Requirements". Each tenderer has the opportunity to submit a tender for one, several or all lots. No limit is set regarding the number of lots that can be awarded to a single tenderer. Organisation of sessions Sessions shall be organised on demand. Only sessions actually ordered shall be invoiced. Consultancy team For all lots, consultancy sessions taking place in accordance with receptive bilingualism (participants expressing themselves in their language role), the tenderer must, on pain of nullity of the tender, propose consultants who understand the interventions of the participants in both official languages of the Brussels-Capital Region (French or Dutch); or must propose at least 1 primary French-speaking consultant and at least 1 primary Dutch-speaking consultant. In addition, the tenderer may propose substitute consultants in each of the two language roles. Place of performance The various lots of the support system may be organised in an in-person or remote format, depending on the circumstances and the needs of the administrations. In-person services shall be provided in Brussels on the premises of ERAP or within the Brussels administrations benefiting from the services carried out under the contract. Estimated quantity The duration of this contract is set at 36 months and commences on the date indicated upon notification of the contract award decision. During this period, the contracting authority may place subsequent contracts (orders) in accordance with the arrangements defined in these special tender conditions, without however exceeding the maximum volume of orders specified below. The contracting authority does not undertake to order up to the maximum quantity, which therefore does not constitute a quantity to which the contractor is entitled upon conclusion of the framework agreement. Conversely, if the maximum quantity of orders is reached, the framework agreement has exhausted its effects and no further orders may be placed, even if the framework agreement has not reached its term in terms of duration. Estimated quantity: 780 half-days of 3h00 of consultancy for lot 1 "Audit Consultancy" for the duration of the public contract. 252 half-days of 3h00 of consultancy for lot 2 "Finance Consultancy" for the duration of the public contract. 189 half-days of 3h00 of consultancy for lot 3 "Internal Control Consultancy" for the duration of the public contract. These estimates are not binding on the contracting authority. Lot 1 "Audit Consultancy" The mission of ERAP is to support Brussels public administrations in strengthening their organisational control through a dynamic and continuous management cycle. This cycle, based on the Deming approach (Plan-Do-Check-Act), includes the planning, execution, verification and adjustment of processes, thereby enabling continuous improvement. Internal audit, an independent function within public administrations, intervenes ad hoc in this cycle to evaluate the effectiveness of management systems and measure their performance. It makes it possible to identify process weaknesses, analyse risks, and propose recommendations. Furthermore, within the more specific context of whistleblowers, audit ensures the independence and objectivity of the handling of reports, while ensuring process compliance and the implementation of corrective actions when necessary. The services consist of carrying out audits to evaluate management systems and internal processes, while providing expertise to improve internal audit systems. This support is primarily intended for Managers and Internal Auditors of the administrations.; Lot 2 "Finance Consultancy" In a context of increasingly limited resources and growing demands, local authorities face complex challenges to ensure the continuity and efficiency of their missions. Maintaining a short- and medium-term budgetary balance while reconciling financial imperatives with a citizen-centred approach constitutes a major challenge. In this context, exploring new sources of funding, optimising expenditure and strategic management of investments are becoming essential priorities. Finance consultancy services consist of supporting the efficient management of financial resources by proposing tailored solutions adapted to the specific features of the public sector. They aim to optimise the organisational structure of financial services, support the improvement of financial processes and accompany the transition towards new practices, while fostering team buy-in for the necessary changes.; Lot 3 "Internal Control Consultancy" The Brussels-Capital Region has driven the implementation of internal control within local authorities through several legislative articles, including articles 263-11, 12 and 13 of the ordinance of 5 March 2009 "amending the New Communal Law", as well as those of the Ordinance of 14 March 2019 amending the law of 8 July 1976 and the organic law of CPAS. These provisions make communes and CPAS responsible for the implementation and monitoring of internal control of their activities. This internal control, defined as a set of measures and procedures, aims to guarantee security, compliance and performance in several key areas: 1.

The achievement of objectives 2. Compliance with laws and procedures 3. The reliability of financial and management information 4. The efficient use of resources 5. The protection of assets 6. The prevention of fraud In this context, the services consist of supporting a global and integrated approach to internal control, with an emphasis on risk management, process optimisation and the strengthening of an organisational culture geared towards continuous improvement. They intervene by identifying, evaluating and managing risks, while establishing and optimising action plans aimed at controlling these risks. In parallel, they thereby strengthen the culture of internal control within the administrations. Finally, they introduce practices making it possible to continuously evaluate and improve the internal control system, thereby guaranteeing its long-term effectiveness.

sig_458037be25f5ba8cc32b.description: 1. Objective As part of this market survey, suitable software solutions for the digital management and tracking of human milk processes (mother's own milk and donated human milk) in a clinical environment are being sought. The goal is a system for the complete, audit-proof mapping of all processes, taking into account the requirements of the SoHo Regulation, with a focus on patient safety, traceability and process automation. 2. General requirements The software must ensure end-to-end digital documentation and traceability; provide interfaces to SAP and Copra 5/6; automate workflows and notifications; integrate label printing and scanning processes; and enable role-based access. 3. Mother's Own Milk The software should enable the registration of mothers on the ward with an SAP connection, assign a unique mother ID, record CMV status including information and consent, document the amount of milk expressed, allow labels to be created by staff or the mother, track the storage location and inventory, and provide automatic alerts for CMV inactivation (day 7 and 32+0 weeks of gestation). Data on the children such as name, date of birth, week of gestation and weight should be automatically transferred from SAP or Copra. 4. Processing Mother's Own Milk CMV-inactivated milk should be pooled by day, assigned in batches by bottle, labelled, inactivation documented, and cooling processes and storage locations noted. Centrifuged milk should be processed analogously, including documentation of duration and revolutions, labelling as skimmed, assignment of analyses and storage. 5. Administration The software should enable the assignment of milk batches to children, offer interfaces to Copra 5/6, record partial quantities via scan and document retrievals. 6. Batch management The software must automatically generate batches based on mother ID, week of gestation, calendar week of birth, calendar week of milk collection and processing type (raw or pasteurised). Colour coding by week of gestation should be adjusted automatically, as should the documentation of the processing day. 7. Human Milk Bank Potential donors should be identified automatically (e.g. >600 ml/day), be able to fill out digital information and anamnesis forms with a signature, and receive a donor ID. Interfaces to SAP, Copra and the laboratory (e.g. ix.serv) should automatically adopt laboratory findings. The software should enable approvals by specialist staff, evaluation of findings and labelling of pasteurisation requirements. 8. Donated milk The software should record milk quantity, date, time, calendar week, temperature, microbiological samples and storage locations. 9. Processing of donated milk Raw milk should be pooled by day, assigned in batches and stored until release. Pasteurised milk should be processed with documentation of pasteurisation, cooling and storage. CMV-inactivated milk should document pooling, inactivation, cooling and release. Centrifuged milk is processed analogously to mother's own milk, if necessary with additional pasteurisation. 10. Non-released milk The software should document measures such as discarding, re-pasteurisation, training of the donor and repeat samples. 11. Dispensing The software should enable the assignment of batches to wards and individual children and record partial quantities via scan. 12. Summary We are looking for an integrated software solution for the secure, automated management of human milk processes with complete traceability, high system integration and user-friendliness. 13. Participation in the market survey Interested companies are requested to submit their participation and information on the solution by email to vergabestelle@klinikum-stuttgart.de no later than 15.05.2026. The market survey serves exclusively to prepare for a possible procurement procedure. There is no entitlement to the implementation of such a procedure.

sig_45aa5d107594438d760c.description: The London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU) is undertaking a virtual market engagement exercise Wednesday 5th August 2026 @ 10am , via MS Teams, to inform the commissioning of the Online Harms Digital Youth Work Pilot Programme. The London Violence Reduction Unit (VRU) is committed to understanding the factors that place children and young people at risk of violence, exploitation and harm, and to working collaboratively with partners to deliver long-term, sustainable solutions. We work across communities and sectors, including youth services, local government, education, health, policing and the voluntary and community sector, championing a public health approach that combines prevention, early intervention and effective support for those experiencing the greatest levels of risk and vulnerability. At the heart of our approach is the belief that violence is preventable, not inevitable. We recognise, however, that many children and young people are already navigating the impacts of trauma, exploitation, abuse and complex community dynamics. As such, our work seeks not only to prevent harm before it occurs, but also to strengthen the systems, services and trusted adults responsible for safeguarding, supporting and intervening with those most affected. Central to this approach is a commitment to partnership working, evidence-informed practice and ensuring that the voices, experiences and expertise of young people and communities shape the solutions designed to support them. The Mayor's Violence Reduction Unit (VRU) is seeking to engage with the market in advance of a forthcoming procurement opportunity relating to the delivery of its flagship Digital Youth Work Pilot Programme. The programme forms part of the VRU's wider public health approach to violence reduction and sits within a London-wide model developed following extensive consultation with young people, practitioners, safeguarding professionals, academics and sector experts. Digital life brings clear benefits for many children. Ofcom found that 99% of 13–17-year-olds see at least one benefit to being online, including help with schoolwork, learning new skills and maintaining social connections. 93% of children in the UK play video games, and children report that gaming helps them socialise with friends, learn new skills and have fun, with most online interactions taking place with friends they already know offline. At the same time, the VRU is concerned that these same digital environments expose children and young people to a wide range of harms and risks. Digital safety is increasingly a public safety and public health concern. Children and young people are navigating identity, relationships, influence, exploitation and conflict across interconnected online and offline environments. However, systems, services and safeguarding responses have often struggled to keep pace with the rapidly evolving nature of digital spaces. This matters for the VRU because online harms do not sit separately from wider concerns about violence, vulnerability, exploitation and safeguarding. The VRU is seeking delivery partners to pilot innovative Digital Youth Work (DYW) approaches across London that drive new models of engagement with young people and promote safeguarding in digital spaces. The VRU is seeking approaches that: Design, deliver and test new or existing digital youth work models Extend trusted, relationship-based youth work into digital environments Strengthen early intervention, prevention and safeguarding online Generate learning, insight and practical outputs to strengthen future activity The programme aims not only to deliver effective pilot activity, but also to contribute to sector-wide innovation and the development of scalable models of digital youth work across London. Scope of delivery The programme will be structured into three complementary lots: Lot 1: Supporting High-Need and Digitally Dependent Young People Testing approaches that improve accessibility and engagement for young people who face barriers to traditional provision, including SEND. Lot 2: Early Intervention and Prevention of Online Harms Testing models that enable early identification, prevention and response to online risks, with a focus on safeguarding and preventative practice of deterring online to offline violence. Lot 3: Universal Digital Youth Work and Positive Opportunities Exploring how digital youth work can foster connection, creativity, play, participation and digital citizenship for all young people. Bidders may apply for one, two or all three lots. Applications may be submitted by individual organisations or as partnerships/consortia. Target Audience The programme will focus on delivering digital youth work to children and young people aged 11–25 across London, including but not limited to: Young people at higher risk of being impacted by online harms Those facing barriers to traditional youth provision, including SEND and young people who may be more digitally dependent and/or digitally excluded Young people experiencing vulnerability linked to violence, exploitation or disadvantage Young people with caring responsibilities Young people in the care system Young people affected by Violence Against Women and Girls (VAWG) The wider youth population through universal provision Potential delivery settings and workforces may include, but are not limited to: Community-based youth organisations and youth services Detached, outreach and neighbourhood-based provision Faith and community organisations SEND and disability-focused youth provision Organisations supporting young people experiencing vulnerability, exclusion or barriers to traditional youth provision Specialist services working with young people affected by violence, exploitation or online harms Informal education, mentoring and participation-based youth provision Indicative Outcomes The programme is expected to contribute to: Increased engagement of young people in safe, supportive digital environments Improved accessibility of youth work for young people who do not traditionally engage with youth work and are digitally dependent and/or digitally excluded) Strengthened early identification and prevention of online harms in the digital space Increased use of technology to foster positive opportunities Strengthen young people’s digital citizenship Increased workforce confidence and capability in incorporating digital youth work into traditional practice and safeguarding policy Development of scalable models, guidance and practical tools A stronger London-wide evidence base on digital youth work and online safety Timeframe and Budget The maximum estimated budget for this programme is up to £650,000 excl. VAT over a full contract period from November 2026 – March 2029, subject to confirmation of funding, internal governance and relevant approvals. This comprises: £390,000 core funding across the 2026/27 and 2027/28 financial years from November 2026 to March 2028 An extension option of up to £260,000 for a further 12 months from April 2028 The VRU welcomes bids from individual organisations as well as collaborative partnerships and consortia. We recognise that expertise may be distributed across different organisations, and we encourage applications that bring together complementary skills, knowledge and experience. Providers do not need to demonstrate strength across every area independently, provided that the partnership as a whole can evidence the required expertise and capacity to deliver the programme. This may include, for example, combining specialist knowledge in DYW, supporting SEND or neurodiverse children, digital safety, contextual safeguarding, fostering positive digital opportunities, and preventative violence reduction approaches. Market Engagement / Response The VRU welcomes engagement from organisations with expertise in: Youth work and youth engagement Digital youth work Gaming, AI, technology Safeguarding and contextual safeguarding Online harms, exploitation and violence prevention Working with vulnerable and hard-to-reach young people Youth participation and co-production Learning, evaluation and evidence generation If you are interested in the opportunity and meet the core capabilities as set out above, then please join us for our early market warming event on Wednesday 5th August 2026 at 10:00AM. Attending the early market warming session does not constitute a commitment to participate in any future procurement process. The Eventbrite link for market warming session can be found here - https://www.eventbrite.co.uk/e/london-vru-online-harms-digital-youth-work-pilot-market-warming-session-tickets-1994744836503?aff=oddtdtcreator Please note that this exercise is in no way a call for competition and will not result in the award of a contract to any respondents to this notice. If have any further questions about this opportunity, please contact: vruprocurement@london.gov.uk For more information about this opportunity, please visit the eSourcing portal at: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/tenders/UK-UK-London:-Digital-mapping-services./5SJUMP2G3Z To respond to this opportunity, please click here: https://www.delta-esourcing.com/respond/5SJUMP2G3Z Lot 1: Supporting high-need and digitally dependent young people. Background and problem: The DEHSt has been operating end-to-end digitised specialist procedures for approx. 20 years. Central components of the IT landscape used by the DEHSt are in a phase of renewal. The number of software artefacts to be developed by the DEHSt is growing continuously – schedules are therefore becoming increasingly tight and parallelisation and complexity are increasing. Several legacy systems must also be completely replaced. To remedy this, the DEHSt has developed a Software Development Kit (SDK), which consists of software and extensive documentation, for example for commissioning a test and integration environment. The aim of the SDK is, on the one hand, to carry out a technological renewal and, on the other, to significantly increase development speed while maintaining standards. The SDK provides documentation, software libraries, several independent services for the centralised control (workflow control) of the specialist applications, as well as a base and an example application that integrates into the existing software and process landscape of the DEHSt (i.e. addresses existing central services, the so-called 'DEHSt platform'). The SDK and the DEHSt platform are based on a separation of frontend (AngularJS, NgRx, Material), backend (Spring-Boot), distributed web services and a build pipeline in GitLab as well as scalable operation on a container basis (Docker images on RedHat OKD). . Aim and subject of the project: This procurement measure is for a framework agreement with a term of 4 years. The framework agreement can be extended twice by one year each. The project is to include the development and maintenance of the entire Software Development Kit (SDK) as well as the development of specialist applications based on it. We distinguish between three related but parallel task areas: 1) Lot 1: SDK maintenance and management 2) Lot 2: New development of specialist applications 3) Lot 3: Migration and replacement of legacy systems For the SDK team, the goal is to increase the benefit for the administrative staff but also to positively influence the development time of the developer teams. For the developer teams, it must be a goal to develop a high-quality application in the shortest possible time based on an elaborated specification. Lot 1: SDK maintenance and management . According to the current planning status, the contracting authority intends to commission tasks with up to 2.560 person-days (PD) in the first four years. Subject to possible changes in the legal situation regarding European and national emissions trading, the contracting authority expects that at least 50% of the upper limit for person-days mentioned here will be commissioned. Should the contract be extended by one year each, the contracting authority expects tasks amounting to 640 PD per extension (up to 25% of the original scope). For the purpose of approximate capacity planning, we see a demand of approximately 960 PD in the first year and an average of 500 PD per subsequent year. It is assumed that the workload can be distributed relatively evenly over the months so that a constant utilisation of a development team can be achieved.; Lot 2: New development of specialist applications . According to the current planning status, the contracting authority intends to commission tasks with up to 3.056 person-days (PD) in the first four years. Subject to possible changes in the legal situation regarding European and national emissions trading, the contracting authority expects that at least 50% of the upper limit for person-days mentioned here will be commissioned. Should the contract be extended by one year each, the contracting authority expects tasks amounting to 764 PD per extension (up to 25% of the original scope). For the purpose of approximate capacity planning, we generally see a demand of 500 PD per year, but in 2028 and 2029 an increased demand of about 1.000 PD. The utilisation over the course of the year can vary greatly. In most cases, the provision of the specialist applications must take place by fixed legal deadlines. This means that several development projects must be processed in parallel. This is accompanied by an increased personnel requirement that must be covered by the contractor (e.g. two to four development resources work on one specialist application, at the same time up to four specialist application projects must be processed). The legal deadline can unfortunately generally not be influenced by the contracting authority.; Lot 3: Migration and replacement of legacy systems . According to the current planning status, the contracting authority intends to commission tasks with up to 4.472 (person-days) PD in the first four years. Subject to possible changes in the legal situation regarding European and national emissions trading, the contracting authority expects that at least 50% of the upper limit for person-days mentioned here will be commissioned. Should the contract be extended by one year each, the contracting authority expects tasks amounting to 1.118 PD per extension (up to 25% of the original scope). For the purpose of approximate capacity planning, we generally see a demand of 650 PD per year, but in particular from mid 2028 until the change of the trading period in 2030 an increased demand of about 1.450 PD annually. The utilisation over the course of the year can vary greatly. The provision of the specialist applications must in most cases take place by fixed legal deadlines. This means that several development projects must be processed in parallel. This is accompanied by an increased personnel requirement that must be covered by the contractor (e.g.

two to four development resources work on one specialist application, at the same time up to four specialist application projects must be processed). The legal deadline can unfortunately generally not be influenced by the contracting authority.

sig_4702e05e930780e5c8a5.description: The subject of this public contract is a security solution – software and hardware (hereinafter: equipment) for the contracting authority's cyber resilience needs, divided into three lots, namely: • LOT 1: NOZOMI GUARDIAN • LOT 2: SANITISATION OF USB DATA MEDIA • LOT 3: INCREASE OF LICENCE CAPACITY FOR SPLUNK Each tenderer may submit a tender for an individual lot or all lots together. It must be clearly evident from the submitted tender for which lot or lots the tender is being submitted. The exact specifications and requirements of the contracting authority for each individual lot are described in the document Technical Specifications and Requirements of the Contracting Authority, no. 285-60/4-2026 dated 20. 8. 2026, which is an integral part of the documentation related to the award of the public contract or the tender documentation. The subject of lot 1 is the expansion of the existing Nozomi ADS solution for monitoring and detecting cyber threats in the operational and IoT environment - Guardian. The purpose of the lot is to provide sufficient capacities for processing the increased volume of data and thereby maintain an appropriate level of protection and resilience of operational systems. More detailed requirements of the contracting authority are in the document Technical Specifications in point 2.1.; The subject of lot 2 is the supply of a solution for the secure use of removable USB data media in the information and operational environment. The purpose of the lot is to reduce the risk of system compromise via portable media and to ensure a controlled and secure way of transferring data between different environments. The solution must enable simple and secure use and operation without impact on the availability and stability of existing systems. More detailed requirements of the contracting authority are in the document Technical Specifications in point 2.2.; The subject of lot 3 is the expansion of the licence capacity of the existing and already established Splunk system, which is used for the centralised collection, processing, analysis and monitoring of log and security events of information systems. Due to the expansion of the system's scope, the integration of additional information sources and the consequent increase in the amount of log data, the existing licence capacity no longer suffices for actual needs. The subject of the contract is therefore the increase of the existing licence capacity by an additional 30 GB of data per day (30 GB/day) for the period from 1.11.2026 up to and including 31.5.2027. This contract does not concern the establishment of a new SIEM system, but rather the expansion of the licensing of the already implemented and operational Splunk environment, thereby ensuring sufficient capacity for the continued integration of data sources and the smooth execution of centralised monitoring and analysis of security events. More detailed requirements of the contracting authority are in the document Technical Specifications in point 2.3.
sig_4702e05e930780e5c8a5.title: Security solutions - software and hardware

sig_47117cc1f7e8df31d55e.buyer_name: South Karelia Wellbeing Services County; Päijät-Häme Wellbeing Services County
sig_47117cc1f7e8df31d55e.description: This is not a procurement notice or a call for tenders, but a request for information (RFI) whereby the wellbeing services counties of South Karelia and Päijät-Häme invite system suppliers to register their interest for a potential procurement procedure. This is an RFI/market dialogue through which the wellbeing services counties of South Karelia and Päijät-Häme are exploring potential system suppliers for an income and wealth assessment service to determine client fees in social welfare home care and housing services (community-based and round-the-clock living), as well as for compiling maintenance calculations in family law services and potentially for utilisation in other social welfare calculations. With this RFI, the wellbeing services counties of South Karelia and Päijät-Häme are exploring digital solutions for compiling income and wealth assessments for client fee decisions using robotics. The client fee decision is made in connection with the client's service decision, and this has an impact on the management of the client process as well as on invoicing interruptions and terminations. The aim of the market survey is to find out what kind of product solutions containing the functionalities described below are available on the Finnish market. Through the market dialogue, the wellbeing services counties aim to: 1 Obtain information on market supply and different suppliers' solutions 2 Potential implementation of integrations into various platforms or systems 3 Evaluate the implementation of information security and data protection 4 Obtain an overview of pricing models and cost structures (no individual tenders) 5 Explore delivery and service models The market dialogue is open to all suppliers that can offer product solutions falling within the scope of this solution package. The focus of the dialogue is on solutions based on the automated compilation of income and wealth assessments to support client fee decisions. Suppliers are requested to present services that are under development or ready-made solutions. Suppliers participating in the dialogue are expected to present functionality to be put into production and information on how cooperation with the necessary actors to implement integrations has been taken into account in the preparation of the income and wealth assessment service. There is no need for a system solution based on process control, as this would result in additional recording requirements due to system changes. The core data contents consist of, inter alia, the Incomes Register and tax decisions of the Finnish Tax Administration, and benefit data from Kela. In connection with registration, suppliers are requested to briefly describe: Purpose of use and environment The system must be suitable for the wellbeing services county's use for managing the following service forms: - income and wealth assessment for home care - income and wealth assessment for community-based housing, - income and wealth assessment for round-the-clock living - maintenance calculation for family law services, which forms part of a maintenance agreement concluded by parents. The maintenance calculation requires the data of both parents. - In all fees, the income data of spouses must be taken into account where necessary User groups include - children's supervisors - makers of client fee decisions in wellbeing services counties Key functionalities - produce, as part of the determination of client fees, income and wealth data on the basis of which a proposal for the amount of the client fee or solvency is formed - the calculation must not be saved in the income and wealth assessment service, meaning it does not create an archiving obligation. However, it must be possible to generate a PDF/PDF-A document from the document, which the wellbeing services county can attach as part of the decision and archive in a manner it deems fit. Integrations - Data transfer connection to the Finnish Tax Administration via the LIPA service bus (Incomes Register and tax data) - Data transfer connection to Kela's benefit data service via the LIPA service bus Technical requirements - The system must meet DPIA information security requirements - Data flow diagram and architecture description - User authentication and access control - Generation and management of log data Additional information - What other essential features does your solution include? - How is the implementation of the system typically carried out? - What kind of support and training do you offer? - Estimate from decision to implementation - The wellbeing services county's resource requirement Responses to the questions are requested to be sent by 14.9.2026 at 15:00. Responses are requested to be brief and informative. Responses are requested to be sent to hankinnat@ekhva.fi and hankinnat@paijatha.fi Message subject: "Market survey - Income and wealth assessment service system" This RFI/market survey does not request tenders nor are tenders submitted in response to this RFI; it requests ONLY information related to the procurement. Participation or non-participation in the market survey/RFI does not affect the tenderer's position in a potential tendering procedure. sig_473df8db9ba357f2ba51.description: The Universitätsklinikum Münster (UKM) is conducting a market exploration for the introduction of a digital mailroom. The aim is to obtain information on available solutions, technical procedures, price levels and supplier structures. The survey is conducted in a technology- and process-open manner. The processing of incoming and outgoing mail is currently largely manual. External mail is sorted centrally, distributed and then re-sorted within the buildings. This process is time- and resource-intensive. Outgoing mail comprises both bulk and individual mailings. Providers who can already demonstrate successfully implemented solutions and present them as part of a system presentation are invited. Particular areas of focus are: - OCR/AI-supported text recognition in the scanning process - Handling of mail marked personal/confidential - Integration of the special electronic authority mailbox (beBPo) - Digitalisation of internal mail distribution The market exploration serves exclusively to gather information. This is not associated with a procurement decision. Interested providers are requested to submit proposed solutions and references for comparable projects to Universitätsklinikum Münster. Subsequently, the University Hospital will contact applicants it deems suitable.

sig_475872817e19da0f367f.description:
Delivery/provision of a cloud-based software system for time recording (time management - ZWS) & personnel deployment planning (PEP) for medical services, nursing services & other service types. The subject of the procurement procedure is the provision of a cloud-based software solution (Software as a Service) for time recording (time management – ZWS) and personnel deployment planning (PEP) for the medical service (approx. 720 employees), the nursing service (approx. 2.180 employees) and other service types (approx. 1.372 employees – medical-technical service, functional service, administrative service, personnel of the training centres). In addition, approx. 500 internal and approx. 300 external students must also be managed in the system. A market-available standard solution is expressly being tendered, which can be adapted to the client's requirements through parameterisation. Individual solutions or in-house developments are excluded. This applies in particular to the bidirectional interface to the existing SAP ERP R/3 HCM infrastructure as well as to the new SAP S/4HANA environment. Further requirements for implementation, parameterisation, training and process standardisation are part of the tender documents or the specifications. The software must cover the following task areas in particular and must be provided as an integrated overall solution: -Personnel deployment planning incl. holiday and absence management (PEP) -Time management (ZWS) -Preparatory payroll accounting through the creation of collective agreement-relevant wage types in hourly or € values -Employee Self Service (ESS) -Manager Self Service (MSS) -Reporting and statistics. The interaction of these task areas is indispensable for efficient and modern personnel deployment planning, control and accounting. For this reason, these tasks must be closely linked and should appear as a single unit from a technological and user perspective. The solution must be able to be integrated without problems into the IT infrastructure available at the KC (SAP ERP R/3 HCM & SAP S/4HANA HCM & SAP IS-H/i.s.h.med) and must necessarily communicate with the software solutions already in use via standardised interfaces (state of the art). Both master data as well as attendance, absence and wage data must flow uni- and bidirectionally (depending on the data type) via the interfaces. The interface must necessarily work with change data records (data records to be changed in SAP are deleted and newly created or overwritten with new data records) in order to ensure the highest degree of automation and to minimise the need for manual intervention as far as possible. To map smooth processes, the PEP solution must ensure a consistent, secure and media-break-free data exchange. This is essential, especially for employee payroll accounting, and if it were to fail, it would have a lasting negative impact on the operation of the KC. The most automated transfer possible of required data from the legacy systems must be ensured. The new PEP solution must be able to import data from the IS-H/i.s.h.med, convert it into personnel requirements and integrate it into the deployment planning. With the help of the PEP solution, the wage types currently required at the Klinikum Chemnitz for the correct payroll accounting of all service types must be generated in accordance with the collective agreement regulations and transferred to the SAP HCM payroll and salary system in a time-controlled manner. In the medical collective agreement, 39 different wage types must currently be mapped, and in the non-medical collective agreement, 32 wage types. In some cases, wage types are created on an individual employee basis and depend on different conditions such as department, employee qualification, individual agreement. Especially with on-call duties, it happens that within a department, on-call duties are remunerated according to a fixed flat rate or according to the collective agreement regulations. The software solution must be able to map these constellations even within a month (see also the specifications). The connection of employees to the new PEP software solution is to take place in pre-defined waves. Accordingly, it must be ensured that some of the employees continue to be managed on the SAP PEP and other employees on the new PEP solution. The contractor must ensure that both systems function productively in parallel for the duration of the implementation and rollout and do not influence each other. The S/4HANA migration of the SAP ERP R/3 HCM planned in 2026 (Unicode conversion, database migration and S/4 application) must be taken into account. This concerns both project management and the function (bidirectional integration with the legacy systems HCM and ERP and the migration target, no PEP function maintenance after S/4HANA migration in the HCM). In addition, integration with the parallel project S/4HANA migration is required. The PEP solution is to be introduced on the current SAP HCM version ECC 8. Starting 2026, the transition of the SAP ERP R/3 HCM to SAP S/4HANA HCM is to take place, and with it the migration of the PEP software to the new system. Accordingly, it is assumed that the contractor has already successfully migrated the interfaces of their software solution from SAP ECC to S/4HANA and that all required functions are also fully available in the integration with an S/4HANA system (HCM and ERP). A project-specific EVB-IT cloud contract & service contract will be concluded for the procurement. The draft contract is part of this publication as well as the tender documents for the initial offer and can be further specified by the client within the framework of the procurement negotiations. The procurement is for a minimum contract term of 36 months after operational readiness has been established.

Thereafter, the contract shall be extended by one year at a time, unless it is terminated by one of the parties six months before the end of the contract. Details on this can also be found in the tender documents of the subsequent offer phase or offer phases.
sig_475872817e19da0f367f.title: Delivery/provision of a cloud-based software system for time recording (time management - ZWS) & personnel deployment planning (PEP) for medical services, nursing services & other service types

sig_47c4a4474b4f65daf56d.description: The Authority is seeking to engage with the market regarding the upcoming procurement of a national Conversion Practices Victim Support Service. This service provides critical remote support to individuals who have gone through, are going through, or are at risk of conversion practices. The requirement comprises two primary components: Helpline Service: The operation of a bespoke helpline, or integration of comprehensive support into an existing vulnerable-person helpline. Service must operate a minimum of Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm, via telephone & live web-chat/email. Website Management: Transfer, maintenance & expansion of existing information website, which serves as a public repository for legal protections, resources & signposting. A draft copy of the requirements are attached to this notice. Additional information: 3. Key Procurement Parameters & Constraints Contract Duration: 24 Months (with a formal performance review at the 12-month mark). Estimated Financial Value: Strict maximum budget of £80,000 per annum (Inclusive of VAT), totaling £160,000 over the 24-month term. Bids exceeding £80,000 in either year will not be considered. Anticipated Call Volumes: 300 to 2,000 calls per year (call rates are expected to vary and will likely spike at times when conversion practices are receiving media attention). 4. The Transition & Timeline Scenario The Authority is operating under strict budgetary constraints & has no budget available for dual-running contract costs. Contract start date is currently 1 October 2026 (but may be subject to shifting timelines). Regardless of the exact calendar date the transition will be structured as follows: The Final 4-6 Weeks of the Current Contract: The outgoing supplier will utilise this time to execute their exit plan, compiling all necessary data, scripts, website hosting configurations & asset packages. Contract Day 1 (New Contract Start Date): Compiled handover package will be passed to winning bidder on this day. Day 1 Go-Live: Incoming supplier is expected to be fully operational, answering live helpline calls & managing the website immediately from Contract Day 1. 5. Market Engagement & Expression of Interest (EoI) Questions Authority invites interested suppliers to review this information & submit responses to the following questions: Question 1: Primary Requirements Please confirm you are able to fulfil our two primary requirements; Helpline Service & Website Management? (Yes/No) Question 2: Expression of Interest Are you interested in bidding for this requirement when formal contract notice is published? (Yes/No) Question 2: Onboarding Feasibility The outgoing supplier will spend the last 4 weeks of their contract completing their exit plan to hand over to the new supplier on Contract Day 1. We want to know if this is feasible for your organisation. Given you will receive handover documentation & asset package on Contract Day 1, is it operationally feasible for your contact centre to handle live helpline calls and manage the website immediately without a mobilisation period? If not, what specific risks does this present to your organisation, and what alternative solutions within the strict £80,000 p.a. budget framework would you propose? How long would you need to become fully operational? 6. How to Respond Interested suppliers should submit their Expression of Interest and responses to the questions above by July 24th 2026 at 17:00 BST. Please find link to the Contracts Finder Notice which contains a link to the draft statement of requirements as an attachment. Please submit your response via email to commercial@cabinetoffice.gov.uk with the subject line: "Preliminary Market Engagement Response - Conversion Practices VSS".
