The company was established in 2023 and, at the beginning of 2024, operations were transferred from the City of Tampere's municipal enterprise to a corporate form. Tampereen Vesi Oy provides water utility services in its operating area. The operating area mainly covers the zoned area of the City of Tampere. Tampereen Vesi Oy is inviting tenders for total payroll services, a time and attendance system and an HR system. The procurement is divided into parts as follows: PROCUREMENT PART A: Total payroll services (incl. payroll accounting, salary payment and expert services, as well as the payroll system used by payroll clerks) and a time and attendance system (incl. time and attendance tracking and shift planning). OPTION IN PROCUREMENT PART A: Travel management services (incl. travel ledger and travel and expense claim system). PROCUREMENT PART B: HR system (incl. personal data system and HRD system). A candidate may participate in both or only one of parts A or B. The procurement parts are independent, and a contractor will be selected separately for each part. In both procurement parts, the language of service is Finnish. All systems must have a Finnish-language user interface and instructions. The systems must enable a multi-company environment. In both procurement parts, the systems used will process personal data extensively, so data protection requirements must be taken into account. The systems must also have the possibility to restrict access rights on a role-based basis. Both procurement parts also include the commissioning of services and systems, related advisory and expert services, and system support services. The subject of the procurement is described in more detail in Annex 1 Preliminary service description. Information may be clarified during the procurement procedure. sig_482c9301eb09a942aa13.description: Kirkon keskusrahasto is launching a market consultation with this notice regarding the procurement of a core financial management system. Operating alongside the Church Office is the bookkeeping and payroll service centre of the Evangelical Lutheran Church of Finland, which manages the bookkeeping, purchase invoices, accounts payable, sales invoices, accounts receivable, fixed asset accounting, payroll, travel and expense claims, and associated payment transactions for parishes, parish unions, dioceses, kirkon keskusrahasto and the church pension fund. At the Church Service Centre, core financial management processes are currently supported by a SAP-based solution. The end-of-version support schedule announced by the manufacturer of the current SAP environment requires the contracting entity to evaluate system alternatives for the coming years on a broad scale. The market consultation will examine the suitability of alternative core financial management systems alongside SAP. The aim of the market consultation is to build a comprehensive picture of the technical, functional and economic benefits of the various alternatives and to help evaluate them objectively before launching the actual procurement. Based on the results of the market consultation, the contracting entity may opt for a technology-neutral tender or, for a reasoned reason, restrict the procurement to the current SAP technology. If the technology restriction is justified, the tender will focus on the upgrade of the SAP solution and the selection of an implementation partner. Otherwise, the tender will be implemented as open to all suppliers, including solutions utilising SAP technology. Any future tender will most likely be implemented as a competitive dialogue procedure in compliance with the principles of the Public Procurement Act. If a supplier has references from projects where a client has transitioned from a SAP-based financial management solution to another system, these references are of particular interest from the contracting entity's perspective. The purpose of these references is to help the contracting entity understand the implementation model, workload, risk areas and overall scope of such a transition - not to anticipate the system selection of any potential future procurement. Suppliers can express their interest in participating in the market consultation by submitting an expression of interest and a brief presentation of the core financial management system they offer, along with reference projects, by email to anette.tolvanen@evl.fi NO LATER THAN FRIDAY 17.4.2026. The presentation is requested to be submitted in either PDF or Office file format. As a starting point, 6 suppliers will be invited to the dialogue, selected by comparing the submitted system presentations and named reference projects against the subject of the procurement described below. The comparison will be made as an overall assessment taking into account, inter alia, the scope of the services currently being procured and the comparability of the submitted reference clients/projects to the operations of Kirkon keskusrahasto. Preliminary subject of the procurement The Church Service Centre is planning to tender a core financial management system. The aim of the future procurement is to overhaul and harmonise key financial management processes and ensure a modern, integrated system entity that supports automation. The content of the procurement may consist of, for example, the following core financial management functions: • bookkeeping, financial statements and fixed assets • processing of purchase invoices and accounts payable • sales invoicing, accounts receivable and debt collection • payment transactions • financial reporting and monitoring • financial planning, budgeting and forecasting • archiving • as well as options for extensions and functionalities to be procured later The purpose of this request for information is to map out supplier and solution alternatives related to the procurement. This notice is not a procurement notice or a call for tenders, but an invitation to participate in a market consultation implemented via a prior information notice as part of the preparation of a possible procurement. This request for information does not oblige the contracting entity to carry out the procurement. Current financial management processes are partially automated, but still involve a lot of manual work steps, resolution of exceptions, and fragmented practices between different service areas. The development of the system entity aims, for example, at: • harmonising processes and increasing automation • improving data transfer and integrations • reducing exceptions and errors • improving turnaround times and cost efficiency • better transparency and reporting to support management The aim of the market consultation is to map out solutions available on the market and obtain suppliers' views in particular on: • automation opportunities and best practices • streamlining the current processes of the Church Service Centre using the supplier's offered solution • integrations in a challenging multi-vendor environment • development model and service level requirements • price level and scalability of total costs in light of various scenarios • implementation and migration of the system, including schedule and costs • information security and data protection • architecture

sig_48ec3dda190e795f6681.description: The "Strengthening environmental and social governance in the extractive sector" component, co-financed by FONAREDD from CAFI (Central Africa Forest Initiative) resources and BMZ, will be implemented by GIZ for the Ministry of the Environment and Sustainable Development (MEDD) of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The project is being carried out by the Integrated Economic Development of the Mining Sector Project (DISM II), in partnership with the Congolese Environment Agency (ACE), which is responsible for environmental and social assessments and for monitoring and controlling the implementation of ESMPs at national level. Following a 1st Strategic Environmental and Social Study of the mining sector in the DRC in 2010, and in view of the changing international context, it is planned, in agreement with the donor and partners, to launch Strategic Environmental and Social Studies (SESES) for the key sector of mining and hydrocarbons, in order to analyse the expected positive and negative impacts of their development at national level. This work will make it possible to identify good and bad practices in the provinces affected; and in partnership with the various partners and civil society, to propose recommendations integrating REDD+ standards into the extractive sectors. Finally, best practice guides will also be drawn up, based on the experience gained with dialogue platforms in the extractive sector. Adaptations of the various texts relating to the legal and regulatory provisions linked to the environmental and social governance of the extractive sectors will also be proposed in order to be consistent with REDD+ standards and the principles of the Extractive Industries Transparency Initiative (EITI). Lot LOT-0001: 10007377-Strategic Environmental and Social Assessment (SESA) of the oil and gas sector to be carried out in the DRC. An open international call for a tender is published for services to be provided for 12 months, requiring a total of 5 experts, including 2 experts with international experience, respectively head of mission and deputy head of mission, with skills in the environment, strategic studies, and knowledge of the hydrocarbon sector. The team will be backed up on site by 3 experts with national experience with skills in social responsibility and oil and gas sector law and public policy. The services to be provided under this contract include measures for human capacity development and organisational and strategy advice in the following thematic areas: 1. Identifying and increasing attention to potential environmental and social risks, direct and indirect impacts and concerns around the development of the oil and gas sector; 2. Identifying and strengthening environmental and social management approaches and practical tools for the Government to manage sectoral environmental and social governance 3. Identifying and strengthening instruments and approaches that can improve environmental and social accountability, including by increasing the transparency of processes in the oil and gas sector and establishing simple, safe and accessible feedback and/or complaint mechanisms. 4. Support strengthening actors" capacity relevant for the sector to manage environmental and social risks related to the development of the oil and gas sector according to the mitigation hierarchy (avoid, minimise, mitigate and offset). The Contractor is responsible for the performance of the services and the production of the following outputs: 1) Strategic environmental and social assessment (SESA) of the oil and gas sector in the DRC. 2) SWOT analysis and recommendations for the oil and gas sector. 3) Socio-environmental management standards for the DRC. 4) Guide to good environmental and social practices for the DRC 5) Draft implementing legislation for the DRC.
sig_48ec3dda190e795f6681.title: 10007377-Strategic Environmental and Social Assessment (SESA) of the oil and gas sector to be carried out in the DRC

sig_48f22d7bbaabae436448.description: Scotland has the highest drug and alcohol related death rates in the UK and Europe. People with substance use issues (PWSUI) often need help outside normal 'office' hours or from a distance from offices, and support is not uniformly available throughout Scotland. The support landscape in Scotland is fragmented, hard to navigate, and varies by locality. When support isn’t readily available (or isn’t trusted), people and their families and friends often default to emergency services or remain unsupported. As a result, those who use substances often experience avoidable crisis escalation, or remain in extremely difficult situations, and support services miss opportunities for early, harm-reducing interventions. The Preventing Harm, Promoting Recovery: Scotland’s Alcohol & Drugs Strategic Plan 2026 – 2035 specifically addresses the crucial need to tackle early intervention and widen an individual’s ‘circle of support’. This ‘circle of support’ is at the heart of this Challenge, and a successful solution would enable people to access the right support sooner, regardless of locality. It should harness the power of existing trusted services, family and community to reduce avoidable demand on emergency and NHS services – and if possible, create a ‘feedback loop’ of learning, intelligence and insight so that the overall issue can be tackled in a continually improving manner.
sig_48f22d7bbaabae436448.title: CivTech 12.1 - How can digital technologies assist people living with substance use issues (and their families/friends) to easily connect with trusted help and substance use support when services are unavailable?

All interfaces must be provided in such a way as to ensure seamless, secure, and consistent data exchange between the systems. There are no individual licences at the user or terminal workstation level. A quantity-independent licence (so-called campus licence) is required. The scope of services further includes the delivery and assignment of the required software licences or usage rights, setup and parameterisation, data migration from legacy systems, connection of legacy systems, training and documentation, as well as subsequent software maintenance and support. The contractual basis for the supplies and services to be provided will be an EVB-IT framework agreement, which consists in particular of elements of the EVB-IT System, the EVB-IT Assignment Agreement Type A, the EVB-IT Cloud Contract, and the EVB-IT Maintenance S Contract, each with the corresponding EVB-IT general terms and conditions

sig_492da5f8ba39144d025c.description: THIS IS NOT A PROCUREMENT NOTICE OR A CALL FOR TENDERS, BUT A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR MARKET RESEARCH AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE. This request for information is used to survey the market and obtain information regarding the procurement. The contracting authority is not initiating a tendering procedure with the publication of the request for information; instead, any potential procurement notice and call for tenders will be published later. The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Responding to the request for information is not a precondition for participation in any subsequent tendering procedure that may be organised. Suppliers will not be paid compensation for responding to the request for information or for participating in the market dialogue. The responses provided to this request for information will be used in planning the procurement of a personnel planning system. The subject of the procurement is a personnel planning system which: - supports strategic personnel planning and takes into account the qualitative (incl. staff competency structure) and quantitative planning of personnel required for organising service operations - enables the planning of personnel resources at the supervisory level - operates in accordance with processes defined by labour legislation (takes into account the starts, changes, terminations, etc., of employment relationships) - takes into account that the volume of personnel resources is guided by the level of service operations (increases / decreases / remains the same), care intensity and the budget, rather than a static, administrative vacancy system - can be integrated into HUS's other systems - scales to HUS's current personnel and organisational structure and its potential future changes - is a ready-made overall solution / service package. Personnel planning has a close connection to financial planning / the planning system (personnel costs). BACKGROUND TO THE PROCUREMENT Personnel planning is based on HUS's strategy and objectives. Personnel planning is carried out in both the short and long term. Strategic personnel planning is the organisation's long-term personnel planning. It can be used to anticipate changes in the operating environment and evaluate cost impacts. Personnel planning supports the organisation in achieving its objectives by ensuring access to the right capabilities, in the right place and at the right time. The objectives of planning are: - To identify the required number and structure of personnel as well as competence - To define the measures needed to ensure the personnel in accordance with the objective. These may include: • structural solutions related to the organisation of work and divisions of labour • development of personnel competence • renewal of processes • utilisation of digitalisation / new technologies The purpose of the request for information is to survey suppliers on the market and their product and service ranges. The purpose is to ascertain technical solutions, pricing principles and the cost level for the budget. HUS-yhtymä requests your written comments in particular on the following questions: - What kind of system / service package are you offering (description of implementation) and with what functionalities does the solution meet the needs of the contracting authority described in this request for information? - What are the integration possibilities of the solution you are offering? - What is the pricing model of the solution you are offering (e.g. licences, maintenance and support)? - Is the system / service package you are offering in use in other similar organisations (wellbeing services counties, health and social services operators)? Please note that all material is intended solely for conducting this market dialogue. The contracting authority will process your responses confidentially. Based on the responses to the request for information, suppliers may be offered an opportunity to present their solutions in a manner to be announced later. Suppliers that have responded to the request for information may be given preliminary call for tenders documents for comment. We kindly ask you to submit your responses to the request for information and notify us of your interest no later than 11.12.2025 by 12:00 to the address kilpailutus.ict@hus.fi. The subject line of the message must state "HUS 495-2025 - Request for information: Personnel planning system".
sig_492da5f8ba39144d025c.title: Request for Information: Human Resources Planning System

sig_49677a748a77a2a2c212.description: Maintenance, support and management of CEFTA cloud infrastructure, hosting, managed services, security and business continuity. The contract will cover the end-to-end operation, administration, monitoring, maintenance, security, backup, disaster recovery, business continuity, and optimisation of CEFTA’s cloud-hosted infrastructure and related ICT services. This includes Microsoft Azure, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), Oracle databases, WebLogic middleware components, cloud and software licences, security platforms and tools, hosting environments, and associated support arrangements. The services will ensure the stable, secure, resilient, and continuous operation of CEFTA digital systems and applications, including Customs SEED+, CEFTA TRACES NT, and other related platforms and services. The contractor shall ensure the availability, confidentiality, integrity, and resilience of CEFTA’s infrastructure, systems, applications, and data, in line with industry best practices and applicable security, compliance, and governance requirements. The scope includes infrastructure and platform administration, performance monitoring and tuning, capacity planning, availability management, patch and configuration management, incident, problem, change and release management, and service request fulfilment. The contractor shall provide a combination of proactive and reactive operational support. Proactive services will include continuous monitoring, preventive maintenance, performance and capacity management, security assessments, vulnerability management, patching, security hardening, resilience improvements, cost optimisation, compliance support, and recommendations for continuous service enhancement. Reactive services will include incident response, troubleshooting, service restoration, problem resolution, emergency remediation activities, security incident handling, and support for unplanned events affecting the availability, performance, integrity, or security of CEFTA systems and services. The contract will also include security monitoring, threat detection, cybersecurity risk assessments, vulnerability remediation, backup management, disaster recovery planning and testing, business continuity planning and validation, data protection measures, recovery readiness activities, cloud cost management, infrastructure lifecycle management, operational reporting, service-level performance tracking, documentation maintenance, knowledge transfer, and technical and architectural advisory services, ensuring alignment with CEFTA’s operational, security, and strategic business objectives while maintaining the confidentiality, integrity, availability, and recoverability of CEFTA information assets and digital services. Maintenance, support and management of CEFTA cloud infrastructure, hosting, managed services, security and business continuity. The contract will cover the operation, monitoring, security, backup, continuity and optimisation of CEFTA’s cloud-hosted infrastructure and related ICT services, including Microsoft Azure, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, Oracle databases, WebLogic components, licences, security tools and related hosting and support arrangements. The services will support the stable, secure and continuous operation of CEFTA digital systems and applications, including Customs SEED+, CEFTA TRACES NT and related platforms, as well as incident and change management, security monitoring, vulnerability management, cybersecurity assessment and remediation, disaster recovery, business continuity, cost optimisation, technical advisory support and reporting.

sig_49699bf79cfa029bec3b.description: West Northamptonshire Council (WNC) is a relatively new Local Authority that has inherited a wide range of electronic document systems and storage methods from predecessor councils. These legacy solutions vary in functionality, levels of automation, and overall maturity, which often results in manual processes to meet compliance, retention, and operational needs. Key services such as Housing, Revenues & Benefits, Regulatory Services, the post room and Pensions and Payroll rely heavily on electronic document and records management to process and store critical information from residents, businesses, and other stakeholders. The Council uses several inherited systems for records management, each supporting different service areas. Additionally, WNC have an archive and heritage service that require archiving for long-term retention of digital materials. The project will consider opportunities to bring these capabilities together into a more consistent and modern corporate approach; in some cases, for archive data only.

Digital skills, Artificial intelligence (AI) and automation skills, data literacy and data management, digital transformation and innovation capability, cybersecurity skills, digital marketing and e-commerce. With the acceleration of digital, the following are also subject areas that are in high demand: Digital skills focus on strong digital communication and collaboration abilities alongside cloud and productivity fundamentals. Artificial intelligence (AI) and automation skills centre on understanding foundational and responsible AI principles as well as applying process automation tools. Data literacy and data management priorities include the ability to interpret and visualise data effectively and uphold good data governance and ethics. Digital transformation and innovation capability requires skills in digital strategy and change leadership, paired with service design and user centred design approaches. Cybersecurity skills focus on building strong cyber hygiene and user awareness, supported by basic risk management and incident response knowledge. Digital marketing and e commerce emphasise SEO and analytics, combined with content creation and digital advertising to drive engagement and growth. Accredited and non-accredited opportunities ranging from SCQF5 and above requested. Training in widely used, industry standard digital tools- such as Microsoft Teams, OneNote for collaborative working, and digital bookkeeping platforms - is also in high demand. Lot 2: Management Skills. Strategic leadership & future planning, workforce development & talent management, change management and digital adoption, people, leadership & wellbeing management, operational & performance management. Businesses require managers who can demonstrate strong strategic leadership and future planning, workforce development and talent management, change management and digital adoption, people focused leadership and wellbeing management, and effective operational and performance management. Building these capabilities ensures leaders can respond to rapid technological change, manage skills gaps, and support resilient, high performing teams. Training should develop practical management capabilities including project management, change management, managing through crisis situations, supervising hybrid or home based teams, leading and motivating others, and building strong supervisory skills. Programmes should also strengthen interpersonal and developmental capabilities such as assertiveness, change and recovery management, coaching skills, developing individuals, and Insights Discovery profiling to support self awareness and team effectiveness. These subject areas are designed for new supervisors, emerging managers, and those seeking to upskill for career progression. Both accredited and non accredited options should be available. Non accredited workshops can be delivered as half day or full day sessions and should be contextualised to the specific needs of the business, particularly for bespoke contracts or sector specific requirements. Lot 3: Marketing. Businesses require marketing training across a wide range of evolving subject areas, including AI enhanced marketing skills, agile and adaptive marketing capability, data driven marketing and analytics, search engine optimisation SEO, content strategy and digital advertising, customer engagement and trust building, omnichannel and customer experience design, and advanced digital platforms and mobile first technologies. Alongside these, there is growing demand for brand creation and management, communications and PR, marketing strategy development, crisis communications, and video production, as well as understanding the difference between amplification and publication as businesses seek growth, explore new markets, or reposition for new audiences. Practical creative skills such as graphic design — particularly 2D/3D animation and Photoshop/Illustrator upskilling to enhance in house capability and deliver more impactful digital content. Digital marketing and social media skills are increasingly essential, enabling businesses to build visibility, engage target audiences, and compete effectively across fast moving online platforms. Lot 4: Communication and Soft Skills. Communication & interpersonal skills, teamwork and collaboration, adaptability & resilience, emotional intelligence & people skills, leadership & soft aligned skills, customer focused skills. Strong communication and soft skill capabilities to help teams adapt to rapid technological, economic and workforce change, clear and confident workplace communication, active listening, teamwork, collaboration, resilience, adaptability and emotional intelligence, as well as core interpersonal skills such as delivering effective presentations, problem solving, assertiveness and customer service communication. Training to mitigate the widening internal skills gaps and meet the growing importance of adaptability, creativity and strong communication. Seeking non accredited, introductory to intermediate level training, typically delivered in half day or full day formats, allowing staff to quickly upskill in essential, business ready soft skills that support productivity and workforce effectiveness. Lot 5: Health and Safety. Practical, compliance focused health and safety training that ensures staff are competent, up to date and able to manage modern workplace risks. Address gaps in documentation, risk assessments and ongoing training. COSHH Awareness, Human Factors in Health and Safety, IOSH Managing Safely, IOSH Working Safely, IOSH SHECW, NEBOSH qualifications, and broader Occupational Health and Safety training, support with legal duties around safe working environments. Fire risk awareness, mental health and wellbeing, and maintaining workforce competency through regular refresher learning. Alongside accredited options, non accredited, short format courses to provide flexible, cost effective, introductory or refresher training tailored to SME’s operational needs. Lot 6: Construction and Trades. Essential electrical safety and compliance training, including the City & Guilds 18th Edition Electrical Wiring Regulations (full qualification and industry update) and PAT Testing and Inspection & Testing Upskilling for renewable energy systems, EV charging installation, battery storage safety, Lock Out–Tag Out (LOTO) procedures and electrical diagnostics. Ensuring staff remain competent, compliant and able to work safely with modern technologies. These may be delivered through accredited qualifications or short, non accredited practical courses to support flexible, cost effective workforce development. Lot 7: Training and Assessing. Workforce development training that strengthens internal capability, particularly through Assessor and Verifier qualifications, Coaching and Mentoring, and Train the Trainer programmes, enabling businesses to build in house expertise, support staff progression and maintain quality assurance across learning and development activities. Delivered as accredited or non accredited options, offering flexible, cost effective pathways that allow organisations to choose between formal qualification routes or shorter, practical sessions tailored to operational needs. Lot 8: Care, Mindfulness and Wellbeing. Safeguarding, Child Protection and Adult Protection training to ensure staff can recognise, respond to and escalate concerns in line with current legislation and best practice. Autism training, including delivery aligned to D&A certificated programmes and SQA certificated courses, supporting organisations to work confidently and inclusively with neurodiverse individuals. Trauma Informed Practice, Mental Health First Aid, Equality, Diversity & Inclusion (EDI) awareness, De escalation and Behaviour Support, and Professional Boundaries & Safer Working Practices, reflecting an increased emphasis on safe, ethical and inclusive service delivery. All programmes can be offered as accredited or non accredited options, providing flexible, practical learning tailored to organisational and sector requirements. sig_4c47cea478f16d9de663.description: In order to meet its legal obligations (Section 146a of the German Fiscal Code (AO) and the Cash Register Security Ordinance (KassenSichV)), the BSI must update the protection profiles BSI-CC-PP-0104 Cryptographic Service Provider (CSP) and BSI-CC-PP-0111 CSPLight (CSPL). To this end, the aforementioned protection profiles are also to be adapted within the project for broader use in the eID / EUDI wallet, 5G and FIDO / passkeys areas. This also requires the drafting of a standardised interface description for CSPLight products in central data centre operations in order to increase interoperability and minimise dependencies on proprietary architectures. The project is divided into three separate lots (professional lots within the meaning of Section 97 Paragraph 4 of the Act against Restraints of Competition (GWB)): - Lot 1: Adaptation and updating of the CSP protection profile and CSPL protection profile (Update-CSPL) - Lot 2: Evaluation of CSP-PP/CSPL-PP (Eval-CSPL) - Lot 3: Standardised interface description (API-CSPL) Lot 1 comprises the updating and modularisation of the protection profiles PP-CSP and PP-CSPL. Following on from this, in Lot 2, an evaluation of the CSP and CSPL protection profiles is carried out in accordance with EUCC. Finally, in Lot 3, a uniform, standardised interface description for the CSP Light is drawn up on the basis of the protection profile created in Lot 1. Details can be found in the specifications (see attachments). Lot LOT-0001: Lot 1: "Adaptation and updating of the CSP protection profile and CSPL protection profile (Update-CSPL)". The objective in Lot 1 is the adaptation and updating of the protection profiles PP-CSP and PP-CSPL. In this context, the two protection profiles are to be merged while pursuing the multi-assurance approach. The new protection profile is to be designed modularly so that it is possible to serve various application purposes and enable broad application. The core of the PP is to be restricted to the minimum necessary functionality of the CSP(L). All functionalities that are only required for specific purposes are to be outsourced to modules. Dedicated PP configurations are to be drawn up for the individual application scenarios mentioned above, which can in each case contain suitable combinations of functional modules. In this lot, a draft concept is first drawn up together with the contracting authority, then the detailed architecture is to be described, and in a further work package the focus lies on the actual creation of the PP. The objective of the lot is an updated and modularised protection profile as well as at least one corresponding PP configuration for the cash registers and eID use case. Lot LOT-0002: Lot 2: "Evaluation of CSP-PP/CSPL-PP (Eval-CSPL)". The subject of the contract in Lot 2 is the evaluation of the protection profile created in Lot 1. The result of Lot 2 consists of complete individual inspection reports, so that the available reports can be submitted for certification of the protection profile and its configuration and all formal requirements are met. Lot LOT-0003: Lot 3: "Standardised interface description (API-CSPL)". The objective in Lot 3 is the creation of a uniform, standardised interface description for the CSP, so as to enable manufacturer-independent use of a CSP on a secure server architecture for external applications. The basis for the interface description shall be the updated and modularised protection profiles, or the merged protection profile from Lot 1, as well as the current BSI TR-CSP2.
sig_4c47cea478f16d9de663.title: Project 1025 "CSP Update, Evaluation, Recertification and API (CUERA)"

sig_4c4869a7988d7a21fb6e.description: This tender concerns the conclusion of a contract for the Contracting Authority's procurement of an integrated financial and payroll system with a special focus on secure, stable and efficient operation. The contract covers the supply and implementation of the solution as well as subsequent operation, maintenance and support. The financial part includes debtors, collection, etc., and the payroll part also includes rostering. sig_4e0f3a5f7e829612a581.description: The Piedmont Region, within the scope of the Electronic Health Record (EHR), manages radiological images through local and regional PACS systems, but the current architecture is fragmented and poorly standardised across the various Healthcare Authorities. This situation generates inefficiencies, difficulties with updates and suboptimal access to images, especially in clinical contexts where timeliness is crucial. Furthermore, viewing functionalities are limited and not fully integrated with regional digital services and telemedicine. To respond to the new requirements of interoperability, continuity of care and telemedicine, it is necessary to evolve towards a federated, scalable and user-centred platform capable of guaranteeing immediate, secure and integrated access to radiological images. With this market sounding, CSI-Piemonte therefore intends to verify the presence on the market of solutions that meet the aforementioned technical-functional and organisational requirements.

sig_4e2be62957b3ffaefa98.description: Puolustusvoimien logistiikkalaitos (hereinafter the contracting authority) invites you to submit a request to participate in the Haapajärvi charging plant production line development project for the Finnish Defence Forces in accordance with this call for requests to participate and its annexes. Subject of the procurement: Planning and development site located in the production area of the Haapajärvi unit of the explosives centre. The main tasks are: The contracting authority wishes to develop the production line using automation and robotics. The aim is simultaneously to minimise the number of personnel. The candidate must state the number of personnel required for the modernised line at the stated capacities. The contracting authority has selected the following objects for automation: Renewal of the existing lower conveyor, including automation of the existing laboratory work (includes thread cleaning and inspection, attaching / installing the intermediate piece, and loading the upper conveyor), automation of the attachment of the existing cavity base and automation of the existing weighing operation. The procurement includes all necessary design work, dismantling of obsolete technology, and delivery and installation of new technology in the explosive premises (IP54 T4) as a turnkey delivery in accordance with the procurement documents. The selected supplier must design all possible operations of the procurement object to be automated and to operate automatically. Likewise, the machines and equipment to be modernised must be designed to function as independent parts of the rest of the existing production equipment. The modernised line must meet the ergonomics requirements and capacity needs with 81 VRTKR, 120 VRTKR and 155 TKR products. There are various versions of these products, and these versions are specified in separately delivered drawings. The main tasks included in the delivery are listed as follows: 1) Production capacity in accordance with requirements and minimisation of the number of personnel 2) Renewal of the existing lower conveyor 3) Automation of the operations of the existing laboratory work (including thread cleaning and inspection, installation of the detonator, attaching / installing the intermediate piece, and loading the upper conveyor) 4) Automation of the operations of the existing cavity base attachment 5) Automation of the existing weighing operation. Items 2 to 5 include design, dismantling of the existing redundant part, and necessary equipment deliveries and installations. The objective is to carry out the procurement (including the design phase) during the years 2026 to 2027, such that the timing of the installation of the new technology would be as follows: Working hours at the site are possible 19.07.2027 to 15.10.2027 (weeks 29 to 41). The delivery must be ready by 15.10.2027. Working on site is permitted during installations around the clock every day of the week, if necessary. Before starting the installations, the selected supplier must carry out all necessary design. The selected supplier must present (in written and oral form) the entire implementation proposal for the procurement (including necessary plans and capacity calculations) to the Customer in good time, i.e. when the necessary plans are, in the supplier's opinion, ready for presentation. The final implementation documentation is included in the delivery scope of the procurement. The contracting parties shall agree on the more precise installation schedule within the aforementioned delivery schedule in accordance with the terms of the procurement contract to be signed after the selection of the supplier. The final acceptance is preceded by trial runs (cold run / hot run), capacity runs, training, delivery of final documentation and official inspections. The new equipment must be fully ready for use and production by 15.10.2027. The contracting authority will send the invitation to tender and its annexes (incl. technical specification) on the basis of this call for requests to participate to the tenderers approved by the contracting authority.

sig_4e71d728d133d6d9af83.description: Aarhus Vand is a utility group that manages water and wastewater activities. In this context, Aarhus Vand owns, operates, and maintains many kilometres of water and wastewater pipes distributed across the supply area. To ensure efficient operation of the pipes, Aarhus Vand requires accurate, updated, and accessible registration of the pipe network. For this purpose, Aarhus Vand needs a pipe registration system. Aarhus Vand wishes for a collective agreement comprising both the licences for the pipe registration system itself and consultancy services for ongoing development and maintenance of the system. Aarhus Vand hereby invites to a market dialogue regarding the above. The purpose of the market dialogue includes determining which systems are on the market that can fulfil Aarhus Vand's factual and objective needs. Aarhus Vand has identified the following requirements as being important in relation to a future pipe registration system. It is important to Aarhus Vand that these requirements can already be fulfilled now. The list is not considered exhaustive: 1. Full support for DANVA's latest models, currently: Dandas 3.1.2, TV inspection and manhole report 3.1.2, Danvand 2.1.2, cables, third-party pipes, and areas 1.1, burst registration 1.1.1. For all models, this applies to all concepts, attributes, codes, relations, and interfaces as well as DANVA's guidelines and data manuals. The system is configurable so that it can be easily and quickly adapted to changes in both the models and the user interface 2. All registrations are saved / data resides in one and the same database 3. The system must support data exchange in XML format. There must be an option for direct updating via e.g. SQL. There must be direct access to data, as well as the possibility of making direct integrations with other systems. 4. Quality assurance. XSD validation, predefined validations, etc., which support pipe registration and work with data, and thus ensure and maintain good data quality. 5. Possibility to work in "jobs" in connection with the digitalisation of an area / project / subject, which can subsequently be upgraded to be the master. That is, so that one does not work in the master until changes have been upgraded to the master. 6. The language in the system must be Danish. To a minor extent, it can be in English. 7. User interface. An intuitive and user-friendly user interface. Workflows must be supported by configurable templates/flows. Must contain a tool for replacing, splitting, and merging objects, e.g. pipes. Must have various construction tools. Must have 3D support. 8. User management via AD integration. Users must be able to have different roles/rights. 9. The solution must have stable and high performance 10. There must be an auto-save feature, or recovery of unsaved work or similar. All market operators who believe they can meet the above requirements are encouraged to register for the market dialogue. FRAMEWORK AND PARTICIPATION OF THE DIALOGUE As a general rule, the market dialogue will take place physically at Aarhus Vand, Hasselager Allé 29, 8260 Viby J. The dialogue is held individually per market operator. Interest in the market dialogue must be reported to Christoffer Larsen at christoffer.larsen@aarhusvand.dk or indkob@aarhusvand.dk no later than 20.10.2025. The dialogue meetings are held in the period from 21.10.2025 to 31.10.2025.
sig_4e71d728d133d6d9af83.title: Invitation to market dialogue regarding IT system for utility registration in connection with water, wastewater, etc.

sig_500928eb240e422aaf60.description: This Market Engagement seeks to identify options to enable procurement of a dedicated backup collection tool for Operational Technology (OT) environments. The solution will ensure that the complete data state of critical OT assets is consistently captured and securely stored across multiple sites, serving as the organisation's data of last resort. The tool must collect the full backup state of OT assets including configurations, control logic, firmware, hardware metadata, and associated files. It must support both automated, policy-driven backup collection and authorised manual backup initiation, operating through secure and non-intrusive protocols that do not interact with OT control or programming interfaces and have no impact on live operations or safety-critical systems. The solution must be vendor-agnostic, deployable fully on-premise or within a private cloud, and capable of operating in air-gapped environments, with full audit trails and compliance reporting. IMPORTANT: Please read this section before deciding whether you wish to register for this event. This section provides you with information regarding the scope of this procurement and details some of the key requirements that a successful applicant MUST be able to deliver.
sig_500928eb240e422aaf60.title: Data of Last Resort Data Collection

The purpose of the request for information is to survey the solutions available on the market and to obtain comprehensive information regarding them so that the procurement in preparation can be carried out as appropriately as possible. Responding to the request for information is not a prerequisite for participating in the competition and does not affect the tenderer's position in it. The subject of the request for information is a document management and archiving service at various information security levels (SaaS and On-Premise) including electronic signature, the possibility of integrations and the utilisation of automation, as well as customer support. The customer support service hours are fundamentally during office hours 8-16.15, but it must be expandable according to customer needs (possibly also at weekends). Customer support is available in Finnish and Swedish, with good oral and written skills in Finnish as a requirement. The anticipated scope of the procurement in the initial phase is approximately 20 central government organisations of varying sizes, a small proportion of which require the On-Premise service. We kindly ask you to register for the market dialogue by responding to this request for information in Tarjouspalvelu by the deadline. The market dialogue is divided into two phases: 1. The meetings will be held in weeks 45 and 46. We reserve the right to present additional questions to suppliers if it is deemed necessary for the advancement of the competition. Any additional questions will be presented electronically to those who have participated in the market dialogue. The contracting authority will select a maximum of 5 potential tenderers for the market dialogue that have the capability to produce the service in accordance with the subject of the procurement in its planned scope. The capability of potential tenderers will be assessed based on the responses given to the questions presented later in this request for information. An invitation to the meeting will be sent to the suppliers selected for the market dialogue by the end of week 43. Those who have responded to the request for information or participated in the market dialogue will not be paid any compensation for responding to the request for information or for costs arising from participation in the market dialogue. sig_50a618e0b85da91cb217.description: "Evaluation services regarding the implementation of the South-West Oltenia Regional Programme interventions 2021-2027" will be purchased in order to obtain an independent, objective and evidence-based evaluation regarding the implementation and results of the South-West Oltenia Regional Programme 2021–2027, which will support the programme management and the preparation of the future programming period. The services will be provided in accordance with the minimum requirements in the specifications. The contracting authority will respond clearly and completely to all requests for clarifications on the 11-th day before the deadline for the submission of tenders. An evaluation study regarding the implementation of the South-West Oltenia Regional Programme interventions 2021-2027" will be purchased, which consists of providing consulting services for the implementation of the Evaluation of the implementation of the South-West Oltenia Regional Programme interventions 2021-2027, respectively the evaluation in an integrated approach of the investment priorities related to the South-West Oltenia Regional Programme 2021-2027, for the Managing Authority of the PR SV Oltenia. The general objective of the evaluation of the use of PR SV Oltenia resources 2021-2027 is to determine the effectiveness, efficiency, relevance, coherence (internal and external), added value for the Union, of the interventions financed through PR SV Oltenia 2021-2027, including through the technical assistance priority. In accordance with the Evaluation Plan of the PR SV Oltenia 2021-2027, the evaluations also follow the assessment of visibility, regional social cohesion, inclusiveness, the green character and the non-discriminatory one. The programme evaluation must highlight, in particular, the progress and performance recorded in the management and implementation of the PR SV Oltenia interventions through the prism of the criteria mentioned above and the evaluation questions. The evaluation aims to analyse the implementation method of the South-West Oltenia Regional Programme 2021–2027, in an integrated approach, at the level of all priorities (P1–P10). Specific objectives of the evaluation • determining the coherence of the interventions within the PR SV Oltenia 2021-2027 for the period for which the evaluation is carried out; • determining the EU visibility through the interventions financed within the PR SV Oltenia 2021-2027; • constituting a source of new information regarding the achievement of the objectives formulated within the PR SV Oltenia 2021-2027 of the interventions financed within the PR SV Oltenia 2021-2027 which will contribute to making decisions based on real information; • analysing the evolution of the priorities targeted by the evaluation; • analysing the fulfilment of the enabling conditions for the adequate implementation of the interventions; • analysing the complementarity and synergy of the interventions with other interventions financed from Union funds and from other national and European instruments as well as their added value for the EU; • analysing the necessity and ease of accessing funding opportunities by potential beneficiaries; • analysing the capacity to carry out investments, including adopting new technologies by applicants and beneficiaries; • analysing the way in which the target groups of people, firms and institutions, targeted by the priorities, are engaged in the supported activities; • analysing the way of integrating horizontal principles (equality between women and men, non-discrimination, accessibility, inclusiveness, sustainable development, including the principle of doing no significant harm) in the selected projects and their implementation; • measuring the effects of the interventions from the perspective of the specific objectives of the programme, to support its effective and efficient implementation.
sig_50a618e0b85da91cb217.title: Evaluation services regarding the implementation of the South-West Oltenia Regional Programme interventions 2021-2027

These framework agreements comprise in particular the advice, development, conception, implementation and evaluation of evaluations. For this purpose, future contractors shall propose and implement suitable evaluations in accordance with the topics, issues, objectives and target groups specified by the demand bearers. The awarding of these services takes place in two lots. A detailed description of the service to be provided can be found in the contracts and the specifications. In addition to the evaluation of this external communication, this lot also enables the evaluation of internal products of the demand bearers (e.g. intranet, newscenter, etc.) as well as internal processes by surveying the employees of the demand bearers (internal communication). It includes qualitative methods such as group discussions, qualitative workshops, insight communities, in-depth interviews as well as quantitative methods such as computer-assisted surveys (CATI, CAPI, CASI, CAWI), written postal interviews/push-to-web surveys, mixed-mode surveys, embedding questions in an omnibus survey and on-site surveys. In addition, usability tests are also possible (using qualitative or quantitative methods). sig_50e6f55429fac1a7de36.description: THIS IS NOT A CONTRACT NOTICE OR AN INVITATION TO TENDER BUT A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR MARKET RESEARCH AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE. HUS-yhtymä (hereinafter also referred to as the contracting authority) is using this request for information to survey the market to support the planning of a potential procurement of data centre equipment. The purpose of the request for information is to survey suppliers in the market and their product and service ranges. The equipment to be procured includes both technology-specific and technology-independent equipment. HUS currently uses data centre equipment from manufacturers including the following: Dell Technologies, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Hitachi Vantara and F5. The equipment to be procured may also be of other brands on a case-by-case basis. Much of the equipment in use still has a significant part of its lifecycle remaining, so in addition to new equipment, the procurement need also concerns, for example, extensions and support services for existing equipment. We ask suppliers interested in the procurement to reply in writing, particularly to the following questions: - What data centre equipment from the above-mentioned equipment brands (Dell, HPE, Hitachi, F5) is available through you? - What other equipment brands can you supply? - What kind of support, maintenance and expert services do you offer in connection with the data centre equipment you sell? - Do you offer services related to the intermediate storage of equipment? - What is your company's partner status (e.g. Dell, HPE, Hitachi, F5)? - What training or certification requirements do you meet in service deliveries? - What is the operational model you use for placing, tracking and delivering equipment orders? - How do you deliver equipment configuration documentation to the customer? - What references do you have for deliveries of the above-mentioned and other equipment brands? If you wish, you can also attach brochures or other information about the products and services you offer to your reply. We kindly ask you to submit your replies to the request for information by 9.4.2026 to the address kilpailutus.ict@hus.fi. Please include the subject line "HUS 029-2026: Data centre equipment". Replies given to this request for information may be used in the planning of the procurement. The contracting authority may, at its discretion, propose clarifying market dialogue discussions with those who have replied to this request for information. Please note that all material is intended solely for conducting this market dialogue. The contracting authority will treat your reply confidentially. The contracting authority is not initiating a tendering procedure by publishing the request for information; any subsequent contract notice and invitation to tender will be published later. The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Responding to the request for information is not a prerequisite for participation in any subsequent tendering procedure that may be organised. Suppliers will not be paid any compensation for responding to the request for information or participating in the market dialogue.

sig_51dd928abedab57fcef9.description: The U.S. Military Academy at West Point's mission is "to educate, train, and inspire the Corps of Cadets so that each graduate is a commissioned leader of character committed to the values of Duty, Honor, Country and prepared for a career of professional excellence and service to the Nation as an officer in the United States Army." The United States Military Academy is located at West Point, New York. USMA executes research to enhance the education of cadets, develop the faculty professionally, and address important issues facing the Army and the Nation. In addition, the Academy conducts research and analysis in emerging fields that may realize novel or vastly improved Army capabilities. At West Point, research is organized and administered through centers and institutes, most of which reside within academic departments. These centers and institutes, affiliated with each other through the Academy Research Council (ARC), coordinated and supported by the Academic Research Division (ARD), provide the infrastructure necessary to tackle the nation’s and the world’s most challenging problems. Our research centers and institutes bring context to the classroom, are central to our vibrant and pioneering faculty, and are one way West Point connects to the Army and to the Nation. Our students are driven, our faculty is world-class, and through our centers, scholars and scientists thrive and produce their best work. Cadets regularly win Best Paper Awards at national and international graduate-level conferences, our faculty hold fellowships and chairmanships in their discipline's national organizations and our products are deployed to the soldier. In addition to applied research, there are centers and institutes at West Point that focus on other aspects of the USMA mission. The USMA BAA identifies topics of interest to the USMA departments, directorates, and research centers and institutes. These groups focus on executing in-house research programs, with a significant emphasis on collaborative research with other organizations. The groups fund a modest amount of extramural research in certain specific areas, and those areas are described in this BAA. The USMA BAA seeks proposals from institutions of higher education, nonprofit organizations, state and local governments, foreign organizations, foreign public entities, and for-profit organizations (i.e., large and small businesses) for research based on the following campaigns: Socio-Cultural; Information Technology; Ballistics, Weapons, and Protections; Energy and Sustainability; Materials, Measurements, and Facilities; Unmanned Systems and Space; Human Support Systems; and Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Quantum Technologies. Proposals are sought for cutting-edge innovative research that could produce discoveries with a significant impact to enable new and improved Army technologies and related operational capabilities and related technologies. The specific research areas and topics of interest described in this document should be viewed as suggestive, rather than limiting.

sig_520c3a78e4d7855a5f4a.description: Mobile operational data collection in road maintenance operations at Hessen Mobil for the East Hesse and West Hesse departments As part of this tender, road maintenance operations at Hessen Mobil for the 8 road maintenance depots of the Operations and Traffic Department East Hesse and the 8 road maintenance depots of the Operations and Traffic Department West Hesse are to be optimised through the deployment of a mobile operational management system (EMS). The main objectives of the new operational management system (EMS) in winter maintenance are legally secure verification of the operations carried out in the context of the duty to maintain road safety, operational evaluations, performance billing with external contractors and other road construction authorities, as well as efficient operational control using real-time monitoring. Furthermore, drivers are to be relieved of workload during winter maintenance by means of route guidance functions. The basis for the new operational management system of the Operations and Traffic Departments East and West Hesse is automated operational data collection in the approx. 140 winter maintenance vehicles (vehicles from Hessen Mobil and external contractors) that carry out winter maintenance within the area of responsibility of the 16 road maintenance depots. The contracting authority intends to conclude an EVB-IT service contract (with a system delivery contract) with up to 3 extension options of 12 months each.

sig_526a6b73b5712fbec3ec.description: DCMS is seeking to commission a two-phase research project to investigate UK media consumption habits and public trust in media. Phase 1 would consist of a behavioural cohort study (or another appropriate methodology) to map the specific "user pathways" audiences take to find, consume, and value information across different media sources, such as traditional news broadcasts and social media, across different demographics. Building on these findings, Phase 2 would explore how individuals perceive trust in different media sources due to their own perception of mis/disinformation, assess the broader effects of these consumption pathways on factors such as viewer retention and wider social cohesion, as well as overall integrity of the UK's information ecosystem. This project will be commissioned either through a Competitive Flexible Procedure under the Procurement Act 2023, or through the RM6126 Research and Insights framework. This is part of the DCMS Science and Analysis R&D Programme, which supports R&D capability within the department. This project will run concurrently alongside three other large projects across 2027-2030; these include 'what works' research into AI adoption in DCMS sectors; a continuation of previous research to develop data-intensive approaches for capturing engagement at unticketed cultural, heritage, and sporting events/activities/locations, e.g. using mobile app data to model how people participate in our events; and a continuation of previous research to design and improve methods for holistically tracking the long-term impact of major events, tested on a major event. Lot 1: .

Upon completion of the market consultation, the results will be definitively evaluated by the contracting authority and taken into account within the scope of the intended award procedure. If it turns out after completion of the market consultation that the contracting authority's requirements can indeed only be fulfilled by a single company, a negotiated procedure without a call for competition pursuant to § 14 para. 4 no. 2 of the Public Procurement Ordinance (VgV) will be conducted with the affected company, otherwise a competitive award procedure.

sig_52e3c59ec11b9c31cf76.description: The Ogden Air Logistics Complex (OO-ALC) at Hill Air Force Base, Utah, intends to issue a solicitation to provide comprehensive management and supply of aircraft coatings and sealants. This effort aims to ensure uninterrupted aircraft maintenance operations through robust inventory management, timely delivery, and technical support. This effort will include frequent ordering and quick delivery on specified items. The selected contractor will be responsible for continuous deliveries and support of Coatings and Sealants, including: 1. Order Fulfillment and Material Handling: Sourcing, storing, and delivering all required coatings and sealants (see attached list). This includes meeting a strict four (4) hour delivery timeline for urgent requirements and handling specialized materials, such as Premixed Frozen Material (PFM) requiring transit at -80F. The contractor must maintain a minimum of 85% shelf life for all products upon delivery. The contractor will also be responsible for managing shelf-life and ensuring proper storage and handling of the products prior to delivery. 2. FMS-3600 Coating Management: For this specialized product, implementing a lock and key ITAR-compliant storage system and maintaining rigorous chain of custody for the material. 3. Technical Assistance: Providing technical assistance that includes rapid response (within one business day) to material failures, on-site technical support during monthly visits, product change support, and quality audit reporting. 4. Online Ordering System: Furnishing a secure, web-based ordering and tracking system with real-time visibility of lead times and minimum stock levels (MSLS). 5. Ramp-Up Plan: Executing a ramp-up plan to achieve full performance readiness within eight (8) months of contract award. The anticipated contract will be a Firm Fixed Priced (FFP) IDIQ to include an 8-month ramp up period, a 5-year ordering period, and a 6-month allowance for remaining deliveries on the back end. Total period of performance is anticipated to be 6 years and 2 months. This is a total small business set-aside. The Government anticipates awarding a single contract. All interested small businesses are encouraged to respond. The official solicitation will be posted on SAM .gov. The Government intends to award a single contract resulting from the upcoming solicitation to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the Government. This effort requires Contractors to be CMMC level 2 self-certified, therefore if you are not currently level 2 certified and are interested in this requirement you will need to begin the process to become level 2 certified immediately. The solicitation draft documents are attached. Dates on the solicitation are subject to change based on the actual award date. Please review and submit any questions or suggestions to the point of contacts on this 15-day synopsis. The anticipated solicitation number is FA8224-26-R-0010 (subject to change). The anticipated solicitation release date is October 2, 2026 (subject to change).

sig_53859266daf39dfe09a0.description: 2M-IT Oy (hereinafter also the "Contracting Authority" or "Client") is establishing a dynamic purchasing system (DPS) for data-driven management and artificial intelligence services. Organisations providing services under the dynamic purchasing system (DPS) may submit requests to participate in the dynamic purchasing system throughout its duration. All candidates who have submitted a request to participate and who meet the suitability requirements set for candidates will be admitted to the dynamic purchasing system. The internal competitions of the dynamic purchasing system to be established will cover data-driven management and AI platforms, solutions and services, licences, and expert services, as well as various combinations thereof. The aforementioned are to be procured for services produced for social and healthcare organisations, which will be specified in more detail in the call for tenders for the DPS internal competition. Solutions may be procured for use in specialised medical care, primary healthcare, and social services, as well as in support activities related to these tasks. They may be implemented in the service production of 2M-IT Oy as part of the services for one or more clients. In addition, 2M-IT Oy may also procure solutions for the needs of its own business operations. The actual procurements will be made on the basis of separate calls for tenders as internal competitions within the DPS, in which the contracting authority will specify and describe its detailed procurement need. The subject of the procurement of platforms and licences may be, for example, a solution based on commercial off-the-shelf software for data-driven management or AI, software usage rights, licences, and/or an open-source software solution. The subject may also include, among other things, tools for data-driven management, data warehouse automation, integration, analytics and reporting, and visualisation. The solutions and services to be procured may consist of the supplier's own services and products or services and products licensed by a subcontractor provided through the supplier. In service production, either the Client's existing own operating service and other capacity can be utilised, or this can be included in the subject of the procurement. The subject of expert services can be specified in areas such as: • Data-driven management and AI consulting • Planning and management of data management and governance projects • Concept, data, and interface modelling and architecture definition • Development, testing, training, and planning of maintenance, management, and monitoring of data pipelines (ETL) and integrations • Knowledge of open interfaces and standards and integrating AI as part of applications • Planning, development, testing, training, and planning of maintenance, management, and monitoring of data warehouses, data cubes, and data lakes • Development of analytics, advanced analytics, machine learning, and robotics • Development of AI algorithms into finished products in various technologies • Implementation expertise in various technologies (e.g. Google AI, AWS Cloud computing, Microsoft AI) • User interface and application development (Chatbot etc.) • Definition and development of cost accounting • Definition of services, processes, and governance models • Selection, consulting, and training of tools used in development • Machine training, converting original material into a processable format, and teaching artificial intelligence

sig_53930fa9072f523f79cf.description: The Rheumazentrum Mittelhessen has decided to tender for a complete hospital information system for the site, which fulfils the KHZG funding requirements 3- 6 and which, furthermore, maps all administrative and clinical processes of an acute, AHB and (DRV) rehabilitation clinic. At the site in Bad Endbach, an acute clinic with 80 beds and an Anschlussheilbehandlung (AHB) and rehabilitation clinic with 36 beds are available for the holistic therapy of acute and chronic rheumatic diseases. The clinic complex also includes two practices with medical rheumatology consultations and an outpatient therapy facility for physiotherapy, physical therapy and occupational therapy. Over the years, the clinic area has been constantly modernised and the infrastructure expanded. The Rheumazentrum Mittelhessen has decided to tender for a complete hospital information system for the site, which fulfils the KHZG funding requirements 3- 6 and which, furthermore, maps all administrative and clinical processes of an acute, AHB and (DRV) rehabilitation clinic. The future HIS is to be set up in such a way that it is the patient-leading system in interaction with other subsystems/modules. The HIS is to be introduced on the basis of a "best practice" approach within the framework of joint project work. The contractor is accordingly expected to provide a consultative and optimising process approach within the framework of the software implementation. The software to be supplied must have the capabilities and instruments that, for example, enable users to manage the patient's treatment progress as efficiently as possible, as well as to document and bill services quickly, in a revenue-secure manner and in compliance with the KHZG (FTB 3-6). The providers are therefore requested to submit a tender for a complete KHZG-compliant HIS including all necessary services for implementation and maintenance/service, which fulfils the mandatory criteria of the KHZG funding requirements 2 - 6 (the mandatory criteria for the admission and treatment management of the FTB 2 are fulfilled via the portal solution of the company Samedi, the discharge and transfer management via the solution of the company Verbund Pflegehilfe (see "Interfaces" tab of Annex 1), the contractor only owes the connection in this area in accordance with the technical requirements and interoperability standards of the KHZG). The new HIS is intended to significantly support the digitalisation and efficiency of hospital processes and thus optimise patient care.
sig_53930fa9072f523f79cf.title: Hospital information system

sig_53a626abe4f48fbd998b.description: Dumfries and Galloway Council – WEF Wanlock Water, Wanlockhead and WEF Nith Nature Reserve, Dumfries. The work is split across two Lots: Lot 1 Wanlock Water (RIBA1); Lot 2 Nith Nature Reserve, Dumfries(RIBA 1&2). Because of the multidisciplinary nature of the work, we would welcome either a single consultancy/ company that has all the skills in house or a consortium that can bring all of the skills required together. However, we appreciate it may be unlikely that a single consultancy has capacity and multiple disciplines. A detailed Description of Services for Lot 1 and 2 is currently being prepared. Lot 1: Wanlock Water Restoration Project- Indicative scope and outputs. The Contracting Authority intends to procure a feasibility study focusing on improving water quality and flows along with enhanced biodiversity, industrial heritage awareness and climate resilience for the Wanlock catchement and its communities. The commission is tasked to develop the project brief and test the feasibility of potential interventions, gathering information on constraints, risks, costs and potential delivery routes. The study is expected to be undertaken within the policy and funding context of the Scottish Environment Protection Agency’s (SEPA) Water Environment Fund (WEF), which supports the identification and delivery of measures to improve the ecological status of water bodies. As such, the feasibility work should consider the objectives of the Water Framework Directive (WFD) and identify opportunities for restoration and enhancement that may be eligible for future WEF support. The commission for the Wanlock Water is anticipated to require a minewater pollution reduction and treatment feasibility assessment, based on existing knowledge and characterisation of the problem, along with a scoping and feasibility study of wider opportunities and constraints to define future locations of works. Opportunities may exist to undertake treatment trials and to deliver multiple benefits within the riparian zone and floodplain and on the hill and moor landscape. The commission shall allow the project to complete Stage 1 of the framework of the Royal Institute of British Architects (RIBA) Plan of Work.. Scope TBC Review existing data and info - gap analysis. Targeted field surveys/assessments Delivery of opportunities & constraints mapping to assess feasibility. Baseline hydrological assessment of catchment. Outputs: project brief; feasibility report and high level summary; opportunity and constraints mapping; risk register; recommended next steps Lot 2: Lot 2 Nith Nature Reserve - Indicative scope and concept design outputs. The commission for the Nith Nature Reserve Project is to complete RIBA stages 1 and 2. This project aims to deliver a riverside nature reserve for people and wildlife by creating an enhanced natural setting for the Nith River. We will deliver significant ecological improvements, enhance the biodiversity and natural habitat and create a multiuse recreational area that is accessible to everyone in the community and provides multi-sensory experiences and educational opportunities. There are opportunities for improvements that would reduce morphological pressure capacity through habitat creation and could benefit flood risk and reduce sediment deposition further downstream. Dumfries and Galloway Council aim to deliver the drivers for biodiversity, climate resilience and better access to blue green infrastructure, access and amenity for local communities. The commission shall allow the project to complete Stage 1 and Stage 2 of the framework of the Royal Institute of British Architects (RIBA) Plan of Work.. TBC: Review existing data & gaps Field surveys/assessments Opportunities and constraints mapping to assess feasibility. RIBA Stage 1: project brief, geomorphological assessment, feasibility, constraints/risk register, next steps RIBA stage 2: preferred option report, concept designs informed by geomorphologist and landscape architect, visualisations and arcGIS style storyboard to present
