sig_5439fdf38566ca016a1f.description: The new State Parliament of the Federal State of Brandenburg is located at the site of the 1959 demolished City Palace on the Alter Markt in the city centre of Potsdam and commenced operation in the year 2014. Alongside offices for members of parliament, parliamentary group staff and the parliamentary administration, it features a large number of meeting and conference rooms. The heart of the State Parliament is the centrally located plenary chamber. The plenary chamber as well as the larger meeting and conference rooms are equipped with complex conference and multimedia systems that were implemented during the construction phase and upgraded during ongoing operations. Given their long service life, the equipment is now largely technologically obsolete and, due to wear and tear, also exhibits declining reliability and functionality, as well as reduced compatibility with current media formats. It is therefore to be renewed, adapted, supplemented and updated in several steps over time through the measure described here. In some cases, components have already been replaced by devices corresponding to the current state of the art. These are to continue to be used and integrated into the new systems. Overview of Equipment The scope of the envisaged measure covers the media-technology equipment of the following rooms: - Plenary chamber with control room, including speaker and interpreter booths - State press conference / visitor room (3-fold partitionable) - 3 meeting rooms on the ground floor - 3 meeting rooms on the first floor (1), partially partitionable - 2 meeting rooms on the second floor (2), partially partitionable - 2 meeting rooms on the third floor (3) - 1 meeting room (secure against eavesdropping) in the basement - Central control room in the lower ground floor - Mobile sound reinforcement including projection The multimedia systems in the plenary chamber and the other large meeting and conference rooms currently consist essentially of the following subsystems: - Video projections or displays - Cameras with controls (including video follows audio) - Conference systems with delegate units - Loudspeaker / PA systems for playback - Video conferencing systems - Vision mixers / scalers - Media control systems For recording and signal playback as well as for AV transmission, all these rooms are networked via a central control room in the lower ground floor using dedicated infrastructure (fibre optics, etc.) via a digital matrix. In addition, a digital signage system with a large number of screens in a server/player architecture is operated within the house network. The focus of the systems is on high reliability as well as ease of use for users and operators. In particular, virtually all components should be centrally operable and capable of being monitored. The aforementioned systems are to retain their fundamental function and structure, but are to be renewed, adapted, supplemented and updated in several steps within the scope of the measure described here. In this context, it must be noted that all affected rooms are fully utilised almost all year round and that, during the planned renewals or adaptations, only minimal operational interruptions are possible outside of times when no meetings are taking place. Scope of Services, Overview The following services are to be tendered: - Preparation of planning documentation: working and assembly planning in consultation with the client - Procurement, installation, configuration and commissioning of all media-technology components - Dismantling and disposal of old technology in consultation with the client The following additional services are to be tendered: - Cabling (local connection cables in the individual rooms, mainly CAT7) - Commissioning and user-appropriate parameterisation - Briefing / training - Documentation - SLA (service level agreement) where applicable with remote maintenance / remote monitoring / remote control - Suitable spare parts package.
sig_5439fdf38566ca016a1f.title: Renewal of media technology

sig_5477f5bfdf0227efa4b8.description:
This is a negotiated procedure with a call for competition pursuant to Section 11 Paragraph 1 Sentence 1 Alt. 2 of the Ordinance on the Award of Public Contracts (VSVgV). The subject matter of the contract to be awarded is the procurement for the delivery and setup of software as an overall system a) for the analysis, IT-supported comparison, and research of mass data in a stock of several partly federated source databases as well as ad-hoc imported data, in particular from the backups of digital evidence by the police of Schleswig-Holstein, b) for the technical integration of existing data sources in a central data integration platform (data integration component). The license requirement initially comprises 30 concurrent users; the license quantity required for this is to be procured. Optionally, there shall be the possibility to expand the number to up to 75 concurrent users. This option must be included in the tender, but the actual uptake is optional. The contracting authority provides for a staggering of the additional licenses to be acquired optionally. The additional licenses are offered in stages: Option 1 enables the procurement of 20 additional licenses (a total of 50 users), Option 2 another 25 licenses each, so that a maximum number of users of 75 can be reached. The term of the license is three years from the award of contract. The contracting authority has the right to extend the term up to three times by twelve months each time. Licenses acquired within the framework of options 1 and 2 have a term of three years from their provision, which can also be extended three times by twelve months each time, but the licenses procured by exercising options shall end at the latest simultaneously with the term of the licenses initially procured as a base. The contracting authority uses an EVB-IT Transfer Agreement Type B, an EVB-IT Maintenance Agreement, and an EVB-IT Service Agreement as the basis for the contractual agreement. These will be made available together with the other documents in the bidding phase. The procurement essentially comprises the following services: The rental of an overall system consisting of • an analysis software for cross-cutting analysis, IT-supported comparison, and research of mass data in the inventory of several partly federated source databases as well as ad-hoc imported data, in particular from the backups of digital evidence by the police of Schleswig-Holstein and • a central data integration platform (data integration component) for the integration of existing data sources, which can be installed in the computer centre of Dataport - on-premise. This includes a productive, development, and test system which is to be integrated into the existing IT infrastructure of the police of Schleswig-Holstein. sig_5641f7ba56ecb950d39b.description:
The procurement comprises the following work packages: Work package 1: Detailed design as preparatory work for the implementation of work package 2 This work package comprises the detailed designs necessary for the provision and, above all, the customising of the data management system. In particular, the following points are to be addressed in the detailed design: - Overall architecture (hardware and software, instance and tenant model) - Data modelling, tagging and representation - Role and rights system, user groups - User interfaces / UI (data input) - Quality standards and duplicate checking or consolidation - Data synchronisation between instances and connectors for importing from external data management systems via API - Implementation of compliance requirements (accessibility, data protection, laws / regulations (EU AI Act, EmpCo etc.)) - Representation of data upon export in data output management - Dashboards for system management and monitoring (KPIs) - Initial data migration for import from existing data inventories Work package 2: Customising (input and output management), incl. data migration, training and documentation At its core, this work package comprises the provision and, above all, the customising of the data management system building upon work package 1. This includes the implementation of standard settings (data model, roles / rights, interfaces, API management, etc.) and the setup of 12 instances incl. data synchronisation. To introduce the system, data migration from legacy systems as well as two legacy APIs (XML) for maintaining data flows for interface consumers to previous data systems must also be implemented. The work package comprises training for the TMB (administrators and operators of regional instances), training materials and documentation. Work package 3: Operation of API management As part of the project, the API infrastructure is to be transitioned from the historically grown logic of XML exports to modern API management. The contractor shall take over ongoing technical operation of the data management system's API management and ensure the reliable, secure and high-performance provision of APIs for the users to be connected. Work package 4: System operation, hosting, support The contractor shall take over ongoing technical operation, hosting and technical support of the data management system, including the system components required for this, and ensure their reliable, secure and high-performance availability during the term of the contract. This includes, in particular, monitoring the system environment, maintenance and updating of the components used, as well as the processing and rectification of technical faults. For the ongoing system operation and hosting of all components, the following services are required, which are to be provided either directly by the contractor or by third parties commissioned by the contractor. In both cases, the contractor is the central point of contact for the contracting authority and must ensure the following requirements (where applicable, together with its subcontractors or the third parties to be designated). Work package 5: Conception and setup / integration of a Graph-RAG-capable infrastructure into the data management system Graph-RAG-capable services are necessary where fact-based, context-sensitive answers from curated content are to be generated using AI systems, for example in the tourism network (as a state-wide information system e.g. for tourist information offices), in service assistants, chatbots or in internal knowledge systems. To become future-proof in this area, this work package is being tendered. Work package 6: Operation of a Graph-RAG-capable infrastructure The contractor shall take over the technical operation of the Graph-RAG-capable infrastructure provided for the TMB and ensure its reliable, secure and high-performance use during the term of the contract. Operation comprises in particular the availability of the required components for semantic search and the provision of knowledge for connected applications. Work package 7: Further development of the data management system and connected components This work package serves for the calculation of further development orders that are triggered and implemented via individual commissioning. Work package 8: Consulting for API management The contractor shall support the TMB in advising and supporting the approximately 200 existing and newly added users of the data management system's APIs. The aim is to provide API users with professional and technical support in the individual use, configuration and further development of their data connections and to ensure the most frictionless possible use of the data streams provided. The volume of the contract is estimated at 332.500,00 Euro for a period of four years. Lot LOT-0001: Provision, customising, operation and further development of a state-wide tourist data management system. The procurement is associated with the following needs and requirements (objectives): Against the background of new strategic and legal bases (Brandenburg tourism strategy (2023), TMB corporate concept (2025), EU Artificial Intelligence Act or the Artificial Intelligence Regulation, among others) on the one hand, and general developments in the field of digitalisation (in particular AI) on the other, the TMB wishes to procure a new uniform data management system as the basis for work in the Brandenburg content network. At its core, a data management system for all kinds and

types of data and content (B2C and B2B) with the following components are to be provided: - Input management / maintenance layer - AI and service layer - Output management / distribution layer The targeted target architecture is based on technologies established on the market, maintainable and manageable by personnel, as well as open standards. To safeguard digital sovereignty, proprietary special developments are deliberately avoided in favour of modular, future-proof software structures. A consistent API-first approach is also intended to ensure that individual functional modules can be replaced and expanded at any time independently of the manufacturer and seamlessly connected to any third-party systems. The current separation of POIs and tours (DAMAS), events (TDH) and media (media archive) is to be consolidated into a single data management system. This also applies to the content of the B2B portal as well as the portals of the B2C website frameworks. This is intended to promote the implementation of a "headless CMS approach", which aims for a complete separation of content and design. In its current form, data management is - for historical reasons - centrally structured. Control and coordination of the system lies with the TMB. For example, all tenants are created by the TMB (incl. user management, rights control, contractual matters, etc.). In the future system, a less hierarchical and flexible system is to be applied. In this context, the eleven travel regions of the state are taking on a more central role than previously. They are to receive their own instances of the state system, for example to manage regional editors independently. The regional instances are technically completely independent systems. Therefore, this is not a classic central tenant system with merely logically separated views of a state-wide data inventory. Rather, each instance has its own data storage or database with its own tenant structure. Data exchange is to take place via defined synchronisation mechanisms between the independent instances. Database architecture - Central data input for the TMB and the Brandenburg content network is distributed, as shown above, across the POI database DAMAS, the events database (TDH) and the media archive. Thus, apart from the geographic information system QGIS, there is no centralised and generic data storage. The main objective is to operate only a single system for data and content management. This also applies to the currently standalone B2B portal and the portals of the B2C website frameworks. - The architecture is to be decentralised at the same time by implementing an instance model in order to utilise the advantages of state-wide cooperation while also enabling the individuality of partners, in particular the travel regions. This enables a lean standard roles and rights system that can be differentiated within the instances. - The data model is being further developed - building upon the integration of data from the databases described above and the previously separate B2B data. A data model for all data types is designed as a state standard. - A state-wide quality standard is being introduced. - The merging of all data and content into a uniform data model and technical infrastructure provides the basis for implementing a "headless CMS approach". Input management - There is to be only a single interface for entering data and content. - Content is to be importable from external systems into the state system via API. - The use of responsive, as accessible as possible input interfaces is aimed for. AI and service layer - Data entry is to be largely automated with the support of AI applications. - Provision of AI-driven dashboards for management and monitoring of the database as well as an associated task manager. - Development and management of a Graph-RAG-capable infrastructure as the basis for internal knowledge systems and guest services Output management - Provision of an easy-to-use management interface for output management - Provision of configurable standard APIs (REST / GraphQL) - Provision of connectors to common inventory systems - Provision of configurable accessible widgets - Provision of a configurable MCP server and a WebMCP service - Provision of a reading WebDAV interface for media, with which data can be displayed directly, e.g. as directories in Windows Explorer - Provision of a media portal on which media is made available for download by various interested parties with the stored licences.
sig_5641f7ba56ecb950d39b.title: Provision, customisation, operation and further development of a state-wide tourism data management system

At the same time, we aim to familiarise ourselves with the market situation of services related to the service, contract terms and commercial conditions such as pricing. Responding to the request for information is voluntary and is not a prerequisite for participation in a potential tendering procedure nor does it bind Istekki to publish a tendering procedure. sig_57834ae89fbcdf435cb5.description: RVK is a modern transport company that has been under municipal ownership since 1996. The company was formed in 1976 through a merger of railway and postal omnibus services. Its transport area extends across the Rheinisch-Bergischer Kreis, the left-bank Rhein-Sieg-Kreis, the Euskirchen district, and the cities of Cologne, Bonn, Leverkusen, Hürth, Brúhl, and Wesseling. RVK thus connects urban population centres with sparsely populated, rural areas. With capacity, competence, and years of experience, RVK ensures that people in the region travel reliably and safely – in an environmentally friendly, sustainable, and innovative manner. The RVK bus fleet comprises over 600 vehicles, some of which are operated independently and some on behalf of RVK. The transport network encompasses 132 routes with a total length of 2.595 km. In addition, 58 routes are operated by RVK for other transport companies. In total, RVK provides a transport performance of approx. 22,6 million km with approx. 23 million passengers annually. In order to successfully drive forward the vision of sustainable, clean mobility in the service area in the future and thus sustainably reduce local pollutant emissions, Regionalverkehr Köln GmbH (RVK) is implementing extensive measures for digitalisation and networking, and thereby more attractive public transport to reduce NOx and other pollutant emissions, as part of its internal "Null Emission" project (https://www.rvk.de/projekt-null-emission). Based on successful projects in the field of sales backend systems with electronic tickets, subscription online (Abo-Online), and digital timetable information, a stable basis for central customer management has already been established. The planned measure of developing a mobility app within the framework of the "Mobility App and Platform" project builds upon these existing structures and must be seamlessly integrated into the existing sales landscape. As part of this new measure, which is particularly tailored to rural areas, a multitude of previously analogue or isolated mobility offerings are to be bundled into an integrated, intermodal mobility app. Both regional and interregional transport services will be integrated to give users seamless access to various forms of mobility. The project is funded by the Federal Ministry of Transport (BMV). The approval period is fixed until 31.12.2026 and cannot be extended. Encompasses the programming of frontend, backend, and interfaces as well as the integration of the application into the existing system landscape.; Development of a user-centred design concept including UX design, design system, wireframes, prototyping, and accessible design. The results serve as the basis for technical implementation in Lot 1. Both lots are closely related from a technical perspective and will be implemented in parallel or sequentially. The contracting authority coordinates the cooperation between the contractors of both lots to ensure a smooth exchange. In particular, regular coordination and joint review meetings are planned.
sig_57834ae89fbcdf435cb5.title: Digitisation of municipal transport systems for sustainable mobility solutions in rural and urban areas - mobility app and platform

The pathway will support adults with obesity who are waiting lists or at risk of economic activity due to obesity and related long-term conditions. To enable this at scale, NENC ICB is exploring options to procure a digital partner to provide an integrated platform that will act as the digital "spine" for the pathway. The intended service is expected to support the following: 1. Identification and invitation of eligible patients (for example via population-health tools and waiting-list data) 2. Digital referral, consent and triage 3. Patient-facing tools for self-assessment, remote monitoring and behavioural support (including AI meal planning) 4. The platform will need to integrate with existing NHS systems (for example NHS App, GP clinical systems and provider electronic patient records), support high standards of clinical safety, information governance and cybersecurity, and generate data and dashboards required for independent evaluation of outcomes, equity and value for money. This Market Engagement Event is intended to help NENC ICB understand the capabilities, innovations and constraints within the digital health market, and to test our emerging requirements and delivery approach. sig_581f3be67b191e7d1eff.description: The aim of the project is the implementation of the new Diavgeia taking into account modern institutional, operational and technological developments, the more correct implementation of the institutional framework with emphasis on the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the optimal utilisation of Diavgeia information with a data-based architecture and secondarily document-based. The project seeks to increase the efficiency and productivity of public services by enriching the applications of the Diavgeia Programme, supplementing functionality for the collaborative drafting and management of documents to be published based on standardised documents and data structures, and also to add value to the Programme by utilising and enriching the information gathered within it through the use of other information sources with the aim of creating a system of complex reports and other complementary application subsystems and solutions. The new system will allow the monitoring of the operation and organisational structure of public administration in combination with information related to the competences of bodies in the context of multi-level governance and also of personnel as recorded in the Human Resources Register of the Hellenic Republic. The aim is to provide objective evidence for the implementation of the National Administrative Procedures Policy and the prioritisation of the actions of the National Programme for Administrative Simplification. To this end, care has been taken to significantly enhance its interoperability with third-party public sector systems for the dissemination of information without necessarily requiring intervention from the end user. Additionally, through the expansion of information kept in a structured manner (metadata set), it will be possible to capture data groups with special characteristics that enhance transparency at the level of monitoring/evaluation by the general public of indicators related to, for example, the operation and structure of public administration and/or financial figures (public spending). For this purpose, data from other sources and publicly available data will also be utilised to support the monitoring of the operation and action of bodies and to support decision-making. The solution will include the creation of a system for the correct (and as complete as possible per sector) structured collection and processing of data from various public data sources and subsequently making them available to the general public. Illustrative examples of sources are data from systems under development for GOV ERP, HRMS, the Civil Society Organisations Register, ESIDIS, KHMDIS. A distinct subsystem will be developed for further utilisation and extraction of specialised reports with the aim of monitoring the structure, operation and action of public administration as well as monitoring expenditure and procurement and supporting the decision-making process. The system will be scalable for the addition of new sources arising from other actions. Also, within the framework of the action, improvements will be made in relation to identified problems associated with the management of the very large volume of documents collected by Diavgeia at a sharply increasing rate, which also led to the necessary migration of the infrastructure to public cloud services. In this context, advanced services provided by public clouds will be better utilised in order to ensure the uninterrupted provision of services and the monitoring of their provision at the lowest possible cost. The action, taking into account the life cycle of the administrative documents that are published, will address challenges such as the cleaning of multiple copies of the same documents, the extraction of all information in data format and the optimisation of the quality of Diavgeia metadata as well as the automatic publication of important data sets in the central open public data repository www.data.gov.gr. The project also aims to adopt a new architecture that will allow a drastic reduction, by at least 65%, of the required storage space and computational resources while ensuring the proper functioning of the system. To achieve the above goal, both emerging artificial intelligence and language model technologies and techniques for the correct entry of metadata into relevant information will be utilised to facilitate their search, categorisation and utilisation. This contract concerns a single subject matter and is not subdivided into lots due to the project's architecture, the strong interdependencies and complementarity of the individual services that compose it, as well as the high interoperability requirements that must be ensured on the one hand between the functional units (subsystems) to be developed within the framework of this project and on the other hand with third-party systems of Hellenic Republic bodies. The non-subdivision of the contract enhances the quality and security of the project, since unified management reduces the chances of security gaps or incompatibilities appearing between the different systems and facilitates the coordination of its implementation. The duration of the contract is set at thirty-two (32) months including the procedure for checking and acceptance of deliverables. The contract will be awarded on the basis of the most economically advantageous tender, based on the best price-quality ratio. [para. 1.3. & ANNEX I of the Call for Tenders]
sig_581f3be67b191e7d1eff.title: «Restructuring of the DIAYGEIA Programme - DIAYGEIA III»

sig_585545d84402cc436169.description: Iarnród Éireann (IÉ) currently operates and maintains a national GSM-R mobile network which provides driver to CTC communications via on-board GSM-R cab-mobile equipment provided by Siemens Mobility. Currently, GSM-R is in operation on the DART network, with national rollout expected to occur in 2026 on the rest of IE’s fleets. As part of the overall maintenance of the GSM-R mobile network, IÉ carry out monitoring and drive- testing which at present requires IÉ Telecoms personnel to perform this task. The task requires staff to travel onboard IÉ Trainsets with monitoring equipment, which can be both onerous and time consuming. IÉ require the provision of an automated drive-testing and RF monitoring solution that will negate the requirement for staff to travel. To achieve this requirement, it is therefore required to provide a GSM-R Modem and hardware (option)/software/firmware capable of interfacing with the modem and providing the end-user (IE) with a HTTP REST API. This can be integrated with the existing IÉ hosted servers which run a combination of NodeJS applications, InfluxDB and Grafana for recording and visualization of the obtained data or hosted on a supplier provided cloud-based solution that is accessible by IÉ. Further specific details will be provided to the companies who are pre-qualified to the ITT stage. (This tender was previously issued under Resource ID 7911685, which was cancelled).

Therefore, no tenders are requested or to be submitted in response to this request for information. No comments or questions received via the request for information will be answered. One of the tasks of the Finnish National Agency for Education is the publishing of learning materials and publications. Customers include both private individuals and organisations, in particular schools and educational institutions. Products are delivered to the customer either physically (e.g. textbooks) or digitally (e.g. electronic learning materials). We request up-to-date information on a comprehensive service encompassing product logistics, licensing, and online shop services. The service to be procured includes • a SaaS online shop solution where customers can purchase non-fiction books, textbooks, publications, and licences for digital learning materials published by the Finnish National Agency for Education, as well as downloadable files, using commonly used payment methods • a logistics and distribution service for textbooks and publications, including distribution to key resellers such as Library Service, bookshops, and learning material intermediaries • a digital product licence management service, and • a sales settlement service, including inventory value reporting. Service requirements • The online shop must serve our customers in Finnish, Swedish, and English. • The service must meet the accessibility requirements of the Act on the Provision of Digital Services. • It shall be possible to integrate the service with the Finnish National Agency for Education's digital learning platform (licence management) and product register. • The online shop solution must provide the capability for the Finnish National Agency for Education to edit the layout, texts, and settings of the online shop. In addition, it must be possible to add sample pages, reading samples, and promotional videos to the online shop. We request the following information 1. Does the Supplier have a comprehensive service meeting the above description to offer? 2. What pricing model does the Supplier use? 3. Based on the above description, does the Supplier have any comments on the potential requirement specification for the procurement? 4. Optional additional question: The Finnish National Agency for Education is exploring alternatives to replace its self-developed product information system and royalty register. Is it possible to tailor a product and royalty register into the Supplier's service that includes the necessary databases and user interface? The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement or to implement it in the manner described in the request for information. The contracting authority is not obliged to take account of responses received to the request for information when drawing up the call for tenders. Responding to the request for information does not bind the tenderer or affect the tenderer's position in any potential procurement procedure. sig_5a2866a220714cf5e2a2.description:
This procurement forms part of the project "Transformation of public services through digitalisation in Comuna Chetani, Mureș County", financed through the Central Regional Programme 2021–2027, within project call PRC/444/PRC_P2/OP1, and aligns with the objective of supporting the digital development of the Commune of Chetani Town Hall. It targets the development, testing and piloting of two innovative digital solutions: a front-office type solution and a back-office type solution, intended to improve the interaction between the authority and the citizen/taxpayer and to facilitate access. The project supports the transition to an intelligent and innovative economy. In the context of a decentralised software infrastructure within the town hall, where each department uses specific software, the need is highlighted for two integrated solutions that unify e-government services and document management, ensuring the traceability of the town hall's internal and external activities. Thus, the project pursues the development, testing and piloting of two complex digital solutions: 1. The front-office digital solution – an online solution that facilitates the digitalisation of public administration by offering online services by the ATU to citizens, supporting the interaction between the Town Hall and the citizen/taxpayer. The front-office solution is designed to optimise the flow of information between the Town Hall and citizens, addressing both individuals and legal entities. The platform will allow users intuitive and efficient access to relevant and personalised information. The front-office solution will include the following: Info-kiosk application (IoT); Digital solution for offering online services Tax online services, Digital solution for offering online services regarding the agricultural register, Digital solution for urban planning online services, Information publication and management portal, Local Official Gazette digital solution, Participatory budgeting mechanism, Online communication solution for data and documents with judicial executor offices, Digital solution for offering online services to citizens, Mobile device application with shared services addressed to citizens 2. The back-office digital solution – an integrated computer system intended for the automation, streamlining and securing of the institution's internal workflows and supporting collaboration between departments. Designed to centralise and manage data and administrative processes, this system includes functionalities adapted to the operational specifics of local public administration, ensuring optimised management of internal activities. The front office solution will include the following: Digital Document Management solution, Registry Module, Mobile solution for the inventory of fixed assets and inventory items, Digital solution for ROeID, Electronic archive solution, Cyber security solution of IDS type, Citizen and address data aggregator (web and mobile), prescriptive debits management module, treasury import solution, F2201/F2202 / Garnishments, Court of Accounts Module, Communication of documents and data in structured electronic format with the DRPCIV, Video surveillance solution, Information application regarding energy efficiency. This procurement forms part of the project "Transformation of public services through digitalisation in Comuna Chetani, Mureș County", financed through the Central Regional Programme 2021–2027, within project call PRC/444/PRC_P2/OP1, and aligns with the objective of supporting the digital development of the Commune of Chetani Town Hall. It targets the development, testing and piloting of two innovative digital solutions: a front-office type solution and a back-office type solution, intended to improve the interaction between the authority and the citizen/taxpayer and to facilitate access. The project supports the transition to an intelligent and innovative economy. In the context of a decentralised software infrastructure within the town hall, where each department uses specific software, the need is highlighted for two integrated solutions that unify e-government services and document management, ensuring the traceability of the town hall's internal and external activities. Thus, the project pursues the development, testing and piloting of two complex digital solutions: 1. The front-office digital solution – an online solution that facilitates the digitalisation of public administration by offering online services by the ATU to citizens, supporting the interaction between the Town Hall and the citizen/taxpayer. The front-office solution is designed to optimise the flow of information between the Town Hall and citizens, addressing both individuals and legal entities. The platform will allow users intuitive and efficient access to relevant and personalised information. The front-office solution will include the following: Info-kiosk application (IoT); Digital solution for offering online services Tax online services, Digital solution for offering online services regarding the agricultural register, Digital solution for urban planning online services, Information publication and management portal, Local Official Gazette digital solution, Participatory budgeting mechanism, Online communication solution for data and documents with judicial executor offices, Digital solution for offering online services to citizens, Mobile device application with shared services addressed to citizens 2. The back-office digital solution – an integrated computer system intended for the automation, streamlining and securing of the institution's internal workflows and supporting collaboration between departments.

Designed to centralise and manage data and administrative processes, this system includes functionalities adapted to the operational specifics of local public administration, ensuring optimised management of internal activities. The front office solution will include the following: Digital Document Management solution, Registry Module, Mobile solution for the inventory of fixed assets and inventory items, Digital solution for ROeID, Electronic archive solution, Cyber security solution of IDS type, Citizen and address data aggregator (web and mobile), prescriptive debits management module, treasury import solution, F2201/F2202 / Garnishments, Court of Accounts Module, Communication of documents and data in structured electronic format with the DRPCIV, Video surveillance solution, Information application regarding energy efficiency. The solutions provided for in this project aim to digitise the public administration of the commune of Chetani by providing online services for citizens, thus facilitating direct interaction between the Town Hall and the citizen/taxpayer. These solutions will be developed to improve the exchange of information between the Town Hall and citizens, targeting both individuals and legal entities.

sig_5a9387b58d272c68c288.description: The International Charter: Space and Major Disasters (“the Charter”) is a global agreement which aims to provide a unified system of space data acquisition and delivery to those affected by natural or man-made disasters. It provides and enables transmission of earth observation satellite data and pre-authorised resilience/emergency response bodies in response to “activations”. Further details on the Charter can be found at https://disasterscharter.org/ Unlike many space faring nations in the Charter, the UK Government does not own or operate its own national EO satellite system assets. The UK Government therefore fulfils its Charter commitments through partnership with the UK EO commercial sector. This procurement seeks to maintain and strengthen that model by securing operational support from an organisation with UK licensed and operated EO satellite data assets that can be contributed to Charter activations. The continued participation of UK EO commercial satellite operators in the Charter delivers both public benefit and strategic value by showcasing sovereign EO capabilities, supporting international disaster response and demonstrating operational utility of UK-developed EO missions. The Contracting Authority is intending to launch this requirement by the 9th of October - prospective bidders should note it may launch earlier at the Contracting Authority's discretion: all dates provided are estimates at this stage. Lot 1: . None
sig_5a9387b58d272c68c288.title: UK Space Agency - Operational Support to the International Charter: Space and Major Disasters

sig_5b6f66aa5bfd3cada2e4.description: Verkehrsgesellschaft Landkreis Gifhorn mbH (VLG) intends to gradually convert its bus fleet to electromobility within the framework of the requirements of the Clean Vehicles Procurement Act. For this purpose, electric buses and the charging infrastructure required for their operation are to be procured and integrated into operational processes. VLG plans to initially provide charging infrastructure for initially 11 vehicles by the year 2027. A charging and load management system is to be introduced for the centralised control and monitoring of charging processes, for limiting grid load as well as for supporting operational vehicle dispatching and vehicle stabling. With the introduction of electromobility, additional requirements arise for the planning and control of vehicle deployment, charging processes and available electrical power. Vehicle availability, battery charge state, energy demand, planned departure times, charging point occupancy and available grid capacity must in future be brought together and taken into account in a system-supported manner. The initial expansion stage comprises the charging infrastructure for 11 vehicles. The exact number and design of the charging points, their technical properties as well as the operational systems and data sources to be integrated are described in a binding manner in the quantity framework, in the interface descriptions and in the appendices to this specification. The increasing requirements in the course of the progressive electrification of the bus fleet as well as the expansion of the charging infrastructure require a high-performance charging, load and energy management system. With the introduction of an LMS, charging processes are to be controlled taking into account the boundary conditions from charging infrastructure, vehicle data, battery charge states and range requirements. The LMS must control the charging processes in such a way that the charge states required for the planned vehicle deployment are reached in good time. The charging infrastructure is to be integrated into the LMS so that the status of the charging units can be centrally monitored and controlled.
sig_5b6f66aa5bfd3cada2e4.title: Procurement and introduction of a charging management system for VLG

sig_5bd60a64138ad98ac5e2.description: The Scottish Government is pursuing a comprehensive programme to reform and modernise Scotland’s compulsory purchase system. Lot 1: . The overall aim of this research is to provide information about the compensation received by those whose land is acquired under compulsory purchase powers. The evidence generated through the research is intended to inform decisions on potential future legislation by the Scottish Government and scrutiny of any such legislation by the Scottish Parliament. The objectives of the project are to address the following questions: a. How frequently and to what extent are compensation payments affected by the prospect of future planning permission (“hope value”)? b. In cases where hope value is a factor, to what extent are payments affected by the timing, costs and risks of implementing any such prospective planning permission? c. To what extent does the current condition of property affect the market value calculated for the purpose of compensation?
sig_5bd60a64138ad98ac5e2.title: Compulsory Purchase Compensation Research

sig_5c570f68fc4d8b9d2297.description: Our Workplace Innovation Leadership Academy supports the ongoing development of business leaders at all levels and stages of experience. The Leadership Academy delivers programmes under a framework agreement with multiple suppliers across the Scottish Enterprise area, the programme plays a key role in cultivating leadership capability and innovation within businesses. The current framework expires early April 2026 and we anticipate commencing a new procurement process in December 2025. To inform this process, we are seeking to engage with the market to better understand current capabilities and approaches to delivering high-impact leadership development. We welcome expressions of interest from suppliers who possess specialist knowledge, proven experience, and the capacity to deliver innovative and effective leadership programmes tailored to diverse business needs. The Workplace Innovation Leadership Development Framework will consist of a series of one-day workshops, one-to-one coaching sessions, and topic specific diagnostic tools, delivered over a period of 2 - 6 months, depending on the Lot. Delivery will follow a hybrid model, combining online and face-to-face formats to maximise accessibility and impact. The Framework will deliver programmes across the Scottish Enterprise area, responding to demand. Where appropriate, programmes may also be delivered in collaboration with other enterprise agencies across Scotland. Lot 1: Transformational Leadership Programme. A cohesive leadership programme designed for both emerging and established leaders, with consistent core themes and tailored content to reflect each group's unique needs and experiences. Lot 2: Innovating Leadership: AI, Data & Emerging Tech. To empower leaders to embed AI, data, and emerging tech into strategy, foster ethical leadership, and drive internal innovation in a tech-enabled world. Lot 3: Growth Through Risk & Ambition. To support leaders in evaluating growth strategies, embracing risk as a catalyst for innovation, and exploring strategic options like investment, mergers, and ESG-aligned finance. Encourages a culture of learning through experimentation. Lot 4: Leadership in Times of Geopolitical & Economic Volatility. Helps leaders build resilience, agility, change capability and foresight to lead through uncertainty, global disruption, and change—while staying focused on long-term sustainability and stakeholder trust.

sig_5cb6de6c4d3736be684f.description: Description: The State of Saxony-Anhalt has its own state data network, which is currently operated technically by an IT service provider. The state data network was set up by this IT service provider. The intention now is to retender the operation of the state data network as a high-performance and integrated state data network (LAN/WAN) as well as all measures and services necessary for this. The operation of the operations centre with, among other things, network-related services, the operation of components and systems within a data centre and necessary operational and technical tools are also to be awarded. To prepare for this retender, the MID as the responsible authority for the State of Saxony-Anhalt is conducting a market exploration in accordance with § 28 of the VgV. The aim is in particular to explore what organisational, technical and economic solutions are available on the market to ensure operation on a permanent, secure, reliable and scalable basis, as well as the conditions that may be necessary for this and the general time schedule. This is expressly not a call for competition or any other bidding procedure, but rather a non-binding market analysis for orientation and as a basis for decision-making for the preparation of any subsequent procurement procedure. Companies that wish to participate in the market exploration will be provided with further documents in the market exploration procedure. In order to gain access to these documents, an expression of interest and the submission of a non-disclosure agreement are required to protect sensitive data regarding critical infrastructure. Interested parties are therefore requested to express their interest in participating in the present market exploration procedure by 28.11.2025 at the latest by sending an email with the subject 'Market exploration procedure state data network' to the following email address: lnstender@sachsen-anhalt.de and stating the necessary contact details (name of the company, registered office of the company, address of the company and email address). You will then receive a draft non-disclosure agreement, which must then be completed and returned signed. Upon receipt of the non-disclosure agreement, the further documents for the market exploration will be sent to the interested parties concerned. These contain further information and documents. It is planned to conduct online market exploration discussions with the interested parties. These are expected to be scheduled in the four calendar weeks following the above-mentioned deadline. To prepare for the discussions, participants are asked to complete and submit a prepared questionnaire. Further information on this can be found in the market exploration documents, which will be made available after the submission of the non-disclosure agreement.

sig_5d9a534841588521dec8.description: The task is to prepare the licensing and detailed design plans for the Eger bypass road in accordance with the technical content specified in the design task description issued as part of the procurement documentation. The Eger bypass road starts from the roundabout junction of the M25 motorway, runs on the eastern side of the town of Eger, provides a connection between main road Nos 25 and 24, and connects to main road No. 25 by bypassing the Felnémet district. Tasks: Preparation of complete licensing plans together with the decision-preliminary documentation providing the basis for its details and individual technical parameters, obtaining permits, preparation of a feasibility study, as well as the preparation, licensing, and approval of complete detailed design plans, in accordance with the technical content specified in the design task description issued as part of the procurement documentation. The main estimated quantities for information purposes: Approximately 17 km of national public road, which is planned to have a 2x2 lane layout over a length of ~1,4 km (by rebuilding the existing 2x1 lane road), and a continuous national public road with 2x1 traffic lanes (designed on a new alignment) over a continuous length of ~15,6 km. The project includes the design of approximately 9 km of local public roads (~6 km of new alignment, ~3 km of pavement strengthening), 13 roundabout junctions (of which 3 are turbo roundabouts), the reconstruction of 7 at-grade junctions, the creation of 12 simple junctions or junctions with vehicle sorting lanes, the construction of 6 new structures, as well as the reconstruction of 3 existing structures, and the establishment of 1 at-grade railway crossings. Among the structures, a new national public road bridge over a railway with 2x2 lanes and a maximum superstructure length of 81,8 m is planned. The design of climbing lanes, retaining walls, and cuttings on certain sections of the bypass road, as well as the design of cycle path sections (new alignment, length of ~1 km), the creation of footpaths and pavements (over a length of 2,7 km), and the expected creation of 2 pedestrian crossings are also part of the project. The successful tenderer is obliged to cooperate in the public procurement procedures conducted for the implementation of the construction investment based on the plans prepared by them or parts thereof, as detailed in the draft contract. In the case of complete licensing and complete detailed design plans, building information modelling (BIM) based design shall take place, in accordance with Decree 31/2024 of the Ministry of Construction and Transport (VIII. 22.). The BIM requirements are contained in the design task description. The Contracting Authority draws attention to the fact that - the basic task to be performed within the framework of the contract to be concluded as a result of this procedure is the preparation of the decision-preliminary documentation, the feasibility study, and the complete licensing plans, and obtaining the permits; - with regard to the preparation of the complete detailed design and tender plans, as well as volumes III, IV, and V of the (public) procurement documentation suitable for construction, the Contractual Agreement issued as part of the procurement documentation contains a separate entry-into-force condition in view of Article 41 paragraph (1) of the Public Procurement Act; - the designer's site supervision arising during the implementation phase of the state construction investment, specified in Article 19 paragraph (1) of the Public Procurement Act, will be called upon as an option (for more details see: point "II.2.11) Information relating to options", field BT-53). Within the framework of the designer's site supervision, the tasks of the successful tenderer are: - to monitor the execution of the project, - to verify the implementation of the detailed design documentation prepared by them, - to draw attention to factors hindering or promoting implementation according to the plans, - to make proposals for the professional resolution of technical uncertainties and problems arising during construction, - to facilitate the resolution of professional questions arising during construction in connection with the detailed design documentation. A detailed description of the task is contained in the design task description.
sig_5d9a534841588521dec8.title: Preparation of permission and detailed design plans for the Eger bypass road

sig_5ddac62cdd050fb6ea26.description: LapIT Oy is an IT company owned by the municipalities, joint municipal authorities, and municipal limited companies of Lapland and Koillismaa, which provides comprehensive information management and IT services. Our company's head office is located in Rovaniemi. LapIT is considering putting the financial management system out to tender and offering it to its owner-customers. Currently, there are 10 municipal customers interested in the procurement. According to preliminary plans, the procurement would cover the following processes: - from financial planning to forecasting - from procurement to payment - from sales to debt collection - from bookkeeping to financial statements - authority reporting (municipal reporting) Based on preliminary information, the procurement would cover the financial management solution as a comprehensive service, including implementation and user training, migrations from old systems, and integrations. LapIT requests willing potential tenderers to participate in a dialogue. In principle, we will accept into the market dialogue those tenderers who meet at least the following criteria: - The supplier must have at least 2 references for the solution for municipal customers. The systems reported as references must have been in production use for at least 2 years. - The solution must comply with high data security and the data must be located in the EU/EEA area. - The tenderer must offer implementation support and continuous service support in the Finnish language. The tenderer must attach to their registration: - A description of their service in Finnish. - Presentations of at least two reference deliveries as stated above. - The description should show the lifecycle status and development roadmap of the system. Willing participants can register for the dialogue by notifying us by email at jasmine.suopanki@lapit.fi by 5.11.2025. The intention is to start the market dialogues as soon as possible. LapIT will select the suppliers it chooses for the market dialogue based on the descriptions. LapIT reserves the right to limit the number of those who have participated in the market dialogue. The implementation method of the market dialogue will be decided later (written/meetings). Participation in the market dialogue does not in any way affect the tenderer's position in a possible future tendering process. The market dialogue will be carried out in the Finnish language. Everything presented in the market dialogue and the discussions held during it are preliminary and do not bind LapIT Oy or the tenderer. No compensation will be paid to those who have participated in the market dialogue for their participation. This is not a procurement notice or a call for tenders but a request for information/invitation to a market dialogue. This preliminary information notice does not bind the client to the procurement; the actual procurement notice will possibly be published later. The decision on launching a possible procurement process will be made later.
sig_5ddac62cdd050fb6ea26.title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION/PRIOR INFORMATION NOTICE: Financial management systems for municipal needs

sig_5e416c2ddb19360f6b6d.description: 1 INTRODUCTION The purpose of this request for information is to survey the SRM (Supplier Relationship Management) system solutions available on the market and to collect information on their features, implementation options and suppliers to support the preparation of a future procurement. Through this request for information, the contracting authority aims to form an overall picture of the market supply and to assess the options related to the implementation of the procurement. The subject of the procurement is described at a preliminary level in the appendices to this request for information. The preliminary description of the subject of the procurement and the contracting authority's current view of the needs are presented in the appendices to the request for information 1-5. Questions about the materials are presented in the appendix to the request for information 6. The procurement will be implemented by default through the Modern Digital Work, Microsoft Power Platform, Microsoft Dynamics 365 and Microsoft Windows device management: expert services, consulting and ready-made solutions 2025 -2029 (DPS) category 2. Suppliers are encouraged to join the relevant DPS system to submit a tender. 2 ORGANISING THE MARKET DIALOGUE AND RESPONDING TO THE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION Suppliers are requested to notify their willingness to participate in this request for information / technical dialogue by advance notice via email to the address hankinnat@istekki.fi no later than 21.9.2026. If the tenderer has registered for a previous request for information publication concerning this procurement "REQUEST FOR INFORMATION – Tools for the procure-to-pay process", registration does not need to be done separately. Responses to all materials of the request for information and the questions presented must be submitted no later than 30.09.2026 via email to the address hankinnat@istekki.fi. The advance registration must contain the following information: - Tenderer's name - Email address for the delivery of the remaining materials The purpose of the advance registration is to support the preparation of the technical dialogue and to enable the delivery of supplementary materials related to the dialogue to the participating suppliers. The contracting authority will later provide the registered suppliers with a draft contract for comment. This request for information is implemented as a technical dialogue. 3 OTHER MATTERS TO BE NOTED The request for information is not a contract notice, a call for tenders or an invitation to tender. Responding to the request for information does not bind the respondent or the contracting authority to a subsequent procurement procedure. The contracting authority will utilise the received responses in the planning of a possible future procurement and in the preparation of the call for tenders. It is good to note that this request for information does not oblige Istekki Oy to carry out the procurement in the manner presented in this document or its appendices. A possible call for tenders may also be left unorganised. No separate compensation will be paid for responding to the request for information or participating in presentation events. This is a request for information, not an advance notice, a contract notice or a call for tenders. The purpose of the request for information is to get to know the market situation and to collect information related to the subject of the procurement to support the planning of the future competitive tendering. Responding to the request for information is voluntary, and it is not a prerequisite for participating in a possible call for tenders and does not bind Istekki to publish a call for tenders. Please note that the information, descriptions and estimates of the schedule for the competitive tendering presented in this request for information are preliminary and indicative. The final schedules will be refined as the preparation progresses. We greatly appreciate the information provided by the suppliers, as it helps us to build the future competitive tendering as functional and clear a whole as possible.
sig_5e416c2ddb19360f6b6d.title: Call for tenders materials for reading / Procurement of a Supplier Relationship Management (SRM) system for Istekki 2026

The service required is composed of three main work packages: hardware provisioning (covering the supply and lifecycle of user devices), software licensing (managing procurement and compliance of key applications), and workplace support (providing user assistance and incident resolution). The aim of this RFP and the resulting agreement is to consolidate and enhance this model by integrating these key functions into a single, cohesive service. The selected vendor will work closely with EIT Urban Mobility’s internal Technology Department to deliver a coherent service fully aligned with the company’s strategic roadmap, while contributing added value through expertise, quality, and continuous improvement. EIT Urban Mobility currently has over 185 users (and over 210 including external collaborators). sig_5ee014d4aebe9663afd1.description: Project reason TenneT requires a portfolio management system (PMS) to support electricity trading in the short-term market (day-ahead and intraday) in Germany. Objective of the tender The objective is the procurement of a high-performance PMS to support electricity trading. In accordance with TenneT's architectural guidelines, the solution is to be cloud-based, preferably operated in the tenderer's cloud. In coordination with TenneT, deployment in a third-party provider's cloud (e.g. Azure) or at TenneT is also possible. The system must enable the management of multiple portfolios and support the processes for participating in day-ahead and intraday auctions as well as continuous intraday trading. The system will be used in the electricity trading sector and must cover the following main functions: - Portfolio management - Connection to power exchanges - Trading overviews & GUI - Algo-trader / trading support in continuous intraday trading - Data management - Reporting & analysis - Settlement - Schedule management Scope of services - Provision of a COTS software solution (licences) - Support & maintenance of this solution (maintenance) - Hosting of the solution - Application management services - Consulting and training services Procedural notice A detailed specification of services as well as other procedural-relevant documents will be provided after signing a non-disclosure agreement. Please send this to us completed and signed via the Mercell messaging function. The tender is being conducted in accordance with the SektVO (Sectoral Procurement Ordinance) via a negotiated procedure with a call for competition. Accordingly, TenneT is already bound to confidentiality pursuant to Section 15 SektVO. As things stand, the value of the tender cannot be reliably estimated.
sig_5ee014d4aebe9663afd1.title: Portfoliomanagement-System für den Energiehandel

sig_5fce472d03558e520413.description: The Tribal Colleges and Universities Program (TCUP) provides awards to federally recognized 1 Tribal Colleges and Universities, Alaska Native-serving institutions, and Native Hawaiian-serving institutions to promote high quality science (including sociology, psychology, anthropology, linguistics, economics and bioeconomics, statistics, and other social and behavioral sciences; natural sciences; computer science, including, but not limited to, artificial intelligence, quantum information science, and cybersecurity), technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM), STEM education, research, and outreach. Support is available to TCUP-eligible institutions (see the Additional Eligibility subsection of Section IV of this solicitation) for transformative capacity-building or community engagement projects through Instructional Capacity Excellence in TCUP Institutions (ICE-TI) , Targeted STEM Infusion Projects (TSIP) , TCUP for Secondary and Elementary Teachers in STEM (TSETS) , TCU Enterprise Advancement Centers (TEA Centers) , Cyberinfrastructure Health, Assistance, and Improvements (CHAI) , and Preparing for TCUP Implementation (Pre-TI) . Collaborations led by TCUP institutions that involve non-TCUP institutions of higher education are supported through TCUP Partnerships , with the participation of other NSF programs to support the work of non-TCUP institutions. Finally, research studies that further the scholarly activity of individual faculty members are supported through Small Grants for Research (SGR) . Through the opportunities highlighted above, as well as collaborations with other National Science Foundation (NSF) divisions and directorates, and other organizations, TCUP aims to increase Native individuals' participation in STEM careers, improve the quality of STEM programs at TCUP-eligible institutions, and facilitate the development of a strong STEM enterprise in TCUP institutions' service areas. TCUP supports transformative capacity-building, community engagement, or research projects at TCUP-eligible institutions through the following funding tracks: Instructional Capacity Excellence in TCUP Institutions (ICE-TI) projects provide support to design, implement, and assess comprehensive institutional improvements in STEM education and research capacity at TCUP-eligible institutions of higher education. By strengthening STEM education and STEM education research, successful projects will increase the number of STEM students and improve the quality of their preparation. ICE-TI projects create and/or adapt and assess innovative models and materials for teaching and learning in STEM, embody knowledge about how students learn most effectively in STEM teaching and learning activities, and bring STEM disciplinary advances into the undergraduate or graduate experience. The objective of this strand is to expand STEM degrees offered by TCUP-eligible institutions or significantly enhance instructional approaches. Targeted STEM Infusion Projects (TSIP) support the attainment of a short-term, well-defined goal to improve the quality of STEM education at an eligible institution. Targeted STEM Infusion Projects could, for example, enhance academic infrastructure by systematically adding traditional knowledge to the scope or content of a STEM course, updating curricula, modernizing laboratory research equipment, developing and delivering professional development for K-12 STEM educators, or improving the computational infrastructure. The objective of this strand is to expand STEM degrees or significantly enhance instructional approaches. TCUP for Secondary & Elementary Teachers in STEM (TSETS) supports in-service professional development in STEM disciplinary or STEM education content and/or research for K-12 STEM teachers in the relevant service area. Examples of project activities include, but are not limited to, professional development involving seminar series and engagement in STEM instruction and content during the academic year, structured series of summer intensive workshops and trainings, and summer research opportunities. The objective of this strand is to broaden the instructional capacity for STEM in the K-12 workforce and thereby to the entire community, and to build the capacity for STEM disciplinary or education research among participating educational professionals. TCU Enterprise Advancement Centers (TEA Centers) coalesce the STEM and/or STEM education expertise into a team, designed to support and promote the STEM goals, needs, aspirations, or interests of the chartering reservation or tribe(s). TEA Centers may address a critical tribal or community need or focus on a realm of research or design that is beyond the scope of individual research grants or that is of interest to multiple tribes. The objective of this strand is to build on the capacity developed through prior TCUP support and apply expertise to collaborations with communities in the institution’s service area, or nationally. The Cyberinfrastructure Health, Assistance, and Improvements (CHAI) strand supports projects at TCUP-eligible institutions of higher education to upgrade the cyberinfrastructure necessary to conduct, expand, manage and administer STEM programs of study, including research. The objective of this strand is to equip TCUP institutions to meet the demands of virtual instruction, advanced computing, and data science opportunities. Preparing for TCUP Implementation (Pre-TI) provides support for activities that prepare an institution for Implementation-level projects. Consequently, they are available only to TCUP-eligible institutions of higher education that have never received TCUP support, have not received TCUP support within the previous five years, or are embarking on a significantly novel STEM strategic plan. Examples of supported activities include completing an institutional assessment of its current STEM instructional capacity, or engaging in conversations necessary to formulate a shared vision of what that capacity should be and how to achieve it. Pre-TI awards can support staff and faculty release time, travel, stakeholder gatherings, and associated administrative costs. The objective of this strand is to conduct self-studies and formulate strategic plans for the development of STEM instructional programs of study. The TCUP Partnerships strand provides support for collaborations that will improve TCUP institutions' instructional and research capacity in STEM fields supported by NSF; attract, retain, and support TCUP students in internships and research endeavors deemed to be necessary for a complete curriculum offering; and engage partner universities to provide an academic grounding and a successful transition for students who wish to study or attain degrees in STEM fields supported by NSF. TCUP Partnerships broaden the number of scientific disciplines available to students at TCUP institution through collaborations with non-TCUP institutions. Active Pre-Engineering Education Collaboratives or Partnerships in Geoscience Education awards are not affected by this revision. The objective of this strand is the development, through instructional and research capacity-building, of academic and career pathways for TCUP students through supporting collaborative projects between and among TCUP and non-TCUP institutions. Interested teams of collaborators for which a TCUP institution serves as lead should contact the TCUP program directors. Support for non-TCUP partners must be obtained from other NSF programs, which follows the procedures of the prior Partnership strands. Small Grants for Research (SGR) strand support STEM or STEM Education faculty members at TCUP-eligible institutions to initiate or pursue research projects or programs that may include undergraduate or graduate student engagement. Awards are intended to help further the faculty member's research capability and effectiveness; improve research and teaching at his or her home institution and create and study new models and innovations in STEM teaching and learning. International research or collaborations are strongly encouraged. TCUP students may seek support for international research opportunities under the guidance of a TCUP STEM or STEM education faculty member and an international research collaborator. These awards are particularly appropriate as a means of recruiting and retaining highly qualified scientists, engineers, and educators at TCUP-eligible institutions. The objective of this strand is to support faculty research and professional development that build research capacity at TCUP institutions. [1] Executive Order 13021 defines Tribal Colleges and Universities ("tribal colleges") as those institutions cited in section 532 of the Equity in Educational Land-Grant Status Act of 1994 (7 U.S.C. 301 note), and other institutions that qualify for funding under the Tribally Controlled Community College Assistance Act of 1978, (25 U.S.C. 1801 et seq.), as well as Navajo Community College as authorized in the Navajo Community College Assistance Act of 1978, Public Law 95-471, Title II (25 U.S.C. 640a note). The term "Alaska Native-serving institution" means an institution of higher education that is an eligible institution under section 1058(b) of the Higher Education Act; and that, at the time of submission, has an undergraduate enrollment that is at least 20 percent Alaska Native students. The term "Native Hawaiian-serving institution" means an institution of higher education that is an eligible institution under section 1058(b) of the Higher Education Act; and that, at the time of submission, has an undergraduate enrollment that is at least 10 percent Native Hawaiian students. Most TCUP-eligible institutions of higher education are two-year or community colleges. See the Who May Submit Proposals section in this solicitation for further details.

sig_5fcea02b484c0f4bd326.description: Horley Town Council invites quotes from suitably qualified suppliers for website design, development, hosting and maintenance services. REQUIREMENTS: We require a comprehensive website solution meeting all statutory requirements for local government, including: - Full WCAG 2.2 Level AA accessibility compliance from launch - Compliance with Local Government Transparency Code 2015 - Support for Assertion 10 audit requirements for digital and data compliance - Modern, mobile-responsive design with intuitive CMS - Secure hosting with SSL, backups and disaster recovery - Multiple user licences for content management - SEO optimisation and social media integration - Events calendar and booking system - News section and photo galleries - Document library with version control - Committee and councillor information pages - Online consultation and engagement tools - Resident reporting tools for local service issues (highways, fly-tipping, etc.) - Forms for council services and applications - Venue hire booking system - Contact forms (GDPR compliant) - Newsletter subscription functionality - Mapping for local amenities - Portal links to planning authority and online meetings (Webex) - Migration of existing website content with URL redirects - Comprehensive staff training on CMS - User manuals and video tutorials ONGOING SUPPORT: - Regular software updates and security patches - Continuous performance monitoring - Technical support during business hours - Annual accessibility compliance review (included in core service) - Maintenance of WCAG 2.2 AA compliance - Regular backups - Website analytics and usage reporting - Proactive notification of legislative/regulatory changes ESSENTIAL CRITERIA: Suppliers must demonstrate: - Minimum 3 years' experience with town and parish council websites in England - Portfolio of at least 5 current websites meeting WCAG 2.2 AA standards - Detailed knowledge of Local Government Transparency Code 2015 and Assertion 10 requirements - Proven technical capability for accessible website delivery - Adequate support infrastructure - Financial stability and appropriate insurance CONTRACT: Initial 2-year period with performance monitoring through quarterly reviews. Full specification available at: https://www.horleysurrey-tc.gov.uk/news/article/1544 SUBMISSION: Quotes by email to info@horleysurrey-tc.gov.uk by Friday 27 February 2026 at 12:00 noon.

sig_5fd4c4eb1fe23425d9fe.description: The services involve the drafting of the forest management plan, a product of management activity with technical-organisational content, ecologically substantiated, by which the works necessary to be executed in a production unit are established for a period of time, with the aim of bringing and subsequently maintaining the structural characteristics of the stands and of the forest as a whole at the values pertaining to the optimal structural model defined in accordance with the ecological, social and economic objectives pursued through sustainable management. According to the provisions of Article 63 paragraph (11) of Law No. 331/2024 on the Forest Code, with subsequent amendments and completions, it is necessary that the drafting of forest management plans be carried out through public procurement procedures. The management of the state's public property forest fund constitutes a priority obligation of the forest fund administrators. The manner of managing the state's public property forest fund is regulated by forest management plans. Forest management plans and amendments thereto are approved by order of the head of the Authority. In the case of state public property land, the plans provide data and information necessary for their registration/updating in the centralised inventory of property in the state's public domain and for registration in the integrated cadastre and land register system. Clarifications regarding the tender documentation may be requested before the deadline for submitting bids, as follows: at the latest on the 18 -th day before the deadline established for submitting bids in the notice of participation. The Contracting Authority will clearly and completely respond to all requests for clarifications, as follows: at the latest on the 10 -th day before the deadline established for submitting bids in the notice of participation. NOTE: The contracting authority is not obliged to respond to requests for clarifications/additional information that were not addressed within the established deadline. Forest management services for the Brad Forest District - DS Hunedoara, with an area of 18.486,87 ha, in accordance with the specifications.
