sig_5ffa3471f05cf4c9fb5c.description: The Authority is seeking to appoint a suitably experienced and compliant Bidder to provide a secure, efficient and fully compliant electronic bulk ("e‐Bulk") solution for the end-to-end administration of DBS applications. The solution must support the Authority's Registered Body status and provide a fully hosted, cloud-based platform that enables the secure processing, tracking and management of DBS applications across multiple Council services and user groups. The Successful Provider must be an approved DBS e-Broker, authorised to submit applications on behalf of Registered Bodies. The Authority requires an accessible, bilingual in Welsh and English, compliant with Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WGAC) 2.2 AA accessibility standards, and capable of supporting multiple Council service areas and user roles. An optional Digital Identity Verification service may also be awarded as part of the contract, subject to the Authority's assessment of the Provider's data protection, information governance and security arrangements. The procurement process will be conducted in four (4) stages. Bidders must successfully meet the requirements of each stage before progressing to the next stage of evaluation. Where a stage is assessed on a pass/fail basis, bidders must achieve a "Pass" outcome in order to proceed. Where a stage is subject to scored evaluation, bidders must achieve the minimum threshold score specified within the tender documentation. Any bidder that fails a pass/fail requirement, receives a score below the minimum required threshold, or otherwise fails to satisfy the requirements of a stage, will be excluded from further consideration and their tender submission will not be evaluated in subsequent stages. The Council reserves the right to reject any tender that fails to meet the mandatory requirements of this procurement exercise. Full details can be found in the ITT.
sig_5ffa3471f05cf4c9fb5c.title: Provision of an E Bulk Solution for the Administration of Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS)

sig_60106b1aa7da1b8b3fdd.description: We ask you to submit your answers to this information request concerning the procurement of a certificate automation system. We greatly appreciate all the answers we receive, and each of them will be taken into account in the preparation of a possible tendering procedure. The purpose of the information request is to ensure that those preparing the tendering procedure have as comprehensive and up-to-date a picture of the market and the solutions on offer as possible. With this information request, we want to survey suppliers' offerings of systems that support the automatic renewal of public SSL certificates and the managed installation of certificates for systems using them. At the same time, we aim to familiarise ourselves with the market situation of services related to the systems, products possibly related to the use of the system, contract terms and conditions, and commercial terms such as pricing. Based on the responses to the information request, market dialogue sessions may be organised, where suppliers can present their own services, products and alternatives for the implementation of the procurement subject. If market dialogue sessions are organised, they will be conducted in the Finnish language. Istekki will announce more detailed schedules and a Teams meeting link to the companies participating in the sessions later. Please note that the information, descriptions and estimates of the publication date of the tendering procedure presented in this information request are still preliminary and indicative. Final schedules will become more precise as the preparation progresses. We ask you to submit your answers by email to hankinnat@istekki.fi no later than 15.4.2026 at 12.00. We hope that the answers are submitted in a separate enclosure in Finnish, so that their processing is as smooth as possible. If you wish, you can also include Finnish-language brochures or other material that supports the content of your answer. Based on the answers received, Istekki will, at its discretion, select 1-5 tenderers to present their solution in a market dialogue meeting. By default, the presentation will be implemented as an approximately one (1) hour Teams meeting between Istekki and the supplier in question at one of the following preliminary times: • Time 1: 24.04.2026, at 09-10 • Time 2: 24.04.2026, at 10-11 • Time 3: 29.04.2026, at 9-10 • Time 4: 29.04.2026, at 10-11 • Time 5: 29.04.2026, at 13-14 All answers received to the information request will be taken into account in the preparation of the invitation to tender, and they are an important part of understanding the entity as a whole. It is good to note that this information request does not oblige Istekki Oy to carry out the procurement in the manner presented in this document or its enclosures. A possible tendering procedure may also not be organised. No separate compensation will be paid for responding to the information request or participating in possible presentation sessions. We would like to mention once again that this is an information request, not a prior information notice, a procurement notice or an invitation to tender. The purpose of the information request is to familiarise ourselves with the market situation and to gather information related to the subject of the procurement to support the planning of the upcoming tendering procedure. Responding to the information request is voluntary and is not a prerequisite for participation in a possible tendering procedure, nor does it bind Istekki to publish a tendering procedure. At the same time, however, we greatly appreciate the information provided by suppliers, as it helps us build the future tendering procedure into as functional and clear a whole as possible.
sig_60106b1aa7da1b8b3fdd.title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION Procurement of a certificate automation system

The Legal AI Workspace software to be procured must serve as a specialised working environment to support legal professional work within the KfW Group using generative artificial intelligence. The software will be used in particular for legal research, analysis and the preparation of legal content, as well as for the (partially) automated creation, revision and structuring of documents and other legal work results. Users are personnel from the Legal department as well as other specialist departments and subsidiaries within the KfW Group. A Legal AI Workspace connects large language models with specialised processing layers that are optimised for working with legal content. It differs from general AI assistants in that it brings together legal professional processes in a unified working environment and employs mechanisms that are indispensable for professional legal practice. These include, in particular: the traceable anchoring of generated statements in verifiable sources, the structured processing of complex documents, and the rule-based review of contract content. The software must provide the following core functions. Legal research: The software must be able to answer complex legal questions based on relevant legal sources. Every generated statement must be traced back to concrete, verifiable sources (in particular statutes, case law, commentary literature) and made transparent for the users. KfW considers integrated access to curated legal databases to be a quality-enhancing feature. Furthermore, the software must be able to work with documents and internal knowledge databases provided by KfW. Document analysis and contract evaluation: The software must be able to process and evaluate the content of documents, including complexly structured contracts, tabular content and scanned documents, without essential structural information being lost. This includes the ability to systematically and completely compare contract content against specified review standards. Text creation and drafting support: The software must support the creation and revision of legal texts, in particular contract drafts, memoranda and opinions. Proposed changes must be able to be tracked directly in the document; the mere provision of generated text for manual adoption by the users does not meet the requirements. The software complements a general AI software already in use at KfW. The new software will be operated as an independent tool and will use a model infrastructure provided by the contractor. It is expected that the software will achieve significant increases in efficiency and quality in daily legal advice, document creation and review, and recurring standard legal tasks. Without prejudice to the provision of the software as a Service (SaaS) described in this document and the usage rights granted in connection therewith, the provision of the software must be carried out in such a way that it at least satisfies the intended purpose. KfW is entitled to at least the usage rights required to fulfil the intended purpose. The contractor is therefore liable for the following services: (a) provision of software with the functional scope, (b) execution of a project for the implementation of the software, (c) operation as SaaS, (d) provision of additional services as required, (e) termination support. Further details can be found in the 'Service Description' and in particular the mandatory criteria in accordance with the annex to the Service Description 'Mandatory and Optional Criteria'. We may carry out the tendering procedure differently, postpone its schedule or decide not to carry it out at all. sig_6147e73e78c8ff9c06ad.description: Consultants from COWI are currently conducting a feasibility study for Sporveien in Oslo. The purpose of this study is to define technology-independent and supplier-independent functional requirements for the future signalling system of the Oslo tram network, which consists of more than 130km of tracks with almost 100 stopping points. The tram infrastructure in Oslo has a history stretching back over 150 years, and has recently seen significant investment in modern rolling stock. This provides a unique opportunity to assess future solutions for a modern signalling system, and Sporveien has expressed a desire to invest in a future signalling system for the trams. As part of this project, we wish to gather information from suppliers of signalling and light rail systems. We therefore invite relevant suppliers to share information about your solutions, technologies, and experiences. We are particularly interested in systems that support safe, modern operation and that are adaptable to both the current and future needs of the Oslo tram network. Additionally, Sporveien AS and COWI AS are planning a dialogue conference with suppliers in Oslo on November 13th. This conference will provide an opportunity to discuss future collaborations and explore new opportunities for growth and development. We hope to see you at this conference. Once we have established contact with your organization and received your company’s contact information we will send you a letter of invitation with the complete aganda. Please see https://www.sporveien.no/for-leverandorer/trikkens-fremtidige-signalsystem/dialogue-conference/ for more information.

sig_615a7ad8699f790a495c.description: The North East Mayoral Strategic Authority (North East MSA) seeks to commission an external consultant to undertake an independent programme level evaluation of the Child Poverty Action Plan 2025-2030. The evaluation will assess the design, implementation, and impact of a complex, multi-strand programme delivered between August 2025 and March 2030. This will include directly funded activities, wider activities mobilised through the programme and selected aligned activities where appropriate and supported by the available evidence. The commissioned evaluation is intended as a cross-cutting programme-level evaluation of the Child Poverty Action Plan as a whole. It is recognised that individual projects, interventions and delivery activity within the wider programme will be subject to separate monitoring, evaluation and research activity commissioned by the North East MSA or undertaken by delivery partners. The evaluation will synthesise evidence generated through proportionate project level evaluations (including light touch monitoring and in depth project deep dives) to provide a coherent, programme wide assessment and will not be responsible for conducting primary project-level evaluations, except where explicitly agreed. This will support strategic assurance, learning and decision making, and inform future iterations of the Action Plan and wider North East MSA and regional policy and investment decisions. The programme-level evaluation will therefore consider both the evidence relating to individual interventions and the combined contribution of the wider programme towards the intended outcomes of the Child Poverty Action Plan. The programme‐level evaluation will also seek to determine the degree to which reducing child poverty has been embedded as a cross-cutting theme across North East MSA activity, and that of partners. This will include examining how the Child Poverty Reduction Unit and the regional Child Poverty Action Plan have influenced strategic priorities, programme and project design, funding and delivery decisions, and whether they have contributed to changes in policies, practices and activities beyond those directly funded through the programme. sig_616312374931479809b7.description: This is not a procurement notice or an invitation to tender, but an information request with which Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue is asking system suppliers to register their interest for a potential tendering procedure. This is an information request/market survey with which Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue is surveying potential service suppliers to act as a customer feedback system supplier. To obtain an overview of pricing models and cost structures (no individual tenders) 5. The focus of the dialogue will be on solutions that are already in production. The supplier must explicitly state in the brochure provided any presentations of solutions that are under development or only at the conceptual stage, as well as providing an estimate of the potential implementation schedule. Participating or refraining from participating in the market survey will not affect the tenderer's position in a potential tendering procedure. Advisory services for the format "Digi-Expert-kommunal" for the Hessian Ministry for Digitalisation and Innovation in two lots Lot LOT-0001: Foundations of digital transformation. Hessian municipalities are currently in very different phases of digital transformation. Municipalities have very different advisory needs in the course of digital transformation and in the planning and implementation of digitalisation projects. Projects with a high degree of innovation in particular bring with them a wide range of issues that must be answered promptly and individually for successful implementation. This can also be clearly observed in the digitalisation projects funded via the promotion of smart municipalities and regions under the "Starke Heimat Hessen" programme. The Smart Region office anchored in the Hessian Ministry for Digitalisation and Innovation (HMD) will therefore expand its advisory services for municipalities. The new advisory format "Digi-Expert-kommunal" is intended to offer Hessian municipalities individual, provider- and product-neutral ad hoc advice on various topics: from digital strategy, change management, project management to specialist topics such as data platforms, open source, artificial intelligence (AI), digital twin, digitalisation of services of general interest (smart city/smart region). The HMD will make available a pool of experts via the Smart Region office, from which municipalities can choose as needed. They can book them for various occasions/settings via the Smart Region office. This is intended to provide an impetus for the digital transformation of the municipalities and to dismantle hurdles in digitalisation. From October to December 2025, the format "Digi-Expert-kommunal" was piloted with selected topics and a limited quota. In the three-month pilot phase, a total of 52 advisory discussions were brokered. These were accounted for by 40 municipalities. 26 municipalities were each brokered one advisory discussion, 14 municipalities were brokered two or three advisory discussions. The advisory effort (= duration of discussion + preparation and follow-up) per municipality was limited to ten hours. Each of the advised municipalities took up an average of 5,7 hours of advisory effort from the following topics in the short pilot phase: AI in administration/AI in services of general interest, procurement advice (not the subject of this call for competition), digital strategy, digital services of general interest/smart region in general, change management/digital mindset, digital twin, project management/project control, open source/proprietary solutions. The format was very well received within a very short time and with minimal communication effort. The feedback from the municipalities was consistently positive and once again confirmed the need for tailor-made and short-term advice. The advisory need could not be nearly covered within the pilot phase. During the evaluation, the municipalities wished for a continuation and expansion of the offer. Lot 1 comprises general advisory topics relating to digital transformation and thus creates the basis for municipalities to deal with technical implementation later (Lot 2). In particular advice on: • Digital strategy, • Project management, • Change management, • Digital services of general interest, • Citizen participation. For this lot, based on the figures from the pilot phase and an assumed number of 270 interested municipalities, a demand of 810 hours per year is estimated. This estimated quantity serves calculation purposes only. There is no entitlement to call off this quantity. Further details can be found in the specification of services. sig_6174fa7d86935402e7f5.description: Support for the school data centre in the IT services and project environment. The specific tasks and project priorities are defined, specified and fleshed out in the course of the individual awards. The main areas of support focus on the new and further development of software solutions (including in the area of official school administration). This support relates both to the implementation of new functional requirements and to technical software updates. The requirements can lead to either existing applications having to be revised or new independent applications having to be developed. Should a new application be necessary, it must be embedded in the existing system landscape. In particular, the new development of software modules requires the drafting and analysis of software architecture designs. For the school administration area, the following must be observed: For legal and organisational reasons, this is a distributed software system. Both central services are operated in the IT-DLZ, but, depending on the software component, components are also operated on-premise by different operators on up to 1.600 servers. The central components include, among others, an identity management system and a central school server, as well as other applications. Software components, such as lesson management, are operated decentrally. The central components are used by all schools and must be designed for a corresponding load. It should be noted that Windows, Linux and MacOS must be supported for the operation of the decentralised components. Web components are expected to function for different browsers on different operating systems (e.g. Chrome, Firefox, Safari). As a rule, the implementation of new requirements means that both the central components and the decentralised components must be taken into account. The new and further development of the applications takes place on the basis of individual development packages. The basis is formed by the functional compilation of requirements for the system. Technical requirements are compiled by the IT-DLZ and bundled with the desired functional requirements. These technical requirements are subsumed under the term 'maintenance and care'. The IT-DLZ is responsible for the existing software modules to ensure that the functionality of the software is maintained. This means in particular that the software components are adapted to new versions of, for example, operating systems, application servers, databases or third-party libraries used. The functional requirements are drawn up, for example, by the StMUK and coordinated with the IT-DLZ. The IT-DLZ as the contracting authority then coordinates the requirements with the contractor. One part of the tasks will be the preparation of a rough technical implementation proposal with an assessment of the effort. On the basis of the analyses, the functional requirements are prioritised and bundled into development packages. Following the complete compilation of a further development package, the final estimate of effort for the implementation of this further development package takes place. Based on this estimate of effort, the StMUK, for example, commissions the contracting authority (IT-DLZ) with the implementation of the further development package. The implementation of released further development packages follows an agile software development process.

Nordværk I/S is inviting tenders for the procurement, implementation, and subsequent operation and maintenance of a new specialised system for the administration and support of waste collection, hereinafter referred to as the Solution. The procurement is carried out with the aim of replacing the current system support for Nordværk's waste management area and establishing a comprehensive, modern and future-proof Solution that can support the business processes associated with the administration, planning, case processing, execution, registration, follow-up and documentation of waste collection. The procurement includes the delivery and implementation of the Solution as well as the services necessary to establish and commission the Solution. This includes, among other things, clarification and configuration, migration and establishment of relevant data, establishment and adaptation of integrations, testing, training, documentation, commissioning, as well as subsequent operation, support, maintenance and further development in accordance with the Contract and the Contract's appendices. The Solution must support Nordværk's entire value chain in the waste management area from a citizen's or customer's scheme, enquiry or order to the planning and execution of the specific waste management task, as well as subsequent registration, case processing, follow-up, controlling, documentation and the basis for billing. The procurement is part of Nordværk's work to ensure efficient, cohesive and data-driven administration and operation of waste collection. The Solution must support standardised and verifiable workflows, high data quality, a reduced need for manual processes and better opportunities for management, follow-up and ongoing development of the waste management area. At the same time, the Solution must be able to integrate appropriately into Nordværk's other system landscape and support organisational, operational and technological changes over the term of the Contract. The overall purpose of the Solution is in particular: i) to support cohesive and efficient workflows within customer administration, case processing, operational planning, task execution, registration, controlling and follow-up, ii) to support operational waste collection for both Nordværk's own and external waste collectors, including planning, routes, navigation, registration of completed tasks, handling of deviations and operational follow-up, and iii) to establish a flexible and future-proof system foundation with high data quality and good opportunities for integration, configuration, automation, reporting and ongoing further development. The business processes and functionality applicable to the Solution are described in more detail in Appendix 3 of the tender documents – Delivery Description. The Solution is expected to support several different internal and external user groups. This includes, among others, approx. 186-200 internal waste management employees, 55-65 administrative employees, 10-20 administrators/superusers, 40-50 administrative users at external waste collectors and 100-110 waste management employees at external waste collectors. The user groups will have different roles and access needs in the Solution. The Solution must be established on a technical platform that supports the requirements for availability, security, integration, scalability, operation and further development set out in the Contract and the Contract's appendices. The more detailed technical requirements for the Solution and its establishment appear in the relevant appendices of the tender documents. The Solution must have an open, transparent and well-documented architecture and must be able to be integrated into Nordværk's overall system landscape. The Supplier must deliver and maintain the documentation necessary for, inter alia, operation, administration, integrations, configuration, troubleshooting and further development of the Solution, in accordance with the requirements of the Contract and the Contract's appendices. The Solution supports business-critical processes in connection with the daily administration and execution of waste collection. Requirements are therefore set for, among other things, the Solution's availability, stability, security, traceability and data integrity, so that data and registrations can be used reliably in operational management, customer service, case processing, controlling, documentation and as a basis for billing. The Solution must be integrated with a number of Nordværk's other systems and technical solutions. This includes, among other things, relevant interfaces to the billing system, GIS and data basis, self-service solutions, registration equipment, weighing systems and other third-party solutions where data exchange is necessary to support cohesive workflows. The specific requirements for integrations and interfaces appear in the relevant appendices of the tender documents. The tender also contains a number of options for additional functionality and deliveries that Nordværk may choose to use in accordance with the Contract. The specific options and the terms thereof appear in the Contract and the Contract's appendices, including Appendix 3 – Delivery Description. Commissioning of the Solution must take place after the completion of the agreed activities regarding, among other things, clarification, configuration, data migration, integrations, testing, training and approval. The detailed procedure and schedule for implementation and commissioning are determined in accordance with the Contract and the relevant appendices. The Contract thus contains an implementation period of up to 12 months as well as, after commissioning, an operating period of 6 years with the possibility of extension by 2 times 12 months. sig_62522eb6d83997d63de7.description: THIS IS NOT A PROCUREMENT NOTICE OR INVITATION TO TENDER BUT A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR MARKET RESEARCH AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE. This request for information is used to survey the market and obtain information concerning the procurement. The contracting authority does not initiate a tendering procedure by publishing the request for information; instead, a potential procurement notice and invitation to tender will be published later. The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Answering the request for information is not a precondition for participating in a potentially organised subsequent tendering procedure. Suppliers are not paid compensation for answering the request for information or participating in the market dialogue. HUS-yhtymä is preparing the procurement of an Information Security Monitoring and Management Service (CSOC) to maintain the cybersecurity of ICT systems and services owned and managed by HUS-yhtymä and procured from third parties. The procurement may potentially be implemented as a procurement ring with one or more wellbeing services counties of Southern Finland. The answers given to this request for information will be used in planning this procurement. The service to be procured will be delivered by the selected supplier with a 24/7/365 service period under the requirements and service level agreements defined later in the invitation to tender. The offered service must be able to detect, analyse, respond to, report on, and, if necessary, escalate cyber security-related threats, observations and disruptions within the response times given to the customer, and report the aforementioned events and the information security situation in accordance with reporting requirements. The objective of this request for information is to inform about the upcoming procurement and to survey suppliers that have the capability and interest to offer HUS-yhtymä an information security monitoring and management service. The service must include, among other things, CSOC services, vulnerability management, threat hunting, situational awareness service and digital forensics service. The supplier must implement the service using a hybrid model utilising HUS-yhtymä's devices and systems. These systems include, inter alia, SIEM, XDR, NDR, IPS, DLP, SOAR, as well as other modern information security solutions, such as automation utilising artificial intelligence. The supplier must also be able to offer assistance in developing automation. HUS-yhtymä's CSOC experts must retain the necessary rights to all systems. In addition, the purpose is to ascertain suppliers' views on the subject of the procurement and the implementation of the planned tendering. We also want to hear suppliers' views on a contemporary and modern information security monitoring and management solution for a supply-critical organisation of HUS-yhtymä's size. We request suppliers interested in the procurement to submit a service description of their available services in accordance with the request for information in PDF format. Please note that all material is intended solely for conducting this market dialogue. The contracting authority will handle your answers confidentially. Based on the answers to the request for information, suppliers may be invited for interviews in a manner to be announced later. Suppliers that have answered the request for information may receive preliminary invitation to tender documents for comment. We request that answers to the request for information and notifications of interest be submitted no later than 17.4.2026 at 12:00 by email to the address kilpailutus.ict@hus.fi. The subject of the message must mention "HUS 192-2026 - Tietoturvallisuuden valvonta- ja hallintapalvelu (CSOC)".
sig_62522eb6d83997d63de7.title: Information request: Information security monitoring and management service (CSOC)

sig_626e0fe9980779c88162.description: Digitalisation of invoice processing in relation to billing processes in accordance with § 302 SGB V and § 105 SGB XI. The AOK Baden-Württemberg (hereinafter: AOK BW or contracting authority) is a body governed by public law with joint self-administration by insured persons and employer representatives. It is divided into 14 district directorates and the head office in Stuttgart and insures over 4,6 million people in the state of Baden-Württemberg. To further increase efficiency in the processes, invoice processing is to be digitalised. Specifically, this concerns the billing processes in accordance with § 302 SGB V and § 105 SGB XI. The currently practised workflows differ according to the type of documents transmitted. In around 80-85 % of cases, a data record with a collective invoice is transmitted. In this case, invoice verification by the staff of the AOK Baden-Württemberg is difficult, as the invoice receipts cannot be directly assigned to a file. Around 10 % of cases are purely paper-based. The remaining cases are transmitted with a structured data set and an image. The postal recipients are filled in automatically. The task of the future service provider will be to scan the paper documents and generate a single invoice together with the associated documents. The requirements of the BSI TR-03138 RESISCAN requirements catalogue must be strictly adhered to. Participation in the initiated competition requires that the requirements of the BSI TR-03138 RESISCAN requirements catalogue are met and that the future contractor either proves certification in accordance with the BSI TR-03138 RESISCAN requirements catalogue with the tender or undertakes to submit the application in relation to the services covered by the contract within two months of the award of the contract. If the certificate is not submitted within twelve months of the award of the contract, the contracting authority is entitled to immediate extraordinary termination. Details are set out in the service description.

sig_62902b9bc476a5f53fa6.description: This PIN provides early information about the expected starting date and purchase volume for a pre-commercial procurement (PCP) carried out by the THERESA PCP project and about the open market consultation (OMC) that is organised in preparation of this pre-commercial procurement (PCP). The THERESA Buyers Group of healthcare providers have identified a shared need for innovative and sustainable solutions to treat hospital wastewater (HWW) at the source, before it reaches the municipal network, to reduce environmental and health risks linked to pharmaceutical residues, antimicrobial-resistant microorganisms and genes, and other hazardous contaminants. The THERESA PCP aims to stimulate the development of environmentally sustainable, cost-effective, and scalable on-site HWW treatment systems capable of efficiently removing cytostatic drugs, X-ray contrast agents, antibiotics, antimicrobial-resistant bacteria (ARB) and genes (ARG), while minimising energy consumption, chemical use, and carbon footprint. The contract notice is expected to be published in May-2026 and phase 1 to be started in January 2027, following the PCP timeline. The procurement will take the form of a Pre-Commercial Procurement (PCP) awarding R&D service contracts to several providers in parallel, through a phased and competitive process comprising three stages: Solution design, prototyping, and original development and validation/testing of the first products in real hospital environments. After each phase, intermediate evaluations will down-select the best-performing and most innovative solutions. The contractors with the best-value-for-money solutions will be offered a specific contract for the next phase. The PCP is a joint cross-border initiative coordinated by Fundación Miguel Servet (Spain) as Lead Procurer, on behalf of a Buyers Group of hospitals and public health institutions from Spain, Estonia, Poland, Belgium and the Netherlands, supported by technical and innovation partners. Testing is expected to take place in Spain, Estonia, Poland and the Netherlands to ensure adaptability. Price is not the only award criterion, and all criteria are stated only in the procurement documents. The selected contractors will retain ownership of the Intellectual Property Rights (IPRs) generated during the PCP and will be able to commercially exploit the developed solutions beyond the scope of the procurement. The R&D services will be carried out primarily within the European Union and/or countries associated with the Horizon Europe Programme. At least 50% of the total value of R&D activities will take place within the EU or associated countries. In addition, contractors must ensure that none of the contracted services are performed in countries nor by entities that are subject to EU restrictive measures under Article 29 of the Treaty on the European Union (TEU) and Article 215 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the EU (TFEU)23 (sanctions). They must ensure that none of the goods procured or used for the procurement were developed, produced or supplied in countries or by entities that are subject to such restrictive measures. Duration of the contract in months: 30 months (January 27 to June 29). The duration covers all three PCP phases: Solution design, prototyping, and original development and validation/testing of the first products. The PCP is expected to start after the publication of the Contract Notice and to end upon completion of the validation phase. This contract is not subject to renewal.
sig_62902b9bc476a5f53fa6.title: Pre-Commercial Procurement (PCP) of innovative and sustainable solutions to treat Hospital and Healthcare System Wastewater – THERESA PCP

sig_62c985fe42f03983f924.description: This concerns the procurement of an intelligent (web-based) SaaS application for the automated execution of self-scans, acting as a gateway for all ground-breaking work. Users (engineers, work preparers and contractors) must be able to import route alignments or enter them manually. Subsequently, on the basis of map layers, the system generates a real-time status (Green/Orange/Red) for soil, unexploded ordnance, archaeology, and flora and fauna respectively. Based on the information currently known to us, we estimate the volume of this tender at a range of 28.000 to 45.000 self-scans per year. One self-scan here comprises the automated assessment on all four research themes (soil quality, archaeology, flora & fauna and unexploded ordnance). Calculated over the duration of the framework agreement, this amounts to: • Estimated quantity over the initial term (4 years): approximately 112.000 to 180.000 self-scans; • Estimated quantity over the total maximum term (8 years, including both extension options): approximately 224.000 to 320.000 self-scans.

sig_6512f77e4da294323564.description: This notice is not an official launch of our procurement(s), it is to alert the market to future opportunities and allow us to begin conversations that will shape plans for multiple future requirements. The Cabinet Office (Government Skills Group) is transforming the way learning and development (L&D) is designed, procured, and delivered across the Civil Service. Following the announcement by the Chief Secretary to the Prime Minister, the government is establishing the new National School of Government and Public Services (hereon The National School). The National School is tasked with delivering high-quality, targeted training to approximately 558,000 civil servants, developing executive leadership in the wider public sector, and to partner with public sector training bodies. The strategic goal of the National School is to shift away from the historically outsourced prime-supplier managed-service model. In its place, the Cabinet Office is building an insourced, hybrid capability. Under this new Future Operating Model (FOM), the Cabinet Office will directly manage core operations, standard curricula, and stakeholder engagement. However, expert external provision will remain a critical element of the programme. The National School transformation programme relies on three core, interdependent pillars to transition Civil Service training away from fully outsourced prime-supplier models toward an in-house, hybrid operating model by April 2028. Together, these pillars work to build direct relationships with suppliers, provide a modern digital learning infrastructure, and establish robust in-house operational workflows. Pillar 1: Future Supplier Partnerships (FSP) The FSP project serves as the commercial enabler of the new operating model, building the in-house capability required to buy learning services and manage supply chains directly. We aim to establish direct, value-driven contractual relationships with UK-based SMEs, universities, business schools, and niche providers. The project team have identified an indicative Three-Stage Roadmap to enable this delivery: Stage 1 (Immediate - April 2027): Procuring urgent digital and specialist training needs that cannot be fulfilled through existing frameworks. Stage 2 (April 2027-March 2028): Phased procurement for core, National School-sponsored curriculum, coaching, and talent programmes. Stage 3 (March 2028 onwards): On-going phased procurements falling out of Stages 1 and 2, depending on the length of contracts identified. The scope of the requirements will cover several key procurement categories, including, but not limited to, specialised coaching pools (including for neuro-diverse leaders), blended training delivery, learning design (retaining Crown Intellectual Property), access to subject matter experts including within academia, independent research and evaluation, helpdesk/admin surge, and off-the-shelf qualifications. Pillar 2: Future Technologies (FT) The Future Technologies project focuses on designing and implementing the digital architecture required to run a personalised training operation for approximately 558,000 civil servants. The core objective here is the setting up and integration of platforms to manage the access, booking, payments, and evaluation of learning materials. This involves transitioning away from heavy manual processes to maximise technological efficiencies. At this stage the project team has identified the central deliverable as a unified online portal allowing learners to access the full National School offering. Key technologies in scope for procurement include, but are not limited to, a new Learning Management System (LMS)/ Learning Experience Platform (LXP), Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems to centralise stakeholder engagement, and design/delivery tools. Pillar 3: Future Learning Operations (FLO) The Learning Operations project is responsible for building the actual systems, processes, and internal capabilities required to run the day-to-day training operations in-house. Their core objective is establishing an integrated operational function by April 2028 that supports over 558,000 civil servants in completing their learning journeys. It is highly dependent on the digital and commercial pillars to develop the underlying platforms that support operations. Market Involvement As part of the initial phases of the programme, the project teams are keen to connect with the market and gain insight into current trends, operations and barriers. sig_65304a5679f41cb71107.description: The Maritime and Coastguard Agency (MCA) intends to undertake preliminary market engagement (PME) to consult with suppliers in relation to the MCA’s next generation procurement of its Command and Control Programme (C2P). The C2P aims to improve resilience, interoperability, situational awareness, and support for maritime incident management, pollution response and front-line search and rescue operations. sig_654e236c4fe1c73fa01a.description: The Contracting Authority is tendering a contract regarding a common Operating Platform for the Contracting Authority's IT system portfolio. After Transition In, where the Support Systems are transitioned to the Operating Platform, the Supplier shall be responsible for operation, including Data Centre operation/Hybrid Cloud Custom Services/Hybrid Cloud Standard Services and Infrastructure operation, as well as Support and maintenance of the Operating Platform. Furthermore, after Transition In, the Supplier must ensure Subsequent Transitions to and Transformations of the Operating Platform. The purpose of the common Operating Platform is, among other things, to obtain secure and stable operation with high availability as well as a modern technological platform with a high degree of scalability that supports the needs of the Customer and the municipalities. It is the Contracting Authority's business need that all Services are delivered with high delivery reliability and robustness, and that the Supplier demonstrates proactivity in the collaboration. In addition to the focus on secure and stable operation, the Supplier must ensure a successful Transition In of the Support Systems with the least possible disruption to the Contracting Authority's business, as well as Subsequent Transitions and ongoing Transformation, including a gradual transition to Hybrid Cloud Standard Services and, to the extent that it supports the needs of the Contracting Authority and the municipalities, Managed Public Cloud Services. In connection with Transition In, a high level of information security must be established, which must be continuously maintained and improved throughout the Contract. The contract has the following 4 main services: I. Transition In, where the Contracting Authority initially wishes for the establishment of and secure and stable transfer to an Operating Platform for the Support Systems, based on Hybrid Cloud Services, with the implementation of, for example, project management, transition organisation, building of operational capacity, transfer of Environments and data, and takeover of knowledge from the Outgoing Supplier. Subsequently, the Contracting Authority wishes to carry out successive Subsequent Transitions for a number of the Contracting Authority's other IT systems from the current operating models to the Operating Platform, based on Hybrid Cloud Services. II. Ongoing Services for the Operating Platform, including; a. Support; b. Hybrid Cloud Services, including Hybrid Cloud Standard Services and Hybrid Cloud Custom Services; c. Tools for supporting Application Suppliers; d. Governance, Operational Processes, security services, Documentation, and operational reporting. III. Service catalogue with the use of standardised methods, technologies, and services, through which the Contracting Authority wishes to be able to provision services on a cloud platform that; a) Offers a wide range of services; b) Is accessible via the public internet; c) Has a publicly available price structure with settlement of services according to consumption on subscription terms. IV. Methods and tools for supporting collaboration with the Contracting Authority and the Contracting Authority's application suppliers, where the Contracting Authority wishes for the delivery of the future operating platform to be supported by proactive collaboration across the Contracting Authority's IT system portfolio.

sig_669ae692b39c16d39190.description: What is HUP? Born in Bradford’s Healthy Urban Places (HUP) is carrying out research to help understand what makes the places we live, work and socialise healthier places. HUP research is taking place in Bradford and Liverpool. In each city four areas have been chosen (8 in total) as centres for carrying out community-led research. In Bradford these 4 areas are: 1. Keighley Central (BD20, BD21, BD22) 2. Bolton Woods (BD2, BD18) 3. Barkerend and Bradford Moor (BD3) 4. Parkside (BD5) This tender only relates to the Parkside area of Bradford The focus of the research The research is about what makes a healthy urban place. We want to design research questions with the community in order to answer the following overarching themes: • What urban and environmental factors have an impact on wellbeing and which of these does the community prioritise? • How do healthy places develop over time? • How do different communities experience and benefit from different features of urban places over time? • How can we measure and track changes in urban places that are important for health and wellbeing? How will it work? By bringing together community members who live in and are impacted by changes in urban areas, and those responsible for decisions about them, we want to produce relevant and impactful research that can reduce unfair and avoidable differences in health (health inequalities) and improve health and wellbeing long-term. In order to do this HUP wants to work with community organisations with expertise in engagement of often marginalised groups and an underlying ethos of working in partnership. Together we will create a ‘Community Collaborative’ – a community-based research partnership – which will involve the HUP team, community organisations, and other stakeholders (such as residents, schools, places of faith, clubs, policy makers, council members and more). The Community Collaborative will work together to produce evidence on what makes a healthy urban place and explore how we can achieve healthier cities. We will share the findings and learning from the research within communities in creative ways, and develop community-led reports for policy makers and government to influence future positive changes in urban areas. What will a Community Collaborative involve? The HUP team are looking for community organisations in each site to join us in partnership over the lifetime of the HUP programme until spring 2027. As a partnership, we’ll all bring something to the table: • HUP will bring research skills, provide training for those in the local community (staff or service users), support local communities to get involved in and/or lead research, and help create opportunities for community members to meet with policy makers and implementors. • Community organisations will bring local knowledge and lived experiences, skills in community & participatory engagement, introductions to community members, and access to physical assets, such as rooms and buildings. Community organisations can apply to be a HUP partner to Bradford Teaching Hospitals Foundation Trust. Funding will be provided for core costs (e.g. staff time, use of building and for carrying out specific research projects. Organisations within one area can apply alone or in partnership, and at more than one site if they have required links to the community. What the research process will look like At each site, the organisations involved in the Community Collaborative will jointly organise some 'inception' workshops with the HUP team. Together, we'll decide how we want our partnership to run (e.g. our ways of working, etc). We’ll start to explore factors that have impacted on wellbeing in the local urban area over time. Jointly we’ll prioritise what we want to explore first and will decide how we want to learn about it. We might, for example, decide together to develop a series of fun, creative and engaging mini-projects in which community members can be trained as community researchers to find out about healthy urban places. The findings and learnings from these projects will be shared with our communities, the wider public and those involved in policy making locally, regionally and nationally. The allocation of funds for this will be jointly decided. The Collaboratives will run for 2 years, with most of the work being conducted in 2025 and 2026, and finalising the process in 2027. Funding will reflect this, with the bulk of funding being provided in 2025 and 2026. However, during the process, we’d hope to be able to identify further opportunities and funding to work together on research in the future. What is expected of a collaborative partner? Community organisations will have a range of responsibilities that are noted in more detail in the procurement specification. Briefly, they will be co-partners in the Community Collaborative, and over the length of the funded period will: • Contribute to the set up and development of the Community Collaborative • Attend and assist in organising, facilitating and hosting meetings & workshops in the local area • Connect the HUP team to community members and service users • Co-design community-based research with the HUP team and wider stakeholders • Co-design creative ways of engaging community members in finding out about healthy urban places • Co-design engaging ways of sharing the learning and findings of research • Distribute payments to community participants in the research – for example, any community researchers who get involved in finding out about healthy urban places • Attend city-wide Collaborative meetings in Bradford and with partners in Liverpool Lot 1: .

sig_66b9ac335d1e3cef31cd.description: With this notice, Istekki announces the organisation of market dialogues for a service voucher and purchased service system. The purpose of the dialogue is to ensure that those preparing the procurement have access to as comprehensive and up-to-date a picture of the market and available solutions as possible. The subject of the procurement is the service voucher and purchased service system entity and its interfaces with other systems, the delivery project (including e.g. migrations, conversions), maintenance and support of off-the-shelf software, support services, separately ordered expert services, as well as customer service. Further development may be carried out on the procured system during the contract period. The service voucher and purchased service system is used for granting service vouchers and payment commitments and for purchasing services from private service providers or other public actors. Through the system, it is necessary to centralise the creation and use of service vouchers and purchased service orders (payment commitment) and the settlement of accounts for rendered services to private service providers or other public actors. The service voucher and purchased service system must take into account needs from the perspectives of the service organiser, the service producer and the customer using the service. Through the system, the service organiser must have the option to manage service provider agreements, plan service provision, grant service vouchers and payment commitments, allocate payments, handle correction requests and monitor various report views. The service provider must have the option to apply to become a service provider through the system. In addition, the service provider must be able to record the service received by the customer in the system and thereby handle settlement based on approved transaction entries. The customer must receive the granted service voucher / payment commitment for use via the system. The service voucher customer must have the option to compare or view service providers, monitor the execution of the service from the system and provide feedback on the service. The contracting authority will organise the market dialogues either as remote meetings or in writing, or utilising both methods. The market dialogues will be held in Finnish. Istekki will notify the companies participating in the dialogue of more detailed schedules and instructions later. Please note that the information, descriptions and estimates of the publication date of the tendering procedure presented in this notice are merely preliminary and indicative. Final schedules will become more precise as preparation progresses. If you are interested in participating in the market dialogue, please notify us of your interest no later than 11.09.2026 at 14.00 to hankinnat@istekki.fi. If you wish, you can also attach Finnish-language brochures or other material regarding your own service. It is worth noting that this notice does not oblige Istekki Oy to carry out the procurement in the manner presented in this document or its appendices. A potential tendering procedure may also be omitted. No separate remuneration is paid for responding to the dialogue or participating in any presentation events. We would like to mention again that this is not a contract notice or call for tenders. The purpose is to familiarise oneself with the market situation and gather information related to the subject of the procurement to support the planning of the upcoming tendering procedure. Responding to the request for information is voluntary and is not a prerequisite for participating in a potential tendering procedure or bind Istekki to publish a tendering procedure. At the same time, however, we greatly appreciate suppliers' participation, as it helps us build the upcoming tendering procedure into as functional and clear an entity as possible.
sig_66b9ac335d1e3cef31cd.title: Service voucher and purchased service system, market dialogue

sig_67da10303e40f5199415.description: ARTE G.E.I.E. in Strasbourg employs 590 people on permanent contracts and 300 people on temporary contracts: fixed-term contracts, freelance workers and intermittent workers. The HRIS ensuring administrative management and payroll is SAP ECC6, with a migration to SAP S/4HANA planned. It is currently supplemented by a UKG solution to cover the functionalities of an electronic safe, electronic signature and electronic personnel file. The purpose of the contract is the supply, implementation, hosting, maintenance and support of an integrated solution for the digitisation of human resources management processes covering the following functions. The interfaces, documentation and support are provided at a minimum in French and German. • Employee digital safe. Personal space held by the employee, intended for the storage and availability of HR documents provided to them for a period of at least fifty years, from the date of their deposit or signature. It allows ARTE to satisfy the obligation to make the payslip available in electronic form as provided for in Article D. 3243-8 of the Labour Code. This space remains accessible to the employee after the end of their employment contract and beyond the term of the contract. • Electronic personnel file. Documentary archive with probative value, accessible to authorised personnel, constituting the employee's individual file for the duration of their employment contract as well as during the recruitment phase that precedes it and the legal retention period that follows it. The solution ensures classification by document type, search, guarantee of integrity and traceability of access and actions, the lifecycle, and retention periods. • Electronic signature. Signature service whose level of proof is adjustable according to the process concerned, for internal as well as external signatures, in individual or bulk mode, including automated signatures for documents issued in series. It guarantees the retention of associated evidence and their retrieval. • Employee portal. Service allowing the employee to consult their documents and initiate human resources management requests by means of standard forms and configurable validation workflows, with progress tracking. • Distribution of individual human resources management documents. Secure, individualised and traceable distribution of documents produced by ARTE to each employee, including employment contracts and amendments, letters, management decisions, certificates and end-of-contract documents, regardless of the upstream production process. This function covers in particular the distribution of payslips, carried out in five campaigns per month. The solution supports the employee's objection to the digitised delivery of their payslip. The contract includes the recovery, in the electronic personnel file, of documents and signature evidence created since 2019. It includes a commitment to service continuity, reversibility at the end of the contract, as well as the regulation of any use of artificial intelligence excluding the collection, reuse or training based on ARTE's data. The hosting, processing, administration and backup of data are carried out exclusively on the territory of the European Union or the European Economic Area, including for each subcontractor. The contract involves the processing of personal data. Selected candidates must demonstrate, during the procedure, their ability to present appropriate guarantees regarding data protection, which must be maintained throughout the execution of the contract. The procedures and documents to be produced will be specified in the consultation.
sig_67da10303e40f5199415.title: Integrated solution for the digitisation of HR processes

sig_68225bdb357591370d7b.description: Technical renewal and digital expansion of the parking system for Smart Parking Lot LOT-0000: Bad Homburg v. d. Höhe municipal area, Smart Parking - parking system for Smart Parking. The subject is the technical renewal and digital expansion of the existing parking systems at 5 locations of Kur- und Kongreß-GmbH Bad Homburg v. d. Höhe, as well as the complete renewal of the parking system in the Karstadt multi-storey car park. The goal is a modern, service-oriented and functionally uniform parking infrastructure. The existing facilities are to be supplemented in such a way that modern digital parking processes based on number plate recognition, QR code functions, cashless web payment, digital discounting and self-service functions for short-term and long-term parkers can be used consistently and across all locations. The intention is not an isolated replacement of individual devices, but the functional expansion of an already existing overall system. Scope of services: delivery, installation, integration, commissioning and acceptance of the components at all locations; provision and setup of the central software and control computer components. Technical requirements and integration: - All components must be centrally manageable via the existing control computer/cell computer topology. - A continuous parking process (entry - identification via ticket, number plate or QR code - payment at machines/web service/discount point - exit - audit-proof accounting) must be guaranteed across the entire system. - Interfaces, firmware/backend versions and data models must be provided by the manufacturer in a coordinated manner. Installation, commissioning and acceptance: - Installation and commissioning during ongoing operation while minimising downtime; coordination with the project manager. - Acceptance criteria and partial acceptances: partial acceptance per location after successful functional/integration test; formal final acceptance after complete system integration. Other services: - Complete technical documentation in German. - Instruction/training of personnel: instruction of operating personnel per location as well as administrator training for the control computer system. A maintenance contract must be concluded for the maintenance of the systems, which covers the following areas: software, control/cell computer, availability of a technical service centre reachable 24/7, on-call service for on-site maintenance & repair.
sig_68225bdb357591370d7b.title: Bad Homburg v. d. Höhe municipal area, Smart Parking - parking system for Smart Parking

sig_6824e87e6a593ea0459a.description: Kansaneläkelaitos (Kela) invites tenderers to a market dialogue concerning the payment commitment concept developed by Kela to ensure national impact. This is therefore an invitation to a market dialogue (not a prior information notice, contract notice or call for tenders). The purpose of the market dialogue is to survey suppliers on the market and hear the views of potential tenderers. Participation in the market dialogue does not bind any party. Participation in the market dialogue is not a prerequisite for participation in any subsequent tendering procedure. Participation does not in any way affect a tenderer's position in a potential tendering procedure. No remuneration is paid for participation in the market dialogue. Interested parties are requested to register for the market dialogue by email at myntti-tuki@kela.fi no later than 23.9.2026 at 16.00. The market dialogue will be carried out in two stages. First as a written procedure, in which the materials and related questions will be sent by email to those who have registered for the market dialogue 24.9.2026. Answers to the market dialogue must be provided by 5.10.2026. In the second stage, based on the responses, we will invite organisations to Teams discussions. Information provided in the market dialogue will be treated confidentially. The names of companies involved in the market dialogue or other information concerning companies will not be published in connection with the responses. Information provided in the market dialogue does not bind any party. The market dialogue will be conducted in the Finnish language.

sig_6858bb78cc291b25b1ab.description: The project is aimed at potential international travellers and describes the possibility of active travel in Germany (focusing on hiking, cycling, and canoeing where applicable). The experience does not present individual destinations or tourism products, but rather conveys the characteristic qualities of Germany as a diverse active travel destination. The focus is on typical travel experiences and the combination of nature, physical activity, culture, culinary enjoyment, and relaxation that characterise active holidays in Germany. The project serves not only to impart knowledge, but the guest should be addressed, "taken by the hand", complete simple tasks, and be emotionally engaged. This has at least the same priority as the information. Objective: Extension of the length of stay. The project is to be developed for the output channels virtual reality (including inflight entertainment on aircraft with VR headsets), mobile, and web in order to generate the widest possible reach. This pilot project concerns a new type of destination marketing in which combinations of user engagement, user guidance, and content presentation from gaming, VR, artificial (AI-supported) content generation, and real content are combined. The bidder must combine these different skills and create an appealing, interactive product that fascinates customers with Germany as a travel destination. In addition to virtual environments, scenarios, and avatars (or digital entities/objects), the project should also incorporate existing media from the GNTB (photos, films, drone footage, 360-degree panoramas, etc.) and present them in an impressive, interactive form. Depending on the concept, further media may need to be digitally created, purchased, or shot. In addition, the use of (a few) Gaussian splats is planned for the first time, provided it makes sense in terms of content and technology. To our knowledge, the planned mix of (partially photorealistic) digitally created content and real images, panoramas, videos, and avatars is unprecedented in tourism marketing. Further information can be found in the service description in the tender document. Lot LOT-0000: Active travel in Germany. sig_68e9e3c7d8bb768a7d86.description: The employee survey in The Norwegian Defence Estates Agency is carried out annually, usually at the end of January/February. The Norwegian Defence Estates Agency has had a very high response percentage in recent years, between 82 % and 87%. In 2025, the survey was sent out to just over 2,000 respondents. The Norwegian Defence Estates Agency currently uses Rambøll as its supplier and they are responsible for the entire process - from dispatching and administration to analysing the results. The results will be presented in an insight report that will be presented to the management team. With new competence in the HR department, including HR analyst competence, Forsvarsbygg is now considering taking a greater degree of ownership of the survey. The Norwegian Defence Estates Agency is looking at an option to administer the survey itself and get access to raw data, so that own analyses can be carried out, etc. Practical if the market dialogue: There is a form (excel sheet) that can be answered and the deadline is set at 12:00 1 December 2025.Input and form is submitted by using the communication model in Mercell.Based on received responses, the Norwegian Defence Estates Agency will make an assessment and possibly call in some suppliers for 1:1 conversations - if the Norwegian Defence Estates Agency deems it appropriate. sig_68fb7a7789389a47f1f5.description: The Council is considering the future procurement of an independent assessment of the efficiency, effectiveness and long term sustainability of Housing Services and the HRA. While a robust 30 year HRA Business Plan is already in place, the Council wishes to obtain independent assurance on current arrangements and identify opportunities for improvement, innovation and value for money. This Prior Information Notice (PIN) is issued for the purpose of early market engagement only and is intended to inform the scope, approach and procurement strategy for any potential future tender exercise. Publication of this PIN does not constitute a commitment by East Renfrewshire Council to commence a procurement process. Lot 1: . East Renfrewshire Council manages a ring fenced Housing Revenue Account (HRA) which supports the delivery of social housing and associated landlord services. The Council is considering the future procurement of an independent assessment of the efficiency, effectiveness and long term sustainability of Housing Services and the HRA. While a robust 30 year HRA Business Plan is already in place, the Council wishes to obtain independent assurance on current arrangements and identify opportunities for improvement, innovation and value for money. This Prior Information Notice (PIN) is issued for the purpose of early market engagement only and is intended to inform the scope, approach and procurement strategy for any potential future tender exercise. Publication of this PIN does not constitute a commitment by East Renfrewshire Council to commence a procurement process. Indicative Scope of the Requirement: Should the Council proceed to a formal procurement exercise, it is anticipated that the scope of services may include, but would not be limited to, the following areas: - A strategic review of Housing Services, including performance, capacity and value for money. - Independent assessment of the robustness and long term sustainability of the HRA Business Plan. - Benchmarking and comparative analysis against Local Authorities of comparable size and stock profile and Registered Social Landlords with similar stock archetypes. - A detailed review of repairs and voids service delivery, including performance, cost control, productivity and customer experience. - Review of the factoring service, including financial performance, customer experience and options to move towards full cost recovery. - Review of stores and materials management arrangements within the context of a DLO led repairs model. - Review of sheltered housing provision, including revenue and capital costs and the relationship with the HRA. Across all areas, the Council anticipates a strong focus on evidence based analysis, benchmarking, customer feedback and elected member priorities, together with practical and deliverable recommendations. Information Sought from the Market - Economic operators are invited to provide non binding information to assist the Council in shaping any future procurement exercise. Responses may include information on: - Relevant organisational experience in delivering comparable Housing Services, HRA or landlord service reviews. - Experience working with Local Authorities and/or Registered Social Landlords of comparable scale and complexity. - Indicative approaches to delivering a commission of this nature, including benchmarking and stakeholder engagement. - Capacity to deliver the requirement and typical delivery models. - Innovative approaches or added value relevant to Housing Services. - Indicative commercial models and key cost drivers for similar commissions. This is not a tender or pre qualification exercise and no evaluation or scoring will take place at this stage. Submission of Expressions of Interest - This Prior Information Notice is issued for the purpose of market engagement only. Economic operators who wish to express an interest in this opportunity, or to provide information to assist the Council in shaping any future procurement exercise, are invited to submit a brief, non binding written response. Responses should be clearly marked “PIN Response – Housing Revenue Account Efficiency Review” and submitted to mary.harvey-welsh@eastrenfrewshire.gov.uk Responses should be limited to 4 x A4 and provided by 12 noon, 30th April 2026.. The Council reserves the right not to proceed to a formal procurement process and shall not be bound by any information received in response to this PIN.

sig_692b79910178a859851a.description: Procurement of a software solution The Institute of the Fire Brigade of North Rhine-Westphalia (IdF NRW) is the state fire service school of the State of North Rhine-Westphalia. For the efficient planning, organisation, and documentation of the approximately 500 to 850 seminars per year with around 17.000 to 18.000 participants, the IdF NRW intends to procure new educational management software that supports in particular course administration, participant organisation, as well as evaluation and reporting functions. As part of the IT project, an overall works contract will be concluded, specifically using the "EVB-IT Systemvertrag" form with various adjustments, which are highlighted accordingly. Within this overall service, the purchase of standard software (No. 4.3 EVB-IT Systemvertrag), the creation of the overall system with the establishment of operational readiness, incl. customising and integration as well as interfaces (Nos. 4.5, 4.7 and 4.10 EVB-IT Systemvertrag) as well as - after acceptance of the overall system - system service, including restoration and maintenance of operational readiness as well as the delivery of new program versions (No. 5.1 EVB-IT Systemvertrag) and further development (No. 6.1 EVB-IT Systemvertrag), including training and documentation, shall take place; these services are largely remunerated on a lump-sum basis (see price sheet). Furthermore, optionally retrievable services are offered by the tenderer, such as migration and other services before and after acceptance, which are generally remunerated on a time-and-materials basis (No. 7 EVB-IT Systemvertrag) (see also price sheet). Mandatory A criteria (must criteria), the complete fulfilment of which in the operational overall system is owed, follow from the criteria catalogue, as well as additionally scored, non-mandatory B criteria, which are to be provided insofar as they were indicated as offered by the tenderer in the procurement procedure. Regarding the contract term: For the system service services, the provision of services begins contractually on the day after successful acceptance; a minimum contract duration of 84 months is envisaged. Ordinary termination of the system service is possible for the first time at the end of the minimum contract duration with a notice period of 24 months; without timely termination, the contractual relationship continues for an indefinite duration. Regardless of this, the entire EVB-IT Systemvertrag (as a works contract) can be terminated pursuant to section 648 BGB; the consequences of termination result from No. 18.7 EVB-IT Systemvertrag. Note on differing contract lengths: While the software purchase is designed for the long term, the system service runs for at least 84 months and can be terminated ordinarily thereafter. This textual summary serves for the rough classification of the contract structure (overall works contract, software purchase, services, price logic, criteria binding, term and termination) and does not replace an independent, complete, final review and legal or economic evaluation of the contract documents.

The Contracting Entity is not committed to carrying out the procurement covered by the request for information. Decisions on initiating a possible procurement process will be made after the market consultation. SUBJECT OF THE PROCUREMENT The subject of the procurement is a digital pathology production system and related services. The procurement comprises slide scanners, server software, viewer software and image analysis software used on pathologists' workstations, and centralised physical storage systems, as well as related services. The objective of the procurement is set as a modern and modular digital pathology solution that supports Fimlab's operations and whose sub-components can be flexibly replaced as technology evolves and Fimlab's needs change. The request for information will be used to determine, among other things, into which procurement packages the solution can be appropriately divided and how these packages should be competitively tendered in order to acquire an overall solution that meets Fimlab's needs. sig_6a0ea0101631906fdc67.description: The subject of the contract is the lot-by-lot supply, installation, integration and commissioning of software solutions for radiation therapy at St. Elisabethen-Klinikum Ravensburg, a site of Oberschwabenklinik gGmbH. Lot 1 comprises an SGRT system (Surface Guided Radiation Therapy) including all necessary software components for patient positioning and monitoring as well as integration into the existing IT and LINAC infrastructure. Lot 2 comprises the treatment planning software (Treatment Planning System, TPS) for irradiation planning for photons and electrons, including installation, data migration from the legacy system, training of operating personnel and maintenance/support. Both lots will be awarded under a negotiated procedure with a call for competition. Tenderers may apply for one or both lots. Contract execution will take place during ongoing clinical operations. The subject of this lot is the supply, installation, integration and commissioning of a system for surface-guided radiation therapy (Surface Guided Radiation Therapy, SGRT) including all necessary software and hardware components for patient positioning and monitoring. The service includes complete connection to the hospital's existing linear accelerator and IT infrastructure, training of operating personnel as well as maintenance and support over the envisaged period.; A treatment planning system (TPS) for the radiation therapy of Oberschwabenklinik gGmbH is being procured. The system is intended to enable the planning of photon-guided irradiations with the existing linear accelerators while supporting all relevant clinical workflows (3D-CRT, IMRT, VMAT). Complete integration into the existing IT and PACS environment is expected, including interfaces to the R&V system, DICOM-RT and archiving system. The service includes supply, installation, commissioning, validation, training of specialist personnel and maintenance.

sig_6a1c3dbeafff2d320ec8.description: Dundee City Council intends to procure a construction consultant resource and project management system to improve the planning, allocation and monitoring of architectural, engineering and specialist consultancy resources across its capital and housing programmes. The information gathered will assist the Council in developing its procurement strategy, refining its requirements and determining the most appropriate route to market. As part of this exercise, the Council intends to invite selected suppliers to participate in product demonstrations, currently anticipated to take place during early October 2026 (please note, these dates are indicative only). These demonstrations will provide an opportunity for the Council to gain a greater understanding of available solutions, functionality, implementation approaches and delivery models. Suppliers wishing to be considered for participation in the demonstration stage are requested to complete and return the attached questionnaire.
