Suppliers who do not submit a completed questionnaire will not be considered for participation in the demonstration stage. The Council reserves the right to limit the number of demonstrations undertaken and participation in this market engagement exercise will not confer any advantage or disadvantage in any subsequent procurement process. Additional information: This PIN is issued for market engagement purposes only and will not be used to evaluate, select or exclude suppliers in any future procurement process. Information received will help Dundee City Council understand the market, develop its requirements and determine the most appropriate procurement approach. Participation is voluntary and does not commit the Council to proceed.

sig_6a25f60d592dc1362e77.description: This is an invitation/request for information for a market dialogue (not a prior information notice, contract notice or call for tenders). No tenders are submitted in response to the request for information; instead, by registering for the market dialogue, entities indicate their willingness to participate in the preparation of the procurement. SUBJECT: Kela is planning a competitive tendering process for a centralised printing and inserting line concerning A4 sheet printers and related software, peripherals, maintenance services, supplies and printing paper. The market dialogue will survey market solutions as well as technical and functional implementation alternatives, particularly regarding printing and software solutions. The procurement will replace the printing line reaching the end of its lifecycle with new A4 sheet printers suitable for continuous and heavy-duty use. The scope also includes print management software, a delivery and commissioning project, training as well as other services and supplies that ensure the uninterrupted continuation of letter production in Kela's production environment. Currently, the printing line processes over 20 million A4 sheets and several million letters annually. In addition, the procurement includes an inserting machine modification project and its maintenance services. In the inserting machine modification project, the inserting machine will be modified to receive finished A4 sheet stacks, or it can be replaced entirely with another device. Subdomains of the market dialogue: 1) A4 printers, software and maintenance services – Printing devices and related software – Maintenance and support services – Necessary peripherals and supplies 2) Inserting machine modification project and maintenance service – Inserting machine modification work – Device maintenance and support 3) Paper suppliers – Printing paper supply package Suppliers may register for one or more subdomains according to their offering. General material common to the dialogue will be provided to all participants. In addition, separate subdomain-specific questions and materials will be targeted to each subdomain. This ensures that operators can provide relevant and expert feedback regarding their specific subdomain. During the dialogue, subdomains may also be merged if necessary for the procurement. MARKET DIALOGUE: The aim of the market dialogue is to form as comprehensive a picture as possible of the solutions offered by the market and to ensure that the requirements of the tendering process are appropriate, feasible and treat the market equally. During the dialogue, participants are asked to, among other things: - present the offering available on the market - answer questions concerning the procurement - comment on preliminary minimum requirements, for example regarding conflicts of interest - present potential development proposals to improve the solution and the tendering process. The dialogue will be carried out in a versatile manner: partly through in-person meetings in Jyväskylä, partly by email and, if necessary, via remote connection using Kela's Microsoft Teams. The material related to the market dialogue is in Finnish. The market dialogue will be conducted principally in the Finnish language; if necessary, the dialogue can also be conducted partially in English. The contracting authority has no obligation to translate documents or other material related to the market dialogue unless the contracting authority specifically decides otherwise. A party participating in the market dialogue is responsible for obtaining any translations it needs and for their accuracy at its own expense. Preliminary schedule of the dialogue: - Familiarisation with the offering, defining the subject, familiarising with the subject: Until June 2026 - Finalisation of the call for tenders: July-September 2026 The schedule and the alignment of phases will be reviewed in more detail with tenderers during the dialogue. Participation: Interested participants are requested to declare their willingness to participate in the market survey by email to it.tarjouskilpailut@kela.fi by 25.3.2026. Example of message content: Message subject: Company xx participation in xxx market dialogue Message: It is advisable for the message to indicate the supplier's name, business ID and contact person through whom the dialogue will be conducted, as well as the subdomain being participated in. Confidential material may be handled during the dialogue and, consequently, all persons handling confidential material, location data and other confidential information must sign a non-disclosure agreement. Persons participating in the handling can be added during the dialogue if necessary. Kela will send the non-disclosure agreements electronically to the designated handlers for signature before handling begins. Other: The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement or to implement the procurement in the manner described in the request for information. The contracting authority is not obliged to take into account the responses received to the request for information when drawing up the call for tenders and the contract template. No compensation is paid to those who responded to the request for information for responding to it. Answering the request for information does not bind the supplier to participate in the tender contest, nor is it a prerequisite for participating in the actual tender contest later. Answering or failing to answer the request for information does not affect the tenderer's position in the actual tender contest. Information obtained through the request for information will be treated confidentially.

The area of each lot is specified in the description of the lots. The services involve the development of a forest management plan, a product of the management activity with technical-organisational content, ecologically grounded, through which, for a period of time, the works necessary to be executed in a production unit are established, in order to bring and, subsequently, to maintain the structural characteristics of the stands and the forest as a whole at the values corresponding to the optimal structural model defined in accordance with the ecological, social and economic objectives pursued through sustainable management. According to the provisions of Art. 63 para. (11) of Law no. 331/2024 on the Forestry Code, as subsequently amended and supplemented, it is necessary that the development of forest management plans be carried out through public procurement procedures. The management of the state-owned forest fund constitutes a priority obligation of the forest fund administrators. The method of managing the state-owned forest fund is regulated by forest management plans. Forest management plans and their amendments are approved by order of the head of the Authority. In the case of state-owned land, the management plans provide data and information necessary for their registration/updating in the centralised inventory of state public domain assets and for registration in the integrated cadastre and land registry system. Requests for clarification formulated by tenderers during the advertising period of the participation notice can be made with a deadline of at least 15 days before the deadline for submission of tenders (the 16 day). The contracting authority will respond to all requests for clarification formulated in compliance with the above deadline, only once, in a consolidated manner, 10 days before the deadline for submission of tenders (the 11 day). sig_6b40aaf9d6703f049b5f.description: The aim of the Energy Export Initiative (EIE) of the Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy (BMWE) is to support German companies (UN) offering climate-friendly energy solutions with market entry abroad and to position German products and services internationally. An integral part of the funding offer is the Energy Business Trip Programme. The aim of (digital) energy business trips is to prepare market entry for German SMEs by building up in-depth market knowledge and targeted brokering of contacts with potential business partners in the respective target markets, and to further expand the existing foreign activities of German SMEs. The digital energy business trip (dGR) funding module consists of a trip profile, a target market analysis (ZMA), an online briefing and an online expert conference. The core element of the measure is individual discussions by German UN for targeted business initiation with potential business partners in the target country. Target country : Fiji, Cook Islands, Samoa, Tonga Field of application : Power generation Possible date : Q4 2027 Objective : The digitally conducted energy business trip is intended to make market development easier for German SMEs from the areas of hybrid mini-grids and grid modernisation. The focus of the virtually conducted business trip is on targeted contact brokerage and individual B2B discussions with potential customers, partners and relevant stakeholders from the target region. In particular, the target market of Fiji is to be brought into focus. The markets of the Cook Islands, Samoa and Tonga can be incorporated into the dGR as additional sales markets. The measure is aimed at German SMEs with solutions in the areas of battery storage and energy management, SCADA/control technology and digitalisation, inverters/power electronics and protection technology, system design/hybrid optimisation, and O&M concepts/training. Note : A longer regional ZMA (special version) covering Fiji, the Cook Islands, Samoa and Tonga is to be drawn up. The specifications described in the guideline must be applied during project implementation.
sig_6b40aaf9d6703f049b5f.title: Digital business trip within the framework of the Energy Export Initiative of the BMWE 2027, 2. Tranche

sig_6b692a82e072d7a22034.description: The National Violent Death Reporting System (NVDRS) is CDC's state-based surveillance system for violent deaths and suicides. NVDRS combines information from death certificates, coroner or medical examiner reports, including toxicology reports, and law enforcement reports to provide comprehensive, incident-level data on the circumstances surrounding violent deaths. Through this Notice of Funding Opportunity, CDC will support eligible state, territorial, and local government entities, or their bona fide agents, in operating and modernizing NVDRS. Recipients will conduct statewide or territory-wide surveillance by collecting, linking, managing, analyzing, and submitting high-quality data on violent deaths and suicides. A central focus of this NOFO is timely and complete data reporting through two coordinated reporting processes: quarterly provisional data pulls and annual data closeout. Beginning in Year 1, recipients will prepare data for CDC's quarterly provisional data pulls to support earlier access to preliminary, actionable information. Recipients will progressively update case records as additional source documents and information become available. Annual data closeout is the primary process for producing the complete, finalized, and validated NVDRS dataset for each data year. Recipients must ensure that all eligible cases are fully abstracted, updated, validated, and completed using all required and available data sources by the annual closeout deadline. The finalized annual dataset supports national reporting, analysis, dissemination, and public health action. This NOFO also emphasizes modernization of data systems and workflows to increase efficiency, reduce reporting burden, improve data quality and timeliness, and enhance data usability. All recipients will complete a modernization readiness assessment within six months of award and implement at least one modernization pilot during the period of performance. Pilot activities may include automated data import and extraction, electronic data exchange and interoperability, workflow automation, data-quality tools, and enhanced data analysis and visualization. With CDC approval, recipients may also participate in optional activities that link NVDRS data with other relevant data systems to improve surveillance and expand public health insights. The intended outcome is a sustainable, modernized national surveillance system that produces timely provisional data and complete, reliable, high-quality annual data to inform violence and suicide prevention and support public health action.
sig_6b692a82e072d7a22034.title: Modernizing Violent Death and Suicide Surveillance Using the National Violent Death Reporting System (NVDRS)

sig_6b717637e2d7dc2a6ac8.description: MARKET DIALOGUE The subject of the market dialogue is the planned procurement of translation, language editing, subtitling and transcription services for the needs of Väylävirasto. Väylävirasto produces a wide range of official communications, expert content and stakeholder-targeted materials in multiple languages as part of its statutory duties. Translation and language editing services are a key part of the accessibility, quality, comprehensibility and consistency of official communications. BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES The subject of the procurement is a comprehensive service package for translation, language editing, subtitling and transcription services, through which subscribers can procure translation services for various language pairs, language editing for texts written in the target language, and subtitling and transcription services for video and audio materials. Service needs are focused in particular on the Swedish and English languages. The materials to be handled are principally factual texts, presentations, documents (e.g. call for tenders, contracts), speeches, brochures, articles and web content. Subtitling and transcription services relate, inter alia, to videos, online events and audio recordings, taking accessibility requirements into account. The aim of the procurement is to ensure a high-quality, cost-effective and reliable service package that supports subscribers' communications, information accessibility and the fulfilment of official obligations. The objective is a procurement model that enables smooth ordering, consistent end results and an administratively light operating method even in situations where the volume of assignments is large and the value of individual assignments is small. By means of the market dialogue, the contracting entity seeks to obtain information on service models existing in the market, pricing structures, quality assurance practices, and the utilisation of artificial intelligence and other automation as part of the production of translation and language editing services. The dialogue will also examine various contractual and supplier models, including the suitability of single-supplier and multi-supplier models. The procurement includes a cooperation model in which the subscriber and the supplier systematically develop the service throughout the contract period. The aim of the cooperation is the continuous improvement of the service, taking into account the subscriber's guidelines and terminology, and developing the service to meet changing needs and operating environments. The subject matter, scope and technical solutions of the procurement may be refined and/or changed as the procurement preparation and market dialogue progress. PRELIMINARY TIMETABLE The subscriber's target timetable for carrying out the market dialogue and procurement is: - Market dialogue (technical dialogue), February-March 2026 - Publication of the call for tenders and calculation period, March-April 2026 - Comparison of tenders and procurement decision, April-May 2026 - Contract entry into force and commencement of cooperation, May 2026 onwards ----- ADDITIONAL NOTICE DETAILS This notice is a prior information notice. This notice does not request tenders. The prior information notice is accompanied by an invitation to a market dialogue, whereby all suppliers interested in the procurement have the opportunity to engage in a technical dialogue concerning the procurement with Väylävirasto. The purpose of the technical dialogue is to discuss the subject of the procurement and its definition at a general level. The technical dialogue does not bind Väylävirasto to carry out the procurement. Nor does the technical dialogue bind the supplier to participate in a possible tendering procedure. The technical dialogue will be organised through commenting on draft versions of the call for tenders material and answering the subscriber's questions relating to the subject of the procurement. Instructions for registration: The supplier must notify its interest in participating in the market dialogue by 25.2.2026 at 12.00 by sending a message to tommi.aarnio@vayla.fi with the subject heading: "Käännöspalvelut - markkinavuoropuhelu" [Translation services - market dialogue]. The supplier is requested to provide the following information in the message: - the email address of the supplier's contact person The subscriber reserves the right to also invite suppliers to bilateral negotiations or to continue the technical dialogue in another manner to be announced separately, which will be notified later if necessary. The descriptions presented in this prior information notice and the estimated publication date of the procurement notice, as well as the draft dialogue materials to be provided later, are preliminary and indicative prior information regarding the procurement. Participating companies will not be paid compensation for responding or participating.
sig_6b717637e2d7dc2a6ac8.title: Invitation to market dialogue: Procurement of translation services

The information provided will be treated confidentially. Secure forms 6. Secure workspace 7. Secure instant messaging 8. Secure file transfer 9. Critical communication 10. Undefined procurement category - to be specified later 11. Istekki Oy reserves the option to establish categories 10-12 during the period of validity of the dynamic purchasing system. According to the provisions of Art. 63 para. (11) of Law no. 331/2024 regarding the Forestry Code, with subsequent amendments and additions, it is necessary for the preparation of forest management plans to be carried out through public procurement procedures. The management of the state-owned public forest fund constitutes a priority obligation of the forest fund administrators. The method of managing the state-owned public forest fund is regulated by forest management plans. Forest management plans and their amendments are approved by order of the head of the Authority. In the case of state-owned public lands, the management plans provide data and information necessary for their registration/updating in the centralised inventory of assets in the state's public domain and for registration in the integrated cadastre and land register system. Requests for clarification formulated by tenderers during the advertising period of the contract notice may be made with a deadline of at most 15 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. The contracting authority will respond to all requests for clarification formulated in compliance with the above deadline, once, in a consolidated manner, 10 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. The services include preparatory works, field data collection, data processing and drafting of the forest management plan, preparation and development of the GIS database and management maps, preparation of the necessary environmental documentation, obtaining the regulatory act issued by the competent authority for environmental protection, supporting the documentation within the Technical Commission for Forestry Approval (CTAS) and obtaining the order for the approval of the forest management plan.; Forest management plan preparation services for the state-owned public forest fund managed by the Suceava Forestry Directorate – Falcău Forestry Office, field phase 2026, for the area of 150,00 ha. sig_6c8a0c2a7cec95c30dbf.description: Die BREPARK GmbH intends to introduce a central service portal for the digitalisation and optimisation of customer management and the associated business processes. Lot LOT-0000: Service Portal/Digital Customer Management, V0470/2026. The BREPARK GmbH intends to introduce a central service portal for the digitalisation and optimisation of customer management and the associated business processes. The future system is intended to serve as a central platform for managing customers, contracts, access media, billing and communication with customers. The planned scope of services comprises in particular the provision, setup, customisation and operation of an integrated service portal with the following components: End Customer Portal (EKP): A digital portal through which customers can independently use services provided by BREPARK GmbH. This includes in particular registration, management of customer data, conclusion and management of contracts, viewing of parking operations and invoices, as well as communication with BREPARK GmbH. Employee Portal (MA Portal): A central work surface for employees of BREPARK GmbH for managing and processing customer transactions. This comprises in particular the maintenance of customer data, processing of contract enquiries, management of contracts and access media, execution of checking and approval processes, and support for internal administrative processes. Business Customer Portal (GKP): The solution must provide a business customer portal through which authorised business customers can independently manage their contract-related data and access permissions. BREPARK manages various parking facilities on behalf of third parties and manages long-term parking permissions for business customers, amongst other things. Around 7.000 access media for business customers are currently managed. The aim is to provide business customers with a digital option for independently managing their permissions and access media, thereby simplifying administrative processes. The service portal is to be integrated into the existing system landscape of BREPARK GmbH. This includes in particular connection to SAP Business ByDesign as the leading ERP system and the required interfaces to existing parking management and access systems. The contractor must provide an operational overall system which fulfils the requirements of this specification of services and enables the further development of the digital customer processes of BREPARK GmbH. In addition to the provision of the software, the scope of services also includes the required configuration, customising, integration into the existing system landscape, data migration, execution of tests, commissioning, and the required training, maintenance and support services for ongoing operations. Implementation takes place as an overall system. The contractor bears responsibility for the total technical and functional integration of all required components and interfaces.

sig_6d2b297d9c88d9c9864f.description: The National Institute of Mental Health (NIMH) intends to issue a single-source cooperative agreement award to the University of California, Santa Cruz. The award will renew the Data Resource and Administrative Coordination Center (DRACC), a component of the Scalable and Systematic Neurobiology of Psychiatric and Neurodevelopmental Disorder Risk Genes (SSPsyGene) Consortium. The long-term goal of SSPsyGene is to systematically study how risk genes for neurodevelopmental and psychiatric disorders (NPDs) affect molecular, cellular, circuit, systems/organismal biology. The renewed DRACC will refine its focus on developing a sustainable knowledge base, with shared terms, definitions, and data standards that are interoperable with other knowledge platforms and will enable the use of artificial intelligence to accelerate research on brain function and NPDs. This resource will be made available for broad use by the biomedical community. Projects that propose to build on the DRACC's current role in refining methods and standards to harmonize data from the SSPsyGene Assay and Data Generation Centers and facilitate submission to data archives are encouraged. This is a forecast for a single source NOFO that will invite application(s) from eligible organization(s) to apply. Please see Section III. Eligibility for additional information. In accordance with NIH standard peer-review processes, the application(s) will be peer-reviewed, and only meritorious application(s) will be considered for funding.
sig_6d2b297d9c88d9c9864f.title: Single Source: Scalable and Systematic Neurobiology of Psychiatric and Neurodevelopmental Disorder Risk Genes: Data Resource and Administrative Coordination Center (U24 Clinical Trial Not Allowed)

sig_6dabd753c32e71f5ef91.description: Description of the procurement: The Danish Agency for Digital Government (Digitaliseringsstyrelsen) operates on behalf of the Danish State a national qualified trust service for the management of qualified electronic signature creation devices under Regulation (EU) No 910/2014 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (eIDAS2). As part of modernising the signing service to meet the requirements of eIDAS2, the Agency is procuring a Qualified Signature Creation Devices (QSCD) to be installed and operated within the Agency's data centers (currently two). The Contract includes an Option to upgrade the throughput capacity of the QSCD and an Option to extend the deployment to a third data centre. The Contract covers the Initial Delivery of the certified QSCD in accordance with eIDAS2. The Initial Delivery includes all Licences, Documentation, and support necessary for the Agency to install and operate the QSCD as part of its qualified trust service. The QSCD must integrate with the Agency's existing infrastructure, including the Agency's certificate authority, authorisation server, and signing components. The Supplier's principal obligations comprise: (a) the Initial Delivery of certified QSCD Hardware sized and configured for operation across two data centres with redundant active/active configurations with a defined minimum production throughput per second, measured in RSA 4K operations equivalent; (b) Ongoing Services, including support and maintenance of the Hardware, security patching, and up to two replacements of Hardware during the contract term to maintain valid certifications; (c) Ordered Services, comprising Time-Based Services (services for installation, configuration, key ceremonies, and similar tasks) and Options; and (d) Cross-cutting Services, comprising Documentation and security, provided as an integral part of the Ongoing Services and Ordered Services throughout the term of the Contract.

sig_6e410eacad34c2b05f1c.description: This is not a prior information notice, contract notice or call for tenders, but a notice on the initiation of a market dialogue as part of procurement planning and an invitation to participate in the market dialogue. Vantaan kaupunki and other municipalities are jointly planning a tender contest for a low-carbon assessment tool for detailed local planning, so the procurement will likely be carried out as a joint procurement group of several contracting authorities. The contracting authorities are surveying suppliers' interest in participating in the market dialogue for the low-carbon assessment tool for detailed local planning. The subject matter of the procurement is a browser-based software service delivered via the data network for assessing the climate impacts of land use plans, with which the contracting authority can assess and compare the climate impacts of detailed local plan level land use plans based on the carbon footprint and carbon handprint calculated by the tool. The subject matter of the procurement includes implementation projects for the low-carbon tool, rights of use, support and maintenance services, supplementary expert services ordered separately, and additional procurement opportunities. The aim is to obtain a solution that is suitable for the Finnish land use and construction context and for the evaluation of detailed local plan level land use plans. The solution is also intended to be further developed to improve the assessment of the climate impacts of urban land use planning. Commercial use of the low-carbon assessment tool for detailed local planning will start according to municipality-specific schedules estimated during Q2/2026-Q1/2027. The solution to be procured must preliminarily include the following key functionalities and features: - The solution is map- and GIS-based. - The evaluation method of the solution must take into account the entire life cycle of the land use plans being evaluated, including the climate impacts of the project before use, during use and after use, as well as impacts outside the life cycle and potential climate benefits. - The solution must be able to utilise national and city-specific parameters and data. - The evaluation method must comprehensively take into account the climate impacts of detailed local plan level land use projects, also considering climate impacts other than those produced by buildings, such as the climate impacts of transport or energy consumption. - The solution takes into account the Finnish Green Building Council's definition of a carbon-neutral built area. Operators participating in the market dialogue are requested to register for the market dialogue and provide answers to the preliminary questions presented in the market consultation notice by Friday 13.3.2026 by 12 to the following address: jonna.hirvonen@vantaa.fi. Registrations must be headed as follows: "Registration for market dialogue: Procurement of a low-carbon assessment tool for detailed local planning". Registrations must contain the following information: - Name of the participating company - Name, telephone number and email address of the contact person - Name of the solution offered by the company - Answers to preliminary questions
sig_6e410eacad34c2b05f1c.title: Information request and invitation to market dialogue: Procurement of a low-carbon assessment tool for detailed local planning

sig_6eb9572aae3b7818c770.description: The National Institute on Aging (NIA) intends to publish a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) to solicit applications to develop, operate, and sustain a cloud-based data storage and computing platform that democratizes access to large-scale Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and AD-related dementias (ADRD) genetic and genomic data. The platform must be secure, scalable, and interoperable. The platform will support the NIA Genetics of Alzheimer's Disease Data Storage Site (NIAGADS), the primary NIA-supported repository for the archiving and distribution of human genetic data related to AD/ADRD. The purpose of the platform will be to: Enable efficient ingestion, curation, harmonization, and analysis of multi-ancestry, large population-scale datasets; Provide robust analysis, visualization, and artificial intelligence -ready resources within secure cloud workspaces; Ensure compliance with federal security and data-sharing policies; Promote interoperability with other NIH- and NIA-supported repositories; and Provide user support, training, and community engagement. The NOFO aims to foster collaboration, accelerate discovery, and maximize the scientific value and impact of AD/ADRD genetics research for the broader research community. By improving data accessibility, interoperability, reporting, reproducibility, and scalable computational systems that enable rigorous, reproducible, and transparent research, the NOFO seeks to align with the NIH’s plan for Gold Standard Science and the AD/ADRD Research Implementation Milestones . Additionally, the NOFO seeks to address the Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine's recommendation of ensuring broad, secure access to high-value datasets and enhancing data usability to maximize the return on research investments and support future discoveries in AD/ADRD. Moreover, the NOFO intends to directly advance NIA’s Strategic Directions , particularly Goal G to support the infrastructure and resources necessary for high-quality research, by strengthening data sharing, computational infrastructure, and research rigor across the AD/ADRD community. The NOFO intends to utilize the U24 activity code. Applications are not being solicited at this time. This notice is being provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations and responsive projects.
sig_6eb9572aae3b7818c770.title: The NIA Genetics of Alzheimer's Disease Data Storage Site (NIAGADS)

sig_6ed7cd14dea6dc521d15.description: The overarching goal of this notice of funding opportunity (NOFO) and its companion opportunities is to establish the Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) Program to support development of innovative, reliable, cost-effective, and sustainable multimodal AI-based clinical decision support (CDS) tools. PRIMED-AI CDS tools are based on the integration of clinical imaging with other types of multimodal health data to enhance care for patients with a wide range of health conditions. The PRIMED-AI Program seeks to catalyze the adoption of AI-based CDS tools into clinical workflows to enable novel personalized medicine strategies that address significant health challenges.The purpose of this NOFO is to create a Logistics Center for the PRIMED-AI Program to facilitate and coordinate PRIMED-AI activities to maximize impact for the PRIMED-AI community. Within the Logistics Center, three integrated Cores will serve the functions of Administration, Evaluation, and Outreach for the PRIMED-AI Consortium. It is expected that the Logistics Center will work closely with other PRIMED-AI consortium members to collect, curate and disseminate information regarding tools developed by the PRIMED-AI award recipients, and will facilitate widespread access and awareness across the relevant scientific, patient, and clinical communities.

sig_6f7590633fbe75aa4fc7.description: The Havelland district intends to award external expert support for the following services: 1. Support with and preparation of the next four rescue service fee calculations (planned cost accounting including operating cost accounting) 2. Analysis and processing of financial deficits from concluded stay-of-enforcement agreements from the years 2021-2024 relating to the so-called false-call issue, including adjustment based on the judgment of the Higher Administrative Court of Berlin-Brandenburg (OVG 6 A 13/25) 3. Advice on a legally secure and sustainable fee structure Lot LOT-0001: Advisory and support services for fee calculation in the rescue service as well as for deficit processing (stay-of-enforcement agreements 2021-2024) in the Havelland district. The consultant shall analyse for the client the effects of the judgment of the OVG Berlin-Brandenburg, 28.01.2026, ref. OVG 6 A 13/25 on the respective rescue service fee budget and prepare a written opinion thereon. This also includes an analysis of the written grounds for the judgment. The consultant shall implement all work arising therefrom as part of an amicable solution with the statutory health insurance funds (GKV) in the interest of the client. The required advisory services include, in particular, data collection, the evaluation of all data as well as the adjustments of the relevant rescue service fee calculations and support for the hearing procedure with the cost bearers. Part 1) - Procurement of technologies for server rooms The subject matter of this part of the public contract is the comprehensive supply, expert implementation and subsequent commissioning of a complete technological solution for the expansion and supplementation of the existing data centre infrastructure, both physically and technologically. Specifically, this involves the installation and integration of physical infrastructure elements, a modern air conditioning system, an uninterruptible power supply, a CCTV system for monitoring and security purposes, fire safety systems and the establishment of an optical connection with a dedicated backup server room, which will ensure high availability and operational continuity. Part 2) – Procurement of network technologies The subject matter of this part of the public contract is the supply, implementation and commissioning of a comprehensive solution to increase LAN access security and modernise the backbone and access network infrastructure. This includes the replacement of active components in both the access and backbone layers, the deployment of a network access control (NAC) system with support for IEEE 802.1X and the supply of central switch management in the form of on-premises or cloud management. New switches (2 backbone switches and 7 access switches) will be deployed within the access layer to ensure secure connection of end devices using authentication and authorisation based on IEEE 802.1X. This part forms the basic communication and authentication layer of the infrastructure and is designed in direct succession to the security, monitoring and logging systems specified in the technical specification - part 3, with which it must be fully interoperable at the level of access control, security events, logging and automated response. Part 3) – Supply and implementation of security and monitoring software The subject matter of this part of the public contract is the supply, implementation and commissioning of high-performance servers to increase system availability, strengthen operational computing power by supplying two high-performance rack servers and an enterprise All Flash disk array. The aim is to expand the computing and storage capacity of the hospital infrastructure with an emphasis on high performance, redundancy, scalability, advanced management and security features, including support for virtualisation, high availability and data services. Furthermore, the supply, implementation and commissioning of a comprehensive solution for the security of the organisation's perimeter, security policy management and cyber threat detection. This includes the deployment of a high-availability firewall cluster, a central security event management system and training of responsible personnel. Finally, the supply and installation of a system for central log collection and the supply and installation of hardware and software equipment that form a comprehensive solution for long-term and detailed monitoring and evaluation of network traffic using data flows (NetFlow, IPFIX, sFlow, etc.). The solution specified in this part is designed as a superior security, analytical and management layer that builds on the network and authentication infrastructure defined in the technical specification - part 2 and uses it as a primary source of network data, identities, events and telemetry. sig_6fcb6f1f758a9219b3e3.description: This invitation to tender ('ITT') relates to Lake District National Park Authority's (the 'Authority') procurement for a Countryside Land Management and Estate Maintenance Framework Agreement, for our Ranger Services Team and others. Successful Tenderers will be appointed onto a multi-supplier Framework Agreement divided into Lots. The Framework Agreement will be available for use by the Authority and by other bodies in the Authority's network by prior agreement. The Authority is seeking a mix of contractors to bid for a place on the Framework Agreement, including companies, consultants, sole traders, and Small and Medium Sized Enterprises. This procurement is divided into Lots (and sub-lots in the case of Lot 4). Suppliers may bid for one or more Lots/sub-lots provided that you can supply at least one of the services mentioned in the Lot Specification at Table A. Please note that you do not need to be able to provide all of the services listed in the Lot specification, provided you can supply at least one of the services mentioned in that Lot you may submit a tender. All Prices should be submitted as a maximum for provision of your goods/services and will be a commitment for the duration of the Framework Agreement, subject to the allowed increase in price annually. This Framework Agreement will allow for Direct Award and Further Competition of Call-off Contracts. Tenderers should read the instructions contained in this ITT carefully before submitting a response. Failure to comply with the requirements set out in this ITT may result in the rejection of the Tender. Tenderers are advised to acquaint themselves fully with the extent and nature of the goods and/or services in the Statement of Requirement and with the Terms and Conditions. Participation in this procurement automatically signals that the Tenderer accepts the Terms and Conditions contained in this ITT. If a Tenderer is awarded a place on any Lot of the Framework, a draft Framework Agreement will be provided after all awards have taken place (est. February - March 2027). Any award is not legally binding and subject-to-contract until the final Framework Agreement between the Authority and the Tenderer is signed. The Lake District National Park Authority looks after the Lake District National Park, encouraging people to enjoy and understand its beauty and supporting those who live and work here. Further information about the LDNPA, including our statutory functions, is available on our website. We are working towards making the Lake District an inspirational example of sustainable development in action. We want its prosperous economy, world class visitor experiences and vibrant communities to come together in sustaining the spectacular landscape, wildlife and cultural heritage here. Details of how we are doing this are outlined in our Vision: Our purpose and vision - Lake District National Park Our Ranger Services Team at LDNPA has a focus on maintaining and improving the Rights of Way and other access in the Lake District National Park, while encouraging and educating users in responsible outdoor recreation on accessible land and navigable lakes. They support visitor management and nature recovery initiatives, and the enhancement and maintenance of our rural properties, in line with our strategic priorities. They work closely with communities to help them meet their needs in ways that contribute to our Vision. The Ranger Team's workload includes project work, such as the Coast-to-Coast and Fix the Fells. The Historic Environment Team commissions specialist consultancy support to inform the conservation, management and enhancement of the National Park's historic environment. This may include heritage impact assessments, conservation area appraisals, historic building recording, conditions surveys, archaeological investigations, landscape and townscape character assessments, design advice, and other specialist heritage and built environment studies to support planning, conservation and place-shaping objectives. Our needs are specific and will vary. We are looking for Suppliers who understand the work we do and not only can provide exceptional services, but who can contribute to our wider Vision for the Lake District. Please note that the Lot Descriptions in section 2 are included to provide some background information on the work of the Authority. The following are examples of types of services which may be required by our Ranger Service. This is not exhaustive but is intended to demonstrate the breadth of the services which will be required: Providing services on a recurring and annual basis, such as our bridge maintenance responsibilities and sourcing of materials for daily use; Providing advice and practical work on specific public sector funded projects, such as the Coast-to-Coast project. Providing specific advice to our internal team of individuals and organisations with whom we operate, for internal projects involving our own land and property, and also to our partner organisations such as Fix the Fells. Lot 1: Bridges Supply, Repair and Maintenance. The Authority supplies, installs and maintains bridges on public rights of way throughout the National Park including bridleways and footpaths for use by horse riders, cyclists, mobility scooters and pedestrians. We are seeking suppliers who can assist with the following: • Supply bridge materials as component parts and/or complete structures in a variety of materials including recycled plastic, metal, timber, concrete, stone. These bridges will need to be to our specification or bespoke design in some cases. • Using the materials listed above, build and install those bridges in a wide variety of locations, including some remote and difficult to get to. This can include machine work, working with helicopter delivery companies, working with hand tools, demolition and construction of abutments. • To repair existing bridge structures in situ, including replacement of handrails, decking boards, beams, abutments e.g. stonework. • To provide designs to structural engineers' standards to meet the supplied specifications for a wide range of bridge types, including footbridges, bridleway bridges and those suitable for road traffic in some instances. This might include reviewing and revising our existing designs and specifications, to producing bespoke designs for individual unique locations and bridge types. • For structural engineers to inspect the current condition of bridges and abutments to check they meet the standards for the required user groups and to sign off newly installed bridges to verify that they meet the required specification and standards. • To provide, erect and use scaffolding, including in remote locations, to complex designs, to enable the team to carry out maintenance and construction work on the bridges and other rights of way work in a safe and secure manner, following current industry and health and safety standards. Services required: • Supply of prefabricated bridge kits • Provision of materials e.g. timber/ plastic/ metal • Bespoke design of bridges • Installation of bridges • Repair of bridges • Engineer surveys on bridges • Scaffolding on bridges to support safe installation or repair Lot 2: Supply of Materials. The Authority requires qualified suppliers for the supply, delivery and installation of materials and services to support our countryside construction and maintenance projects. It aims to ensure high-quality, timely, and cost-effective delivery of materials and services while complying with health, safety, and environmental standards. It also aims to facilitate the provision of locally sourced materials to reduce transport mileage, to support the economic wellbeing of the National Park, and to showcase local products. Suppliers under this framework must demonstrate relevant experience, proven quality standards and the capacity to meet delivery schedules. Services and materials will be provided according to defined specifications, with monitoring of performance through key indicators such as timeliness, quality, and responsiveness. Suppliers must ensure that all materials supplied meet relevant British Standards or industry-recognised equivalents. Goods required: • Pipes/drains • Grass seed • Treated and some graded timber for fencing and the construction of timber boardwalks • Gates • Waymark roundels for Public Footpaths, Bridleways, Byways and permitted routes • Local stone (from the Lake District) for construction of unbound surface paths, stone for drainage works and dry-stone walling and bridge revetments • Plastic boardwalks from 1m to 3m width with non-slip finish • Metalwork (gate springs, gate hinges, catches screws, nuts, etc.) • Screened (inert) topsoil • Fingerposts and Waymarkers • Benches • Fencing wire • Metal fencing (i.e. Clipex) • Native tree species grown from seeds sourced in seed zone 301, or if unavailable, 302. Lot 3: Minor Practical works under £50,000. The Authority requires a range of qualified suppliers for delivery of practical works and services supporting our countryside access and nature conservation projects across the National Park. This often requires working in remote locations with challenging access. All work standards and specifications will be set out in relevant documents. All work will need to be carried out to all relevant legislative requirements by appropriately trained and qualified staff. Examples of the types of work the Authority requires are: construction, repair and maintenance of structures, furniture and surfaces forming part of Public Rights of Way work (PROW) such as footpaths, bridleways and byways. Surfacing -The supply, construction, repair and maintenance of; • Un-bound, bound, crushed stone or tarmac paths. • Machine construction of profile inversion (subsoil) paths • Supply and delivery and laying of stone flags • Construction and repair of pitched stone paths using local stone. Drainage works - The supply, construction, repair and maintenance of; • Plastic drainage of all sizes. • Stone culverts • Drainage ditches. Fencing, Walling and hedgerows- The supply, construction, repair and maintenance of; • All forms of fencing including Post and rail, post and wire, metal estate style • Drystone and bound (mortared) walling in local vernacular style. • Hedgerows planted and maintained in the local vernacular style. Vegetation management • Mechanical and chemical control of vegetation on public rights of way, open land and formal sites including control of Invasive Non-Native Species (INNS). Countryside Furniture - The supply, construction, repair, and maintenance of; • Wooden and metal fingerposts, signs, benches, gates stiles, boardwalks and other countryside furniture. Tree Works • Surveying, planting, felling, maintaining and high access rope work relating to tree management. • Supply of native tree and plant species. Transportation • Transportation of plant, machinery, materials to accessible parts of the National Park. Habitat Restoration Works • Restore peatland areas by hand and or machine. • Planting of native species Traffic Management Supply and management of traffic control systems on public highways up to 'A' road standards. Please see our Rights of Way Specification Resource Pack at Appendix 1. Services required: • Surfacing • Drainage installation and maintenance • Sub soiling • Installation of stone flags • Pitching to create paths • Fencing • Walling • Vegetation control and clearance • Installation of countryside furniture (e.g. fingerposts/benches) • Tree works • Planting (trees and hedgerows) • Spraying (herbicides) • Hedge trimming • Salting and gritting paths • Trail sweeping • Mooring works (Ullswater/servicing) • Graffiti removal • Woodland management through thinning, coppicing, halo thinning, girdling, and processing of timber • Bracken management through mowing, rolling, or chemical application • Scrub management • Hedge laying • Grassland restoration and management activities; mowing, baling, weed wiping, harrowing, seeding, plug planting • Chemical control of invasive, non-native species Please also see Appendix 1 of the ITT. Lot 4: Consultancy and Specialist Services. The Authority requires a range of consultancy services to assist it in carrying out its statutory duties and project work. Our work is incredibly varied, and consultancy is required in relation to all stages of a project from feasibility, design, planning, and surveying. We require specialist advice in relation to Rights of Way, and lake/water works. Other areas of the Authority's work include historic buildings and environment, planning and architectural surveying so we welcome consultants from a range of specialist practice areas. Advice sought could be, for example, in the form of written reports, design drawings to agreed standards, survey datasets (in agreed formats) or overseeing the delivery of defined projects around nature recovery or access and recreation related works. This Lot is divided into three individual sub-lots based on the type of consultancy required. Lot 4a: Access and Recreation services required: • Traffic management e.g. traffic lights • Planning consultancy • Structural engineering design • Construction Design and Management works • Electronic counting surveys - people, horses, vehicles, bikes etc • Rights of Way consultants • Project managers • Visitor monitoring and data • Property management and consulting Lot 4b: Natural Environment: • Ecological surveys (e.g. habitat surveys using NVC, UKHAB frameworks/Habitat condition monitoring using BNG or CSM methods/specialist surveys for taxonomical groups i.e Bryophytes, Lichens, protected species groups, insects) • Baseline surveys • Biodiversity Net Gain Habitat Management and Monitoring Plans • Biodiversity Net Gain Habitat bank monitoring survey and reporting • Habitat and property management and monitoring planning • Drone Surveys • Geospatial surveys Lot 4c: Historic Environment: • Historic Structure Surveys (e.g. condition surveys, archaeological and structural assessments and repair schedules) • Archaeological surverys (e.g condition surveys, fieldwork, heritage assessments) • Contract administration services for Historic Structure Construction Projects Lot 5: Training and Development. he Authority requires qualified companies to provide essential training to ensure that individuals working in various roles are equipped with the knowledge and skills needed to work safely and in compliance with regulatory requirements and legislation. The training requirements cover a range of topics, including first aid, manual handling, chainsaw, plant and equipment operation (to name a few - please see Appendix 2 for a full concise list), which are required to minimise risks and ensure a safe working environment. Courses will need to be accredited by recognised bodies, providing learners with the necessary qualifications to meet industry standards. • First aid • Manual handling • Practical countryside management training e.g.: walling, fencing • Plant and machinery operations e.g.: 4WD training, chainsaws, quad bikes, strimmers; • Species management training (e.g tree conditions surveys) • Please see Appendix 2 of the ITT for a list of all training requirements. Lot 6: Supply and repairs of Equipment, Plant and Machinery. The Authority has an internal fleet of various machinery, equipment and plant. We require services for maintenance and servicing of all types of equipment, plant, and machinery. We also require suppliers who can source and provide new equipment, plant and machinery as required. For example, current categories include: • Plant: diggers, dumpers, tracked power barrows, remote flails, chippers. • Vehicles: land rovers, pick-ups, 4x4s, electric vans and cars. • Power tools: compressors, jet washes, cement mixers, drills, stone saws, angle grinders chop saws etc. • Hand tools: spades, panel saws, shovelers, tampers, steel bars etc. • PPE: chainsaw trousers, hard hats, eye protection, hearing protection etc. • Fuel (Aspen, diesel, petrol, LPG etc.) • Servicing and safety inspections (e.g. LOLA checks on lifting strops and chains, and general servicing of tools like compressors) • Bi-annual service of outboard motors for patrol boats • Servicing of patrol boat trailers • Annual servicing of life jackets, patrol boat radar systems and CCTV systems. We require maintenance and servicing of all machinery and vehicles. Services required: • Servicing • Repairs • Maintenance (boats, outboard engines, trailers, lifejackets, diggers, dumpers, radar, CAT scanners, generator calibration) • Inspection of kit/ equipment • LOLER items checks • Supply of new machinery as required Lot 7: Helicopter Operations. Provide helicopter operations for the transportation of stone and other materials to remote locations throughout the Lake District: movement of prebagged fell stone in one-ton bags to high altitude worksites on popular mountain paths. Stropping, bunding and prepping materials such as flagstones, fence posts or bridge materials prior to flying. Providing specialist safety advice to officers involved in helicopter operations - before during and after any operations. Provide experienced ground crew for hooking on and assessing loads, receiving loads where necessary and ensuring specialist kit or equipment such as signage strops and radio headsets are available. To provide an indication of volume, in 2025 LDNPA flew over 400 tonnes of stone to high altitude sites. Suppliers must hold all relevant Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) approvals, USL Licensing and operate in accordance with UK aviation regulations. Services required: • Transport of materials and equipment within the Lake District National Park using helicopters • Airlift operations • Load preparation (stropping, bunding) • Ground crew provision • Flight planning and risk assessment Lot 8: Higher Value Practical Works - £50,000 and over. The Authority secures frequent bids for grant money provided by national, regional and local government as well as charitable organisations and private funding organisations. This funding enables the Authority to undertake larger scale and usually multi-facetted projects or programmes of work varying in value from the high tens of thousands of pounds to the low millions of pounds. Such projects may involve delivery of one type of product or service across a range of sites throughout the park or a multi-facetted project including access, nature conservation, interpretation, and conservation of the heritage-built environment. We are looking for suppliers who can provide work at scale and across a range of areas, either directly or by acting as Primary Contractors and providing project management and delivering work through co-ordinating multiple suppliers and contractors. Examples of such work packages include the establishment of the Coast-to-Coast National Trail, barn restoration through the Farming in Protected Landscapes programme and Access for All projects. Services required: • General construction project work (see description) • Sub soiling • Stone flags • Pitching • Construction Design and Management work • Supply and construction of bridges • Public path works • Securing relevant consents, assents and planning permissions • Woodland Management • Grassland restoration • Riverbank Stabilization

sig_702054ac59d9cdae4923.description: Kent Fire and Rescue Service (KFRS) is exploring options for a Project Portfolio Management (PPM) solution to support the planning, management, oversight and reporting of projects and programmes across the organisation. KFRS is open to different solution and delivery models, including established Software as a Service (SaaS) products and Microsoft/Power Platform-based solutions. Please note: For the purposes of this market engagement, KFRS is only seeking responses in respect of solutions which are currently available for procurement through an existing Government Commercial Agency (GCA) framework (formerly CCS). Suppliers should identify the relevant framework, Lot (where applicable) and service/solution listing within their response. The purpose of this exercise is to undertake a short and proportionate test of the market before KFRS determines its procurement strategy and route to market. In particular, KFRS wishes to understand: •what potentially suitable solutions are available within or around the stated affordability envelope; •the broad alignment of available products with KFRS's functional and technical requirements; •the different solution and service models available and the respective responsibilities of KFRS and the supplier; •indicative licensing/subscription, implementation, support and ongoing configuration/development costs; •the extent to which solutions allow KFRS to retain appropriate control and portability of its organisational data; •any observations from the market which may help KFRS refine its requirements; and •the specific GCA/CCS framework, Lot and/or service listing through which the proposed solution can be procured. Nature of this Exercise This is a preliminary market engagement exercise and not a competitive procurement or invitation to tender. The functional and technical requirements provided with this brief represent KFRS's current understanding of its needs. They are being provided to give suppliers sufficient information to determine whether they have a product or solution that could potentially meet the requirement. Suppliers are not required to provide a detailed response against each individual requirement or complete the requirements schedules on a line-by-line basis. Responses will not be evaluated or scored as tender submissions. Instead, KFRS is seeking a brief, high-level response that will enable us to understand whether a proposed solution appears sufficiently aligned with our needs to warrant further exploration. KFRS would also welcome constructive feedback on the requirements themselves. This may include identifying areas which would benefit from clarification, or alternative approaches or current market capabilities which KFRS should consider. Please respond via the Kent Business Portal. Additional information: The contracting authority considers that this contract may be suitable for economic operators that are small or medium enterprises (SMEs). However, any selection of tenderers will be based solely on the criteria set out for the procurement.
sig_702054ac59d9cdae4923.title: GB-Maidstone: Preliminary Market Engagement via GCA Framework - Brief Project Portfolio Management Solution

The objective of uni-assist e.V. is to develop a new service IT system to support admission preparation at German higher education institutions. Starting from a proprietary software (aBIS) that has reached the end of its lifecycle and in view of the accelerating digitalisation of admission preparation, the continuing growth in interest among international degree seekers in studying in Germany, as well as the currently frequently described demand for (international) skilled workers in Germany 1 it is essential for the association to quickly establish a new system in order to (i) provide international prospective students with an intuitive and easy-to-use platform for submitting their study applications, (ii) enable the German higher education institutions organised within the association to conduct a transparent and fair selection procedure, (iii) map internal evaluation processes efficiently and with high quality, and (iv) develop recommendations for action and procedural optimisations for internal and external stakeholders based on the generated data. Central objectives of the new development are (i) the gradual technological replacement of the legacy system, (ii) the increase in the degree of automation in the procedural processes, and (iii) the most complete possible digitalisation of the processes with (iv) a simultaneous increase in usability for users as well as (v) the preservation and assurance of all (data protection) legal standards. For this purpose, the contracting authority requires the following IT services (category): 1. Support in software development (e.g. programming, managing Scrum teams, testing) 2. Support for requirements management 3. Support in system administration 4. Support in maintaining and further developing IT and data protection security 5. Support in the coordination of the software development project and consulting for the IT department (e.g. PMO, project management, agile coaching, data management) After its foundation, uni-assist developed a complex, cross-institutional software: aBIS (assist Applicant Information System). After the first application procedure could be successfully handled with this software in the year 2004, additions and improvements were made: this second generation aBIS2 is in use to this day. The main focus areas of this software are: - support in certificate evaluation, - provision and evaluation of results for the higher education institutions, - presentation of the application process for prospective students. In over 20 years, the framework conditions have changed completely: from 41 founding higher education institutions, it has grown to just under 150 member higher education institutions, the study system has been fundamentally changed by the Bologna Process, and online applications are taken for granted in a digital world. The software solution currently in use is therefore massively reaching its expansion limits. There is a monolithic structure that is no longer maintainable and has reached the end of its lifecycle. The very limited documentation and the increasing binding of personnel for maintaining operations lead to a growing risk for uni-assist. Supported by funds from the BMBF, the launch of the application portal (mya) and the higher education institution portal (PoMM) was recently completed in the years 2016 to 2019. Both have created the prerequisites to also cope with large increases in applications. 2.2. State of the art The most important objectives for the development of uni-assist's new service system are, compared to the legacy system, to reduce complexity and to make the software as a whole more flexible and robust. Both the service architecture, the system architecture and the technological implementation in development must be taken into account. Aspects of domain-driven design help to make the software more robust and at the same time more flexible on all three levels. Supported by funds from the BMBF, the launch of the application portal (mya) and the university portal (PoMM) was recently completed in the years 2016 to 2019. With both, the prerequisites were created to also cope with large increases in applications. 2.2. Goal The goal of uni-assist e.V. is to develop a new service IT system to support admission preparation at German universities. Starting from proprietary software (aBIS) that has reached the end of its life cycle and in view of the accelerating digitalisation of admission preparation, the further growing interest of international degree seekers in studying in Germany as well as the currently frequently described need for (international) skilled workers in Germany 1 it is essential for the association to quickly establish a new system in order to (i) provide international prospective students with an intuitively and easily usable platform for submitting their study applications, (ii) enable the German universities organised in the association to have a transparent and fair selection process, (iii) map internal evaluation processes efficiently and with high quality and (iv) develop recommendations for action and process optimisations for internal and external stakeholders based on the generated data. Central goals of the software development project are (i) the technological successive replacement of the legacy system, (ii) the increase in the degree of automation in the procedural processes and (iii) the most complete digitalisation of the processes possible with (iv) simultaneous increase in usability for the users as well as (v) the preservation and assurance of all (data protection) legal standards. 2.3. State of the art The most important goals of the development of the new service system of uni-assist are, in comparison to the legacy system, to reduce complexity and to make the software more flexible and robust overall. This requirement places special demands on the software architecture. Both the service architecture, the system architecture and the technological implementation in development must be taken into account. Aspects of domain-driven design help to make the software more robust and at the same time more flexible at all three levels. The services to be awarded via the DBS are divided into 5 categories / subject areas: 1. Support in software development (e.g. programming, managing the Scrum teams, testing) 2. Support for requirements management 3. Support in system administration 4. Support in maintaining and further developing IT and data protection security 5. Support in coordinating the software development project and advising the IT department (e.g. PMO, project management, Agile coaching, data management) Further information regarding the services sought and the requirements necessary for this, as well as details on the specific service period, will be published in the second phase of the procedure. In principle, the contractor is free in the performance of their tasks in terms of time, place and manner. The start and end of the assignment depend on the project-related requirements. If there is an obligation to be present, the services must be provided from Monday to Friday during the business hours of uni-assist. If there is no obligation to be present, the services must be provided from Monday to Friday between 6:00 and 21:00. The services are generally carried out independently and without instructions for the completion of the specifically described tasks. The service is provided in consultation with the contact person of the client and the contractor named in the call-off. The persons deployed by the contractor to provide the service report regularly to the contact person of the client named in the call-off regarding the technical results achieved during the reporting period and the current status. sig_7134fbf7fa12cfaf3ae8.description: The subject of this tender is the procurement of a highly available virtualization platform including the required hardware, software licences, manufacturer support and services to replace or modernise the existing virtualization infrastructure of the Gemeinschaftsklinikum Mittelrhein. The new solution must ensure the operation of currently around 300 virtual machines in an active-active data centre architecture and provide the essential functions of the existing VMware vSphere Enterprise Plus / VMware Cloud Foundation environment with functional equivalence. These include in particular high availability, automated load balancing, live migration of virtual machines, cross-location operation and central administration. The tender is designed to be open to all manufacturers and technologies. Solutions based on alternative virtualization platforms as well as concepts in which VMware continues to be used can be offered. The solution offered must meet the functional, technical and economic requirements defined in the tender documents. Bidders must submit an architecture and migration concept that provides either for the continued use of the existing Dell VxRail hardware or its complete replacement. The use of hyperconverged as well as classical 3-tier architectures is permitted. The use of VMware vSAN is not a prerequisite. The scope of services also includes the provision of all required hardware and software components, the integration of the existing Veeam Backup & Replication environment using agentless backup procedures, the implementation including knowledge transfer as well as support for the migration of all virtual machines. The existing VMware subscription ends on 30.03.2027. The solution offered must therefore be fully operational, migrated and accepted, including all productive workloads, by 15.03.2027 at the latest. The period between 15.03.2027 and the expiry of the existing VMware licensing serves as a risk buffer and stabilization phase. Lot LOT-0001: Renewal of virtualization environment. The detailed description of the procurement is described in the specification of services.

sig_7181f96b85e030152f2b.description: MARKET DIALOGUE The subject of the market dialogue is the procurement of a system for the remote monitoring and management service of maritime safety equipment currently under preparation for the needs of Väylävirasto. Väylävirasto is responsible for the maintenance, development and usability of maritime safety equipment in Finland as part of the authority's tasks in fairway management. The remote monitoring service is a key part of the operational reliability, situational awareness and remote management entity of safety equipment. BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES The subject of the procurement is the implementation, maintenance and ongoing development of a remote monitoring and remote management service for maritime safety equipment. The service receives status, fault and location data from safety equipment, processes and stores the data, and forwards it to the key systems of Väylävirasto, particularly Reimari and analytics solutions. There are approximately 1 800 pieces of remotely monitored safety equipment, some of which are fixed and some floating, and some of the equipment can also be managed remotely. The equipment communicates via a mobile network, and in the target state, message transmission is based on the LTE-M network and the MQTT protocol in accordance with IALA specifications, with secure encryption. In the target state, the remote monitoring and management service is located in Väylävirasto's cloud environment (AWS). The service is responsible for the processing of all received remote monitoring data, including raw data storage, data processing, the provision of interfaces and necessary calculation operations, such as post-calculation of position measurements. The remote monitoring service does not provide a separate user interface, but the data is viewed via Reimari. The procurement includes system maintenance to ensure that the service remains operationally reliable, secure and responsive to users' needs throughout the contract period. Maintenance covers, among other things, technical support, updates, bug fixes, and compatibility with safety equipment and integrations. Ongoing system development is also implemented as part of the procurement. The aim of ongoing development is to gradually enable new functionalities, interfaces and integrations, and to support changes in the operating environment, technology and legislation. The procurement also examines various architectural options for communication between safety equipment and the remote monitoring service. The procurement includes a cooperation model in which the contracting authority and the supplier develop the service in a planned and long-term manner. The objective is a comprehensive solution that supports the lifecycle management of safety equipment, the utilisation of data and the continuous improvement of the service. One (1) supplier will be selected as the service provider. The subject, scope and technical solutions of the procurement may be refined and/or modified as the preparation of the procurement and the market dialogue progress. PRELIMINARY SCHEDULE The contracting authority's target schedule for the implementation of the market dialogue and procurement is: - Market dialogue (technical dialogue), January-February 2026 - Publication of the call for tenders and calculation period, March-April 2026 - Evaluation of tenders and award decision, April-May 2026 - Contract entering into force and commencement of the development project, during the year 2026 ----- ADDITIONAL INFORMATION ON THE NOTICE This notice is a prior information notice. This notice does not constitute a request for tenders. The prior information notice includes an invitation to a market dialogue, whereby all suppliers interested in the procurement have the opportunity to engage in a technical dialogue concerning the procurement with Väylävirasto. The purpose of the technical dialogue is to discuss the subject of the procurement and its definition at a general level. The technical dialogue does not bind Väylävirasto to carry out the procurement. Nor does the technical dialogue bind the supplier to participate in a potential tendering procedure. The technical dialogue is organised through commenting on draft versions of the call for tenders documentation and answering the contracting authority's questions related to the subject of the procurement. Instructions for registration: Suppliers must express their interest in participating in the market dialogue by 11.2.2026 by 12.00 by sending a message to the address tommi.aarnio@vayla.fi with the subject: "Kaukovalvonta - markkinavuoropuhelu". Suppliers are requested to state the following information in the message: - the supplier's contact person's email address The contracting authority reserves the right to invite suppliers also to bilateral negotiations or to continue the technical dialogue in another manner to be announced separately, which will be notified later if necessary. The descriptions presented in this prior information notice and the estimated publication date of the contract notice, as well as the dialogue draft materials to be provided later, are preliminary and indicative prior information on the procurement. Participating companies will not be paid any compensation for responding or participating.
