sig_7184071bd66d805d60a4.description: Background Registers of Scotland (RoS) is undertaking a strategic review of its current data licensing position as part of its ambition to maximise the value of the data it holds. RoS currently delivers a range of statutory and commercial data products to a diverse customer base, including citizens, public sector bodies, and commercial organisations. This breadth of demand has led to an increasing need to develop scalable and sustainable data products. The development of these products is shaped by existing licensing arrangements, including the Public Sector Geospatial Agreement (PSGA) and Postal Address File (PAF) frameworks. These define the terms under which data can be used, reused, and shared, particularly where third-party data is integrated with RoS datasets. RoS is seeking specialist support to work with existing RoS departments to define a data strategy that reflects the organisation’s current and future priorities. Purpose of this Notice This notice is issued to engage with the market and identify organisations with expertise in public sector data licensing, data commercialisation, and governance. The feedback received will inform the scope, structure, and requirements of a potential future procurement exercise. Scope of Potential Requirement RoS is seeking a partner to provide expertise and support in the following areas covering both current and future activity. 1. Review of Current Licensing Landscape Assess RoS’s current licensing arrangements, including PSGA, PAF, and other third party agreements Identify constraints, risks, and opportunities in the current model Advise on how existing frameworks can be leveraged to support data products and services while ensure statutory obligations remain paramount 2. Definition of Data Principles Support RoS in developing clear data principles covering: Data sharing and reuse Commercialisation and monetisation Transparency, fairness, and public value Ensure alignment with public sector obligations, corporate objectives and customer expectations 3. Recommendations and Implementation Roadmap Provide actionable, practical recommendations for: Optimising the use of RoS data Enabling new data products and services Managing licensing risks and compliance Clear options, trade-offs, and decision frameworks to support senior decision-making Develop an implementation roadmap that RoS can deliver internally 4. Capability and Skills Development Identify the organisational skills, roles, and capabilities required to: Sustain data commercialisation Govern data and licensing frameworks effectively Recommend approaches to embed these capabilities within RoS operations Key Context for Suppliers RoS operates within a complex licensing environment, particularly where third party data is embedded in its products There is a tension between legacy licensing models and ambitions for more open, scalable data products, which has been identified as a systemic issue RoS is exploring different strategic options, including changes to licensing arrangements and potential use of external partners to support commercialisation Market Engagement RoS invites expressions of interest from organisations with experience in: Public sector data licensing and governance Data commercialisation and product development Navigating complex multi party licensing frameworks Supporting organisations to unlock the value of their data assets Responses to this notice will help shape the design of any future procurement. sig_719c57caeed697069b5c.description: NHSScotland is exploring options for the potential procurement of a multi-channel remote health monitoring and communication solution capable of supporting the delivery of enhanced care pathways, including home and mobile health monitoring. Remote health monitoring (RHM) is a digitally enabled model of care that allows people to record, submit and share clinically relevant health information from their home or community setting. This enables health and care teams to monitor health status, support self management and intervene proactively, reducing the need for routine face-to-face contact. RHM can support management of long term conditions to reduce escalation and prevent admissions and can also support earlier discharge and hospital at home models where appropriate. Connect Me is NHSScotland’s national remote health monitoring service, currently delivered using the Inhealthcare platform. The service supports the collection of measurements and patient reported information through a range of channels including automated telephone calls, SMS messages and digital access via web browser or mobile application. Lot 1: . This PIN serves as a soft market test to assess available options, continuity of key services, migration approaches and indicative costs. A Market Research Questionnaire can be downloaded from the Additional Documents area and returned as instructed within the document by noon on Monday, 25 May 2026. Suppliers are also invited to attend an online briefing session on 7 May 2026 at 2:30PM. Teams login details will be confirmed via this Public Contracts Scotland portal.

sig_71a636995c5e6bc24f51.description:
Supply of a forest fire location system divided into two parts. Part No. 1 - Supply, installation and commissioning of a forest fire monitoring system based on long-range fire-fighting cameras together with software for automatic smoke detection. Part No. 2 - Supply, installation and commissioning of a complete unmanned aerial vehicle system with an automatic docking station for fire monitoring of forest areas. A detailed description can be found in the relevant parts of the contract. The subject of the contract consists of sets of equipment together with installation and commissioning, the task of which will be to enable automatic detection and location of forest fires, including long-range fire-fighting cameras mounted on observation towers together with necessary accessories and the equipment of the Inspectorate's Alarm and Dispatch Point (ADP). The purpose of the system will be to carry out continuous fire monitoring of forest areas. Fire-fighting cameras mounted on observation towers are to work with the supplied software for automatic fire detection, which is intended to increase the effectiveness of monitoring in the given area. The image from the cameras must be sent to the ADP via a radio link in the unlicensed band, supplied and installed under this contract. The transmission system must be designed in a way that enables the future change of the transmission medium from radio to fibre-optic without the need to replace cameras, software and active network devices, with the exception of terminal devices used for connecting the fibre optic.. The Baczków and Hysne towers should be retrofitted with an Off-Grid power supply installation, and the ADP with a UPS emergency power supply system. The power supply must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62040-5-3:2017-05 (UPS systems) or equivalent. The installation must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62446-1:2016-08 (Photovoltaic installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62446-1:2016-08/A1:2019-01 (Testing of PV installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62109-2:2011 (Inverter safety) or equivalent and PN-EN IEC 62619:2023-02 (Lithium battery safety) or equivalent. The contract includes: - dismantling of the existing fire monitoring system, - supply and installation of 3 cameras for observing forest areas on the Baczków, Hysne and Dąbrowa fire-fighting towers, - supply and installation of sprinklers together with a fluid tank for the mounted cameras, - supply and installation of an off-grid power supply on the Baczków and Hysne towers. The installation must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62548 (Photovoltaic installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62446 (Testing of PV installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62109 (Inverter safety) or equivalent and PN-EN IEC 62619 (Lithium battery safety) or equivalent. - supply and installation of an alarm system and anti-burglary cameras on the fire-fighting towers, - supply and installation of radio links establishing connections: ● Baczków tower – Hysne tower in the 5 GHz band, ● Hysne tower – Dąbrowa tower in the 5 GHz band, ● Dąbrowa tower – Church in the 60 GHZ band with a backup 5 GHz, ● Church – Inspectorate building in the 60 GHZ band with a backup 5 GHz, ● Baczków tower – Dąbrowa tower in the 5 GHz band (redundant connection), - supply and installation of devices to provide backup communication 5G/LTE, - supply and installation of ADP equipment: ● supply and installation of 3 televisions for observing images from fire-fighting cameras, ● supply and installation of a computer with two monitors, ● supply and installation of a control console, ● supply and installation of a UPS emergency power supply. The power supply must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62040 (UPS systems) or equivalent. - supply, installation and commissioning of an automatic smoke detection system, - training on system operation. The Contractor is obliged to execute a complete work from the point of view of the purpose it is to serve. The Contracting Authority permits the installation of additional devices not included in the specification if they are necessary to achieve the required functionalities. Other information can be found in the procurement documents - Appendix No. 2 to the ToR; Supply, installation and commissioning of a complete unmanned aerial vehicle system with an automatic docking station for fire monitoring of forest areas - equipment under the FEnIKS project entitled: Comprehensive project for the adaptation of forests and forestry to climate change - prevention, counteracting and limiting the effects of threats related to forest fires (FIRE 2). 1. Subject of the contract 1.1. The subject of the contract is the supply of one complete, factory-new and unused UAS system comprising an unmanned aerial vehicle, an automatic docking station, a multi-sensor observation head, a control device, software, accessories, installation, configuration, commissioning, training and warranty service. 1.2. The system will be intended primarily for: automatic and ad-hoc patrols of forest areas during the fire hazard period; remote verification of smoke or fire alarms, including alarms transmitted by the alarm and dispatch point, camera system or rescue services; locating heat sources and determining their coordinates; live transmission in the visible and thermal imaging band; monitoring fire development, access roads, endangered objects and control after extinguishing a fire. 1.3. The subject of the contract has been described through functional requirements and minimum performance parameters. The Contracting Authority does not require a product of a specific brand or a single manufacturer's solution. However, all elements must form one compatible system, for the correct operation of which the Contractor is responsible. 2. Basis and rules for describing the subject of the contract. The description was drawn up taking into account in particular Article 16, Article 99, Article 101 and Article 105–107 of the Act of 11 September 2019 on Public Procurement Law (unified text: Journal of Laws of 2026, item 793 as amended). References to standards are to be understood as references to the indicated standard or an equivalent standard.

• Each indicated parameter is a minimum parameter, unless expressly stated otherwise. • Structurally different technical solutions are permitted if they ensure at least the same functionality, level of security and performance parameters. • If meeting a requirement requires an additional module, licence, modem, antenna, service or accessory, this element must be included in the tender and price. • All costs necessary to use the full functionality of the system for the period indicated in the OPZ must be itemised in the price form. Other information can be found in the procurement documents - Appendix No. 2 to the ToR

sig_71b044f6ea8a0fde2b93.description: The U.S. Embassy Athens Public Diplomacy Section (PDS Athens) of the U.S. Department of State is pleased to announce funding is available through its Public Diplomacy Grants Program in fiscal year 2025. This is an Annual Program Statement, outlining our funding priorities, the strategic themes we focus on, and the procedures for submitting requests for funding. Please carefully follow all instructions below. The deadline for grant applications is July 11, 2025. Funding decisions will be made on these applications on a rolling basis after this deadline, with a goal of informing all applicants of the final funding decision by September 30, 2025. Applicants may apply for funding between $25,000 and $100,000 . Please use the grant application documents and budget template found on the Embassy website https://gr.usembassy.gov/education/ . Purpose of Grants program: PDS Athens invites proposals for projects that strengthen ties between the United States and Greece through concrete demonstrations of cooperation between our two peoples, aiming at making America safer, stronger and more prosperous . All grant proposals must convey an element of American history, culture, or shared values. Competitive proposals should support a priority program area (see below). They should also include a connection with American expert/s, organization/s, or institution/s that will promote increased cooperation between the people of the United States and Greece even after the program has finished. Priority Program Areas: The Public Diplomacy Section is focused on the following priorities in the form of programs, exchanges, and media opportunities that: Promote American Excellence in Emerging Technologies Celebrate 250 Years of American Excellence: Spotlight on America’s Achievements, Innovation, and Leadership Promoting American Excellence in Emerging Technologies Greek students and professionals in emerging technologies have demonstrated a strong technical foundation that can be strategically leveraged to benefit U.S. technology firms and bolster American leadership in critical industries. By channeling this talent to serve the needs of American companies, we can reinforce U.S. technological dominance, strengthen innovation pipelines, and ensure that international engagement directly supports American economic and strategic priorities. We invite proposals aimed at enhancing U.S.-Greece technological cooperation in ways that clearly advance U.S. national interests. Proposals must focus on initiatives (not conferences) that help U.S. firms address critical workforce and skill shortages, expand the reach of American products and innovation standards, and create structured pathways for Greek talent to contribute to U.S.-driven innovation. Prioritized activities include, but are not limited to: Public-private partnerships that connect U.S. technology firms with high-potential Greek talent through American-led career readiness programs, skills development, and reskilling/upskilling initiatives tailored to U.S. industry standards and needs. Training modules designed for integration into Greek higher education or vocational curricula that: Align directly with the needs of U.S. employers; and Target high-demand fields such as artificial intelligence (AI), biotechnology, cybersecurity, data analytics, and cloud computing—strengthening the global competitiveness of U.S. firms. Innovation bootcamps that feature U.S. technologies, platforms, and products, familiarizing international talent with high-quality American tools and practices. Collaborative projects between U.S. technology companies and Greek educational institutions to promote the adoption and use of American-developed AI and other emerging technologies, reinforcing the global footprint of U.S. innovation. All proposals should demonstrate a clear benefit to the United States and prioritize American commercial and strategic interests, consistent with the principles of the America First policy. Celebrating 250 Years of American Excellence: Spotlight on America’s Achievements, Innovation, and Leadership On July 4, 2026, the United States will commemorate the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence. This historic milestone presents a powerful opportunity to celebrate American excellence, leverage people-to-people ties, and highlight our achievements, legacies, and contributions as part of America’s story of excellence. We invite proposals that underscore American excellence and contribute to the celebration of America250 , highlighting this momentous occasion through impactful and engaging programs. We welcome submissions that promote U.S.-Greece bilateral engagement and spotlight American achievements, innovation, leadership, and the role of faith and religion in democratic societies. Proposals should feature initiatives (not conferences), and include activities such as (but not limited to): Podcasts and/or public lectures on U.S. history, its ties to Greece, democracy, and its global impact Roadshows showcasing 250 years of American innovation and U.S.-Greek cooperation Sports activities or themed games/events Secondary educational modules that will reach Greek classrooms and help to enhance Greek students’ and educators’ positive understanding of America All proposals should demonstrate a clear benefit to the United States and prioritize American strategic interests, consistent with the principles of the America First policy.

sig_729b45308c6d2eb6e263.description: Background Arendal municipality has an ongoing need for graphical services connected to information material and visual communication aimed at inhabitants and internal target groups. The municipality produces some material itself, but needs external assistance for assignments that are more complex, time consuming or require special professional competence. The procurement shall ensure access to capacity and relevant competence within graphical design, at the same time as the municipality takes care of the need for uniform visual communication and clear identity. The municipality shall be one sender. It is also important to ensure that material and visual deliveries fulfil the requirements for universal design and ensure accessible and understandable communication for different user groups. The municipality therefore needs to establish a new framework agreement that provides predictable access to graphical assistance as needed, both for smaller ongoing assignments and for major or more strategic deliveries. Description of the assignment The procurement is for graphic services for Arendal municipality. The delivery shall cover the development and production of various types of graphical material and visual elements, including information material, reports, presentations, templates, graphics for digital surfaces, infographics, illustrations and professional design consultancy services. The assignments will vary in extent and complexity. The municipality needs a tenderer who can assist with both smaller, limited assignments and large deliveries that require more planning and close cooperation with the contracting authority. Minor assignments means limited deliveries such as, for example, an ad, poster, presentation or simple illustration. Larger deliveries means assignments that include planning, coordination and multiple sub-services, such as a report or campaign material. The deliveries shall be able to be used further in the municipality ́s own channels and tools, and it is important that the deliveries can be further developed and adapted internally. The framework agreement shall also include the design of profile material and profile articles, as well as graphic materials connected to the use of, among other things, vehicles, buildings and work clothes. Web design for arendal.kommune.no is not included in the procurement. It is important to have clear contact points, effective clarifications and a good understanding of the municipality ́s graphical profile, communication needs and targets for clear, available and recognisable communication.
sig_729b45308c6d2eb6e263.title: Graphic services

sig_72fc7eb88055e268874c.description: Government and the nation face a talent shortfall in artificial intelligence (AI) and cybersecurity. The CyberAICorps Scholarship for Service ( CyberAI SFS ) program welcomes proposals that address AI and cybersecurity education and workforce development. CyberAI refers to using AI in cybersecurity as well as providing security and resilience for AI systems. The Scholarship Track provides funding to establish, or to continue, scholarship for service programs with integrated AI and cybersecurity components (CyberAI). Scholarship recipients must be U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents and work after graduation in the AI or cybersecurity mission of a government organization for a period of at least the length of the scholarship. The Innovation Track supports projects that enhance preparation of AI and/or cybersecurity professionals. Projects may expand existing educational opportunities, curricula, degree programs, educational pathways, methods and interventions, and partnerships among institutions of higher education, government, and employers. Two statutes authorize this program: 15 USC §7442 (cybersecurity) and 42 USC §18993 (AI). CyberAI SFS aligns with the Executive Order 14277 to prioritize AI within scholarship for service programs. CyberAI is managed by NSF’s Directorate for STEM Education in collaboration with the U.S. Office of Personnel Management (OPM) and U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS).
sig_72fc7eb88055e268874c.title: Artificial Intelligence and Cybersecurity Education Innovation and Scholarship for Service (CyberAI SFS)

sig_7301433f6d2a0ac4a43d.description: This Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) invites exploratory grant applications, hereafter referred to as the Novel Experiential Technologies Assisting Individual learning Hubs or NExT AI Hubs (formerly Learning Disabilities Innovation Hubs), to address the impact of Artificial Intelligence (AI) technologies on developmental outcomes in children diagnosed with or at risk for developing a specific learning disability (SLD) impacting reading, writing, and mathematics. NExT AI Hubs include a single Research Project and a Leadership Core that support the goals and aims of the Hub. This NOFO seeks to serve as a catalyst to 1) speed the maturation of nascent/novel, high-impact, high-risk research that advances understanding of the role AI technology plays in supporting, improving, or limiting the learning, cognitive, and socio-emotional needs of children at risk for or diagnosed with SLDs, 2) build an evidence base for the SLD community to inform policy or practice, and 3) provide project-embedded, career-enhancing research and professional development opportunities to support the next generation of transdisciplinary SLD scientists. This initiative provides opportunities to support planning and building a body of research and corresponding intellectual infrastructure to enable NExT AI investigators to compete for large research and program project opportunities in the future.This NOFO aims to integrate research topics that are of relevance to various research programs at the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development (NICHD) and align with the NICHD Strategic Plan. The NOFO intends to build cross-programmatic, transdisciplinary and cross-cutting scientific research, and critically nurture the development of early career investigators capable of conducting this research.
sig_7301433f6d2a0ac4a43d.title: Novel Experiential Technologies Assisting Individual Learning (NExT AI) Hubs (P20 Clinical Trial Optional)

Part 1) - Procurement of technologies for server rooms The subject matter of this part of the public contract is the comprehensive supply, expert implementation and subsequent commissioning of a complete technological solution for the expansion and supplementation of the existing data centre infrastructure, both physically and technologically. Specifically, this involves the installation and integration of physical infrastructure elements, a modern air conditioning system, an uninterruptible power supply, a CCTV system for monitoring and security purposes, fire safety systems and the establishment of an optical connection with a dedicated backup server room, which will ensure high availability and operational continuity. Part 2) – Procurement of network technologies The subject matter of this part of the public contract is the supply, implementation and commissioning of a comprehensive solution to increase LAN access security and modernise the backbone and access network infrastructure. This includes the replacement of active components in both the access and backbone layers, the deployment of a network access control (NAC) system with support for IEEE 802.1X and the supply of central switch management in the form of on-premises or cloud management. New switches (2 backbone switches and 7 access switches) will be deployed within the access layer to ensure secure connection of end devices using authentication and authorisation based on IEEE 802.1X. This part forms the basic communication and authentication layer of the infrastructure and is designed in direct succession to the security, monitoring and logging systems specified in the technical specification - part 3, with which it must be fully interoperable at the level of access control, security events, logging and automated response. Part 3) – Supply and implementation of security and monitoring software The subject matter of this part of the public contract is the supply, implementation and commissioning of high-performance servers to increase system availability, strengthen operational computing power by supplying two high-performance rack servers and an enterprise All Flash disk array. The aim is to expand the computing and storage capacity of the hospital infrastructure with an emphasis on high performance, redundancy, scalability, advanced management and security features, including support for virtualisation, high availability and data services. Furthermore, the supply, implementation and commissioning of a comprehensive solution for the security of the organisation's perimeter, security policy management and cyber threat detection. This includes the deployment of a high-availability firewall cluster, a central security event management system and training of responsible personnel. Finally, the supply and installation of a system for central log collection and the supply and installation of hardware and software equipment that form a comprehensive solution for long-term and detailed monitoring and evaluation of network traffic using data flows (NetFlow, IPFIX, sFlow, etc.). sig_74c799560328d6793623.description: Nest is seeking to appoint one supplier to provide, implement and support one hosted software-as-a-service solution for Nest Invest, comprising two mandatory capabilities: Asset Allocation and Total Portfolio View. The Asset Allocation capability must support Nest Invest’s multi-level fund-of-funds structure and its controlled, model-driven asset allocation process. This includes strategic and tactical asset allocation, portfolio modelling and optimisation, configurable targets, limits and tolerances, portfolio rebalancing, asset restrictions, workflow and approval controls, auditability, scenario analysis and the generation of implementation instructions or outputs for downstream parties. The Total Portfolio View capability must provide a consolidated view of Nest Invest’s portfolio across public and private assets, including positions, exposures, performance and look-through information where available. It must support aggregation and analysis across Nest Invest’s fund structure. The supplier will be required to provide software licensing or subscription services; implementation and configuration; integration with retained data sources and Nest Invest’s planned cloud data platform through appropriate data interfaces and APIs; transition and migration from the incumbent IRP solution; testing and user acceptance support; training and documentation; go-live and transition support; and ongoing hosting, maintenance, technical support and product-roadmap services. The solution must be configured for Nest Invest and supplied electronically as a hosted service. Investment and portfolio data will be received from retained sources, including the fund administrator and custodian, and the solution must generate the required information, reporting and implementation outputs for Nest Invest and its downstream processes. The contract will be awarded to one supplier for an initial term of five years. Nest may extend the contract for an additional two years and subsequently for a further one year, giving a maximum potential term of eight years. The contract does not guarantee any minimum volume of services or minimum expenditure. Lot 1: . None

sig_74ed8c2f9e1f5915e195.description: During the autumn of 2025, the City of Copenhagen will issue a tender for a new app-based digital solution for carrying out parking enforcement and processing parking fines. The app solution must be capable of being used on the municipality's compatible, standard smart mobile phones. The solution must enable the printing of parking fines on the Contracting Authority's current printers. Tenders are requested for both the app, which is used by the parking attendants for issuing fines, and for a web solution for handling, storing and transferring data to the municipality's existing relevant systems. The tender will include a number of functional requirements for the app and web solution, but also a number of IT security requirements. Before the tender is issued, the Parking Department would like to have the industry's feedback on the security requirements that the municipality is setting – the so-called non-functional requirements. This includes, in particular, the above-mentioned requirements.
sig_74ed8c2f9e1f5915e195.title: Technical consultation regarding non-functional requirements for a parking fine app for parking attendants

sig_75a3dfeacef639c5452e.description: ***SUMMARY ONLY - SEE ATTACHED COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION DOCUMENT FOR FULL DETAIL*** APS _ Combined Synopsis/Solicitation Brief: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation for Commercial Items Agile Professional Services ("APS”) Department of the Army Project Name: Agile Professional Services ("APS") Solicitation Number: W900KK-26-R-A023 NAICS Code: 541990 (All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services) Set-Aside: Total Small Business Set-Aside Contract Type: Labor Hours/T&M 1. General Information This combined synopsis/solicitation is issued by Army Contracting Command - APG - Orlando Division to procure Agile Professional Services ("APS"). The acquisition is structured to support critical technical and professional operations under a flexible framework, to be proposed and developed by the successful offeror. Key acquisition parameters include: • Set-Aside Status: 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside. • Small Business Size Standard: $19.5M as defined by SBA regulations. • Primary NAICS Classification: 541990 — All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services. • Contract Vehicle Type: Labor Hours/T&M 2. Solicitation Details This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. This combined synopsis/solicitation is prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular FAC 2025-06, effective August 27, 2025.and DFARS Publication Notice (DPN) July 2, 2026. As described in the attached FAR 52.212-2, The Army will adopt aspects of FAR Part 15 evaluation procedures. Considering the novel, and commercial, nature of these services this is deemed necessary to balance fairness, transparency, and competition with the interests of expediency and flexibility 3. Description of Requirement CPE ST3 has a need for Agile Professional Services (APS) support services to provide the organization with the ability to augment its Military and Government Civilian workforce in order to execute its mission. The services will be limited to providing professional support services, under a Performance Based Services model, to CPE ST3 and CPE ST3 customers for limited requirements which are related to CPE ST3’s mission. Since its inception, CPE ST3 has relied on contractor support to conduct its mission in all phases of life cycle management due to insufficient personnel within the organization to successfully perform the required services. This model of a Government footprint with a scalable contractor workforce has enabled CPE ST3 to be very flexible and agile in its mission to support the changing needs of the Army. The services to be performed will include related activities in support of all aspects of providing responsive integrated and interoperable infrastructure for simulation, training, testing, and threat solutions. APS support services are required for effective, efficient, and responsive full lifecycle management of efforts to include, but not limited to: vision statements and doctrine, development of architectures, program support (e.g., acquisition and budget planning, business and financial programming and execution, modeling, simulation, simulator, training device, and instrumentation development, documentation, fielding and execution, system analysis and integration, integrated logistics support, strategic planning, contingency and mission support, security cooperation/international relations, program oversight, independent verification validation and test evaluation, prototype development, sustainment and operations, and analysis of emerging technologies support), and subject matter experts on military tactics, techniques, and procedures. Potential areas of growth are envisioned but not limited to be in the areas of Cyber and Information Warfare, Robotics, Unmanned Vehicles, Home Station Training, Multi-Sensory Simulation, Artificial Intelligence, Hypersonics, Directed Energy, Electronic Warfare, Autonomous Systems, Multi-Domain Integration, Target and Threat Systems, Environment Modeling, Human Performance Training, Security Cooperation, Nuclear Engineering, and Medical Training. The critical performance requirement is the successful development and transition of CPE ST3 from a traditional, staffing-based support model to a task-based, outcome-driven Agile delivery framework that is to be developed by the Performer. Success will be measured by the contractor's ability to develop and iterate, through performance under the resultant contract, a framework that both provides the following, and is able to be replicated across future requirements. 4. Period of Performance / Performance Locations: Total Performance Period shall not exceed 66-months: • Base Period – (15-Feb-27 to 14-Aug-27) Agile Development and Transition In • Option Period 1 – (15-Aug-27 to 14-Aug-28) – Enterprise Performance • Option Period 2 – (15-Aug-28 to 14-Aug-29) – Enterprise Performance • Option Period 3 – (15-Aug-29 to 14-Aug-30) – Enterprise Performance • Option Period 4 – (15-Aug-30 to 14-Aug-31) – Enterprise Performance • Option Period 5 – (15-Aug-31 to 14-Feb-32) – Enterprise Performance and Transition Out • Option Period 6 – (15-Feb-32 to 14-Aug-32) – Option to Extend the Term of Service under FAR 52.217-8 * Work will be performed at Government facilities, Contractor facilities, and Remote locations. Primary Government sites include Orlando, FL, and Redstone Arsenal, AL (including 24/7 operations). Additional Government sites include: Fort Campbell, KY; Fort Hood, TX; Fort Drum, NY; Fort Irwin, CA; Fort Polk, LA; Fort Rucker, AL; Fort Bragg, NC; Hohenfels, Germany; and Camp Humphreys, South Korea. 5. Applicable FAR Provisions/Provisions: See Attachment 7. The provisions and clauses apply to this acquisition and are incorporated by reference or full text as applicable. The full text of the FAR and DFARS clauses may be accessed electronically at https://www.acquisition.gov/. 6. Proposal Submission Instructions Phase I responses to this solicitation are due by 13 October 2026 / 11:59pm (Eastern). Submission due dates for all subsequent Phases will be issued via Advisory Notifications / Invitations. All submissions must be submitted via email to the designated POCs listed below: Branch Chief / Contracting Officer: Lovisa D. sig_76b65243e3cf6f2cefb5.description: Huoltovarmuuskeskus invites market operators interested in the procurement to respond to a request for information and to register for the market dialogue. The subject of the procurement is an on-premises project portfolio tool that enables the management of programme and project activities. The objective of the procurement is to tender for software that: • supports current and developing project portfolio and programme management, and • reduces the amount of manual work related to processes and reporting. • The system solution to be procured and the supplier's operations must meet the security requirements for security-classified information. • In addition, the system also supports the work of an external project manager during the project planning, implementation, monitoring and closing phases. The aim is, in principle, to procure off-the-shelf software that can be configured according to the requirements and needs of HVK. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION AND BILATERAL MARKET DIALOGUE SESSIONS With this request for information, Huoltovarmuuskeskus (hereinafter HVK) is launching a market survey for the procurement. The purpose of the request for information is to identify potential market operators, collect information on solution alternatives available on the market, and compile insights regarding the subject of the procurement and its implementation. Furthermore, the goal of the request for information is to collect information from market operators and ensure that the procurement planning is based on the current market situation. In the request for information, service providers are asked to present preliminary alternatives for project implementation models. In addition to the request for information, the contracting authority may, if necessary, organise market dialogue sessions. Bilateral discussions on other matters related to the implementation of the project can also be held during the market dialogue. More detailed descriptions of the subject of the procurement, the request for information questions, and instructions can be found as an attachment to this notice. INSTRUCTIONS FOR RESPONDING TO THE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION We ask market operators to: a) Respond to the questions in the attached questionnaire in a free-form manner no later than 21.1.2026 at 16. - Message subject/heading: "Huoltovarmuuskeskus/ project portfolio - Request for information" - Responses are to be sent by email to anni.partanen@kpmg.fi b) In connection with responding, the market operator may register for a more detailed market dialogue session to be held via Teams. MARKET DIALOGUE The contracting authority reserves the right to organise an oral market dialogue session and the possibility to limit the number of candidates invited to the oral market dialogue section. The session requires the signing of a non-disclosure agreement. Potential market dialogue sessions will be held via Teams on 28.1.2026. The estimated duration of the session is 60-90 minutes. The contracting authority reserves the right to change and refine the schedule. Supplier-specific market dialogue invitations will be delivered to the registered market operators after the deadline for the request for information. The discussions will be held in Finnish. Participation in the market dialogue is not a condition for participating in the procurement process to be carried out later.
sig_76b65243e3cf6f2cefb5.title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: Procurement of a project portfolio as an On-Premises solution

sig_76e8b1f0b3f7be62f9f4.description: The subject of the contract is the design, development and operation of an event- and user-based RMV-KombiTicket system as Software as a Service (SaaS). The system is used for the issuance and management of public transport travel authorisations in conjunction with event and service tickets. It includes, in particular, web access for RMV administrators, a web app and the appropriate interfaces for connecting event organisers and ticketing service providers. The RMV-KombiTicket is to be provided as HandyTicket-Mobil, HandyTicket-Wallet and Print@Home-Ticket. Users must be able to retrieve a successfully issued RMV-KombiTicket in all three ticket forms and use it as a valid travel authorisation. Issuance must be enabled both through direct retrieval by the event organiser and through personalisation and activation by the user. In addition, a procedure for the provision and distribution of event codes without a direct interface connection must be provided. The system must support the user roles of user, event organiser, ticketing service provider and RMV, each with appropriate functions and authorisations. In addition to the technical implementation, the contractor shall assume responsibility for the secure, reliable and permanently available operation of the RMV-KombiTicket system, including the associated services.
sig_76e8b1f0b3f7be62f9f4.title: RMV-KombiTicketsystem (Wallet, Mobil und Print@Home)

sig_76efaff15002776a3b58.description: Banedanmark expects to publish the tender for acquiring a solution to monitor and diagnosing railway telecommunications and signalling systems in Spring 2026. To be sure that the process for tender and the contract is aligned with the capabilities of the market, Banedanmark wishes to invite potential vendors for a written market dialogue and verbal hearing regarding the upcoming tender for acquiring a solution to monitor and diagnose railway telecommunications and signalling systems. The purpose of the market dialogue is to get the markets feedback on the scope and if it is aligned with the market regarding the composition of the products/services, the commercial conditions, the price structure, market conditions, risks, and the partnership after having entered the contract etc. In that way Banedanmark will be able to optimize the tender material accordingly to how the market is today before making the tender public. The market dialogue process is the following: Banedanmark has attached an appendix to this document, which Banedanmark request the potential vendors to answer and return via EU-Supply. - Appendix 1 Questionnaire and answers (Potential vendors must fill out this document). The potential vendors must return their answers through EU-Supply not later than 05.12.2025 Depending on the answer’s Banedanmark will have the option to invite potential vendors to a digital meeting via Microsoft Teams. The selection of potential vendors to the meeting will be done through the criteria, to secure a representative of the market, to discuss the answers and possible implications. The topics in Appendix 1 will provide the initial questions for the market dialogue. If the potential vendors are invited for a meeting and find it relevant, they are welcome to send any suggestions for other topics that should be discussed during the market dialogue. The digital meeting will be held, if relevant, 11.12.2025 and 12.12.2025. Banedanmark will, with the invite to the digital meeting, send a Teams link. The duration of the meeting is approx. 1,5 hours (CET+1) in the span of 8-16 Thursday (11.12.2025) and 8-12 Friday (12.12.2025). If the potential vendor suggests meeting times/dates, Banedanmark will try to accommodate those requests.

sig_76f807f0b1843e44a55d.description: The subject of the public contract is the supply, installation and commissioning of a complex interactive projection system for shooting training intended for the training of security forces and other authorised users. The system must form a single functional unit enabling the implementation of shooting training using both live weapons and weapons with laser shooting simulation. The system includes, in particular, projection technology, hit detection equipment, control and evaluation software, audiovisual and communication equipment, as well as all related technical and safety elements necessary for operation in a shooting range environment. The system must allow for the projection of static and dynamic shooting scenarios, real-time hit evaluation, archiving and subsequent analysis of shooting progress, and support for the creation and editing of custom training scenarios by the user. The delivery also includes complete integration into the shooting range area, including the installation, calibration and commissioning of all components, the supply of necessary hardware and software equipment, the provision of safety measures and protection of technologies against the effects of shooting, as well as the supply of related accessories for the implementation of training. The delivery also includes training and maintenance of the system for a period of five (5) years.
sig_76f807f0b1843e44a55d.title: Interactive shooting system

Procedure aimed at concluding a framework agreement 3 in parts for Visit Hungary Nemzeti Turisztikai Szervezet Közhasznú Nonprofit Zrt. for the performance of strategic media agency, digital media agency and market research tasks. In order to achieve the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, the Contracting Authority plans to implement complex communication and media campaigns on domestic and foreign target markets. The aim of the Contracting Authority's communication activity is to promote Hungary for tourism purposes, strengthen inbound tourism from abroad, stimulate domestic tourism, and present the Hungarian tourism offering domestically and internationally. The task of the Winning Tenderer is to perform the tasks specified in the Technical Specification for the Client on the basis of the framework agreement, individual orders, and briefs handed over by the Client. The Contracting Authority wishes to conclude a framework agreement for the performance of strategic media agency tasks up to a net framework amount of 3.200.000.000 HUF. The Contracting Authority undertakes an obligation to call off 70% of the framework amount. In order to achieve the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, the Contracting Authority plans to implement complex communication and media campaigns on domestic and foreign target markets. International tourism advertising campaigns may be implemented in multiple countries, with a different media mix and target group approach per country. The task of the Winning Tenderer is to perform strategic media agency, media planning, media buying, campaign management, reporting, and other auxiliary tasks directly related to media appearances for the Client on the basis of the framework agreement, individual orders, and briefs handed over by the Client. The exact professional content, performance deadline, quantity, technical parameters and individual expectations of the tasks are contained in the individual orders. The Contracting Authority's domestic campaigns are typically implemented with a net campaign spend of the magnitude of 250 million HUF, over an average campaign period of 6–8 weeks. Campaigns of the Contracting Authority affecting target markets outside Hungary are typically implemented with a net campaign spend of the magnitude of 80 million HUF, over an average campaign period of 8–10 weeks. Tasks to be performed in particular: - preparation of a media strategy, integrated media mix and media plan in harmony with the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, - preparation of market, media market, competitor and target group analyses adapted to the campaign's objective, target markets, target groups and channels, - strategic media agency tasks on specified channels - preparation, execution and monitoring of campaigns, campaign management, preparation and execution of media buying tasks, and continuous optimisation of campaigns, - proposal for a KPI system adapted to the nature, objective, channels and target markets of the given campaign, as well as tracking, interpretation and evaluation of campaign performance, with special regard to tourism KPIs - preparation of regular, inter-campaign and campaign-closing reports according to an agreed reporting structure. The Winning Tenderer is obliged to designate one permanent contact person. Detailed requirements set against performance are contained in the technical specification and draft contract.; The Contracting Authority wishes to conclude a framework agreement for the performance of digital media agency tasks up to a net framework amount of 820.000.000 HUF. The Contracting Authority undertakes an obligation to call off 70% of the framework amount. In order to achieve the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, the Contracting Authority plans to implement complex communication and digital media campaigns on domestic and foreign target markets. International tourism digital advertising campaigns may be implemented in multiple countries, with a different digital media mix, targeting logic, platform usage and target group approach per country. The task of the Winning Tenderer is to perform digital media agency, digital media planning, digital media buying, campaign management, optimisation, measurement, analytics, reporting, and other auxiliary tasks directly related to digital media appearances for the CA on the basis of the framework agreement, individual orders, and briefs handed over by the CA. The Contracting Authority's domestic digital campaigns are typically implemented with a net budget of the magnitude of 50–60 million HUF, over an average campaign period of 8–9 weeks. Digital campaigns of the Contracting Authority affecting target markets outside Hungary are typically implemented with a net budget of the magnitude of 50–60 million HUF, over an average campaign period of 8–9 weeks. Tasks to be performed in particular: - formulation of a digital campaign strategy and digital media plan, development of digital targeting, platform and channel proposals, - performance of digital media buying and campaign management tasks, continuous tracking and optimisation of campaign performance, support for measurement and analytical settings, - evaluation and reporting of digital KPIs, (with special regard to tourism relevance) - support for the compilation of performance certification documentation, - preparation of a digital campaign strategy, digital media mix and digital media plan in harmony with the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, - preparation of market, digital media market, competitor and target group analyses adapted to the campaign's objective, target markets, target groups, digital channels and advertising platforms, - performance of media agency tasks on specified channels and platforms, - preparation of digital campaigns, - launching of digital campaigns, campaign management, preparation and execution of digital media buying tasks, and continuous optimisation of campaigns, - establishment, management and operation of an agreed advertising account structure, - support for the establishment, operation and, where necessary, development of the measurement environment related to digital campaigns, - preparation of inter-campaign reports and campaign-closing evaluation. The Winning Tenderer is obliged to designate one permanent contact person. Detailed requirements set against performance are contained in the technical specification and draft contract.;

The Contracting Authority wishes to conclude a framework agreement for the performance of market research tasks up to a net framework amount of 320.000.000 HUF. The CA undertakes an obligation to call off 70% of the framework amount. In order to achieve the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, the CA plans to implement complex communication and media campaigns on domestic and foreign target markets. Research and analysis tasks may also cover domestic and international target markets, different target groups, campaigns, brands, destinations, communication objectives, consumer motivations, media usage characteristics, tourism decisions or campaign effectiveness issues. The CA's research projects are of a mixed nature: they include quantitative research with larger sample sizes directed at Hungary and affecting target markets outside Hungary, primary research affecting multiple target markets, as well as smaller-element qualitative, motivational, service quality, mystery shopping or other decision-supporting research tasks. The Contracting Authority generally performs the implementation of a residential quantitative research of 1000 persons once a year in 10-15 countries, and in addition initiates a minimum of 2 qualitative, small-group focus group researches in Hungary (focus groups are generally implemented with 4–8 groups, with an average participation of 6 persons per group) and manages a nationwide mystery shopping annually with a minimum of 80 trial purchases. The task of the Winning Tenderer is to perform market research, data acquisition, analysis and decision-supporting tasks for the CA on the basis of the framework agreement, individual orders, and briefs handed over by the CA. Tasks to be performed in particular: - preparation, organisation, execution, analysis and documentation of research, data acquisitions, analyses and decision-supporting materials founding, supporting or evaluating marketing and communication activity. - preparation of a research plan or methodological proposal adapted to the given research, data acquisition, analysis or decision-supporting task, - organisation, execution, coordination and control of research data recording, fieldwork or data collection. - processing, checking, cleaning, systematisation, analysis, interpretation of data available as a result of research or data acquisition, and formulation of decision-supporting conclusions, - with the prior approval of the CA, may carry out data purchases, procure syndicated research, or utilise an external data source or study on behalf of the CA, - performing administration related to possible research modifications, data recording changes, cancellations, data purchase or syndicated research limitations, - the Winning Tenderer is obliged to present the results of the given research, data acquisition, analysis or decision-supporting task according to a structure agreed with the Client. The Winning Tenderer is obliged to designate one permanent contact person. Detailed requirements set against performance are contained in the technical specification and draft contract.
sig_77b737912b9b27e0aad5.title: Media agency and market research tasks

sig_77cef8d490f54bd5e1a6.description:
The project comprises the planning and execution of internal audits and security revisions in the area of information security to maintain the information network of the EU Paying Agency Brandenburg-Berlin, which is certified based on BSI IT-Grundschutz in accordance with ISO 27001. The ISO 27001 certification is proof of the Union law eligibility criterion of "security of information systems" of the EU paying agency (Article 1 in conjunction with Annex I point 3 letter B of Delegated Regulation (EU) No 2022/127) and requires the regular execution of internal audits and security revisions in accordance with BSI IT-Grundschutz. Internal personnel resources and competencies for carrying out internal audits are not available, which is why, in accordance with chapter 8.3, BSI standard 200-1, it has been decided to award the execution of the audits to external experts. The previously awarded project with the same project content expires in the year 2026, which is why a multi-year follow-up project is being awarded to ensure continuous and long-term internal auditing until 2030. The subject matter of the project shall be flexibly retrievable auditing services for the information network of the EU paying agency, which consists of the organisational units of the Ministry for Agriculture and Nutrition, Environment and Consumer Protection Brandenburg (MLEUV) and the directly subordinate State Office for Rural Development, Agriculture and Land Consolidation (LELF), as well as the other bodies involved in the paying agency procedure (districts, state forestry enterprise, investment bank and technical service providers), which as outsourcing partners or the components outsourced to them, shall represent the essential audit subjects of the audits. Based on an jointly prepared audit schedule, four audits per year are planned. The project is to be awarded to demonstrably experienced experts in the field of information security revision or ISMS auditing in accordance with BSI IT-Grundschutz. Lot LOT-0001: Internal audits and security revisions to maintain the information security of the EU paying agency in the MLEUV. The contract subject matter comprises the planning and execution of internal audits and security revisions for an information network certified on the basis of BSI IT-Grundschutz in accordance with ISO 27001 and its participating outsourcing partners. The information network to be audited "Operational running of the EU Paying Agency Brandenburg-Berlin" consists of the organisational units of the Ministry for Agriculture and Nutrition, Environment and Consumer Protection of the State of Brandenburg (MLEUV) and the directly subordinate State Office for Rural Development, Agriculture and Land Consolidation (LELF), which perform the professional tasks of approval, control, disbursement, accounting and administration of arrears of subsidy funds of the European Agricultural Guarantee Fund (EAGF), the European Agricultural Fund for Rural Development (EAFRD) and the European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund (EMFAF), as well as the other bodies involved in the paying agency procedure (districts, state forestry enterprise, investment bank and technical service providers), which are treated as outsourcing partners. The essential audit activities are to be carried out for the outsourced components of the information network at the outsourcing partners. With these institutions, a transfer of paying agency tasks has been agreed on the basis of responsibilities ordinances, transfer ordinances or other regulations. Based on a federal-state interface model for EU paying agencies coordinated with the Federal Office for Information Security (BSI for short), the outsourcing relationships are essentially differentiated into: 1. Organisational interfaces (S-O): Institutions that perform transferred tasks of approval and control within the business processes of the paying agency and use central paying agency specialist applications within the information network to fulfil tasks, as they do not provide central paying agency specialist applications themselves and do not operate any specific application environments. In Brandenburg, this currently affects: - 14 approval offices (offices for agriculture) in the districts, - the State Forestry Enterprise (LFB), - the Investment Bank of the State of Brandenburg (ILB). 2. Technical interfaces (S-T): Institutions of the technical operation of the central paying agency specialist applications and systems as well as data storage. In Brandenburg, this currently affects: - the central Brandenburg IT service provider (ZIT-BB), - Land Surveying and Basic Geographic Information Brandenburg (LGB) - init AG for the operation of an application procedure. A medium three-digit number of persons work in the information network. Every year, several million euros in a three-digit amount of EU, federal and state funds are administered. The paying agency specialist applications essentially comprise client/server and web applications, for which an IT system landscape consisting of terminal, web, application and database servers is deployed. Use is made by administrative units using virtual clients via the state administration network of the State of Brandenburg. Applicants access the online application systems operated in a demilitarised zone (DMZ) via the internet. In coordination with the client and based on the documentation of the ISMS, the contractor shall draw up and carry out a multi-year audit schedule. The planning and execution of the audits takes place with the participation of the information security officer of the EU paying agency. Based on empirical values, four audits per year are to be carried out with different procedure participants respectively, which should be flexibly retrievable.

Per audit, the workload in person-days (PD) is estimated at approx. 10 PD. The contract subject matter comprises the audits for the years 2027 up to and including 2030. The client reserves the right, with the award of optional services, if contractor capacities are available, to commission further audits in accordance with the schedule of services for the year 2026. Accordingly, the following scope of work is expected - 2026: 2 audits - 20 PD (optional, upon availability) - 2027: 4 audits - 40 PD - 2028: 4 audits - 40 PD - 2029: 4 audits - 40 PD - 2030: 4 audits - 40 PD - Total: 18 audits - 180 PD The execution of the audits should take place along the relevant standards for audits and security revisions according to the BSI IT-Grundschutz methodology (BSI auditing scheme or the guideline for IS revisions based on IT-Grundschutz). The client reserves the right to optionally commission the contractor in the year 2026 with up to two (2) further audits for two (2) audit subjects in accordance with the schedule of services.
sig_77cef8d490f54bd5e1a6.title: Internal audits and security revisions to maintain the information security of the EU paying agency in the MLEUV

sig_7878a26982273c6ddef9.description: The objective of this procurement is to secure a modern, cloud-hosted, configurable off-the-shelf Grant Management System capable of supporting the full grant lifecycle for applicants, assessors, panellists, and Arts Council staff. The solution will provide a secure and accessible digital platform for application management, assessment workflows, award administration, post-award monitoring, reporting, and integration with the Arts Council’s existing Finance Management System. The organisation's strategic preference is for a solution that requires minimal custom development and can be configured using standard platform functionality. The replacement programme will be delivered through a phased implementation approach centred on the successful completion of a Proof of Concept (PoC) using a live Arts Council funding programme. This approach is intended to validate vendor capability, system performance, user experience, and organisational readiness before progressing to full production deployment. The Arts Council is seeking a long-term technology partner capable of delivering a proven solution while supporting a structured, low-risk transition from the existing environment. The new system must support bilingual service delivery (Irish and English), modern digital user experiences, robust security controls, workflow automation, management reporting, and interoperability with current and future finance platforms. The solution should also align with public sector best practice, including cloud-first principles, accessibility requirements, data protection obligations, cybersecurity standards, and emerging NIS2 requirements.
sig_7878a26982273c6ddef9.title: Provision of a Cloud-Based Grant Management System

sig_7893b4cf744ecf10e15f.description: GENERAL Fimea has started preparing for the procurement of the Fimea.fi website renewal. Fimea is a central agency under the Ministry of Social Affairs and Health that acts as the licensing and supervisory authority for medicines, medical devices, blood and tissue products, biobanks, and operators in the pharmaceutical sector intended for humans or animals. As part of the preparation of the procurement, the contracting authority is conducting a market dialogue. The actual procurement will be implemented as an open procurement procedure. Please note that this is a market survey notice and not a call for tenders. This market survey notice does not yet request tenders. Participation in the market dialogue is completely voluntary. Participation or non-participation in the market dialogue does not affect a tenderer's opportunities to participate in the procurement procedure to be implemented later. The market dialogue does not oblige anyone to participate in the actual tendering, nor does it exclude anyone from it. PRELIMINARY DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCUREMENT The aim of the procurement is to renew the Fimea.fi website and content management system so that the public site is user-friendly, accessible and supports the management of up-to-date content. The procurement will preliminarily be implemented using a hybrid model consisting of three separate parts: 1. Service design service, expert work • Design of user journeys and concepts • Definition of user interface and information architecture • Visual plan • Architecture description and solution description • Accessibility plan 2. New content management system and website implementation • Ready-to-use content management system (using SaaS model) • Renewed site structure and user interface • Language versions (Finnish, Swedish and English) • Content management features (preview, scheduling, version history) • Integrations and technical interfaces • Accessibility and data protection • Commissioning, training and documentation 3. Maintenance and further development Fixed-price maintenance: • Includes continuous usability of the service, security updates, backups, monitoring and SLA services. • Fixed monthly price for the contract period Hourly-rate minor development: • Includes small changes and additional features according to the agile model. • Invoicing according to actual work at an hourly rate. Both parts will be implemented as a SaaS service, where the supplier is responsible for technical management and continuity. The service design and definition phase as well as the implementation project are preliminarily scheduled for the years Q2/2026 – Q2/2027 and the maintenance and further development phase from Q3/2027 onwards. The website will be renewed at the same time in terms of appearance and structure in a way that better serves users. The basic content of the website will publish text, images and attachments. Contents will also include embedded videos or audio files. Embedded audio/video files are hosted on other services. The contents (articles and podcasts) of the Sic web magazine are intended to be integrated as part of the Fimea.fi entity as part of the website implementation. However, the web magazine will not be brought to the Fimea.fi site as a separate entity. MARKET DIALOGUE The market dialogue is intended for companies interested in tendering, and it includes commenting on preliminary tender documents before the publication of the call for tenders. Written commenting on the tender documents is preliminarily planned to be organised around the turn of January and February 2026. The publication of the actual call for tenders is preliminarily planned for February 2026. The information provided in this notice and in the market dialogue itself is preliminary and may change as the preparation progresses. The announced schedule of the procurement is also preliminary and may change as the preparation of the procurement progresses. Please note that the market survey does not include a question & answer phase. Companies interested in the procurement are requested to register in accordance with the instructions described below. REGISTRATION FOR THE MARKET DIALOGUE Companies interested in the procurement are requested to report their contact details by email to the address kilpailutus@hansel.fi. The registration shall be headed as follows: "Fimea.fi verkkosivu-uudistus – Ilmoittautuminen markkinavuoropuheluun". State in the message the name of your organisation and the email address of the contact person to whom the draft tender documents will be delivered. sig_78c5b72c81dbabda0bf0.description: Industrial biotechnology offers enormous potential for sustainable growth by replacing fossil raw materials with renewable biological resources, achieving climate targets and strengthening competitiveness. Germany is well positioned in the research and development of bioeconomic products and processes. Previous funding measures by other departments and the federal states show that bioeconomic products and processes can be implemented on a laboratory scale. However, there is a lack of broad implementation of bioeconomic products and processes on an industrial scale. Therefore, to support the transformation of the economy into a sustainable, climate-neutral economic model, the funding programme "Industrial Bioeconomy" was initiated, which started with the entry into force of the "Directive for funding the use and construction of demonstration plants for industrial biotechnology" of 16 December 2020 on 29 December 2020 (BAnz AT 28.12.2020 B2). This funding guideline was superseded by the "Funding guideline for the establishment of an industrial bioeconomy through the further development and scaling of bio-based processes and the establishment of regional innovation clusters" (BAnz AT 27.09.2024 B1), published in the Federal Law Gazette on 27 September 2024. The aim of the programme is to unlock the potential of new bio-based processes for industry and to transfer sustainable products into broad application. In order to reduce the economic and technical risks of development and market launch, the funding is intended to demonstrate the potential of bio-based products and processes at an early stage. Projects are funded that have a high potential for industrial application, the creation of new value creation and new jobs, strengthen the market position of the participating companies and make a relevant contribution to sustainability. sig_78e20f1ffea36bd743b3.description: The National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) seeks to advance its mission by supporting multidisciplinary, consortium-based research using precision systems biology approaches to uncover links among chronic illnesses, infectious diseases and microbiomes. There is an urgent scientific and clinical need to understand the pathways by which infections lead to chronic lifelong health issues or alternatively, how long-term illnesses might predispose or exacerbate acute infections. The objective is to harness cutting-edge technologies along with longitudinal patient cohorts and biobank data for comprehensive analysis of genetic, environmental, and lifestyle factors leading to advances in prevention and treatment strategies for both chronic and infectious diseases. The cutting-edge technologies may include multi-omics, computational modeling, artificial intelligence, organoid-based validation systems, and integration of real-world data, alongside improved access to digital health records and advanced clinical informatics tools. The goal is to generate meaningful insights into disease progression and host-pathogen interactions. Grant authorities that allow NIAID to forecast this opportunity are as follows: Sections 301 and 405 of the Public Health Service Act as amended (42 USC 241 and 284) and under Federal Regulations 42 CFR Part 52 and 2 CFR Part 200.
sig_78e20f1ffea36bd743b3.title: Precision and Systems Biology to Uncover the Link Between Chronic and Infectious Diseases

sig_7922b435cef825e3fe8f.description: This is a request for information, which is not a prior information notice, a contract notice or a call for tenders. The purpose of the request for information is to survey the market and collect information regarding the subject of the procurement for a future tendering process. Responding to the request for information is not a prerequisite for participating in the tendering process. To ensure the success of the future tendering process, it is important that tenderers provide the contracting authority with the requested information as extensively as possible. This request for information is used to clarify the supply available on the market regarding substitute management systems and suppliers. A substitute management system enables a single centralised service channel for the sudden substitute needs of professionals. With the help of a substitute management system, we want to streamline substitute management processes. The need is to find a modern and user-friendly, off-the-shelf SaaS system intended for the management and coordination of substitutes, as well as for the notification and booking of temporary work shifts. In addition, we want to improve and modernise the user experience of our substitute management systems so that the applicant experience and communication are improved. The systems must be integrable via standard interfaces with, among other things, the client organisation's user information and access rights management service. The objectives of the services are equal accessibility, timeliness and continuity. The goal of the procurement is to move from heavy services to proactive and preventive services, whereby the effectiveness of the services can be improved. We offer system solutions to our clients in the social and health care sector as well as the municipal sector. The scope of the future procurement, the procurement method and the parties will be specified as the preparation of the call for tenders progresses. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCUREMENT The goal of the procurement is to find a system: - that is an easy-to-use, off-the-shelf SaaS solution - that can be integrated into the client organisation's AD and reporting environment via open interfaces - that is information secure and takes data protection into account - whose supplier has a clear implementation model that includes extensive documentation and guidance for the client and contracting organisation - that can be used on mobile devices and via a browser. In addition to the system procurement, the procurement includes connection interfaces to other systems, licences, a delivery project, maintenance and support for off-the-shelf software, as well as other separately ordered expert services, for example, the planning and implementation of system change and development needs and development projects. The solution must scale to the organisational structures of social and health service organisations and the municipal sector. The implementation of the solution must be based on generally used standards and system-independent interfaces. The solution to be procured must function as part of the existing technical and functional environment. The solution includes at least two separate environments in terms of its functions; production and test/training environments, which are identical in their basic structure. OPERATING ENVIRONMENT The following are descriptions of the operating environments of the organisations related to the request for information, which are requested to be used in describing the functionality and pricing model. Users of the data transmission system are, for example, users from wellbeing services counties and municipal organisations. Users of the information systems are also stakeholders and external users. RESPONDING TO THE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION The request for information must be answered by 25.9.2025 at 12:00. Responding takes place by email to the address hankinnat@istekki.fi. Please head your message as follows: "Markkinavuoropuhelu: Sijaisvälitysjärjestelmä" (Market dialogue: Substitute management system). Responses to the Questions attachment of the request for information must also be submitted with the response. You may also attach, for example, brochures to the response. Based on the responses received, Istekki Oy will select 3–5 suppliers to present their solutions in one-hour Teams meetings. The meeting between the selected respondent, Istekki and the representatives of the clients will be recorded. The information provided at the request for information stage will be treated as confidential. Please indicate in your request for information response which of the times below suit you best: Mon 29.9. at 10 – 11 Mon 29.9. at 13 – 14 Mon 29.9. at 14 – 15 Tue 30.9. at 11 – 12 Tue 30.9. at 12 – 13 Tue 30.9. at 13 – 14 The times will be confirmed supplier-specifically after the response time for the request for information. Instead of these deadlines, the deadlines in the request for information document shall be followed.

sig_7930cd76349c9ff07931.description: Shropshire Council is undertaking Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) to understand the current market for digital solutions that support unpaid carers. This engagement will help inform the Council’s future commissioning approach before any decision is made about whether to tender, use an existing compliant route, develop an alternative model, or take no further procurement action. Shropshire Council has an established Unpaid Carer Support offer. Recently this has become an all-age offer supporting Young Carers and Parent Carers. The Unpaid Carers portal will be an online offer which will be available to Unpaid Carers 24/7 throughout the journey of their caring role. We are aware there are a large proportion of people who do not identify as an Unpaid Carer, we envisage the portal will support with that identification and will provide relevant up to date information to support families in a preventative manner. Any proposed solution should offer the following support: Increase the identification recognition and early interventions for unpaid Carers Delay and reduce the need to access high-cost statutory provision Improve accessibility to information, advice and guidance, improve links and signposting to services that are already available nationally, regionally and locally. Support Unpaid Carers to access self-help and self-management support to reduce the need for Unpaid Carers crisis interventions. Include access to Unpaid Carers 'self-assessment' focused on individualised outcomes The solution should have the capacity to collect and produce relative data regarding demographics, ethnicity, age range as well as information such as when and where the portal is accessed.
