sig_85bec1a283e55de29bb2.description: Vantaan kaupunki is planning the procurement of a new cultural heritage system to replace the current collection management system (Kirsti), which was implemented in 2014. The current system is technically obsolete, slow, and difficult to develop. The goal is a modern, easy-to-use, and efficient solution that supports museum operations, cultural heritage management, and digital transition. The system must support, among other things, object, image, AV, paper, and cultural environment archives, a reference library, actor information, and press clippings. Integrations are required for Finna, Finto, MapInfo, Matti, the Finnish Heritage Agency's spatial data, and the PAS service. Key features: efficient search, clarity, ease of use, and compliance with GDPR requirements. Users: Museum staff, consultants, authorities, collection service customers, and the public via Finna. Targeted benefits: Better availability of information, increased work efficiency, reduction of unnecessary work, and improvement of processes. Strategic importance: supports the digital transition, has a broad impact, and generates value for over 10 000 residents.

sig_8608455ddad914e0e75c.description: This notice (PIN) announces a public market consultation and provides information on a planned pre-commercial procurement (PCP) on the subject of the "Low-Voltage Toolkit". The project responds to the need for a cost-effective, scalable, platform-independent and user-friendly toolkit for active distribution network management in low-voltage networks – particularly for small and medium-sized distribution network operators and municipal utilities. The toolkit is intended to include the following core functions: (1) Visualisation of the low-voltage network through automated data integration, processing and modelling, which brings together measurement data, network documentation and external information (e.g. weather and market data). (2) Reliable low-voltage state estimation (LV DSSE), which delivers robust statements on voltages, currents and loads even with low measurement density and in near real time. (3) Automated topology detection, which detects and corrects erroneous or incomplete network diagrams and also correctly maps complex urban structures. (4) Forecasting models that identify bottlenecks and voltage violations at an early stage and incorporate external information (e.g. weather and market data). (5) Comprehensible decision support for network operators, including via user-friendly visualisations, recommendations for action and warnings that can be integrated into existing workflows. (6) Semi-automated congestion management with transparent workflows ("Suggest – Evaluate – Confirm – Execute") instead of fully automated network operation. (7) Plug-and-play approach for integration into a large proportion of existing infrastructures at distribution network operators; the tools are intended to be modularly introduceable (e.g. initially only a topology detection module or state estimator), in contrast to current solutions which often require extensive hardware conversions and high investments. Those addressed are in particular small and medium-sized distribution network operators, municipal utilities, manufacturers of network control and planning software, data platform providers as well as research institutions with relevant expertise. Further information on the upcoming public market consultation and the planned PCP can be found here http://go.fzj.de/2eVf9 in the German language.
sig_8608455ddad914e0e75c.title: Pre-commercial procurement (PCP) of research and development services for a toolkit for active low-voltage distribution network management.

sig_86162daacf1775ecac5d.description: The Norwegian Defence Materiel Agency (FMA) is the contracting authority and responsible for implementing the procurement. FMA is a part of the defence sector, directly under the Ministry of Defence (FD). FMA shall ensure that the Norwegian Armed Forces and other entities in the defence sector have access to cost efficient and secure material and services in line with approved long-term plans. FMA ́s main assignments are planning, procurement, management and disposal of material for the Norwegian Armed Forces and other departments under FD. Organisational reasons can be required during the contract period to transfer the resource to Cyber Defence ́s IT Department (CIT) DRIV. DRIV is responsible for the technical operation and further development (DEVSECOPS) of the Joint Integrated Management System (FIF). FIF is a SAP ERP system integrated with a number of other different applications. Internal processes are based on flexible frameworks (Scrum, SAFE), the Security Act and different industry standards for safety and ITIL for operation. DRIV consists of approx. 150 persons, most of whom are located in Oslo. Both employees and consultants staff the organisation. The aim of this notice is to fill the role of solution expert in Project P1160 'Critical Upgrade of ERP' and DRIV. The consultant shall take care of the role within the discipline SAP Defense and Security (D&S). The role can involve cooperation with other departments and/or projects in the Norwegian Armed Forces.

sig_8619e337dca715e1a15c.description: The subject of the procurement is an appointment booking and video conferencing system (hereinafter also the "System") for use by the City of Mikkeli's customer services. The System to be procured must enable the management of customer service appointments for the City of Mikkeli's employment services and customer meetings via video conferencing through a single system. The objective is to procure a SaaS ready-made solution that is easy to use, meets data protection and other legislative requirements, and can be implemented on a rapid schedule. The procurement seeks a comprehensive appointment booking and video conferencing system as a ready-made solution that offers pre-built functions for managing appointments and conducting video conferences. A ready-made solution refers to a finished end product that can be configured for the Subscriber's use without the procurement involving the development of a completely bespoke system. In the initial phase, the System will be for the use of the City of Mikkeli's employment services. Later, the City of Mikkeli must have the option to expand the use of the System to other units. The procurement seeks one (1) party with overall responsibility to supply the System as a SaaS service. The overall service must include the necessary software interfaces, programs, firmware, licences, and maintenance and support services in accordance with the call for tenders and its appendices. The contract period is estimated to begin in November 2026 and the contract is valid until further notice.

Braunschweig Beteiligungen GmbH (BSBG) is a wholly owned subsidiary of the City of Braunschweig. At the same time, it is the parent company of a group and holds a number of subsidiaries that are active in the field of services of general interest. With currently twelve employees, BSBG essentially provides commercial services for its subsidiary, Braunschweiger Verkehrs-GmbH (BSVG). Braunschweiger Verkehrs-GmbH (BSVG) is a wholly owned subsidiary of BSBG, which provides public transport services in Braunschweig with around 780 employees (of which around 520 are in driving service). BSVG has the "Lindenberg" bus depot as well as the "Am Hauptgüterbahnhof" depot for the light rail system, including the administrative headquarters. sig_868a12b403c32ff5ee4a.description: The subject of the service is the design, development, implementation, commissioning and initial optimisation of an AI-supported, multimodal visitor guide for use in the tourist visitor operations of Westfälischer Zoologischer Garten Münster GmbH. The contractor's service covers the complete project lifecycle from conception through development, piloting and rollout to productive operation, including support, monitoring, security, optimisation and operational services. Lot LOT-0001: Development and implementation of an AI-supported visitor guide. The AI technology is the heart of the SKADI project. As a digital system, it is intended to include functions such as barrier-free communication and precise navigation in the smallest of spaces. In addition to strengthening accessibility and digitalisation, the system helps to convey important topics such as sustainability and species protection through its function as a digital learning offer - on a regional and international basis. Furthermore, the system uses artificial intelligence and machine learning algorithms to analyse user behaviour and suggests suitable experiences based on preferences and current location data. In addition, the system enables the networking of tourist / natural history offers through the integration of specifically named sources. Users can not only obtain individual information about animal species, habitats, protected areas and events, but can also design things themselves via the digital guide, for example.

sig_86a204079f2c82c65933.description:
WISTA stands for Wissenschafts- und Wirtschaftsstandort Adlershof and is a state-of-the-art technology park in the Adlershof district of Berlin (Treptow-Köpenick borough). It is considered one of the most advanced high-tech parks in Europe and is a central hub for science, business, and start-ups. WISTA Adlershof is a location with an area of approx. 4,2 km2, approx. 1.300 companies, research institutions, and university institutes with 28.000 employees. The WISTA Management GmbH acts as a site developer, service provider, and economic promoter. It supports companies, research institutions, and start-ups at the site and fosters innovation and growth in the region. In addition to its real estate portfolio, WISTA possesses its own campus network, which consists of a high-performance cable network as well as a 5G infrastructure. The network has been continuously expanded and technologically developed since 1998 – from classic telephony and data services to Gigabit and 10G connections, cloud and UCC integration, campus-wide Wi-Fi and IoT applications, through to local 5G and current network 4.0 topics. It thus forms an essential digital infrastructure of the campus and is the subject of the expression of interest procedure. The attractiveness of the campus network stems from its established telecommunications infrastructure at a dynamically growing high-tech location. The network has an existing customer base, established line routes and network nodes, as well as redundant carrier connections. Additional development prospects arise from the continuous expansion of the campus through new buildings, the expansion potential for cloud, security, and UCC services, as well as the addition of a local 5G campus network. The campus network thus offers a resilient infrastructural foundation with further economic and technological growth potential. The reasons for the sale by WISTA are a strategic further development of the campus network by a specialised provider with qualified personnel and the necessary expertise. Subject of sale: Passive infrastructure (fibre optic, copper, conduits, manholes, cable distribution cabinets, building connections) Active infrastructure (switches, routers, servers, telecommunications system) Customer contracts (insofar as transferable, consent/transfers still to be checked) Frequency allocation 5G (not alienable, subsequent use/transfer still to be checked from a regulatory perspective, application for own allocation required) Land/line rights (insofar as transferable, easements/permissions still to be checked) Software/licences (insofar as transferable, licence terms still to be checked) Cable network: The WISTA campus network at the science and business location Adlershof forms the central communication infrastructure for voice and data services in the core area of the technology park. It currently serves around 400 customers as well as approx. 4.400 participants in the voice sector and is therefore an essential location factor for Germany's largest science and technology park. The existing infrastructure includes a high-performance cable duct system, a line network based on copper and fibre optics with a total length of almost 20 kilometres, as well as a Gigabit Ethernet backbone. Technically, fibre optic backbone connections, single-mode and multi-mode fibre optic cables, copper cables, copper cross-cables, and FM cables with 100 double cores are used in particular. At the active network and services level, the campus network includes transmission and switching equipment for voice and data communication, routing/switching components, data core and access areas, network gateways to wide area networks, as well as a communication network consisting of communication systems from the manufacturer Unify. The users' existing voice and data infrastructure is connected to the network; some users are connected via LAN ports under 100 Mbit/s or VDSL, while other users have connections from 100 Mbit/s. The WAN connection is designed to be redundant with at least two external carriers and has two redundant gateways with 100 Gbit/s. The campus network is particularly interesting as an established, operator-capable infrastructure with an existing customer base, available line routes, documented network gateways, and development potential. The future operator is to operate, maintain, further develop, and actively market the network to users on their own responsibility. In addition to the existing copper, fibre optic, and fibre infrastructure, the existing customers, the available telecommunications and data network components, the expansion potential at the growing Adlershof location, and the possibility of introducing new cloud, security, VoIP, and UCC services are of value. 5G network: The WISTA 5G campus network is designed as a local private 5G campus network at the science and business location Adlershof. It serves as a supplement to the existing cable infrastructure and is to be gradually expanded at outdoor and indoor locations. Initial expansion has been carried out in the area of Albert-Einstein-Straße 16 (central outdoor location) as well as in the showroom/a:head context (indoor location). The regulatory basis for the 5G infrastructure is a local frequency allocation by the Federal Network Agency for the frequency range 3.700–3.800 MHz. The allocation holder is WISTA Management GmbH. The allocated bandwidth is 100 MHz; the frequency allocation is limited until 20.02.2030. The allocation area covers an area of approx. 0,873273 km2. Technologically, the 5G infrastructure is based on a Nokia DAC/NDAC Medium+ environment with 5G standalone architecture, Edge Core, NDAC manager, Nokia AirScale components, HPE Edge servers, router and switching components, and SIM kit. WISTA Management GmbH intends to sell its cable network and 5G campus network at the science and business location Adlershof.

Only 99 years were stated as the duration because the announcement platform mandates the specification of a limited period. The sale is permanent and is not intended to be reversed after 99 years.

Any interested economic operator has the right to request clarifications/additional information regarding the contract documents 22 days before the deadline set for the submission of tenders. The contracting authority shall respond clearly and completely to all requests for clarifications/additional information regarding the contract documents on the 12-th day before the tender submission deadline. The contracting authority will not respond to requests for clarifications submitted after the set deadline. Description of the products to be purchased and their destination: Processing and storage architecture Complex monitoring and storage solution Train traffic monitoring solution Processing and storage architecture A central component and a local component are provided. The initial architecture of the applications within the IRIS system was conceived in the context of activities distributed across railway locations throughout Romania to a radial topology network implemented with SDH technology and low transfer speed (32 kb/s for small work points and up to 1 Mb/s for large work points). For this reason, the applications were designed with a distributed architecture (client components on users' workstations, local servers) or with the elimination of the process/services layer. With technological evolution, data transmission speeds on the RENTRAD network have increased to a min. of 10 Mbps for locations with 1-2 workstations. In this way, conditions were created for the consolidation of operations in the central datacenter while maintaining local architectures in the regional agencies of Societatea Informatică Feroviară SA. The local architectures will implement virtualisation solutions and will be used for process/service servers and for the administration of regional IT infrastructure. In defining the requirements for the technical specifications, several objectives were pursued: - The architecture will be implemented in the form of several medium virtualisation clusters; - The virtualisation solutions were chosen according to the nature of the hosted applications (Oracle Virtualization for the Oracle environment, Hyper-V for the Windows application environment, and RedHat OpenShift for the containerised staging environment); - Separation of production and development/testing/training environments into distinct clusters in order to ensure safe testing conditions in the event of firmware updates; Use of virtualisation platforms that allow the implementation of multi-tenant solutions with isolation. In this way, zones with different security levels can be implemented on each cluster (critical production environments, development environments, testing workflows); - Separation of the storage platform into two components: - high-performance storage (all-flash, at least 4 controllers, NVMe transfer, high transfer rate, block only) for the production environment, - storage with a classical architecture (low transfer rate, low disk speed, large capacity, block and file) for historical data, cluster for DMZ and repository; - All servers will be of the enterprise class but with a general architecture so that they can be easily replaced in the event of a failure; - Network equipment must integrate into the architecture in operation in the central datacenter. The local component consists of two servers each, installed in the data rooms of the regional IT agencies, a NAS-type storage device and equipment. A NAS-type storage device identical to those in the regional agencies will be installed in the Informatică Feroviară datacenter and is intended for saving operational information, service documentation, and intermediate data. The solutions must have capacities for capacity expansion. Complex monitoring and cybersecurity solution The components of the solution must ensure the following functionalities: - Communications infrastructure monitoring: - Ensuring network visibility in the core zone and the datacenter router zone, - Monitoring traffic information in the core zone and the datacenter router zone; - Protecting the internal network through detection and response solutions against cyber attacks with a local sandbox environment; - Increasing the security level of essential services by ensuring: - Access management for privileged users (system and database administrators, content administrators, users with access to confidential and critical information); - Database access monitoring; - Vulnerability management; - Access control towards the TSM-ERTMS network; - Security information and event management (SIEM). Train traffic tracking solution This solution is addressed to the technical personnel within CNCFR involved in train traffic programming and tracking activities as well as to those in the railway traffic safety compartments. The following components are included: - Workstations for CNCFR personnel involved in the process of programming and tracking train traffic and in railway traffic safety; - Integrated system for the retrieval, display, and management of video sources which will retrieve information from the traffic tracking subsystem; - Videoconferencing solution. The products requested for the IT infrastructure targeted within this project create a computing platform with a complex central architecture and local (regional) architecture that allows the implementation of a high security level. Contract duration: 84 months (60 months representing the warranty period) from the date of signing the contract by both parties. The estimated value of 110.552.200,00 lei excluding VAT is broken down as follows: - 99.552.200,00 lei excluding VAT for IT products (hardware and software components) -11.000.000,00 lei excluding VAT pt.

installation, commissioning, integration and testing services.

sig_885f62654a70046ee804.description: Heka is extensively renewing its information systems in the coming years. The most central objectives for all system development are improving the customer experience, digitising operating methods, and improving the quality of information supporting decision-making. The subject of this procurement is accounting and internal accounting, as well as accounts payable solutions, the related implementation project, and ongoing maintenance service. In addition, a budgeting system may be added to the procurement later based on a framework agreement. The solution package will be implemented at Heka and Heka's subsidiary, Kiinteistö Oy Laivalahdentori. The goal is a so-called off-the-shelf software solution that covers Heka's needs. The primary objective is to procure the solution as a cloud or SaaS service. The solution must enable flexible integrations with systems outside the procured solution. Systems already in use and the renewing solutions must function side-by-side as a whole, relying on the existing technical environment where necessary. It must be possible to transfer the data required in the solution from source systems and to source systems via a data warehouse. Some data may be transferred directly between the source system and the procured solution. The procured solution must enable the transfer of master data with a master data system outside the procurement in both directions. With this request for information, suppliers are invited to a market dialogue regarding questions related to the procurement. The goal of the request for information is to obtain comprehensive information regarding the procurement so that a potential call for tenders can be carried out as appropriately as possible. This request for information is not a call for tenders, and it does not bind Heka to publish a call for tenders later. The contracting authority does not commit to carrying out the call for tenders in the described manner. All information and requirements presented in the request for information and its attached materials regarding the planned procurement are still preliminary at this stage and may change. Responding to the request for information does not bind the supplier, and responding to the request for information is not a prerequisite for participating in a potential call for tenders to be published later. The contracting authority may use the information received through the request for information in the planning of the procurement. The information collected through the request for information will remain confidential. The goal is to launch the procurement procedure during the spring of 2026. A contract notice will be published regarding the procurement. We ask you to familiarise yourself with the attached appendices (01-02) and to respond to the questions presented in the "Questions" document (appendix 03). Please also indicate in the document whether you would be willing to present the solution you are offering via Teams. We ask you to send the completed "Questions" appendix 03 as well as the "Requirements" appendix 02 by 7.1.2026 at 15.00 by email to hankinnat@hekaoy.fi.

sig_88fe649111a131b35915.description: The subject of this tender is the procurement of a central, high-performance, scalable and highly available backup infrastructure for Magdeburg University Hospital. The aim of the tender is to provide a future-proof and demand-oriented expandable central backup solution that enables reliable backup as well as fast and reliable recovery of the business-critical and medically relevant data and IT systems arising at Magdeburg University Hospital. The solution to be procured must take into account the requirements for secure, highly available and permanently available operation in a KRITIS-relevant environment and thus make a significant contribution to the operational safety, fail-safe operation and resilience of the IT infrastructure of Magdeburg University Hospital. The overall solution to be procured is to consist of four coordinated system components: • a high-performance all-flash backup appliance for processing large amounts of data and a high number of parallel backup and restore processes, • a highly available backup storage system as the primary backup target with integrated deduplication function, • a high-performance enterprise rack server as a Veeam backup server as well as • two appropriately dimensioned enterprise rack servers as Veeam backup proxies. The backup infrastructure is to be designed in such a way that it takes into account the existing and foreseeable future requirements of Magdeburg University Hospital. In addition to the delivery of the required hardware and software, including all components and licences required for intended operation, the scope of services also includes the professional installation, configuration and integration of the overall solution into the existing IT infrastructure of Magdeburg University Hospital. Furthermore, the scope of services includes the commissioning of the overall solution as well as the execution of the required functional, performance and acceptance tests. The contractor must provide a fully functional and ready-for-operation overall solution that complies with the requirements laid down in the specification of services and the schedule of services. All services are to be provided in compliance with the legal, regulatory and technical requirements applicable at the time of service provision as well as the relevant norms and standards. Lot LOT-0000: Central backup system. Procurement of a central, high-performance, scalable and highly available backup infrastructure for Magdeburg University Hospital. The specific functional requirements result from the schedule of services.
sig_88fe649111a131b35915.title: Procurement of a central backup system

sig_88febc65a127ab508f9e.description: University of Limerick is seeking to procure an enterprise-level, cloud-based Systematic Review Management Platform to support researchers, academics, students, librarians and research support staff in conducting high-quality evidence synthesis activities across the institution. The proposed solution must provide an integrated end-to-end workflow for systematic reviews and related evidence synthesis methodologies, including citation management, screening, full-text review, data extraction, risk of bias assessment, collaboration, reporting and publication-ready outputs. The platform should facilitate efficient collaboration between internal and external researchers, provide enterprise-grade administration and reporting capabilities, and support recognised methodologies such as systematic reviews, scoping reviews, rapid reviews, mixed-methods reviews and meta-analyses. The successful Tenderer will be required to deliver a fully managed Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) solution, including implementation, training, ongoing support, systematic review methodological expertise, security and compliance assurances, and enterprise-level service management. The solution must align with the University's information governance, security, accessibility and architectural requirements, while providing value for money and supporting the University's strategic ambition to strengthen research excellence and evidence-informed decision-making across the institution.
sig_88febc65a127ab508f9e.title: UL1084 Enterprise-level Systematic Review Management Platform to the University of Limerick

sig_89acec772031c0972bea.description: The subject of the framework agreement for the procurement is the provision, implementation, and configuration of a web-based, audit-proof, and configurable specialist application for the funding management of Netzwerk Universitätsmedizin NUM GmbH (NUM). The scope of services comprises in particular software provision, hosting, and technical operation by the contractor, setup and customising, data migration, interfaces, and exports including system-neutral transfer to the financial software selected at a later date, a documented API, support, maintenance, training, and documentation. The subject of the framework agreement for the procurement is the provision, implementation, and configuration of a web-based, audit-proof, and configurable software solution for the funding management of Netzwerk Universitätsmedizin GmbH (NUM). The solution must digitally map the funding processes from application through review, approval, contract creation, payment request, and interim and final reports. NUM is in an organisational transition phase. Previous processes are partially connected to existing structures of Charité, external project management agency processes, SharePoint or file shares, Excel tables, PDF documents, and easyOnline/XML data. In future, the office is to establish its own structures for processing, reviewing, and documenting funding processes. The software must support both administrative processing and review (currently the Administration, Finance, and Controlling team) and specialist processing and review (currently the Science Management team). The respective reviews take place in parallel, sequentially, or consecutively depending on the process. Input masks, checklists, review notes, task lists, and status logic must therefore be able to traceably depict both review perspectives. The software does not execute the actual payment order, bank execution, or direct retrieval from the Federal Treasury. However, it must provide the data required for forwarding the funds in a structured and system-independent manner. Since the client's financial software will only be selected after this procurement, the technical transfer must be possible via at least a documented, configurable exchange format. The concrete target format and field assignment will be agreed upon in the implementation project after the financial software is selected. The actual retrieval of financial funds from the Federal Treasury and the bank execution take place outside the software. The provision of the retrieval data package and the technical implementation of the agreed data exchange are part of the scope of services. The subject of the tender is an integrated specialist application for funding management with which administrative and specialist review, processing, and decision-making processes can be fully digitally mapped. Document management is a central component of this specialist application and must ensure the process-related linking, structured storage, versioning, management, and retrievability of documents. What is being sought is therefore neither a pure document repository nor an isolated form system, but an end-to-end funding management solution. Insofar as products, procedures, or manufacturers are named in this specification of services, this is done exclusively to describe the required scope of services; equivalent solutions are permitted. Existing target systems of the client determined before publication, or those determined prior to publication, are clearly named in the procurement documents, including the required integration scope.
sig_89acec772031c0972bea.title: Grant management software

sig_8a2ff45572d92c9c256c.description: MARKET DIALOGUE The subject matter of the market dialogue is the expert services in information security and data protection under preparation as well as the assessment services of conformity assessment bodies for information security for the needs of Väylävirasto. BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES Väylävirasto is putting out to tender the following two expert service procurements: Expert services in information security and data protection This tender procures experts to support the safeguarding and development of information and cyber security, data protection and information management of Väylävirasto. Väylävirasto has several different administrative or technical projects and undertakings underway in which operations are developed and existing information systems are renewed or new ones are ordered. What all these projects and undertakings have in common is that they must implement information security and the fulfilment of central government information security requirements in a manner suitable for the organisation. The subject matter of the procurement is information and cybersecurity consulting and auditing services. The work takes place largely in a multi-supplier environment, but also as internal consulting for individual projects or undertakings. Information security audits are also carried out regularly in the supplier environment. In addition, an assessment is made of, among other things, the impact of information security instructions directed at central government on the projects and operations of Väylävirasto. In addition to the office environment, the subject matter of the procurement is the infrastructures managed by Väylävirasto (Finnish Transport Infrastructure Agency), i.e. state-owned road, rail and waterways. Each transport mode has its own cyber security development needs, which in certain respects may differ significantly from each other. The aim of the procurement is to obtain a partner for Väylävirasto with which the organisation's and the various transport modes' information and cybersecurity development can be carried out. Assessment services of conformity assessment bodies for information security This tender procures conformity assessment body services to support the safeguarding of the information and cybersecurity, data protection and information management of Väylävirasto. Within the scope of this contract, conformity assessment bodies will produce assessment services in the role of an information security conformity assessment body approved by the Finnish Transport and Communications Agency (Traficom). When offering and producing assessment services, the information security conformity assessment bodies must comply with the current legislation, official regulations, recommendations, guidelines and other obligations directed at conformity assessment bodies by the authorities concerning conformity assessment body activities. Particular attention must be paid to the instruction issued to conformity assessment bodies by the Finnish Transport and Communications Agency for information security conformity assessment bodies 210/2016 O. During the course of the dialogue, the contracting entity will separately assess the need for a market dialogue regarding the assessment services of conformity assessment bodies for information security. sig_8a8294f19b8f37f5b23d.description: The project will develop a coherent framework for understanding how territorial cohesion and resilience operate under conditions of persistent low growth, demographic contraction and structural decline. Based on European-wide territorial mapping, it will elaborate typologies of territories facing persistent low growth and demographic contraction, and produce territorial maps of vulnerability, adaptive capacity and resilience. Through comparative qualitative case studies across different territorial contexts, it will document adaptive territorial practices and governance innovations. Finally, the project will offer practical policy guidance suggesting how cohesion policy, territorial governance and resilience planning frameworks may need to evolve in response to persistent low growth and structural territorial contraction.

sig_8b4bf10de5e76b471c05.description: South Lanarkshire Council seeks a Creative Consultancy to deliver a Market Assessment, Branding Strategy, Website Development, Content Library and Wayfinding Strategy for the Douglas Valley Outdoor Recreation and Adventure Tourism initiative within the Hagshaw Energy Cluster. 1. Market Assessment Review existing project documentation and identify implications for branding, marketing and website development. Analyse visitor data, market trends and audience segmentation, including visitor case studies. Benchmark comparable projects and destinations. Provide recommendations to inform branding, website design, content and future marketing activity. 2. Branding Development Develop and consult on three branding concepts before producing a final identity. Create brand assets including logo, name, tagline, colours, fonts and digital/print applications. Produce brand guidelines covering signage, interpretation, promotional materials and integration with existing site branding. Include recommendations for social media and future marketing activity. 3. Website Design, Build and Launch Create a branded website promoting Douglas Valley as a destination to live, work, visit and enjoy, supporting ambitions to attract up to 100,000 annual visits by 2036. Develop a scalable, content-led website with a planned lifespan of ten years. Include six core pages: Home, About, Explore, See & Stay, News and Contact. The Explore section will feature an interactive map highlighting key recreational and active travel routes, points of interest and route information including distance, elevation, difficulty and duration. Build the site on an accessible CMS suitable for community and council users. Host on a secure UK-based platform with maintenance and support arrangements. Ensure accessibility compliance and provide flexible management of route information and temporary diversions. 4. Photography and Video Library Establish a copyright-cleared library of photography and short-form video content for web, social media and print use. Source content through community engagement, youth-focused workshops and professional photography where required. Content will reflect identified visitor segments and feature strong people-focused imagery. Coverage will include renewable energy, local communities, nature, heritage and identity, local economy and outdoor recreation. Key locations include Coalburn, Douglas, Glenbuck, Glespin, Lesmahagow, Mainshill, Muirkirk, Poneil, Rigside, Douglas Water and Spireslack, alongside significant natural, heritage and recreation assets. 5. Wayfinding Strategy and Design Guidance Develop a first-phase wayfinding strategy focused on Coalburn, Douglas, Glespin, Douglasdale Community Woodland and connecting active travel routes. Establish a hierarchy of signage including gateway signs, orientation panels, interpretation boards, directional signage and waymarkers. Produce a spatial strategy identifying suitable signage locations. Develop design guidance covering dimensions, materials, specification, siting and future rollout. Prepare detailed proposals for priority installations to support future procurement. Work with Community Action Lanarkshire on implementation of information signs, directional signage and waymarkers along the NCN-Coalburn-Douglas route. Ensure all strategy, design and implementation follow inclusive design principles. Lot 1: . sig_8c312876c641ea21f026.description: THIS IS NOT A PRIOR INFORMATION NOTICE, CONTRACT NOTICE OR CALL FOR TENDERS, BUT A NOTICE OF THE LAUNCH OF A MARKET DIALOGUE AS PART OF PROCUREMENT PLANNING. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue is mapping suppliers' interest in the tendering for the coordination of resources, patient visits and space utilisation planning. The subject of the procurement is the better coordination than previously of customer and patient visits and space utilisation planning and monitoring. In the target state, space and resource planning is carried out using a scalable system entity. In the future, it can be linked to, among other things, the Numeron work shift planning system, property information system and patient and customer information system to be introduced in the wellbeing services county. Currently, health and social welfare professionals in the wellbeing services county use a single patient and customer information system from the same product family (SosiaaliLifeCare, TerveysLifeCare or both). In the target state, it would be essential that the professional would not need numerous systems to manage patient and customer work entries, appointments, arrivals and room bookings. The wellbeing services county currently does not have a master system for spatial data. The data is fragmented across different systems. Consequently, data-driven management views related to spatial efficiency are also not comprehensively available. In the future, for patients and customers, the wellbeing services county's own application Lunna will be the main transaction portal through which the customer or patient can handle their health and social welfare matters, and e.g. make appointments, register for appointments and receive (physical) customer guidance at the location. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue invites suppliers to market dialogues to discuss their solution models and present their products. The market dialogue discussions will take place in May during weeks 20 and 21 in Otaniemi, Espoo. The duration of the presentation session is preliminarily planned to be approximately two hours per supplier. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue reserves the right to invite the number of suppliers it deems necessary to the presentation session. Expressing interest in the information request does not bind suppliers to participate in the tendering procedure, nor is it a prerequisite for participating in the tendering procedure. Suppliers interested in the procurement are requested to declare their interest in the procurement via the tarjouspalvelu.fi portal. Expressing interest in the information request does not bind the service provider/supplier to participate in the tendering procedure, nor is it a prerequisite for participating in the actual tendering procedure later. Interest in the procurement is requested to be submitted by 06.04.2026 at 12.00 via the tarjouspalvelu.fi portal. We will contact everyone who has expressed their interest.

sig_8cab755f3e31b4ef5778.description: The overarching goal of this notice of funding opportunity (NOFO) and its companion opportunities is to establish the Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) Program to support development of innovative, reliable, cost-effective, and sustainable multimodal AI-based clinical decision support (CDS) tools. PRIMED-AI CDS tools are based on the integration of clinical imaging with other types of multimodal health data to enhance care for patients with a wide range of health conditions. The PRIMED-AI Program seeks to catalyze the adoption of AI-based CDS tools into clinical workflows to enable novel personalized medicine strategies that address significant health challenges.The purpose of this NOFO is to catalyze the translation of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled, image-centered, multimodal CDS tools, developed as Software as a Medical Device, from training and testing of prototypes towards clinical applications that address unmet health challenges in precision medicine. These projects are expected to have high potential for demonstrable, positive impact on patient outcomes and/or healthcare processes.

sig_8cd7b85ff300eecc505c.description: Carmarthenshire County Council is undertaking an Early Market Engagement exercise to better understand the care rostering, scheduling and workforce management solutions currently available within the market. The Council currently utilises a rostering and scheduling solution across its Residential and Domiciliary Care Services and wishes to engage with suppliers to understand available products, functionality, market developments and delivery models that may support future service requirements. This exercise is intended to inform future planning and does not represent a commitment to undertake a procurement process. The Council is particularly interested in solutions that support: • Domiciliary Care scheduling and visit management. • Residential Care rostering and workforce management. • Workforce resource teams and shared staffing models. • Mobile working for frontline care staff. • Leave, absence and availability management. • Skills, compliance and workforce competency management. • Payroll, travel and workforce payment processes. • Reporting, operational oversight and management information. • Continuity of care and workforce utilisation. • Integration with care management, HR, payroll, finance and identity management systems. The Council intends to provide a high-level requirements document to interested suppliers and may invite suppliers to demonstrate how their solution supports the functional areas identified. Participation in this engagement is for information and planning purposes only and does not commit the Council to any procurement or award. All interested parties are encouraged to register their interest by 22/09/26 to participate in the demonstration sessions which we are planning to hold in October. Details of any formal tender will be provided in due course. Lot 1: . None

sig_8ceb6a750d48331c8bf4.description: The German Academic Exchange Service (DAAD) is the world's largest organisation for the international exchange of students and researchers as well as the internationalisation of German universities. Since its foundation in the year 1925, the DAAD has supported over 2,9 million academics at home and abroad. As an association, it is supported by German universities and student bodies. In addition to awarding scholarships, the DAAD promotes the internationalisation of German universities, strengthens German studies and the German language abroad, supports developing countries in building efficient universities and advises decision-makers in cultural, educational and development policy. To this end, it maintains an external network with regional offices, information centres and information points in more than 60 countries. Worldwide, more than 1.200 committed employees in Bonn, Berlin and regional offices work towards the goals of the DAAD. The DAAD is financed predominantly from federal funds from the Federal Foreign Office, the Federal Ministry of Education and Research, the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development and the European Union. Other sponsors include foreign governments, companies, foundations and the Stifterverband für die Deutsche Wissenschaft. The DAAD is inviting tenders for services in the areas of usability, user experience and continuous success measurement. A contractor (AN) is sought with specific competence and experience in the areas of usability, user experience, conducting user acceptance tests, continuous success measurement, optimisation and requirements analysis. The AN designs and conducts user-centred studies (e.g. usability tests, acceptance tests, user surveys, target group interviews), continuously measures the success of existing and new features, analyses information architecture, navigation and interaction design and derives concrete optimisation proposals from this. In addition, it supports the DAAD in requirements analysis and prioritisation of further development needs and documents the results in compact, decision-oriented reports for the product managers. The services mentioned below can be commissioned in combinations adapted to the respective project, both in individual studies and in long-term projects. Corresponding tasks may also have to be carried out for mobile apps under Android and/or iOS, possibly also accompanying development. So far, however, no development is specifically planned. The DAAD expects the following services from the contractor: a) Usability and user acceptance tests (in-person or remote) b) User surveys and target group interviews (in-person or remote) c) Laboratory use or rental for in-person tests d) Conception of customised UX monitoring systems for continuous success measurement e) Creation of personas and user structure analyses f) Workshops and design thinking (in-person or remote) g) Consulting, continuous optimisation support, content review and expert analysis h) Result documentation and presentation i) Web analysis and user tracking For further information, please refer to the service description in Annex 02.
sig_8ceb6a750d48331c8bf4.title: Framework agreement for services in the areas of usability, user experience and continuous success measurement

sig_8d0615bc5a9d1269f25b.description: Framework Agreement for Procurement Consultancy and Procurement Services for Vehicles and Equipment for Civil Protection Baden-Württemberg. The services are tendered as a framework agreement. The client is looking for a service provider to support it in the procurement of vehicles and equipment for civil protection. The contractor must in particular provide the following predominantly technical services, while the legal assessment and decision remain with the client: - Carrying out market surveys on the vehicles and equipment to be procured for civil protection, in particular with regard to the current state of the art and technical possibilities - Drawing up specifications taking into account technical specifications and the special needs of civil protection - Developing proposals for suitability and award criteria, including technical evaluation criteria - Processing technical applicant/tenderer questions - Processing complaints, in particular preparing complaint response letters - Evaluating requests to participate or tenders as well as developing award proposals for the contract award - Preparing prior information notices - Preparing procurement records - Advising in review procedures In addition, the contractor must optionally support and accompany the client upon respective call-off after the respective award in the procurement process, for example at construction meetings, prototype inspections, quality inspections and acceptances and, where applicable, also regarding the warranty phase after acceptance. Legal advice services are not covered by the contract. The services are tendered in the form of a framework agreement. The client determines the specific services to be provided and their deadlines individually in each individual contract. The contractor has no entitlement to the call-off of services from the framework agreement. There is no entitlement to further commissioning. The type and scope of the individual commissioning can vary per individual project. The client is entitled to an ordinary right of termination at any time for each individual contract issued on the basis of the framework agreement. The client reserves the right to commission any further special services. The framework agreement has a maximum duration of four years from the start of the services with regard to the non-optional services pursuant to Section 21 Paragraph 6 of the Ordinance on the Award of Public Contracts (VgV). Insofar as the client calls off the optional services, the conditions of the framework agreement for the individual contracts issued until the maximum duration is reached shall continue to apply until their final processing by the contractor even after termination of this framework agreement. The maximum quantity of services expected under the framework agreement amounts to up to a total of 500 vehicles and equipment, which the client can call off bundled in individual contracts for each individual contract.

sig_8d37de87e460fcc3ef51.description: The MSHIP Program is an initiative by TransnetBW aimed at supporting Germany's energy transition by developing a sustainable, scalable, and efficient grid management system. It focuses on modularity, automation, and simplicity to enhance operational security and reduce costs. The architecture is based on a self-hosted, cloud-native platform specifically designed for secure and data-driven operations. The MSHIP - LFC ensures continuous monitoring of the power balance and thus a stable energy supply. The controller detects deviations in the power balance or frequency and activates the appropriate secondary control power providers on a price-based basis to stabilize the balance and thus also the frequency. In addition, a controller is to be developed for special emergency situations in which no conventional control power market environment is available. The purpose of this RFI is to identify potential providers and solutions that can meet the requirements of the MSHIP - LFC. The RFI is intended to provide an initial market overview and to evaluate possible technological approaches and their ability to integrate into the existing MSHIP architecture. The aim is not to commit to a specific system, an architecture or provider in advance. Openness to different approaches remains the main guiding principle. The information gathered will serve as a basis for future decisions and possible tenders. Participation in this market exploration will not result in any advantages or disadvantages for the participants as potential bidders in a future - not yet binding - tender procedure. Please note that also responses are invited and will be considered that do not cover all listed functionalities.
sig_8d37de87e460fcc3ef51.title: MSHIP Market Survey for LFC

sig_8dfed59770476e947318.description: For the electric commercial vehicles, Disposal + Recycling requires power distribution cabinets in the two motor vehicle halls at the Forsthaus energy centre, each with at least 6 charging points, distribution boxes for the individual vehicles and a load management system (software). The power distribution cabinets must meet the following requirements: · Suitable for use in depots (municipal works yards) with fixed, schedulable charging times. · Suitable for 24/7 use in a frost-protected environment (hall, marquee). · Suitable for normal charging and rapid charging of individual vehicles. · Equipped with LAN, WLAN and mobile communications (at least 4G). The distribution boxes for the individual vehicles must be compatible for CCS charging cables with 5 m, 7 m and optionally 10 m. The boxes must have at least IP54 protection. Wall mounting is intended in principle. Optionally, ceiling mounting with a cable reel featuring a 7 m long cable is to be tendered. The installation (excluding electrical installation) of the power distribution cabinets and distribution boxes must be carried out by the tenderer. Commissioning is to be carried out by the supplier and must be recorded in a report. The electrical installations are tendered separately and are not part of the scope of services. However, the software for load management must be offered as well. Since Energie Wasser Bern is constructing a new building on the site of the Forsthaus energy centre from July 2027, the distribution cabinets and boxes of the North motor vehicle hall must be accommodated in a provisional structure (temperature-controlled marquee) and will only be installed in the motor vehicle hall after a construction period of approx. 3 years. The distribution cabinets and boxes for the East motor vehicle hall can be installed at the final location upon delivery. The installation of the infrastructure must take place by early June 2027 at the latest. With regard to the software, it is important that not all vehicles are charged simultaneously, but rather that the entire available time (approx. 16 hours to 06.30 hours) is utilised. In addition, the system must restart automatically in the event of a power or network failure and issue a notification. Furthermore, the following requirements are placed on the software: · Locally installed hardware/software solution, also possible web-based, which controls the charging processes locally. · Autonomous functionality of the system even in the event of an internet failure or malfunction. · Arbitrary scalability when retrofitting additional charging points. · Immediate clearance of the charging process following successful authentication. · Online access (web UI) via desktop computer and mobile end devices. · German language selection. · Display of energy consumption per vehicle live and retroactively. · Evaluations and statistics on energy consumption, charging processes and efficiency per vehicle as well as comparison options between the vehicles. · Export of consumption and charging data (e.g. CSV or Excel). · Guarantee that the software will be actively supported for at least five years after acceptance of the installation (delivery of security patches, adaptation to new versions of peripheral systems, elimination of functional errors, etc.). The detailed technical requirements can be found in the bill of quantities in the appendix. The bill of quantities must be completed in full without references to additional documents. Product, brand, design or type designations are dispensed with. If such designations are listed in exceptional cases, equivalent alternatives are permitted. Equivalence must be proven by the tenderer.
sig_8dfed59770476e947318.title: Charging infrastructure and load management for electric lorries

sig_8e275a5238ed1ec42ade.description: BIM Berliner Immobilienmanagement GmbH (BIM) intends to procure and introduce a new document management system (DMS) for company-wide use. The aim of the project is to provide a central, secure and audit-proof platform for managing, processing and archiving documents and files. The DMS is intended to support cross-departmental collaboration, reduce existing media discontinuity and ensure compliance with statutory, data protection and organisational requirements. Operation will initially take place on-premises in the BIM data centre. In the long term, the solution is intended to technically support hybrid and cloud-based operating models respectively. The scope of services comprises in particular: - Provision, implementation and introduction of the DMS software including installation, configuration and training, - Integration into existing systems, in particular SAP S/4HANA, email and office environments, - Migration of existing documents and metadata, - Design and implementation of defined workflows, archiving and authorisation structures, - Ensuring information security, digital accessibility and GDPR compliance, - Operation, maintenance and software support (support S) including service level management. The project is part of BIM's digitalisation strategy and is closely linked to the parallel projects "BIM SAP 2028" and "BitX", in which core business processes and specialist procedures are modernised and integrated. The contract term is 48 months with the option for a one-time extension of up to 24 months. The basis for the provision of services is the EVB-IT system contract in its currently valid version.

sig_8e6aa294f87c09cd46f5.description: Danmarks Nationalbank (the Customer) seeks to establish a framework agreement with one Supplier for the provision of specialized cybersecurity advisory and assessment services. As the operator and overseer of critical financial infrastructure in Denmark, Danmarks Nationalbank supports essential processes and systems that require a high level of security, resilience, and trust. The Customer continuously introduces new technologies, vendors, services and architectural changes that may impact its security posture. To ensure informed decision-making and maintain an appropriate level of cyber resilience, the Customer seeks access to independent technical experts capable of evaluating cybersecurity risks from an adversarial perspective. The purpose of the agreement is to provide the Customer with on-demand access to highly skilled technical cybersecurity experts with offensive security backgrounds, capable of delivering rapid, pragmatic and risk-based assessments of new technologies, systems, solutions, architectures and security-related questions. The service shall complement the Customer's internal cybersecurity capabilities by providing independent expert judgement, specialized technical expertise and threat-informed analysis to support secure decision-making, risk management and operational resilience. The Supplier shall provide access to cybersecurity specialists with relevant expertise across infrastructure, cloud, applications, identity and access management, emerging technologies, adversarial techniques and offensive security methodologies.
sig_8e6aa294f87c09cd46f5.title: Tender for a framework agreement on the delivery of Cybersecurity advisory and assessment services

sig_8f2b0eb238d2e4596b74.description: The purpose of this prior information notice is to inform about and prepare the market for a coming competition. This prior information notice is not intended to shorten the tender deadline in accordance with the Public Procurement Regulations §20-2 (2). NHN wants to start a procurement process for broadband access for small and medium sized locations. The accesses are used by members in the health network, service providers and entities in the central health management. The accesses represent an important part of a robust and secure infrastructure for transporting digital services for the entire health and welfare sector. Limitations: Accesses to large locations such as hospitals, computer centres etc. are not a part of this procurement. The aim is to enter into an agreement with one or several tenderers. Furthermore, we see great opportunities in further developing digital interaction systems that make NHNs and the supplier's work processes more efficient for the establishment, operation and termination of accesses. The Contracting Authority intends to sign a contract by the end of 2026, starting the agreement from January 2027. About NHN: NHN is a government company owned by the Ministry of Health and Care Services. Our task is to develop, administer and operate national e-health systems and infrastructure. We are responsible for national e-health services such as e-prescription, helsenorge.no, core journal and basic data. We also provide services within ICT, procurements and archives for the health administration agencies. NHN operates 80 national ICT systems and has 1,000 capable employees distributed across offices in Trondheim, Oslo, Tromsø, Moss and Svalbard. Read more at the https://www.nhn.no. At the time of the prior information notice, NHN plans to conduct the procurement in accordance with the Norwegian Public Procurement Act and Regulations, based on the procedure competitive procedure with negotiation after prior publication above the EU/EEA threshold (1.49 MNOK) pursuant to FOA Parts I and III. To further strengthen the market’s ability to participate in the competition, and to facilitate a well‐executed procurement process, NHN is considering market research and supplier dialogue in accordance with FOA §§12‐1 and 12‐2. Any supplier dialogue will be announced via Mercell and Doffin/TED as a follow-up to this prior information notice. We intend to engage in dialogue with the market to obtain additional information and insights related to our needs.
sig_8f2b0eb238d2e4596b74.title: Accesses for Norsk helsenett SF (NHN)

sig_8fefea72088ce0135a52.description: THIS IS NOT A CONTRACT NOTICE OR A CALL FOR COMPETITION BUT A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR MARKET RESEARCH AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE. This request for information is used to survey the market and obtain information regarding the procurement. The contracting authority is not initiating a tendering procedure by publishing the request for information; instead, any procurement notice and call for competition will be published later. The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Responding to the request for information is not a prerequisite for participation in a possible later tendering procedure. Suppliers will not be paid compensation for responding to the request for information or participating in market dialogue. Responses given to this request for information will be used in planning the procurement of expert services to support the management of software assets (licence management). Expert assistance is needed flexibly across several different areas. The main user of HUS's centralised licence management system and product responsible persons for different areas maintain information on the most important software rights in a centralised system (Matrix42, SAM tool). In addition, supplier-specific portals are in use. In the planned procurement, the licence experts of the supplier to be procured would analyse and report quarterly on the current situation regarding agreed software rights (e.g. Microsoft, Oracle, Adobe and IBM manufacturers). They would compare information from different supplier portals with information in the centralised SAM tool, observe deficiencies and provide HUS with recommendations related to optimisation and compliance. The supplier should provide SAM Manager expertise, helping to manage valid software contracts. The supplier should advise on products, contract models, software lifecycles and usage rights. In addition, the supplier is hoped to provide support in building the management model for licence management. It is planned to include as an option in the procurement the entry of licence, cost and contract information into the SAM tool by the supplier instead of HUS personnel. HUS-yhtymä is renewing its ITSM system. In connection with this, the integration of licence management as part of this entity will also be evaluated. External expertise will also be needed for this. The purpose of the request for information is to survey suppliers available on the market and their service range. The purpose is to clarify service solutions, pricing principles and the cost level for the budget. HUS-yhtymä requests suppliers interested in the procurement described above to notify the contracting authority of their interest and attach to the response a general description/brochure of the service solution you offer for the need described above. Please note that all material is intended solely for conducting this market dialogue. The contracting authority will treat your response confidentially. Based on the responses to the request for information, clarifying questions may be presented to the supplier and/or an opportunity offered to present their solutions in a manner to be notified later. Suppliers that have responded to the request for information may possibly receive preliminary call for competition documents for comment. Responding or failing to respond to the request for information does not affect the supplier's position in a potential tendering procedure. We ask that responses to the request for information and notifications of interest be submitted no later than 20.3.2026 at 12:00 to the address kilpailutus.ict@hus.fi. The subject of the message should state "HUS 090-2026 - Lisenssienhallinnan asiantuntijapalvelut".

sig_90116dd5159cffb33fea.description: The Student Loans company (SLC) have an agreement for Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service expiring April 2028. In order to provision for a retender of the agreement SLC are undertaking pre-market engagement with regards to the provision of the following: • Requirement A: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - MXDR Service (2026-TR-0109a) • Requirement B: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Vulnerability Management (VM) Service (2026-TR-0109b) • Requirement C: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Breach Attack Simulation (BAS) Service (2026-TR-0109c) • Requirement D: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI) Service (2026-TR-0109d) • Requirement E: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Digital Forensics and Incident Response (DFIR) Retainer Service (2026-TR-0109e) • Requirement F: Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Security Architecture and Engineering Support Services (2026-TR-0109f) SLC is considering an approach to the market to give the suppliers an option to bid for one or ALL of the contractual requirements. Requirement A Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - MXDR Service The Supplier will provide a Managed Extended Detection and Response (MXDR) capability operating on a hybrid customer/supplier model. MXDR Service The Supplier will provide: • 24x7x365 monitoring of SLC security telemetry. • L1 and L2 Security Operations Centre capability (SLC retain L3). • Incident identification, triage and investigation. • Security use-case monitoring and tuning. • Management of Microsoft Sentinel detections. • SOAR playbook execution and optimisation. • Escalation management. • Alert enrichment. • Threat hunting capability. • Malicious activity investigation. • Service governance and performance management. • Security reporting at operational, tactical and strategic levels. Security Engineering (Operational) The Supplier shall provide: • L3 Engineering support for Sentinel. • Analytics rule development and tuning. • SOAR playbook management. • Connector maintenance and health monitoring. • Logging optimisation. • Onboarding and validation of agreed log sources. • Detection engineering support. • Detection gap analysis and monitoring coverage reviews. • Security use case development and continuous improvement. • Monitoring health checks. • Monitoring and remediation of ingestion issues. • Security platform optimisation. • Proactive automation support and development. • Threat intelligence-led detection improvements. Data Loss Prevention (DLP) & Phishing The Supplier shall: • Monitoring, triage and investigation of DLP, phishing, business email compromise (BEC), malicious email, malicious attachment and malicious URL alerts. • Investigation of suspected data loss, data exfiltration and policy breach events. • Support for user reported phishing submissions. • Escalation and coordination of confirmed incidents in accordance with agreed response procedures. • Identification and analysis of phishing campaigns, attacker infrastructure, indicators of compromise and emerging attack trends. • Recommendations for improvements to DLP policies, email security controls, detections and response processes. • Monthly reporting, trend analysis and security improvement recommendations. Reporting The Supplier shall provide: • Weekly operational reports. • Monthly service reports. • Quarterly service reviews. • KPI and SLA reporting. • Security metrics and trend analysis. Requirement B Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Vulnerability Management Service The Supplier shall provide Vulnerability Management services Monday to Friday, UK Core Hours (09:00-17:00). Vulnerability Management The Supplier shall: • Monitor vulnerability management queues. • Investigate vulnerability notifications. • Manage vulnerability triage. • Validate vulnerability findings. • Perform exploitability assessments. • Provide remediation recommendations. • Support exposure management activities. • Support CTEM activities. Stakeholder Engagement The Supplier shall: • Conduct monthly technical review meetings. • Support resolver teams. • Assist remediation planning. • Review remediation performance. • Provide vulnerability prioritisation guidance. Dashboarding & Reporting The Supplier shall: • Maintain executive dashboards. • Enhance Power BI reporting. • Produce technical reports. • Produce executive reports. • Produce PCI compliance reports. • Produce risk trending reports. Tooling The Supplier shall support: • Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. • Rapid7. • SLC PCI ASV Scanning tooling. • Jira. • Power BI. Requirement C Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Breach Attack Simulation Service The Supplier shall provide a Breach Attack Simulation (BAS) capability, currently using AttackIQ or similar. BAS Service The Supplier shall: • Operate and maintain the BAS platform. • Deploy and maintain BAS agents. • Configure integrations. • Execute scheduled simulations. • Execute customer-specific simulations. • Execute retests following remediation activities. Adversary Simulation Testing scenarios shall include: • Initial Access. • Execution. • Persistence. • Privilege Escalation. • Credential Access. • Lateral Movement. • Command and Control. • Exfiltration. • Malware. • Ransomware. • Advanced Persistent Threat activity. Security Validation The Supplier shall assess: • Security control effectiveness. • Security monitoring effectiveness. • Detection coverage. • Response capability. • Incident handling. • Use-case effectiveness. Reporting The Supplier shall produce: • Monthly BAS reports. • Executive summaries. • Technical findings. • Remediation recommendations. • Retest outcomes. Requirement D Enhanced Security Operations Managed Service - Cyber Threat Intelligence Service The Supplier shall provide strategic, operational and tactical Cyber Threat Intelligence services. Threat Intelligence Managed Service The Supplier shall provide: • Threat Intelligence reporting. • Integration into Microsoft Sentinel. • Indicator of Compromise feeds. • Threat actor intelligence. Operational Intelligence The Supplier shall provide: • Threat alerts. • Vulnerability intelligence. • Emerging threat notifications. • Campaign tracking. • Industry specific intelligence. Strategic Intelligence The Supplier shall provide: • Threat landscape assessments. • Quarterly threat reports. • Executive intelligence briefings. • Board level threat summaries. • Sector specific threat reporting. Security Operations Support The Supplier shall provide: • Intelligence support during incidents. • Threat hunting support. • Intelligence driven use-case creation. • Intelligence enrichment services. sig_90a14e14039ee7844efb.description: Bournemouth University ("BU" or the "University") is exploring options for the provision of a co-managed Security Operations Centre (SOC) service to enhance and future-proof its cyber security operations capability. The University is seeking market feedback from experienced Managed Security Service Providers to better understand available service models, implementation approaches, commercial arrangements and indicative costs. BU has invested significantly in its internal cyber security capability and Microsoft security technologies, including Microsoft Sentinel, Microsoft Defender XDR, Entra ID Protection, Security Copilot and related services. The University is now considering how external specialist support could complement its in-house team through a co-managed SOC operating model. The key objectives of a future service are expected to include: - Enhancing monitoring, detection and response capabilities through either 24/7 or out-of-hours SOC coverage. - Improving threat detection, triage, false-positive reduction and incident response effectiveness. - Providing additional specialist expertise, operational resilience and surge capacity during major incidents or periods of heightened risk. - Maintaining and continuously improving detection rules, playbooks, automation and security monitoring capabilities. - Leveraging threat intelligence, sector insight, automation and AI-enabled capabilities to strengthen cyber resilience and operational effectiveness. - Establishing a robust governance, reporting and service management framework with clear responsibilities between BU and the supplier. - Maximising the value of the University's existing Microsoft security investments while minimising the need for additional tooling wherever appropriate. The University wishes to understand how the market can support these objectives, together with the costs, benefits, risks and implementation considerations associated with different service models. Supplier feedback received through this Preliminary Market Engagement exercise will help inform the University's future requirements, budget planning and procurement strategy. Lot 1: .
sig_90a14e14039ee7844efb.title: Security Operation Centre

sig_92184a9dd035c8c68422.description: HAUS Finnish Institute of Public Management Ltd (HAUS) is establishing a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for the period 2026–2030 for the procurement of expert services related to digital transformation, innovation, governance, institutional development and public sector development. The estimated total value of procurements conducted under the DPS during its validity period is approximately EUR 40 million (excluding VAT). The DPS will be used to procure expertise for international development cooperation projects, technical assistance assignments, advisory services, capacity building initiatives, studies, evaluations and other expert services implemented globally. Assignments may be funded by, among others, the European Union, the Ministry for Foreign Affairs of Finland, development finance institutions and other international cooperation partners. The DPS is divided into the following categories: 1. Digital Transformation, Data, Artificial Intelligence & Cybersecurity 2. Governance, Public Sector Development & Capacity Building 3. Innovation, Investment Readiness & Technical Assistance 4. Communications, Media, Creative & Visibility Services The DPS is open to suppliers from Finland and internationally. Suppliers may apply to one or several categories and, once admitted, will have the opportunity to participate in mini-competitions launched throughout the DPS period 2026–2030. Further information regarding the scope, eligibility requirements and application process is provided in the procurement documents.
sig_92184a9dd035c8c68422.title: HAUS DPS 2026–2030 for Digital Transformation, Innovation and Public Sector Development
