sig_9240c1547de3b0fae646.description: This is a request for information, which is not a contract notice or a call for tenders. The purpose of the request for information is to collect information regarding the subject of the procurement for a future tender. Responding to the request for information is not a prerequisite for participating in any potential later tender. To ensure the success of the future tender, however, it would be important for potential tenderers to provide the contracting authority with the requested information as extensively as possible. The request for information does not oblige Istekki Oy to carry out the procurement in the manner described in the request for information or its appendices, and the tender process may also be left unimplemented. The subject of this request for information is work-life permit and card training, and the purpose is to clarify the supply on the market, for example regarding occupational safety, first aid, and hot work training, as well as the market situation, products, contract terms, and supplier pricing related to additional services. In addition, we request an answer to the questions we have presented, which are in the appendix to this request for information "Tietopyyntö ja kysymykset". Currently, the annual need for training is 90–100 training sessions, depending on the training required. The procurement includes the organisation of training as both online and contact teaching. The training includes, among others, the following qualifications: - Occupational safety card - Hot work card - Risk assessment - Basic training for chemical use supervisors - Occupational safety responsibilities and co-operation at the workplace - Electrical safety card SFS 6002 - Emergency first aid for electrical work (0,5 day training) - Emergency first aid course, incl. SPR® versions (0,5 and 1 day training) - SPR EA1® (2 day training) There is a need for training implemented as contact teaching primarily in Mikkeli, Kuopio, and Tampere. If necessary, training can also be organised at Istekki's other locations, i.e., Oulu, Jyväskylä, and Espoo. The request for information must be answered by 30.9.2025 at 14.00 by email to hankinnat@istekki.fi. The information provided will be treated confidentially. In the response to the request for information, you are kindly requested to indicate your willingness to participate in a market dialogue meeting. Based on the responses received, Istekki will select, at its own discretion, 1-5 tenderers to present their services in a meeting of approximately one hour via Teams. More detailed information on responding and the market dialogue, as well as preliminary dates for the meetings, are stated in the appendix "Tietopyyntö ja kysymykset". No compensation will be paid to those who have responded to the request for information for making the request for information or for participating in any presentation events related to the request for information. The tender service automatically creates deadlines for submitting questions and responding to the request for information. Instead of these deadlines, the deadlines in the request for information document shall be followed. Any additional questions should, in principle, be asked as part of the responses to the request for information. The contracting authority will not publish additional questions submitted during the request for information phase.

sig_92caf0427995304453c5.description: The Universität Hamburg (hereinafter 'UHH'), as a university of excellence with more than 43.000 students and approx. 6.000 employees, is one of the most research-intensive universities in Germany and at the same time one of the largest training institutions in Northern Germany. With its 'Flagship University' concept in the Hamburg metropolitan region, it maintains innovative and cooperative links with scientific and non-scientific partners. It produces future-oriented social goods for the location – but also nationally and internationally – namely education, knowledge and the exchange of knowledge, under the guiding principle of sustainability. The executive boards of the 6 Hamburg universities signed a Letter of Intent in April 2024 regarding the joint IT operation of the Hamburg universities. The aim here is to establish a joint organisation that is controlled by the universities and understands, bundles, and implements their needs, and provides high-quality IT services specifically for scientific institutions across the entire service spectrum. A service centre is to be built and established with the goal of creating synergies and thus providing digital services more efficiently, in a more targeted and user-centred manner, more comprehensively, and at the same time with better quality and protection against cyberattacks. In the course of this joint IT operation, it is necessary to create a joint, federated Identity and Access Management (IAM) structure for the Hamburg universities. The overarching goal is the provision of services for all Hamburg universities based on established federation technologies. Each university is to be equipped with a local IAM system, and the then technology-compatible systems are to be integrated into a joint, federated state identity and access infrastructure. The authoritative management of identities remains decentralised at the individual institutions. A central master directory is to be set up to hold the personal attributes necessary for joint operation. Such a federated infrastructure enables the universities to participate in jointly or centrally provided services (e.g. cloud, collaboration and e-learning services) and at the same time significantly increases the security of access, as modern, open standards such as SAML, OpenID Connect (OIDC), SCIM and FIDO2 are to be implemented throughout. For an organisation-independent, uniform and permanent identification of users, e.g. also when changing between universities, the nationwide federation service of the German National Research and Education Network (DFN-AAI), including the eduID service, is to be used as a basis. The joint state federation is intended as a sub-federation within the DFN-AAI in order to enable cross-university coordination beyond a uniform attribute set. The project aims to design, build and transfer this joint federated state IAM infrastructure into regular operation. A later inclusion of further scientific institutions in Hamburg is not excluded.
sig_92caf0427995304453c5.title: Establishment of a joint federated identity and access management infrastructure for Hamburg universities

sig_92d4574971aba33d56ff.description: NOW IS YOUR CHANCE TO INFLUENCE THE PROCUREMENT DURING THE MARKET CONSULTATION PHASE! The main applicant and administrator of the project is the Urban Environment Division of the City of Lappeenranta. In addition to the City of Lappeenranta, the project includes the cities of Turku, Vaasa, Kouvola, Oulu, Espoo, Kokkola, Tampere, Järvenpää and Helsinki. For the planning of this AI project, the municipalities have invited the Ministry of the Environment, Senate Properties, the Association of Finnish Cities and Municipalities (AFCM), universities, and other Finnish, European and international public organisations to participate in stakeholder cooperation. The main driving force behind the need for a new AI service is the national need for the use of data analysis models arising from the reform of the Building Act and Decree. In Finland, the new Building Act was adopted by the Parliament in February 2023. With this market survey, the Municipalities AI development project is identifying markets and potential suppliers to identify an AI service for automatic inspection and building control use cases for buildings, built environment and Geographic information. For a more detailed description of the requirements of the solution sought, please refer to the 'Description of the Acquisition' section of this notice. This notice does not call for tenders or requests for participation. Company-specific interviews via teams will be held via Teams during October – November 2026. The organizer reserves the right to record the event if needed. For companies who are interested in participating in the interviews and market dialogue please provide your answers to given pre-questions by latest by October 07, 2026. The contracting entity reserves the possibility of inviting the companies that have expressed interest to present their products or solutions at company-specific events and to send a possible draft invitation to tender for comments to interested companies before the possible publication of the actual contract notice or tender. The aim is to organize possible company-specific presentation events during October 2026 (in principle remotely). The timetables and other information provided in this notice, such as the planned market dialogue, are preliminary and indicative and may change as the preparation of the notification progresses. The information provided is not binding on the contracting entity. Failure to respond to the market survey will not prevent a supplier from participating in a potential tender and will not affect the supplier's position in the actual tender. This notice does not call for tenders or requests for participation. The market survey is accompanied by an invitation to a market survey, where the contracting entity can conduct a market dialogue with the operators that have expressed an interest. The outcome of this market survey will be used by the municipalities and stakeholders in Finland, such as ministries, to prepare a separate development project and a competitive tendering process for the procurement of suitable products according to the market. We warmly invite interested companies to participate in the market dialogue!

sig_93b42c4d078a0b1e073b.description: The Pathways to Enable Secure Open-Source Ecosystems (PESOSE) program supports the translation of open-source science and engineering-focused research products into safe and sustainable ecosystems that address national and societal challenges. Open-source tools such as software, hardware, machine learning models, languages, and data platforms are designed to be shared as they are publicly-accessible and modifiable. These tools spark innovation in critical fields as varied as artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud computing, banking, healthcare, research, education, next-gen manufacturing, mobility, and National security (including cybersecurity). PESOSE supports the creation of managing organizations for these ecosystems, ensuring strong governance, distributed development, and broad user communities across academia, industry, and government. PESOSE also supports enhancements to the safety, security, and privacy of Open-Source Ecosystems (OSE) by addressing significant vulnerabilities, both technical and socio-technical, to improve the resistance of the ecosystem against threats. This solicitation seeks three types of proposals, allowing teams to propose specific activities to: 1) scope and plan the establishment of an OSE, 2) establish and expand a sustainable OSE based on a robust, promising open-source product that meets an emergent societal or national need, and 3) improve the safety, security, and privacy of an existing OSE and its products.
sig_93b42c4d078a0b1e073b.title: Pathways to Enable Secure Open-Source Ecosystems (PESOSE)

sig_94329553e52c261ebc1a.description: The client's IT encompasses a very wide range of services from merchandise management and billing systems such as SAP through control centre systems to apps, such as MVGO. IT demand sometimes grows faster than internal staff can be built up and should it decrease, reducing internal staff is sluggish. This scaling requirement is addressed by awarding services to external parties. One form of this is the external takeover of testing of software applications in a scope appropriate for each application (test concept, test management, test case definition, execution of functional and non-functional tests (e.g. L&P tests, regression tests, exploratory tests, ...), test automation). This support takes place in both traditional and agile environments. The client currently has 3 candidate groups of applications for which they wish to outsource testing. The known support effort is approx. 3 to 5 FTE. During the contract term, applications may be added, removed, or the annual effort for them may fluctuate. A framework agreement is being tendered. The individual applications are commissioned via call-off (possibly also with multiple call-offs). The client's experience shows that domain knowledge is essential for service delivery, especially when testing. The tender covers the following domains: • Public transport sales: Sales processes (app- and web-based sales channels, mass customer billing) • Purchasing and logistics (SAP MM/SD/CS) • Finance (SAP FI/CO) • Maintenance including mobile maintenance (SAP PM, app applications) There is no obligation for the client to exhaust the contract under this framework agreement. Services are fundamentally to be provided remotely. Exceptions that require on-site service delivery are workshops and, where applicable, tests in connection with hardware that is only available on-site at the client (e.g. a ticket vending machine). Other special conditions for contract performance: Contract execution in German, written and oral; within EU GDPR

sig_953d35e7ecb0dc9c7a32.description: The aim of the award procedure is to commission a high-performing managed service provider (MSP) that will take over the complete planning, management, implementation and operational transfer of the brownfield transformation of the existing SAP ECC system landscape to SAP S/4HANA Cloud, Private Edition, as part of "RISE with SAP". The subject of the contract is a holistic transformation and operational service. This includes in particular the technical and functional analysis of the existing system landscape, the SAP S/4HANA conversion, the transfer to the private cloud environment, test migrations and data conversion, the adaptation of custom developments, add-ons and interfaces, as well as the implementation and optimisation of the relevant commercial processes. In addition, SAP Fiori, reporting and embedded analytics, as well as the necessary integration services, in particular using the SAP Business Technology Platform and the SAP Integration Suite, must be taken into account. The contractor shall accompany the transformation including tests, cutover, go-live, hypercare, training and handover to regular operations and shall subsequently take over the agreed managed services as well as operational, support and further development services. In this context, particular account must be taken of the clean core approach, the maintenance of ongoing clinical operations, the existing dependencies on SAP IS-H, i.s.h.med, SAP HCM and other peripheral systems, as well as requirements regarding data protection, information security, compliance, availability, scalability and an orderly exit scenario. The contractual basis is intended to be the conclusion of an EVB-IT cloud contract, which covers both the transformation and implementation services up to acceptance and the managed services, operational, support and further development services to be provided thereafter.
sig_953d35e7ecb0dc9c7a32.title: TNWB: S/4HANA procurement

sig_95cf5ff5ad4732ed2382.description: Pursuant to Article L. 2113-2 of the Public Procurement Code, SMO Nord Pas-de-Calais Numérique acts as a central purchasing body in the sense that this buyer acquires supplies or services for other contracting authorities, public undertakings or contracting entities. The purpose of this contract is the supply of: • personal RGS** and eIDAS authentication and signature certificates, on a USB key type medium, for the agents and elected officials of the member local authorities and public establishments; • NFC cards on a physical medium, intended for the agents and elected officials of the member local authorities and public establishments, supplied according to the same ordering, delivery and handover procedures as personal certificates on a physical medium (cf. point 3.5). The Syndicat mixte Nord-Pas-de-Calais Numérique, in partnership with the Territorial Civil Service management centres of the Nord (Cdg59) and the Pas-de-Calais (Cdg62), operates a central purchasing body for the local authorities and public establishments of the Nord and Pas-de-Calais departments. This central purchasing body facilitates access to the authentication and electronic signature certificates necessary for the dematerialisation of administrative procedures and documents. It offers member entities a shared system, allowing them to benefit from negotiated rates and a simplified ordering process. At the date of launch of this consultation, 560 local authorities and public establishments belonging to the central purchasing body have access to a dematerialised platform allowing them to order their certificates directly. This contract is a continuation of the previous contract. It aims to guarantee the continuity of the service provided to the members of the central purchasing body, within an updated regulatory framework marked in particular by the evolution of the eIDAS regulation 2.0 and the strengthening of security requirements. This consultation pursues the following objectives: - To guarantee, for all members of the central purchasing body, the continuity and quality of the service for the supply of RGS** and eIDAS certificates; - To promote the consistency of digital public services open to users and facilitate their adoption, thanks to interfaces and operating modes that are similar from one local administration to another; - To promote the dematerialisation of exchanges in order to save time, eliminate time or location constraints, reduce costs related to paper and postage, and optimise the tracking and searching of documents; - To allow fully digital management of data and documents produced internally or transmitted by partners, whether they are administrations, citizens or suppliers.
sig_95cf5ff5ad4732ed2382.title: CONTRACT FOR THE SUPPLY OF RGS** AND EIDAS 2.0 AUTHENTICATION AND SIGNATURE CERTIFICATES (NATURAL PERSONS) AND SERVER CERTIFICATES (WEB)

sig_95d910cedef83f709841.description: DESCRIPTION OF THE SUBJECT The subject of the procurement currently being prepared is a company, credit and control information retrieval service for the use of Valtiokonttori. Valtiokonttori is an agency under the Ministry of Finance (VM), which is responsible for state debt management, investment and financial services, as well as the administration and supervision of state loans, guarantees, warranties and interest subsidies. In addition, it handles the state's central accounting and the preparation of financial statements, as well as compensation and benefit matters. Valtiokonttori maintains a financial information repository for municipalities and wellbeing services counties, produces analysis and reporting services for the state administration, manages the EU's Recovery and Resilience Facility, and maintains an electronic procurement notification system. Valtiokonttori manages loans, interest subsidies and state guarantees and warranties granted by the state. Up-to-date company, credit and control information is needed daily, e.g. in making payment and grant decisions and in risk management. The goal of Valtiokonttori is to renew the currently used - company and credit information retrieval service - control service - integration into the Microsoft Dynamics CRM system The service has approximately 40 users, of which 2 users act as main users. The subject of the procurement possibly also includes a sanctions list retrieval service. GENERAL Please note that this is a prior information notice (hereinafter notice) and this notice does not yet request tenders. We ask companies interested in tendering to register for the market dialogue concerning the competitive tendering. By registering for the market dialogue, companies interested in tendering have the opportunity to engage in a dialogue regarding the procurement with the contracting authority. Participation or non-participation in the market dialogue does not prevent participation in a possible procurement procedure. The notice does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement procedure. All information presented in this notice is preliminary and indicative prior information. This notice does not bind the contracting authority to any kind of decision. Hansel Oy is in a consultative role in this competitive tendering. MARKET DIALOGUE The market dialogue is intended for companies interested in tendering and includes commenting on draft tender documentation before the publication of the final call for tenders. In addition to written comments on the draft tender documentation, the Contracting Authority reserves the possibility to meet interested companies in Teams meetings. REGISTRATION FOR THE MARKET DIALOGUE We ask companies interested in tendering in the competitive tendering to register for the market dialogue by providing the following information by email to the address kilpailutus@hansel.fi with the subject "VK/4262/2025 Valtiokonttorin company, credit and control information retrieval service": • company name and business ID • name of the contact person • email address of the contact person. We ask you to register no later than 6.11.2025, but registration is also possible after this. The personal data of those who have registered will only be used for contacts related to this competitive tendering. Personal data will only be stored for the duration of the preparation of the competitive tendering in question and any related tendering process.
sig_95d910cedef83f709841.title: Valtiokonttorin company, credit and control information retrieval service

sig_95f9baedbbe9315de7ed.description: The aim of this procedure is to procure modern and autonomous mobile systems intended for monitoring fruit and vegetable crops. The Contracting Authority expects the delivery of three systems in identical hardware and functional configuration, enabling their parallel use in different locations or by different user teams. The subject of the contract is a complete, integrated system combining the functions of a mobile robotic platform, measurement, data acquisition and processing systems, and analytical software supporting plant condition assessment. The aim of the contract is to create a tool enabling repeatable, automated and spatially located measurements in actual agricultural and horticultural production conditions, in a more accurate and efficient manner than classical manual observations. The system is to support ongoing crop monitoring and provide data for the further development of analytical algorithms, including solutions based on artificial intelligence methods. The ordered robots are to act as mobile measurement platforms, capable of working in various agrotechnical conditions. The robots must be adapted to work in actual agricultural conditions, including variable ground, terrain unevenness, moisture, dust, mud, vegetation and farm infrastructure elements. Each system should also be adapted for transport between locations and include appropriate transport equipment enabling safe loading and unloading without the use of specialist lifting devices.
sig_95f9baedbbe9315de7ed.title: Construction and delivery of a robot meeting the requirements of precision horticulture in the form of an autonomous electric platform equipped with remote sensing sensors

sig_9615901c52843cc4f9ad.description: Danmarks Nationalbank ("Nationalbanken") is Denmark's central bank. Nationalbanken's operations are based on the Act on Danmarks Nationalbank from 1936, according to which Nationalbanken's task is to maintain a secure monetary system in Denmark and to facilitate and regulate the circulation of money and lending. This task description remains applicable to Nationalbanken's role and responsibility as a central bank. Nationalbanken performs a number of socially critical tasks, including the operation and monitoring of critical payment infrastructure as well as the exercise of central monetary policy functions. The processes, systems and data supporting these tasks are of crucial importance for financial stability and confidence in the Danish financial system. Nationalbanken's business needs must ensure that the contract supports a high level of delivery security, robustness and continuity in the provision of the Services. The Supplier is therefore expected to exhibit a proactive approach to both daily delivery and the handling of risks, opportunities for improvement and technological development. Nationalbanken has a high focus on information security, and the Supplier must ensure a security level corresponding to that found in comparable organisations with a corresponding threat profile. Nationalbanken's security requirements apply to all deliveries and activities carried out for or on behalf of Nationalbanken as part of the provision of the Contract's Services. This places high demands on security, robustness and operational resilience. On this basis, requirements are set that the Supplier must, throughout the contract period, be certified according to ISO/IEC 27001:2022 or an equivalent international standard. In addition, the Contract requires that the Supplier complies with SWIFT CSP requirements and can document this compliance to both Nationalbanken and SWIFT. Nationalbanken primarily uses Microsoft-based technologies and tools in its IT architecture and system support. Furthermore, Service Delivery Management is based on ITIL v3 principles and processes. The purpose of the contract is to establish supplier cooperation for the delivery of services related to IT workplaces, device management, on-site support and service desk. The IT workplace includes, among other things, the supply and support of desktop computers, laptops and peripheral equipment, as well as service desk functions and related operational and support services. In addition, support for tablets and smartphones. In connection with the implementation of Windows 11, Nationalbanken has carried out a major replacement of older devices, which has led to a significant modernisation of Nationalbanken's PC portfolio. This is a high-end PC model issued to all employees and external consultants. The Supplier must in this connection acquire ownership of certain assets (hardware). The Supplier must act as a central contact interface (Single Point of Contact) for the covered services and engage in close cooperation with Nationalbanken's internal functions, Nationalbanken's Service Integrator and other suppliers. Nationalbanken uses a multi-supplier setup, and the Supplier must therefore support effective integration and cooperation with other suppliers, including relevant service management processes and tools. The Customer makes the Customer's ITSM solution available to the Supplier for use in the subsequent provision of the services. The Supplier must use Nationalbanken's ITSM solution for the processes, case registrations, knowledge articles, updates and activities designated by Nationalbanken. Likewise, Nationalbanken makes a collaboration platform available to the Supplier for use in the collaboration between Nationalbanken and the Supplier. The Supplier may be met with requirements to observe the Act on Transfer of Undertakings.
sig_9615901c52843cc4f9ad.title: Tender for contract regarding IT workstations, device management and service desk

sig_966964fa4ce72f0599dd.description: Sunderland City Council ("the Council") is undertaking Preliminary Market Engagement regarding the proposed opportunity to appoint a Managing Agent to provide a range of key services at the Council's Business Centres as identified in the draft Specification ("the Centres"). The Council would welcome feedback regarding the draft Specification, the procurement timetable and the general delivery model to be shared within this Preliminary Market Engagement Questionnaire. A draft Specification has also been shared, detailing an overview of the proposed requirements, however, please note this document is currently in draft form only and therefore remains subject to further development by the Council. Please complete and share information that you feel is relevant to the response to each question. As detailed within the draft Specification, all of the Centres are currently managed in-house by the Council and together, as at July 2025, are home to 75 businesses, collectively employing a total of 363 people. It is now considered that external expertise is required to provide a combination of strategic and operational leadership to work alongside the Council in order to drive optimum performance from the Centres, both in terms of securing operational efficiencies and maximising their economic impact, which are the Council's dual objectives. It is proposed that the Managing Agent would be required to deliver the following core services for the Council: • Strategic management of the Centres including targeted improvement of operational practices. • Marketing and lettings of vacant spaces. • Integrated culture of business development / support to stimulate business growth and expansion. • ICT Managed Service Provision available to businesses on an opt in / opt out concession basis and • Provision of routine repairs and maintenance. The proposed roles of the Managing Agent and the Council are further described in the draft Specification. Lot 1: .
sig_966964fa4ce72f0599dd.title: The Appointment of a Managing Agent for Sunderland City Council Business Centres

sig_96b721fbe0907b462a8b.description: Modernisation of the central firewall system in the Forschungsverbund Berlin e.V. Lot LOT-0000: Modernisation of the central firewall system in the Forschungsverbund Berlin e.V.. The aim of the project is the modernisation of the overall firewall and security architecture incl. next-generation endpoint protection of the research association. The future solution must meet the current and future requirements for information security, availability, scalability, multi-tenancy, traceability of administrative activities and economical operation. General requirements for the new firewall structure: - Multi-stage firewall structure with centrally operated perimeter firewall cluster and segmentation firewall clusters per institute, whereby different manufacturers must be provided (dual-vendor strategy) B-criterion in BM - VLAN- and IP-based institute-related segmentation - Virtual domains for segmentation of the perimeter firewall of corporate IT - At least two appliances per geographical location in active-passive operation - Expansion of backbone throughput to 10 gigabits per second with the option to expand to 40 gigabits per second without replacing the hardware as well as loop-free design of the network - Number of simultaneous sessions: 20.000 to 65.000; number of VPN uses per institute: at least 40 to 70 users; maximum all employees in the FVB (1.600 employees) - Consideration of QoS mechanisms for VoIP and latency-sensitive applications - Granular, association-wide uniform role and authorisation concept for administrative access - Multi-factor authentication for users (native or via identity provider) and administrators (native) - NGFW functionalities: o IPS and IDS o Application IP o Geo IP filter - Separation of networks (e.g. laboratory networks) via VLAN - Central DNS security service, DoS defence, content filtering and advanced threat protection as well as the integration of external blacklists at perimeter level - Powerful and practicable DoS defence - Common, multi-tenant WAF service for web applications - Platform support for VPN access for Windows, Linux and MacOS - Compliance check for all operating systems - Central management for perimeter (mandatory) and segmentation firewalls (optional) - Tenant separation with granular graduation of administration rights - Open interfaces to support REST- or XML-based APIs, Syslog, Net-Flow/IPFIX, SAML, LDAP, RADIUS and other common market integration interfaces - Remote access: the support of established procedures with split tunnelling and carrier-grade NAT must be provided - Identification of institute affiliation, for example via certificates or naming conventions - SSL interception (inbound for published services as well as outbound for critical servers/clients - E-mail security, multi-tenant, optionally acquirable per institute - Sandbox functions - Out-of-band management - Min. interface for the automatic integration of certificates - IPv6 future-proofing (a conversion to IPv6 is not planned within the scope of the project) - Central, multi-tenant log management with at least three months retention period, local buffering or short-term fallback retention and interfaces to a possible SIEM - Tenant-related and institute-specific logging Suitable support and service services must be offered for the procured hardware, software, subscriptions and management components. These include fault clearance, maintenance, software support, manufacturer and system house support, hardware replacement, patch and release management, operational support and a comprehensible escalation process. The availability of the future solution is to be set at at least 99,9 % per year. The specific SLA design, in particular reaction times, recovery times, service times, planned change windows and emergency changes, will be discussed jointly in dialogue taking into account redundancy, economic efficiency and operational risk. In addition, NOC services with security analysis must be provided by the future service provider. Pure SOC services are to be treated as a supplementary option or add-on. For SOC-related services, in particular monitoring, triage, analysis, alerting, initial processing, incident response, notification chains, on-call duty, multi-tenancy, SIEM/SOAR connection, log sources, sensor technology, reporting and communication channels must be considered.
sig_96b721fbe0907b462a8b.title: Modernisation of the central firewall system in Forschungsverbund Berlin e.V.

sig_971ad5f0459d229fae7b.description: The contracting authority is PD - Berater der Öffentlichen Hand GmbH. A client of the contracting authority has established 2021 with the Quality Sign for Sustainable Buildings (QNG), an umbrella brand for sustainable construction in Germany. The Quality Sign for Sustainable Buildings (QNG) is intended to promote sustainable construction on a broad scale in Germany and to ensure a minimum quality for "sustainable buildings". In addition, it is intended to create a legally secure basis for the award of funding that enables grants in the construction sector to be in compliance with social objectives (sustainability objectives). Since 2022 the contracting authority has been supporting the client with the establishment and setting up of a QNG office with all associated activities, such as a hotline, operation of a website and further development of the QNG requirements with the associated publications. In order to provide up-to-date information on the seal and the processes to be observed, the QNG website https://www.qng.info/ was developed and set up in the year 2022 with an external service provider. The QNG website represents a knowledge platform that processes ongoing developments and changes, and provides users with basic procedures, interfaces and assistance. The contract is awarded in two lots: - Lot 1: Hosting, further development and support of the existing website - Lot 2: Technical support (pool of experts) for the Quality Sign for Sustainable Buildings (QNG). The lot-specific tasks are described in more detail below. Bids may be submitted for one or for both lots. The contractor assumes continuous support, operation, hosting, and provision of the server infrastructure for the operation of the already existing website. Services include: 1. Website support, provision of licences 2. Website hosting and optimisation 3. Hosting and further development of an AI-based, self-learning chatbot The contractor shall ensure a seamless transition from 01. January 2027. The contract has a term of 4 years. The basis for the award in Lot 1 is an EVB-IT cloud contract.; The pool of experts is intended to provide support for consultations on enquiries resulting from the application of the QNG in practice, as well as for the further development of the QNG requirements and the introduction and implementation phase of the revised requirements. Services include: • Support for the content-related further development of the quality seal • Support for the revision and quality assurance of the associated documents with regard to comprehensibility and technical correctness • Support for the creation or revision of accompanying materials such as FAQs and quick answers • Creation of training materials for certification bodies and auditors as part of the introduction of the revised requirements • Support for the processing of complex or technically demanding enquiries, where applicable support for the ongoing quality assurance of new FAQs and quick answers The commencement of services is 01.01.2027. The contract has a term of 4 years. The basis for the award in Lot 2 is a service contract. There is no fixed purchase quantity. The estimated volume results from the estimated quantity specified in the price sheet. The contract is limited to 280.000 euro.

This market dialogue is a replacement/update of previously completed market dialogues. See previously completed market dialogue: https://doffin.no/notices/2023-653193 Invitation to market dialogue - Framework agreement for the procurement of digital joint user equipment/AV equipment and the accompanying services Bærum municipality invites tenderers to a market dialogue with suppliers for a framework agreement for the procurement of digital joint user equipment/AV equipment and accompanying services. The aim of the procurement is to replace the current framework agreement for the procurement of "Digital joint user equipment - meeting room equipment and infotainment". The new agreement will cover an equivalent area and the need for digital joint user equipment (DFB) for all entities and buildings where Bærum municipality is responsible for such joint equipment. The municipality has separate agreements for client control and user-related equipment. Bærum municipality would like to invite the market to a dialogue in connection with a coming procurement in order to cover the municipality ́s need for digital joint user equipment/AV with the accompanying services. The intention is that the agreement shall cover Bærum municipality ́s total need for digital joint user equipment/AV equipment, entertainment, meeting room equipment, accessories and accompanying services in the contract period. The contract shall ensure that digital joint user equipment/AV equipment for Bærum municipality ́s entities and buildings always has access to updated equipment/products and services with modern and good quality. The aim is not to replace the existing equipment that covers the current user need. In addition to the delivery and operation of new equipment, we would like a new supplier to provide support and service for the current equipment. The consultancy services will be strengthened in the contract and the tenderer must reckon on assisting the Contracting Authority as needed, both as regards assessment/supplementation of equipment, support and maintenance. Expanded support and assistance can be required at major events and video conferences. The aim of the market dialogue is to gain insight into the market now and forward, establish increased knowledge on the supplier market, inform about the coming planned procurement and get any feedback on the planned procurement before the announcement. Bærum municipality is one of Norway's largest municipalities. Both inhabitants and employees have high expectations for the municipality ́s IT systems, both in regard to response, availability, information security, cost efficiency as well as the ability to implement new functions quickly and efficiently. According to Bærum municipality ́s digitalisation strategy, the municipality ́s employees and inhabitants shall experience "One Bærum - digital first choice" via, among other things, access to best and correct practices in service deliveries, access to process support and technology to simplify our own everyday lives and get a better tool for interaction, case processing and service production. The procurement is planned to be carried out as a tender contest with notice before summer 2026. Tenderers are invited to a joint card information meeting in Kommunegården in Sandvika for orientation of the upcoming planned procurement friday 13.03.2026, 09:00 – 10.00. Tenderers who register for the market dialogue will be sent parts of the tender documentation draft for a planned competition, so that they can provide input on the tender documentation before the competition is announced. The aim of the written input is to get a general description of the tenderer ́s system and feedback sent out documentation and a planned procurement. The meetings will be confidential and only for internal use by the work group in the municipality. Input from the dialogue can be used in the subsequent competition. sig_97ade33b90377832169a.description: Procurement of an integrated chromatographic instrument and data management platform for an analytical research laboratory Lot LOT-0001: Chromatography Data System (CDS). Procurement, delivery, installation, configuration, integration, commissioning, training, documentation, warranty and support of a Chromatography Data System (CDS) as a central platform for instrument control, data acquisition, data processing, reporting, auditability and controlled management of chromatographic data. The CDS must support the integration of the analytical systems procured under lots 2 to 5 and provide functions for data integrity, user and role management as well as for connection to institutional data management structures. Lot LOT-0002: GC-MS/FID system. Procurement, delivery, installation, commissioning, integration, training, documentation, warranty and support of a gas chromatography-mass spectrometry system with a dual detector configuration consisting of a flame ionisation detector (FID) and a single quadrupole mass spectrometer (MSD). The system is used for the qualitative and quantitative analysis of small molecules and metabolites in complex sample matrices and must support integration into the central Chromatography Data System (CDS). Lot LOT-0003: UHPLC with dual detection. Procurement, delivery, installation, commissioning, integration, training, documentation, warranty and support of an ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography system (UHPLC) with dual detection consisting of a PDA/DAD detector and a universal gradient-compatible detector for non-UV-absorbing compounds. The system is used for the separation, detection and quantification of organic compounds in complex matrices and must support integration into the central Chromatography Data System (CDS). Lot LOT-0004: LC-MS single quadrupole. Procurement, delivery, installation, commissioning, integration, training, documentation, warranty and support of an LC-MS single quadrupole system with an integrated liquid chromatography front end. The system is used for the qualitative and quantitative analysis of small molecules, metabolites and impurities as well as for carrying out high-throughput screening workflows including flow injection analysis (FIA). Integration into the central Chromatography Data System (CDS) must be ensured. Lot LOT-0005: Semi-preparative HPLC. Procurement, delivery, installation, commissioning, integration, training, documentation, warranty and support of a semi-preparative HPLC system for the isolation, purification and recovery of organic compounds in the milligram to gram range. The system must support automated and traceable fraction collection, purification workflows and integration into the central Chromatography Data System (CDS).

sig_981f60924d2f84773b74.description: GENERAL This is not a procurement notice or request for tenders, and the notice does not launch a procurement procedure. The aim of this information request and market sounding is to obtain additional information on options available on the market and to hear suppliers' views on the subject of the procurement so that any subsequent procurement procedure can be carried out appropriately. Answering the information request or participating in the market sounding has no effect on the position of market operators in any actual procurement procedure that may be initiated later. BACKGROUND AND SUBJECT OF THE PROCUREMENT Digi- ja väestötietovirasto (DVV) is planning and preparing a procurement through which, on the basis of the resulting contract or contracts, DVV may procure, as needed, the printing and processing services for the right-to-vote notifications (so-called notification card) and their annexes defined in the Election Act, as well as other related printing, enveloping and folding services. The whole to be put out to tender includes - the production of paper and electronic notification cards and their delivery for sending, as well as - the distribution service for paper notification cards in accordance with the Postal Act, and the return of undelivered consignments to the sender address - in the case of electronic consignments, their transfer for sending to the Suomi.fi Messages service, and the production of the metadata required for this - expert services for preparing the graphic layout of these consignments In addition, the procurement may include other information letters for European Parliament elections as well as regional and municipal elections. The regular elections during the new contract period in the years 2027-2030 will be the following: 1. Parliamentary elections 2027 2. Regional and municipal elections 2029 3. European Parliament elections 2029 4. Presidential election 2030 In addition to regular elections, the contract covers any other elections that will be held during the contract period. Occurrence in the contract period is determined according to the date of election day (in the case of the presidential election, 1. election). Such non-regular elections may be, for example, a presidential election held mid-term due to the death or permanent incapacitation of the president, or early parliamentary elections ordered by the President of the Republic, or elections to be rerun following a court decision as a result of an appeal. In addition to elections, the contract also covers corresponding procurements in state consultative referendums. The notification card is regulated by section 21 of the Election Act. Other election-related information drawn up by the Ministry of Justice may be attached to the notification card consignment. As a rule, in all election types, in addition to the notification card sheet itself, a list of advance polling stations in the recipient's local area and an information insert about the body to be elected in the election are attached to the consignment. In addition, in the presidential election, two notification cards are sent to each person entitled to vote, one for each (possible) round of the two-round election. Other attachments are also possible; for example, during the pandemic caused by the Covid19 virus, municipal elections held featured an additional insert page about health safety in voting. The smallest composition for a notification card consignment is 3 sheets (notification card, one sheet for the list of advance polling stations, information leaflet about the body to be elected), and at most the size of the consignment could be (estimated) 7 sheets. The purpose of the notification card is to provide information on the approach of elections and the recipient's right to vote in them, and to give them the opportunity to request further information and, if necessary, rectification from the authority in good time if they consider that any information relating to their right to vote shown on the notification card is incorrect. In some rarer situations, the notification card can also be used to streamline the voting procedure, but it is never a prerequisite for voting or sufficient proof of identity and right to vote at the polling station. Notification cards are drawn up on forms according to the formula confirmed by the Ministry of Justice (VaaliL 193 §). For paper consignments of notification cards, their manufacturer produces windowed envelopes with election-specific prints and takes care of enveloping the consignments. Regarding the regular elections of the contract period put out to tender, estimates of the quantities of electronic and paper letter post are presented in the annex to this notice. The stated estimates of the distributions of the format and delivery method of notification cards have been estimated on the basis that the legislation on the priority of digital official communication will be completed and its application will begin in the spring of 2026. INFORMATION REQUEST AND MARKET SOUNDING The information request section of this notice presents questions to potential tenderer candidates interested in the procurement. The information request aims to survey market operators' views on, among other things, whether it is appropriate to put the service package out to tender in one or two parts (production and distribution separately). On the basis of the responses received to the information request, DVV may, at its discretion, also hold more detailed bilateral discussions on the specifications of the procurement and/or request comments on the preliminary tender documents from those who responded to the information request prior to the actual procurement.
sig_981f60924d2f84773b74.title: Information request and market sounding: Production and distribution services for election notification cards 2027-2030

sig_985973cf72f36e8bcb7b.description: All Zurich notaries are simultaneously bankruptcy offices and land registry offices. Zurich bankruptcy offices are obliged not only to keep their own files from a bankruptcy proceeding, but also the business files of the respective bankrupt company. The statutory retention obligation is generally 10 years (for individual files 30 years). In particular for the ten-year retention of business files, the notaries currently operate nine so-called central archives. The nine central archives are located at seven sites and are each affiliated with a local bankruptcy office/notary. The management of an archive (storage inventory, additions and removals) is carried out by a notary employee from the local notary. An IT application provides an overall overview of the capacity utilisation of the individual archives. The increasing number of bankruptcies in the Canton of Zurich means that the volume of bankruptcy and business files is also increasing and the existing central archives of the notaries are reaching the limit of their capacity, and in some cases have already reached it. For this reason and the need not to additionally burden the bankruptcy offices of the canton with storage services, the management of the Notary Inspectorate has decided to outsource the storage of bankruptcy files as a future-proof, scalable solution.
sig_985973cf72f36e8bcb7b.title: Centralised archiving for bankruptcy files

In total, the measured values, up to 40.000 - 50.000 data points, are collected and archived in the smallest possible resolution (> 1 second). They serve as a data source for the Asset Framework, PI Vision, a simulation server, as well as for external customers who need to access live and historical data. For this purpose, the API interface of the PI System is also required. The retention of historical data goes back to the year 1999. It includes all existing measured values and data points. These are permanently mapped in the PI Data Archive and are therefore available for retrieval within milliseconds at any time. The following questionnaire is intended to evaluate whether a migration to an alternative system is possible and economically viable.

sig_99f9bef848b651fa1187.description: This Expression of Interest (EOI) outlines Macmillan Cancer Support's request for agencies to collaborate on designing, testing and delivering a new cancer information and support offer(s). The project is part of Macmillan's 2025 strategy commitment to reach more people living with cancer and to improve the support we offer for people who experience inequitable access to cancer care and treatment. The design challenge for this project is "How Might We develop a scalable solution that helps people understand their rights, choices and influence in decisions about their care, irrespective of their confidence, self-advocacy skills or system knowledge?" This is an end-to-end Innovation project that we require to be delivered in its entirety by the supplier(s), with input and guidance from Macmillan. This includes insight development and analysis, solution development, prototyping and testing of a Minimum Viable Product (MVP). The solution should be scalable and likely be digital or include digital elements. The supplier must have extensive experience designing with communities and individuals that are marginalised. The supplier should be an expert in approaches including designing from the margins and embed meaningful and equitable participatory approaches into every phase of the project. Given the nature of the requirements, we are open to working with 2 suppliers who can deliver different elements or phases of the project. The agency must be able to recruit participants who reflect Macmillan's priority cancer support audiences to take part in user research, co-design and testing of solutions; people who have been diagnosed with cancer in the past 5 years. This includes people who are currently undergoing anti-cancer treatment (more details in attachment). Timelines • Expression of interest response deadline by 10/03/2026. • Selected agencies will receive the full RFP pack in March / April. • The anticipated project duration is 4-6 months from kick-off. The final timeline will be agreed with Macmillan during the tender process. Supplier Response Instructions Via email, interested suppliers should provide: (1) A brief outline of their research, design and innovation approach, including how they will use design from the margin approaches (see examples here); (2) evidence of prior engagement and participatory work with marginalised communities (3) evidence of developing and delivering scalable products and/or services (especially digital) (4) identification of gaps in their ability to meet the full requirements and if there are gaps (5) willingness to partner with another agency. Responses at this stage do not need to be extensive. Responses should be sent to procurement@macmillan.org.uk with the subject line EOI - Innovation Advocacy/Empowerment.
sig_99f9bef848b651fa1187.title: Expression of Interest for a Macmillan Cancer Support Innovation project

sig_9a717a6eb198dcbccd00.description: Terveyden ja hyvinvoinnin laitos (THL) is planning a tender for a condition monitoring system for its Kuopio office. THL is an independent state expert and research institute that promotes the well-being, health and safety of people. The institute's laboratories store millions of samples as well as reagents required for analytics in various storage conditions. The condition monitoring system must centrally collect temperature and alarm data from all measurement points. The primary objective of the system is to provide alarms when temperature limits are exceeded and to manage these alarms. The system must also be able to monitor and record condition data in both normal and alarm conditions. Monitoring and operational update tasks are intended to be performed by THL users. The intention is that the system will include all components required from measurement to alarm and data recording, with the exception of THL's existing sensors used in deep-freeze freezers (Pt100), which are intended to be used as part of the system. THL's Kuopio office deep-freeze freezers currently use approximately 20 Pt100 sensors. The deep-freeze freezers have a separate 4-conductor Pt-100 sensor, which is attached to the transmitter with a spring loaded connector. sig_9b0dcb019dbedcf267c5.description: Procurement of research-based services in the project "Digital Smart Regulations" for occupational health and safety - Development and testing of approaches for the use of digitised regulations and rules in occupational health and safety Lot LOT-0001: Procurement of research-based services in the project "Digital Smart Regulations" for occupational health and safety. Starting point of the project: Digital solutions are useful for the drafting, provision and application of technical rules in the field of occupational health and safety. This applies both to rule-making in the occupational health and safety committees at the Federal Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs (see https://www.bmas.de/DE/Arbeit/Arbeitsschutz/Arbeitsschutzausschuesse/arbeitsschutzausschuesse.html ), as well as to the publication of the rules by the BMAS and their application in companies as well as for advice and enforcement. In the field of standardisation, the concept "Digital Smart Standards" is available from the Digital Standards Initiative by DIN and DKE (IDiS) (see https://www.dke.de/idis ). This was applied as an example in a previous research project F 2542 of the BAuA (see https://www.baua.de/DE/Forschung/Forschungsprojekte/f2542 and project website https://digiasr.blogs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/ ). A methodology for the step-by-step development of machine-readable and machine-executable testing rules was derived from this (A. Aziz, D. Napps, M. König, S. Gabriel, A. Richter, S. Voß (2025): Approaches for the transformation of technical rules for workplaces into digital rules. https://www.baua.de/DE/Angebote/Publikationen/Fokus/F2542-2). Subject matter of the contract and objectives: Based on the existing approaches and findings, a study is to be conducted to investigate the extent to which approaches for "Digital Smart Standards" can be transferred to further areas of the body of regulations and rules on occupational health and safety, and whether the occupational health and safety rules drawn up in the occupational health and safety committees can be converted into "Digital Smart Regulations", i.e. into level 2 "Machine-readable document", and further developed in future for level 3 "Machine-readable and executable content" and level 4 "Machine-readable and interpretable content". This study is the subject of the services to be provided by the contractor. The aim is to draw up recommendations for action for the further digitalisation of occupational health and safety regulations and rules in Germany. In key technical application contexts and use cases, which are to be selected in cooperation with the occupational health and safety committees at the BMAS, the processes from creation through management and provision to the operational application of rules as well as implementation options must be considered. Requirements from occupational health and safety regulations and rules must be taken into account in practice, particularly during risk assessments by employers. The contractor must therefore investigate in the project how the contents of the occupational health and safety rules can be applied in exemplary digital implementations of the risk assessment processes and in any existing data models and coordinated with further requirements. The contractor systematically compiles and evaluates the results and derives concrete recommendations for action based on them. The project contributes to making the respective body of rules clearer and easier to apply digitally for users in future, as well as to making the processes for creating, further developing, administering and providing the rules more efficient.
sig_9b0dcb019dbedcf267c5.title: Procurement of research-based services in the project "Digital Smart Regulations" for occupational health and safety

sig_9bbc52f64dff547fec2a.description: The Göttinger Verkehrsbetriebe GmbH (GöVB) is a municipal transport company 100% owned by the City of Göttingen. It operates local public transport in the city of Göttingen and adjacent regions and ensures the daily mobility of residents and guests with its bus fleet. As a sectoral contracting authority within the meaning of § 100 of the Act against Restraints of Competition (GWB), GöVB is responsible for the procurement of services and systems that secure the operation and further development of local public transport. GöVB pursues the goal of gradually converting its bus fleet to alternative, in particular electric, drive systems. In doing so, it makes a significant contribution to sustainable mobility, the reduction of emissions, and the achievement of the climate targets of the City of Göttingen. The expansion of the e-bus fleet is accompanied by a considerable need for modern charging infrastructure that enables efficient, reliable, and economical operational management. To support this transformation, GöVB is planning the introduction of a charging and load management system (LLEMS). This system is intended to enable intelligent control and monitoring of all charging processes at the depot and, in the future, also in scheduled service. The focus is on ensuring vehicle availability, grid and load optimisation, and the safe and economical operation of electromobility in local public transport in Göttingen.

sig_9c80d0bb7dbdefcd3c06.description: Revenue Scotland is seeking information from the market in relation to the next version of / replacement for its existing tax administration platform, SETS. The current platform supports the collection and operational management of devolved Scottish taxes. It enables taxpayers and their agents to submit tax returns and make payments to Revenue Scotland, and enables staff to process returns, manage taxpayer records through a number of statutory processes, reconcile inbound & outbound payments with tax declared, and undertake tax compliance activity and operational casework. Lot 1: . Revenue Scotland is seeking a strategic partner to help it deliver and support a cloud-hosted tax administration and case management platform for the collection and operational management of devolved taxes in Scotland. The system will manage tax data, support staff in administering tax returns and taxpayer records, and enable efficient case management of statutory tax management processes, workflow automation, and integration with external systems. Additionally, the solution needs to provide reporting capabilities in terms of management information and data export to our own analytics platform. We anticipate additional taxes and legislative change being introduced over the lifetime of the contract, and so the solution should be flexible enough to easily accommodate new functionality. Through this Prior Information Notice, Revenue Scotland wishes to consider the fullest range of modern, UK-based cloud-based solutions which support: - A portal for taxpayers and agents to view, edit and submit tax information - case management - workflow automation - operational processing - integration with other corporate systems such as our finance (general ledger) systems, contact management (telephony), and third-party print and post solutions. The next version of SETS will support at least five taxes and must provide a highly configurable and scalable platform capable of supporting evolving tax policy and operational requirements. Currently up to 80 back-office staff users across a range of different functional teams use the platform. Revenue Scotland welcomes engagement from suppliers with experience of delivering platforms capable of supporting complex administration and case management.. This contract may be split into lots, where market intelligence has suggested this to be viable and beneficial
sig_9c80d0bb7dbdefcd3c06.title: Scottish Electronic Tax System (SETS)

sig_9cb691d0cc2d7ff560c5.description: Salon kaupunki (hereinafter contracting authority/subscriber) invites tenders for the procurement of a recruitment system in accordance with this invitation to tender and its annexes. The subject of the procurement is a browser-based recruitment system as an off-the-shelf solution and software as a service (SaaS) for the City of Salo for the management and coordination of the recruitment process and substitution pooling. The off-the-shelf solution seeks a software service that is quick to deploy and continuously developed by the supplier. The procurement consists of the following main components: • Recruitment system • Substitution recruitment system • Implementation project, including main user training & test plan • Support and maintenance services • Opportunity to use the training database • Integration opportunities The objective is to provide the city with a reliable and user-friendly recruitment system. The system must also provide a user-friendly and as automated as possible platform for the management and coordination of substitutes. The objective is a clear and easy-to-use tool for use by the entire organisation. The system must be up-to-date and renewable. The system must include the software supplier's support services and introductions to any new features for users. In addition, the system must have good and efficient reporting and analytics features. The contract period is intended to start in February 2028. The contract will be concluded as an open-ended contract with a six-month notice period on both sides. The requirements for the subject of the procurement, i.e., the recruitment system, are described in the invitation to tender and its annexes.

sig_9d9ffc50e7cd2401e0ac.description: The contracting authority is tendering a contract regarding Transition In, development of the Modernised Support Systems, application operation, application maintenance, support, ordering services, including further development of the Support Systems, as well as Transition Out. The contract consists of the following 3 main services: I. Transition In, including, among other things, a secure and stable takeover of the application responsibility for the Support Systems, implementation of, for example, project management, transition organisation, transfer of source code and documentation, implementation of technical transition and necessary transformation, takeover of knowledge from the outgoing supplier as well as establishment of the operations organisation, including establishment of the collaboration with the operations supplier. II. Ongoing services for the Support Systems, including; a. Support, including, among other things, responsibility for Service Desk, user administration, handling of incidents, problems, service requests, early life support, cf. the operational processes, with the aim of ensuring high availability for the users; b. Application operation, including, among other things, database operation, operation of middleware, backup, restore, monitoring and logging, 2. and 3. line support, configuration, patch, and release and deployment management, cf. the operational processes, and operational reporting with high requirements for uptime and response times; c. Application maintenance, including, among other things, ongoing and preventive maintenance of the IT systems, minor changes, new versions, bug fixes, release management, cf. the operational processes, with the aim of supporting high requirements for uptime and response times; d. Governance, including close collaboration with the operations supplier, operational processes, security services, documentation and operational reporting. III. Agile development, e.g. via a design and planning phase, including proof of concept, as well as a development phase based on the supplier's product vision and advice. Development of the Modernised Support Systems takes place agilely in close collaboration between the parties regarding support for the contracting authority's business goals and needs, so that the Modernised Support Systems can be implemented after a time-limited period. Development includes any new functionality as well as any re-implementation and reuse of parts of the current Support Systems. Further development of the Support Systems also takes place agilely in close collaboration between the parties. It is the contracting authority's business need that all services are delivered with high delivery reliability and robustness, and that the supplier demonstrates proactivity in the collaboration. In Transition In, the supplier must take over the application responsibility for the Support Systems and, from the transition day, deliver ongoing services, including, among other things, application operation, application maintenance and further development, to the Support Systems. The further development will take place in a close, agile collaboration with the contracting authority. The supplier must also, in a close, agile collaboration with the contracting authority, carry out a modernisation of the Support Systems based on the contracting authority's modernisation wishes. The Support Systems are part of the overall joint municipal infrastructure, and the supplier must therefore collaborate partly with the other suppliers, including the operations supplier as well as suppliers who deliver other parts of the joint municipal infrastructure, and partly with users of the infrastructure. It is the contracting authority's business goal and need, among other things, to give parts of the current Support Systems a quality boost in the form of a modernisation that supports the Modernised Support Systems appearing attractive, reliable, future-proof and secure, so that the municipalities also in the future have a strong foundation to deliver the best digital services to the citizens in an increasingly more coherent, efficient and modern public sector.
sig_9d9ffc50e7cd2401e0ac.title: Tender for Support Systems

The contracting authority shall conclude a contract for a period of 12 calendar months with a single economic operator, following the application of the simplified procedure, for the provision of simulator maintenance services, as follows:  Existing simulator software maintenance – software recommissioning, software repair, ensuring conventional hardware replacement by reinstalling the software; In situations where conventional hardware (standard computers making up the simulator) breaks down, or must be replaced for reasons of physical or moral wear and tear, the contractor shall undertake to ensure the reinstallation of the software on this equipment (procured by the contracting authority/entity), so that the simulator as a whole maintains its functionality;  Specific maintenance of the existing simulator hardware – periodic check and repairs/replacement, cleaning; In situations where specific hardware (proprietary hardware modules or equipment dedicated to the specific operation of the simulator and making up the simulator) breaks down, the contractor shall undertake to ensure its repair or replacement (the costs of these operations being borne by the contracting authority/entity, not forming part of the object of the contract), reinstallation of the equipment so that the simulator as a whole maintains its functionality;  Existing simulator technical support - provision of all available software modifications and remediation of deficiencies contained by the installed system. During the execution of the contract, the contractor's activity shall be carried out as follows:  The contractor shall perform maintenance – computer technical assistance, taking into consideration the latest version marketed by the manufacturer, where applicable, being accompanied by manufacturer licenses;  Any subsequent version must ensure functional requirements and take into account the existing hardware configuration;  If the subsequent version requires standard hardware or software modifications (for example PCs with another configuration, operating systems), the contractor shall communicate this aspect to the contracting authority/entity, before installation, in order to be able to prevent a non-functioning state and so that the buyer can make an appropriate decision;  If required, the contractor shall perform installation and configuration activities of licenses at the buyer, as an extension of the existing system;  The contractor shall provide user, operation and administration documentation in Romanian or English, technical description of database structures, relations between modules and procedures, naming conventions used, etc.;  The contractor shall ensure, at the buyer's request, technical assistance for the installation and configuration of delivered licenses at the buyer's headquarters;  The contractor shall ensure permanent on-line computer and operational technical assistance for software, hardware and operation at the buyer's headquarters, upon request, (no later than 2 (two) working days from the date of announcing the necessity), throughout the contract period;  During the present contract, the contractor shall obligatorily include a service session at the beneficiary's headquarters, with a duration of at least 4 days x 1 man, of which one day for the installation of the new software version. Expenses related to travel shall be borne by the contractor;  The contractor shall train instructors with regard to the novelties/modifications brought by maintenance – computer technical assistance of the software;  The contractor shall ensure the remaking of documents (certificate instructors) certifying that the personnel of the contracting authority/entity are capable of providing appropriate training according to software versions;  In the case of on-site installations (at the contracting authority/entity's headquarters), the service report shall obligatorily have attached a check-list through which all software and hardware modules falling under the incidence of the service contract, respectively all simulator components, will be nominated;  It shall be specified in this check-list, the operating state of all updated (update) or added (new) modules. The verification by the contracting authority/entity of the veracity of these sheets shall take place at the end of the visit, for 1 (one) day, together with the contractor. This day shall be specially dedicated to verifications and shall be included in the on-site intervention period (at the contracting authority/entity's headquarters). Quarterly, the provider's representatives shall draw up a service report (which shall obligatorily contain the simulator model), specifying the operations that were carried out for each individual piece of equipment and signed by both the service provider and the contracting authority/entity. Confirmation can also be made via e-mail.
