Procedure aimed at concluding a framework agreement 3 in parts for Visit Hungary Nemzeti Turisztikai Szervezet Közhasznú Nonprofit Zrt. for the performance of strategic media agency, digital media agency and market research tasks. In order to achieve the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, the Contracting Authority plans to implement complex communication and media campaigns on domestic and foreign target markets. The aim of the Contracting Authority's communication activity is to promote Hungary for tourism purposes, strengthen inbound tourism from abroad, stimulate domestic tourism, and present the Hungarian tourism offering domestically and internationally. The task of the Winning Tenderer is to perform the tasks specified in the Technical Specification for the Client on the basis of the framework agreement, individual orders, and briefs handed over by the Client. The Contracting Authority wishes to conclude a framework agreement for the performance of strategic media agency tasks up to a net framework amount of 3.200.000.000 HUF. The Contracting Authority undertakes an obligation to call off 70% of the framework amount. In order to achieve the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, the Contracting Authority plans to implement complex communication and media campaigns on domestic and foreign target markets. International tourism advertising campaigns may be implemented in multiple countries, with a different media mix and target group approach per country. The task of the Winning Tenderer is to perform strategic media agency, media planning, media buying, campaign management, reporting, and other auxiliary tasks directly related to media appearances for the Client on the basis of the framework agreement, individual orders, and briefs handed over by the Client. The exact professional content, performance deadline, quantity, technical parameters and individual expectations of the tasks are contained in the individual orders. The Contracting Authority's domestic campaigns are typically implemented with a net campaign spend of the magnitude of 250 million HUF, over an average campaign period of 6–8 weeks. Campaigns of the Contracting Authority affecting target markets outside Hungary are typically implemented with a net campaign spend of the magnitude of 80 million HUF, over an average campaign period of 8–10 weeks. Tasks to be performed in particular: - preparation of a media strategy, integrated media mix and media plan in harmony with the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, - preparation of market, media market, competitor and target group analyses adapted to the campaign's objective, target markets, target groups and channels, - strategic media agency tasks on specified channels - preparation, execution and monitoring of campaigns, campaign management, preparation and execution of media buying tasks, and continuous optimisation of campaigns, - proposal for a KPI system adapted to the nature, objective, channels and target markets of the given campaign, as well as tracking, interpretation and evaluation of campaign performance, with special regard to tourism KPIs - preparation of regular, inter-campaign and campaign-closing reports according to an agreed reporting structure. The Winning Tenderer is obliged to designate one permanent contact person. Detailed requirements set against performance are contained in the technical specification and draft contract.; The Contracting Authority wishes to conclude a framework agreement for the performance of digital media agency tasks up to a net framework amount of 820.000.000 HUF. The Contracting Authority undertakes an obligation to call off 70% of the framework amount. In order to achieve the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, the Contracting Authority plans to implement complex communication and digital media campaigns on domestic and foreign target markets. International tourism digital advertising campaigns may be implemented in multiple countries, with a different digital media mix, targeting logic, platform usage and target group approach per country. The task of the Winning Tenderer is to perform digital media agency, digital media planning, digital media buying, campaign management, optimisation, measurement, analytics, reporting, and other auxiliary tasks directly related to digital media appearances for the CA on the basis of the framework agreement, individual orders, and briefs handed over by the CA. The Contracting Authority's domestic digital campaigns are typically implemented with a net budget of the magnitude of 50–60 million HUF, over an average campaign period of 8–9 weeks. Digital campaigns of the Contracting Authority affecting target markets outside Hungary are typically implemented with a net budget of the magnitude of 50–60 million HUF, over an average campaign period of 8–9 weeks. Tasks to be performed in particular: - formulation of a digital campaign strategy and digital media plan, development of digital targeting, platform and channel proposals, - performance of digital media buying and campaign management tasks, continuous tracking and optimisation of campaign performance, support for measurement and analytical settings, - evaluation and reporting of digital KPIs, (with special regard to tourism relevance) - support for the compilation of performance certification documentation, - preparation of a digital campaign strategy, digital media mix and digital media plan in harmony with the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, - preparation of market, digital media market, competitor and target group analyses adapted to the campaign's objective, target markets, target groups, digital channels and advertising platforms, - performance of media agency tasks on specified channels and platforms, - preparation of digital campaigns, - launching of digital campaigns, campaign management, preparation and execution of digital media buying tasks, and continuous optimisation of campaigns, - establishment, management and operation of an agreed advertising account structure, - support for the establishment, operation and, where necessary, development of the measurement environment related to digital campaigns, - preparation of inter-campaign reports and campaign-closing evaluation. The Winning Tenderer is obliged to designate one permanent contact person. Detailed requirements set against performance are contained in the technical specification and draft contract.;

The Contracting Authority wishes to conclude a framework agreement for the performance of market research tasks up to a net framework amount of 320.000.000 HUF. The CA undertakes an obligation to call off 70% of the framework amount. In order to achieve the Contracting Authority's communication objectives, the CA plans to implement complex communication and media campaigns on domestic and foreign target markets. Research and analysis tasks may also cover domestic and international target markets, different target groups, campaigns, brands, destinations, communication objectives, consumer motivations, media usage characteristics, tourism decisions or campaign effectiveness issues. The CA's research projects are of a mixed nature: they include quantitative research with larger sample sizes directed at Hungary and affecting target markets outside Hungary, primary research affecting multiple target markets, as well as smaller-element qualitative, motivational, service quality, mystery shopping or other decision-supporting research tasks. The Contracting Authority generally performs the implementation of a residential quantitative research of 1000 persons once a year in 10-15 countries, and in addition initiates a minimum of 2 qualitative, small-group focus group researches in Hungary (focus groups are generally implemented with 4–8 groups, with an average participation of 6 persons per group) and manages a nationwide mystery shopping annually with a minimum of 80 trial purchases. The task of the Winning Tenderer is to perform market research, data acquisition, analysis and decision-supporting tasks for the CA on the basis of the framework agreement, individual orders, and briefs handed over by the CA. Tasks to be performed in particular: - preparation, organisation, execution, analysis and documentation of research, data acquisitions, analyses and decision-supporting materials founding, supporting or evaluating marketing and communication activity. - preparation of a research plan or methodological proposal adapted to the given research, data acquisition, analysis or decision-supporting task, - organisation, execution, coordination and control of research data recording, fieldwork or data collection. - processing, checking, cleaning, systematisation, analysis, interpretation of data available as a result of research or data acquisition, and formulation of decision-supporting conclusions, - with the prior approval of the CA, may carry out data purchases, procure syndicated research, or utilise an external data source or study on behalf of the CA, - performing administration related to possible research modifications, data recording changes, cancellations, data purchase or syndicated research limitations, - the Winning Tenderer is obliged to present the results of the given research, data acquisition, analysis or decision-supporting task according to a structure agreed with the Client. The Winning Tenderer is obliged to designate one permanent contact person. Detailed requirements set against performance are contained in the technical specification and draft contract.

The National ID forum (informal forum) has decided to organize a joint RFI event. The idea is to organize a single RFI involving several national agencies and ministries, which would maximize synergy benefits and be a cost-effective model. The ID Forum is a national informal cooperation forum that focuses on comprehensive identity management, its development, and creating a situational picture. The aim is to produce national services that develop capacity in identity management, coordinate training and information events, and improve the common situational awareness and ability to combat abuse. Identity is therefore at the heart of the forum and is dealt with within the remit of each member organization. The ID Forum consists of several Finnish agencies and ministries; Immigration Service (FIS), Border Guard Force (BGF), National Bureau of Investigations (NBI), National Police Board (NPB), Police departments, Customs, and Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA). The subject of the RFI and information about the procedure are described in more detail in Appendix 1.

sig_9f8973bfd621c9f402e2.description: The subject of the contract aims to provide cloud resources in Microsoft Azure on a subscription basis, with a reservation period for the main computing resource of - 3 years, for the installation and operation of the Moodle e-learning and distance learning platform. Scope of the service: Provision of a single virtual machine for Moodle, running under Linux; Provision of managed disks for the operating system and data; Provision of public network connectivity and a static public IP address/resource in accordance with the calculation; Provision of a backup service for Azure VMs with LRS redundancy; Provision of a capability for centralised management, monitoring, administration and optimisation of resources; Provision of support through an electronic ticketing platform/portal; Minimum technical requirements for the virtual machine: Resource type - Virtual machine in Microsoft Azure; VM size - Standard_E20as_v5 or equivalent/better; vCPU - minimum 20 vCPU; RAM - minimum 160 GB RAM; Operating system - Linux; Reservation - 3 years reserved capacity for the VM resource; Local temp disk - not required; Premium Storage support - Yes; Purpose - Moodle platform, database and applicable components in a single VM. Storage and backup requirements: OS Managed Disk - 1 managed disk P4, 64 GB-LRS; Data Managed Disk - 1 managed disk Premium SSD P40-LRS; Backup - Azure Backup for 1 VM instance up to 2 TB-LRS; Backup tier - Standard tier, without Archive tier-LRS. Network connectivity requirements: Public IP - Static public IP address; Public IP Prefix - Public IP Prefix resource, if applicable according to the calculation; Internet egress - Minimum 500 GB monthly outgoing internet traffic; Management, security and support requirements: The solution must have an interface for centralised management and policy definition in Microsoft Azure; It must be possible to monitor, manage and optimise the resources used; It must be possible to use multi-factor authentication for administrative access; The contractor must provide access to an electronic platform/portal for registering and tracking support requests; The tenderer must have the right to provide Microsoft Azure services as a CSP partner or equivalent provisioning model compatible with the Microsoft Customer Agreement. Requirement for an implemented and functioning helpdesk system - The tenderer must have an established and functioning helpdesk system, ensuring 24-hour support for the communication system with access via a single number of the type 0700 xxxxx or 0800 xxxxx with national coverage and a web-based interface. The tenderer must describe in detail the service procedure provided by the helpdesk system and indicate a link to the system where its functionalities can be checked. sig_9feb5763347fe22f0e13.description: This prior information notice serves exclusively to conduct a market survey in accordance with § 28 para. 1 of the German Public Procurement Ordinance (VgV) in preparation for a possible future procurement. However, a procurement procedure is not initiated by conducting this market survey. As part of such a market survey, the GIZ would like to obtain an overview of suitable potential solution providers to identify marketable systems for an integrated system portfolio for the digital support of its global procurement and contract processes, as the GIZ currently does not have sufficient market knowledge of the companies available on the market and potentially interested in the contract to be awarded. The goal is to identify a future-proof solution environment that meets high requirements for legally compliant procurement, supplier management, contract transparency, and international applicability. Companies interested in participating in this market survey are therefore requested to declare their interest to the specified email address. The GIZ will then send a questionnaire to the company, which will then be considered in the course of the market survey. Participation in the market survey is voluntary and does not oblige the GIZ to carry out a procurement, nor does it oblige the participants to conclude a service or supply contract.

The framework agreement shall remain in force for 24 months from its entry into force or until the framework amount is exhausted. Framework amount: net 85 000 000 HUF. The Contracting Authority undertakes a call-off obligation for 70 % of the framework amount during the term of the agreement. Name of procedure: Support and consulting for medical and related systems. Ensuring operational support for the medical and related systems operating at Semmelweis Egyetem and consulting through the conclusion of a framework agreement. The framework agreement shall remain in force for 24 months from its entry into force or until the framework amount is exhausted. Framework amount: net 85 000 000 HUF. The Contracting Authority operates a mixed system consisting of the character-based MedSolution and the web-based e-MedSolution IT system, with the necessary subsystems, interfaces, database management and middleware components. The number of users of the MedSolution / e-MedSolution system exceeds 4.000 named users. The maximum number of concurrent users is 1.200. Pursuant to Section 2/A ( 1 ) of Government Decree 29/2022 (I. 31 ) on central health informatics services, the MedSolution / e-MedSolution system is a hospital information system provided as a public service by ESZFK (Health Informatics Service and Development Centre), which the Contracting Authority is obliged to use under the legislation. (2) Users pursuant to paragraph (1) are obliged to use the hospital information system provided by the Service Centre. Main modules and function groups: • outpatient administration module • inpatient administration module • surgical module • pharmacy module • medication module • nursing module • care module • dental module • EFI module • ward stock requisition module • waiting list module • patient appointment booking module The systems operating at the Contracting Authority are operated by the Contracting Authority's application operations team, which provides L1 and L2 support in relation to the systems. The subject of this procurement procedure is the engagement of resources necessary to perform the L1 and L2 support activity, which covers the following main tasks: End-user support ( L1 ), - its aim is to provide a quick and simple solution and relieve the higher-level resolving groups in handling basic issues. • Receipt and logging of tickets. Receipt, logging and administration of reports received from end-users via telephone, email and ticketing system • Basic troubleshooting. Resolution of simple technical problems, such as password reset, modification of software settings, checking network connection. • Information gathering. Detailed and accurate documentation of reports, which assists resolution at further levels if there is no resolution at the L1 level • Forwarding of problems. If a problem exceeds the remit of L1 support, it is forwarded to the L2 or higher support group. • Administration and setting of permissions in respect of MedSolution / eMedSolution and related subsystems Expert support ( L2 ) – its aim is to handle more complex problems requiring deeper expertise, which require a specialist with specialised, more detailed knowledge. • Handling of events escalated by L1 support, proposing solutions or handing over to the licence manufacturer • Receipt, coordination and documentation of development needs • Testing of developments and introduction of functions • Performance of module owner tasks, such as consulting, system parameterisation, introduction, testing. • Tasks related to the preparation and processing of monthly reports; • Provision of regular and ad-hoc data supplies • Expertise and project management related to medical systems • Performance of parameterisation and operational tasks related to the interfacing of subsystems • Organisation and holding of end-user training • Keeping user documentation continuously up to date Planned service hours for 24 months: Service Manager: 500 hours Medical Consultant: 1800 hours Medical System Operator: 3800 hours Main service period: Monday to Friday from 8:00 hours to 17:00 hours Central European Time (CET), excluding Saturdays, Sundays and all public holidays in Hungary. In detail, as set out in the Technical Specification forming part of the procurement documents.

sig_a116bdb035226ad5a861.description: The subject matter of the procurement is the procurement and implementation of an Extended Detection & Response (XDR) solution, with the aim of significantly increasing IT security through modern detection and response mechanisms and, in particular, identifying advanced threats early and addressing them effectively. Lot LOT-0001: Extended Detection & Response (XDR) solution. Klinikum Esslingen operates an extensive IT infrastructure with numerous IT endpoints, including PCs, thin clients and servers. In addition, there are networked medical devices (IoMT) and building management systems (BMS), which are not, however, the subject of this tender. The endpoint security currently in use is based on a signature-based basic solution (Sophos) that does not provide advanced functions such as behavioural analysis or Endpoint Detection & Response (EDR). The project pursues the following strategic and operative goals: • Replacement of the existing signature-based endpoint security with an XDR solution featuring behavioural analysis, machine learning and forensic analysis capability in accordance with the state of the art • Establishment of complete endpoint visibility and control for all IT endpoints (clients and servers) of Klinikum Esslingen • Activation of Sophos Synchronized Security: real-time communication between endpoint agents and the existing Sophos XGS Firewall for automated network isolation of compromised endpoints • Creation of forensic analysis capabilities: continuous endpoint telemetry recording, root-cause analysis and threat hunting across all endpoints • Activation of cross-domain correlation (XDR): linking endpoint events with firewall, email, cloud and identity data sources as well as preparing the MDR service connection • Fulfilment of regulatory requirements from NIS-2 and GDPR regarding endpoint security as well as orientation towards the state of the art (B3S Gesundheit) • Support for vulnerability management through endpoint-based vulnerability visibility
sig_a116bdb035226ad5a861.title: Extended Detection & Response (XDR) – Lösung

sig_a1d31a611e6e4549cb68.description: The objective of the procurement is to acquire IT project manager and expert resources to support, among other things, the definition, programming, testing and management of the Finnish Tax Administration's new and existing systems. The expert resources will operate in projects, development tasks and ongoing service production. The purpose of the procurement is to secure specialist expertise and sufficient resources. The procurement is divided into six (6) lots, for each of which three (3) suppliers and three (3) reserve suppliers will be selected. The lots and their contents are described in more detail below. More detailed descriptions of the contents of the assignments for the procurement lots are described in the appendix Description of the subject matter of the procurement in section 3. The objective is for the contract to enter into force on 16.11.2026. The contract shall be valid for 72 months. Verohallinto develops and maintains digital services primarily as cloud-based and cloud-native solutions. The development work utilises application, integration, data and platform services provided by the Microsoft Azure cloud platform, as well as modern software development, information security and operational practices. Solutions vary in scope and criticality from mission-critical core applications to more limited services targeting specific business needs. The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is expert services for cloud-based software development implemented in the Microsoft Azure environment. The lot includes in particular architecture design for cloud solutions and cloud applications, application and integration development, DevOps, the development and maintenance of cloud platforms, and the technical information security of cloud environments and applications. Key expert roles include cloud solution architect, cloud application architect, cloud software developer, integration developer, cloud DevOps specialist, cloud platform specialist and technical information security specialist.; The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is expert services for applications and information system solutions utilising artificial intelligence, generative artificial intelligence and machine learning. The solutions are implemented primarily in the Microsoft Azure cloud environment, utilising the artificial intelligence capabilities offered by Microsoft Foundry and other Azure services. The solutions can be standalone AI applications or parts of broader information systems, digital services and software solutions. Expert work concerning new technologies may relate to the assessment of the possibilities, suitability, information security and risks of technologies, experiments and prototyping, software and hardware integration, the development of embedded systems, preparation for deployment, or the practical utilisation of technologies. Key expert roles for AI applications include AI application specialists, AI developers, AI solution architects, machine learning specialists and software developers participating in the implementation of AI applications.; The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is expert services aimed at improving the efficiency, quality and transparency of the organisation's operational and data-driven processes through automation, hyper-automation, analytics and systematic development methods. The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is primarily process automation expert services as well as process analytics and process development expert services in a cloud-based operating environment.; The Finnish Tax Administration's technological operating environment strongly includes the development of infrastructure, analytics, information security and cloud services. The Finnish Tax Administration uses the Gentax core taxation system and several smaller systems (e.g. supporting administration). The National Incomes Register and the Positive Credit Register are also the responsibility of the Finnish Tax Administration. The subject matter of the procurement for this lot includes: - project manager services for the development, creation and deployment of operating models and processes, as well as the development of related applications. The scope of impact of operational development can be internal to the organisation and/or customer-related. - technical project manager services, particularly for the areas of infrastructure and information security - Scrum master/team lead services for operational and technical development teams.; The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is IT service management expert services for the ServiceNow environment, as well as expert services specialised in ServiceNow development for architecture, consulting and development tasks. The tasks include ICT architecture and expert tasks in the ServiceNow modules used by the Finnish Tax Administration, including (* supplemented 4.9.2026): • ITSM (IT Service Management) • ITOM (IT Operations Management) • ITBM / SPM (Strategic Portfolio and Demand Management) • SecOps / SIR* (Security Operations) • IRM (Risk Management)* • CMDB (Configuration Management)* • IAM / AM (Access Management, Identity Management)* Expert tasks may include system development, configuration, maintenance, testing and training tasks for the modules in question, as well as related functional and technical architecture design.; The subject matter of the procurement for this lot is user-driven development expert services. By expert service, we mean working under the direction of the Finnish Tax Administration as part of the Finnish Tax Administration's development teams or in close cooperation with them, consulting, business sparring and/s or the implementation of various assignments. Verohallinto can also order fixed-price assignments for e.g. system accessibility audits.

sig_a313894175b835fb0039.description: Iraq faces a persistent gap between its people and the financial system. Banks have long leaned on large state-owned institutions, credit has flowed mainly to established borrowers, and micro and small businesses along with women entrepreneurs and displaced communities have been largely left out. ProDIGI project, full name Promoting Employment in the Digital and Green Economy in Iraq, is trying to change that in a practical, grounded way. ProDIGI is a multi-donor initiative commissioned by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ), co-financed by the European Union, and implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH. The project covers central and southern Iraq as well as the Kurdistan Region, with a focus on areas where joblessness, displacement, and limited access to services overlap. Within the project, Output 3 targets the financial inclusion side of the challenge. The starting point is a clear-eyed look at what the sector lacks: financial service providers that are capable, willing, and equipped to design products that fit the people they are supposed to serve. Banks and microfinance institutions in Iraq today mostly offer standardised products with high collateral requirements and limited digital capabilities. Reaching women led small businesses, rural communities, or young entrepreneurs running green or tech ventures requires a different kind of product, and often a different kind of institution. To bridge that gap, the project works directly with Iraqi financial service providers: banks, microfinance institutions, digital payment companies, fintechs, and government lending programmes. The approach combines needs assessments, hands-on advisory services, staff training, product design support, and pilot testing. The goal is not to deliver a finished product from outside, but to build the knowledge and process capacity within each institution so that change remains after the project ends. By the close of the assignment, at least three new or significantly adapted financial products must be in place, and these products must be actively reaching real users at a minimum of 950 individuals and 50 companies. The work also emphasises gender equality: women-led businesses are a priority target group, and all capacity-building activities must include a meaningful share of women participants. The broader context matters too. Iraq's Central Bank launched the national financial inclusion strategy that encourages digital payments, SME lending, and consumer protection improvements. ProDIGI project aligns directly with those priorities, making it both a practical intervention at the level of individual institutions and a contribution to the country's wider financial sector development. The selected firm will work directly with three to five financial service providers (FSPs) operating in Iraq. These may include commercial banks, microfinance institutions, digital payment providers, fintechs, and government lending schemes. GIZ will have pre-selected up to two FSPs before the contract starts, so work can begin without delay. The remaining FSPs will be selected by the contractor and GIZ jointly, based on agreed criteria. Lot LOT-0001: 10009293-Development of inclusive financial services and products. The assignment is structured around three work packages. The first covers the selection and appraisal of partner FSPs. The contractor will conduct an institutional diagnostic for each FSP, reviewing their current product offering, business model, lending processes, digital infrastructure, client outreach capacity, and staff skills. Based on that analysis, a cooperation agreement will be signed with each FSP, along with a detailed work plan laying out what the collaboration will achieve and by when. This phase should be completed within the first three months. The second work package is where the core technical work happens. The contractor will support FSPs in designing or adapting financial products that genuinely respond to the needs of target groups, particularly women-led businesses, rural borrowers, and MSME clients who currently lack access to suitable financing. The process follows a structured product development methodology: from prototype design, through pilot testing, to assessment and refinement, and finally roll-out. Alongside the product work, the contractor will help FSPs develop marketing materials and outreach strategies, adjust internal procedures and manuals, and train front-line staff such as loan officers and branch managers. At least three financial product prototypes must be developed by the fifth to seventh month, piloted by month eight, and formally adopted with updated manuals by month ten. The third work package covers cross-cutting contributions: occasional training inputs for financial sector stakeholders such as the Central Bank of Iraq and sector associations; support for GIZ's monitoring and evaluation activities; and at least three public communication outputs, case studies, blog posts, fact sheets, or similar, documenting the work done with each FSP.
sig_a313894175b835fb0039.title: 10009293-Development of inclusive financial services and products

In addition, support services aimed at increasing and promoting a data culture within the Administration are considered, as well as all those that provide support and serve to drive the corporate strategy regarding data, including those for support and assistance in the drafting of data-related policies, instructions and procedures.

sig_a40a8adf098b749304a2.description: By & Havn is facing the task of transforming Levantkaj in Nordhavn from an existing container terminal into a modern city district. With the current local plan proposal, it is expected that approx. 350.000 square metres of floor space for housing, service businesses and public functions as well as approx. 50.000 square metres of parking distributed across two parking structures on Levantkaj can be established. The local plan will also enable the construction of an elevated metro line, a new metro station as well as pedestrian and cycle connections linked to the main connections in Nordhavn. The local plan proposal will designate the area as a mixed residential and commercial area with the character of a residential area with an expected distribution of housing and commerce of 75/25 with associated facilities such as a school and football pitch, day nurseries, church, sports hall complex, care centre, etc. The local plan proposal is expected to be politically approved in Q4 2026, and the final local plan is expected to be adopted in Q3 2027. By & Havn will be responsible for construction works, establishment of parking structures as well as the sale of building rights, and By & Havn has an ambition that all urban areas are DGNB-certified to a minimum of Platinum. In connection with By & Havn's upcoming sale of building rights, By & Havn wishes with this tender to conclude an agreement with an adviser on economic and commercial consultancy related to By & Havn's development of primarily ground floors containing retail and public-oriented service businesses at Levantkaj, which By & Havn will carry out in a joint venture with a collaboration partner/investor. The adviser's service relates to consultancy on, as a starting point, approx. 6.000 – 7.000 m2 retail and public-oriented functions on the ground floors - which is the area that the joint venture is to own and let out - and does not comprise assistance with the sale or development of other residential building rights or other properties on Levantkaj. However, By & Havn is considering the possibility of expanding the joint venture company's task to include parts of the commercial plots. The tendered agreement consists of two main parts (main tasks), which may overlap in time: • Business plan: Preparation of a detailed business plan for use in the process regarding finding a collaboration partner/investor. The business plan must describe how a company between the collaboration partner/investor and By & Havn is to be structured and describe at a detailed level, among other things, liquidity, ownership distribution, rent level, phasing in of rent and return requirements, etc. • Organisation and implementation of a process to find a collaboration partner/investor: With inspiration from the process during By & Havn's development of the Århusgadekvarteret in Nordhavn, By & Havn wishes to find a collaboration partner/investor who can enter into a joint venture with By & Havn to own ground floors containing retail and public-oriented service businesses at Levantkaj with a view to joint letting. The collaboration partner/investor must be the active party in locating the right tenants for these ground floors. The adviser must assist in organising and implementing a process to find the right collaboration partner/investor, including identifying potential candidates as well as conducting negotiations. In connection with the preparation of the business plan and through dialogue with potential collaboration partners/investors, the adviser must assess together with By & Havn whether some of the commercial plots are to be included in the joint venture collaboration, in order thereby to create a more attractive business case. The execution of the agreement is expected to be initiated immediately following the conclusion of the contract, which is planned to take place immediately before the Christmas holiday 2026. As a clear starting point, the agreement runs until the joint venture agreement with the collaboration partner/investor has been concluded. Based on the expectations for the adoption of the local plan for Levantkaj, it will be optimal for By & Havn if the contract with the collaboration partner/investor (the joint venture agreement) is in place before 1 August 2027 and preferably already before the industrial summer holiday starts. However, By & Havn acknowledges that a number of circumstances may lead to it not being possible to have the joint venture agreement in place within the desired timeframe. In any event, the adviser must anticipate that the work on both main tasks will be intense and require a competent and flexible project organisation. By & Havn has chosen to tender one single contract instead of dividing the contract into lots, as it is By & Havn's assessment that it is firstly necessary to have a joint business plan for the whole of Levantkaj, and secondly that it is clearly most appropriate in relation to interfaces and in relation to rapid execution that the same adviser performs both main tasks.
sig_a40a8adf098b749304a2.title: Udviklingsselskabet By & Havn I/S tender for an agreement on financial advisory services and assistance regarding the development of retail and public-oriented service businesses at Levantkaj

sig_a4d9ea61c5c212fc525c.description: Background: Although many of the world"s fastest-growing economies are in Africa, trade among African countries remains limited. The continent mostly exports raw materials and agricultural products, while it imports machinery, equipment, and food mainly from outside Africa. The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), which is one of the African Union"s (AU) flagship projects for the implementation of its Agenda 2063, aims to change this. It is expected that, with the introduction of the free trade zone, intra- African trade will be 15% to 25% higher by 2040 (UNECA). The AfCFTA agreement has been signed by 54 of the 55 African Union Member States (MS) and became effective under international law in May 2019. The full implementation of the AfCFTA will lead to a continental single market of more than 1.4 billion people with an aggregate GDP exceeding USD 2 trillion. Our Approach: The GIZ implemented project "Support to the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) II" cofinanced by the BMZ and the EU, seeks to improve framework conditions for the realisation of the AfCFTA and supports the outstanding negotiations and the implementation of the AfCFTA. For this, the programme supports the African Union, specifically the Department for Economic Development, Trade, Tourism, Industry, Minerals (ETTIM) and the AfCFTA Secretariat at the continental level in the coordination of AfCFTA implementation. On the regional level the programme cooperates with Regional Economic Communities (RECs), specifically EAC (East African Community), ECOWAS (Economic Community for West African States) and SADC (South African Development Community, plus additional RECs based on request). The programme also supports Member States (Ethiopia, Ghana, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Malawi, Rwanda, Tunisia, Zambia, plus additional Member States based on request) by working with national institutions, like trade ministries and customs, to implement the agreement. Lastly, the programme works closely with private sector and civil society actors to increase trade under the AfCFTA. Together with the named partners, the programme covers interventions across all technical areas of the AfCFTA. The EU co-financed part of the programme, the EU Technical Assistance Facility, operates as a multi-partner contribution agreement between the European Commission, GIZ (lead implementing agency), Expertise France, and FIAP. A Project Management Unit, which is housed in the AfCFTA Secretariat, oversees the implementation of the programme and the execution of activities. Lot LOT-0001: 10022598-Short-Term Expert Pools to support negotiations and implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA). The project seeks the services of a consulting firm to provide technical experts under different short-term expert (STE) pools, which can be deployed flexibly according to the specific demands of the project. The Contractor will contribute to the implementation of all BMZ and EU outputs of the project. The overall goal of this assignment is to support the implementation of the AfCFTA at the continental, regional, and national level by providing advisory services and capacity building for governmental as well as private sector and civil society stakeholders. When the need for support to the project"s partners within a particular thematic area is identified, experts shall be mobilised to provide demand-driven technical advisory services and/or capacity building to national, regional, and continental government partners and/or the project itself. The contract is for the provision of pools of qualified STE to cover a broad range of issues relating to AfCFTA negotiations and implementation in general and the programme objectives in particular. The services to be provided under the contract include measures for human capacity development and organisational and technical advice in the following thematic areas: - Removing barriers to Trade in Goods, Trade in Services and Digital Trade - Support for further AfCFTA negotiations (among others on Rules of Origin, Trade in Services) - Support for the ratification of the Phase II Protocols (Competition Policy, Intellectual Property Rights, Investment, Digital Trade, Women & Youth in Trade) - Implementation of AfCFTA regulations at the national and regional levels - Monitor and review the implementation of AfCFTA Protocols in African Union Member States (AU MS) - Improve access to trade information to relevant line ministries and to the private sector - Support the African private sector to trade under AfCFTA rules on the national and regional level - Support relevant authorities to setup inclusive policies for women & youth traders to participate in trade under AfCFTA The contractor will identify and manage pools of STE that will assist the initiatives in the programme"s areas of intervention. While the project operates Africa-wide, it focuses interventions at national level in 8 countries: Ethiopia, Ghana, Ivory Coast, Kenya, Malawi, Rwanda, Tunisia, and Zambia. At REC level it focuses at EAC, ECOWAS, and SADC. Interventions to additional AU MS and RECs will be implemented based on partner demand. Across the work packages named below, the contractor is responsible for the following tasks: - Supporting the GIZ in defining the required expertise to reach the project objectives under the described outputs - Identifying and proposing suitable experts from the STE pool - Selecting experts together with the GIZ team - Managing the deployment of experts Expected services that may be included in the work packages are: - Technical, operational, and strategic policy advisory services in the thematic areas listed above - Support in developing, drafting and reviewing reports, studies, analyses, position papers, guidelines, action plans, strategies, implementation plans, legislation, regulations in the thematic areas listed above. - Research and analysis, including diagnostic missions to assess implementation efforts of the AfCFTA protocols, identify obstacles and propose measures to advance implementation. - Facilitation of private sector participation in policy-making processes, facilitation of dialogue and coordination between public and private sector actors relevant to AfCFTA negotiations and implementation - Facilitation of national, regional, and continental workshops and conferences, including interpretation and translation services and providing expert inputs - Provision of support services to the project, including on optimising M&E systems, the design of communication materials, workshop moderation, translation and interpretation services. Deliverables will mainly be in English or French, but may also be in the other official AU languages (Arabic, Portuguese, Spanish, Swahili) depending on the context of the activity The required services are focused, but not limited, on five work packages which are oriented to different stakeholders: Work package 1: Strengthen the AfCFTA Secretariat"s capacity to guide and monitor AfCFTA implementation. Work package 2: Strengthen AUC ETTIM"s capacity to support and monitor the enabling environment for production of goods and services for African markets. Work package 3: Support the coordination of the AfCFTA implementation approach among selected RECs (EAC, ECOWAS, and SADC). Work package 4: Support the domestication and ratification of the AfCFTA Protocols and their Annexes in selected AU MS. Work package 5: Enable private sector actors to trade under AfCFTA rules on the country and regional level. Additionally, the contractor is required to support the provision of support services to the project as well as to partner institutions at the continental, regional and national level under all the work packages above. This includes communication services, moderation services, Monitoring & Evaluation support, translation services, and interpretation services.

Description A Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) that offers automation services and licences for use by the public sector, including their associated bodies and agencies. Automation services are needed to streamline processes and systems for public sector customers. The agreement offers the following services: strategy and business transformation problem solving with tech solutions resources and training software licences What is out of scope? Products and services out of scope include but are not limited to: any hardware and infrastructure hosting networks or connectivity services Benefits accessible route for suppliers – accessible for all suppliers (including SMEs) and suppliers can apply to join at any time government specific terms and conditions (Ts&Cs) – these have been created based on an agile approach using the public sector contract a dynamic filtering system – giving buyers flexibility based on their requirements. There is no option for direct award. Before running your mini competition, find out which suppliers could meet your requirements using the Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) Marketplace. The steps below outline how to search for suppliers, create a shortlist and carry out a mini competition. Register as a buyer on the Dynamic Purchasing System Marketplace. Note: although pages are headed ‘Supplier registration’ this is also where you can register as a buyer. Navigate to the Automation Marketplace DPS under Technology, choose the ‘Access as a buyer’ option and confirm your acceptance of the customer access agreement. This is how you filter the suppliers that can meet your requirements. When creating a new category use the filtering tool (select all that apply) to specify your requirements and create your supplier shortlist. Save your filtered list of capable suppliers by clicking the ‘Save Category’ option and give the shortlist a unique name specific to your competition. From your ‘Manage your Category Exports’ page you can then export the list of suppliers and contact details (export is to an Excel spreadsheet) Quit the DPS. Use the list to run a Further Competition. Invite the suppliers identified by the DPS to bid against your detailed specification, evaluation criteria and contract format. The list is valid for only 2 working days , from the date of its creation, because new suppliers may apply to join at any point. If your Call for Competition excludes eligible suppliers it potentially breaches procurement regulations. You will need to get a fresh supplier list (steps 3.2 to 5) if you don’t use your list within 2 working days by clicking the ‘Search Again’ option for your export. Your tender process should be proportionate to the value and complexity of your requirement. suppliers will need a reasonable period of time to review and prepare a response. This includes allowing sufficient time for suppliers to ask clarification questions and consider your answers before the deadline for written responses. Evaluate the responses. Request from the winning supplier(s) any required evidence that they can meet your requirements. Set a 2-day deadline for submitting evidence. sig_a5656958da206bcbea74.description: Invitation to participation in the market dialogue. Asker, Bærum and Drammen municipalities plan to hold a competition for a new contract for the operation and development of websites on Optimizely DXP. Before the competition is announced, we would like a dialogue with the market in the form of one-to-one meetings with relevant tenderers, who can offer systems that cover the municipalities ́needs. The dialogue meetings will be held digitally during week 9. We would like to carry out a combined procurement process to enter into three separate contracts with the same tenderer. The municipalities have in common that we use the same CMS (Optimizely DXP) on version CMS12. The aim is that cooperation, development and sharing across the municipalities take place seamlessly between the three municipalities. Through new contracts a collaborating partner shall be able to support the operation and development of the websites in Asker, Bærum and Drammen municipalities. A collaborating partner must be able to contribute to and deliver the following (the list is not exhaustive): - Stable and safe operation - High competence in Optimizely DXP and resource robustness. - Continual improvement - Development and future orientated focus. - User-oriented focus - Consultancy and competence sharing. - Project management in development. System integration - Design and concept development Close dialogue in both daily operation and development. We would like tenderers to give a presentation of their service offer, which states something about how they can contribute to fulfil the municipalities ́needs. We would also like tenderers to have prepared answers to questions defined in annex 2. Tenderers wishing to participate can register their interest by sending an email to elfrid.nygaard.stabellini@asker.kommune.no, and at the same time state the preferred time for the meeting: - Monday 23.02: 10.00-11.30 - Monday 23.02, 12.30-14.00 - Monday 23.02, 14.30-16.00 - Tuesday 24.02, 08:30 - 10:00. - Tuesday 24.02, 10.30-12.00 - Tuesday 24.02, 13.00-14.30 The registration deadline is 19.02.2026. Annex 1 - Agenda Dialogue Meeting 1. Presentation of meeting participants and cards on the municipalities ́needs. 2. Presentation from the tenderer and review of questions and answers in Annex 2. Annex 2 - Questions and Answers The questions shall be reviewed in the dialogue meeting, and answered and returned in written form to the customer by 27.02.2026: 1.Technical operation and stability A. How do you ensure stable and secure operation of Optimizely DXP for customers with complex needs? B. How do you work with proactive operation and continual technical improvements? c. How will you describe your form of cooperation and dialogue with customers (response time, CRM, regular status meetings)? 2. Development and future oriented focus A. Can you describe how you internally ensure competence development and further development of your employees? B. Beside the main delivery covered by this agreement, assistance can be required for major development projects throughout the contract period. There may be a need for more capacity and special competence from the tenderer. Do you have the opportunity to carry out projects of a larger nature and set aside large amounts of resources in limited periods? Key competence in major projects may, for example, be linked to artificial intelligence in order to proactive information work on the websites and to make content available to target groups that can have challenges with using digital channels. c. How do you envisage that a municipal web will look like in 5 years? 3. Work across three municipalities A. What competence do you have in the municipal sector (or similar entities/organisations) Please give examples. B. How will you organise the cooperation so that development, operation and further development occur seamlessly across Asker, Bærum and Drammen municipalities? How can you facilitate re-use of systems across the municipalities? c. What experiences do you have with working with several customers in joint projects? d. How do you ensure good priorities when three municipalities shall share the same supplier? How do you ensure that there are enough resources with the right competence available? 4. User focus and availability A. How do you work with user testing and insight and how do you use this for continual improvement? 5. Design and concept development A. How do you work with design and concept development at Optimizely DXP, and what methods do you use to make systems uniform and user friendly? Describe how you involve ordering, handling design principles, and ensuring consistency in both visual and content design. 6. How do you share experiences, insight, and best practice with the customers you work with? Do you, for example, have forums or seminars that your customers can participate in for inspiration and competence development? 7. Can you discuss how your company currently works with environment and sustainability and what actions do you take to reduce damaging environmental impact? 8. Can you describe the price model you use? Annex 3 - Documentation that shall be submitted after the dialogue meeting. Deadline: 27.02.2026 1. Presentation from the dialogue meeting, including replies to the questions in annex 2. 3. Three reference customers with a comparable solution (with contact information). 4. Generic price list for their consultants based on seniority and competence.

sig_a62ce7ae50674cb84864.description: Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are enabling extraordinary scientific breakthroughs in fields ranging from protein folding, natural language processing, drug synthesis, and recommender systems to the discovery of novel engineering materials and products. These achievements lie at the confluence of mathematics, statistics, engineering and computer science, yet a clear explanation of the remarkable power and also the limitations of such AI systems has eluded scientists from all disciplines. Critical foundational gaps remain that, if not properly addressed, will soon limit advances in machine learning, curbing progress in artificial intelligence. It appears increasingly unlikely that these critical gaps can be surmounted with increased computational power and experimentation alone. Deeper mathematical understanding is essential to ensuring that AI can be harnessed to meet the future needs of society and enable broad scientific discovery, while forestalling the unintended consequences of a disruptive technology. The National Science Foundation Directorates for Mathematical and Physical Sciences (MPS), Computer and Information Science and Engineering (CISE), Engineering (ENG), and Social, Behavioral and Economic Sciences (SBE) will jointly sponsor research collaborations consisting of mathematicians, statisticians, computer scientists, engineers, and social and behavioral scientists focused on the mathematical and theoretical foundations of AI. Research activities should focus on the most challenging mathematical and theoretical questions aimed at understanding the capabilities, limitations, and emerging properties of AI methods as well as the development of novel, and mathematically grounded, design and analysis principles for the current and next generation of AI approaches. Specific research goals include: establishing a fundamental mathematical understanding of the factors determining the capabilities and limitations of current and emerging generation s of AI systems, including, but not limited to, foundation models, generative models, deep learning, statistical learning, federated learning, and other evolving paradigms; the development of mathematically grounded design and analysis principles for the current and next generations of AI systems; rigorous approaches for characterizing and validating machine learning algorithms and their predictions; research enabling provably reliable, translational, general-purpose AI systems and algorithms; e ncouragement of new collaborations in this interdisciplinary research community and between institution s. The overall goal is to establish innovative and principled design and analysis approaches for AI technology using creative yet theoretically grounded mathematical and statistical frameworks, yielding explainable and interpretable models that can enable sustainable, socially responsible, and trustworthy AI.
sig_a62ce7ae50674cb84864.title: Mathematical Foundations of Artificial Intelligence

sig_a70d48788e7c199ea108.description: The contracting authority is striving for the digital modernisation of its individual agendas. One of these agendas is the parking policy of the city of Olomouc (hereinafter also referred to as the "PPMO"). Currently, the territorial scope of the parking policy applies to only two parking zones (A and B). In the planned expansion to zones C and D (including their sub-areas), it is also necessary to adjust and strengthen the existing part of the PPMO, which handles the registry of parking permits. Therefore, the contracting authority has decided to procure the acquisition of services for a new, modern system for the registry of parking permits, whereby these services will be used to optimise faster processing for citizens, ensure connection to state administration registries, and connection to other PPMO systems for more efficient processing of transferred data, and a modern graphical interface meeting current trends will also be achieved. The provision of the services of the system for the registry of parking permits must also fulfil all current legislative and security requirements. The subject matter of performance of this public contract is: a) performance of a requirements analysis, processing and implementation of the target concept, establishment and commissioning of the Portal Solution for the registry of parking permits (hereinafter referred to as the "PPMO Portal Solution"), data migration, testing, provision of training, provision of licences and provision of all other related performance necessary for the proper commissioning of the PPMO Portal Solution; b) provision of the PPMO Portal Solution as a service (in service mode), ensuring its maintenance and support, provision of the IT infrastructure necessary for the operation of the PPMO Portal Solution; c) provision of development services, analytical and methodical services, implementation of change requests and provision of other related performance based on the requirements of the contracting authority. A more detailed specification of the subject matter of performance is contained in the relevant parts of the tender documentation (hereinafter also referred to as the "TD"), in particular Appendix No. 2 and Appendix No. 3 of the TD. The types of parking permits are outlined in Appendix No. 12 of the TD. The types of parking permits may change over time.

sig_a7d1f416274e89243a7d.description: Henneberg Clinics - Mobile Laboratory Automation and Robotics The subject matter is the planning, delivery, integration, conformity assessment, commissioning, acceptance and service of a fully mobile robotics/automation solution for barcode-supported sample flow between intake, pre-analytics, analysis systems, special dispensing, cooling and archiving. The solution must function as an overall system with laboratory equipment, LIS/middleware, building infrastructure and operator processes. Not the subject matter of this lot are medical laboratory services, the permanent provision of laboratory personnel, or the immediate procurement of transport or cleaning robots. Laboratory equipment and laboratory IT are procured separately. However, the robotics contractor remains responsible for the complete mechanical, electrical, software, control and safety engineering integration of the overall system they offer. Target image and functional equivalence: • Permanent robotics-supported in-house laboratory operations at the Hildburghausen site from 01.01.2027; no transitional supply. The first expansion stage is the mobile laboratory robotics system. • Documented peak intake: maximum approx. 30 samples per hour. The solution must not be unnecessarily oversized for this, but must demonstrate a comprehensible operational reserve. • Fully mobile, autonomously navigating robotics systems (AMR) or functionally equivalent mobile automation solutions are permitted. Stationary robot cells, linearly guided systems and permanently installed tracks do not meet the target image. • The solution offered is not an isolated robotics island: it is seamlessly integrated into order, sample, equipment, result, priority and error management and networked via a centrally provided orchestration and fleet management software. The software and platform architecture must be provably scalable for subsequent transport and cleaning robotics at two sites of the clinic association. A common or interoperable traffic logic, building and elevator interfaces, identity and certificate management, as well as a uniform operating and service concept must be provided. The initial procurement must not create unnecessary binding to proprietary laboratory equipment or closed building interfaces. sig_a845c8ec58fb938f4a6a.description: The Finnish Medicines Agency Fimea (later Fimea) is preparing the procurement of a system for receiving, validation and reviewing marketing authorisation applications for medicinal products and other regulatory submissions. Fimea is primarily looking for a software as a service (SaaS) off-the shelf solution that is provided from a public cloud. The system shall enable the necessary integrations with Fimea's other systems, which will be defined later. The procurement will also include the deployment, support and maintenance services for the system to be procured. Life cycles of the medicinal product dossiers (sequences and attributes) must be migrated to the system. Migration will be part of the procurement. The purpose of this request for information is to identify potential tenderers and to gather information on the solutions available on the market. Following the market dialogue, a call for tenders for the procurement will be prepared. DESCRIPTION The system to be procured shall support the receipt and validation of regulatory submissions, as well as the view and review of application materials. The system shall ensure a smooth and consistent user experience for the marketing authorisation specialists and to minimise manual steps through automated workflow functionalities. Preliminary requirements for the procurement are: - Data import functionalities: The solution shall support automated and manual import of regulatory submissions related to medicinal products. • Different types of submissions: o eCTD (electronic Common Technical Document, all formats), (v)NeeS (Non-eCTD electronic Submission), non-standard based submissions, ASMF (active substance master file), PSUR (Periodic Safety Update Report) • The sources of data: o Common European Submission Portal (CESP) o Other possible sources, e.g. EMA Common Repository (CR), Union Product Database (UPD), PSUR repository o Manual import of material (e.g. from email) to the system also enabled - The system sends a notification about a new submission and forms a job queue - Technical validation of regulatory submissions, including all versions of eCTD - Flexible dossier and sequence management for agency administrators - API capabilities: The system shall include flexible API capabilities to enable integrations with other relevant systems and repositories, such as case management systems and archiving solutions - User management: The system shall include advanced user management features, enabling the administration of access rights and roles for different user groups - View and review of the dossier in the system • Different view modes (single sequence vs. cumulative view of the application) • Advanced search functionalities • Possibility to use AI-assisted review: The system shall include or support the integration of AI#assisted tools - The location of the data needs to be in the EU region, and the cloud service provided by the service supplier
sig_a845c8ec58fb938f4a6a.title: System for receiving, validation and reviewing marketing authorisation applications and other regulatory submissions for medicinal products

sig_a8f679baea262f7d8cbc.buyer_name: German Corporation for International Cooperation (GIZ) GmbH
sig_a8f679baea262f7d8cbc.buyer_original: Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH
sig_a8f679baea262f7d8cbc.description: Background Many developing countries and emerging economies are negatively impacted by trade constraints resulting from red tape in the form of complicated customs documents, import surveillance and border procedures that lack transparency. High transaction costs make it difficult for them to tap into global value chains and make their businesses less competitive. Many enterprises are thereby denied opportunities to grow through trade. In 2017, the World Trade Organization"s (WTO) Trade Facilitation Agreement (TFA) entered into force with the objective to simplify, modernize and harmonize export and import processes in order to facilitate the cross-border movements of goods. It also establishes measures for effective cooperation between customs and other relevant authorities on trade facilitation and customs compliance. Additionally, it contains provisions for technical assistance and capacity building. Measures to facilitate trade play an important role across a variety of policy areas and sectors. They have a positive effect on food security, rural development, consumer protection, investment promotion and good governance among others. Project rationale The GIZ global program "Partnerships for Sustainable Trade" (PST) has been commissioned by the German Federal Ministry of Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) to establish measures that facilitate trade and support environment and climate protection. Its duration is from 07/2024 to 12/2027. The program focuses on implementing the Trade Facilitation Agreement of the World Trade Organization (WTO) and promotes cooperation between companies, business and trade associations as well as state institutions. As an implementation partner of the Global Alliance for Trade Facilitation (the Alliance), it aligns development objectives with economic interests. The Alliance supports low and middle-income countries in streamlining trade-related processes to move goods across their borders as quickly, safely, and cost-effectively as possible. The Alliance is an initiative that puts public private partnership at the heart of its approach to trade reform, believing that governments and businesses of all sizes working together represents the best way of delivering transformative, positive change. The Alliance is jointly hosted by the World Economic Forum, the International Chamber of Commerce and the Center for International Private Enterprise and works in cooperation with the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH. It is currently funded by the governments of Canada, Germany, Sweden, and the European Union (EU). Program measures include: - Planning and implementing trade facilitation measures in various countries in Africa, the Balkans, and Asia; - Increasing efficiency and reducing customs clearance costs by digitising processes and commercial documents; - Simplifying import and export procedures in developing and least developed countries (LDCs) through digital solutions and public-private partnerships; - Supporting developing countries in representing their interests in the multilateral trading system and in the WTO. The program is co-funded by different donors. At the beginning of 2025, the EU joined the Alliance as a new donor through co-funding the GIZ program. The EU contribution to the Alliance focusses on strengthening trade facilitation in least developed countries. Further co-financing comes from the World Trade Organisation (WTO) for the implementation of projects of the WTO Trade Facilitation Assistance Facility and by the EU Delegation to Madagascar for the implementation of an Alliance project in the country. Structure of the PST program The overall objective of the project is: In countries of the Global South, government, private actors or non-governmental organizations are equipped with improved instruments and competencies for the further development of the multilateral trading system for a Just Transition. The program is structured in 4 different Outputs: Output 1: Selected countries of the Global South are equipped with options for action for an inclusive, economic, and ecologically sustainable development of the multilateral trading system. Output 2: Proven trade facilitation instruments are embedded in selected countries of the Global South. Output 3: Innovative, climate and environmentally friendly approaches to trade facilitation have been further developed. Output 4: Trade facilitation instruments are embedded in selected LDCs. The project countries are specified in the Terms of Reference. The PST program seeks the services of a consulting firm to provide technical experts under different short-term expert (STE) pools, which can be deployed according to the project proposals and operational plans of each project country. The services will be delivered mainly by short-term experts in form of technical and administrative services for the development and implementation of specific trade facilitation measures in partner countries. The services also cover cross-cutting areas such as stakeholder engagement, workshop and training facilitation, and process management. Specifically, in the context of the respective in-country project workplans, the experts are foreseen to provide expertise in technical fields aimed at change management and capacity building of the respective identified border agencies. The services to be delivered in the project countries include: - Conducting analyses and gap assessments on specific IT solutions or processes for Customs and other border agencies - Business process engineering of customs and logistics procedures - Technically oversee the implementation of IT solutions by IT solution providers - Support Customs and other partner agencies in developing and implementing change management plans - Developing and facilitating public-private dialogue formats - Developing training materials and conducting trainings (specifically train the trainer approaches) - Potentially, support for the scoping of Global Alliance for Trade Facilitation projects through fact finding missions and concept/proposal development[LL2.1]. Several new projects will be designed in the coming months. Potential countries for these new projects include Brazil, Cote d"Ivoire, Kenya, India, Indonesia, South Africa. Specifically, the following technical areas within respective work packages are covered through services provided by the STE pools: Work package 1. Customs modernisation and digitisation, including change management and process optimisation - Stabilizing and upgrading (ASYCUDA) and other customs management systems, - Reviewing customs management processes and drafting standard operating procedures (SOPs), - Supporting customs in piloting and rolling-out newly developed IT solutions or re-engineered processes; including specifically for airfreight and express clearance procedures. Work package 2. Support for specific Customs procedures - Improving customs workflows for tariff valuation and classification, fall-back and continuity procedures, - Development and roll-out of advance ruling systems. Work package 3. Risk management, including Authorised Economic Operator Schemes - Review existing risk management approaches, - Revision of selectivity rules, - Gap analysis of the policy and regulatory framework and on-the-ground implementation, - Development and proposal of improved risk management systems, approaches, or specific rules, adaptation or extension of existing approaches and systems to cover additional specialised cases, such as perishable goods, express shipments, or low value shipments, - Development and implementation of preferential schemes for trusted economic operators (Authorised economic operator schemes), - Pre-arrival processing of manifest information to trigger risk analysis, - Post Clearance Audits. Work package 4. Import and export permits/ certificates - Implementation of the IPPC ePhyto certification solution, - Development and implementation of processes / digital solutions for issuing (electronic) certificates for fish exports (eFish) as well as for animal products (eVet), - Digitisation of line Ministry agencies" import/export permit or certification processes (e.g. by Ministry of Agriculture, Bureau of Standards, Animal health board, etc.), - Process re-engineering, improvement of phytosanitary risk management systems, - Integration of the approvals/permits into the respective customs management systems and any other relevant platform (e.g. trade single windows), - Revision of workflows and processes. Since the focus of this tender lies on the provision of technical expertise through the mobilisation of short-term experts, the contractor is expected to implement rigorous processes for the selecting, preparing, training and steering the experts assigned to carry out the advisory services.

sig_a9621991a0ec5f1287b9.description:
Maintaining and swiftly empowering a digitally competent working society that contributes to a productive and competitive economy despite demographic change and skills shortages is in the strategic interest of the Federal Government. Securing the skills base is crucial, in particular, for the competitiveness of companies. In view of an ageing society, there is an urgent need for action to keep employees in businesses under good and healthy working conditions for as long as possible, to tap into unused domestic potential and to make the working world more inclusive and diverse. Digital technologies and, above all, Artificial Intelligence (AI) offer the opportunity to keep people with age-related, cognitive or mental impairments in the labour market or to integrate them for longer and in better health, and to create an environment suited to older people and those with disabilities. The research contract to be awarded (performance period: 2027–2028) aims to identify the opportunities and needs of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) and workers with impairments regarding the use of technological support in the workplace and thus to unlock labour potential with the aid of digitalisation and AI. Since there is as yet no systematic and comprehensive presentation of this, there is a need for practice-oriented and practicable scientific research on how SMEs can support employees with impairments in the workplace through the use of new technologies (e.g. AI). A contribution is also to be made to safeguarding the experiential knowledge of employees and strengthening existing (advisory) structures by supporting higher-level institutions (e.g. inclusion offices, chambers of industry and commerce, top-level business associations) in advising SMEs on issues relating to digital transformation. The research contract is being tendered Europe-wide as a competitive dialogue with a preceding call for competition. The services may be provided by a consortium. In order to achieve the set objectives, the contractors implementing the research project must perform at least the following work packages. The precise design is to be explained by the tenderers within the framework of the competitive dialogue: 1. Basic research and needs analysis: o Conducting an empirical-exploratory study to identify and systematically present the needs of SMEs and their employees with impairments. o Preparation of an overview of suitable technological and AI-based solutions. o Suitability testing of AI technologies for specific fields of work; if they are not suitable, the need for alternative solutions is to be demonstrated. 2. Implementation strategies and implementation: o Development of implementation proposals and assistance for the implementation and long-term use of the identified technologies. o Identification and creation of target-group-appropriate information resources and channels. o Integration of feedback and evaluation through a co-creative approach. 3. Review and adaptation: o Review and testing of the developed information resources and channels, as well as their refinement and adaptation. o Examination of the effectiveness of the (AI) support instruments. 4. Dissemination including a broad-impact support service across the board: o Continuous dissemination to enhance the public profile of the project objectives and results. Addressees of the research contract: scientific institutions, universities and research institutions. Subject matter and addressees of the research measure: SMEs and higher-level institutions, which are to be involved accordingly in the implementation of the project. The perspectives of affected workers, self-representation, advisory and self-help organisations and associations of and for people with disabilities must also be taken into account. E39 Smiene-Harestad, includes i.a.: • 4.7 km of open air four lane roads, • Connection to the Smiene junction • New two-level crossings o Tasta junction o Finnestad junction and o Harestad junction • Three bridges of 98 m, 90m and 24m respectively. • Foot and cycle path • 400m Environment culvert • and related technical installations. The E39 Smiene-Harestad shall open at the same time as the E39 Rogfast. The project, together with E39 Rogfast, will be able to connect Western Norway in a new way. Western Norway and Norway are in an increasingly tough national and international competition situation for people and resources. E39 Smiene-Harestad together with E39 Rogfast will open to greater synergy, freedom and expanded living and labour market area for the population. This can contribute to increased business growth in the area. The project notice is expected to be published in 2027. One-to-one meetings can be held for a period after the market meeting.
