sig_a9ca8221a2856ecefe15.description: The subject of the procurement is the development of a new electronic system for the Croatian Science Foundation for the submission of project proposals, evaluation and monitoring of funded projects. Hrvatska zaklada za znanost (HRZZ) as the Contracting Authority, is the central national organisation for the funding of scientific, higher education and technological programmes and projects in Croatia. Every year, HRZZ announces a series of calls for proposals to support scientific research, thereby ensuring stable funding for research groups engaged in internationally and/or nationally significant scientific issues that create new knowledge and improve existing knowledge through basic, applied or development research. In order to ensure the selection and funding of the best projects, HRZZ has developed a project proposal evaluation procedure based on the internationally accepted practice of peer review, in which scientists from Croatia and abroad participate. The procedure for applying to HRZZ calls for proposals, the evaluation and selection of project proposals, and the monitoring of the implementation of contracted projects takes place via the Electronic System for Project Submission and Monitoring (hereinafter: EPP system). In this regard, the existing EPP system was developed in 2011. and has been upgraded several times over the years. The total server space it currently occupies is ~720 GB. The total number of active registered users in the system is 21.875, while on an annual basis about 7.000 users in various roles and 30 HRZZ employees work with the system. However, following the above, it is necessary to build a new modular system that the Contracting Authority can independently adapt to the type of call for proposals, the type of evaluation procedure and the involved users. The system must allow the Contracting Authority to select from predefined elements those that will be used in a specific call period (e.g. criteria for checking applicant eligibility, cards or forms that the user fills out, mandatory fields, documentation for uploading, etc.). Following the above, a detailed description of the subject of procurement is contained in the Technical Specifications document, which forms Appendix I to this Procurement Documentation.
sig_a9ca8221a2856ecefe15.title: Development of a new electronic system for the Croatian Science Foundation for the submission of project proposals, management and monitoring of funded projects

sig_aa9bf871720f9c6c88a4.description: The Assignment comprises the supply, implementation and support of a new Energy Management System (EnMS) for the Universiteit Leiden. A well-functioning Energy Registration and Monitoring System (EBS) forms an integral part of the EnMS solution. An EBS is legally required for the majority of buildings. The EnMS solution must therefore comply with the applicable guidelines as established by the Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO). With this tender, the Contracting Authority aims to have a scalable, future-proof and securely configured SaaS solution that unlocks reliable energy information and provides support for legal obligations, financial processes and sustainability objectives. The EnMS acts as the primary system for long-term storage, management and analysis of the Contracting Authority's energy data. The EnMS must integrate in a robust and traceable manner with existing systems and data sources of the Universiteit Leiden and be suitable for data exchange within the existing information provision. The Assignment consists of the following components: the supply, implementation and support of an EnMS as a SaaS solution, the supply of monitoring services focused on data quality and continuity, the supply of additional functionality modules and dashboards (optional). There is no purchase obligation for component 3. The Contracting Authority wishes to be able to purchase modules and dashboards optionally and separately from each other according to use during the term of the Agreement. Whether or not the full offering of component 3 is provided does not constitute grounds for exclusion. The extent to which the functionality of the requested modules and/or dashboards is offered will, however, be taken into account in the quality assessment of the tender.
sig_aa9bf871720f9c6c88a4.title: Energy Management System

sig_ab7ff793e66f36db5343.description: The objective of the Cybersecurity Innovation for Cyberinfrastructure (CICI) program is to advance scientific discovery and innovation by enhancing the security and privacy of cyberinfrastructure. CICI supports efforts to develop, deploy and integrate cybersecurity that will benefit the broader scientific community by securing science data, computation, collaborations workflows, and infrastructure. CICI recognizes the unique nature of modern, complex, data-driven, distributed, rapid, and collaborative science and the breadth of infrastructure and requirements across scientific disciplines, practitioners, researchers, and projects. CICI seeks proposals in four program areas: 1. Usable and Collaborative Security for Science (UCSS): Projects in this program area should support novel and/or applied security and usability research that facilitates scientific collaboration, encourages the adoption of security into the scientific workflow, and helps create a holistic, integrated security environment that spans the entire scientific cyberinfrastructure ecosystem. 2. Reference Scientific Security Datasets (RSSD): Projects in this program area should leverage instrumented cyberinfrastructure to capture metadata from scientific workflows and workloads as reference data artifacts that can help support reproducible security research, testing and evaluation. 3. Transition to Cyberinfrastructure Resilience (TCR): Projects in this program area should improve the robustness, trustworthiness, integrity, and/or resilience of scientific cyberinfrastructure through testing, evaluation, hardening, validation, and technology transition of novel cybersecurity research. The TCR area further encourages transition activities that advance the deployment and use of reproducibility in CI, workflows, and data. 4. Integrity, Provenance, and Authenticity for Artificial Intelligence Ready Data (IPAAI): Projects in this program area should enhance confidence and reproducibility in AI produced scientific results by improving the integrity, provenance, and authenticity of scientific datasets used by Artificial Intelligence systems.
sig_ab7ff793e66f36db5343.title: Cybersecurity Innovation for Cyberinfrastructure

sig_ac713fa09508499cc094.description: NHS Supply Chain is preparing a national framework agreement that will support the procurement of dental consumables, clinical solutions, equipment, digital technologies, diagnostics, and practice infrastructure, structured across the following indicative lots: The following lot structure is indicative and subject to final confirmation: Lot 1: Dental Consumables & Appliances Lot 2: Specialist Clinical & Bespoke Solutions Lot 3: Operatory Equipment Lot 4: Dental Laboratory & Digital Solutions Lot 5: Dental Imaging & Diagnostics Lot 6: Dental Environment, Decontamination & Practice Building Lot 7: Mobile Dental Clinics & Equipment Note: For future tenders the following requirements will apply: • ISO Certification: Tenderers must have ISO 9001: 2015 or BS EN ISO 13485:2016 certification or Medical Device Single Audit Program (MDSAP) certification accredited by the United Kingdom Accreditation Service (UKAS) (or international equivalent) to cover all segments of the Tenderer’s and the product’s supply chain. Link for acceptable alternatives https://iaf.nu/en/accreditation-bodies/ (‘Notified Bodies’). • CE Certification and Declaration of Conformity certificates are required where applicable to be presented at submission stage of the tender. • Modern Slavery for Tenderers that have an annual turnover of at least £36 million must have a link to their modern slavery statement on their website • Modern Slavery Assessment Tool (MSAT) Tenderers must have a score of 41% or above within 12 months of the Tender Publication Date via https://supplierregistration.cabinetoffice.gov.uk/ • Evergreen Sustainable Supplier Assessment – Tenderers will need to have completed the assessment and achieved Level 1 within the 12 months prior to the Tender Close Date. Link for instructions and access for this assessment: https://www.england.nhs.uk/nhs-commercial/central-commercial-function-ccf/evergreen/ • Carbon Reduction Plan (CRP): Tenderers must have a valid CRP link on their website that meets the requirements of PPN 006 as outlined in the PPN, OR Where Supplier has no website, the CRP is provided in PDF format that meets the requirements of PPN 006 as outlined in the PPN, OR Excused in exceptional circumstances. • Cyber Security: If you handle patient or personal data, or provide any IT systems, services, or devices you will need to have a Cyber Security Essentials Plus Certificate. Lot 1: Dental Consumables & Appliances. This Lot provides dental consumables and appliance-based solutions designed to support the delivery of routine and specialist dental care across primary, community, and secondary care settings. These products include single use and repeat use materials, small appliances, and consumable items required for preventive dentistry, restorative procedures, orthodontics, minor oral surgery, anaesthesia, and infection control. The scope includes consumables and all associated accessories, where applicable, required to support safe, effective, and compliant dental treatment. Lot 2: Specialist Clinical & Bespoke Solutions. This Lot covers specialist clinical systems, implantology and orthodontic products, as well as bespoke dental laboratory appliances and restorations manufactured to individual patient requirements. It covers powered systems, procedure kits and software enabled treatment solutions that support diagnosis, planning and delivery of specialist dental care. The scope includes devices and all associated equipment, accessories, consumables (where part of a system), maintenance, software, technical support and training. Additionally, it covers the provision of patient specific and bespoke restorations. Lot 3: Operatory Equipment. This Lot provides dental operatory equipment used for routine chairside patient care within dental treatment environments. It includes dental treatment units, delivery systems, operating lights, handpieces, micromotors, ultrasonic scaling systems, mobile treatment carts and associated operatory infrastructure, including suction systems and compressors. This Lot excludes specialist clinical systems used within defined endodontic, implantology, orthodontic and oral surgery workflows, which fall within the scope of Lot 2 – Specialist Clinical & Bespoke Solutions. Lot 4: Dental Laboratory & Digital Solutions. This Lot provides digital dentistry and laboratory solutions spanning the design, manufacture and finishing of dental restorations and appliances, and supports associated digital workflows. sig_adeabf193c7fb0efdf52.description: Public procurement of services for developing a Metaverse platform and implementing a Digital Twin management system for the DANUBIUS-RI infrastructure Hub, within the Project with the acronym DANUBIUS-RO-2, Financing contract for the Programme 5.9 Research in areas of strategic interest, Subprogramme 5.9.4 River, delta and sea systems - DANUBIUS within the National Research, Development and Innovation Plan 2022-2027, no. 1D of 03.10.2025. The National Institute for Research and Development for Biological Sciences Bucharest (INCDSB) nationally coordinates the DANUBIUS-RO project through which the construction and operationalisation of the Romanian components of the pan-European DANUBIUS-RI infrastructure are financed: the Hub and the Danube Delta Supersite. DANUBIUS-RO is established as a complex network of laboratories, field stations and observation points intended for monitoring the marine, coastal and river environment, with an emphasis on areas of strategic interest such as the Danube Delta, the Black Sea coastline and the lower sector of the Danube. The continuous development of the research infrastructure through applied research projects carried out by INCDSB and its partners in the Danube Delta Biosphere Reserve area - including within national and European programmes dedicated to natural risk monitoring, environmental protection and climate change adaptation - requires particular attention to the sustainability and resilience of the set of buildings belonging to the Hub in Murighiol. This must support increasingly large flows of scientific data, images and complex measurements originating from the field, with a view to transmitting them to processing and analysis centres in Murighiol, Tulcea, Galați, Constanța and Bucharest. In the context of the expansion of the network of observation points and the increase in the volume of information generated by monitoring and research equipment, it has become necessary to modernise the integrated data processing infrastructure for the collected data. Therefore, the acquisition of services for developing a Metaverse-type platform and implementing a Digital Twin-type management system is required for the DANUBIUS-RI infrastructure Hub, enabling the unitary integration of data collected within the Hub's laboratories and activities related to the Danube Delta Supersite for monitoring the marine and fluvial environment, geodynamic risks and coastal erosion processes. This infrastructure will contribute to improving analysis, early warning and decision-making support capabilities, consolidating the role of INCDSB and institutional partners in sustainable resource management and in the efficient organisation of research ecosystems of national and European importance.
sig_adeabf193c7fb0efdf52.title: Services for developing a Metaverse platform and implementing a Digital Twin management system for the DANUBIUS-RI infrastructure Hub

sig_adf3ec62fa9c411ec75b.description: The Contractor shall provide Think Trends Software as an Agentic AI and Document Intelligence solution capable of processing structured, semi-structured, and unstructured adverse event documents, including scanned PDFs, handwritten or machine-generated forms, narratives, attachments, medical records, product complaints, lab reports, follow-up submissions, and case correspondence. The solution shall support end-to-end adverse event document processing through the following capabilities: A. Agentic Document Intake and Classification Think Trends Software AI agents shall automatically receive, classify, and route adverse event documents by submission type, FDA Center, product category, source, urgency, and case-processing requirements. The intake agent shall identify whether a document relates to drugs, biologics, devices, veterinary products, tobacco products, combination products, or other FDA-regulated products. Key capabilities include: • Automated ingestion of scanned PDFs, forms, emails, images, attachments, and electronic documents. • Classification of documents by Center-specific workflow, product type, and reporting pathway. • Detection of new cases, follow-up cases, duplicate submissions, incomplete submissions, and supporting attachments. • Intelligent routing to appropriate review queues, case-processing teams, or downstream systems. B. Agentic OCR and Intelligent Data Extraction Think Trends Software Agentic OCR shall combine optical character recognition, computer vision, natural language processing, large language models, and rule-based validation agents to extract key adverse event data elements from complex documents. The platform shall extract and structure critical case information, including: • Reporter, patient, animal, subject, or consumer information. • Product information, including drug, biologic, device, tobacco, or veterinary product details. • Adverse event terms, symptoms, outcomes, seriousness, and event narratives. • Dates, timelines, exposure details, dose, route, duration, lot numbers, manufacturer information, and product identifiers. • Medical history, concomitant products, lab results, device problem codes, clinical narratives, and follow-up information. • Center-specific data elements required for CVM-Drugs and CVM-Food, CDRH, CTP, CDER, CBER and HFP. C. Center-Specific Adverse Event Processing Agents The Contractor shall configure specialized AI agents within Think Trends Software to support unique regulatory and operational needs across FDA Centers. Each agent shall apply Center-specific data models, validation logic, terminology, business rules, and review workflows. Examples include: • CVM Agent: Processes veterinary adverse event reports, animal species, breed, weight, product exposure, dosage, outcome, and veterinarian/reporter information. • CDRH Agent: Processes device-related adverse events, device identifiers, manufacturer information, malfunction details, patient impact, and device problem descriptions. • CTP Agent: Processes tobacco product adverse experiences, product use patterns, health effects, consumer narratives, and product category information. • HFP Agent: Processes HFP-specific adverse event reporting requirements and associated workflows. • CDER Agent: Process drug product adverse experiences, product use patterns, health effects, consumer narratives, and product category information. • CBER Agent: Processes biologics product adverse experiences, product use patterns, health effects, consumer narratives, and product category information. D. Case Validation, Quality Control, and Human-in-the-Loop Review Think Trends Software shall incorporate validation agents to compare extracted data against business rules, required fields, confidence thresholds, terminology standards, and case-processing logic. Records that meet defined thresholds may proceed automatically, while exceptions shall be routed for human review. Key quality-control features include: • Confidence scoring at field, document, and case levels. • Source traceability to page, section, table, and line references. • Automated flagging of missing, inconsistent, conflicting, or low-confidence data. • Human-in-the-loop review screens for case processors and safety reviewers. • Reviewer acceptance, correction, override, and approval workflows. • Full audit trail of AI extraction, human edits, and final approved values. E. Data Standardization and Regulatory Output Generation Think Trends Software shall transform extracted adverse event information into structured formats required for case management, analytics, and downstream regulatory processing. The platform shall support configurable mappings to FDA data standards, Center-specific systems, XML structures, APIs, and reporting formats. Capabilities include: • Normalization of adverse event terms, product names, dates, identifiers, and narrative fields. • Mapping to Center-specific safety data models and controlled terminology. • Generation of structured case records for downstream review and processing. • API-based integration with FDA systems, case-processing platforms, data lakes, document repositories, and workflow tools. • Export to XML, JSON, CSV, database tables, or other required formats. F. Agentic Workflow Automation and Triage Think Trends Software shall automate repetitive case-processing steps while maintaining reviewer control for regulatory decisions. The system shall support configurable AI agents capable of executing multi-step workflows, requesting missing information, summarizing case narratives, identifying seriousness indicators, detecting duplicates, and prioritizing work queues. Workflow automation shall include: • Case prioritization based on seriousness, product risk, event severity, due dates, and Center-defined rules. • Automated summarization of long adverse event narratives and supporting attachments. • Duplicate and follow-up detection across submissions. • Exception handling and escalation workflows. • Generation of reviewer-ready case summaries. • Dashboard visibility into case volumes, processing status, aging, backlog, error rates, and productivity metrics. G. AI-Enabled Redaction for FOIA Compliance ThinkTrends will provide AI-powered redaction capabilities to support FDA's obligations under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA). The platform will automatically identify and redact personally identifiable information (PII), protected health information (PHI), commercially confidential data, law-enforcement-sensitive content, and other exemption-covered materials from adverse event documents prior to public release or response to FOIA requests. Key capabilities include: • Automated detection and redaction of PII and PHI, including patient names, addresses, dates of birth, medical record numbers, Social Security numbers, and other personal identifiers. • Identification and suppression of trade secrets, proprietary formulations, manufacturing processes, and commercially confidential submitter information protected under FOIA Exemption. • Detection of law-enforcement-sensitive and inter-agency deliberative content subject to FOIA Exemptions. • Configurable exemption profiles aligned to FDA FOIA policy, Center-specific guidance, and applicable federal regulations. • Confidence-scored redaction recommendations with source traceability, enabling FOIA reviewers to accept, modify, or override AI-proposed redactions. • Human-in-the-loop review workflow allowing FOIA analysts to validate, annotate, and finalize redacted documents before release. • Generation of redacted PDF and document versions with visible redaction markers, exemption codes, and reviewer audit annotations. • Full audit trail recording every AI-proposed redaction, reviewer decision, exemption code applied, and final release determination. • Support for bulk redaction processing across large FOIA request batches, including multi-document packages and rolling requests. • Integration with FDA FOIA tracking systems, document repositories, and case management workflows. 1.3 SALIENT FEATURES OF THINK TRENDS SOFTWARE Think Trends Software provides the following differentiating capabilities relevant to FDA adverse event reporting modernization: 1. Agentic OCR Beyond Traditional OCR: Think Trends Software does not merely convert images to text. It applies AI agents that read, interpret, validate, cross-check, and structure regulatory information from complex adverse event documents. 2. Center-Agnostic Core with Center-Specific Configuration: The platform provides a common document intelligence foundation while allowing FDA Centers such as CVM, CDRH, CTP, and HFP to configure unique workflows, data models, rules, and outputs. 3. End-to-End Adverse Event Case Automation: Think Trends Software supports intake, classification, extraction, validation, triage, routing, human review, data transformation, and downstream submission/output generation. 4. Human-in-the-Loop Regulatory Control: The system keeps FDA reviewers in control by allowing them to review, correct, approve, or override AI-generated outputs before final case acceptance. 5. Explainability and Source Traceability: Each extracted field can be traced back to the original source document, page, section, and text reference, supporting transparency, auditability, and reviewer confidence. 6. Confidence-Based Processing: Think Trends Software assigns confidence scores to extracted data and automatically routes low-confidence or inconsistent records for human review. 7. Multi-Document and Multi-Format Processing: Think Trends Software shall process scanned PDFs, structured forms, unstructured narratives, tables, handwritten content where feasible, images, attachments, correspondence, and supporting records. 8. Duplicate and Follow-Up Detection: AI agents shall compare incoming submissions against existing records to identify potential duplicates, follow-ups, related cases, and case-history updates. 9. Reviewer-Ready Case Summaries: Think Trends Software shall generate concise adverse event summaries, chronology, product-event relationships, missing-field lists, and review-ready case packages. 10. Secure FDA-Aligned Deployment: Think Trends Software shall be deployable in secure government cloud, FDA-managed, or approved hosting environments with role-based access, audit logs, encryption, and integration with enterprise identity management. 1.4 TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS Implementation of Think Trends Software for adverse event document processing is expected to deliver the following outcomes: • Reduction in manual data entry and repetitive case-processing tasks. • Faster adverse event intake, triage, and reviewer preparation. • Improved data quality through AI-assisted validation and standardization. • Greater consistency across FDA Centers while preserving Center-specific workflows. • Enhanced traceability, auditability, and regulatory transparency. • Improved ability to manage high-volume document backlogs and surge workloads. • Increased reviewer productivity through AI-generated summaries and exception-based review. • Scalable platform foundation for future FDA adverse event modernization initiatives. Please view the attached Request for Quote (RFQ) RFQ FDA-SOL-75F40126Q00384 document for additional information.

sig_ae09df885b46a839920c.description: BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF THE INFORMATION REQUEST Helsingin kaupunki, kaupunkiympäristön toimiala (hereinafter referred to as "KYMP") is preparing a procurement procedure regarding the "Procurement of an application for infrastructure construction supervision and situational awareness". Before initiating the actual procurement procedure, KYMP is surveying the market supply, willingness and interest to tender for the procurement in question, and is seeking answers to questions related to the planned procurement. The information request is not a contract notice or a call for tenders, but a market dialogue. The publication of the information request does not initiate a procurement procedure. The contract notice and call for tenders will be published later. The information request does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Answering the information request is not a prerequisite for participating in any later procurement procedure that may be organised. Market operators will not be paid compensation for answering the information request or participating in the market dialogue. Information obtained through the information request may be used in the preparation of procurement documents. BACKGROUND AND OBJECT OF THE PROCUREMENT The Urban Environment Division (KYMP) is implementing the procurement of an application for infrastructure construction supervision and situational awareness. The City of Helsinki has not previously used a system intended for infrastructure construction contract management. In the current situation, information related to an individual contract is scattered across the systems of the Client and contractors, a large part of communication takes place solely via email, operating models in different contracts and among contractors vary, and up-to-date information is not easily accessible to all parties to the contract or in cover situations. In the current situation, contract management processes such as reporting, site diaries and defect repairs lack modern tools that can be smoothly utilised in fieldwork; instead, a large part of the entries are first made on paper and recorded digitally afterwards. Tools intended for the management of infrastructure site contracts have been piloted and test-used in the sector, and it has been observed that the use of a contract management system can speed up and streamline, among other things, the preparation of inspection reports and the sharing of reports between the parties. The key objective of the procurement is the procurement and implementation of a system suitable for monitoring infrastructure construction projects from project preparation to the end of the warranty period, and particularly for management, tasks, communication and field conditions during the contract implementation phase. The background and object of the procurement are described in more detail in the appendix to the information request, Description of the object of the procurement. INFORMATION REQUEST KYMP requests informal answers to the questions in the document "Change proposal table_for technical market dialogue_TENDERER_FILLS IN" attached to the information request, and to mark any proposed changes. Please submit your answers by email to kymp.icthankinnat@hel.fi no later than 17.4.2026 at 16.15. KYMP will treat the answers confidentially. PROCUREMENT PROCEDURE AND SCHEDULE Preliminary schedule of the procurement: March 2026 Information request May 2026 Publication of the call for tenders June 2026 Procurement decision and conclusion of the procurement contract

Supply of a forest fire location system divided into two parts. Part No. 1 - Supply, installation and commissioning of a forest fire monitoring system based on long-range fire-fighting cameras together with software for automatic smoke detection. Part No. 2 - Supply, installation and commissioning of a complete unmanned aerial vehicle system with an automatic docking station for fire monitoring of forest areas. A detailed description can be found in the relevant parts of the contract. The subject of the contract consists of sets of equipment together with installation and commissioning, the task of which will be to enable automatic detection and location of forest fires, including long-range fire-fighting cameras mounted on observation towers together with necessary accessories and the equipment of the Inspectorate's Alarm and Dispatch Point (ADP). The purpose of the system will be to carry out continuous fire monitoring of forest areas. Fire-fighting cameras mounted on observation towers are to work with the supplied software for automatic fire detection, which is intended to increase the effectiveness of monitoring in the given area. The image from the cameras must be sent to the ADP via a radio link in the unlicensed band, supplied and installed under this contract. The transmission system must be designed in a way that enables the future change of the transmission medium from radio to fibre-optic without the need to replace cameras, software and active network devices, with the exception of terminal devices used for connecting the fibre optic.. The Baczków and Hysne towers should be retrofitted with an Off-Grid power supply installation, and the ADP with a UPS emergency power supply system. The power supply must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62040-5-3:2017-05 (UPS systems) or equivalent. The installation must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62446-1:2016-08 (Photovoltaic installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62446-1:2016-08/A1:2019-01 (Testing of PV installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62109-2:2011 (Inverter safety) or equivalent and PN-EN IEC 62619:2023-02 (Lithium battery safety) or equivalent. The contract includes: - dismantling of the existing fire monitoring system, - supply and installation of 3 cameras for observing forest areas on the Baczków, Hysne and Dąbrowa fire-fighting towers, - supply and installation of sprinklers together with a fluid tank for the mounted cameras, - supply and installation of an off-grid power supply on the Baczków and Hysne towers. sig_aeb74ace210c4b154643.buyer_name: German Federal Bank, Procurement Central Division
sig_aeb74ace210c4b154643.description: The progressive digitalisation of core business processes, geopolitical developments and rising European requirements for data sovereignty and compliance require a future-proof and resilient IT infrastructure. As the independent central bank of the Federal Republic of Germany and part of the European System of Central Banks (ESCB), the Deutsche Bundesbank establishes the highest requirements for the autonomy, sovereignty and performance of its IT portfolio. To achieve the combination of these ambitious goals, the Deutsche Bundesbank requires reliable partners also for sovereign cloud services. With the strategic decision to use sovereign cloud services in addition to other public cloud services, the Deutsche Bundesbank pursues the goal of strengthening the digital sovereignty and security of its IT infrastructure without having to dispense with the innovative strength and scalability of modern public cloud offerings. In the course of this strategic orientation, the Deutsche Bundesbank is therefore initiating a structured market exploration. The aim of this measure is to systematically determine the performance and suitability of the sovereign cloud services available on the market. In doing so, it is to be examined in particular to what extent the existing service portfolios of the providers meet the technical, legal, organisational and security-related requirements of the Deutsche Bundesbank. This market exploration therefore focuses on cloud computing offerings that fulfil the European Commission's understanding of full digital sovereignty ("Technology and operations under complete EU control, subject only to EU law, with no critical non-EU dependencies", cf. EU Cloud Sovereignty Framework). The Deutsche Bundesbank reserves the right to define the concept of digital sovereignty more broadly and deviating from the aforementioned scope. Further details on the Deutsche Bundesbank's requirements for sovereign cloud services can be obtained exclusively upon request from the email address provided in the contact details. This market exploration also serves to involve the market at an early stage in a potentially pending EU-wide procurement procedure by the Deutsche Bundesbank for the procurement of cloud services and forms, among other things, a basis for decision-making for its technical design. This market exploration is not a procurement procedure directed at the award of a public contract and does not constitute either an offer or an invitation to conclude a contract. The implementation of a procurement procedure, including with a different service scope, remains reserved. Participation in this market exploration has no consequences (neither preferential treatment nor disadvantage) for the participating company within the framework of a potential future procurement process. Participants in this market exploration have no entitlement to the acquisition of knowledge from the results of the market exploration.
sig_aeb74ace210c4b154643.title: Market exploration: Sovereign cloud services for the Deutsche Bundesbank

sig_b0c1708c04f418b41358.description: In the field of traditional software, Software Bills of Materials (SBOMs) – that is, parts lists containing information about software components and their dependencies – have long been in use and are even required by the Cyber Resilience Act (CRA). This requirement also applies to AI systems, yet the idea of an SBOM specific to AI systems is relatively new. Initial approaches therefore carry the risk that they do not cover all necessary aspects with regard to the transparency of the AI supply chain. In this project, the concept "SBOM for AI - Minimum Elements" published within the G7 framework is to be put into practice and a technical implementation of the defined criteria developed for this purpose. The SBOM for AI is to be generated automatically and output in a suitable format. The developed implementation is subsequently to be made available to all stakeholders in order to make an important contribution to the cybersecurity of AI systems.
sig_b0c1708c04f418b41358.title: Project 1034: Technical implementation of an SBOM for AI (SBOM4AI)

sig_b154032bf832453654ce.description: THIS IS NOT A PRIOR INFORMATION NOTICE, CONTRACT NOTICE OR CALL FOR TENDERS, BUT A NOTICE OF THE LAUNCH OF MARKET DIALOGUE AS PART OF PROCUREMENT PLANNING. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue is surveying suppliers' interest in the tendering process concerning a financial planning system. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue (LUVN) is responsible for organising social welfare and healthcare services as well as rescue services in its region. The wellbeing services county employs approximately 10 000 persons, and its annual net expenditure is approximately 2 billion euros. Operations are managed as an entity of five service areas and forty service lines. Approximately 400 persons participate in financial planning annually, and the entity to be planned covers approximately 1 000 cost centres. This information request is part of a market dialogue, the aim of which is to survey the solutions available on the market to support financial planning. The information request is not a contract notice, nor does it bind the wellbeing services county or suppliers to subsequent procedures. 1. SUBJECT OF THE PROCUREMENT AND OBJECTIVE LUVN is planning the procurement of a financial planning system, which can be used to prepare a budget, financial plans, forecasts and other financial planning at various levels of the organisation. The objective is to survey possibilities to improve the quality, rolling nature, consistency, transparency and operational reliability of financial planning in the wellbeing services county's extensive operational entity. The objective is also to automate processes by, among other things, utilising artificial intelligence. The following features, among others, are desired from the system: - Preparation of budget and forecasts - Personnel planning: Planning is carried out on a FTE basis so that the output contains both a personnel plan and a monetary budget - Internal invoicing: cost allocation and support for invoicing processes. The organisation operates 3 responsibility areas (Digital Services, Service Centre, Property Services), whose costs are invoiced to the rest of the organisation on the basis of causation. The entity is significant both in terms of financial impact and required workload - Purchase service planning: customisable driver-based calculation models and planning structures - Extensive support for calculation dimensions: mandatory and optional entry dimensions - High-quality data transfer and reporting features - The system must provide an interface through which data can be transferred at a frequent update interval to the customer's database 2. PARTICIPATION IN THE MARKET DIALOGUE Suppliers are invited to participate in the market dialogue by responding to this information request. The requested information is provided in section "Other information" of the form. The questionnaire responses collect basic company information, contact details, and in-depth system information, which serve as the basis for selecting the suppliers with which LUVN will hold further discussions in the form of remote meetings. Any additional information and attachments are requested to be attached to the response in section "Other information, Brochure / other possible attachments". 3. IMPLEMENTATION OF THE MARKET DIALOGUE The wellbeing services county will process the information provided by all suppliers and, if necessary, organise separate remote meetings where understanding of the functionalities of the systems and their suitability for the organisation's needs can be deepened. Participation in the market dialogue is voluntary and does not bind suppliers to future procurement procedures.
sig_b154032bf832453654ce.title: INFORMATION REQUEST: Procurement of a financial planning system

sig_b1beabd691d4eaf994e6.description: The Contractor shall provide Think Trends Software as an Agentic AI and Document Intelligence solution capable of processing structured, semi-structured, and unstructured adverse event documents, including scanned PDFs, handwritten or machine-generated forms, narratives, attachments, medical records, product complaints, lab reports, follow-up submissions, and case correspondence. The solution shall support end-to-end adverse event document processing through the following capabilities: A. Agentic Document Intake and Classification Think Trends Software AI agents shall automatically receive, classify, and route adverse event documents by submission type, FDA Center, product category, source, urgency, and case-processing requirements. The intake agent shall identify whether a document relates to drugs, biologics, devices, veterinary products, tobacco products, combination products, or other FDA-regulated products. Key capabilities include: • Automated ingestion of scanned PDFs, forms, emails, images, attachments, and electronic documents. • Classification of documents by Center-specific workflow, product type, and reporting pathway. • Detection of new cases, follow-up cases, duplicate submissions, incomplete submissions, and supporting attachments. • Intelligent routing to appropriate review queues, case-processing teams, or downstream systems. B. Agentic OCR and Intelligent Data Extraction Think Trends Software Agentic OCR shall combine optical character recognition, computer vision, natural language processing, large language models, and rule-based validation agents to extract key adverse event data elements from complex documents. The platform shall extract and structure critical case information, including: • Reporter, patient, animal, subject, or consumer information. • Product information, including drug, biologic, device, tobacco, or veterinary product details. • Adverse event terms, symptoms, outcomes, seriousness, and event narratives. • Dates, timelines, exposure details, dose, route, duration, lot numbers, manufacturer information, and product identifiers. • Medical history, concomitant products, lab results, device problem codes, clinical narratives, and follow-up information. • Center-specific data elements required for CVM-Drugs and CVM-Food, CDRH, CTP, CDER, CBER and HFP. C. Center-Specific Adverse Event Processing Agents The Contractor shall configure specialized AI agents within Think Trends Software to support unique regulatory and operational needs across FDA Centers. Each agent shall apply Center-specific data models, validation logic, terminology, business rules, and review workflows. Examples include: • CVM Agent: Processes veterinary adverse event reports, animal species, breed, weight, product exposure, dosage, outcome, and veterinarian/reporter information. • CDRH Agent: Processes device-related adverse events, device identifiers, manufacturer information, malfunction details, patient impact, and device problem descriptions. • CTP Agent: Processes tobacco product adverse experiences, product use patterns, health effects, consumer narratives, and product category information. • HFP Agent: Processes HFP-specific adverse event reporting requirements and associated workflows. • CDER Agent: Process drug product adverse experiences, product use patterns, health effects, consumer narratives, and product category information. • CBER Agent: Processes biologics product adverse experiences, product use patterns, health effects, consumer narratives, and product category information. D. Case Validation, Quality Control, and Human-in-the-Loop Review Think Trends Software shall incorporate validation agents to compare extracted data against business rules, required fields, confidence thresholds, terminology standards, and case-processing logic. Records that meet defined thresholds may proceed automatically, while exceptions shall be routed for human review. Key quality-control features include: • Confidence scoring at field, document, and case levels. • Source traceability to page, section, table, and line references. • Automated flagging of missing, inconsistent, conflicting, or low-confidence data. • Human-in-the-loop review screens for case processors and safety reviewers. • Reviewer acceptance, correction, override, and approval workflows. • Full audit trail of AI extraction, human edits, and final approved values. E. Data Standardization and Regulatory Output Generation Think Trends Software shall transform extracted adverse event information into structured formats required for case management, analytics, and downstream regulatory processing. The platform shall support configurable mappings to FDA data standards, Center-specific systems, XML structures, APIs, and reporting formats. Capabilities include: • Normalization of adverse event terms, product names, dates, identifiers, and narrative fields. • Mapping to Center-specific safety data models and controlled terminology. • Generation of structured case records for downstream review and processing. • API-based integration with FDA systems, case-processing platforms, data lakes, document repositories, and workflow tools. • Export to XML, JSON, CSV, database tables, or other required formats. F. Agentic Workflow Automation and Triage Think Trends Software shall automate repetitive case-processing steps while maintaining reviewer control for regulatory decisions. The system shall support configurable AI agents capable of executing multi-step workflows, requesting missing information, summarizing case narratives, identifying seriousness indicators, detecting duplicates, and prioritizing work queues. Workflow automation shall include: • Case prioritization based on seriousness, product risk, event severity, due dates, and Center-defined rules. • Automated summarization of long adverse event narratives and supporting attachments. • Duplicate and follow-up detection across submissions. • Exception handling and escalation workflows. • Generation of reviewer-ready case summaries. • Dashboard visibility into case volumes, processing status, aging, backlog, error rates, and productivity metrics. G. AI-Enabled Redaction for FOIA Compliance ThinkTrends will provide AI-powered redaction capabilities to support FDA's obligations under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA). The platform will automatically identify and redact personally identifiable information (PII), protected health information (PHI), commercially confidential data, law-enforcement-sensitive content, and other exemption-covered materials from adverse event documents prior to public release or response to FOIA requests. Key capabilities include: • Automated detection and redaction of PII and PHI, including patient names, addresses, dates of birth, medical record numbers, Social Security numbers, and other personal identifiers. • Identification and suppression of trade secrets, proprietary formulations, manufacturing processes, and commercially confidential submitter information protected under FOIA Exemption. • Detection of law-enforcement-sensitive and inter-agency deliberative content subject to FOIA Exemptions. • Configurable exemption profiles aligned to FDA FOIA policy, Center-specific guidance, and applicable federal regulations. • Confidence-scored redaction recommendations with source traceability, enabling FOIA reviewers to accept, modify, or override AI-proposed redactions. • Human-in-the-loop review workflow allowing FOIA analysts to validate, annotate, and finalize redacted documents before release. • Generation of redacted PDF and document versions with visible redaction markers, exemption codes, and reviewer audit annotations. • Full audit trail recording every AI-proposed redaction, reviewer decision, exemption code applied, and final release determination. • Support for bulk redaction processing across large FOIA request batches, including multi-document packages and rolling requests. • Integration with FDA FOIA tracking systems, document repositories, and case management workflows. 1.3 SALIENT FEATURES OF THINK TRENDS SOFTWARE Think Trends Software provides the following differentiating capabilities relevant to FDA adverse event reporting modernization: 1. Agentic OCR Beyond Traditional OCR: Think Trends Software does not merely convert images to text. It applies AI agents that read, interpret, validate, cross-check, and structure regulatory information from complex adverse event documents. 2. Center-Agnostic Core with Center-Specific Configuration: The platform provides a common document intelligence foundation while allowing FDA Centers such as CVM, CDRH, CTP, and HFP to configure unique workflows, data models, rules, and outputs. 3. End-to-End Adverse Event Case Automation: Think Trends Software supports intake, classification, extraction, validation, triage, routing, human review, data transformation, and downstream submission/output generation. 4. Human-in-the-Loop Regulatory Control: The system keeps FDA reviewers in control by allowing them to review, correct, approve, or override AI-generated outputs before final case acceptance. 5. Explainability and Source Traceability: Each extracted field can be traced back to the original source document, page, section, and text reference, supporting transparency, auditability, and reviewer confidence. 6. Confidence-Based Processing: Think Trends Software assigns confidence scores to extracted data and automatically routes low-confidence or inconsistent records for human review. 7. Multi-Document and Multi-Format Processing: Think Trends Software shall process scanned PDFs, structured forms, unstructured narratives, tables, handwritten content where feasible, images, attachments, correspondence, and supporting records. 8. Duplicate and Follow-Up Detection: AI agents shall compare incoming submissions against existing records to identify potential duplicates, follow-ups, related cases, and case-history updates. 9. Reviewer-Ready Case Summaries: Think Trends Software shall generate concise adverse event summaries, chronology, product-event relationships, missing-field lists, and review-ready case packages. 10. Secure FDA-Aligned Deployment: Think Trends Software shall be deployable in secure government cloud, FDA-managed, or approved hosting environments with role-based access, audit logs, encryption, and integration with enterprise identity management. 1.4 TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS Implementation of Think Trends Software for adverse event document processing is expected to deliver the following outcomes: • Reduction in manual data entry and repetitive case-processing tasks. • Faster adverse event intake, triage, and reviewer preparation. • Improved data quality through AI-assisted validation and standardization. • Greater consistency across FDA Centers while preserving Center-specific workflows. • Enhanced traceability, auditability, and regulatory transparency. • Improved ability to manage high-volume document backlogs and surge workloads. • Increased reviewer productivity through AI-generated summaries and exception-based review. • Scalable platform foundation for future FDA adverse event modernization initiatives. Please view the attached Request for Quote (RFQ) RFQ FDA-SOL-75F40126Q00384 document for additional information.

sig_b1f961554688efa86265.description: KS Digital has, on behalf of the Committee Council, established a work group that shall review how the municipal sector can cooperate on the future childhood and school administration systems (OAS/SAS), digital ecosystems and possibilities for future joint procurements. The work includes both education and school administrative systems (OAS/SAS), the digital eco-system included in them, and how the municipal sector can strengthen coordination, standardisation and any future joint procurements. As a part of this work, we invite the supplier market to a dialogue. We want insight into how the market assesses developments in the area, what technological and organisational possibilities exist, and how the municipal sector and the supplier market together can contribute to a more open, coherent and future orientated digital ecosystem for the education sector. The work is anchored in a reported need from the municipalities for stronger coordination in relation to requirements, standardisation, architecture, data sharing, procurements and further development of digital systems in the area of adolescence. The aim is not to define a new system, but to assess how the municipal sector together can contribute to a more coherent, open and future orientated digital ecosystem for children, youths, guardians, employees, managers, owners and associated services. An important goal is also to contribute to a supplier market that supports this development, through clear common needs, standards and framework conditions that stimulate innovation and sustainable development of the systems. Information on the market dialogue including registration will be in the tender https://ksdigital.no/markedsdialoger-og-anskaffelser/

sig_b284571d28359b987a79.description: The Brandenburg IT Service Provider (ZIT-BB) is the central service provider for the direct state administration of Brandenburg for the provision of IT services. Its extensive task portfolio includes, amongst other things, the planning, provision and operation of technical infrastructure as well as the coordination and support of both authority-specific and cross-authority and joint IT procedures. Its area of responsibility also includes IT security management for the state administration's IT infrastructure and responsibility for the Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT). From its central location in Potsdam, ZIT-BB currently supports approx. 18.000 workstations in the Brandenburg state administration. The number of workstations to be supported will increase further in the coming years. With the centralisation of the state administration's IT, supporting the authorities and institutions of the State of Brandenburg in the planning, design and use of information technology, as well as consulting on IT security issues, has become a core field of activity for the operation. Furthermore, ZIT-BB provides services in accordance with the Brandenburg e-Government Act, in particular for municipalities, administrative offices and municipal associations of the state. The main location of ZIT-BB is located at Steinstraße 104-106 in 14480 Potsdam. Due to its nationwide responsibility, ZIT-BB has branch offices in Cottbus, Frankfurt (Oder), Wünsdorf, Gransee and Eberswalde, among others. It operates its data centre in Berlin. Lot LOT-0001: External Information Security Officer for the Brandenburg IT Service Provider. sig_b3aff275208f654a526c.description: The UK Home Office (referred to hereafter as the Authority) is inviting prospective bidders to take part in a series of pre-market engagement activities for the Authority's planned QAT procurements. The Authority currently has a number of contracts for QAT capability, aligned to portfolios across the Home Office. The future commercial strategy is to consolidate these services into two core testing capability contracts by Autumn 2027. The exact scope, duration and values of the new contracts is still to be confirmed, however the current expectation is that each contract will have a minimum term of 3-years, with a maximum spend of £150m (including any extensions). The intention is to compete these contracts via the GCA Dynamic Purchasing System, RM6148, however the pre-market engagement is open to all suppliers. Before any tender activity is launched, the Authority wishes to invite feedback from prospective bidders on the proposed strategy and gather information that will help it to refine its procurement and contracting approach further. Key topics that the Authority wishes to explore include, but are not limited to: 1. Route to market 2. Transition approach 3. Key Performance Indicators & contractual incentives (i.e. Service Credits) 4. Cost drivers 5. The use of innovation and AI to drive efficiency 6. Roles and Capability 7. Tooling and hardware 8. Removing barriers for SMEs 9. Support in the transformation from a Programme SDLC to a Product SDLC, including using experience gained from other clients to help shape and drive the change 10. Support in the transformation from Quality Assurance to Quality Engineering, including using experience gained from other clients to help shape and drive the change This engagement shall start with an in-person event from 10:30 until 13:00 on Monday 27th July at the TechUK office in London; 10 Saint Bride St, London, EC4A 4AD. Each supplier may bring a maximum of 2 delegates to the day, and should confirm who these individuals are no later than 17:00 (BST) on Thursday 23rd July. Suppliers can register their interest for this event by registering an account on the Authority's eSourcing Portal (https://homeoffice.app.jaggaer.com) and navigating to the opportunity titled 'pqq_823 - Pre-Market Engagement for Home Office Quality Assurance & Test Engineering (QAT) Contracts'. Once registered against this opportunity, you should submit a response to the 'Qualification Envelope' with the names and email addresses for the 2 delegates who you plan to attend the event. NOTE: Expressions of interest for this opportunity should NOT be sent via email and must be done as instructed via the eSourcing Portal above. Following the event, a Request for Information questionnaire will be issued to all suppliers who have expressed an interest in the opportunity; attendance at the in-person event is not mandatory for this, but is encouraged to help your understanding.
sig_b3aff275208f654a526c.title: Pre-Market Engagement for Home Office Quality Assurance & Testing (QAT) Contracts

The contracting authority is procuring the supply of server hardware, hypervisor, storage (vSAN), network switches, and the execution of the software update of OpenScape Voice V10 to the current release V11 including all connected applications. The services must be provided by 01.04.2027 at the latest. Necessary measures for taking over the maintenance, e.g. - Migration of existing systems - Familiarisation with system documentation and systems - Onboarding of employees - Setup of remote accesses on the contractor side so that the remote maintenance accesses of the contracting authority can be used - Registration / re-registration of the service partner with the manufacturer must be carried out in full by the contractor prior to service takeover. - The contractor shall provide a migration plan with milestones upon submission of the tender.

The purpose of this contract is to carry out numerical modelling work in support of CSL projects. These interventions will typically cover the following areas: • Mechanical modelling: preliminary design and structural analysis (modal, static, stability analyses, dynamic responses to sinusoidal, random and shock excitations); • Thermomechanical modelling (using finite elements) in order to verify the level of stress and deformation under the influence of temperature; • Model reduction by condensation (Craig-Bampton); • The modelling will be carried out using SAMCEF or NASTRAN software. However, models to be transmitted to CSL clients must be exported in NASTRAN; • Technical interactions (definition of calculations and discussion of results) with CSL engineers will take place at the CSL; for this purpose, the service provider will travel to the CSL with their workstation and their own licence; Mesh and calculation services that do not require interaction with the CSL may be carried out at the service provider's site in order to benefit from more adequate computing resources. sig_b4cb85529a2d918a2c26.description: The purpose of this combined Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 35 and Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) under 2 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 200.204 (henceforth referred to as “BAA”) is to solicit research proposals for submission to the U.S. Army Artificial Intelligence Integration Center (AI2C) for funding consideration. This Broad Agency Announcement (BAA), for the Army Artificial Intelligence Integration Center (AI2C), is issued under the provisions of paragraph 6.102(d)(2) and 35.016 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), which provides for the acquisition of basic, applied, and advanced research and that part of development not related to the development of a specific system or hardware procurement. This will be done through the competitive selection of proposals, and 10 U.S.C. 4001, 10 U.S.C. 4021, and 10 U.S.C. 4022, which provide the authorities for issuing awards under this announcement for basic, applied, and advanced research. The definitions of basic and applied research may be found at 32 CFR 22.105. Proposals submitted in response to this BAA and selected for award are considered to be the result of full and open competition and in full compliance with the provisions of Public Law 98-369, "The Competition in Contracting Act of 1984" and subsequent amendments. The Army Artificial Intelligence Integration Center (AI2C) is seeking artificial intelligence research and development whitepapers and proposals in support of new technologies and translational research-based approaches that support the identification, alignment, and exploitation of basic, applied, and advanced research. AI2C’s foundational research mission spans basic research (budget activity 6.1) and applied research (budget activity 6.2) as defined by 32 CFR 22.105 but may include advanced technology development (budget activity 6.3) and advanced component development and prototypes (budget activity 6.4) when opportunities arise to directly or indirectly help achieve AI2C’s mission. This publication constitutes a BAA for awards as contemplated in FAR 6.102(d)(2) and 35.016 as well as a merit-based, competitive procedure in accordance with the Department of Defense Grant and Agreement Regulations (DoDGARS) at 32 CFR 22.315(a) and the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment Other Transaction Guide version 2.0 dated July 2023.

sig_b520decbe8b7969a9634.description: Enhanced Information Service for Emergency Calls (EISEC) or caller line identification (CLI) enables fire control room operators to confirm the caller's location swiftly. This is a critical first step in the call handling process, since the line could be 'cut', leaving the location unknown. EISEC technology provided by call handling agencies allows the billing address of the phone from which emergency calls are being made to be displayed to the control room operator. This speeds up the information process. This technology can also be used to locate the whereabouts of mobile phone callers, identifying the cell network from which they are calling. Additional information: Provides Location of caller on emergency lines

Within the investment objective "DigiTEL Green Pilot Project - Retrofitting of the 220/110/20 kV Mostiștea substation as a digital substation concept with low environmental impact" – Procurement 1, the following contract objects have been defined: • Object 1 - Sub-object 1.1: Electrical Substation; - Sub-object 1.2: Related Systems (Digital Twin, Augmented Reality, Robotic Assistance/inspection and drones); • Object 5 – The electronic security system (ESS) of the objective and the fire security system (FSS); • Object 6 – The photovoltaic system. The detailed description can be found in the tender documentation. Number of days by which clarifications can be requested before the deadline for the submission of tenders: 22 The contracting entity shall respond clearly and completely to all requests for clarification / additional information in two stages, as follows: - on the 17th calendar day from the publication of the contract notice and - on the 11th calendar day before the time limit for the submission of tenders. The contracting entity shall respond only to requests for clarifications addressed by economic operators by the established time limit. 1.1 Object 1 – Retrofitting of the Mostiștea substation This object consists in turn of two sub-objects and the corresponding Specifications: 1.1.1 Mostiștea electrical substation The 220 kV substation shall be of outdoor type, with air insulation, implemented with conventional equipment, located on the decommissioned surface of the current 220 kV substation. The 110 kV substation shall be of indoor type, equipped with enclosed switchgear panels, with air/technical gas insulation, in three-phase construction. The 20 kV substation shall be located in the building of the current medium voltage substation. In this project, two new, independent auxiliary services units have been provided, namely a direct current (d.c.) unit and an alternating current (a.c.) unit respectively, as follows: • a d.c. auxiliary services unit supplying the d.c. consumers of the 220 kV, 110 kV, 20 kV substation, autotransformers AT1, AT2 and transformer units T1 and T2 110/20 kV; • an a.c. auxiliary services unit supplying the a.c. consumers of the 220 kV, 110 kV and 20 kV substation Within the work "DigiTEL Green Pilot Project - Retrofitting of the 220/110/20 kV Mostiștea substation as a digital substation concept with low environmental impact", the technical condition module will be implemented in accordance with the Smart Grid reference architecture, for asset management at the level of the Mostiștea substation, called "Condition Monitoring System (CMS)". In the telecommunications field, within this project the following shall be performed: • ensuring the technical equipment for data and/or voice transmissions (HW&SW) necessary for: o carrying out the traffic required by the EMS/SCADA System; o remote control of the substation from the CTSI/DET level; o monitoring and parameterisation of protection systems from the level of the SSCPA of the Bucharest Branch and the DEN headquarters; o data-voice transmissions for operation and maintenance needs; o ensuring telecommunication facilities for the control of the substation; o the interzonal oscillation monitoring system (synchrophasors); o ensuring the transmission channels for metering data, local metering and power quality data. o ensuring hardware redundancy for interfaces that receive/transmit data and/or voice, which require this. o creation of telecommunication facilities to ensure the voice and/or data traffic requirements due to the emergence of a new Integrated IT/Information System, provided, at this stage, to be composed, in principle, of the following Systems:  Components/Sub-systems of the Asset Management System in Procurement 1 of the project:  AR, Digital Twin and PIA  BMS (also receives information from SIS - Integrated (Physical) Security)  Integrated (Physical) Security; • provision of technical equipment for cybersecurity (HW&SW); • provision of transmission equipment for teleprotection (HW&SW) Construction and installation works related to the performance of retrofitting works in the 220/110/20 kV Mostiștea substation as a digital substation concept with low environmental impact: The new control block building will be a ground floor + 1 storey construction, designed according to the nZEB concept and as an intelligent building. Within this project, a dedicated building management system (BMS) architecture will be provided at the level of the Bucharest Branch, capable of integrating both the local BMS from the Mostiștea substation and the future BMS systems belonging to the other electrical substations under the management of the Bucharest Branch. The BMS system to be implemented in the Mostiștea substation will have the following integrated: • The control block; • The 110 kV GIS building; • Old medium voltage building; • Relay containers and photovoltaic installation container; • Perimeter lighting in the substation. 1.1.2 Related systems: I. Digital Twin and Augmented Reality – consisting mainly of: • equipment (hardware and/or software), (re)configurations, services, tests/measurements and works in:  The 220/110 kV Mostiștea Substation;  Bucharest Branch;  CNTEE Transelectrica SA Head Office. • integration/interfacing with the telecommunications infrastructure; • integration/interfacing with the systems in the 220/110/20 kV Mostiștea electrical substation from which it retrieves data/information, mainly:  Condition Monitoring System;  BMS; • integration into the Beneficiary's existing and new installations. II.• Substation robotic inspection assistance (Intervention and Assistance Platform - PIA). In the 220/110/20 kV Mostiștea substation, advanced monitoring solutions will be implemented by developing inspection and analysis platforms that include both physical robots, such as drones and hardware robots, and software robots, capable of improving monitoring, maintenance and intervention processes.

1.5 Object 5 – "Electronic Security System (ESS) of the site and Fire Security System (FSS)" The 220/110/20 kV Mostiștea substation shall be provided with the ESS+FSS Integrated Security System. 1.6 Object 6 – Photovoltaic System Within the investment project "DigiTEL Green Pilot Project - Retrofitting the 220/110/20 kV Mostiștea substation as a digital substation concept and with low environmental impact", considering the nZEB building and energy efficiency requirements as well as the transition to GIS technology of the 110 kV substation, on the surface of the current 110 kV substation cleared following the retrofitting, a ground-mounted photovoltaic system shall be implemented, with photovoltaic panels mounted on a metal structure, and with the related equipment mounted in a dedicated metal container. Estimated contract execution duration - 40 months according to the execution schedule in the specifications.
sig_b5285b4fbd447a5b1d37.title: "DigiTEL Green Pilot Project - Retrofitting the 220/110/20 kV Mostiștea substation into a digital substation concept with low environmental impact" – Procurement 1

sig_b62fed6617ef5e4b3bf0.description: Description Essex Record Office (ERO) is seeking to engage with the market to understand available solutions and supplier capabilities that can support the modernisation of its archive management, digital preservation and public access services. ERO is undertaking this Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) exercise to inform future procurement activity and ensure that any proposed solutions align with the organisation's statutory responsibilities, service requirements and long-term digital preservation ambitions. ERO is looking to understand the market's ability to provide solutions that can deliver the following outcomes: • Replacement of the current in-house developed Archive Management System (SEAX), which underpins over 80% of ERO's operations and public-facing services, including income-generating online services. • The archive management system will need to: o facilitate viewing the catalogue on-site at Essex Record Office locations and online o provide free access to digital and digitised collections on-site at Essex Record Office locations o provide online access, outside of ERO locations, to digital and digitised collections via a subscription service o facilitate the creation of user accounts with role dependent security/access levels o provide a paywall to access certain collections o manage the personal data of users of the service, including taking payments from them • Support for statutory archive, records management and civil registration functions. • Secure, scalable and standards-compliant digital preservation capabilities to support the long-term preservation, integrity and accessibility of digital records. We require a solution for preserving digital records with retention periods of 100 years or more, as well as potentially shorter retention periods. The solution must be able to deal with a variety of file formats including proprietary software files and a range of sound and moving image files. • Progression towards National Digital Stewardship Alliance (NDSA) Level 4 digital preservation maturity. Specifically, we require: o For digital records storage: three copies in at least two geographic locations (storage will need to be in the UK or EU) o A means of controlling, auditing, and recording file permissions o A means of recording sufficient metadata about the files using an appropriate metadata standard e.g. METS (Metadata Encoding and Transmission Standard), PREMIS (PREservation Metadata: Implementation Strategies), BagIt (BagIt File Packaging Format) and/or Dublin Core o Periodic integrity checking and disaster simulation, and a means of regularly updating the results of these checks o A means of recording details of people and software that have accessed or taken preservation actions on files. • Improved management and discovery of digital assets through modern digital asset management capabilities. • Enhanced public access, search and discovery through modern online archive and catalogue services. • Improved customer journeys and increased public engagement. • Support for current income generating services and potential for enhanced income generation opportunities. • Integration capabilities with existing and future corporate platforms and digital services. • Modern, intuitive and user-friendly interfaces for both staff and public users. As a minimum, we will need: o The ability to allow members of the public to access suitable digital preservation files o A means of providing redacted access copies of the content where necessary o A means of recording when files have been accessed and by whom o A means of ensuring the content is protected from unauthorised changes and any loss • Scalable architecture capable of supporting current digital holdings of 88.8TB and significant future growth over the coming decades. • Strong governance, audit, compliance and security features to support statutory and regulatory requirements, including the Public Records Act, Freedom of Information legislation and Data Protection requirements. Background Archive Management System It is estimated that over 80% of the work of the ERO is currently managed through an in-house developed tool called SEAX. SEAX was created by Essex County Council as a bespoke system. It was created over 25 years ago in a now archaic programming language. Seax Explorer was written in VB (Visual Basic) and uses forms to create the different screens of its various modules (e.g. Catalogue Manager, Accession Manager, etc.). These forms have been written in a custom language based loosely around XML and are stored within the Seax Explorer database. The online element of the system is known internally as Seax PAM and to the public as Essex Archives Online. This includes our online catalogue and income-generating subscription service and income-generating single-image service. Seax PAM was written using .NET framework and C# and is currently using an old version of .NET framework. We are seeking a modern, sustainable and future-proofed solution for managing our requirements for accessioning, cataloguing, storage locations, document production, reader management and user access (at the ERO and online). The ERO has a staff of around 25 people. Up to 12 users are likely to require login access to the staff side of the AMS, including generic logins for Searchroom staff, document production staff, volunteers, etc. Digital Preservation As of July 2026, the ERO has 88.8TB of digital data. This figure is expected to grow at an estimated rate of 5TB per year. Within the 88.8TB of data, 3.3TB consists of born-digital records; the other 85.5TB being content the ERO has digitised from its manuscript, image, sound and video collections. This data is all currently stored on Microsoft Azure Cloud Storage. Most of the content is listed in basic form on a spreadsheet. Detailed metadata at file level is being added as resources allow. Further documentation about rights is kept in separate filing and on our archive management system (alongside information about our paper and analogue collections). The ERO has a dedicated ingest PC through which we process digital collections as they arrive. We are able to take images of disks using ISO Buster software, transfer files as they are or transfer them to a file format with greater longevity. Transfers can be made using Teracopy software and we can interrogate the files we receive using TNA’s Droid software. The main element of NDSA (National Digital Stewardship Alliance) Digital Preservation Level 1 we are not currently achieving is the requirement to have two complete copies of our digital content in separate locations. Our aim is to progress through the NDSA digital preservation levels to meet NDSA Level 4. Areas of Interest ERO is particularly interested in understanding solutions relating to: • Archive Management Systems (AMS) • Digital Preservation Management Systems (DPMS) • Digital Asset Management Systems (DAMS) • Preservation storage and hosting solutions • Public catalogue and online archive access platforms • Migration services from legacy archive systems • Integration and API capabilities Contract Considerations At this stage, ERO is seeking supplier feedback on: • Appropriate contract lengths and commercial models • Implementation and migration timelines • SaaS, cloud-hosted and hybrid delivery models • Opportunities for phased delivery across AMS, DPMS, DAMS and public access capabilities • Scalability to support long-term digital preservation requirements. The information gathered through this PME will help shape ERO's future procurement strategy, solution design and business case development. Lot 1: .

sig_b6c9b295c79f5a0cdd30.description: The subject of the procurement is the Summa system, which includes the system's functionalities, commissioning, integrations into existing information systems and interfaces, maintenance and support services, and further development of the solution during the contract period. Summary civil claims are processed in the Summa system. Summary civil claims are undisputed matters that the district court decides in written proceedings. These include, for example, rent receivables, consumer credits, telephone and electricity bills, and matters concerning eviction or recovery of possession. Summary application for a summons are currently processed in nine district courts. In the target state, the processing of summary debt collection cases uses a modern and uniform solution that enables the processing of constantly growing application quantities quickly and reliably. The data processed in the target state system are in a structured form, making them easier to search within the system or via system interfaces. The future objective is to increase automation in the processing of debt collection cases. The Summa system and the requirements related to the procurement are described in more detail in the annexes to the invitation to tender. Excluded from the delivery project carried out at the beginning of the procurement are the decommissioning of existing systems and their data migrations. For the avoidance of doubt, it is stated that during the contract period, the Contracting Authority may order data migration work for separately defined assignments.
