sig_b73609a1959d2a08b811.description: Dolwen Residential Care Home is a 32-bedroom facility that was built in the 1960s. It is struggling to meet the complex needs of citizens who require residential care. The purpose of the project is to provide premises that are fit for purpose, modern and accessible, and which have sufficient space for current and future provision. It will use digital technology and Artificial Intelligence. It will be well-located to provide care closer to home and meet the health and care needs of local people, including unmet needs, i.e. provision for the elderly who are mentally frail, and support service delivery within the building itself and in the local community. At present, the following issues need to be addressed at Dolwen home: - Small rooms which limit the service provider's ability to meet the needs of residents; for example, there are rooms that are suitable for hoists, but this is not the case throughout the facility. This restriction limits who can be provided with accommodation, depending on their needs. - None of the rooms are en-suite, and they do not offer sufficient living space or the facilities expected by modern standards. - The service provider is struggling to meet complex needs, which means it is not possible to provide accommodation for patients as they would like. A wide range of factors influences the proposal: - an expected increase in the older population of Denbighshire to 30.9% by 2040; including the fact that current facilities will not be suitable for the needs of residents; improving service provision; bringing services closer to the community; improving current provision for older people and the need to overcome limitations such as access, space and parking, and meeting Denbighshire's challenge and goal to be carbon neutral by 2030. This project, which is led by Denbighshire County Council (DCC) in collaboration with Community Housing, Denbighshire Voluntary Services Council and Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board, is a project to review the potential development of Dolwen Residential Care Home. The project proposes an extension and modernisation work for Dolwen, including: - Residential capacity for the mentally frail elderly, i.e. developing a dementia wing. - Providing an extra care lite model in the older people's housing facility bordering Dolwen, in partnership with Community Housing. - A hub and spoke model of community support on an outreach and in-reach basis in conjunction with Community Housing and Denbighshire Voluntary Services Council. - Upgrading and modernising the current residential facility from 32 to 50 beds. This will include an extension and will enable the current accommodation to be redeveloped to ensure that it meets future complexity needs, e.g. a hoist in every room and en-suite facilities. - Improving current dementia support provisions in the community of Denbigh and the surrounding area. sig_b73c43bfb419c9e44341.description: EUROMOD is the tax-benefit microsimulation model of the European Union (EU), which covers in a consistent manner the tax-benefit systems of all EU Member States. The model allows to study the effects of taxes and social benefits on household incomes and work incentives for the population of each country and for the EU as a whole. EUROMOD is unique in its area as it features great flexibility in the scope of its simulation and ensures cross-country consistency of the modelling approach and comparability of the results. The model is widely used by the Commission services in the European Semester context and other EU policy initiatives. Additionally, the model represents a valuable research infrastructure for the academic community in the area of fiscal policy analysis, with highly cited research conducted using EUROMOD being published in top journals. The contracts are intended to provide the Commission with services that support the development and update of the microsimulation model EUROMOD for 26 EU country-specific modules. The modules are as follows: Lot 1: Support to EUROMOD for Austria Lot 2: Support to EUROMOD for Belgium Lot 3: Support to EUROMOD for Bulgaria Lot 4: Support to EUROMOD for Croatia Lot 5: Support to EUROMOD for Cyprus Lot 6: Support to EUROMOD for Czechia Lot 7: Support to EUROMOD for Denmark Lot 8: Support to EUROMOD for Estonia Lot 9: Support to EUROMOD for Finland Lot 10: Support to EUROMOD for France Lot 11: Support to EUROMOD for Germany Lot 12: Support to EUROMOD for Greece Lot 13: Support to EUROMOD for Hungary Lot 14: Support to EUROMOD for Ireland Lot 15: Support to EUROMOD for Italy Lot 16: Support to EUROMOD for Latvia Lot 17: Support to EUROMOD for Lithuania Lot 18: Support to EUROMOD for Luxembourg Lot 19: Support to EUROMOD for Malta Lot 20: Support to EUROMOD for Netherlands Lot 21: Support to EUROMOD for Poland Lot 22: Support to EUROMOD for Portugal Lot 23: Support to EUROMOD for Romania Lot 24: Support to EUROMOD for Slovenia Lot 25: Support to EUROMOD for Spain Lot 26: Support to EUROMOD for Sweden

sig_b7d7def91dc097edaa1c.description: Procurement of a UCC solution for the State of Hesse The project comprises a modern and comprehensive communications solution that integrates numerous central components. The following expectations are placed on the tendered service: In the area of telephony and voice (formerly HessenVoice), contemporary voice communication is provided that replaces and expands existing systems. In addition, the softphone functionality enables telephony to be used directly via PC or mobile end devices without the need for additional hardware. Webex is currently used as the web conferencing solution (VKS); however, the solution should also support future developments and hybrid working forms in the best possible way. In addition, chat and messaging functions create a secure and efficient platform for text-based team communication. High requirements apply to security and data protection as well as accessibility in order to offer all employees secure and inclusive access to the solution. The operator model defines clear responsibilities and processes for operation, while accompanying training measures support the introduction and foster acceptance. The solution will be fully compatible with the HessenPC and enable secure, high-performance access via the HessenNetz connection. Another component is the provision as a price-per-port Full Managed Service, which impresses with transparent pricing and comprehensive service management. Manufacturer neutrality is respected in order to avoid dependencies and ensure long-term flexibility and openness to competition. The procurement and implementation of the tendered UCC solution takes place with special consideration of the requirements for information security, data protection and interoperability with existing authorities' infrastructures. For use in public administration, compliance with the compendium for internal organisational telecommunication systems with an increased protection requirement (KomTK ) published by the Federal Office for Information Security (BSI) must be ensured. This guideline defines binding security measures - including technical, organisational and infrastructural requirements - for telecommunication systems with an increased protection requirement and serves as a benchmark for the planning, operation and safeguarding of the offered solution. The protection of personal data is a central criterion in the selection and implementation of communication systems. The legal requirements of the General Data Protection Regulation ("GDPR") and the Hesse Data Protection Act ("HDSIG") provide for safeguarding the rights and freedoms of data subjects and consistently implementing data protection principles - such as lawfulness, purpose limitation, data minimisation, accuracy, storage limitation, integrity and confidentiality. While Unified Communications solutions are primarily designed for applications with a normal protection requirement in accordance with the specifications of the Federal Office for Information Security ("BSI") when using cloud components, there are scenarios in which a higher level of security is required. In cases where a higher level of security is required, an on-premise system is frequently used, which is operated entirely within the own IT infrastructure and can thus better meet the requirements for a high or very high protection requirement. By operating in a controlled environment, a higher degree of control over data flows, access protection, encryption as well as emergency and recovery measures can be ensured. Unified Communications and Collaboration (UCC) solutions represent a central component of modern IT infrastructures and serve the integrated networking of a wide variety of communication and collaboration services. In order to meet the operational requirements for reliability, security, scalability and interoperability, specific technical prerequisites are indispensable. These requirements form the basis for the selection, implementation and operation of a high-performance UCC solution that ensures efficient and uninterrupted cooperation within the organisation. In order to bring about rapid project success, close cooperation between the contractor and the contracting authority is necessary. The contractor MUST closely coordinate with internal and external stakeholders on the part of the contracting authority as part of the implementation in order to take account of necessary and inevitable interactions with other systems of the contracting authority (e.g. firewall, network, etc.) as early as possible in the implementation of the project and to implement necessary adjustments and interventions on these systems as smoothly and time-critically as possible. The service contents presented in this specification MUST be provided by the contractor for the contractually defined period in full and with ultimate responsibility for the outcome, flexibly according to the respective needs of the contracting authority in the form of a "Managed Service". Within the scope of this tender, special emphasis is placed on the accessibility of the Unified Communications and Collaboration (UCC) solution to be supplied. Accessibility means that the solution can be used unrestrictedly and equally by all users, regardless of individual impairments or restrictions. This includes in particular people with visual, hearing, motor or cognitive impairments. The detailed service requirements can be found in the respective chapters of the service specification (Chapters 1 - 7).
sig_b7d7def91dc097edaa1c.title: Procurement of a UCC solution for the State of Hesse

sig_b7e29810d5e4fbc721d9.description: Na Gaeil Óga CLG organises more than 1,000 Irish language based events each year for participants aged 3 years and upwards. These include sports training, games, workshops, social and cultural events, Irish classes and parent and toddler activities. The club has 500 active members. At present, the club rents various facilities such as grass-based pitches, all-weather pitches, halls, gyms, ball walls and meeting rooms in Lucan and the surrounding areas to host its activities. The club’s members feel that a centrally located facility, managed by the club, would provide many advantages in terms of the development of both the club and the Irish language in the area. The club intends to engage a consultant to prepare a Strategic Assessment and Preliminary Business Case in accordance with the Infrastructure Guidelines issued by the Department of Public Expenditure, National Development Plan Delivery and Reform and as further detailed in the tender documents to support capital funding applications to various Government departments into the future. The club will be applying to An Roinn Forbartha Tuaite agus Pobail agus Gaeltachta for funding to undertake the Strategic Assessment and Preliminary Business Case.

sig_b88b90a90c1e247f6069.description: The Ogden Air Logistics Complex (OO-ALC) at Hill Air Force Base, Utah, intends to issue a solicitation to provide comprehensive management and supply of aircraft coatings and sealants. This effort aims to ensure uninterrupted aircraft maintenance operations through robust inventory management, timely delivery, and technical support. This effort will include frequent ordering and quick delivery on specified items. The selected contractor will be responsible for continuous deliveries and support of Coatings and Sealants, including: 1. Order Fulfillment and Material Handling: Sourcing, storing, and delivering all required coatings and sealants (see attached list). This includes meeting a strict four (4) hour delivery timeline for urgent requirements and handling specialized materials, such as Premixed Frozen Material (PFM) requiring transit at -80F. The contractor must maintain a minimum of 85% shelf life for all products upon delivery. The contractor will also be responsible for managing shelf-life and ensuring proper storage and handling of the products prior to delivery. 2. FMS-3600 Coating Management: For this specialized product, implementing a lock and key ITAR-compliant storage system and maintaining rigorous chain of custody for the material. 3. Technical Assistance: Providing technical assistance that includes rapid response (within one business day) to material failures, on-site technical support during monthly visits, product change support, and quality audit reporting. 4. Online Ordering System: Furnishing a secure, web-based ordering and tracking system with real-time visibility of lead times and minimum stock levels (MSLS). 5. Ramp-Up Plan: Executing a ramp-up plan to achieve full performance readiness within eight (8) months of contract award. The anticipated contract will be a Firm Fixed Priced (FFP) IDIQ to include an 8-month ramp up period, a 5-year ordering period, and a 6-month allowance for remaining deliveries on the back end. Total period of performance is anticipated to be 6 years and 2 months. This is a total small business set-aside. The Government anticipates awarding a single contract. All interested small businesses are encouraged to respond. The official solicitation will be posted on SAM .gov. The Government intends to award a single contract resulting from the upcoming solicitation to the responsible offeror whose proposal represents the best value to the Government. This effort requires Contractors to be CMMC level 2 self-certified, therefore if you are not currently level 2 certified and are interested in this requirement you will need to begin the process to become level 2 certified immediately. The solicitation draft documents are attached. Dates on the solicitation are subject to change based on the actual award date. Please review and submit any questions or suggestions to the point of contacts on this 15-day synopsis. The anticipated solicitation number is FA8224-26-R-0010 (subject to change). The anticipated solicitation release date is October 2, 2026 (subject to change).

sig_b8df9178fb2e1adf6314.description: UHS is seeking to engage with interested parties to discuss and refine an opportunity to become a strategic endoscopy partner to the Trust. UHS provides a regional endoscopy service to a population of 3m+, offering a comprehensive range of diagnostic and therapeutic interventions. Following a fire earlier this year, UHS has reviewed its long-term endoscopy requirements and is considering a new purpose-built regional diagnostic endoscopy centre situated close to the main hospital. UHS has existing endoscopy equipment to the value of approximately £8-10m. This will need to be refreshed throughout this contract. UHS has an indicative budget of £20-25m for the design and construction of the new centre. This will be designed to meet current and projected future endoscopy and motility needs, 'a one-stop-shop' and be an important centre to both trial new technology and techniques and provide training for the next generation of the endoscopy workforce. This opportunity is to explore and discuss how a partnership approach may drive better outcomes for patients, for innovation, for UHS clinicians, and for the partner[S(1.1][L(1.2]. This opportunity may include, but not necessarily be limited to: 1: Provision of endoscopy equipment to a new offsite location, both for the use of clinicians undertaking NHS clinical activity, and for use as a test bed for innovation and new technique development, and for use within a training environment. 2: Regional Training Centre: The physical co-location of experienced UHS staff, clinicians, data, patients with an industry partner seeking to promote best practice and create future workforce. 3: Joint Innovation Deal & Test Bed: The provision of a live, data-rich NHS environment to validate new technology, and techniques, for example artificial intelligence (AI) diagnostic tools and ergonomic designs and potentially the exploitation of emerging shared Intellectual Property. This would also include SME and VCSE participation for research and innovation. 4: Commercial Sponsorship Opportunity with Associated Rights and Benefits: In addition to the core procurement opportunities above, there is potential to explore a complementary commercial sponsorship arrangement, which may include the provision of value-in-kind goods and/or services that support contract delivery. This strategic partnership approach would identify and agree a range of associated rights and benefits for suppliers who also become sponsors. These may include appropriate sponsor recognition, opportunities for collaboration and innovation, shared learning, thought leadership engagement, and other mutually agreed activities that support the objectives of all parties. UHS, with support from the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC), is trialling the integration of commercial sponsorship into this procurement opportunity to explore how strategic partnerships can deliver additional value while supporting the successful delivery of contract outcomes. Whilst this notice is not intended to create a commitment to a contract, it is running alongside a live funded NHS capital project to develop designs and take forward the concept of a regional endoscopy centre. This hybrid procurement and sponsorship model is being piloted by the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) and UHS, offering potential suppliers a unique opportunity to play an active role in delivering a best-in-class new facility for patients: supporting improved care, championing innovation and delivering lasting benefits for all parties. To ensure fair and open competition in any future procurement, the developing design and specification will remain supplier-neutral and will not be tailored to any specific manufacturer, supplier or solution.
sig_b8df9178fb2e1adf6314.title: Co-Developing the 'Digestive Disease Centre' at University Hospital Southampton, Hybrid Procurement and Sponsorship Opportunity

sig_b9e44041454269a4f2c0.description: Digipolis is looking, for the City of Antwerp among others, for a partner responsible for the supply, installation and maintenance of: • Sensors and reading out the current fill level of small-volume waste systems such as paper bins and other (waste) systems; • Software to monitor the current fill level of (waste) systems, predict the fill-level evolution based on historical measurement data and then plan the complete and most optimal route for collection vehicles to carry out emptying. In doing so, the available vehicles must be deployed optimally in the field depending on the required capacity for emptyings. This software is used for both existing, already installed sensors and sensors to be installed in the future. It is not the intention to replace all existing sensors. The software must also be able to include unique, self-chosen collection points, e.g. for collecting illegal dumping, in the route calculation. The purpose of this contract is to achieve optimal emptying taking into account personnel, working time, vehicles, weight, volume, consumption, CO2 emissions, costs and traffic situations. The contract is divided into two lots: • Lot 1: framework agreement for the supply, installation and maintenance of sensors for above-ground waste systems and paper bins including real-time API with sensor data. • Lot 2: framework agreement for offering a software solution as described above. • Lot 1: framework agreement for the supply, installation and maintenance of sensors for above-ground waste systems and paper bins including real-time API with sensor data.; • Lot 2: framework agreement for offering a software solution as described above.

sig_baf88bfdde099b508258.description: The Bundesbank manages four staff canteens under its own management. The management of a further eight Bundesbank canteens is carried out by external caterers under contract management. For the canteens under its own management, the Bundesbank uses an inventory management system and a checkout/payment system on its own infrastructure (cash or direct debit for internal employees; cash for external employees and guests). The checkout/payment system is integrated into the Bundesbank's SAP landscape. Orders to suppliers are placed by PDF/email; a B2B connection is not available. In daily operations, many steps are currently carried out manually or twice due to a lack of integrations. The same checkout/payment system is used in the contract-managed canteens (including integration into SAP), but inventory management is carried out independently by the caterers outside the Bundesbank's IT landscape. The inventory management system and checkout/payment system are outdated, meaning that the Bundesbank has initiated a project to replace these systems with a SaaS solution. With this new SaaS solution, which is then to be introduced in the following one to two years, modern payment methods (cards, mobile end devices, digital euro) are to be introduced alongside cash and direct debit. In addition, the solution is to be B2B-capable in order to enable a B2B connection of suppliers. Further focus is placed on automation and digitalisation in order to significantly reduce manual effort, e.g. during stocktaking, and the associated sources of error. In the course of this strategic alignment, Deutsche Bundesbank is initiating a structured market exploration. The aim of this measure is to systematically determine the performance and suitability of the SaaS-based gastro-system platforms available on the market (inventory management with checkout and payment system). In particular, it is to be examined to what extent the existing service portfolios of the providers meet the technical, legal, organisational and security requirements of Deutsche Bundesbank. A key focus is inter alia on: - Support for modern payment methods (cash, direct debit, cards, mobile end devices, digital euro) - B2B capability including connection of suppliers - Integration capability into the Bundesbank's SAP landscape - Functions for automation and digitalisation (e.g. for stocktaking) - Operation as SaaS in a BSI C5-certified cloud - Use both in canteens under own management and contract management - German-language project management, support and documentation This market exploration also serves to involve the market at an early stage in a potentially upcoming EU-wide procurement procedure by Deutsche Bundesbank for the procurement of the described services and forms, amongst other things, a basis for decision-making for its technical design. This market exploration is not a procurement procedure directed at the award of a public contract and constitutes neither an offer nor an invitation to conclude a contract. The execution of a procurement procedure, including with a different service scope, remains reserved. Participation in this market exploration has no consequences for the participating company (neither preference nor disadvantage) in the context of a potential future procurement process. Participants in this market exploration have no entitlement to the acquisition of knowledge from the results of the market exploration. Further details on Deutsche Bundesbank's requirements for the SaaS solution described above are available exclusively upon request to the stored e-mail address: Projekt-GastroSys@bundesbank.de
sig_baf88bfdde099b508258.title: Market exploration: GastroSys - SaaS solution for gastronomy systems of Deutsche Bundesbank

The subject of the contract is to ensure access to data from electronic information resources (hereinafter also referred to as "EIR"), which serve as a source of information for the needs of conducting scientific research and the development of science within the Slovak Republic. The subject of the contract is to ensure access to data from bibliographic and bibliometric electronic information resources for a period of 48 months, which serve as a source of information for the needs of conducting scientific research and the development of science within the Slovak Republic, as well as for the needs of recording publication activity and evaluating science. Society-wide order As part of ensuring science and research and responding to the needs of securing scientific and technical tasks in all science and research institutions in Slovakia, as well as in connection with the provisions of Decree of the Ministry of Education, Research, Development and Youth of the Slovak Republic No. 397/2020 Coll. of 5. December 2020 on the central register of publication activity records and the central register of artistic activity records, the electronic information resource Web of Science "or equivalent" must meet the requirements demonstrating the suitability of the database as a specific source of information with a defined structure and content for the evaluation of science and research and the registration of publication activity of higher education institutions in the Slovak Republic. The contracting authority also allows for an equivalent solution to the Web of Science databases that meets all the parameters listed below. 3. Specification of the subject of the contract – minimum scope: The bibliometric citation database is to be a multidisciplinary database that provides an exceptionally broad view of published scientific works, and thus of science and research on a global scale. The bibliographic and bibliometric database must offer tools for sorting, refining and rapid identification of results, with a focus on the results of work in the fields of science, technology, medicine, social and human sciences and the arts. These are the following database titles: Web of Science Core Collection or equivalent: A bibliographic database serving as a primary source for searching for renowned scientific information and evaluating scientific publication activity. In terms of content, it must cover journal titles, books and conference proceedings from at least 200 subject categories, from natural, technical, medical sciences to arts and humanities for tens of thousands of peer-reviewed scientific journals (including open access journals and Early Accessed documents, i.e. a version made available before it is published by the publisher). The database must further contain conference proceedings and book data. The database must allow for the establishment of benchmarks for evaluating science worldwide, which serve to evaluate and compare the results of scientific publication activity based on transparent and globally accepted criteria. The database must allow for citation tracking, which shows how often and by whom each publication has been cited (among others, an extensive citation network of scientific publications and cited references in the Web of Science Core Collection). The Web of Science Core Collection must contain at least: • Science Citation Index Expanded (SCIE) or equivalent, • Social Sciences Citation Index (SSCI) or equivalent, • Arts & Humanities Citation Index (AHCI) or equivalent, • Emerging Sources Citation Index (ESCI) or equivalent, • Conference Proceedings Citation Index or equivalent, • Book Citation Index or equivalent....... A detailed description of the subject of the contract is defined in the tender documents; The subject of the contract is to ensure access to data from an electronic information resource – a database, for a period of 48 months, which serves as a source of information for the needs of conducting scientific research and the development of science within the Slovak Republic. 3. Specification of the subject of the contract – minimum scope: The ProQuest Central Premium Package "or equivalent" database must have multidisciplinary content across all major subject areas of academic research and teaching while also including subject-specialised content at least to an extent comparable to a solution that integrates 8 specialised disciplinary collections / solutions in a single search environment. We require that the ProQuest Central Premium Package "or equivalent" database provides access to at least 8 collections composed of databases from all scientific fields including economic sciences, healthcare and medicine, social sciences, arts and humanities, education, natural sciences and technology, agricultural sciences, religion, philosophy, linguistics and literature. The collection must contain full texts from at least 12 000 scientific journals, at least 2 000 economic and professional journals. The electronic information resource must provide access to at least 1 500 newspaper and journal titles. It must also include dissertations and theses, case studies, market and economic reports, pre-print versions of working papers, video recordings, all on a user-friendly platform with simple and intuitive operation and with artificial intelligence support. Required basic quantitative indicators: • at least 35 000 titles, of which at least 20 000 with full texts. • on the Ebook Central platform or "equivalent" at least 240 000 e-books with full text. • at least 75 % of titles in the English language, international content in other national languages including, for example, Spanish, French, German, Portuguese and others. According to individual document types: • scientific and professional periodicals (including peer-reviewed), • newspapers and current news, • economic analyses at the industry and state level and company profiles, • research reports and conference proceedings, • dissertations and theses, • electronic books, • case studies for economic (and applied natural) sciences, • multimedia content (video recordings), • bibliographic and abstract databases............................. A detailed description of the subject of the contract is located in the tender documents;

The subject of the contract is to ensure continuous online access to a scientific electronic information resource of the CAS SciFinder Discovery Platform type or an equivalent solution for authorised users of the contracting authority and institutions designated by it for a period of 48 months. The information resource must provide an integrated web environment for searching and professional work with scientific literature, patents, chemical substances, chemical reactions, analytical methods, formulations, regulatory data and supplier information in the fields of chemistry, pharmacy, biochemistry, biomedicine, materials science and related disciplines. 3. Minimum functional requirements The information resource must enable in particular: a) searching in professional literature, patents, chemical substances, reactions and related scientific data by keywords, author, organisation, patent, chemical name, molecular formula, chemical structure, substructure, structure similarity, CAS RN registration number or equivalent identifier, b) support for natural language searching, relevance ranking of results, combined text and structure searching, filtering, sorting, saving, exporting results and creating alerts, c) searching, comparing and evaluating chemical reactions including experimental procedures, reaction conditions, yields, catalysts, solvents, atom mapping and linking to related substances and publications, d) retrosynthetic planning and design of synthetic pathways including comparing alternative procedures, taking into account the availability of starting materials, yields, costs and available patent information, e) searching and comparing analytical methods, experimental protocols or bioanalytical procedures, f) working with formulations, components, commercially available products, supplier and regulatory information, g) working with citation and reference links between documents, substances, reactions and patents............. A detailed description of the subject of the contract is defined in the tender documents

sig_bc36d4f46e434011d441.description: It is the ambition of the Welsh Government to develop a thriving and confident agriculture sector in Wales built around innovation and growth, to rise to the challenges we face and make most of the opportunities available. In July 2025 the Welsh Government published its Sustainable Farming Scheme designed to ensure Welsh Government support for agriculture in Wales delivers against the four Sustainable Land Management objectives of the Agriculture (Wales) Act: - Produce food and other goods in a sustainable manner - Mitigate and adapt to climate change - Maintain and enhance the resilience of ecosystems and the benefits they provide - Conserve and enhance the countryside and cultural resources, promote public access to and engagement with them, and to sustain the Welsh language and promote and facilitate its use. Innovation will play a key role in delivering this scheme. In 2023, the Welsh Government published an Innovation Strategy for Wales. Innovation in food and Agri-Food Tech was seen as a key part of Wales’s future economic development. In late 2023, the Welsh Government published an Agri-tech action plan for Wales. The development and adoption of Agri-Tech and Precision Agri-Tech is a strategic area of growth for the Welsh economy and one the Welsh Government deems requiring of focussed attention and a road map for development. The action plan has four priorities: 1. Accelerate Home Grown Welsh Agri-tech Capabilities. 2. Drive on-farm adoption to achieve productivity and efficiencies (incl. Environmental) gains ‘more for less’. 3. Deliver environmental benefits and help transition to Net Zero. 4. Support educational and skills development to equip future and existing agricultural professionals to exploit Agri-tech to its fullest. SCOPE: Cattle mortality data may provide valuable information on animal health, disease emergence and herd management. However, there are opportunities to make better use of mortality data alongside wider animal health surveillance information to generate timely intelligence that supports veterinary decision-making, farmer engagement and evidence-based policy. Improving the collection, access, interpretation and communication of mortality intelligence could enable earlier identification of disease risks, encourage preventative herd health management and support the delivery of the Animal health and welfare framework | GOV.WALES for Wales, while contributing to the objectives of the Sustainable Farming Scheme. We are therefore seeking innovative technologies, digital tools, data-driven approaches or other novel solutions that improve the collection, integration, analysis and application of cattle mortality intelligence to support proactive animal health management. Lot 1: . None

sig_bc517cb3a5e61dfdbab5.description: The UK Government's Partnering for Accelerated Climate Transitions (UK PACT) programme is inviting proposals from qualified suppliers or consortia to deliver technical assistance to the government of Bangladesh. Bangladesh is establishing the foundations for participation in high-integrity carbon markets, including Article 6, CORSIA and voluntary carbon markets. While progress has been made through the establishment of a carbon market framework and supporting governance arrangements, further support is needed to operationalise these systems across government, strengthen institutional coordination, and enable Bangladesh to use carbon markets to support delivery of its NDC 3.0 unconditional mitigation targets. The assignment will provide targeted technical assistance and capacity building to strengthen Bangladesh's carbon market governance, authorisation processes, MRV, reporting and institutional readiness. Working with relevant government agencies, including MoEFCC, DoE, the Power Division, Ministry of Finance and other line ministries, the project will support practical implementation of carbon market rules, CORSIA readiness, UNFCCC reporting requirements, and inclusive, high-integrity market participation. Key outputs are expected to include governance and coordination tools, an authorisation and safeguards toolkit, CORSIA readiness and reporting support, a structured government capacity-building programme, and sector readiness briefs identifying future carbon market investment opportunities. The project aims to strengthen Bangladesh's ability to participate in high-integrity carbon markets, unlock climate finance, improve institutional capability, and support implementation of national climate targets. Interested suppliers are invited to review the documentation provided in this notice, and submit their applications to: targetedfund@ukpact.co.uk
sig_bc517cb3a5e61dfdbab5.title: Bangladesh Carbon Market Governance & Readiness Sprint

sig_bcc2350d3e85d43e278e.description: Negotiated procedure without prior call for competition. The delivery can only be carried out by a specific economic operator for the following reasons: absence of competition for technical reasons. Explanation: The award of the procurement of passenger counting sensors and the necessary adjustments to the MOBILEguide software can only be carried out by INIT GmbH, as there is no competition for technical reasons in accordance with § 13 paragraph 2 no. 3 b) SektVO. The defined requirements in their extensive abundance and combination cannot be met by any other potential tenderers. In this case, only INIT GmbH is able to fulfil the listed requirements. The on-board computers used on Rheinbahn vehicles originate from the company INIT GmbH. Only the company INIT GmbH possesses the necessary technical knowledge to carry out any system additions to the on-board computer software in order to be able to connect these to the central component of the ITCS of the Rheinbahn AG. In the absence of generally binding standardisation, the software of the central component of an ITCS and the software of the on-board computers used on vehicles in public transport only possess the same processes if they are procured from the same system manufacturer. The processes are manufacturer-specific standards and as such are subject to trade secrets; they are therefore not generally and freely available. In this regard, the company INIT GmbH possesses a unique selling point due to the existing on-board computers at Rheinbahn, which must be included. In the absence of generally binding standardisation, a bidirectional interface between the central ITCS and the on-board computers used on the vehicles as a mobile component of an ITCS is only fully functional if the participating interface partners are procured from the same system manufacturer. The interface is a manufacturer-specific standard and as such is subject to trade secrets; it is therefore not generally and freely available. In this regard, the company INIT GmbH possesses a unique selling point due to the existing on-board computers at Rheinbahn, which must be included. As a result of the examination for the procurement of the central components of the ITCS, it must be determined that the company INIT GmbH possesses a unique selling point regarding mandatory requirements to be fulfilled for the services to be procured. Consequently, a public call for competition would be misleading and the associated effort would be temporally and economically inappropriate for all market participants. The procurement law limits of the public contracting authority's freedom to define the scope of services are adhered to, provided that the definition is objectively justified by the subject matter of the contract, the contracting authority has provided comprehensible objective, contract-related and actually existing reasons for this, and the definition does not discriminate against other economic operators. An artificial and therefore impermissible restriction of competition does not exist. The date of the conclusion of the contract with INIT GmbH cannot be entered, as this day is only possible 10 calendar days after the publication of this notice. The procurement office cannot determine exactly at the time of entry when the period of 10 calendar days begins, as the publication is carried out by the Official Journal and generally takes several days that cannot be precisely determined. The procurement office therefore points out that the conclusion of the contract between the Rheinbahn AG and INIT GmbH will take place 10 days after the publication of this notice. Precise information on the deadlines for lodging appeals: §160 para. 3 GWB reads: The application is inadmissible insofar as 1. the applicant has identified the asserted infringement of procurement regulations before submitting the review application and has not complained about it to the contracting authority within a period of ten calendar days; the expiry of the period according to § 134 paragraph 2 remains unaffected, 2. infringements of procurement regulations that are recognisable from the notice are not complained about to the contracting authority by the expiry of the deadline for application or submission of tenders specified in the notice, 3. infringements of procurement regulations that only become recognisable in the procurement documents are not complained about to the contracting authority by the expiry of the deadline for application or submission of tenders, 4. more than 15 calendar days have passed since receipt of the notification from the contracting authority that it does not intend to remedy a complaint. Sentence 1 does not apply to an application for a declaration of the ineffectiveness of the contract according to § 135 paragraph 1 number 2. § 134 paragraph 1 sentence 2 remains unaffected. Despite a grown awareness of the consequences of plastic pollution for the marine environment, there is a persistent threat from ALDFG which is newly introduced into the marine environment or has in some cases already been located there for decades. The aim of UNSEA is therefore to systematically prevent the further input of ALDFG into the North and Baltic Seas, to reduce the negative ecological and socio-economic impacts and to identify and salvage legacy waste, particularly in ecologically sensitive areas. Both commercial, sideline and recreational fishing in the North and Baltic Seas are to be addressed. Aquaculture and mariculture as well as inland fisheries are excluded from the project scope. Existing requirements and agreements of relevant national and international legal provisions are currently still fragmented, without financial backing and are partly up for debate for various reasons. UNSEA is therefore intended to bring together the various sub-aspects in a coherent framework for action, focusing on the implementation of cost-efficient and operational measures. In doing so, it is necessary to rethink the handling of waste fishing gear from the fishing industry in a new and holistic way, to anchor circular economy principles in the management of fishing gear and thereby also address specific findings such as dolly ropes (scuff protection threads on bottom trawls) and net sections from repair work that are frequently found in the marine environment. The project is intended to provide the necessary seed funding over its term and in parallel create long-term structures with clear responsibilities for perpetuation by the federal and state governments. For the first time, a cross-sectoral mechanism is to be established and implemented, which also includes the exchange of knowledge and information. The project can build on existing legal framework conditions, recommendations from research and politics, preliminary work within the framework of measure and action plans and voluntary industry initiatives. In particular, the 2016 established Round Table on Marine Litter (RTM, www.muell-im-meer.de), which is coordinated by the Umweltbundesamt and the State of Lower Saxony, has already carried out comprehensive conceptual preliminary work that can be used as a basis for work for UNSEA. Through this, insights into the dimension of the problem were gained and suitable methods as well as existing and missing elements in the chain from search to the most environmentally sound recycling possible of ALDFG were identified. Furthermore, the results and recommendations of two pilot projects for the implementation of the recovery of lost fishing gear in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania (MV) and Schleswig-Holstein (SH) are to be taken into account. While the project in MV has already been completed (https://www.wwf.de/fileadmin/fm-wwf/Publikationen-PDF/Deutschland/WWF-Abschlussbericht-Landesprojekt-Verlorene-Fischereigeraete.pdf), the publication of the final report of the SH project is expected for August 2026 with planned follow-up activities for the mapping and recovery of fishing gear waste. The work under UNSEA is to be closely coordinated with these activities to avoid duplication of work. sig_beb84f55de3cf7b6e7a1.description: The City of Helsinki Employment Services Public Utility provides employment services to, among others, foreign-language clients who have no skills in Finnish or Swedish or whose skills are weak. Therefore, efficient interpretation solutions are required to support communication between the client and the guiding employee, ensuring that foreign-language clients receive the full benefit of the employment services. The City has existing interpretation service agreements in place for on-site and remote interpretation assisted by an interpreter. Consequently, the City of Helsinki Employment Services Public Utility is procuring an AI-assisted interpretation service. The interpretation service must be capable of providing interpretation in multiple languages. The service must utilise artificial intelligence to provide real-time interpretation. The interpretation service must be confidential and privacy-protecting (the City of Helsinki data protection requirements must be met and will be delivered separately later). The service must be easy to use for both clients and service providers, and the user interface can be used on various devices (computer, smartphone, tablet, etc.). The subject of the procurement is described in more detail in appendices 1 Service Description of the Subject of Procurement and 2 Requirement List.
sig_beb84f55de3cf7b6e7a1.title: AI-assisted interpretation service for foreign-language employment service clients

sig_bf044cea98ad0eddb9c3.description: The subject of the procurement is the provision of maintenance and support services for telecommunications network devices and related network services (hereinafter the "Service"). The procurement covers comprehensive maintenance, monitoring, support and operational services for VR's telecommunications network environment, including network devices located in datacentres, offices, rolling stock (trains and buses) and other operational locations. The Service also includes the maintenance of certain related network services required for the operation of the telecommunications environment. The Service includes, but is not limited to, the following: - Service transition and implementation; - 24/7 monitoring of the telecommunications network environment; - Incident management and fault resolution; - Replacement of failed network devices in accordance with the agreed service levels; - Device configuration changes and other agreed maintenance activities; - Network monitoring, preventive maintenance and operational support; - Service management and designated service management personnel; - Maintenance of network documentation; - Reporting, including service level, capacity and operational reporting; - Integration with VR's agreed service management and ticketing solutions; - Other maintenance, support and expert services related to the telecommunications network environment, ordered separately where required. The procurement concerns maintenance and support services only. Ownership of the telecommunications network devices, software licences and the overall network architecture shall remain with VR. VR is responsible for the procurement of network devices and strategic network architecture, while the selected Supplier shall provide the Services in accordance with the agreed contractual responsibilities. The Service is intended to support VR Group's operations in Finland, Sweden, Denmark and Latvia. The Service may also be extended to other VR Group companies or countries during the contract period. A more detailed preliminary description of the procurement is set out in Annex 1 – Preliminary Description of the Procurement. The subject of the procurement described herein is preliminary and may be further specified, clarified and supplemented during the negotiated procurement procedure. The final scope of the procurement, the detailed requirements and the contractual terms will be set out in the Final Invitation to Tender and its annexes.

sig_bf2e9107a30c194ce5eb.description: The purpose of the Invitation to Tender is to select one (1) economic operator (hereafter “Contractor”) for the component acquisition, delivery, assembly, hardware and software installation and maintenance of an AI-ready EuroHPC machine (“Supercomputer”) to establish an associated “AI Factory” and that will be owned by the EuroHPC JU. The EuroHPC JU will conclude one contract with the successful tenderer in order to acquire, deliver, install and maintain the High-End Supercomputer hosted by the respective Hosting Entity. Therefore, the prospective Contractors should have proven experience of acquiring, delivering, installing and maintaining Supercomputers in similar environments as the ones required in this procurement procedure. The solutions to be procured are expected to outperform existing solutions regarding several of the following aspects: • Performance/TCO; • Programmability and usability; • Versatility; • System stability; • Power and energy efficiency; • Computing density. A high-performance GPU-accelerated computing partition to be delivered as part of the Discoverer ++ GPU & CPU Partition. The solution is designed to support AI workloads, large-scale simulations, and data-intensive research across a wide spectrum of scientific and industrial domains. LOT 1 should contain two different GPU compute infrastructure with fast interconnect and one AI optimized storage with direct GPU access feature.; The cluster must offer at least two AI accelerator chips based on -wafer scale, integrating hundreds of thousands of cores into a single silicon wafer, designed for large-scale deep learning workloads. The Specialized AI Servers must assume the delivery and installation of homogeneous cluster with height density at least 32 AI accelerators or more with very high speed (based on the same hardware and software configuration) compute nodes (servers). This tender specification defines the requirements for procuring FPGA AI-accelerated systems for the BRAIN++ AI Factory at Sofia Tech Park. Each server unit must be configured to host and efficiently operate 4x FPGA accelerator cards, designed for high-performance computing workloads with emphasis on memory-intensive applications.; A high availability N+1 UPS solution with 2N(N+1) for the most critical loads.

sig_bf3ae200ba572e488c45.description: Within the GCA Energy Category, we operate a managed service on behalf of the public sector, aggregating their energy demand and purchasing on the wholesale market under a number of risk strategies. In order to support these activities, we require a cloud-based energy portfolio management solution, suitable for managing the GCA Energy portfolio frameworks, which includes; c.1,200 customers, c.108,000 power / gas meters, c. 80,000 sites There is currently no system in place to meet these requirements. This requirement will run on a 3 month trial period. If after the trial period concludes successfully, the supplier will be awarded the subsequent contract term and value. The value included in this notice is for the trial period only. Any subsequent contract term is subject to further budgetary approval which, will be confirmed at the future procurement stage. The proposed system must be able to accurately record the customer portfolio data for both gas and power, including site and meter information and assigned trading strategy. Each of the meters is assigned to a customer and a site. Each meter is attached to current and future Gas / Power buying strategies with varying buying lengths. The system must support the ability for nominated energy suppliers to access the meter data for their assigned customers. We also require the ability for customers to complete a self-serve audit of their portfolio and buying strategy, including the ability to request changes and additions to their portfolio. The system should have the The ability to extract data via API (REST) to integrate with the rest of our data infrastructure The successful supplier will be expected to provide ongoing management maintenance of the solution throughout the duration of the contract to ensure its effective running and optimisation. The dates included in this notice are indicative and subject to change. GCA intend to run this procurement opportunity via commercial agreement Demand Management & Renewables DPS RM6313. Should you intend to bid, you will need to onboard onto the agreement. Please follow the below link and click "access as a supplier": https://supplierregistration.cabinetoffice.gov.uk/dps/RM6313?nav=0

sig_bf5e743f13ae39e7a39c.description: IKOMM AS invites tenderers, on behalf of Enebakk municipality, to a market survey for the procurement of a new map and management system for water and sewage. Enebakk municipality shall procure a new map and management system for water and sewage in autumn 2026 in the municipality. The municipality needs a future orientated, comprehensive and user-friendly system for managing the water and sewage network. The system shall support both administrative and operative activities and facilitate efficient interaction between employees in offices and personnel in the field. The system must be available via modern web technology and function on different devices (PCs, tablets and mobile), so that registration, updating and posting can be carried out where the work actually takes place. The system shall support efficient registration and management of the pipeline network, manholes and the accompanying technical installations, including the use of GNSS/GPS equipment for precise surveying. The system shall meet strict requirements for information security and stand-by, reduce operational and maintenance costs and ensure that the municipality meets the current environmental and reporting requirements. >: We would like to carry out a market survey (RFI) in order to gain insight into relevant systems, technology and suppliers. Furthermore, we would like to invite up to 3 tenderers to public dialogue meetings to take a closer look at the options that can offer to ensure a good future orientated procurement. Other municipalities in the region will also be invited to participate in this market survey in order to possibly participate in a future competition. > > > > The dialogue meetings are planned to be held in early April as physical meetings in IKOMM ́s premises in Vinterbro, but with an option for participation in Teams. Relevant tenderers will be selected based on relevance, experience and references from equivalent and comparable municipal systems. The objective of the market survey is to: * Gain insight into what systems and suppliers are available in the market * Examine how the tenderers handle technical requirements, integration, security and stand-by * Using the knowledge to improve the requirement specifications and choice of procurement strategy. > This market dialogue will be carried out as a voluntary and non-binding request for information (Request for Information – RFI), cf. FOA § 9-3 and § 12-2, which allow contracting authorities to obtain information about the market before any competition. > > This is not part of a competition and does not involve any obligations for Enebakk municipality or for the tenderers who choose to provide answers. > > Tenderers who participate in the market dialogue will not be given any kind of competition, and participation (or lack of participation) will not lead to exclusion from a later competition. Any future procurements will be implemented in accordance with public procurement regulations, and all tenderers will be able to compete on equal terms. > We therefore invite interested suppliers to provide written input and possibly participate in dialogue meetings. Participation is voluntary and the market dialogue is not binding for the municipality or suppliers. Good if suppliers can give feedback on the possibility of participation in the dialogue meetings that are planned. > attached a disposition/questionnaire for the market survey. > All dialogue will take place in the KDV tool Artifik for traceability. Please use Artifik support if this tool is unknown to suppliers.
sig_bf5e743f13ae39e7a39c.title: Market survey for a new management system for water and sewage Enebakk municipality.

sig_bf9b598cf8293cad25d0.description: The Public Affairs Section (PAS) at U.S. Embassy Tunis invites creative and engaging proposals for programs that strengthen ties between the United States and Tunisia, highlight shared values, and promote bilateral cooperation in ways that make America safer, stronger, and more prosperous. Please see Section C. Program Description for more information. This Annual Program Statement (APS) outlines our funding priorities and the strategic themes we will focus on in FY2025, and the procedures for submitting requests for funding. Based on availability of funding, PAS Tunis will award grants, fixed amount awards, or cooperative agreements between a minimum of $10,000 and up to a maximum of $200,000 (U.S. dollars) each for projects that advance the priorities outlined in this APS. Please carefully follow all instructions in the full announcement. Proposals that fail to conform to the requirements outlined in this APS will not be considered. All proposed programs must include an American element or a connection with American expert(s), organization(s), or institutions in ways that promote increased understanding of U.S. policies, perspectives, and society and/or celebrate U.S. culture and values. Proposals that include programming outside Greater Tunis or across multiple governorates and/or promote increased collaboration and networking among alumni of U.S. government programs are encouraged. PAS Tunis invites creative and engaging proposals for programs that strengthen cultural, educational, professional, scientific, and business ties between the United States and Tunisia through programming that highlights shared values, strengthens people-to-people ties and institutional linkages, and promotes bilateral cooperation, and makes America safer, stronger, and more prosperous. Competitive proposals must focus on at least one grant priority area outlined below. Examples of possible PD small grant proposals include, but are not limited to: · Subject-matter expert, academic, and professional lectures, seminars, and speaker programs that include U.S. speakers/experts. · Programs that strengthen relationships and linkages between U.S. and Tunisian higher education and cultural institutions. · Educational, artistic, and cultural programs, including programs that strengthen English language teaching and learning, music, musical theater, dance workshops, master classes, and performances, live theatre performances, art exhibitions, and sports and culinary diplomacy initiatives that increase mutual understanding between the people of the United States and Tunisia. · Programs, including podcasts, that promote economic empowerment, entrepreneurship, or that share U.S. experiences related to addressing community challenges, including the management of water or energy resources, waste management, urban design and planning, and preparing for and mitigating natural or human-caused disasters. · Cultural heritage conservation and preservation programming, including through the use new and immersive technologies, such as VR technology. (Note: This funding cannot be used to support construction-related activities. End note.) Priority Program Areas and Strategic Themes: Proposals must address at least one of the six priority areas outlined below: · Economic Prosperity and Entrepreneurship: Initiatives that prioritize mutual prosperity, expand economic and commercial links between the United States and Tunisia, promote U.S. entrepreneurial values and practices, and that share best practices of successful U.S. business partnerships, startups, and investors with the aim of increasing economic opportunities for U.S. and Tunisian businesses and investors. · INNOVATION and Collaboration in science and technology: Initiatives that promote collaboration and academic partnerships in STEM fields (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics), including cybersecurity, space, energy, water security, food security, smart agriculture, health technology, and artificial intelligence (AI) between U.S. and Tunisian academic and research institutions, non-governmental organizations, and private companies, as well as programs that promote interest in STEM education among young people. · EDUCATIONAL LINKAGES AND ENGLISH LANGUAGE : Initiatives that expand collaboration and partnerships between U.S. and Tunisian higher education and research institutions through programs and professional and academic exchanges; programs to strengthen English language instruction in Tunisian universities and colleges; programs to expand the teaching of English in sign language and braille; and other programs that support and promote English language learning among Tunisian youth. · LEADERSHIP: Initiatives that provide leadership training inspired by U.S. experiences, models, and best practices to Tunisian young people (high school and university students and young professionals) to help them become effective leaders in their communities and professional field of choice. Such training may include English language, public speaking and interpersonal communication, emotional intelligence, critical thinking and problem solving, financial literacy, goal-setting, and mental health management strategies. · MEGA DECADE OF SPORTS: Programs that leverage the “Mega-Decade in Sports” in North America (2023-2034) when the United States will host the 2025 FIFA World Club Cup, the 2026 FIFA Men’s World Cup, the 2028 Summer Olympics and Paralympics in Los Angeles, and the 2034 Winter Olympics and Paralympics in Salt Lake City, in ways that strengthen people-to-people ties between the United States and Tunisia, promote American values and demonstrate American excellence and leadership in sports and tourism. · Celebrating American Excellence AND U.S.-Tunisian Enduring Partnership: Programs that 1) celebrate U.S. scientific or sport prowess, innovation, economic dynamism, agricultural strength, and national parks and tourism during the 250th anniversary year of U.S. Independence; 2) leverage people-to-people ties and promote the establishment of U.S-Tunisian institutional linkages through cultural diplomacy, including artistic and cultural workshops, performances, exhibitions, or other activities that celebrate American excellence in visual and performing arts, music, cultural heritage protection, and film during the 250th anniversary year of U.S. Independence and the 228th anniversary year of the 1797 treaty of friendship between the U.S. and Tunisia; AND/OR 3) leverage people-to-people or institutional ties through sports or cultural diplomacy initiatives to increase awareness and understanding among broad elements of Tunisian society of the history and benefits of the over two centuries of U.S.-Tunisian friendship, trade, and security cooperation.
sig_bf9b598cf8293cad25d0.title: Annual Program Statement (APS) for Fiscal Year 2025

sig_bfefaf518e9101b75e2a.description: Conducting consumer research on purchasing behavior in Belgium (2027–2031) The fresh vegetables sector within VLAM is launching an information campaign aiming at increasing the awareness of the sustainability efforts of the fresh vegetable sector. VLAM and APAQ-W wish to conclude a new framework agreement with an interested and qualified company to conduct research into the purchasing behaviour of Belgians for the next five calendar years, from 2027 to 2031 inclusive. VLAM (Vlaams Centrum voor Agro- en Visserijmarketing) and APAQ-W (Agence wallonne pour la Promotion d'une Agriculture de Qualité) are the promotional organisations for the Flemish and Walloon agricultural, horticultural, fisheries and agri-food sectors respectively. Both organisations support the marketing of primary products through promotion, communication and market-supporting research. More information about both organisations is available at www.vlam.be and www.apaqw.be. In order to develop and implement various types of campaigns for the different product and service groups and to fulfil their role as a knowledge centre/consumer observatory for the various sectors, sufficient consumer insight is required: • Figures on consumer purchasing behaviour (prp; person responsible for household purchases) in Belgium with regard to food and ornamental horticulture products (flowers, plants, trees, etc.) in general and, in particular, the products promoted by VLAM and APAQ-W. • Trends and developments, over a minimum period of 5 years and measured in a uniform and comparable manner, in consumer purchasing behaviour (prp) for these products, together with interpretation of the figures. • Special analyses of purchasing behaviour data, such as identifying potential target groups, rapid monitoring of purchasing behaviour during promotional campaigns and in the event of sudden changes in the societal context, including crises. VLAM and APAQ-W have chosen to jointly procure this consumer purchasing behaviour research as a framework agreement (through a procurement procedure in which VLAM acts as a central purchasing body with the participation of APAQ-W; see earlier in these tender specifications), because efficiency gains can be achieved for both the contracting authorities and the research agency.
sig_bfefaf518e9101b75e2a.title: Conducting consumer research on purchasing behavior in Belgium (2027–2031)

sig_c0523eb82f29eae8f146.description: The Universitätsklinikum Heidelberg (UKHD) is one of the largest and most renowned medical centres in Germany. Every year, approximately 80.000 patients receive inpatient and semi-inpatient treatment in its specialist clinics, and more than 1.000.000 patients are cared for on an outpatient basis. The Heidelberg campus unites scientific institutes and clinics of the UKHD, offers rich opportunities for cooperation with the life science and humanities faculties of the University, and simultaneously maintains established co-operations with internationally renowned non-university large-scale research institutions. The increasing complexity of and growing demands on the IT infrastructure in healthcare require reliable and efficient management of the IT landscape. In the context of the UKHD, it is of decisive importance that operational and clinical applications run constantly available and without faults in order to ensure optimal patient care and smooth operation. Lot LOT-0001: Provision of implementation, project and operational services for IT applications in the hospital environment. As part of this procurement procedure, the University Hospital is issuing a framework agreement for the provision of support services in IT application management (anticipated) from 1 February 2027 for the following 4 years (planned) incl. extension options. A transition that is as gradual as possible to transfer the services from operations outsourced from the existing provider to an external service provider is planned for the period Q1/Q2 2027. The complete takeover of the provision of all contractual services into regular operations is to take place by 01.07.2027 at the latest. The Centre for Digitalisation and Information Technology (ZDI) of the Universitätsklinikum Heidelberg is operationally divided into individual areas. Supported by contractors as external service providers, they assume end-to-end responsibility regarding the IT of the respective core processes of the contracting authority in order to be able to ensure secure and stable operation, but also the further development of IT performance. Directly affected by the tender and the procurement subject are the areas for Operational Information Systems (BIS), for Hospital Information Systems (KIS), for Integration, Special Systems and Archiving (ISA) as well as directly the ZDI itself. The scope of the tender covers the service requirements of the client for operational services in application management. This includes, in particular, smooth application operation, the rapid and permanent rectification of incidents and problems, as well as releases, upgrades and updates in coordination with the client. Furthermore, this encompasses other supportive project services that are in a direct or close substantive connection with the aforementioned operational services. The future contractor is expected to provide comprehensive and holistic services within the framework of a managed service in order to implement the client's requirements regarding IT architecture, IT security and IT service integration. The integration of IT services based on the ITIL v4 framework must be provided holistically for all specialist areas. In this context, the client will manage the contractor(s) and provide the IT hardware required at the client's locations as well as some of the required software licences.

sig_c0580f79e230c910a4cf.description: In the past almost 20 years since the founding of the Federal Government's Cultural and Creative Industries (KKW) initiative, the framework conditions, market structures, value chains and challenges for the KKW have changed fundamentally. Hardly any sector has been as strongly affected by the effects of the change brought about by transformation, the platform economy, digitalisation and artificial intelligence as the KKW, with impacts including on creative production, distribution and the exploitation of rights. The coming years will be characterised by further profound technological, economic and social upheavals. Digitalisation (especially artificial intelligence), sustainability and new forms of audience engagement have become the central drivers of change. After almost 20 years, it is therefore time to take stock on the one hand, and to look ahead and create foundations for strategic options for action on the other. In order to be able to conduct the further strategy process on an evidence-based footing, a qualitative and quantitative baseline study on future projections for the KKW is to be commissioned. The last baseline study, 'Macroeconomic Perspectives of the Cultural and Creative Industries', also produced on behalf of the BMWE, dates from the year 2009. The study is intended to develop a projection for the coming decade in order to provide strategic responses to structural changes in the sector. The aim is to critically examine the future viability of the KKW, to identify risks and to develop a forecast of opportunities and trends. The study 'Cultural and Creative Industries 2037' (working title) is intended to provide a foundation for the long-term strategic orientation of political and economic steering instruments with the help of future-oriented and forecasted scenario analyses. For a future projection up to 2037, it is therefore crucial not only to extrapolate existing growth trajectories, but to systematically include structural breaks, new value creation logics and disruptive technological developments in the forecast. The Federal Government's projections on macroeconomic growth are to be appropriately taken into account as a basis here. The study is intended to create a scientific foundation for the strategic further development of the Federal Government's Cultural and Creative Industries initiative and, in doing so, to provide in particular a long-term strategic orientation for political and economic steering instruments. The strategy is aimed prospectively at decision-makers from politics, business and administration, as well as at the actors in the cultural and creative industries themselves, who want to jointly set the course for a sustainable, innovative and economically strong creative ecosystem for the next generation. sig_c0f7471166943ec601b9.description: The term intends to enter into a contract for licences for the KI based tool Claude from the supplier Anthropic. Justification for the choice: The term needs an advanced, general KI-tool that can be used by employees across disciplines, including developers, designers and other roles. The aim is to support analysis, development and interaction assignments in line with Sikt's strategic targets for the use of artificial intelligence. After completed needs and market assessments, Visibility ́s assessment is that Claude currently appears to be the best suitable solution for the purpose, particularly in light of: *support for secure and final user-controlled access to data and integrations based on open standards, **good interaction between different user groups, including close collaboration between developers and other professional environments, technical prerequisites for integration with Sikt's existing platform services and architecture. Visibility has assessed alternative systems in the market, including, among other things, Copilot, Gemini, ChatGPT and Cursor, but they are not currently assessed to cover the need to a sufficient degree, especially in terms of the combination of access management, integration options and use across roles. The market for KI tools is developing quickly. The choice of Claude is therefore based on an assessment of available systems at the time of the procurement and is not intended to establish any type of long-term standardisation or supplier binding. Procurement form: The term has examined the possibility of acquiring Claude through the existing framework agreement for software licenses, but has been confirmed that the product cannot be delivered through it. Direct procurements from Anthropic are thus the only available procurement route. Extent and value of the procurement: The procurement concerns licences for Claude, with a staged and needs managed employee disclosure. The estimated total contract value is NOK 3,500,000. The actual cost will depend on the number of users and actual use over time. Options: No options.
sig_c0f7471166943ec601b9.title: Intention notice: Procurement of ki-tool Claude
