sig_c1114644e365759a47be.description: The present notice is not intended to initiate a procurement procedure nor to prepare one. It serves solely for market consultation. The Staatsinstitut für Schulqualität und Bildungsforschung (ISB) is conducting a market consultation in preparation for a procurement in the area of BayernCloud Schule (hereinafter: ByCS), which provides digital applications and services for the Bavarian school community. The contracting authority is examining the future provision, further development, integration and operation of a digital board application for the ByCS. The existing application is a browser-based interactive whiteboard software. The subject of the market consultation is the question of whether suitable market participants are in a position to take over, maintain, service and further develop the existing ByCS board or its code base, or to replace the existing ByCS board with another functionally and technically suitable board application. The aim of the market consultation is to obtain reliable information on solutions available on the market and fundamentally suitable for the described requirement. In particular, it is to be investigated whether an already available or adaptable board application can meet the functional, technical, data protection and operational requirements of the contracting authority and can be integrated, operated, maintained and further developed into the ByCS environment. Within the scope of the market consultation, insights are to be gained in particular as to whether and, if applicable, by whom the described services can be provided. Lot PAR-0001: Free State of Bavaria - Staatsinstitut für Schulqualität und Bildungsforschung (ISB) regarding tender for info services. The existing digital ByCS board application is a browser-based interactive whiteboard software for use in in-person and remote phases of teaching. The application was developed on behalf of the Bavarian State Ministry of Education and Cultural Affairs as a component of BayernCloud Schule and is continuously developed further. In doing so, the application is to fulfil the following criteria in particular: - Platform-independent (device types, operating system) - Browser-based - Responsive design - Offline app / PWA - GDPR-compliant design - Accessible according to WCAG - Collaboration - Very good writing feel / high quality of pen input with palm rejection - Suitable for primary schools -> Simplicity - Special school scripts integrable with individual menus - WOPI connection - Files can be saved offline - Sharing mechanism / permissions between teachers and pupils - Import/export of PDF files and images - Integration of websites and videos - Customisations to ByCS possible (design, repositories, CSP, ...) - Set square and compass - Import of GGS files (previous format) possible Within the scope of the market consultation, insights should be provided in particular on - the extent to which market participants are in a position to take over, maintain, service and further develop the existing board application; - whether other board applications suitable for school use are already available on the market; - whether such applications can meet the functional and technical requirements of the contracting authority; - whether and under what conditions an alternative application can be integrated into the ByCS environment; - what technical, operational and economic risks are associated with the different solution variants. Please contact markterkundung@abante.de by 20 September 2026, 23.59 hrs at the latest if you are interested in participating in the local market consultation. Your participation will not be remunerated. There is also no entitlement to participate in any procurement procedure that may subsequently follow. The decision as to whether a procurement procedure must be carried out is precisely what is to be brought about by the local market consultation. In your initial enquiry, please state as detailed as possible what qualifies you and what capacities you have to provide the envisaged services if the contracting authority decides on a procurement on the market. This is necessary in order to be able to assess the seriousness of the enquiry.

sig_c18c574df88e52eea3b9.description: The Home Office (HO) is the government department responsible for safeguarding the nation through border control, immigration, passport issuance, policing, fire services, counter-terrorism and drugs policies. UK Visas and Immigration (UKVI) plays an integral role in delivering this vision, managing millions of applications annually, enabling foreign nationals to visit, study, work or settle in the UK. As part of the evolution of existing services, UKVI pursues the transformation and modernisation of services in a manner that enhances customer experience and ensures accurate and efficient outcomes. One of the core services delivered by UKVI is the Life in the UK test, an essential component of the route to settlement in the UK and to UK citizenship. The Life in the UK Secure Digital Test and Digital Online Learning Materials Service (LITUK) Project is procuring a new service; enabling the continued delivery of front-end services, balancing continuity with improvements and transformation. LITUK aims to move to a 'Digital-by-Default' approach, while upholding the rigorous standards necessary to support UKVI immigration decisions. The successful provider will deliver a service that combines technological innovation with security assurance, enabling customers to demonstrate their knowledge of life in the UK with confidence and convenience throughout their UK immigration journey. The purpose of this third round of Preliminary Market Engagement is to share information relating to the Authority's vision for the LitUK service and the procurement approach. At this stage, no final decisions have been made regarding the preferred solution. Please Note: the content of this Preliminary Market Engagement Notice may be subject to change. Lot 1: . None

sig_c19ac454b9b9881ff913.description: With over 273,000 people in Scotland living with Stage 3-5 Chronic Kidney Disease (CKD), including 2,000 receiving dialysis treatment, and demand expected to increase fivefold over the next decade, improvements to dialysis transport across NHS Scotland are urgently needed. Dialysis journeys account for more than 40% of all non-emergency patient transport activity, costing 9.1 million GBP annually. Yet current arrangements can be inconsistent, creating avoidable pressures for patients, providers and NHS services. NHS Scotland is seeking innovative, patient-centred and sustainable solutions that improve reliability, efficiency and patient outcomes, while reducing administrative burden and delivering better value for money. CivTech’s mission is to drive daring and innovation in the public sector by collaboratively solving Challenges that make people’s lives better – and in doing so create generations of sustainable, high growth businesses. CivTech brings together public sector expertise and private sector innovation to solve real problems, develop new products, and deliver better, faster and easier services for everyone. Central to the approach is co-production with the citizen. Part of the Scottish Government’s Directorate for Digital, CivTech’s approach is helping transform public sector engagement with tech and innovation, delivering significant benefits to public services, producing genuine uplifts for the Scottish economy - and along the way, making lives better. Across the country there are problems public sector organisations would like to solve and in the current environment the need for smart, efficient and effective products has never been greater. The Scottish Government is aware innovation is a good way to create them and is committed to ensuring a large part of its tech spend goes to innovative businesses - whatever stage they’re at, or size they are. This is where CivTech comes in. The CivTech Innovation Flow is designed to create products as quickly and effectively as possible, and uses a true Accelerator model at the heart of its Innovation Flow model. For you – whether you’re an individual, team or company – it’s an opportunity to take on a Challenge, solve it, and win contracts with a blue-chip public sector organisation. You’ll build a product, and a business to take it as far as possible. Because here’s the kicker: the Challenges we issue aren’t ‘single organisation’ problems – most of the problems we are solving exist worldwide. In short: Open Challenges are set. sig_c1af6f59bca95c4857f3.description: The Bars of Admission (RAKs) in Germany are corporations under public law and currently represent over 160.000 admitted lawyers. Their legal basis is formed by the Federal Lawyers' Act (BRAO). There are a total of 27 Bars of Admission in Germany. The 11 Bars of Admission issuing the tender here are actively involved in the project and contribute their professional, organisational and technical requirements to the design. The participating chambers exhibit varying organisational structures, member numbers and IT landscapes, which underlines the need for a flexible and scalable solution. However, the various Bars of Admission are essentially subject to the same legal requirements, which are primarily dictated by the Federal Lawyers' Act (BRAO). In total, the eleven participating chambers currently look after around 132.000 members, who are administered and supported by approximately 370 employees. To support their tasks, 22 chambers currently use a software solution from DATEV eG. This solution covers core administrative processes, particularly in the areas of personnel administration, billing and complaint or case management. DATEV eG has terminated the existing software solution effective 31.12.2027. This decision makes timely planning and procurement of a suitable successor solution necessary. Against this background, the eleven local Bars of Admission have joined forces with the objective of replacing the currently used software solution, procuring a suitable successor solution and successfully introducing it. The project group is led and coordinated by five Bars of Admission (Frankfurt am Main, Hamburg, Hamm, Munich and Stuttgart). The aim is to procure a modern, high-performance and future-proof software solution that meets the specific requirements of the chambers and completely or with enhancements maps the previous functionalities of the DATEV software. In advance, a structured survey of the technical and functional requirements was conducted. This forms the basis for the drawn-up requirements catalogue. The DATEV software currently in use and to be replaced is utilised in the chambers for the following task areas: (1) Personnel administration: Administration of master data of natural and legal persons, admissions, status changes, specialist lawyer designations, training systems, resignations and reactivations. (2) Billing: Administration and billing of membership fees, charges, credit notes, etc. (3) Complaint management: Administration of professional law procedures, in particular complaints (4) Archiving and deletion: Archiving and deletion of data records from personnel and complaint management The software is deeply integrated into the work processes of users and forms a central basis for daily administrative work. Currently, the eleven participating Bars of Admission each operate independent instances of the DATEV software. While the basic functionalities are comparable in all chambers, differences exist in the specific configuration, particularly with regard to individually defined data fields, differing data structures and chamber-individual usage concepts. The project pursues the overarching objective of identifying a suitable successor solution for the discontinued DATEV software and procuring it within the framework of a structured, voluntary tender procedure.
sig_c1af6f59bca95c4857f3.title: Procurement procedure for a Chamber of Lawyers administration system

sig_c1bd567ef6b192706741.description: SUBJECT OF THE PROCUREMENT The subject of the procurement is the municipality's outsourced financial and payroll administration services, including both service production and the necessary information systems. The selected service provider is responsible for the municipality's overall financial management, which includes bookkeeping, participation in the preparation of the financial statements and budget, statutory financial reporting including municipal data reporting, VAT reporting and tax returns, financial planning, purchase and sales ledgers, payment transactions, and entering memorandum vouchers into bookkeeping. Personnel and payroll administration services cover payroll calculation for the municipality's various collective agreement sectors (KVTES, OVTES, TS), maintenance of personnel data, service period calculation, reporting of absences and income to the incomes register and Kela, as well as the payment of travel and expense claims and trustee allowances. The municipality has approximately 250 employees whose payroll calculation must be handled monthly. The procurement package covers only the municipality's services, not, for example, the municipality's subsidiaries. The currently used systems are FPM for financial planning, Sarastia365 BI for financial reporting, Dooap for purchase invoices, Sarastia365 TalousApp for sales invoicing, and Sarastia365 MuistioApp for memorandum vouchers, as well as Populus 25.2.0 for personnel administration. The service provider must also have the capability for system integration, including sales invoicing from billing systems commonly used in various sectors, such as early childhood education, the water utility, and construction and permit supervision. In connection with the procurement, the possibility of replacing the current financial planning and HR systems with more appropriate solutions will be surveyed. The procurement may include options, such as the electronic archiving of permanently retained financial and personnel administration documents in the contracting authority's own archive, and HR system interface solutions with third-party systems, such as occupational healthcare or employee benefit services. CONTRACT PERIOD The contract period is five (5) years. The contracting authority has the right to extend the validity of the contract by an option period of two (2) years. SCOPE OF THE PROCUREMENT Based on previous outcomes, the annual value of the procurement has been approximately 280 000–330 000 euros (VAT 0 %). REGISTRATION FOR MARKET CONSULTATION Interested tenderers are requested to register for the market consultation by filling out the forms survey 20.4.2026 by 12.00 at https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/2wSrXSgP2e. Tenderers are requested to note that registration for the market consultation cannot be done via Tarjouspalvelu.

sig_c1d104ff0415b9f0f781.description: This notice is a request for information, which is not a prior information notice, contract notice or call for tenders. The Police University College, the National Police Board and the Emergency Services Academy Finland are surveying the market with a view to a potential competitive tender for the selection test system and its related support, maintenance and development services. The system is used for conducting written and multiple-choice tasks of the selection test, sharing links to other external test systems, checking and scoring test tasks, and recording the scores of all test sections, including those carried out outside the system. The purpose of the market survey is to acquire information on operators that would have the capability to provide services for maintaining and developing the system, taking particular account of the system's technological solutions, the security-critical operating environment, the intended use of the system, and the requirements set for the system's reliability and usability. The potential procurement is part of the police education management systems reform project (KOM2). The aim of the project is to produce secure, reliable and modern systems for the Police University College's student application, student admission and student administration. The aim of the request for information is to acquire information in particular on • potential service providers, • systems available on the market and their features, • solution alternatives or service implementation methods, and • pricing models and cost levels of solution alternatives Appendices of the request for information (available from Tarjouspalvelu): Appendix 1 Subject of the request for information Appendix 2 Questions for suppliers (filled in by the supplier) Failing to respond to the request for information does not prevent participation in a possible tender contest. The request for information does not oblige the Police University College to implement the procurement in the manner described in the request for information and its appendices, and the tender contest may also be omitted. The Police University College hopes that potential suppliers would answer the questions as comprehensively as possible. The aim of the request for information is to increase the Police University College's market knowledge, survey the suppliers on the market, their expertise and experience, and gather information for planning a potential future competitive tender, inter alia regarding the pricing and implementation methods of the services. The Police University College may utilise the submitted responses if it decides to organise a tender contest regarding the procurement. The Police University College may also ask respondents to the request for information for additional information on their services and also provide them with preliminary tendering documents for comment. We kindly ask suppliers interested in participating in the market dialogue to respond to the request for information by 9.4.2026 at 15.00 to: polamk@poliisi.fi or by using secure email from https://securemail.poliisi.fi/. The email must be titled "Tietopyyntö; Valintakoejärjestelmä sekä siihen liittyvät tuki-, ylläpito- ja kehityspalvelut". As an attachment to the response, we kindly ask suppliers to provide the completed request for information Appendix 2 "Questions for suppliers". If the response contains the supplier's trade secrets or other confidential information, we kindly ask the supplier to designate the documents as "Trade secret". The Police University College will make the decision on organising a possible tender contest and the schedule after the market survey. Responses given to the request for information will become public when a decision and contract are made in the potential procurement concerning the matter (section 6 of the Act on the Openness of Government Activities). If, based on the survey, it is decided that no contracts will be concluded at all, the documents will become public upon signature of the respective decision.

sig_c286fcbe8807f4ad3370.description: Glasgow City Council (GCC) manages a framework for the delivery of consultancy services in the area of Business Growth. The consultancy services are delivered to SMEs with growth potential across the city, to help deliver sustainable and inclusive growth and improve business start-up and survival rates in the city. With the current framework concluding in March 2027, GCC is now looking to establish a new framework. These services are delivered under a multi-Lot framework, through a mix of 1-2-1, both face to face and online, and group consultancy sessions related to an anticipated 10 specific specialist areas. The council encourage bids from businesses of all sizes, including sole traders, and encourage a diverse and competitive supplier base. The procurement process has been designed to be proportionate, transparent and accessible, with requirements focused on capability and delivery rather than organisational size. Sole traders are encouraged to engage where they can demonstrate their ability to meet the specified requirements. Lot 1: Business Structuring Business Governance, Legal and IP. The Business Governance, Legal and IP Lot will provide support to help determine the assignment and coordination of roles, power and responsibilities within a business. It also defines how information flows between the different levels of management. Introducing a formal organisational structure can help put your business in a better position to achieve its objectives. Services for this Lot should include, but not be limited to, the following: Board Development Company Structuring Franchising Business Succession Company Governance Ethical Management Intellectual Property Lot 2: Business Growth, Sustainable Growth and Productivity. The Sustainable Growth and Productivity lot will provide support to identify areas of improvement processes which help with improving some measure of an enterprise's success. Business growth can be achieved either by boosting the top line or revenue of the business with greater product sales or service income, or by increasing the bottom line or profitability of the operation by minimizing costs. Business growth is a function of the business lifecycle and can be influenced by industry growth trends. Services for this Lot should include, but not be limited to, the following: Strategic Planning Sales & Marketing Change Management Pitching & Procurement Procurement Operations Management Turnaround Mergers & Acquisitions Lot 3: Upskilling, Leadership and Resources. The Upskilling, Leadership and resources lot will provide support to involve reviewing existing Leadership Development processes and preparing a report on their future suitability and/or making recommendations for future actions. It will also provide a range of support across leadership and management as well as capacity building and comprehensive HR support. Services for this Lot should include, but not be limited to, the following: Organisational Development and Succession Planning Leadership and Management Capacity Building and HR Support Lot 4: Financial Readiness and Planning. The Finance Lot will allow support to be provided across a range of areas which will help with the efficient and effective management of money / funds in such a manner as to accomplish the objectives of the organisation. Strategic financial management not only manages a company's finances but allows them to be managed with the intention to succeed. Services for this Lot should include, but not be limited to, the following: Financial Management Financial Readiness Preparing for Investment Alternative Finance Company Valuation Taxation Lot 5: Design and System processing. The Design and System Processing Lot will integrate design thinking principles into a range of organisations across different industry sectors. Promoting the use of design principles and educating SMEs on the benefits directly linked to innovation, sustainability and resilience, this Lot will see an increase in available support that creates design-led companies who can improve effective strategy and product/service development and manage organisational change. Services for this Lot should include, but not be limited to, the following: Problem Solving Development Testing and validation Lot 6: Sales and Digital Marketing. Sales and marketing share two key roles within businesses: attracting more customers and developing and retaining the existing customer base. They also share the collective underlying goal of bringing in more revenue. When sales and marketing work together a substantial improvement is seen on important performance metrics. Variations persist between Business to Consumer (B2C) and Business to Business (B2B) and as a result of differing routes to market (particularly considering the impact of digital) but the above holds fairly true irrespective of the business model. Expert services under this Sales and Digital Marketing Lot assist businesses with the practical approach to marketing, including writing a marketing plan and establishing a marketing communications plan for integrating traditional and digital communications. It will also offer support with developing a marketing and/ or sales strategy, with pricing and market penetration strategies Services for this Lot fall under the following sub-categories; Digital Sales: Marketing Strategies: Branding: SEO Maximisation including Social Media and website Lot 8: Digital Transformation. The Digital Lot will provide support to businesses to use technology to benefit to its internal and external operations. The types of digital support will be varied but will allow businesses to use Technology solutions to help their business to the next level. Services for this Lot should include, but not be limited to, the following: Social Media eCommerce Support Data Analytics Mobile or internet technologies Customisation of software or App development Cloud Computing AI Digital Strategy Cyber Security Lot 9: Sustainable and Net Zero support. Sustainability expert support topics span core pillars like environmental compliance, carbon accounting, circularity, and ESG reporting. They also encompass strategic organisational needs, including Leadership & Culture, Carbon Accounting & Carbon Baseline Assessment, Supply Chain Engagement and Regulatory Compliance & Climate Risk Services for this Lot should include, but not be limited to, the following: Leadership and Culture Carbon Accounting and Carbon Baseline Assessment Regulatory Compliance and Climate Risk Sustainability and Sustainable Marketing Circular Economy Lot 10: Business Acceleration. This Lot will provide support in a different, shorter, more targeted, and innovative way for organisations at various stages of growth. Since the pandemic feedback from businesses has shown that most are now looking for shorter, sharper more focussed interventions. These interventions could focus on emerging themes and could target the key and emerging sectors. It is envisaged that these interventions will be demand driven and will be required on an as needed basis. They could combine traditional teaching methodologies with guidance and mentorship. These programmes could include expert support from Lots 1-9 Business Growth; Business Structuring; Leadership and Skills; Financial Management; Design Thinking and Innovation; Sales and Marketing; Internationalisation; Digital Development and Innovation and Green Business Support. Suppliers will be contacted by the Council when a specific intervention is required, Evidence suggests that organisations who engage with business accelerators benefit from the opportunity presented, leading to greater collaboration with other entrepreneurs and businesses that can yield benefits that allow the business to grow at an accelerated rate. An overview of the objections and intentions of Accelerator programmes is; Acceleration: Learning-by-doing is vital to the process of scaling any venture, and the point of any type of acceleration programme is to accelerate that process. In this way, businesses are able to compress a large amount of learning into a shorter period of time. Our Accelerator programmes will deliver relevant, accessible and practical learning for the leaders of ambitious businesses in the city looking to scale up. It will equip participants with the skills and tools to shape their own learning. It could encourage participants to take ownership of their own development and assume responsibility for coaching their own management teams to embed learning throughout the organisation. It may also help to address organisational, operational, and strategic challenges that the business may face It could also include access to experienced entrepreneurs and mentors, business model refinement, advice on start-up capital, and the opportunity to pitch to potential investors. Any Accelerator programmes required under this Lot will require to be delivered over a specified period. Most programmes will accommodate between 12 – 15 eligible organisations, with a maximum of 15 participating in any programme. Smaller cohorts may be required on occasion. Lot 7: Preparing for Global Growth. The Internationalisation Lot will support businesses access overseas markets, offering an opportunity to increase sales to a much wider customer base. Exporting can be profitable for businesses of all sizes and lead to new job opportunities. Scottish businesses trading internationally have high productivity rates and are often more competitive, with research suggesting that SMEs who export perform better financially and grow more than twice as fast as those that do not. There is already a comprehensive support structure nationally through SDI for exporting support, therefore this Lot aims to fill the gaps in expertise or support businesses unable to leverage other public sector support. Services for this Lot should include, but not be limited to, the following: Support for Exporting , including tariffs and taxes Market Analysis and Development Structuring for Internationalisation

sig_c296d685b63f931fd290.buyer_name: Bielefeld Municipal Utilities Limited Liability Company
sig_c296d685b63f931fd290.description:
The subject of the tender is the conclusion of a framework agreement on the provision of specialist consulting for an identity and access management project of Municipal Utilities Bielefeld. The aim of the project is the further development of IAM processes, the design of role and permission models as well as the introduction of a central technical IAM solution. Lot LOT-0001: Procurement of a consulting service for specialist consulting within the scope of an identity and access management (IAM) project for Municipal Utilities Bielefeld (SWB). Municipal Utilities Bielefeld operate a heterogeneous IT landscape with a multitude of applications and systems. The management of user identities and access rights is currently carried out partly in a decentralised and system-related manner. To improve the control of identities and permissions, a central structure for managing digital identities is being established as part of an IAM project. The aim of the IAM project is the introduction of a central IAM service for managing digital identities as well as for the structured and role-based allocation of permissions for applications and systems. For this purpose, an IAM governance structure is to be established as well as a technical IAM solution introduced and rolled out. Specifically, this means the further development of IAM processes, the design of a role and permission model, the introduction of a central IAM solution as well as integration of applications (from Q3 2027) and the preparation of organisational structures for the future operation of the IAM service. The project is managed by an external project management in close cooperation with the IP business division of Municipal Utilities Bielefeld. In the course of the project, the achievement of the following milestones is generally envisaged: • Elaboration and coordination of an IAM governance structure • Elaboration of a role-rights structure for SWB • Introduction of a technical IAM solution incl. implementation of a pilot • Successive rollout of the technical IAM solution to the entire SWB The subject of the tender is the provision of external specialist consulting to support the IAM project of Municipal Utilities Bielefeld. The consulting service comprises support for the implementation phase of the IAM project through two roles. 1. IAM management consulting 2. IAM process consulting Exactly one person is provided for each role. IAM management consulting supports the IP business division with organisational and strategic issues in connection with the introduction of the IAM service. Core tasks of IAM management consulting are: • Support with the organisational classification of IAM within the IT organisation • Further development of governance structures in the IAM environment • Support with the definition and staffing of roles and responsibilities • Evaluation of organisational impacts of IAM structures and processes • Support with the integration of IAM into existing security and governance structures • Elaboration of decision-making bases for management and project control • Support with coordination with relevant stakeholders • Support with the further development of the organisational operating model for the IAM service • Consulting on covering relevant regulatory requirements • Developing an implementation strategy on guidelines, processes and the tool solution • Coordinating content-related dependencies with other projects and line initiatives • Support with the manufacturer-independent selection of an IAM tool solution IAM process consulting supports the functional design of the processes for managing digital identities and permissions. Core tasks of IAM process consulting are: • Analysis of existing processes for managing identities and permissions • Elaboration of processes for the lifecycle of digital identities • Support with the design of joiner-mover-leaver processes • Development and structuring of a role and permission model • Structuring of processes for granting and changing access rights • Support with the integration of applications into IAM processes • Design of processes for recertification of permissions • Analysis of existing permission structures in applications • Creation of functional concepts and process documentation in the IAM environment • Support with the introduction of the processes and the tool solution • Technical support with required provided services and contribution obligations for the implementation of the tool solution • Elaboration of test cases based on the process descriptions and requirements for the tool solution For IAM management consulting, there is a maximum quantity of 440 person-days or 3.520 hours. For IAM process consulting, there is a maximum quantity of a total of 385 person-days or 3.080 hours Hybrid service provision is generally permissible. A binding ratio between remote and on-site deployments cannot currently be specified. The contracting authority determines the project-related required presence demand. On-site deployments in Bielefeld may be required in particular for project kick-off, workshops, steering committees, coordination meetings with central stakeholders and other appointments with presence requirements. The contractor must ensure that corresponding on-site appointments can also be attended with a reasonably short lead time. The concrete scope of presence services is determined by the contracting authority in accordance with the requirements of the project progress The framework agreement does not establish any minimum purchase obligation on the part of the contracting authority. The quantities, hourly rates, reference quantities, demand values and maximum quantities specified in the procurement documents serve exclusively to determine the contract value, the comparability of bids and the award evaluation.

There is no entitlement to actual commissioning or utilisation of these quantities or services. Call-offs within the meaning of these procurement documents are understood exclusively as individual commissions of services triggered by the contracting authority within the framework of the framework agreement.

sig_c2b884cde6867ed7c2c5.description: The overarching goal of this notice of funding opportunity (NOFO) and its companion opportunities is to establish the Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) Program to support development of innovative, reliable, cost-effective, and sustainable multimodal AI-based clinical decision support (CDS) tools. PRIMED-AI CDS tools are based on the integration of clinical imaging with other types of multimodal health data to enhance care for patients with a wide range of health conditions. The PRIMED-AI Program seeks to catalyze the adoption of AI-based CDS tools into clinical workflows to enable novel personalized medicine strategies that address significant health challenges. The purpose of this Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) is to catalyze the development and testing of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled, image-centered, multimodal Clinical Decision Support (CDS) tools, developed in pursuance as Software as a Medical Device (SaMD). These projects are expected to have high potential for demonstrable, positive impact on patient outcomes and/or healthcare processes.

sig_c33a20807edc4227b7b7.description: The contracting authorities are conducting a competitive dialogue for the development of a chatbot for the Bergisches Servicecenter as well as for the administrations of the three contracting authorities in accordance with the provisions of the German Public Procurement Ordinance (VgV). The tender aims to develop a chatbot for the Bergisches Servicecenter and the three contracting authorities, which is to be used to execute or perform, among other things, both the services of the Bergisches ServiceCenter and the services of the administrations of the cities of Remscheid, Solingen and Wuppertal at the level of information provision to the public and interaction regarding the administrative services of the three cities. In the future, the chatbot is to be further developed in line with the current state of the art, particularly at the interaction and transaction level as well as for internal administrative support. The contracting authorities shall be entitled, both jointly for the Bergisches Servicecenter and individually, to call off services from the contractor regarding the developed chatbot (cf. draft contract, Annex C to the 2. Letter of Procedure). The subject of the contract is the development of a chatbot system to fulfil service tasks or services of the Bergisches Servicecenter at the level of information provision to the population of the cities of Remscheid, Solingen and Wuppertal. Regarding the functional scope of the chatbot, the solution concepts must take into account the future further development of the interaction and transaction level as well as the possibility of internal administrative support. Furthermore, the subject of the contract also includes the maintenance, further development and adaptation of the chatbot system. On the one hand, the chatbot system should be able to implement, within the framework of providing information to citizens, companies and other information seekers, in particular direct information on available services, forwarding to corresponding services and information, and prospectively, at the interaction and transaction level, among other things, advice on services. On the other hand, with regard to internal administration, the chatbot system is prospectively intended to support, among other things, text management, research assistants and an internal service bot. The chatbot is to be implemented in particular as a multilingual, AI-supported large language model, with transparent, consistent and friendly or citizen-oriented language, with constant citation of sources, and in compliance with data protection and IT security law.

sig_c3808ae8c24d6ecf5756.description: South Lanarkshire Council are looking to notify the market of a potential future contract opportunity to deliver Sign In/Sign Out facilities for Operatives within Grounds Services and Waste Services, although it is possible that this may be extended to other Services within the Council in the future. This facility would initially be required for approximately 900 employees across 10 separate locations. Given the nature of the duties which these Operatives carry out, the use of cards, fobs, and lanyards is not practical for Health & Safety reasons. The preference would be to use fingerprint reader technology, although the facility to manually sign in or sign out using alternative methods, such as a username/password or PIN, would be required for both onsite and offsite use. As South Lanarkshire Council has recently implemented Oracle Fusion Cloud and uses the Oracle Time and Labour (OTL) module of that system within some Service Areas, it is a requirement that any Sign In/Sign Out System operates or integrates directly with the OTL module. sig_c447dffcae6a7a3e1937.description: INTRODUCTION The Centre for Emergency Communication (CFB) of the Danish Emergency Management Agency is preparing a procurement procedure for a contract concerning the 112 solution. The contract will cover the operation, maintenance, support and further development of the existing 112 application. The existing 112 solution is described in the attached background note Annex A. Against this background, CFB is conducting a market dialogue with potential tenderers in two phases. In the first phase, CFB is asking tenderers to answer the questions set out in Annex B. In the second phase, CFB will invite up to five tenderers to a follow-up meeting in order to elaborate on the information. First of all, we therefore ask tenderers to answer the questions in the questionnaire and upload it in the ETHICS procurement system. TIMETABLE FOR THE MARKET DIALOGUE The market dialogue has been published in the Official Journal of the European Union in a prior information notice dispatched on 15 December 2025. We will receive answers to the questions no later than 12 January 2026 at 12:00, after which we will select tenderers for follow-up meetings, which we expect to hold on 27 and 28 January 2026. We expect the meetings to have a duration of 11⁄2-2 hours. If a tenderer is invited to market dialogue, the tenderer will be notified no later than 21 January 2026. The agenda for the meetings will be sent out with the invitation, and the agenda will be based on an elaboration of the questions that the tenderer has answered. We will select tenderers based on the submitted answers. The selection will be made based on, inter alia, an assessment of tenderers' relevant experience with similar tasks, tenderers' relevant considerations regarding the task's deliverables, including transition-in, as well as tenderer's answers regarding matters that the tenderer considers to be essential for tendering for the task. THE TENDER We expect to publish the tender in the second quarter of 2026. The procurement procedure will be a negotiated procedure in accordance with the provisions of the Defence and Security Directive. The tender documents will be drawn up in Danish, and answers in Danish will be required with the exception of system documentation and similar. ANSWERING THE QUESTIONS The questions appear in Annex B, and the answer must appear exclusively in the form and not in separate annexes. The questions can be answered in Danish or English. The completed form must be uploaded via the ETHICS procurement system no later than 12 January 2026 at 12:00. CONDITIONS FOR PARTICIPATION It is voluntary for tenderers to participate in the market dialogue, and it is without significance for the subsequent tender whether a tenderer has participated. We will treat the information received as confidential, subject to the limitations arising from the right of public access to documents, cf. the Public Administration Act. QUESTIONS Questions concerning the market dialogue can be asked in the ETHICS procurement system.

sig_c5413b14a87460db9909.description: The Municipality intends to procure a modern, future-proof and comprehensive operational system that strengthens the quality, legal certainty and efficiency of social services. The system must enable digital, cohesive and automated work processes that provide case handlers and service providers with: • increased overview and transparency, • improved decision support, • reduced administrative burden. The procured system is to constitute a central digital platform for the work of social services and be fully integrable through open APIs and standardised information flows, enabling the Municipality to create a cohesive end-to-end solution across system boundaries. The system must be configurable, scalable and adaptable to changing operational needs, new legislation and technical developments. The Municipality's information must be retainable, transferable and reusable without technical or financial obstacles, while maintaining information quality and supporting long-term sustainable information management. Digitalisation and automation are to replace manual tasks, duplicate documentation and parallel support systems to the greatest extent possible. The system shall thus contribute to: • legally secure and uniform case handling, • a good working environment, • high and traceable information quality. Full traceability must exist throughout the information chain – from decisions, interventions and execution to follow-up, changes in system configurations and integrations. The Municipality must at all times be able to track how information has been handled, by whom and on what grounds.
sig_c5413b14a87460db9909.title: Social Services operational system

sig_c57817db33a5b42f1ddb.description:
An IT application is to be procured as a SaaS cloud solution for the digitisation of processes relating to trichinella testing, the management of monitoring samples in the animal health sector, and management in the event of an outbreak of African Swine Fever (ASF). The IT application must be compatible with the hunting statistics application from Condition – Integrierte Softwarelösungen GmbH. This is used in the Free State of Thuringia to record bag data (data on wild animals killed by hunters). The IT application should be available both as a web application (usable in common browsers) and as a mobile app (iOS and Android operating systems). Within the scope of the tender, an app is defined as an application that must be installed on a mobile device before use by the user and can only be used there. As a rule, this takes place on a smartphone or tablet using a so-called app store. There will be two main user groups: a) administrative or laboratory staff b) non-administrative users (e.g. authorised hunters). The non-administrative users record data on killed or slaughtered animals. If necessary, they also submit applications for the testing of these animals for trichinella and/or certain wildlife diseases to the competent authorities or the competent testing facility of the Free State of Thuringia. The test results should be retrievable via the IT application. The competent authorities (veterinary and food monitoring offices of the districts and independent cities - veterinary authorities) operate the trichinella testing laboratories. These should be able to access the application data recorded by external users in the IT application via their own user interface and transmit the test results back to the applicants. In addition, laboratory software should be made available to the competent authorities, with the help of which testing activities can be documented on the basis of the application data. In the case of monitoring samples in the animal health sector, the client's laboratory at the Thuringian State Office for Consumer Protection is the competent testing facility. The laboratory software (LIMS) in use there should be able to access the information on the samples entered by the users via the HIT database. The IT application must therefore have an interface to the HIT database. A direct connection to the LIMS is not intended. The IT application is to be made available to administrative staff for mapping internal administrative processes, as well as to affected users outside the administration for data entry and application submission, and for receiving notifications from the competent authorities. While the use cases of trichinella testing, management of monitoring samples in the animal health sector, and the interface to the hunting statistics application are to be available permanently, the use case of management in the event of an outbreak of African Swine Fever (ASF) is only to be usable and available on an ad-hoc basis. Furthermore, introductory support and training for the staff of the competent authorities should be included in the offer as an initial service. The contract is concluded via an EVB-IT cloud contract. The procurement is carried out by the client for use by all districts and independent cities in Thuringia. The use of the IT application for the aforementioned purposes is mandatory for the districts and independent cities. For hunters, however, use is optional. This means they can refrain from using the IT application. The previous analogue system for sampling will continue to be used in parallel for the time being. The 21 veterinary and food monitoring offices of the 22 districts and independent cities in the Free State of Thuringia are, among other things, responsible for receiving and testing samples of slaughtered or killed animals intended for human consumption for Trichinella spp. Furthermore, there are responsibilities with regard to granting permission for the taking of samples intended for trichinella testing by non-administrative persons. Citizens who wish to make use of the aforementioned administrative services should be enabled to record the required application data digitally in accordance with the principles of the Online Access Act (OZG), to submit the application paperlessly to the respective competent veterinary and food monitoring office, and to receive the notifications from the competent authorities. In addition, the possibility should be created to comply with further reporting obligations (e.g. the recording of hunting bags by hunters) in digital form. The testing of wild boar for Trichinella spp. only takes place if the animal is to become food. Based on experience to date, this leads to the testing of up to 30.000 head of wild boar per year in Thuringia. These figures fluctuate. In addition, the veterinary surveillance authorities are responsible for implementing regular monitoring of killed wild animals for certain animal disease pathogens. Depending on the current animal health status, the number of samples is expected to vary between approx. 5.000 and 30.000 samples per year. Data entry and application submission as well as the receipt of notifications should also be made possible here for the respective affected citizens. The recorded data should be transmitted via the application to the State Office for Consumer Protection responsible for testing the samples. The application part for the management of ASF outbreaks should be based on the aforementioned application parts in terms of operation (esp.

the monitoring of killed wild animals for certain animal disease pathogens) and interact with them in terms of content in accordance with the technical requirements. This application part should be activatable on an ad-hoc basis for each affected authority (veterinary authorities of the districts and independent cities and, if applicable, the client). In addition to an ASF outbreak in Thuringia, it should also be used in the context of exercises to prepare for an outbreak. A final application part includes the recording and reporting of hunting bags by hunters. This report includes all huntable animal species. For this documentation obligation, the kill data from the aforementioned application parts should be reusable, but it should also be possible to record new kill data. A corresponding interface is to be provided for the necessary data exchange with the hunting statistics application of Condition – Integrierte Softwarelösungen GmbH. The hunters already have direct access to the hunting statistics application. The interface should enable them to gain access from within the IT application and thus facilitate reporting through data transfer. The application is to be provided for use by administrative personnel in the Free State of Thuringia as well as the respective affected citizens in the Free State of Thuringia. As a result, the licence and terms of use must enable use by employees of the state, the municipalities, and by non-administrative persons. The number of future users cannot be precisely quantified at present, as the use of the IT application is optional for hunters. However, the number of hunters in Thuringia can be a reference point; it amounts to approx. 13.000. In addition, there are approx. 100 administrative staff.

sig_c5990e4963af4f52e345.description: Hanover Housing Association has been providing housing and support services across Scotland for over forty years. Managing approximately 150 homes with an aspect of care, predominantly for older people, Hanover is committed to enabling tenants to live independently within their communities. Hanover provides housing with care and very sheltered housing services which can range from light touch interventions such as reminding tenants to take medication to helping tenants with daily tasks such as personal care. Lot 1: . Hanover has initiated a Care and Support Systems Review at senior management level to address challenges caused by varied case management practices, inefficient data handling, and outdated digital tools. Two critical areas of improvement have been identified: - Care Scheduling/Planning – modernising currently paper-based processes, ensuring person-centred care and real-time updates. Although a full eMAR system is not required, medication management is a large area requiring support. - Rota Management – replacing fragmented manual scheduling with a centralised, digital platform. Through this forthcoming procurement, Hanover aims to secure a solution that will: - Improve service quality and tenant engagement through modern, digital care planning. - Increase operational efficiency and staff satisfaction via streamlined rota management. - Enhance safety, compliance, and oversight of medication management. - Provide integrated reporting, dashboards, and mobile accessibility. - Support compliance with relevant regulatory frameworks. The service will operate within a framework of continuous improvement with which the service provider will be required to engage; bringing innovation, sharing ideas, and implementing improvement measures to increase operational effectiveness/efficiency and drive out waste.
sig_c5990e4963af4f52e345.title: Provision of a Digital Care and Support System – Care Scheduling/Planning and Rota Management

sig_c5a615a74cdb9a73d4b7.description: Istekki is currently developing the procure-to-pay process. The key objectives of the development project are: • to ensure the functionality and consistency of the entire procure-to-pay process and operating methods • to define the system architecture and tender or select the necessary systems so that their use becomes more efficient and they support the operating models and set objectives • to ensure that Istekki's contracted suppliers perform in accordance with their contracts, that cooperation develops, and that operating models generate added value for both parties • to continuously improve and develop supplier cooperation, particularly with strategic and important suppliers • to provide visibility and manageability through data and reporting • to enable system controls throughout the entire process. In developing the procure-to-pay process, we are focusing in particular on developing ordering practices and supplier management, while at the same time examining the operating methods of the entire process broadly and the following tools: • the tendering system, • the contract management system, • the SRM (Supplier Relationship Management) system, • the purchase order system, • the warehouse management system, and • the purchase invoice processing system . We want to understand what kinds of packages each company has to offer so that the data flow of the entire procure-to-pay process is seamless and efficient. It is equally important for us to figure out in what parts it is advisable to make the tenders so that, on the one hand, the system package supports our operations efficiently, and, on the other hand, many companies are able to submit a tender. The purpose of the request for information is to collect information regarding the subject of the procurement for the upcoming tender process. Answering the request for information is not a prerequisite for participating in any subsequent tender process. However, to ensure the success of the upcoming tender process, it would be important for tenderers to provide the contracting authority with the requested information as extensively as possible. The request for information does not oblige Istekki Oy to carry out the procurement as described in the request for information or its appendices, and the tender competition may also not be carried out. Those who have answered the request for information will not be paid compensation for making the request for information or for participating in any presentation events related to the request for information. The request for information must be answered no later than 17.12.2025 by 12.00. A response form with advance questions is attached to the request for information in Tarjouspalvelu. Responses must be sent at the same time as registering as willing to participate in the market dialogue. Answering takes place by email to the address hankinnat@istekki.fi. The information provided will be treated confidentially. Information session We are organising a Teams session where we will present our needs and objectives to interested tenderers on Monday 15.12.2025 at 9-10. At the same time, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. Register for the information session using the accompanying link (by copying the link below into your browser): https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=ewb-5OsjeUaP1ZOOp9lZERdEXEuHF6JJgdbtjascEOxUMjhGWVVFRzZBUlo5OFZBSThBQldBRVhJOS4u The registration link for the information session can also be found in Tarjouspalvelu in attachment 2 of the request for information. Any additional information questions should in principle be asked as part of the request for information responses. The contracting authority will not publish additional information questions submitted during the request for information phase.

sig_c5f4ed68ce0e43596109.description: Dumfries and Galloway Council intend to commission an organisation to develop and implement the creation of a local Poverty dashboard, designed to provide a clear, accessible view of child poverty across Dumfries and Galloway. The dashboard should be accessible to partner organisations and any other interested party. Dumfries and Galloway Council serve a region of around 148,000 people across the South West of Scotland, stretching from Stranraer in the West, to Moffat and Annan in the East. We are the 3rd largest local authority by area in Scotland. The latest published statistics show that the rate of child poverty in Dumfries and Galloway is 22.7%. This equates to 5,672 children and young people living in poverty in the region. For example, there are some real challenges around improving health outcomes for those experiencing poverty in the early years and to ensure that all families eligible for free school meals are reached. Lot 1: . Dumfries and Galloway have received funding through the Scottish Governments Fairer Futures initiative. The project is early in its inception but has the long-term goal to deliver systematic change in the way public services support parents and families out of poverty. Our approach is to use existing principles and approaches to put families first, focusing on prevention rather than cure. To help achieve this, accurately measuring poverty and low income is crucial, and the availability of real-time data is vital for effective policy-making. The dashboard would have geographic layers, allowing users to explore poverty data at varying levels of granularity, offering insights into where support is most needed, with a particular focus on priority groups identified by the Scottish Government. These include lone-parent households, families with a disabled member, large families, and households with a mother under the age of 25. It is hoped that data can be gathered that will make meaningful impact to household income, targeting those who are not currently accessing all the additional help and support they can. In addition it’s important that we understand the landscape of our household in poverty, not in our dense areas of deprivation. It would be sage if this could also include pertinent health related data around missed appointments, or additional useful information which might allow for a targeted approach to reduce health inequality. The dashboard should; -Filter data by employment status, housing tenure, and age group, enabling a nuanced understanding of the different dimensions of poverty. -Be a dynamic platform with regularly updated data, that can be continually used to inform decision making. -Be publicly accessible, this openness is essential for building trust and ensuring that anti-poverty efforts are responsive to the lived experiences of families across the region. The purpose of the Poverty Dashboard is to make it easier for the Council and its partners, working with our families in poverty, to easily identify the areas of greatest need to support an evidence based and targeted approach when tackling poverty and inequality in the region.. It is anticipated that this procurement requirement will be conducted through Quick Quote portal as a non-regulated procedure, interested organisations are encouraged to express an interest to be added to the quick quote where this goes as planned.
sig_c5f4ed68ce0e43596109.title: Poverty Dashboard for Dumfries and Galloway

sig_c766e67fd02e97d3b9a6.description: The subject of this tender is the design, development and prototypical implementation of a system for the automated detection of dead branches within the infrastructure of Autobahn GmbH des Bundes. Functional specification: AI-based detection of dead branches 1. Introduction and objectives The subject of this tender is the design, development and prototypical implementation of a system for the automated detection of dead branches within the infrastructure of Autobahn GmbH des Bundes. The objective is to provide a digital tool that supports visual inspection through AI-based image analysis, thereby significantly increasing the efficiency and safety of maintenance measures. The specific technical implementation is at the discretion of the bidders. All relevant legal and regulatory requirements must be complied with during the design, development and implementation of the AI system. In particular, the contractor must ensure that the AI system to be developed is in accordance with the requirements of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence (AI Act), insofar as it is applicable.2. Functional requirements for the system (service programme) The service to be provided must fulfil the following core functions, which must be demonstrated in a proof-of-concept (PoC) and in a subsequent prototypical application. 2.1. Data acquisition The system must be capable of capturing visual data (images or video sequences) from a mobile unit (e.g. a vehicle) in a quality suitable for AI analysis. Function: Automated and continuous capture of image material of the surrounding tree landscape. 2.2. AI algorithm for image evaluation The core of the application is an AI algorithm that performs an automated analysis of the captured image data. Function: Automatic detection, classification and spatial localisation (positioning) of dead branches. Requirement: The algorithm must achieve a defined minimum hit rate and reliability under various environmental conditions (daylight, shadows, weather). The results must be clearly assignable and traceable. 2.3. Frontend application (user interface) The system must provide a user-friendly interface for displaying and managing the analysis results. Function: Graphical processing of the AI results for practical use. Requirement: The frontend must enable a clear display of the detected dead branches on a map. In addition, the frontend must contain functions for validation, commenting and approval of the results by the user. 2.4. Data management and interfaces Requirement: A self-sufficient system must be offered which enables data entry and data integration and whose results can be viewed. Integration into existing IT systems of Autobahn GmbH is not intended and is not required. The AI system will be operated entirely by the contractor. The contractor must provide the data and analysis results generated during the provision of the service in electronic form. Formats must be used that are both readable by the contracting authority and machine-processable. Further technical interfaces or system connections are not part of the service to be provided. 3. Non-functional requirements Beyond the functions mentioned, the following qualities of the system are important: Scalability: The system must be designed in such a way that it can be expanded to larger data volumes and further areas of application if required. IT security: The entire architecture and data processing must comply with current IT security standards, particularly with regard to the protection of data and systems in critical infrastructure. Maintainability: The system should be designed so that it can be easily maintained and further developed. The usage rights for the developed software (AI) remain exclusively with Autobahn GmbH des Bundes. 4. Project result Proof of functionality (PoC): After the first phase, a functional proof (PoC) must be provided that demonstrates the feasibility of the AI-based detection. Prototypical application: The final result is a fully functional, prototypical application that meets all the functional and non-functional requirements mentioned above and can be tested in practice. Note: The decision regarding the specific technical implementation (e.g. programming languages used, specific AI frameworks, etc.) is left to the bidders. The decisive factor is the fulfilment of the described functions and objectives. The contract duration is 24 months from the start of the contract. Within this period, the AI system must be fully developed and provided. The data deliveries in accordance with section 2.4 must also be provided regularly within this period.
sig_c766e67fd02e97d3b9a6.title: AI-based detection of dead branches

sig_c7ae57afa624c3022150.description: As part of the "C-Roads" project (CRG-3), a replacement for the analogue-radio-based public transport priority system for motor omnibuses is to be tested. Unlike the predecessor project "LOGIN" (Optimal traffic signal control in local public transport), in which a proof of concept for C-ITS-based public transport priority could be provided with the participation of various research partners, C-Roads relies on production-ready hardware available on the market. In addition, integration into the existing ITCS/control system of IVU Traffic Technologies AG (IVU) is to take place, for example for the visualisation of signal timing forecasts. ÜSTRA has applied for grants for this from the European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA), which were approved by a grant notification dated 16 October 2024. Partial financing was approved. ÜSTRA aims to utilise these grants. ÜSTRA therefore expects the tendered services to be completed on schedule. The subject of the tendered service is the delivery and functional provision of an on-board C-ITS-based public transport priority system, which includes all services for an integrated system. This includes, among other things, the delivery and installation of C-ITS OBUs, antennas, and the integration between these components up to the interface to the ITCS on-board computer. sig_c7f0b7c8993ae6e8b586.description: This is not a procurement notice or a call for tenders, but an information request/market survey with which Kaarinan kaupunki and the Municipality of Lieto (hereinafter the contracting authorities) are surveying the market for the procurement of capacity services. The purpose is to survey the operators in the market and to gather comments from suppliers. The objective is to obtain comprehensive information to support the implementation of the future procurement. Both the Municipality of Kaarina and the Municipality of Lieto aim to tender server capacity services as an open procedure due to an expiring agreement. The estimated commencement date of the agreements is September-October 2026. Description of the information request and invitation to market dialogue. Kaarinan kaupunki and the Municipality of Lieto are organising a joint market survey for the procurement of scalable and modern capacity services that meet certified security requirements (physical and information security): Katakri, ISO27001 or equivalent. Suppliers are requested to respond in writing to the questions concerning the procurement and to state their interest in participating in the market dialogue. Kaarinan kaupunki and the Municipality of Lieto produce their own basic IT services and also maintain their own servers. REGISTRATION Suppliers must respond to the questions in the information request and state their interest in participating in the market dialogue by Fri 6.2.2026 at 12.00 in the supplier service at https://kaarina.toimittajapalvelu.fi/. The contracting authorities will treat the responses confidentially. Based on the responses to the information request, the contracting authorities will continue the market survey with separate market dialogues. The market dialogues will be implemented as Teams discussion sessions between the Municipality of Kaarina, the Municipality of Lieto, and the supplier. The discussion sessions will be held with a maximum of six (6) suppliers. If there are more than six (6) companies registered for the market dialogue, the contracting authorities will select the most suitable suppliers for the dialogue based on their own criteria. The dialogues are intended to be implemented during February 2026. Any additional information concerning the discussions will be provided to the operators heard after registration. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION ABOUT THE NOTICE This notice is an information request for a market survey and dialogues. This notice does not request tenders. The descriptions presented in this notice are preliminary and indicative advance information on the procurement. The information request does not oblige the implementation of the procurement in the manner described in the information request. The contracting authority is not obliged to take into account the responses received to the information request when drawing up the call for tenders. Please note that all material is intended solely for the information request and the conduct of market dialogues. The market dialogues do not bind the contracting authorities to implement the procurement, nor do they bind the supplier to participate in a potential tendering procedure. Participating companies will not be paid compensation for responding or participating. Responding or failing to respond to the information request does not affect the tenderer's position in the actual tendering procedure. SCHEDULE The preliminary schedule plan aiming for the commissioning of the solution is as follows: - Invitation to participate in the market survey, January 2026 - Submission of market survey responses, February 2026 - Selection of suppliers for the market survey discussion, February 2026 - Market survey discussions, February 2026 - Publication of the call for tenders, March 2026 - Submission of tenders, March-April 2026 - Selection of solution, April 2026 - Contract negotiations, April-May 2026 - Service transfer and start-up project May-September 2026 - Production readiness September-October 2026

The solution will be used by Bus Service Operators to effectively monitor and manage Bus fleet related operations in real time as well as Passenger Information and Communication throughout Northern Ireland. Translink require the system to be capable of interfacing with on-street and on-board non-proprietary hardware through RTIG-T047 protocol, ensuring the provision of RTPI on existing Metro, Glider, and Ulsterbus services continues without interruption. Additionally, suppliers will be required to provide all necessary maintenance services. Before embarking on a tender process, we wish to engage with the marketplace to gather information which will be used to inform the sourcing strategy for this contract and thus, the procurement process. We are therefore seeking to engage with experienced Real Time Passenger Information and associated providers, which are capable of fulfilling the requirements listed above. It is anticipated that this contract will commence Q2 2027. Our requirements include, but are not limited to the following: · An open data approach to enable integration to ensure interoperability with other client systems to enhance data flow and automate manual processes. · Integrate with future systems and journey planners. · Provide comprehensive maintenance services for on-street and on-board hardware. · Ensure minimal quantity and frequency of faults and maintain the serviceability of the system. · Fleet Management & Live Vehicle Tracking. · Provide a predictive analysis solution that can support decision-making for control room staff · Driver Interface & Public Address system for Glider. · Performance and Management Reporting. · Provide drivers with intelligence on service performance and communication options. · Provide accurate and timely information about bus arrivals and departures at stops. · Provide on street display content management services. · Facilitate automated audio-visual next stop announcements on vehicles, configurable to multiple languages and tailored branded graphics. · Improve disruption management including passenger messaging. · Support future methods for providing information to passengers. · Implement a solution compatible with RTIG national standards for Traffic Signal Priority.
