sig_c8d22111a723f678e697.description: HUS is planning the procurement of a modern work ability management system. This is a request for information published for the purpose of market research, the aim of which is to gather information from suppliers regarding ready-made solutions currently in production, their functionalities, technical features and service models. The request for information does not initiate an actual tendering procedure or bind the contracting authority to carry out the procurement. HUS is Finland's largest healthcare operator, employing approximately 27 000 professionals and approximately 1 300 managers, and is responsible for specialised medical care across a wide region. The objective of the procurement is a comprehensive solution that supports HUS's work ability management processes, improves data-driven management and standardises operating models. The system is expected to have the capability to gather scattered work ability data together, support early-support operating models, prevent work ability risks through automatic alarms, and provide real-time analytics for various levels of the organisation. The subject of the procurement is a work ability management system delivered as a SaaS service, which is in use in large organisations. The procurement includes the planning and implementation of the deployment project, necessary integrations, expert work, and annual maintenance, support and minor development services. The request for information includes an appendix with a more detailed description of the procurement. Please submit responses to the request for information and express your interest in participating in the market dialogue no later than 19.4.2026 at 12.00 to kilpailutus.ict@hus.fi. Please mark the subject of the message as: "HUS 137‐2026 Procurement of a work ability management system." Based on the request for information, HUS will invite selected suppliers to system demos, which will be held in May–June 2026.
sig_c8d22111a723f678e697.title: HUS 137-2026 Procurement of a work ability management system

sig_c8d8a5a5f2c5bab2ebbc.description: Spark DPS Buy emerging technology products and services, including Internet of Things (IoT), AI and automation, simulated environments, wearables and new improvements in security. Description Spark: the Technology Innovation Marketplace can help government and public sector to access new and emerging technology products. This dynamic purchasing system (DPS) uses a filter system that helps customers find suppliers. The filter system includes defined technology areas developed with customer input. It focuses on emerging technologies predicted to have the largest impact over the next 2 to 5 years. There are 8 technology areas you can filter by: Internet of Things (IoT) Artificial Intelligence (AI) and automation Simulated and enhanced environments Engineering/materials science Data Wearables Transport Security Each of these areas contains between 3 and 17 sub-categories. The DPS filters help customers to identify and shortlist suppliers. The 2 main filters are: problem area technology type You can also filter by: location security classification Suppliers can apply to join the marketplace at any time, and identify their areas of expertise as part of the application process. Successful suppliers need to demonstrate their ability to offer suitably innovative products that meet either of the following 2 definitions: radical innovation: offering a new product, service, process or strategy introduced into a market designed to make a significant impact by completely replacing existing technologies and methods for example, streaming services replacing video rental stores disruptive innovation: creates a new market and value network and eventually disrupts an existing market and value network displacing established market-leading firms, products and alliances for example, light emitting diodes (LEDs) replacing traditional light bulbs As well as their ability to provide innovative products, the supplier’s contract example needs to explain the benefits for the end user and must be approved and confirmed by the customer. Once an application is complete, it can take can take up to a maximum of 15 working days to assess and appoint a supplier to the marketplace. A downloadable copy of the bid pack is available on the supplier registration service . Benefits access to proven technology innovation to solve public sector problems agility and flexibility to meet the public sector’s changing technology needs this agreement has no lots, use the filter system to produce a list of potential suppliers based on your needs quality and price assessment filtered to an individual customer’s requirements an efficient tender process and approach to finding potential solutions, including the option of using a 2 stage competition process and supplier presentations can be used for any size project, there is no minimum or maximum value Products and suppliers Please read the 'How to buy' tab below for detailed instructions on how to find out which suppliers are on this agreement. Lot 1: Spark DPS Expires: 15/02/2029 How to buy Make sure you have received budget approval and have read the RM6094 Spark customer guidance before using this agreement. The following instructions are for conducting a simple call for competition without use of: pre-tender market engagement (PTME) capability assessment presentation These are all also possible under the RM6094 Spark DPS. These terms are explained in the customer guide. Register as a buyer on the Dynamic Purchasing System Marketplace. note: although pages are headed ‘Supplier registration’ this is also where you can register as a buyer Go to the RM6094 Spark DPS under Technology and choose the “access as a buyer” option and confirm your acceptance of the customer access agreement. On your “manage your DPS category exports” page you now have 2 options: view appointed suppliers. click on the link to create a new category export. This is how you filter the suppliers that can meet your requirements When creating a new category use the filtering tool (select all that apply) to specify your requirements and create your supplier shortlist. Save your filtered list of capable suppliers by clicking the “save category” option and give the shortlist a unique name specific to your competition. From your “manage your category exports” page, export the list of suppliers and contact details. Export is to an Excel spreadsheet. Quit the DPS. Use the list to run a further competition. Invite the suppliers identified by the DPS to bid against your detailed specification, evaluation criteria and contract format. the list is valid for only 2 working days, from the date of its creation, because new suppliers may apply to join at any point if your call for competition excludes eligible suppliers it potentially breaches procurement regulations. You will need to get a fresh supplier list (steps 3.2 to 5) if you do not use your list within 2 working days by clicking the “search again” option for your export use our eSourcing tool to run a call for competition the tool is free to use for public sector buyers, or you can use your organisation’s own procurement tool Your tender process should align with the value and complexity of your requirement. Suppliers will need a reasonable period of time to review and prepare a response. This includes allowing enough time for suppliers to ask clarification questions and consider your answers before the deadline for written responses. Evaluate the responses. Request from winning supplier(s) any required evidence that they can meet your requirements. Set a deadline for submitting evidence for 2 days. If you are satisfied with the evidence, award the contract. Where appropriate, notify of the award on Contracts Finder . Explanation of terms: Pre- tender market engagement (PTME) This is optional but recommended and allows you to communicate with suppliers ahead of issuing your final specification to ensure that the market has a clear understanding of your requirements. It also allows you to: shape your specification gather ideas on new innovations understand if there are any changes within the market that may influence your requirements This exercise is not about refining your shortlist. You must provide an outline of your specification and you can ask suppliers specific questions regarding your requirements and specification and for feedback. Capability assessment This is optional but recommended and helps you to identify which suppliers from your shortlist are going to be most suitable. It can be used to refine your shortlist or to assess if any suppliers are capable of meeting your requirement. You can use a series of yes and no questions that suppliers must pass to get to the written stage. Face to face presentation This is also optional. It happens after the evaluation of the written proposals. It is an opportunity for face to face dialogue with the suppliers who were successful in reaching this stage. Suppliers can present more detailed proposals and answer any specific questions you may have regarding their written response. All contract documents remain valid for existing and new contracts, and there are no changes to how you work with us. sig_c90d560f6a5febac5f2d.description: The Environmental Health team of the Care Department is responsible for the preparation, implementation and substantiation of preventive health policy regarding environmental health in Flanders. Environmental health is the component of preventive health policy that focuses on the prevention, early detection and intervention of environmental health damage through a multidisciplinary approach involving at least the scientific disciplines of medicine, toxicology, epidemiology, healthcare, environmental technology and environmental science. Within the Flemish Medical Environmental Health Network (VMMN), the team collaborates with various authorities, knowledge institutions and partner organisations for this purpose. The core activities of the team include climate and health, risk analysis, the promotion of a healthy public space, environmental health focus areas, recreational and drinking water quality, indoor environment, nature and health, and soil and health. Analyses are carried out to assess the environment-related health impact, and advice is formulated on environmental health aspects. However, the knowledge landscape within medical environmental science is growing extremely rapidly. New scientific insights, technological developments, changing regulations and international societal developments ensure a continuous stream of information. The systematic monitoring, assessment and application of this knowledge is currently largely manual and requires considerable staffing efforts. This increases the risk of knowledge gaps, while the Care Department is expected to base advice, policy decisions and health impact analyses on the most up-to-date and reliable insights. To address this challenge, the Care Department wishes to develop an AI-mediated knowledge surveillance system. This system must automatically detect, process, structure and make relevant information from internal and external sources accessible to policy officers and experts. The solution supports the monitoring of scientific literature, policy documents, reports, regulations and other knowledge sources, translating them into usable document fact sheets and syntheses. The system focuses on the four central storylines within Environmental Health: Substances of Very High Concern, Climate and Health, Healthy Public Space, and One Health. Knowledge is organised according to the source-exposure-burden-effect chain (SEBE), allowing users to find and apply relevant insights more quickly in dossiers, risk analyses, policy preparation and advice. These initiatives have their legal basis in the Prevention Decree, the Decree on General Provisions of Environmental Policy regarding environmental hygiene aspects, and the EIA Decree, and are deployed in accordance with the prioritisation of the Environmental Health health objective and the climate health plan. The intended solution supports human expertise but does not replace it. Interpretation, validation and policy-related explanation always remain the responsibility of substantive experts. Therefore, a human-in-the-loop approach is chosen, whereby AI-generated output is supplemented with quality controls and human validation. Furthermore, the solution must comply with applicable requirements regarding privacy, information security, AI governance and regulations, including the GDPR and the EU AI Act. It must connect to the Microsoft and Windows environment of the Care Department and be aligned with the Policy Information and Data (BID) and Communication and IT (CIT) departments, creating a secure, scalable and sustainably manageable solution that can also be applied in other teams within the Care Department.
sig_c90d560f6a5febac5f2d.title: Development of an AI-mediated knowledge surveillance system for environmental health

sig_c979f2eadc8687b2e9fb.description: THIS INFORMATION REQUEST IS AN INVITATION TO AN INFORMATION MEETING REGARDING THE PROCUREMENT OF PTT SERVICES. ICT service production for the City of Jyväskylä has been reorganised in recent years so that the operational production of basic IT services has been largely outsourced. The upcoming procurement will ensure that the service package meets the city's current and developing needs and supports efficient, secure and reliable everyday operations throughout the organisation. Basic IT services are currently produced for the City of Jyväskylä as the following service packages: - User and support services (Service Desk, remote and on-site support, Helppari) - Workstation, device and lifecycle services - ICT environment management and operation - Server monitoring and operating services at the operating system level - Communications SPOC, terminal connection and support services. - Cyber security services (technical information security and incident management) - Service management and production management (ITSM system and system integration between the Supplier and the Customer, SLA, change management) The aim of the upcoming procurement is to reorganise the services so that the service level and user experience are consistent and predictable, service production is transparently managed and measurable, and the package supports the city's operations in a cost-effective manner. The aim is also to strengthen proactiveness and continuous development and ensure that the services take into account the special characteristics of the administrative network and educational network. The current state and objectives described above serve as the starting point for the service areas and requirements defined in more detail in the upcoming invitation to tender.
sig_c979f2eadc8687b2e9fb.title: Invitation to an information meeting on the procurement of basic IT services (PTT services)

sig_c9dd452cedae825acc43.description: This procurement process is being advertised and run by First Greater Western limited on its own behalf and on behalf of the successor operator of the rail passenger transport services in respect of Great Western Railway (GWR). That successor operator will be a public sector company, is expected to be a wholly owned subsidiary of DfT OLR Holdings Limited and will be ultimately owned by the Secretary of State for Transport. The date for transfer of the current operations to the successor operator is not yet confirmed. Where the transfer is completed before contract award under this procurement process, the successor operator may elect (but will not be obliged) to carry on with this procurement process in place of GWR, by taking on the role of contracting entity from the date of completion of the transfer (with this notice and all other procurement documents to be interpreted accordingly). Where the transfer is not yet completed by the time of contract award, contractual rights may be included in the contractual arrangements to enable transfer to the successor operator. Bidders should note that this procurement process (if ongoing), or any awarded contract, may be included in a transfer scheme made by the Secretary of State under section 12 of the Railways Act 2005, or the transfer may be effected outside of, or separate from, such a scheme. If transfer takes place before the contract award the successor operator shall assume all the rights of the Client set out in this document. All references to the Client shall be deemed to refer to the successor operator for the purposes of this procurement and the successor operator shall be entitled to continue or terminate this procurement as if it was involved. This Preliminary Market Engagement will help GWR understand capability in the market and lead to GWR procuring and implementing a new integrated Time & Attendance (T&A) solution that meets GWR's operational, HR, safety, payroll, and organisational requirements. The overall objective of the procurement is to provide GWR a modern, integrated T&A capability with standardised processes, clear governance, seamless system integration, and improved workforce reporting and analytics. GWR currently operates 3 different Time and Attendance systems in different business areas. Proposed system Capabilities must include: o Rostering & scheduling o Time capture (mobile, geofencing, clock-in/out) o Leave & absence management o Fatigue management & compliance o Workflow automation (approvals) Lot 1: .

sig_c9e697a6cb69b664217d.description: **UPDATE 5 APRIL 2024: The proposal submission date has been updated to 24 April 2024. The FOA has been amended to reflect this submission date and include a Question and Answer document based on questions received from interested applicants. Other than the updated proposal submission date in the FOA, the actual FOA Amendment has not been changed. However, the answers provided in the Q&A document are considered part of the FOA Amendment.** **CYCLE 2 UPDATE 20 MARCH 2024 - THE OPPORTUNITY WEBINAR FOR CYCLE 2 WILL BE HELD ONLINE VIA MS TEAMS AT 1500 EDT ON 22 MARCH 2024 AT THE FOLLOWING LINK: https://dod.teams.microsoft.us/l/meetup-join/19%3adod%3ameeting_5fa41fe6fa874484b473d8a6ba7921c6%40thread.v2/0?context=%7b%22Tid%22%3a%22fae6d70f-954b-4811-92b6-0530d6f84c43%22%2c%22Oid%22%3a%22e9f6fc39-8f22-44e5-8bd0-64f0cde32305%22%2c%22IsBroadcastMeeting%22%3atrue%7d **UPDATE 14 MARCH 2024 - CYCLE 2 HAS BEEN POSTED TO THE ANNOUNCEMENT. PLEASE REVIEW THE UPDATED ANNOUNCEMENT IN FULL FOR SUBMISSION TIME, UPDATED TOPIC, AND FUNDING AMOUNT AND SCHEDULE CHANGES FROM CYCLE 1** TACTICAL BEHAVIORS FOR AUTONOMOUS MANEUVER COLLABORATIVE RESEARCH PROGRAM (TBAM-CRP) Future Army forces will be called upon to operate and maneuver in multi-domain operations (MDO), against a modern and capable peer adversary. The battlefield of the future may impose additional constraints on maneuver forces such as disruption in communication as well as positioning services. To field a highly capable fighting force in this future battlefield, novel tactics and doctrines leveraging nascent technologies in robotics and autonomous systems (RAS) will need to be developed. Teams of RAS will serve an increasingly critical role in the future force to deliver situational awareness, defend key locations or positions, or take point in dynamic and hazardous situations. Resilience to disruptions, failures, or unexpected scenarios, is a key quality for teams of RAS to operate alongside other future Army forces. The US Army Combat Capabilities Development Command (DEVCOM) Army Research Laboratory (ARL) is focused on developing fundamental understanding and informing the art-of-the-possible for warfighter concepts through research to greatly improve the scope of mission capabilities of teams of RAS, develop robust and resilient approaches to plan under extreme conditions of uncertainty, to learn coordinated strategies for groups of agents to achieve a common objective, all within a complex maneuver environment including adversaries. The Tactical Behaviors for Autonomous Maneuver Collaborative Research Program (TBAM-CRP) is focused on developing and experimentally evaluating coordinated and individual behaviors for small groups of autonomous agents to learn doctrinal as well as novel tactics for maneuvering in military relevant environments. The TBAM-CRP will leverage developments in other internal and extramural programs as well as identify new research directions to find novel solutions to these maneuver problems in analogical simulations representing complex realistic terrain. The Tactical Behaviors for Autonomous Maneuver Collaborative Research Program (TBAM-CRP) will consist of a series of sprint efforts executed with annual program reviews. Each topic will be focused on addressing a different set of scientific areas which will support the research aims of an associated ARL researcher from a related internal essential research program (ERP) or mission-funded program. The TBAM-CRP has been developed in coordination with other related ARL-funded collaborative efforts (see descriptions of ARL collaborative alliances at https://www.arl.army.mil/business/collaborativealliances/) and shares a common vision of highly collaborative academia-industry-government partnerships; however, it will be executed with a program model adapted from the Scalable, Adaptive, and Resilient Autonomy (SARA), which established a new paradigm for collaborative research. Some key properties of this new approach are described below: • TBAM-CRP sprint topics will be offered on a two-year cycle. Proposals will be solicited for a possible two-year period structured as a first-year pilot followed by a second-year option where the option may be awarded based upon progress assessed at an annual review. The FOA will be amended annually to identify a specific problem statement and scope for that specific cycle. The topics for each cycle will be chosen to address the long-term program goal. • Five new topics (Cycles 1-5) are expected in FY22, 24, 26, 28, 30. Each topic will be carefully chosen based on the previous accomplishments in the prior cycle(s), the development of new technologies and capabilities in the broader research and development communities, and the Army’s evolving needs for future capabilities. • For each topic, funding will be provided to those Recipients selected under a cooperative agreement (CA). • Enhanced Research Program funding from ARL or Other Government Agencies (OGAs) may become available during a cycle which provides a mechanism for growth and enhancement within the TBAM-CRP. A proposal should not include any discussion of the Enhanced Research Program. Recipients receiving a CA will be notified and provided details if the opportunity for Enhanced Research Program funding becomes available during their award period of performance. • There is no limitation on the place of performance, although on-site collaboration at ARL facilities and with ARL researchers as well as with other Recipients are encouraged. Research outcomes in this program must, at the very least, be demonstrated in sophisticated simulations of relevant environments. Together with ARL collaborators, these results may be adapted for higher TRL experimentation on surrogate platforms at ARL test facilities such as the Robotics Research Collaboration Campus (R2C2) at Graces Quarters, Aberdeen Proving Ground, Maryland. • Recipients will be furnished with access to the ARL Autonomy Stack software suite as well as all relevant simulation tools and multi-agent learning support. • Recipients will be provided with information about the current state of the Autonomous Systems Enterprise (ASE) with an overview of developments in the associated collaborative research alliances including Distributed and Collaborative Intelligent Systems and Technology (DCIST), Scalable, Adaptive, and Resilient Autonomy (SARA), as well as internal ARL essential research programs including the AI for Maneuver and Mobility (AIMM), Emerging Overmatch Technologies (EOT), and Versatile Tactical Power and Propulsion (VICTOR). Capabilities demonstrated in simulation should reflect significant appropriate developments. This midpoint review is expected to take place as a mini symposium where Recipients can share results with one another along with the ARL community to foster further collaboration. • At the end of the second year, a capstone demonstration will be executed by those Recipients receiving an option to their award in a set of simulated relevant environments, either those environment scenarios provided by the Government and other program performers, or optionally of a specific environment developed by the Recipient to exhibit their developed capability. Any system level capability demonstration that can be made with the internal ARL collaborator or description of capability development and program contribution can also be made at this time. These system demonstrations are expected to coincide to foster further integration and adoption with related internal research programs as well as partner organizations from within the DEVCOM, other Army and DoD service branches and agencies, in addition to other government agencies. Proposals that follow the requirements of the FOA will be evaluated in accordance with merit-based, competitive procedures. These procedures will include evaluation factors and an adjectival and color rating system. A review team, consisting of a qualified group of Government scientists and managers will evaluate the compliant proposals and provide the results of that evaluation to the decision-maker for the Government. Relevant internal research program materials approved for public release and contact information will be provided to potential proposers during introductory presentations to help facilitate identification of collaboration between proposers and individual ARL researchers or internal research programs. Additional connections to ARL programs can be identified during the proposal review process. Eligible applicants under this FOA include institutions of higher education, nonprofit organizations, and for-profit organizations (i.e., large and small businesses) for scientific research in the knowledge domains outlined throughout this Funding Opportunity. Federally Funded Research and Development Centers (FFRDC) may propose as well, with effort as allowed by their sponsoring agency and in accordance with their sponsoring agency policy.
sig_c9e697a6cb69b664217d.title: Tactical Behaviors for Autonomous Maneuver

sig_ca777df15499f5642027.description: THIS IS NOT A CONTRACT NOTICE OR CALL FOR TENDERS BUT AN INFORMATION REQUEST FOR MARKET CONSULTATION AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE: This information request is used to survey the market and obtain information regarding the procurement. The contracting authority will not initiate a tendering procedure by publishing the information request, but a potential contract notice and call for tenders will be published later. The information request does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. Answering the information request is not a prerequisite for participation in a possible subsequent tendering procedure. Suppliers will not be paid compensation for responding to the information request or participating in the market dialogue. The responses given to this information request will be used in planning the procurement of overall services related to the maintenance and operation of HUS's internal network, the "HUSnet network". HUS-yhtymä's IT Management is planning to renew the comprehensive service agreement for the HUSnet network. The computer network is a critical part of HUS-yhtymä's operations and includes a wide infrastructure of approx. 250 sites in the Uusimaa region as well as connections to cloud services. The equipment base consists of, among other things: - approx. 3 000 L2/L3 switches - approx. 10 000 WLAN access points - firewall environments - peripheral systems. The purpose of the information request and market dialogue is to survey various solution alternatives with which HUS-yhtymä's network environment can be maintained and developed, taking into account potential future requirements. Market dialogues will be held during February-March as in-person or Teams meetings. Service providers are requested to register by 11.2.2026 at kilpailutus.ict@hus.fi. Subject of the message: "HUS 580-2025/HUSnet services". In their responses, service providers are hoped to present their key service descriptions related to, among other things, network management, maintenance and development. In addition, presentations of reference implementations are desired. Advance material speeds up the dialogue held in the meeting. When proceeding to the procurement phase, suppliers who have responded to the information request may receive preliminary tender documents for comment.

sig_cac4bdc488bf635375e4.description: As previously announced, we are reaching out to gather information from the market in preparation for the upcoming Framework Agreement for SI services. sig_cbb9280876598968a99b.description: This notice serves exclusively to conduct a non-binding market consultation in accordance with section 28 paragraph 1 of the Ordinance on Public Procurement (VgV). The aim of the market consultation is to inform the market at an early stage about a potential future procurement requirement and to gather insights on technical, economic and organisational solution approaches, current market conditions, the competitive situation and the fundamental feasibility of the planned project. In particular, the market consultation serves to identify advantages and disadvantages of potential performance components, to record existing market experience and to examine whether and to what extent multiple companies can offer comparable services. In this way, a well-founded overview of market interest and the current competitive situation is to be obtained. The present notice is expressly neither a contract notice nor an invitation to submit tenders or requests to participate. No procurement procedure is initiated by conducting the market consultation. The contracting authority is not obliged to conduct a procurement procedure on the basis of the market consultation and is not bound by its results. Participation does not establish any legal claims whatsoever, in particular no claim to the conduct of a procurement procedure or to consideration in any potential subsequent procurement procedure. Participation in the market consultation is voluntary and free of charge. Participating companies will not be reimbursed for any costs incurred by them in connection with participation, the preparation of statements, concepts or the submission of documents. Participation in the market consultation is not a prerequisite for later participation in a procurement procedure and has no influence on a company's chances of being awarded the contract. The contracting authority requests interested market participants to provide meaningful, comprehensible and advanced feedback. In particular, comments on possible implementation variants, economic framework conditions, opportunities and risks, potential problems or obstacles in implementing the intended concept, as well as own ideas and suggestions for improvement are requested. Where possible, feedback should be provided in a structured format. Interested companies are requested to express their interest immediately and informally by email to ta-vergabestellevol@hu-berlin.de and to submit their statements, ideas, proposals for implementation and economic assessments. Following the evaluation of the submitted documents, selected interested parties may be invited to explain their concepts in more detail as part of a structured dialogue. This deepening can take place in the form of an on-site appointment or alternatively via video or telephone conference and serves to clarify open questions and to evaluate the impact of the proposed solution approaches on the requirements of the contracting authority. All documents submitted as part of the market consultation shall become the property of the contracting authority. By participating, interested parties agree that their submitted concepts, evaluations, proposals and other findings may be used to prepare a potential procurement and to develop implementation proposals and, to the extent necessary, may be passed on to the contracting authority, unless this is expressly objected to. Ideas and suggestions from market participants may, where applicable in anonymised form, become part of a later specification of requirements. The contracting authority guarantees the protection of business and trade secrets. Information obtained as part of the market consultation will not be passed on to third parties, with the exception of the contracting authority itself and, where applicable, consulting firms commissioned by it. The market consultation is to be carried out promptly and is expected to be concluded by February 2026. All submitted feedback will be evaluated and made available to the contracting authority in a consolidated form. Should the contracting authority initiate a procurement procedure based on the results of the market consultation, it will take appropriate measures to exclude any distortion of competition. These include in particular the equal treatment of all interested companies, the provision of relevant information to all applicants and tenderers, and the setting of appropriate deadlines. Anticipated schedule • Expression of interest to participate: immediately • Submission of initial concept: 30.01.2026 at 12.00 hours • Presentations and interviews: February 2026

sig_cc2a89a7cc9fd496b5e0.description: The Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) intends to procure commercial satellite-derived Earth Observation (EO) data and associated Earth Observation services for use across the UK public sector. The procurement will support improved access to commercial EO capabilities, reduce duplicated procurement activity, enable greater sharing and reuse of data across government, and support evidence-based decision making across a range of public sector activities. The procurement has been designed following extensive engagement with public sector users and suppliers and reflects the Authority’s objective of establishing a more coordinated approach to the acquisition and use of commercial EO data and services. The procurement will comprise two Lots: Lot 1 – Core Commercial Earth Observation Data A contract for the supply and licensing of core commercial optical satellite-derived Earth Observation data for use across the UK public sector. The successful supplier will provide data, associated rights, metadata, quality assurance information and supporting services required to support delivery through an access model. Lot 2 – Specialist Earth Observation Services A single-supplier call-off contract for specialist Earth Observation data products, monitoring services and analytical capabilities. Anticipated demand does not constitute guaranteed expenditure or supplier revenue. The procurement will be conducted using a Competitive Flexible Procedure through the Government Commercial Agency Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market (RM6370). The Authority intends to award one contract under each Lot. Contracts are expected to be awarded for an initial period of three years with an option to extend for up to one additional year. The procurement is expected to support public sector use cases including environmental monitoring, infrastructure management, climate resilience, emergency response, agricultural monitoring, rural payments, land management and wider policy development. It has been structured to support both established suppliers and specialist providers, including SMEs, consortia and supply chain arrangements where appropriate. The information in this notice remains subject to final decision-making and suppliers should refer to the Tender documentation once published for final details. Dynamic Market Participation Participation in the procurement will be limited to suppliers admitted to the CCS Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market (RM6370). Suppliers who are not currently members of the Dynamic Market are encouraged to apply for admission as soon as possible. As the Dynamic Market remains open throughout its lifetime, suppliers may seek admission at any stage prior to the procurement closing date. The Authority wishes to maximise competition and encourages all capable suppliers to register. Supplier registration: CCS Space Technology Solutions Dynamic Market (RM6370) The Authority recommends that suppliers allow sufficient time to complete the Dynamic Market admission process before the tender submission deadline. Lot 1: Core Commercial Data. Lot 1 covers the supply and licensing of core commercial optical EO data for use across the UK public sector. The scope of Lot 1 may include: • Current commercial optical EO data products. • Historic imagery to support temporal analysis, seasonal comparison and change detection. • Associated metadata and quality assurance information. • Licensing rights and permissions required to support public sector access and use. Data delivery, integration support and associated technical services required to support the Authority's intended delivery model. Lot 2: Specialist EO data products, monitoring services and analytical capabilities. Lot 2 - eligible UK public sector organisations may procure specialist EO data products, monitoring services and analytical capabilities from the awarded supplier via call-off. The scope of Lot 2 may include: • Routine monitoring data services • Higher resolution and tasked data services • Historic and archive data services • Analytics and monitoring services • Validation and decision-support services • Field evidence collection services • Data access, hosting and delivery services associated with specialist EO products and services • Implementation, training and user support services required to support operational use The Lot 2 contract will not create a commitment by the Authority or any User to place a Call-Off Order.
sig_cc2a89a7cc9fd496b5e0.title: Earth Observation: Data Products and Services for the UK Public Sector 'Public Sector EO'

Specific Objective I – ESTABLISHMENT OF A PRODUCTION UNIT FOR ENERGY FROM RENEWABLE SOURCES, RESPECTIVELY SOLAR SOURCES The objective targets the acquisition of technological equipment with and without assembly, respectively works, with the aim of establishing a production unit for energy from solar sources. The specific objective envisages the execution of specific works for the operationalisation of a renewable energy production unit to be characterised by the following functional parameters: - Newly installed capacity for producing energy from renewable sources: 3.961,44 kWp / 3.900 kW AC; - Net production of primary energy of 391,16 toe/year from renewable sources; - Total net electricity production of 86.623,20 MWh over a period of 20 years; The specific objective is correlated with the indicators assumed through the Financing Application, contributing to ensuring a significant share of the electricity requirement of the Municipality of Bistrița from renewable sources, namely solar sources. Specific Objective II – REDUCTION OF CARBON FOOTPRINT AND PROMOTION OF THE USE OF ENERGY FROM RENEWABLE SOURCES The specific objective envisages reducing the carbon footprint of the Municipality of Bistrița by reducing greenhouse gas emissions resulting from the production of energy necessary for carrying out its own activity. To this end, the implementation of the investment project contributes to reducing greenhouse gases by 53.004,74 tonnes of CO2 equivalent over a period of 20 years (considering a conversion factor of 0,6119 tonnes of CO2 equivalent/MWh). Also, the specific objective envisages promoting the use of energy from renewable sources, the implementation of the investment project contributing to ensuring self-consumption from renewable sources to the detriment of using energy originating from greenhouse gas emission-generating sources. The specific objective targets the use in a percentage of 100% of the electricity produced at the level of the photovoltaic power plant for the self-consumption of the Municipality of Bistrița. The project “Sărata Photovoltaic Panel Park ” will be carried out on a plot of land located in the extra-muros area of the municipality of Bistrița on an area of 47.593 sqm identified with cadastral number 93614, in the pasture category.

In addition to CEED, the ADAPT consortium will include separately funded CBPR projects, which will receive consultative services from the NIH Community Engagement Alliance Consultative Resource (CEACR) and join in the Science Collaborative for Health and Artificial Intelligence Reduction of Errors (SCHARE) platform for the overarching goal of promoting data use and transformational community engagement to optimize oral health for all people. sig_cde81e0fd0ae0a773c8a.description: Micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) constitute the overwhelming majority of economic activity in Jordan. MSMEs account for over 99% of all enterprises, employ around 60% of the formal private-sector workforce, and contribute 40% of Jordan Gross Domestic Product (GDP), making them crucial for economic growth, resilience, and job creation. Despite this importance, MSMEs still face obstacles in accessing appropriate and diversified financial products. Access to formal credit remains limited for many MSMEs. According to the Central Bank of Jordan (CBJ) National Financial Inclusion Strategy (NFIS) 2023-2028, only 28.3% of formal MSMEs had a loan or line of credit from a financial institution, highlighting a significant financing gap for smaller firms in Jordan. Financial exclusion is especially pronounced for underserved segments such as informal and women-led enterprises, which often face higher collateral requirements, limited credit histories, and lower formal borrowing rates. Financial inclusion, defined as access to and use of appropriate, affordable, and sustainable financial products and services, remains a priority in Jordan. The CBJ is pursuing ambitious targets to increase overall financial inclusion, reduce gender gaps, and enhance MSME access to finance, including through digital channels and tailored products. The NFIS aims, for example, to increase MSMEs access to formal lending at an average annual rate of 4% for four years. In a similar vein, Jordan"s Green Finance Strategy 2023-2028 aims to mobilize green investments and position the financial sector as a regional leader in sustainable finance. The strategy highlights that a 92.5% of the Jordan National Determined Contribution (NDC) target cost is to be financed by international support and mobilized private capital. As Jordan advances its Green Finance Strategy, a central priority was establishing clear and credible standards for what qualifies as "green" across the financial system. The Jordan National Green Taxonomy, published in February 2026, provides this clarity by offering a common language for the financial system to classify sustainable economic activities in a transparent and consistent way. By anchoring investment decisions to science-based criteria, the taxonomy helps ensure that future capital flows genuinely support Jordan"s low-carbon, climate-resilient transition. Against this backdrop, the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit GIZ-implemented project, Innovative Approaches for the Financial Inclusion of MSMEs in Jordan (I-FIN), takes a holistic, market-driven approach to strengthening inclusive green finance in the country. The project operates across the policy, institutional, and market levels, helping to improve the broader enabling environment, upgrade the technical and operational capacities of financial service providers, and ensure that enterprises can confidently access and benefit from green finance solutions. The overall objective of the project is to ensure that MSMEs in Jordan benefit from a more inclusive financial system that enables inclusive access to green finance and supports environmentally sustainable and resilient business growth, also with a focus on women-led enterprises. The assignment is structured around four interrelated work packages, 5 key experts, complemented by two pools of experts. Work Package 1: Planning and Inception: aims to review, research, and analyse all relevant information to ensure a comprehensive understanding of the assignment and to refine the implementation approach. Work Package 2: Capacity Development and Technical Assistance for Inclusive Green Credit Guarantees and Risk-Sharing Mechanisms: strengthens the staff and institutional capacities of the Jordan Loan Guarantee Corporation (JLGC) in the area of MSMEs inclusive green finance, through tailored staff capacity development and institutional advisory services across seven operational areas: product development and/or adaptation, risk documentation and/or management, strategy development, monitoring, reporting, setting up of an operational unit, and cooperation with Fintechs. Work Package 3: Capacity Development and Technical Assistance for Financial Services Providers: strengthens the institutional capacities of 5 financial services providers across the same seven operational areas and builds the capacities of at least 120 employees (50 of which are women) in the financial service sector. This work package may target public and private financial services providers, while Activity 3.7 targets financial sector associations, training providers, and academic institutions. The Contractor is expected to ensure strong coordination and alignment with a parallel complementary intervention delivering sector-level standardized training, including regular information exchange, harmonization of approaches, and avoidance of duplication. Work Package 4: Advancing Financial Service Providers' Capacity to Access and Mobilize International Climate Finance: supports financial services providers in submitting at least 3 project outlines (1 of which related to the water sector) for mobilising international climate finance in relation to MSMEs to relevant national actors, in close coordination with the CBJ, Ministry of Environment, and industry associations. All support under this assignment shall be aligned with international best practices and relevant national frameworks, including, but not limited to, the Jordan National Green Taxonomy, ensuring consistency with evolving regulatory and policy developments in the green finance landscape.
sig_cde81e0fd0ae0a773c8a.title: 10021232 - Supporting the Financial Institutions Green Transition

sig_ce1ebfc144dfc23a0d0c.buyer_original: Haaga-Helia ammattikorkeakoulu Oy; Helsingin kaupunki, Kasvatuksen ja koulutuksen toimiala; Laurea Ammattikorkeakoulu
sig_ce1ebfc144dfc23a0d0c.description: 1. Objective and subject of the procurement The subject of the procurement is the co-creation and implementation of a gamified simulation or XR-based learning solution intended for upper secondary vocational education and training in the tourism sector. The solution must also be suitable, where appropriate, for university of applied sciences teaching. The procurement is implemented as part of the European Union co-funded Immersive Learning Ecosystem IMMO project in cooperation with Haaga-Helia University of Applied Sciences, the City of Helsinki and Laurea University of Applied Sciences. The objective is to produce an experiential and working-life-oriented learning experience suitable for the immersive room of the IMMO project, by means of which students can practise knowledge, skills and situations related to tourism degree modules and working life competence needs. The solution may relate to one or more tourism competence areas. The tenderer is not required to have ready-made learning content or a ready-made XR solution at the tender stage; instead, the final contents, learning objectives and use cases of the solution will be specified in co-creation. 2. Content of the delivery The procurement comprises the entire development process from design and conceptualisation to final implementation. The delivery includes at least: - requirement and content workshops as well as conceptualisation and scripting; - three co-creation workshops; - construction of learning and demonstration materials; - implementation of development versions and iterative development; - user testing in the IMMO space and utilisation of feedback; - finalisation of the solution and measures related to commissioning; - handover of source code, editable source files, documentation and other agreed materials; and - final reporting and preparation for open publishing. Tourism students, teachers, company representatives and project experts will participate in the co-creation. The supplier is responsible for the development and test environment it requires. Contract obligations shall be performed within the EU/EEA area. The supplier has the right to carry out the design, content production, development, programming, documentation and other implementation work of the solution independently of location in a suitable location of its choice suitable for information-secure work. Working on the customer's premises is required only to the extent that separately agreed meetings, tests, approval procedures or the use of the immersive room of the IMMO project so require. The customer has no obligation to arrange workspaces for the supplier. 3. Key requirements of the solution The solution must: - be gamified in such a way that gamification is a key design principle of the solution; - enable the user's active action, decision-making or problem-solving as well as feedback on the user's choices; - enable the completion of the learning experience multiple times in alternative ways; - support joint learning, teamwork, teacher-led guidance and the simultaneous participation of multiple users; - include a pedagogically justified progression model; - enable the maintenance, development and expansion of learning contents; - meet the technical requirements of the IMMO space described in the Q/A appendix; and - operate in normal use without continuous or in-use internet connectivity. The objective is an approximately 20–30 minute learning experience. The tenderer may utilise existing technologies, game engines, XR platforms and 360-degree contents if the entity meets the requirements set in the procurement documents. 4. Implementation and schedule The supplier must implement the solution in accordance with the principles of agile and iterative development. The supplier will participate in the kick-off meeting held in November 2026 and the first co-creation workshops held in November and December. Different versions of the solution will be tested with users in the IMMO space starting in January 2027. The supplier will participate in the interim review carried out in February 2027 and finalise the solution based on user feedback. The final solution with its contents must be delivered and approved no later than 28.2.2027. 5. Price and key contract terms The fixed total price of the procurement is 35 000 euros excluding value added tax. The price includes all costs arising from the fulfilment of the obligations according to the procurement contract and its appendices. The supplier may invoice the price only when the Customer has approved the final delivery in writing. A six-month warranty is granted for the delivery. A penalty for delay defined in the contract may be charged for a delay for which the supplier is responsible. The EUPL 1.2 licence or another pre-approved compatible open source licence shall in principle apply to the customer application included in the solution and its documentation. The rights, use, modification, sharing and possible open publishing of learning materials shall be resolved on a material-specific basis. The tenderer must attach to its tender a preliminary learning material rights and publishing list and supplement it during the project. The project output must not be published without the Customer's written approval. The draft contract, JIT 2025 Customer applications open source special terms and conditions and JIT 2025 General terms and conditions shall apply to the procurement contract in the order of precedence specified in the contract. More detailed minimum requirements, technical requirements, approval conditions, responsibilities and other contract terms are determined on the basis of the invitation to tender and its appendices.
sig_ce1ebfc144dfc23a0d0c.title: Co-creation and implementation of an XR-based learning solution for vocational education and training in the tourism sector

The Scottish Sentencing Council seeks to commission a review of relevant academic and jurisprudential literature on the topic of: - Sexual offences involving sexual assault The aim of the literature review on sexual offences involving sexual assault will be to summarise new academic, legal and statistical work relevant to the sentencing of sexual assault as well as any relevant research on the changing nature of sexual assault offending particularly in light of the COVID-19 pandemic and cyber-enabled offending. sig_cef5f71f644c84e946c9.description: YOU CAN STILL INFLUENCE DURING THE MARKET SURVEY PHASE! At the City of Turku, we want to make high-quality procurements and cooperate with companies. We are therefore conducting a market survey before the publication of the actual contract notice. The goal is to inform about the upcoming tendering process, survey the markets for the subject of the procurement, and obtain comprehensive information on the availability of the service, implementation possibilities, and potential suppliers. We will also ask suppliers participating in the market dialogue for comments on the minimum requirements and quality criteria in the procurement documents. The goal of the market dialogue is also to go through the scheduling and implementation of the upcoming tendering process. This is an invitation to a market dialogue concerning the energy consumption monitoring service planned by the City of Turku. Turun kaupunki monitors energy consumption in approx. 600 buildings, of which over 200 have district heating. A measurement hub, which provides more accurate consumption data, can be found in approx. 70 buildings. The goal is to create a digital service that produces energy consumption monitoring, which performs the expert's manual work steps, producing as highly refined information as possible on consumption changes with easy views, explanations, and follow-up measures. The goal is to make consumption monitoring as automatic as possible by reducing manual work steps, such as determining the start time, occurrence, and overall effects of increased consumption. The user should automatically receive the most important prioritised key observations and easily see the analysis of the observation. The market dialogue will be held as a webinar on Teams on 2.10. at 9 -11. Event programme: 9:00-10:00 Presentation of the tendering process 10:00-11:00 Questions, answers, and discussion A warm welcome! REGISTRATION: Registration via the Tarjouspalvelu portal by 25.9.2026 at 16:00 or by email to sari.holmberg@turku.fi. State the persons from your company participating and their email addresses. This notice is not a contract notice or a call for tenders, but an invitation to a market dialogue, which aims to survey the market and develop the procurement's tendering documents. The invitation does not bind those who have responded to it. Not participating in the market dialogue event does not prevent participation in a possible tender competition, and participation in the event does not in any way affect the tenderer's position in the actual tender competition. The contracting entity does not commit to carrying out the procurement based on the market survey, and the presented descriptions/specifications do not bind the client. We announce our upcoming procurements in the Hilma planning tool, where it is possible to set search alerts. Hilma planning tool You can find more information about us at www.turku.fi/hankinnat and we publish current matters on our LinkedIn page “Turun kaupungin hankintapalvelut”.

sig_cf34e4eeaf78bd37f0c0.description: PLEASE NOTE: this program has MANDATORY Notices of Intent, which are due via NSPIRES by 8/20/2026 . See the full posting on NSPIRES for details. ﻿ NOTICE: August 4, 2026. Going forward, a $0.09/SBU charge now applies to all proposing to Earth Science (ROSES Appendix A) to use any NASA high-end computing resource. Proposers must account for this in their budget, per the instructions provided in Section 7.3 of ROSES-25 A.1 Earth Science Research Overview . NOTICE: July 30, 2026. An erroneous reference in Section 4.1 to was corrected to refer to Section 4.2 regarding Sub-element of relevance. Section 4.3.3 "Use of Generative AI" was added. On the NSPIRES cover page, the NOI Program Specific Data Cover Page Element was updated to include the Rough Budget estimate per year which is required. New text is in bold and deleted text is struck through. NOTICE: Amended July 20, 2026. This amendment adds this new program element to ROSES-2025. Mandatory Notices of Intent are due by August 20, 2026, and proposals are due October 20, 2026. Any proposal not preceded by an on-time NOI will be declined without review. Proposals submitted to this program will be evaluated using dual anonymous peer review, see Section 4.4. Proposers to this program element are strongly encouraged to use the optional Earth Science Division template for the required summary table of work effort of the proposal; templates are available at https://science.nasa.gov/researchers/templates-for-earth-science-division-appendix-a-roses-proposals. NOTICE: Research security training required starting August 5, 2026. All PIs and any Co-Is that would spend ≥ 10% time on a proposed grants or cooperative agreements must certify they have taken research security training. NASA will be satisfied with the four online research security training modules on the National Science Foundation's (NSF) Research Security Training website at https://www.nsf.gov/research-security/training or the SECURE Center condensed version of the four modules at https://www.secure-center.org/ctm This synopsis is a generic summary that is posted for each of the many individual "program elements" in NASA’s Research Opportunities in Space and Earth Sciences (ROSES) – 2025 solicitation. For specific information on this particular program element download and read the PDF of the text of this program element by going to Tables 2 or 3 of ROSES at https://solicitation.nasaprs.com/ROSES2025table2 and https://solicitation.nasaprs.com/ROSES2025table3 , respectively, click the title of the program element of interest, a hypertext link will take you to a page for that particular program element. On that page, on the right side under "Announcement Documents" the link on the bottom will be to the PDF of the text of the call for proposals. For example, if one were interested in the Solar System Science program (NNH25ZDA001N-SCUBED) one would follow the link to the NSPIRES page for that program element and then to read the text of the call one would click on “C.2 Solar System Science (.pdf)” to download the text of the call. If one wanted to set it into the context of the goals, objectives and know the default rules for all elements within Appendix C, the planetary science division, one might download and read “ C.1 Planetary Science Research Program Overview (.pdf) ” from that same page. While the letters and numbers are different for each element within ROSES (A.10, B.3, etc.) the basic configuration is always the same, e.g., the letter indicates the Science Division (A is Earth Science, B is Heliophysics etc.) and whatever the letter, #1 is always the division overview. In 2025, most program elements will be set up for application via Grants.gov only if requested at least 30 days in advance of the due date. For more on Grants.gov submissions see Section IV(b)v of the ROSES Summary of Solicitation, that may be found at https://solicitation.nasaprs.com/ROSES2025 . The National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) Science Mission Directorate (SMD) released its annual omnibus Research Announcement (NRA), Research Opportunities in Space and Earth Sciences (ROSES) – 2025 (OMB Approval Number 2700-0092, CFDA Number 43.001) on February 21, 2025. In this case "omnibus" means that this NRA has many individual program elements, each with its own due dates and topics. All together these cover the wide range of basic and applied supporting research and technology supported by SMD. Awards will be made as grants, cooperative agreements, or contracts depending on the nature of the work proposed. However, most extramural research awards deriving from ROSES will be grants, and many program elements of ROSES specifically exclude contracts, because contracts would not be appropriate for the nature of the work solicited. Funded Co-Is at government labs will receive inter- or intra-agency transfers . The typical period of performance for an award is three years, but some programs may allow up to five years and others specify shorter periods. In most cases, organizations of every type, Government and private, for profit and not-for-profit, domestic and foreign (with some caveats), may submit proposals without restriction on teaming arrangements. Tables listing the program elements and due dates (Tables 2 and 3 ), a table that provides a very top level summary of proposal contents ( Table 1 ), and the full text of the ROSES-2025 "Summary of Solicitation", may all be found NSPIRES at https://solicitation.nasaprs.com/ROSES2025 . Frequently asked questions for ROSES are posted at http://science.nasa.gov/researchers/sara/faqs . Questions concerning specific program elements should be directed to the point(s) of contact for that particular element, who may be found either at the end of the individual program element in the summary table of key information or on the web list of topics and points of contact at: http://science.nasa.gov/researchers/sara/program-officers-list . General questions concerning ROSES-2025 may be directed to the office of the SMD Deputy Associate Administrator for Research at sara@nasa.gov . Not all program elements are known at the time of the release of ROSES. To be informed of new program elements or amendments to this NRA, proposers may subscribe to: (1) The SMD mailing lists (by logging in at http://nspires.nasaprs.com and checking the appropriate boxes under "Account Management" and "Email Subscriptions"), (2) The ROSES-2025 blog feed for amendments, clarifications, and corrections to at https://science.nasa.gov/researchers/solicitations/roses-2025/ , and (3) The ROSES-2025 due date Google calendars (one for each science division). Instructions are at https://science.nasa.gov/researchers/sara/library-and-useful-links (link from the words due date calendar).

sig_cf9535f03041162a3dab.description: The ITZBund requires services in the area of software lifecycle management (SLM) for deployed software development and project management solutions. The aim of this tender is the conclusion of a framework agreement to ensure the operation as well as the maintenance and (further) development of the existing software development and project management platform Cloud as well as specialist applications of the ITZBund based thereon. In addition, sovereignty is to be strengthened through the expansion of open source tools to be procured. By open source, the ITZBund understands software whose source code is freely available. In principle, everyone is permitted to use, analyse, modify and pass on this free of charge and without restriction in terms of content regarding object and source code. Specifications of the respective relevant open source licence, in particular regarding licence texts, copyright notices or copyleft effects, remain unaffected. The tendered services comprise services along the entire software lifecycle, in particular operational services, maintenance and support services, support services in connection with releases and rollouts, as well as demand-oriented new and further developments of existing software and software-related tools. The client, who can call off services commissioned by its customers, is authorised to call off. The operation of the procured software products generally takes place within the ITZBund; exceptions in special individual cases allow operation at the client's customers with their own licensing. The services mentioned at the outset are tendered in five lots: - Lot 1: Ensuring the maintenance and (further) development of the deployed software development and project management platform Cloud - Lot 2: Ensuring the operation and automated rollout of releases of the deployed software development and project management platform Cloud - Lot 3: Provision of Sonatype software products - Lot 4: Provision of an open source issue tracker including in particular training, support, further development and migration services - Lot 5: Provision of an open source wiki including in particular training, support, further development and migration services This specification of services considers the subject matter of Lot 4: The subject matter of this lot is the provision of an open source issue tracker including associated training, support, further development and migration services. Lot LOT-0000: Provision of an open source issue tracker including in particular training, support, further development and migration services. For the total contract term of 4 years, an upper limit of 1.450 instances and 150.776 staff hours (SH) or 18.847 person days (PD) results for the estimated calculatory costs.
sig_cf9535f03041162a3dab.title: Provision of an open source issue tracker including, in particular, training, support, further development and migration services

Keski-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialueen TKIO procurement system (hereinafter procurement system) forms a central part of the contracting authority's research, development, innovation and competence development activities and procurement platform. It forms the structure of a cooperation model regulated by an agreement between the subscriber and the research, development and innovation partners. The purpose of the services to be competed in the procurement system is to produce research data, development services and innovations as a basis for the subscriber's development activities and management. The procurement system is divided into categories as follows: Category 1 Innovation services Category 2 Development of service systems Category 3 Project services Category 4 Strategic development Category 5 Scientific communities In addition, the subject matter of the procurement includes piloting and experimentation services as well as continuous development and management services for the subscriber's use. The subject matter of the procurement and the operation of the procurement system are described in more detail in the appendix "Principles of the TKIO dynamic purchasing system". The minimum requirements for each category and the competence requirements for applicants at the establishment stage are described in more detail in this call for participation. The subscriber shall define the subject matter and requirements of the assignments to be competed in the procurement system in more detail in each internal call for tenders of the procurement system. The procurement system shall be valid until 31.10.2029, during which time the internal call for tenders of the procurement system shall be carried out. The subscriber may extend the validity of the procurement system with a new contract notice. Suppliers may apply to join the procurement system at the establishment stage and later during its validity by submitting a request to participate in accordance with the call for participation. The procurement procedure is two-stage. To be able to submit tenders, a supplier must first submit a request to participate and be admitted to the procurement system. After this, the supplier may submit tenders by responding to the call for tenders sent by the contracting authority. The contracting authority shall carry out internal competitions within the procurement system in the future as needed. Requests to participate may be submitted to the dynamic purchasing system throughout its duration. All applicants meeting the suitability requirements shall be admitted to the dynamic purchasing system. Actual procurements shall be made through internal competitions of the dynamic purchasing system, in which the subject matter of the procurement is described and specified. Participation in the internal competitions of the DPS is not possible unless the supplier has been admitted to the procurement system. The submission of a request to participate and admission to the procurement system does not oblige the supplier to submit a tender, but suppliers may submit tenders at their discretion. The contracting authority estimates that the value excluding value added tax of the planned procurements covered by the dynamic purchasing system at the time of publication of the call for participation is 5,6 million euros, taking into account all procurements potentially made within the system. The estimate is preliminary and based on the procurement need known at this time. The contracting authority does not commit to any procurement quantities or minimum purchase obligations with this notice. Category 1 Innovation services includes the generation of innovations and futures research. The purpose of innovation services is to produce innovative solutions and new methods for the organisation and production of services in an impactful way. Innovation can also aim, for example, at anticipating the demand for services and substantive change needs. Innovations include, for example, digital operating models, solutions related to the innovative utilisation of technology, or the utilisation of robotics and artificial intelligence in social welfare and healthcare services. Central to innovations is the consideration of customer experience, quality, impact and cost perspectives. Innovations may also relate to operational monitoring models, measurement of results or strategic work. The result of an innovation may also be a commercialised product or service. Category 1 Innovation services additionally includes Piloting and experimentation services, the purpose of which is to test new innovations and services resulting from assignments or other cooperation in practice. Continuous development and management, the purpose of which is the implementation of new or redesigned services, systems or operations resulting from the results of assignments such that the implementation includes their continuous development as part of service production or other activities of the subscriber. See appendix "Principles of the TKIO dynamic purchasing system" for more details.; Category 2 Development of service systems is expert service, the purpose of which is the development of services, service processes, service networks and service systems. The development of service systems includes the collection and analysis of data on the current state, needs and impact of services. The data is utilised in development activities. The development of service systems may include the production of various methods and tools for the subscriber's needs to support the implementation of changes. The service may include the implementation of stakeholder involvement, for example through service design or equivalent means. The development of service systems may also include coaching service, the purpose of which is to support the subscriber in development activities and the consolidation of results. Category 2 Development of service systems additionally includes - Piloting and experimentation services, the purpose of which is to test new innovations and services resulting from assignments or other cooperation in practice. - Continuous development and management, the purpose of which is the implementation of new or redesigned services, systems or operations resulting from the results of assignments such that the implementation includes their continuous development as part of service production or other activities of the subscriber. See appendix "Principles of the TKIO dynamic purchasing system" for more details.;

Category 3 Project Services includes the entire project process management for the subscriber's research, development and innovation activities. Project services include project planning services, project management services and project services. Category 3 Project Services also includes: - Piloting and experimentation services, the purpose of which is to test new innovations and services resulting from assignments or other cooperation in practice. - Continuous development and management, the purpose of which is the implementation of new or redesigned services, systems or operations resulting from assignments, such that the implementation includes their continuous development as part of service production or other subscriber operations. See the appendix 'TKIO dynamic purchasing system principles' for more details.; Category 4 Strategic development consulting is an expert service intended to provide the subscriber with comprehensive support for development activities and change management, from the perspectives of organiser management and service production. Strategic development consulting produces versatile and comprehensive information, expertise and insights into the development of social and health services and specialised medical care, as well as large-scale integration projects. The consulting offers expert knowledge for promoting the effectiveness, customer-orientation and quality of innovation and development activities in social welfare, health services and specialised medical care, as well as for the design, analysis and implementation of new operating models and process complexes. The strategic development consulting expert service includes versatile expertise in improving the effectiveness and productivity of social and health services, financing systems, improving service accessibility, designing service systems and networks, developing data-driven management capabilities and future forecasting. Strategic development can also include service production management services, which can be used to achieve significant cost savings when service production and the producer field in accordance with procurement contracts can be managed more systematically and purposefully. The service production management service can also help the contracting authority to find consistent and replicable operating processes for managing service providers, with which better service effectiveness, customer satisfaction, quality and cost-efficiency can be achieved. Category 4 Strategic development also includes: - Piloting and experimentation services, the purpose of which is to test new innovations and services resulting from assignments or other cooperation in practice. - Continuous development and management, the purpose of which is the implementation of new or redesigned services, systems or operations resulting from assignments, such that the implementation includes their continuous development as part of service production or other subscriber operations. Services procured from the scientific community in the procurement system may include services considered to be scientific activities, which in their content complement projects implemented within the framework of TKIO cooperation. Scientific activity may include any research activity and services in accordance with the subject of the procurement system, but a scientific and research perspective is always emphasised in these services. Services and research activities may be such that the benefit obtained accrues for use in operations other than those of the contracting authority. Services procured from the scientific community may also be research and development services where the benefit obtained accrues exclusively for use in the contracting authority's operations and the contracting authority compensates for the service performed in full. The nature of the service is specified in each call for tenders within the procurement system. Services can also be ordered from the scientific community directly without a call for tenders within the procurement system, if the conditions for the procurement act's scope exemption concerning research and development services (9 section 1 subsection 13 point) are met. sig_d066c19ac10d4e5b715d.description: School Attendance Monitoring of Children and Young People in Care and Children and Young People with an Education, Health & Care Plan (OOC). Wolverhampton City Council (the Council) has a statutory duty to monitor the school attendance of children and young people in care placed in out-of-city independent placements, and for children and young people with Education, Health and Care Plans (EHCPs) attending out-of-city education settings. This duty is primarily governed by the Education Act 1996 and relevant Department for Education (DfE) statutory guidance. To fulfil this responsibility, the Council requires a remote and secure system for collecting and monitoring attendance data for these two cohorts. The overarching aim is to improve school attendance among Wolverhampton pupils placed outside the city by delivering an effective, responsive, and informative service. This will enable the Council to identify and address poor attendance early, ensuring timely intervention in cases of unauthorised absence. The Provider will be expected to: • Contact selected schools attended by Wolverhampton pupils placed out of city. •Liaise with Council officers, parents, and carers when unauthorised absences occur. • Submit regular attendance reports within agreed timescales, using standardised DfE codes. • Provide business support and access to a secure online portal for Council officers and education settings. Lot 1: .
