sig_d06ddb546c44a243d33c.description: Hanover Housing Association is seeking to engage the market prior to a formal procurement for an HR and People Systems platform. The procurement may encompass Core HR, Payroll, Learning Management, Applicant Tracking and associated modules, either as a single integrated solution or a combination of products. This notice invites supplier engagement to inform the scope and structure of the forthcoming procurement. Lot 1: . Hanover Housing Association is undertaking a programme of HR and People Systems transformation and is conducting this market engagement to understand the range of solutions available. Hanover currently operates a number of separate systems and manual processes to support its HR, payroll, recruitment and learning functions. The purpose of this Prior Information Notice is to understand what the market is able to offer — individually and in combination — across the following functional areas, and to explore the trade-offs between integrated single-platform solutions and best-of-breed combinations. Core HR (Required — Implementation by 31 October 2026) Hanover's current HR system is due to be decommissioned and a replacement Core HR solution must be in place by 31 October 2026. This is a firm deadline. Hanover is seeking to understand market capability across the full range of Core HR functionality, including but not limited to: Employee Records and Data Management Centralised, auditable employee records covering personal details, employment history, contractual information, pay and grading, and document storage. The ability to maintain accurate organisational structures including multiple reporting lines, departments and cost centre allocations. Leave and Absence Management Management of all leave types including annual leave, sickness absence, maternity, paternity and other statutory leave. Integration with timesheets, overtime recording and flexi-time arrangements. Automated accruals, carry-over rules and manager approval workflows. HR Case Management End-to-end management of employee relations cases including disciplinaries, grievances, capability processes and investigations. Structured workflows, letter and document generation, case tracking and audit trails. Hanover is also interested in whether performance management — as a process driven by forms and workflows — could be accommodated within this module rather than as a standalone function. Employee Self-Service and Manager Self-Service A modern, intuitive self-service portal accessible via mobile devices, enabling employees to view and update personal information, submit and track leave requests, access payslips and documents, and engage with HR processes without manual intervention. Manager self-service should support approval workflows, team visibility and basic reporting. Reporting and Analytics Standard and configurable reporting across all HR data, including headcount, turnover, absence and equality monitoring. Dashboard views for HR teams and managers, with the ability to export data for use in wider organisational reporting. Compliance and Policy Management Support for statutory compliance requirements including GDPR-compliant data handling, equal opportunities monitoring, and audit logging. Configurable policy acknowledgement and document sign-off workflows. Organisational Design Visibility of organisational structure, headcount planning at a basic level, and the ability to model or represent changes to structure. This links to the Advanced HR requirement for post and establishment management. Onboarding and Offboarding Structured workflows to support the full employee lifecycle from pre-employment through to leaver processing, including right to work checks, document collection, task assignment and system access coordination.. The service will operate within a framework of continuous improvement with which the service provider will be required to engage; bringing innovation, sharing ideas, and implementing improvement measures to increase operational effectiveness/efficiency and drive out waste.
sig_d06ddb546c44a243d33c.title: Provision of an HR and People Systems Platform

sig_d0d035a1e770e77ef1bb.description: Assumption of the technical programme management of programme P20 The subject of the contract is the assumption of the technical programme management of programme P20 (formerly Police 20/20 programme). Programme P20 was created to implement the Saarbrücken Agenda and is a multiproject spanning several implementation levels and years (target picture 2030+). Its core mandate is to replace the heterogeneous police IT landscape and to unify and harmonise all information systems of the German police forces taking into account applicable legal frameworks. For this purpose, uniform, modern procedures are to be provided that can be used by all police forces of the Federation and the Länder according to equal standards. In order to achieve the target picture 2030+ of police casework through programme P20, a step-by-step approach is pursued. In total, more than 45 projects currently fit together as individual building blocks to form the overall programme P20. Important intermediate pictures have already been achieved. A further important intermediate step is to be achieved in the year 2028.

Investitionsbank Schleswig-Holstein (IB.SH), the central promotional institute of the federal state with currently just under 900 employees, is looking for three framework agreement partners as IT service providers for the provision of IT support services in the field of IT security. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- It is intended to conclude the framework agreement attached to the documents as Appendix 1, the agreement on data processing on behalf with the three bidders who meet the minimum criteria and occupy places 1-3. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The support services specifically required by IB.SH will be called off taking into account the work and project situation, qualification and availability in the context of mini-competitions. The arrangement of these individual call-offs is regulated in Appendix 3 framework agreement (see section 2 of the framework agreement). --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- A framework agreement is to be concluded between IB.SH and three service companies. The framework agreement regulates commissions placed on the one hand by IB.SH and comprising the following services: ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Description of activities: • Support for the client in technical and technical-organisational matters of IT security / cyber security based on the strategies, policies, roles and responsibilities specified by the client; the list of services is not exhaustive. • Elaboration, concretisation, updating and monitoring of technical IT security standards, technical specifications, operating processes, runbooks and implementation guidelines within the framework of existing internal specifications. • Risk-based assessment, classification and implementation support of technical IT security requirements from operations, change management, projects, architecture, service provider management, regulatory requirements and internal guidelines. • Support for technical IT security, digital operational resilience, recovery and restoration capability and continuity of critical IT services, including technical preparatory work for scenario analyses, emergency exercises, alternative procedures, fallback/exit scenarios and measure tracking. • Initiation, evaluation, implementation and tracking of operational security measures for IT infrastructures, applications, platforms, end devices and operating environments, including on-premises, private cloud, public cloud, hybrid cloud, multi-cloud as well as SaaS/PaaS/IaaS environments. • Coordination, evaluation and further development of technical security architectures, inter alia network and zone concepts, segmentation, firewalling, encryption, PKI, DNSSEC, proxy/gateway services, IAM/PAM, endpoint security, server/client hardening, cloud, container/Kubernetes and API security as well as secure administration models. • Initiation, support, evaluation and tracking of vulnerability analyses, penetration tests, technical security reviews, configuration and hardening checks, readiness checks as well as red/purple team or comparable technical security exercises. • Monitoring and evaluation of external reports on vulnerabilities, threats, attack patterns and security-relevant industry developments as well as derivation, support and documentation of technical measures. • Support with security monitoring, logging, detection and response, in particular for SIEM/SOC requirements, log source onboarding, use case design, alert tuning, detection engineering, SOC provider management, triage processes, playbooks, escalation paths and security-related reporting. • Technical support for handling, containment, analysis, documentation and follow-up of IT security incidents including interfaces to incident, problem, change, emergency and service provider management. • Technical-professional control, evaluation and tracking of service provider reports, security proofs, action plans, audit findings and audit points. • Maintenance, updating and quality assurance of technical IT security documentation, runbooks, control descriptions, verification documentation and technical security concepts. • Technical-professional preparatory work for inspections, audits, revisions and regulatory proofs; the performance of original inspection, audit or control functions is not covered by this. • Support for the data protection officer in technical questions as well as coordination and cooperation with the information security officer / information security management • Carrying out awareness-raising measures for employees on the subject of IT security • Proactive identification, evaluation and target-group-oriented preparation of technical IT security topics within the client's area of responsibility. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The support services specifically required by IB.SH will be called off taking into account the work and project situation, qualification and availability in the context of mini-competitions. The arrangement of these individual call-offs is regulated in the framework agreement (see section 2 of the framework agreement).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The IB.SH expects an annual workload of approx. 1.250 person-days. There is no entitlement to the purchase of a minimum quantity. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- The following maximum quantity for the services to be provided applies to this framework agreement in relation to the advertised period: 6.000 person-days. Upon reaching the maximum value, this framework agreement ends automatically without the need for termination. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

sig_d1aa86289da9fcd67343.description: Subject and objective of the procurement The subject of the procurement is mobile robotics technology solutions suitable for the urban environment, which perform tasks in the air, on the ground, or in water. This open call for tenders seeks 6–9 pilots to be implemented. The goal is to obtain information on new and innovative solutions that are suitable for challenging urban environments and support the city's services, maintenance, and decision-making. A particular goal is to help small and medium-sized enterprises solve challenges for which there is an acute need, and to grow their business. Blue City – Digital and safe water city Helsinki can be the world's first city that continuously monitors, measures, and secures its water areas with the help of mobile robotics. The goal is to develop autonomous water robots and data solutions that monitor water quality, map the bottom, and support water and maritime safety. 1. Safe beaches and harbours The goal is to develop an automatic monitoring and tracking system that improves the safety of beaches, harbours, and sea areas. The system detects risks and anomalies in time, tracks the movements of swimmers, and identifies emergencies in real time. Robotics can also be utilised in rescue and retrieval tasks, identification of foreign objects, and monitoring the condition of channels. 2. Smart water quality monitoring and stormwater management Water quality monitoring is currently slow and point-based. The goal is to create a real-time water situational picture based on robotics and data analytics, which enables rapid reaction to anomalies. The solution can monitor turbidity, oxygen content, temperature, electrical conductivity, and nutrient concentrations, as well as automatically take water samples for further analysis. 3. Own solution Companies can also propose their own new robotics solution related to the water environment, which brings added value to the City of Helsinki and its residents. The solution must utilise ground, water, or air robotics and produce data that can be utilised in the city's various service areas, for example in the development of infrastructure, safety, or environmental management. Urban Sky – Smart and managed urban airspace Urban airspace is a new infrastructure where drones and sensors operate as part of the city's everyday life. The goal is to build a safe and coordinated airspace where mobile robotics supports monitoring, maintenance, and decision-making. 1. Smart construction site monitoring Monitoring and supervising construction sites takes a lot of resources and is often manual. The goal is to improve the safety, transparency, and productivity of construction sites by monitoring progress and anomalies in real time. 2. Predictive maintenance – detection of leaks and thermal anomalies The city loses significant amounts of energy and water every year due to unnoticed leaks and heat losses. The goal is to develop a system based on air robotics and thermal imaging that identifies leaks and anomalies at an early stage and supports predictive maintenance. 3. Own solution Companies can also propose their own robotics solution utilising airspace that supports the safety, monitoring, or energy use of the urban environment. The solution must utilise ground, water, or air robotics and produce data that supports the city's services and decision-making. Smart Ground – Functional and sustainable city all year round A functional and sustainable city utilises mobile robotics, data, and the circular economy so that the city's infrastructure, maintenance, and logistics work seamlessly every day of the year. It is the city's nervous system that maintains vitality and the smooth running of services without interruptions. 1. Infrastructure condition monitoring and modelling The city has thousands of kilometres of streets, cycle paths, and tunnels, the condition of which is laborious and fragmented to inspect. The goal is to develop a solution that provides a continuous, up-to-date, and automatically updating view of the state of the city's infrastructure. 2. Automation and logistics of winter maintenance In the year 2028 dumping snow into the sea will be prohibited, which requires new ways to manage snow collection and processing. The goal is to develop a predictive and data-driven robotics solution that supports snow collection, transport, storage, and melting in an environmentally friendly and cost-effective manner. 3. Own solution Companies can also propose their own robotics solution suitable for the ground environment, which improves the operation of the city's infrastructure, maintenance, or logistics. The solution can utilise ground, water, or air robotics and produce data beneficial to the city, for example about the environment, traffic, or energy use.
sig_d1aa86289da9fcd67343.title: Urban Mobile Robotics – We are looking for companies to implement robotics pilots

sig_d232b34ff73335e6cfd1.description: The reason for initiating the ecohydrological study is the stability problems in the Kikbeek pool, as a result of which water level rises in function of achieving the conservation objectives cannot currently proceed. The subject of the ecohydrological study is to investigate the effects of higher pool levels (than current ones) in the Kikbeek quarry on the surrounding groundwater-dependent vegetation. Additionally, it is investigated which additional measures for re-wetting in the Habitats Directive area of the Mechelse Heide, Ziepbeekvallei, Neerharerheide and Asbeek are necessary to arrive at a climate-robust system. The aim of the study is to investigate the impact on groundwater levels and boundary conditions from ecology through water level rises of the Kikbeek pool and hydrological restoration measures in the Mechelse Heide, Ziepbeek, Neerharerheide and Asbeek. This must lead to maximising the restoration and conservation of the groundwater-dependent vegetation. The objective is to achieve climate-robust system restoration, without compromising critical infrastructure (such as the E314 motorway) and the stability of the Berg quarry and the Kikbeek pool in the long term. The drafting of hydrological and ecological model predictions must serve to investigate scenarios for water level rise in the Kikbeek pool and to elaborate and evaluate the development of wet nature in the Habitats Directive area of the Mechelse Heide.
sig_d232b34ff73335e6cfd1.title: ECOHYDROLOGICAL STUDY KIKBEEK and SAC MECHELSE HEIDE

sig_d35a7d3ffd39ee9f9280.description: PURPOSE NIOSH intends to support the Centers of Excellence in Total Worker Health® (TWH). These Centers will conduct rigorous research and translation activities to prevent harmful exposures, improve working conditions, and advance worker well-being. The Centers will develop practical, scalable solutions for employers and workers. All projects must use the NIOSH Worker Well-Being Questionnaire (WellBQ) and share data with the HERO Worker Well-Being Clearinghouse. Large Research Projects require economic evaluation. PRIORITY AREAS • High-risk occupations: First responders, vehicle mechanics, and technicians, with emphasis on occupational exposures, related health risks, and prevention strategies • Young workers, SMEs • Chronic disease • Mental health, stress • Substance use disorder • Artificial intelligence (AI), digital technologies This is a multi-component NOFO. COMPONENT STRUCTURE Percentages indicate maximum share of total budget. Overall Component (Required) Provides Center leadership and integration. Applicants should show strong coordination, scientific direction, and alignment across projects. Administration, Evaluation, and Emerging Issues Core (Required; up to 15%) Supports management and Center-wide evaluation. Applicants should describe oversight, data governance, and quality assurance.Optional activities include emerging issues and shared research resources. Outreach, Dissemination, and Impact Core (Required; up to 15%) Supports communication, worker/employer engagement, training, translation, implementation, and dissemination strategies. Research Projects (Required; about 60 to 70%) Includes all research activities. Applicants may propose a mix of projects. Research project distinctions are based on scope and complexity rather than cost. Projects should demonstrate scientific rigor and potential for sustained impact. Small Research Projects (Required; at least one project; up to 3 years) Exploratory, feasibility, early-stage intervention, surveillance, or measurement studies. Priority areas: high-risk occupations, young workers, SMEs. Should show innovation and potential to expand. Large Research Projects (Required; at least one project; up to 5 years) Multiyear etiologic, mechanistic, intervention, or translational studies. Priority areas: chronic disease, mental health, substance use disorder. Economic evaluation is required. Projects should include strong design and analytic plans. Pilot/Feasibility Program (Optional; 12–18 months) Short-term studies generating preliminary data or testing AI/digital technology approaches.
sig_d35a7d3ffd39ee9f9280.title: NIOSH Centers of Excellence for Total Worker Health® (U19)

sig_d3771785f2bb25cac5ac.description: The National Institutes of Health (NIH) intends to award a Firm-Fixed-Price Purchase Order to Thomas Jefferson University to Obtain Clinical Cohort of Patients with Associated Clinical Outcomes, Radiologic Images, and Associated De-Identified Radiology Reports. In accordance with FAR 6.302-1, Only One Responsible Source and No Other Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements, The requested clinical cohorts, radiographic imaging datasets, clinical outcomes data, and de-identified radiology reports are required to support artificial intelligence-based research focused on evaluating liver cancer risk in patients with cirrhosis and indeterminate liver lesions. The research requires datasets that combine specific patient populations with associated imaging studies and clinical outcomes information to enable the development, validation, and evaluation of predictive models. Alternative datasets that do not include the required patient populations, imaging data, clinical outcomes information, and associated radiology reports would not provide the information necessary to support the approved research objectives. The absence of any of these data elements would limit the ability to correlate imaging findings with clinical outcomes and would reduce the scientific validity and reliability of the resulting analyses. Therefore, only datasets containing the required clinical cohorts and associated imaging and outcomes data will satisfy the Government's minimum needs and support the approved research objectives. The objectives of the maintenance agreement are as follows: The objective of this requirement is to acquire clinical patient cohorts, associated imaging data, clinical outcomes data, and de-identified radiology reports to support the development and evaluation of A.I. models for liver disease and liver cancer research conducted by the Liver Diseases Branch. A determination by the Government to compete this proposed acquisition based upon responses received to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. The proposed contractor maintains an existing cohort of patients with cirrhosis and associated radiographic images collected at six-month intervals, as well as an existing cohort of patients with cirrhosis and indeterminate liver lesions, including associated clinical outcomes data and radiographic images. These clinical cohorts and associated datasets represent a unique research resource available through the proposed contractor. The combination of longitudinal imaging data, clinical outcomes data, and radiographic images associated with these patient populations is available only through the proposed contractor. As a result, only the proposed contractor can provide the requested deliverables necessary to support the research project. sig_d4dd6ae8c237d43343b0.description: The subject of the procurement is a work ability management system as a SaaS service. The procurement includes the delivery of the system, planning and implementation of the deployment, execution of necessary integrations, and ongoing maintenance and support services. In addition, the contracting authority has the option to procure separately agreed minor development during the contract period. The supplier is responsible for ensuring that the system can be deployed in a controlled manner and that it is integrated into the contracting authority's key back-end systems, such as HR and identity management systems. The migration of legacy data can be carried out as expert work as a separately ordered option in accordance with the hourly rate for expert work stated in the price appendix. The contracting authority shall decide on the implementation of the option at its own discretion during the contract period, and the contracting authority is under no obligation to implement the option or order related services. The system must support the contracting authority's work ability management operating models and processes, in particular early support practices, management of sickness absences, identification and prevention of work ability risks, and support for return to work. The objective of the solution is to improve the timeliness of work ability measures, increase operational transparency, and strengthen data-driven management at all levels of the organisation. The system must provide an up-to-date overall picture of the work ability situation at the employee, unit, and organisational level. It must form a clear, user-friendly, and intuitive whole regarding work ability management processes and offer views and access rights according to user roles. User groups include at least line managers, HR work ability specialists, management, and system administrators. Line managers must be able to utilise the system in their daily work ability management work, while for management, the system must offer summary views, reporting, and analytics to support strategic decision-making. The system must enable versatile reporting for different time periods and organisational levels and offer visual views, such as trends, comparisons, and key performance indicators to support decision-making. The supplier must carry out the deployment in cooperation with the contracting authority so that the solution meets the contracting authority's functional needs and the deployment supports a smooth transition to production use. The objective of the procurement is to improve the effectiveness of work ability management, reduce costs caused by sickness absences, strengthen proactive management, and support the staff's work ability, performance at work, and continuation in work. The system must be a modern, secure, scalable, and easy-to-use solution that supports the long-term development of the contracting authority's operations.
sig_d4dd6ae8c237d43343b0.title: Procurement of a work ability management system

sig_d51752b39833df6988a4.description: Valtion talous- ja henkilöstöhallinnon palvelukeskus (Palkeet) is publishing a preliminary notice regarding the procurement of maintenance, support and expert services for Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences, as well as the procurement of additional Precisely Automate licences. Palkeet invites tenderers interested in the market dialogue to express their interest and register for the market dialogue by replying to this request for information. This notice is not an invitation to tender, and its publication does not initiate a competitive tendering procedure; rather, this is a request for information related to market research. This does not oblige Palkeet to carry out the actual procurement, and any information provided is non-binding. The subject matter of the procurement will be refined as the market dialogue progresses, and the content of the subject matter may change during the course of it. Failing to reply to the request for information does not prevent participation in a potential competitive tendering procedure, nor does replying to the request for information affect the tenderer's position in the actual competitive tendering procedure. SUBJECT OF THE MARKET DIALOGUE With the commencing market dialogue, Palkeet wishes to familiarise itself with suppliers in the market that can provide maintenance, support and expert services, as well as potential additional licences, for existing Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences. Palkeet utilises the Winshuttle Evolve solution in its service production, inter alia in accounting and human resources processes. Winshuttle licences are primarily used for mass runs of financial and HR data in Palkeet's Kieku system (SAP HCM, SAP Finance). For these purposes, Palkeet uses perpetual licences: 60 Studio Runner licences and 10 Studio Developer licences. Support and maintenance services mean the maintenance and version management of Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences (e.g. activations, modifications and updates), error correction, and advisory and support services. In addition, there must be an option to separately order further development and other expert services. REQUEST FOR INFORMATION QUESTIONS AND REGISTRATION INSTRUCTIONS We kindly ask tenderers to submit their answers to the request for information questions below. The answers provided, or the failure to reply, do not constitute an obstacle to potential participation in commenting on the draft invitation to tender materials at a later stage. All answers supplied by you and the descriptions attached to them will be treated as confidential and are not public documents. Request for information questions 1. The name of the company registering for the market dialogue, the name of the contact person and the email address. 2. What kinds of references does the tenderer have regarding the maintenance, related support and expert services for Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences? What are the licence types and pricing models of the different environments (on-premise/cloud) or use cases for new Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences? 3. What are the licence types and pricing models of the different environments (on-premise/cloud) or use cases for the maintenance service of current perpetual Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences? Is the model the same with regard to any potential new additional licences? 4. In what different languages can you provide maintenance, support and expert services? Would your supply situation change if all support services could be delivered in English? 5. In what different types of environments (Evolve, Studio Manager, Desktop) have you delivered support services for Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences? 6. Which licence terms apply to the maintenance of Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences and what about for new licences? Please provide your licence terms as an attachment. 7. Are the current names of Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences (Studio Developer and Studio Runner) still in use and if not, what are the names of the licences that correspond to them and are compatible with them? Is there a difference in licence names if the licence is used in an on-premise solution vs. a cloud solution? 8. Is it possible to place Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences on dormant status such that they are not used in a given year, and the maintenance fee is not paid for them during that time either, but the licence is put back into use later? 9. Is it possible to transfer Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences from one user to another and/or from one customer organisation of Palkeet to another in the middle of a maintenance period and/or when the maintenance period changes? 10. Is there anything else special related to Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) licences or their terms that would be good for Palkeet to be aware of? We kindly ask you to register as a supplier interested in the market dialogue and to send your answers to the questions presented in the request for information by 18.9.2025 at the latest at 15.00 by email to the address kilpailutus@hansel.fi; please title the email "Palkeet Precisely Automate (Winshuttle) -lisenssit, markkinavuoropuhelu". The objective is to engage in market dialogue with industry operators who have notified their contact details and are interested in the procurement, which may include answering questions and commenting on draft invitations to tender in September-October 2025. No compensation will be paid to those who have registered for participation in the market dialogue. The dialogues will be conducted in the Finnish language. Valtion talous- ja henkilöstöhallinnon palvelukeskus (Palkeet) is a corporate service provider operating within the administrative sector of the Ministry of Finance. We produce financial and HR services for central government agencies, institutions, funds and state limited company customers for approximately 80 000 individual wage earners with the strength of around 650 professionals.

sig_d5236fe2ac551b3f0357.description: An observation instrument for children's linguistic and mathematical development is to be developed, pilot tested, validated and tested for reliability, derived from the Brandenburg curriculum. The items for assessing children's competences at the end of the Kita period (3 third of the final Kita year) are designed as "Individual learning status analysis at the transition from Kita to school (ILeA 0)" and configured to be compatible with the existing observation instrument for the "Individual learning status analysis in the first 6 weeks after starting school (ILeA plus)". The aim is an integrated, structurally harmonised observation system that records linguistic and mathematical development in a comparable and compatible structure. Lot LOT-0001: Development, pilot testing, validation and reliability testing of an observation instrument for linguistic and mathematical development. The contracting authority expects a standardised, scientifically sound, streamlined and practice-oriented observation instrument. A uniform conceptual approach is of central importance to the contracting authority in order to keep the need for qualification in practice to a low level and to simplify use by educational professionals with the uniform structure of ILeA 0. The service is divided into four work packages: Work package 1 (development of the linguistic aspects of the observation instrument), work package 2 (development of the mathematical aspects of the observation instrument), work package 3 (creation of a guidance document for the observation instrument), work package 4 (pilot testing, validation and reliability testing of the developed observation instrument). Further details can be found in Appendix 12 (specification of services).
sig_d5236fe2ac551b3f0357.title: Development, pilot testing, validation and reliability testing of an observation instrument for linguistic and mathematical development

sig_d56b17f96d7618ba649c.description: Setup, operation and continuous further development of an integrated VoC feedback and analytics system for the entire EUDI Wallet Support Organisation. Covers the collection, evaluation and presentation of B2C and B2B feedback as well as operational support KPIs, trend analyses and automated pattern recognition. The subject of this tender is the award of services for VoC / feedback & analytics of the EUDI Wallet Support Organisation (EWSO). The contractor shall set up the VoC platform, configure all feedback instruments (post-interaction surveys, IVR CSAT, NPS, CES, B2B partner reviews, agent feedback loop) and set up the operational KPI dashboard and the pattern warning system (pattern alerting). The contractor shall accompany the closed beta phase (Q4 2026) and the go-live phase (Q1 2027) with hypercare support. Following an orderly knowledge transfer, they shall hand over operational sovereignty over the VoC system and the analytics platform to the client's internal team. The services comprise in particular data protection-compliant data collection (GDPR, EU hosting, pseudonymisation), API integration with the ticketing system and telephony infrastructure (cf. section 5. of the specification of services), WCAG 2.1-compliant design of all feedback interfaces as well as complete system documentation, training of the internal team and a structured handover plan for independent system sovereignty.
sig_d56b17f96d7618ba649c.title: EUDI-Wallet Support Organisation VoC - Feedback & Analytics

sig_d5a5d80997059cc028a2.description: The provision of temporary and interim staff services to the Scottish Public Sector Lot 1: . The Scottish Procurement and Property Directorate (SPPD) is the organisation tasked with procuring requirements on behalf of Scottish Public Sector Bodies. The current Scottish Government collaborative Temporary and Interim Staff Services Frameworks are a suite of four individual multi supplier Framework Agreements which commenced on 13 April 2023 and are due to expire on 12 April 2027. They are all National Category A Frameworks which are open to all public sector organisations throughout Scotland. They are designed to provide the full range of commonly sought temporary and interim staff services required for daily business. These are national collaborative Frameworks, for commonly required, regularly sought temporary and interim staff services roles/assignments across the Scottish public sector. These Frameworks are intended solely for short term, gap filling purposes and are not intended as an alternative to permanent or fixed term appointment (FTA) recruitment. Work has commenced in developing the procurement strategy options including canvassing of stakeholders views. In order to complete and finalise the strategy, SPPD recognises the value of suppliers having the opportunity to contribute to this process on a non-competitive, non-judgemental basis. This request for information is aimed at collating those views from market participants. Framework participants will be expected to provide a range of Fair Work First measures. This information may be utilised in developing the procurement strategy to help deliver contractual arrangements for Temporary and Interim Staff Services requirements. This notice is issued for information only and does not constitute a call for competition. Scottish Government and the Scottish Ministers shall have no liability for any costs, however incurred, by those attending any information days, attendance at meetings, or involvement in the proposed procurement process. Suppliers and other interested parties should read and complete the following Request for Information Online Questionnaire using the link below. https://forms.office.com/e/cNzCefdZzU The questionnaire will be available for all interested parties until COP 3 March 2026.

sig_d61374e1e3ef8e6cb455.description: The NSF Engineering Directorate (ENG) has launched a multi-year initiative, theProfessional Formation of Engineers, to create and support an innovative and inclusive engineering profession for the 21 st century. Professional Formation of Engineers (PFE) refers to the formal and informal processes and value systems by which people become engineers. It also includes the ethical responsibility of practicing engineers to sustain and grow the profession in order to improve quality of life for all peoples. The engineering profession must be responsive to national priorities, grand challenges, and dynamic workforce needs; it must be equally open and accessible to all. Professional Formation of Engineers includes, but is not limited, to: Introductions to the profession at any age; Development of deep technical and professional skills, knowledge, and abilities in both formal and informal settings/domains; Development of outlooks, perspectives, ways of thinking, knowing, and doing; Development of identity as an engineer and its intersection with other identities; and Acculturation to the profession, its standards, and norms. The goal of the Research in the Formation of Engineers (RFE) program is to advance our understanding of professional formation. It seeks both to deepen our fundamental understanding of the underlying processes and mechanisms that support professional formation and to demonstrate how professional formation is or can be accomplished. Ultimately RFE aims to transform the engineer-formation system, and thus the impact of proposed projects on this system must be described. Principal Investigators (PIs) should provide a roadmap detailing how they envision the proposed research will eventually broadly impact practice within the engineer-formation system, even if these activities are not within the scope of the submitted proposal. In order to accomplish its goals, RFE welcomes proposals in two categories: Research Projects, and Design and Development Projects. Research Projects address fundamental questions of professional formation, while Design and Development Projects provide new approaches to achieving professional formation. Additional details are provided below. Projects in both categories should address the iterative cycle in which research questions that advance understanding are informed by practice and the results of research are, in turn, translated into practice. In other words, proposals should explain how the research results will travel, translate, transfer, or scale. Successful projects identify specific target audiences, effective communication channels, and novel partnerships to ensure effective propagation and scaling. Proposal titles should begin with either “Research:” or “Design and Development:” as appropriate. Research Projects Research proposals are particularly welcome in the following areas: Research that addresses lifelong learning by the engineering workforce. Research on the impact of engineering education research. Proposals addressing this topic could investigate questions such as: How can we measure the impacts of engineering education research? What are effective strategies for scaling reforms? How can we translate knowledge from research to practice? What are the roles of technologies, networks and communities in achieving impact? RFE does not support efficacy, effectiveness, or scale-up studies for specific interventions. Research that addresses culture change in engineering education. Included in this topic are investigations of normative cultures of engineering at any level in the engineering education ecosystem and how these cultures may disadvantage certain groups. Research that addresses engineering formation at the two-year college level in both formal and informal settings. Research that addresses engineering formation at the graduate education level in both formal and informal settings. Research that investigates engineering in P-12 settings. Research in this area could include understanding of approaches to engineering in P-12, how to develop engineering ways of thinking, or the relationship between practices within the sciences and mathematics and engineering thinking. Research on the transitions between education levels, e.g., from high school to two-year college, high school to four-year college/university, two-year college to four-year college/university, undergraduate to graduate school, education settings to the workforce or professoriate, etc. Research that addresses the relationship between engineering and the public. Proposals addressing this topic could consider the social impact of engineering solutions, citizen engineering, education of an informed public, etc. Research that develops or adapts novel methodologies and frameworks appropriate for studying the professional formation of engineers, and especially minoritized, marginalized, or underserved populations. Research that addresses ways in which new technologies (such as artificial intelligence and machine learning) are changing engineering education. Research to transform engineering education so that all students encounter environmental and social sustainability principles as an integrated part of their education and are equipped with the tools needed to incorporate these principles into their future research, careers, and innovations. Proposals submitted to the Research Projects category should have clear research questions informed by an appropriate theoretical framework and a research design that includes sampling, data collection, and data analysis methods. This category will not support proposals that seek funding primarily to develop tools, curriculum, or laboratories, or that seek to implement classroom innovations that have already been shown to be effective in engineering. The program will evaluate the value of proposals by considering the impact and the cost. Research track projects that are small, exploratory, or speculative are especially encouraged. Larger Research track projects should have a correspondingly larger impact. Design and Development Projects RFE supports Design and Development projects (see https://www.nsf.gov/publications/pub_summ.jsp?ods_key=nsf13126 ) that seek to develop and test new approaches in the following areas related to engineering education : Graduate education. Undergraduate education in new engineering technologies and environmental sustainability. Transitions between education levels, for example high school to two-year college, high school to four-year college/university, two-year college to four-year college/university, undergraduate to graduate school, education settings to the workforce or professoriate, etc. P-12, especially approaches to develop engineering thinking, or providing links between engineering, science, and mathematics. Proposals in this category should propose the design and development of new approaches that are informed by existing literature and theory. There should be clear objectives and the evaluation plan should be designed to determine if those objectives have been met. Projects cannot be solely demonstration projects but must add to the engineering education literature to inform future work.
sig_d61374e1e3ef8e6cb455.title: Research in the Formation of Engineers

sig_d62d83a5734601ff281d.description: Provision of a managed wireless network and internet in National Revenue Agency sites – territorial directorates, offices, training centres and bases, and the National Revenue Agency Head Office. The managed wireless network and internet must be completely independent of the available internal business network and external connectivity of the respective National Revenue Agency buildings. The requirements are described in detail in the Technical Specification and include: 1. Provision for use and maintenance of a comprehensive solution for a managed wireless access network and delivery of filtered internet in National Revenue Agency sites, described in Appendices No 1 and No 3 to the Technical Specification; 2. Provision for use and maintenance of a comprehensive solution for a managed wireless access network and delivery of filtered internet in the training centres and bases of the National Revenue Agency (Borovets, Bankya, Pomorie and Dospat), described in Appendix No 2 to the Technical Specification; 3. If necessary, the contractor shall provide a Platform for filtering internet requests in order to restrict access to various categories of content based on the categorisation of web portals on the Internet; 4. The contractor must provide guaranteed internet of 1000 Mbps, which is to be terminated in the platform for filtering internet requests. The same, after filtering, must be shared between the wireless networks across all locations; 5. If necessary, the contractor shall provide a Wireless Access Network Management Platform fulfilling the minimum requirements described in detail in the Technical Specification; 6. Access to the internet by users of the wireless access network must take place via an access portal bearing the National Revenue Agency logo. Access to the National Revenue Agency wireless network shall be carried out by entering a password. It must be possible for the system administrator to change the password; 7. If necessary, all devices and other equipment necessary for the provision of the service (Wi-Fi modules, adapters, etc.) shall be provided by the contractor to the contracting authority for temporary use for the duration of the contract. sig_d6cbbe1ee9be752376d6.description: The aim of the project is the implementation of the new Diavgeia taking into account modern institutional, operational and technological developments, the more correct implementation of the institutional framework with emphasis on the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and the optimal utilisation of Diavgeia information with a data-based architecture and secondarily document-based. The project seeks to increase the efficiency and productivity of public services by enriching the applications of the Diavgeia Programme, supplementing functionality for the collaborative drafting and management of documents to be published based on standardised documents and data structures, and also to add value to the Programme by utilising and enriching the information gathered within it through the use of other information sources with the aim of creating a system of complex reports and other complementary application subsystems and solutions. The new system will allow the monitoring of the operation and organisational structure of public administration in combination with information related to the competences of bodies in the context of multi-level governance and also of personnel as recorded in the Human Resources Register of the Hellenic Republic. The aim is to provide objective evidence for the implementation of the National Administrative Procedures Policy and the prioritisation of the actions of the National Programme for Administrative Simplification. To this end, care has been taken to significantly enhance its interoperability with third-party public sector systems for the dissemination of information without necessarily requiring intervention from the end user. Additionally, through the expansion of information kept in a structured manner (metadata set), it will be possible to capture data groups with special characteristics that enhance transparency at the level of monitoring/evaluation by the general public of indicators related to, for example, the operation and structure of public administration and/or financial figures (public spending). For this purpose, data from other sources and publicly available data will also be utilised to support the monitoring of the operation and action of bodies and to support decision-making. The solution will include the creation of a system for the correct (and as complete as possible per sector) structured collection and processing of data from various public data sources and subsequently making them available to the general public. Illustrative examples of sources are data from systems under development for GOV ERP, HRMS, the Civil Society Organisations Register, ESIDIS, KHMDIS. A distinct subsystem will be developed for further utilisation and extraction of specialised reports with the aim of monitoring the structure, operation and action of public administration as well as monitoring expenditure and procurement and supporting the decision-making process. The system will be scalable for the addition of new sources arising from other actions. Also, within the framework of the action, improvements will be made in relation to identified problems associated with the management of the very large volume of documents collected by Diavgeia at a sharply increasing rate, which also led to the necessary migration of the infrastructure to public cloud services. In this context, advanced services provided by public clouds will be better utilised in order to ensure the uninterrupted provision of services and the monitoring of their provision at the lowest possible cost. The action, taking into account the life cycle of the administrative documents that are published, will address challenges such as the cleaning of multiple copies of the same documents, the extraction of all information in data format and the optimisation of the quality of Diavgeia metadata as well as the automatic publication of important data sets in the central open public data repository www.data.gov.gr. The project also aims to adopt a new architecture that will allow a drastic reduction, by at least 65%, of the required storage space and computational resources while ensuring the proper functioning of the system. To achieve the above goal, both emerging artificial intelligence and language model technologies and techniques for the correct entry of metadata into relevant information will be utilised to facilitate their search, categorisation and utilisation. This contract concerns a single subject matter and is not subdivided into lots due to the project's architecture, the strong interdependencies and complementarity of the individual services that compose it, as well as the high interoperability requirements that must be ensured on the one hand between the functional units (subsystems) to be developed within the framework of this project and on the other hand with third-party systems of Hellenic Republic bodies. The non-subdivision of the contract enhances the quality and security of the project, since unified management reduces the chances of security gaps or incompatibilities appearing between the different systems and facilitates the coordination of its implementation. The duration of the contract is set at thirty-two (32) months including the procedure for checking and acceptance of deliverables. The contract will be awarded on the basis of the most economically advantageous tender, based on the best price-quality ratio. [para. 1.3. & ANNEX I of the Call for Tenders]

sig_d6f20e827ba28a83b6df.description: HZD established the Test Center Hessen in 2022 and has operated it since then as a central organisational unit for standardised test services. Lot LOT-0000: Services for the operation of a test centre. As digitalisation progresses in the state administration, the requirements for quality assurance are also increasing. This is because stable IT operations cannot be guaranteed without sufficiently tested - and therefore quality-assured - solutions. Statutory requirements regarding the security and accessibility of the provided procedures further increase the requirements. Against this background, HZD established the Test Center Hessen (TCH) in 2022 and has operated it since then as a central organisational unit for standardised test services. The Test Center Hessen acts as a central organisational unit for standardised test services and is guided in this by established industry standards and best practices, in particular ISO/IEC 29119 and ISTQB. The Test Center Hessen (TCH) of HZD offers internal and external customers tailor-made services relating to testing. In addition, there are comprehensive services in the form of individually combinable modules. The modules are structured in a largely standardised manner. They can be put together as required. The subject of this tender is the support of the already established and operationally active Test Center Hessen by external IT service providers. The aim of the test centre is in particular to increase software quality and reduce risks in the software lifecycle. To support these aims, the following services are required, among others: • Consulting relating to testing • Standardisation and automation of the testing procedure • Provision of test services in various subject areas (test management, test automation, test data management, load and performance tests, functional (manual) tests including technical quality assurance as well as accessibility tests, see section 4 of the specification of services) • Provision of templates and methods According to the current planning status and taking into account additional requirements of other specialist departments and offices, a total requirement of approx. 37.730 person-days (PD) is assumed for the maximum contract duration of up to 48 months (non-binding estimated quantity).

sig_d7aef53156a66c17afe2.description: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Denmark (MFA) is in the process of streamlining the management of its development cooperation. Part of this effort concerns the simplification of the procurement process of key consultancy services relating to development cooperation. Consultancy contracts are currently procured individually by the case worker responsible for the programme or project. Case workers are MFA staff from MFA services at home in Copenhagen and abroad. In the procurement of individual contracts, they are responsible for the choice of procurement modality, the planning, preparation and management of the tender and contracting process. This process is often lengthy, and can have implications on programme and project timelines. Moreover, the fragmentation of the process makes it difficult to use the feedback from case workers on the fulfilment of the assignments. This makes it challenging to harvest learning from past performance and ensure a sustained quality of services. It is in this context that the MFA wishes to consolidate the procurement of consultancy services through a framework agreement with multiple contractors. The streamlining of the management of Danish development cooperation entailed a revision of the Danida – Aid Management Guidelines (https://amg.um.dk/). This foresees a delegation of key tasks to external consultants, primarily appraisals, and thereby an expected rise in the number of consultancy services to be requested. It is therefore an opportune time to seek a more streamlined procurement process of consultancy services. AMGs contain the policies, guidelines, and tools for the MFA’s development cooperation assistance. They cover different forms of Danish development cooperation modalities. The AMG’s Bilateral Guidelines (https://amg.um.dk/bilateral-cooperation/guidelines-for-programmes-projects-country-strategic-frameworks-and-hard-earmarked-multilat-support) and Financial Management Guidelines (https://amg.um.dk/bilateral-cooperation/financial-management) constitute the basic set of procedures for all Danish bilateral development cooperation. The guidelines outline the processes and requirements for the preparation, formulation, quality assurance, approval, implementation, completion and closure of Danish bilateral programmes and projects. The framework agreement is expected to solely cover bilateral development cooperation programmes and projects designed and implemented by Denmark. Therefore, the expected scope of work of consultancy services solely pertains to Official Development Aid (ODA) funds. The framework agreement is also expected to be divided into two lots. Under each lot, the MFA expects to conclude a framework agreement with between three to seven contractor to establish the terms governing contracts to be awarded during the term of the framework agreement, specifically the terms for award of contracts with/without reopening of competition amongst the contractors on the framework agreement. The expected lots reflect the thematic areas and priorities of Denmark’s Strategy for Development Cooperation: Lot 1: Climate change, environment, private sector development, enabling environment and financing. Lot 2: Governance, response to conflicts, forced displacement, irregular migration, health and education. Each lot is expected to require the provision of the following services pertaining to the design and implementation phases of bilateral development cooperation programmes, namely: Formulation of bilateral programmes and projects. This may include preparatory work in the formulation process if and as needed. Appraisal of the design of bilateral programmes and projects as a quality assurance milestone prior to approval. This includes external appraisals and early appraisals of larger or high-risk programmes/projects. Review of bilateral programmes and projects under implementation. This can span inception, midterm and technical reviews as part of the MFA unit’s monitoring and reporting cycle. The estimated values of the procurement and the lots are preliminary estimates.
sig_d7aef53156a66c17afe2.title: Consultancy framework agreement for formulation, appraisal and review of Danish development cooperation programmes and projects

sig_d851fdac8434e5612e4d.description: SKI hereby invites tenders for a dynamic purchasing system for Specialist Systems (02.19 Specialist Systems) The system contains one procurement category: Specialist Systems, delivered as Software as a Service (SaaS). Specialist Systems are supplied as "Software as a Service" (SaaS). Users subscribe to the software and gain access to it via the internet or via the supplier's application programming interfaces. Specialist Systems must support case processing/task handling of one or more of the customers' tasks/services, within one or more of the service areas mentioned below. The customer's needs determine which service area or areas are covered by the specific procurement. A specific procurement may well cover several of the service areas listed below. Specialist Systems as SaaS are characterised by being "on-demand services" which are owned, developed, maintained, managed and operated by the supplier or by the service owner's subcontractor. Services must be fully developed. Consequently, no services can be offered in the dynamic purchasing system that are developed or further developed specifically for the customer. The content of the service must be suitable for use in the Danish public sector. In addition, a procurement of services must comprise the implementation of the service (handover upon supplier change of a service and start-up upon the new establishment of a service) as well as the termination of the service (in connection with the expiry of the delivery contract). Implementation and termination form part of the overall service. Services are thus generic, fully developed solutions that meet uniform needs across customers, although such that these can be simply and quickly scaled and configured to the specific customer's IT environment, e.g. in relation to capacity, number of users or user rights etc. Consequently, services cannot be procured in the dynamic purchasing system that are intended to be developed for the individual customer on the basis of the customer's needs. The system covers all services and performance in the procurement of specialist systems within the service areas specified below. The service areas are based on FORM services. Reference is made to Annex C for a review of the covered service areas. It is voluntary for all SKI customers, as listed in Annex B, Customer List, to make use of the dynamic purchasing system when they are to procure specialist systems "as a Service".
sig_d851fdac8434e5612e4d.title: Professional systems – Dynamic purchasing system (re-tender)

sig_d860e1ebd6ac5cf540a9.description: In the context of competitive tendering for regional rail lines, the Grand Est Region, the organising authority for regional rail transport, is becoming the owner of the regional rail service lines and the stations concerned. This is a framework agreement with subsequent contracts. The framework agreement is concluded for a fixed duration of six (6) years. It is renewable once for a duration of two (2) years. The services to be provided are divided into three lots: - Lot 1 - Land and financial support for the transfer of ownership of the regional rail service lines (LDFT). This is a framework agreement with subsequent contracts with no minimum amount and a maximum of 2 000 000 euros excluding VAT for the entire duration of the contract, including renewal. - Lot 2 - Land and financial support for the transfer of ownership of the maintenance and stabling depots, as well as for the acquisition or provision of sites with a view to creating a maintenance and stabling site. The lot concerns a framework agreement with subsequent contracts with no minimum amount and a maximum of 2 000 000 euros excluding VAT for the entire duration of the contract, including renewal. - Lot 3 - Drafting and publication of authentic deeds relating to the transfers of ownership of the LDFT and rolling stock maintenance and stabling depots. This is a framework agreement with subsequent contracts with no minimum amount and a maximum of 3 000 000 euros excluding VAT for the entire duration of the contract, including renewal. The service provider shall assist the SPL in the context of the transfer of ownership of the regional rail service lines (LDFT); The service provider shall assist the SPL in the context of the transfer of ownership of the maintenance and stabling depots as well as for the provision or acquisition of sites for the construction of Maintenance and Stabling Sites (SMR); The service provider shall assist the SPL in the context of the drafting and publication of authentic deeds concerning the transfers of ownership carried out for the LDFT and the SMR

sig_d899525985c0fb046ac7.description: The DVLA require expressions of interest for the Provision of Direct Debit Solution. The proposed route to market is the Government Commercial DPS (GCA) Open Banking (Data, Digital Payments & Confirmation of Payee Services) DPS - Lot 1. The estimated value of the contract is c£37,500,000 and the contract will run for a 5-year term. DVLA anticipate issuing the award letter in May 2027 with a contract start date of February 2028, which allows around 8 months for transition and mobilisation activities. To find out how to become a supplier on this commercial agreement, visit https://supplierregistration.cabinetoffice.gov.uk/dps/RM6301, download the 'Bid pack', and read the READ FIRST RM6301-DPS Needs. To apply, or to update your responses, click 'Access as a supplier' to login/register. Registration is free and there is no limit on the number of suppliers who can join this DPS Marketplace. The purpose of this Prior Information Notice (PIN) is to inform the market of this upcoming requirement and invite interested suppliers to attend a virtual market engagement event. This event will provide an opportunity for DVLA to outline its proposed requirements, gather market feedback and help inform the future procurement requirements. Background The DVLA is an Executive Agency of The Department for Transport (DfT), based in Swansea. The Agency's primary aims are to facilitate road safety and general law enforcement by maintaining accurate registers of drivers and vehicle keepers and to collect Vehicle Excise Duty (VED). A Direct Debit (DD) payment option was introduced from 1st October 2014 which enables End Users to currently pay the full annual VED amount in one annual instalment, pay for a 6-month licensing period in one instalment or opt to spread the costs evenly over the term of a 12-month licensing period. All options result in an automatic VED renewal, subject to all business requirements being met, unless the End User opts out of the DD scheme. - Currently, over 1.4 million mandates are created per month, this is split between circa new (40%) and renewed (60%) mandates. - On average, Direct Debit payments total approximately £230m a month. From 1 April 2028 a new requirement will be introduced to collect eVED (Electric Vehicle Excise Duty) it is a new mileage charge for electric and plug in hybrid cars. Market Engagement Event DVLA will host a virtual Market Engagement Event on 18 August 2026 and will consist of an overview session provided by DVLA for all attendees followed by 1-2-1 sessions at the request of suppliers. If you would like to attend the event or wish to reserve a 1-2-1 appointment, please register your interest by emailing sophie.willis@dvla.gov.uk and jason.thomas@dvla.gov.uk by 17:00pm on Thursday 6 August 2026. Please include the names and positions of the individuals you wish to attend. Following registration, DVLA will provide further details, including joining instructions and any relevant pre-event information.
sig_d899525985c0fb046ac7.title: Provision of Direct Debit Solution

sig_d9979f0b8c35ebe15197.description: NOTE! This is not a call for tenders, procurement notice or prior information notice, but a notice on the initiation of a market dialogue as part of procurement planning. Espoon kaupunki has initiated the preparation for the procurement of a shared vehicle monitoring tool and is inviting suppliers to a market dialogue. The objective of the procurement of the shared vehicle management tool is to implement monitoring in accordance with the micro-mobility permit (18 section) referred to in the Act on Transport Services (3030/2025) within the area of the City of Espoo. The management tool is used to collect and monitor shared vehicle movement data and to set operating rules and restrictions for them. The tool aims to improve urban safety and facilitate urban planning based on shared vehicle usage and regulatory data. The subject of the procurement is a shared vehicle monitoring tool procured as a service as follows: - System as a software-as-a-service (SaaS) - Commissioning and customisation of the service for Espoo - Application maintenance services - Further development and expert services of the system according to Espoo's needs. The functionalities of the shared vehicle monitoring tool are aimed to cover the following: - Basic functions of the management tool, i.e. collecting and displaying usage data of approximately 6000 shared vehicles to the user. - Real-time and visual user interface for monitoring shared vehicles, i.e. displaying map-based information regarding shared vehicles and traffic operators based on the location data of the shared vehicles to the user. - Setting area- and shared-vehicle-operator-specific rules and restrictions for shared vehicles, as well as providing the user with notifications based on the rules and restrictions. - Analysis functions of the collected data as well as scenario analyses (proposals) on rules and measures to be set based on the collected data. - Reporting and statistical functionalities. - Management of user roles and access rights. The purpose of the market dialogue is to survey the market situation regarding the procurement of the shared vehicle monitoring tool. Espoon kaupunki wants to hear potential suppliers' thoughts on the implementation of the procurement procedure and the preparation of the call for tenders. SCHEDULE FOR THE MARKET DIALOGUE The market dialogue will tentatively be conducted in two phases: 1. Via Teams tentatively during week 51. The contracting authority reserves the right to invite 3-5 suppliers to the first phase of the dialogue based on the responses to the request for information. The objective of this first phase is to familiarise oneself with the products on the market, for example through supplier demos. 2. Tender documents will be sent to those who have registered for the market dialogue for comments approximately during weeks 51-2. The second phase of the market dialogue will be conducted electronically. Written material will be sent to all those who have registered for the market dialogue for review approximately during weeks 51-2. The dialogue of the second phase will cover the content of the preliminary call for tenders, the requirement specification and the contractual terms. The contracting authority reserves the right to additional dialogues as the market survey progresses. sig_da733f462fe04eea8224.description: This is not a prior information notice, contract notice or call for tenders, but a notice on the initiation of a market dialogue as part of procurement planning and an invitation to participate in the market dialogue. Polkka - Pohjois-Karjalan tukipalvelut oy is a publicly owned service company that produces high-quality catering, cleaning and logistics services for its owners. The company's owners are the Wellbeing Services County of North Karelia, the towns of Joensuu, Kitee and Nurmes, and the municipalities of Heinävesi, Ilomantsi, Tohmajärvi and Liperi. Polkka operates throughout the region of North Karelia, and its administration is located in Joensuu. The company employs a total of approximately 800 staff. Through its operations, Polkka supports the daily lives and well-being of the region's residents by providing reliable and efficient support services. Polkka is planning a procurement procedure where the subject of the procurement is financial and personnel management services and the associated system package. The subject of the procurement includes financial and personnel management services as well as the implementation project for the system package, user rights, support and maintenance services, separately ordered supplementary expert services, and options for additional procurements. Polkka's financial and personnel management services are currently outsourced to Meidän IT ja Talous Oy. The services are managed in the systems administered by the service provider, the key components of which are Raindance, MRDP, Rondo and UDP in financial management and Populus, Titania, Timecon and RegWeb in personnel management. The procurement provisionally includes the following functions and high-level functionalities: Financial management - Superuser service - Basic data - Purchase invoices and purchase ledger - Sales invoicing and sales ledger - Accounting and financial statements - Payment traffic - Reporting and statistics - Financial planning and budgeting - Cash management - Treasury management - Internal accounting - Fixed assets - Electronic archiving Personnel management - Superuser service - Personnel and employment lifecycle management, HRM - Payroll, remuneration and rewarding - Rostering - Working time management - Travel management - Work ability and well-being as well as occupational health - Advanced reporting - Personnel performance and skills development, HRD - Recruitment - Electronic signature - Electronic archiving The procurement will be implemented through an open procedure. The preliminary schedule for the procurement is as follows: - Market dialogue rounds 3-5/2026 - Procurement 5-8/2026 - Implementation project 8-12/2026 Operators who have registered for the market dialogue and are interested in the procurement have the opportunity to answer preliminary questions raised by the contracting authority, participate in upcoming market dialogue sessions and comment on preliminary tender documents in technical dialogue. In the next phase of the market dialogue, five separate market dialogue sessions will be held via Teams. The market dialogue sessions will be held at the following times: - on Monday 13.4. between 8-15 - on Tuesday 14.4. between 12-16 - on Friday 17.4. between 10-16 If more than five operators interested in the procurement register for the market dialogue, the operators will be selected for the market dialogue sessions based on their answers to the preliminary questions. Operators participating in the market dialogue are requested to register, provide answers to the preliminary questions and submit the requested additional information by 7.4.2026 at 12 to the address: tuomas.vepsa@joensuu.fi. Registrations must be given the following subject line: "Ilmoittautuminen markkinavuoropuheluun: Tahe-hankinta". Registrations must include the following information: - Name of the participating company - Name, telephone number and email address of the contact person - Answers to preliminary questions - Names of the offered system or systems - Solution descriptions of the offered system or systems The sessions will be held via Microsoft Teams. We will send a separate invitation to the Teams meeting to everyone selected for the session. The market survey notice does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out an actual tendering procedure. The information presented in the market survey notice is preliminary, non-binding and indicative prior information. Answering or failing to answer the invitation to the market dialogue does not prevent participation in a possible tendering procedure. Information provided in the market dialogue does not bind the parties. No compensation is paid for participation in the market dialogue. Information provided by operators participating in the market dialogue will be treated confidentially, and the names or other information of the operators participating in the market dialogue will not be published.

sig_dab62d47fafb0b0c849e.description: DSB wishes to gain a better understanding of SAP RISE, and therefore an invitation to a market dialogue concerning this is extended. Background: DSB currently uses an SAP S/4HANA solution, which supports a large number of administrative business processes in the company. S/4HANA runs on-premises via an infrastructure and operations agreement with TCS. This agreement expires in the summer of 2028, which is why DSB must carry out an EU tender presumably in 2027. Against this background, DSB is considering whether the tender should comprise either: - Infrastructure and operation services regarding SAP S/4HANA based on on-premises or, - migration of DSB’s SAP S/4HANA solution to a SaaS solution in a private cloud – which is currently marketed under the name SAP RISE. Therefore, DSB wishes via market dialogue to gain insight into what suppliers in the market offer related to SAP RISE. DSB expects the individual supplier to provide a total overview of deliverables and commercial terms. DSB wishes, among other things, answers to: 1) Description of the current market. 2) Description of the supplier's footprint in the market. Generally and regarding SAP RISE. 3) Contract setup including interfaces to SAP SE. 4) Listing of services linked to the service: 4.1) Which services are delivered as standard? 4.2) Which services can be purchased additionally? 4.3) How are these services designed with regard to SLAs? 5) Description of cooperation model. 6) How and according to which structure does settlement of ongoing operations take place? 7) Description of model for transition and settlement of this. Preferably with TCO assessments. 8) Description of hardware, data centres, and geography used. 9) Description of IT security model and IT security management. DSB expects to conduct interviews with a selection of suppliers in December 2025 and January 2026. The purpose of the interviews is to gather information on which solutions and services are offered in the market. DSB plans to conduct market dialogue meetings with a maximum of six suppliers. If more than the six suppliers apply, DSB will make a representative selection among the expressions of interest received.
sig_dab62d47fafb0b0c849e.title: Invitation to market dialogue regarding SAP RISE
