sig_db1df9ef6a0b2f7619a1.description: THIS IS A PTAG SOURCES SOUGHT REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This PTAG 6.1.1 Sources Sought (request for information) Notice (RFI) is strictly for market research ONLY.? It is for informational and planning purposes and shall NOT be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation or commitment by the Government at this time. PTAG The Government contemplates utilizing the Alternative Competition Method in accordance with the Patent and Trademark Office Acquisition Guidelines (PTAG) and the Patent and Trademark Office Efficiency Act 35 U.S.C. 2(b)(4)(A). This Sources sought notice is intended as preliminary market information gathering which the United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) will use to determine which contractor(s) is/are the most likely to successfully meet the agency’s needs and are thereby eligible to participate in an alternative competition. As a result of this market research, the?solicitation will only be issued to the/ those qualified contractor(s) that is/are deemed most likely to successfully meet the agency’s requirements as stated below. This RFI is being made available under PSC U008 - EDUCATION/TRAINING- TRAINING/CURRICULUM DEVELOPMENT and NAICS: 611430 - Professional and Management Development Training REQUEST FOR INFORMATION – PTA TRAINING CONSULTATION, ELEARNING & DELIVERY BACKGROUND The United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) intends to make a firm-fixed price award to a single firm that can fulfill this requirement which includes three (3) major elements. Training Consultation for Program Revision; Development of eLearning Content; Training Delivery Support Services. USPTO’s Patent Training Academy is the training program responsible for preparing new hires to be patent examiners. It is designed to give new examiners the skills, knowledge, and confidence they need to begin their careers. In FY 2026, USPTO hired 963 new examiners. Currently, the training program is delivered over 10-weeks and is comprised of a 125-course curriculum. The program follows a university-style model that uses a mix of large-lectures and small group lab sessions to give examiners opportunity to apply what they have learned. Through a combination of the use of a practice training application, active learning exercises, lecture and dedicated examination time, the goal of the program is to provide patent examiner new-hires the needed competencies to successfully examine in a Technology Center (TC) with guidance from experienced examiners. OBJECTIVE The objective of this RFI is to seek capable contractors who could provide the USPTO with Training Consultation for Program Revision, Development of eLearning Content, and Training Delivery Support Services. sig_db4c659e2692f0df4bde.description: The overarching goal of this notice of funding opportunity (NOFO) and its companion opportunities is to establish the Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) Program to support development of innovative, reliable, cost-effective, and sustainable multimodal AI-based clinical decision support (CDS) tools. PRIMED-AI CDS tools are based on the integration of clinical imaging with other types of multimodal health data to enhance care for patients with a wide range of health conditions. The PRIMED-AI Program seeks to catalyze the adoption of AI-based CDS tools into clinical workflows to enable novel personalized medicine strategies that address significant health challenges. The purpose of this NOFO is to solicit applications for the creation of a Validation Center to serve as a dedicated hub for the comprehensive evaluation and characterization of AI-enabled, image-based, multimodal CDS tools developed by the PRIMED-AI Consortium, to ensure these tools are reliable, reproducible, and generalizable. The Validation Center will focus on verification, validation, interoperability, and uncertainty quantification to comprehensively characterize performance of the CDS tools developed by the program. The core functions of the Validation Center will involve the systematic validation of PRIMED-AI Consortium deliverables, including those emerging from award recipients under the Playbook, Data-to-Model Academic-Industrial Partnerships, and Model-to-Clinic NOFOs.
sig_db4c659e2692f0df4bde.title: Validation Center for Precision Medicine with AI: Integrating Imaging with Multimodal Data (PRIMED-AI) (U54 Clinical Trials Not Allowed)

sig_db5951a98f9d30d176d3.description: Welcome to submit tenders for Migrationsverket. Migrationsverket hereby invites suppliers to submit tenders in this procurement of a contact centre. The procurement relates to a new contact centre platform (hereinafter referred to as the System). The System shall handle the answering of telephone calls and e-mail messages from the general public and manage the routing and follow-up of incoming cases (emails and incoming calls). The System shall provide functionality for Callback and a module for scheduling. Queue and individual statistics shall also be handled in the System. After the implementation of the System is completed, approximately 200 concurrent agents and 20 administrators are estimated to work in the System. Migrationsverket receives approximately 1 400 000 incoming calls and 400 000 emails per year in the current contact centre system. The System needs to be dimensioned to cope with the demand, which may vary over time. The System shall be hosted as a private cloud service. The core functions of the System – that is, the management of calls, e-mails and the scheduling module – shall be hosted in a server hall owned or exclusively rented by the supplier (or its subcontractor) and this shall have its physical location within the EU/EEA. The supplier shall have full technical and administrative control over the hardware, network and operating platform in the server hall. Migrationsverket will provide a separate service for encrypting free text in incoming e-mail messages before they reach the System. This encryption service shall be hosted locally by Migrationsverket. The technical design of the service is not yet fully defined, but will be developed in dialogue with the supplier during the implementation project. The System shall be able to handle e-mail flows where free text content is encrypted upon receipt and decrypted close to the client in the agent's web browser through a component provided by Migrationsverket. The supplier is not responsible for the development or operation of this encryption service, but shall ensure that the System is technically compatible with its mode of operation and supports secure handling of encrypted e-mail messages in accordance with the specification of requirements. Integrations with the Windows environment and Migrationsverket's telephony operator shall be included. In the procurement, the tenderer shall tender: A private cloud service that is complete and fulfils the mandatory requirements set out in the procurement and the evaluation requirements accepted by the supplier.An implementation project that includes planning, integrations, configuration of system settings, fine-tuning and testing of the System to a fully operational condition.The System shall be set up in a test and training environment, as well as a production environment.Integrations with Migrationsverket's system, which appear in the Specification of Requirements.Necessary documentation for the implementation of integration(s).Documentation.Training.Option regarding, inter alia, a screen sharing function (co-browsing) and chat functionConsultancy services in connection with the System.Services for support, fault clearance and further development of the System
sig_db5951a98f9d30d176d3.title: Kontaktcenter

sig_db984e9fe7f8b57441ff.description: To map various ticketing processes, the State Office for Finance (LfF) requires a new ticketing system, which must be operated in the state-owned data centre of LDI (on-premise or in the rlp-Cloud). The new procedure is intended to replace the previously used SAP SOLUTION MANAGER 7.2 with the SP stack 20 - as of 11/2025 - and the previously used ticketing procedure Zammad. The new procedure is also intended to map tickets from other, non-SAP-based areas. The complete implementation of the new ticketing system (including the necessary connection to downstream systems, acceptance testing and multiplier training) is to take place by 31.07.2027. Productive use of the new ticketing system must therefore be ensured for all connected users (including users from other authorities in the federal state of Rhineland-Palatinate) from 01.08.2027 at the latest. Further details can be found in the attached procurement documents, in particular the specification of services, system environment and contract. Lot LOT-0001: Ticketing system. The subject of the procurement is the creation of the overall system described in the procurement documents, including the establishment of operational readiness by the contractor on the basis of a works contract, as well as system service and the further development of the overall system. The overall system consists of a client-specifically adapted, standard ticketing system software (on-premise or in the rlp-Cloud of LDI / rental) that meets the requirements of modern ticket processing by the client, including associated client-specifically created or adapted integrations into the client's IT system in accordance with the further regulations, in particular in accordance with the functional and technical specifications of the client, cf. specification of services. This includes, inter alia, the integration of the ticketing system software into the SAP landscape operated by the client, inter alia connection to transport management, the mapping of various evaluations and reports, the establishment of knowledge bases and migrations from various source systems. To produce the overall system, the software must, inter alia, be set up and configured, in particular user accounts created and data imported in accordance with the specification of services or system environment, the software connected via interfaces to various tools of the client, the required automation established, high interoperability with the named third-party systems established, tested, test instances set up and operated, and the onboarding process successfully completed, including interface integration with the third-party systems and training courses. Productive use after acceptance of the overall system must be contractually possible for all connected users of the client, cf. specification of services, by 01.08.2027. Further details can be found in the attached procurement documents, in particular the specification of services, system environment and contract.

sig_dba07f55a615cb284e3c.description: Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) Closed Two-Step BAA: SAF/FM Cost Estimating Modeling Data Analytics Research (CEMDAR) The Two-Step Process reduces acquisition resources for both the Government and industry. It may be considered when a large number of proposals are anticipated or to determine if further Government interest is warranted. If further interest is not warranted, industry saves unnecessary bid and proposal costs and the Government saves review time. Broad Agency Announcement Number FA7014-26-S-CS02 Announcement Title SAF/FM Cost Estimating Modeling Data Analytics Research (CEMDAR) Federal Agency Name Secretary of the Air Force Financial Management (SAF/FM) Announcement Type & Acquisition Set-Aside Initial Announcement | 100% Small Business Set-Aside NAICS Code & Size Standard 541745 (Small Business Size Standard: 1,000 employees) Estimated Program Ceiling $24,000,000 (Anticipated Awards: 1 single award) White Paper Submission Deadline October 19, 2026, 1300 hrs Eastern Time 1. Overview Information & Two-Step Solicitation Structure SAF/FM is soliciting white papers on the research effort described herein. White papers must be addressed to the Contracting Points of Contact (POCs). This solicitation is a Total Small Business Set-Aside under NAICS Code 541745. White papers and resultant proposals submitted shall strictly comply with this announcement. There will be no separate formal solicitation issued regarding this requirement. This BAA will be republished at yearly intervals for administrative updates and ease of reference. 1.1 Two-Step Acquisition Sequence Step 1 — White Paper Due Date & Submission: White papers may be electronically submitted upon issuance of this BAA until October 19, 2026, 1300 hrs Eastern Time. Only white papers are accepted at this stage. Submissions must be delivered electronically to AFDW/PK at eric.moss.3@us.af.mil and joseph.spear.1@us.af.mil. Step 2 — Formal Proposal Due Date & Time: Formal technical and cost proposals will be requested solely from offerors whose submitted white papers are evaluated as successfully meeting the operational and research needs of the Air Force. Late Receipt Provisions: White paper and proposal receipts after the specified cutoff date and time shall be governed strictly by the provisions of FAR 52.215-1(c)(3). 1.2 Instrument Types and Contracting Guidance The Air Force reserves the right to award the contractual instrument best suited to the nature of the research proposed. Accordingly, the Government may award any appropriate contract type under the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), Other Transaction (OT) for Prototype authority, Grant, Cooperative Agreement, OT for Research, or an applicable technology transfer mechanism. Awards under this BAA are generally anticipated to be cost-reimbursement. Offerors are specifically advised that cost-reimbursement contracts require an accounting system determined adequate by the Government for tracking allocable contract costs. 1.3 Communications & Contracting Points of Contact Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is strongly encouraged prior to proposal submission. Technical discussions shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to fund or award any proposed effort. Only warranted Contracting Officers possess the legal authority to commit the Government. Inquiries regarding this solicitation should be directed to the Contracting POCs: Primary Contracting Officer: Eric Moss — eric.moss.3@us.af.mil Alternate Contracting Officer: Joseph Spear — joseph.spear.1@us.af.mil 2. Section I — Program Description & Strategic Objectives The Department of the Air Force (DAF) has identified critical operational gaps in the enterprise databases, analytical methods, and predictive tools regularly employed for weapon system cost estimating and analysis. DAF is actively committed to modernizing the efficiency, fidelity, and throughput of its cost estimating capabilities. This requirement invests in strengthening, accelerating, and elevating cost data and analytic capabilities using modern data science and cloud engineering technologies to enable faster, higher-quality, and higher-volume analytic decision support across the DAF cost community. The CEMDAR research initiative executes four fundamental architectural shifts across enterprise cost operations: Platform Modernization: Transitioning from legacy desktop-based analytical tools to secure enterprise cloud platforms (e.g., DAF Data Fabric, VAULT, Envision). Relational Data Integration: Moving from isolated, commodity-specific datasets to integrated, relational architectures linking programmatic, technical, cost, and schedule parameters. Pipeline Automation: Replacing static spreadsheets and recurring manual reporting with dynamic, automated data engineering pipelines. Scalable Predictive Modeling: Advancing from low-volume static cost modeling to highly scalable data collection, curation, machine learning, and empirical analytics. 2.1 Strategic Research Objectives Elevating Data Fidelity: Improving the verifiable quality, authenticity, granularity, and volume of empirical data collected and accessible to DAF cost analysts. Relational Enterprise Databases: Engineering centralized, enterprise-level relational cost, schedule, and technical databases adhering to rigorous data science principles and MIL-STD-881 standards. Analytical Workflow Optimization: Constructing capabilities and streamlined workflows that empower analysts to rapidly synthesize large-scale multi-commodity datasets. Predictive Modeling & Decision Support: Establishing authoritative enterprise datasets and generating dynamic Cost Estimating Relationships (CERs), Schedule Estimating Relationships (SERs), Technical Estimating Relationships (TERs), benchmark metrics, interactive dashboards, and cloud-native cost models. The overarching vision is not only to elevate the timeliness and accuracy of program Life-Cycle Cost Estimates (LCCEs) for budgeting, programming, and acquisition milestone decisions, but also to build an agile capability for rapid high-level force design, alternative architecture trades, and component-level engineering trade-off evaluations. 3. Section II — Technical Description & Core Competencies The Department of the Air Force Cost Analysis Agency (AFCAA) is soliciting white papers (and subsequently formal technical and cost proposals from qualified respondents) addressing innovative synchronization of research related to technical, cost and schedule for DoW/DAF programs across the following five Core Competencies. Submitted white papers must move beyond generic capability statements and clearly articulate the offeror's specific technical approach, proposed system architectures and analytical methodologies. Offerors should include concrete examples of relevant past work, demonstrating proven experience in designing data pipelines, executing predictive cost modeling, and conducting targeted cost specific research within defense or similarly regulated enterprise environments. To ensure holistic technical execution, white papers must also address the following staffing and expertise qualifications: Key Personnel Competencies & Experience: Offerors must explicitly summarize the core technical competencies, relevant project experience, and security clearance/access readiness of proposed Key Personnel—specifically the Contractor Program Manager (PM), the Chief Cost Data Scientist (governing Task 2 Level 1 architectural decisions and CADOM pipelines), and any designated Technical / Data Science Task Leads—substantiating the leadership team's qualification to direct contract activities from Day 1. On-Demand Cost & Commodity Subject Matter Experts (SMEs): Offerors must demonstrate an established, agile capability to deploy specialized Cost and Technical Domain SMEs on an as-required basis. These experts must possess deep commodity and engineering expertise to support targeted cost studies, schedule analyses, and novel data pipeline mapping across diverse defense domains—including Aircraft, Space and Launch Systems, Missiles and Munitions, C4ISR, Cyber and Software Systems, and Operations and Support (O&S) Sustainment. 3.1 Core Competency 1: Enterprise Data Governance, Access, and Research Lifecycle Planning (envisioned PWS Tasks 1 & 2) Task 1 — Data Access Permissions, Proprietary Information Protection, and OCI Governance: Establishes the administrative, legal, and multi-tier security foundation required to ingest proprietary defense data. Offerors must structure and manage Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs) across AFCAA, OSD CAPE (for the Cost Assessment Data Enterprise [CADE] repository), Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs), and prime/subcontractor tiers. Because weapon system cost repositories contain business-sensitive Proprietary Information (PROPIN), tasks require rigorous OEM engagement protocols, proactive OCI screening, and monitoring to eliminate conflicts resulting from corporate reorganizations or contractor commercial affiliations. Task 2 — Integrated Research Planning, POA&M Execution, and Agile Governance: This area establishes a centralized, contractor-maintained Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) serving as the operational roadmap governing all contract activities. The integrated POA&M must establish element-level execution schedules, critical path milestones, risk mitigation triggers, and formal go/no-go evaluation gates integrating all technical efforts: foundational data governance and ingestion, automated Medallion pipeline curation (Task 3), empirical studies and predictive model building (Task 4), acquisition database modernization (Task 5), and surge research directives. To ensure seamless technical integration without compromising Government oversight, offerors must establish a disciplined governance framework that strictly delineates contractor operational management from inherently governmental authority: Contractor Operational Governance: Led by the Chief Cost Data Scientist and Contractor PM, the contractor manages internal agile execution, sprint velocity, data quality gates, and Level 1 Architectural Decisions (internal pipeline scripting, routine algorithms, and code refactoring). The contractor must maintain an Integration and Dependency Matrix linking Task 4 analytical use cases directly to underlying Task 3 data pipelines. Government Technical Oversight: The Government retains all approval and baseline acceptance authority. The AFCAA Technical Lead / COR approves Level 2 Decisions (changes to enterprise data schemas, cloud infrastructure, or CADOM standards), while Level 3 Decisions (cross-agency data sharing and multi-service standards) require stakeholder consensus (AFCAA, OSD CAPE, and Service Cost Centers). 3.2 Core Competency 2: Automated Data Pipeline Engineering & Enterprise Architecture (envisioned PWS Task 3) Cost Analysis Data Operating Model (CADOM) & Medallion Pipeline Architecture: Focuses on architecting, testing, and operationalizing scalable ETL/ELT pipelines unifying disparate programmatic, technical, cost, and schedule data streams into an enterprise CADOM schema. Utilizing modern technologies (Apache Spark, Databricks, Python, SQL, cloud data warehouses), pipelines implement a multi-stage medallion architecture: Bronze (raw ingestion), Silver (cleansed, schema-validated, normalized records), and Gold (curated, high-performance analytical views). Work mandates automated quality gates, comprehensive error-handling and telemetry logging, and full audit lineage tracing Gold metrics back to source records. Target feeds include Cost and Software Data Reporting (CSDR/FlexFile), Selected Acquisition Reports (SAR/MSAR), Earned Value Management (EVM/IPMDAR), Air Force Total Ownership Cost (AFTOC), and defense budget exhibits. Enterprise Metadata Schema, Data Lineage, and Catalog Services: Maintains and enriches centralized metadata models, embedding automated tagging routines during ingestion to tag program identifiers, commodity domains, and MIL-STD-881 Work Breakdown Structures (WBS). Develops searchable data catalog services (e.g., Unity Catalog, Foundry), implements Data Fidelity Scorecards measuring authenticity and normalization readiness, and enforces granular role-based access control (RBAC) and attribute-based access control (ABAC) across proprietary and classified boundaries. Enterprise Analytical Applications & AI/ML Data Infrastructure: Builds cross-cutting analytic applications and ML pipelines, such as cross-commodity benchmarking engines, automated NLP-driven WBS mapping from historical CSDR submissions, and Silver-layer anomaly detection routines. Manages version-controlled infrastructure-as-code and reproducible deployment scripts inside government-controlled Git repositories. 3.3 Core Competency 3: Data-Driven Analytics, Predictive Modeling, and Application Deployment (envisioned PWS Task 4) This technical area encompasses research, predictive modeling, and application deployment executed through approved subtasks in the POA&M. Depending on operational objectives, subtasks will combine data analysis, dynamic model development, custom tool engineering, and targeted empirical studies: Dynamic Analysis, Predictive Modeling & Empirical Studies: Applies regression, econometrics, machine learning, and Bayesian methods to develop dynamic models, empirical CERs, SERs, TERs, and cost growth benchmarks. Research covers core weapon system commodities—Aircraft (Fixed/Rotary/Unmanned), Space & Launch, Missiles, Cyber/Software, and Operations & Support (O&S) sustainment. Focus areas include, for example, expenditure time-phasing, flight test benchmarks, commercial space cost adjustments, agile software metrics, and AI-generated code productivity/defects. Custom Analytical Applications & CADOM Deployment: Designs, packages, and deploys user-facing tools, calculation workbooks, and interactive dashboards connected directly to CADOM pipelines. Automates repetitive estimating workflows (e.g., inflation/escalation, price normalization, trade-off analysis). In alignment with the Integration and Dependency Matrix, models and containerized applications must comply with CADOM standards and include reproducible code and technical documentation. 3.4 Core Competency 4: Specialized Acquisition Databases and Statutory Cost Reporting Administration (envisioned PWS Task 5) Task 5 (Option CLIN) — AFCAA Contracts Database (KDB) Modernization and Analysis: Modernizes and hosts the enterprise AFCAA Contracts Database within cloud platforms (e.g., VAULT). Fuses procurement data from SAM.gov, FPDS, EDA, and USA Spending with internal metadata models (CSDR, SAR, EVM). Constructs BI pipelines, refines contract growth classification buckets, conducts Engineering Change Order (ECO) analyses to isolate cost drivers, issues quarterly database releases to CADE users, and delivers hybrid user training. 3.5 Core Competency 5: Mission Augmentation and Surge Analytical Capabilities (envisioned PWS Task 6) Task 6 (Option CLIN) — RDT&E Surge Research and Rapid Prototyping Support: Pre-negotiated surge mechanism to rapidly deploy specialized cost estimators, data scientists, machine learning engineers, and technical SMEs for high-priority emergent research, algorithm development, and novel methodology prototyping requiring RDT&E funding. 4. Section III — Contractual, Security, and Administrative Requirements Within Scope Modifications: Due to the inherent uncertainty of research and development efforts, awards resulting from this announcement may be modified during performance to execute within-scope adjustments, including modifications to increase contract ceiling. 4.1 Period of Performance and Deliverable Schedule The anticipated period of performance spans 12 to 60 months for the technical effort, tailored to individual award determinations. Hardware and specialized software items shall be determined per contract award. Deliverable Category Contractual Requirement Governing Standard / Delivery Frequency Period of Performance 12 to 60 months total duration Tailored to contract award and CLIN structure Data Items (CDRLs) Research reports, POA&Ms, schemas Specified in resultant Contract Work Statement Software / Codebase Data pipelines, containerized tools Delivered to government repositories; Open/Gov Rights Quarterly Releases AFCAA KDB and CADOM deployments Quarterly release cycles into VAULT/CADE environments 4.2 Security, OPSEC, and Export Control Compliance Facility & Personnel Clearance: Program classification requirements span up to and including Top Secret (refer to RFP DD Form 254). Offerors must maintain an active Facility Clearance and ensure current Cognizant Security Office records are registered with DCSA (www.dcsa.mil). All proposed Key Personnel must hold and maintain an active SECRET security clearance at contract award, and offerors must demonstrate that they have immediate access to personnel that possess the access capability to utilize TOP SECRET / SCI clearances and facilities as required for classified studies and task directives. All non-key contractor and subcontractor personnel assigned to this contract must possess, at a minimum, a favorably completed and adjudicated Tier 2 (T2) background investigation (or higher) on Day 1 of contract performance to support Moderate-Risk Public Trust (MRPT) and Common Access Card (CAC) / system access requirements. ). TS/SCI work is anticipated to be a small fraction of the overall work in year 1 but could vary each year as requirements evolve. Operations Security (OPSEC): Contractors and subcontractors must implement Industrial Security, Information Security, Personnel Security, and OPSEC measures to protect critical program data from adversary exploitation and export breaches. Export Control & ITAR: Technical information generated or utilized may be subject to ITAR (22 CFR 120-131) and EAR (15 CFR 710-774). Where applicable, a Certified DD Form 2345 (Militarily Critical Technical Data Agreement) must accompany formal proposals. DFARS 252.225-7048 applies to all resulting awards. Contractor Performance Assessment (CPARS): Interim annual evaluations and a final evaluation will be conducted. Contractors are provided 14 calendar days to review and submit rebuttals before final determinations by the authority one level above the Contracting Officer. 4.3 Logistics, Base Support, and Intellectual Property Rights Government-Furnished Property (GFP) / Equipment (GFE): In accordance with Section VI of the PWS, the Government will furnish standard encrypted laptops, required application software licenses, and cloud platform tenant environments (e.g., DAF VAULT / Data Fabric) for authorized contractor personnel performing work under resulting awards. Provisioning will occur within 10–15 business days following security badge issuance. No additional GFP/GFE is anticipated; any extra equipment requested in an offeror's proposal must be pre-approved by the Contracting Officer. Primary contract performance will occur at contractor facilities. However, the Government will provide on-site base access, workspace, and local network connectivity for contractor personnel designated to work on-site or attend recurring program reviews at government locations in the National Capital Region (NCR), and other AFCAA Operating locations as necessary. 4.4 Data Rights and Commercial Software Licensing The Government desires the following data rights determinations: Noncommercial Technical Data: Unlimited Rights. Noncommercial Computer Software (NCS) & Documentation: Unlimited Rights. Commercial Computer Software: Customary Commercial License consistent with Federal procurement statutes. Final data rights will be determined during contract negotiations in accordance with RFO and R-DFARs. Third-party commercial and noncommercial software not reasonably identifiable at proposal submission must be formally approved by the Contracting Officer or Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) prior to incorporation. Software licenses transferred to the Government must not disclaim all warranties via ‘as is’ provisions, must permit use across Air Force and support contractor facilities, and must allow code embedding/derivative works. Licensors must agree to incorporate standard federal preemption terms nullifying any provisions inconsistent with Federal law. 5. Section IV — Proposal Preparation and Evaluation Review This solicitation executes a Two-Step selection process. White papers and proposals must adhere strictly to the guidelines outlined below. The Government reserves the right to review white papers and fund some, all, or none of the proposals received. ONLY WHITE PAPERS ARE BEING SOLICIATED AT THIS TIME. 5.1 Eligibility Information Eligible Offeror: This is a 100% Small Business Set-aside. Cost Sharing or Matching: Cost Sharing is not required. Government Agencies: If a Government agency is interested in performing work, contact the Contracting Officer identified in the BAA. If those discussions result in a mutual interest to pursue your agency's participation, the effort will be pursued independent of this announcement. Other: Foreign Participation: SAF/FM is authorized to exclude all foreign participation at the prime contractor level for the subject procurement. Foreign participation will be addressed for each white paper that have the potential to best meet the Air Force’s needs based on the white paper evaluation information in Section V. Notice to Foreign-Owned Firms: Such firms are asked to immediately notify the Contracting Officer before deciding to respond to this announcement. Foreign contractors should be aware that restrictions might apply which could preclude their participation in this acquisition. There are no limits on the number of white papers/proposals an offeror may submit. You may be ineligible for award if all requirements of this solicitation are not met on the white paper (and later proposal) due date as identified above. 5.2 Step 1: White Paper Submission Format White papers must be structured into four distinct, concise sections. Total of all sections combined should be no more than 30 pages: Offerors must format white paper submissions in accordance with the standard guidelines below. Requirements are kept intentionally streamlined to minimize proposal preparation burden while ensuring equitable technical evaluation. Page Format & Margins: All pages must be formatted for standard 8.5" x 11" paper with a minimum of one-inch (1.0") margins on all four borders. Page orientation must be portrait. Typography & Line Spacing: Narrative text must be single-spaced using Times New Roman (minimum 12-point), Arial (minimum 10-point), or Calibri (minimum 11-point). Text within tables, figures, charts, and diagrams may be reduced to a minimum of 8-point font, provided all content remains legible at 100% zoom. Electronic File Formats: White papers must be submitted electronically via email as a single, searchable Adobe Portable Document Format (pdf) file. The Cost Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) may also include an optional, unlocked Microsoft Excel (.xlsx) workbook showing active formulas and calculations. Do not submit .zip compressed archives or password-protected files. Header/Footer Information: Headers and footers may fall within margin boundaries and must include the BAA number (FA7014-26-S-CS02), company name, CAGE code, and sequential page numbering ("Page X of Y"). Page Limitations: Pages shall be numbered starting with the cover page being Page 1, and the last page being no greater than Page 30. The Government may remove and not evaluate any pages that exceed the established limitations. Section A — Administrative & Corporate Metadata: BAA Number, Title of Research Effort, Company Name, Business Size, CAGE code, DUNS/UEI number, and Company Technical & Contracting POCs (with direct telephone numbers and email addresses). Section B — Technical Approach & Capability Summary: Statement of task objectives; detailed technical methodology demonstrating alignment with Core Competencies 1 through 5; concrete examples of past work demonstrating automated pipeline engineering and predictive cost modeling; and a concise staffing summary detailing: The qualifications, core competencies, relevant experience, and clearance status of proposed Key Personnel; and The offeror's established approach for providing on-demand Cost and Commodity Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) across weapon system domains as task assignments require. Section C — Cost & Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM): Comprehensive ROM cost estimate reflecting labor, data infrastructure, and travel necessary to execute the proposed research. Section D — Associate Contractor Agreements (ACAs): Identification of anticipated ACA frameworks required to exchange proprietary technical data, software code, and research assets among multiple defense contractors. 5.3 Step 1: White Paper Review Criteria MANDATORY EVALUATION GATE: Only white papers submitted by respondents possessing an active and verifiable Facility Security Clearance (FCL) at the TOP SECRET level (issued and recorded in the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency [DCSA] National Industrial Security System [NISS] at the time of white paper submission will be reviewed by the Government. Submissions lacking verification of an active Top Secret FCL at the time of submission will be rejected without consideration. Teaming Arrangements and Joint Ventures: In any contractor teaming arrangement or Joint Venture (JV), the Prime Contractor must independently hold an active Secret FCL at submission. Cleared entities within the proposed teaming arrangement possessing the requisite FCL must perform at least fifty percent (50%) of the direct labor/technical effort. A cleared subcontractor may not on its own fulfill this requirement on behalf of an uncleared prime contractor. Day-1 Vetting Readiness Attestation: Offerors must certify in Section A of their white paper that: All proposed Key Personnel hold active SECRET security clearances at contract award; All labor planned for Day-1 contract performance possesses, at a minimum, a favorably completed and adjudicated Tier 2 (T2) background investigation (or higher); and The offeror possesses verified access capability to deploy appropriately cleared TOP SECRET / SCI analysts as required for classified projects and studies (e.g., representative efforts identified in PWS Appendix A or subsequent POA&M task directives). Technical Relevance: Is the proposed technical approach rigorously consistent with the research domains and technologies listed in this BAA? Government Interest: Does the proposed technical methodology address urgent analytical gaps and provide high-value decision support to SAF/FM and AFCAA? Fiscal Viability: Is appropriate research and operational funding available to support the proposed scope and period of performance? 5.4 Step 2: Full Proposal Preparation & Evaluation Offerors receiving favorable white paper evaluations will receive an official Request for Proposal (RFP) detailing Step 2 technical and cost submission instructions, review criteria, and formal deliverable requirements. Offerors will be notified regarding recommendation for full proposal submission on or about 30 calendar days following white paper receipt. 5.5 Statutory and Administrative Disclosures Acquisition of Commercial Items: The Government is not utilizing FAR Part 12 policies for this solicitation. Interested firms may submit commercial capability statements within 15 calendar days of notice issuance. Support Contractor Participation: Government employees will conduct all evaluations. Commercial contractor personnel providing administrative support to AFDW/PK are bound by non-disclosure agreements protecting proprietary data. Debriefing & Feedback Sessions: Offerors may request a debriefing session consistent with governing BAA and FAR acquisition procedures. Responsibility Matters (FAR 52.209-9): Applies to awards exceeding $600,000 where affirmative responsibility matters are checked under FAR 52.209-7. Proposal Adequacy Checklist: Pursuant to DFARS 215.408, proposals requiring certified cost or pricing data must include the completed DFARS 252.215-7009 Proposal Adequacy Checklist.

sig_dc7d4b0214ccaf561bc6.description: The Landesverband Lippe, a public-law body, intends to modernise the Externsteine information centre and stage the surrounding area in Horn-Bad Meinberg digitally as an integrated "Externsteine Experience World". The Externsteine, which attract around 600.000 visitors per year, are to be further developed into a sustainable, interactive and low-barrier experience venue. The visitor centre, which is currently not accessible and technically obsolete, forms the central starting and experience point. Lot LOT-0001: LVL Externsteine. The subject of the procurement is the modernisation of the Externsteine information centre and the digital staging of the surrounding area into an integrated "Externsteine Experience World". What is being procured is a concept together with its implementation, meaning on the one hand the conceptualisation including all planning services and official approval and authorisation procedures, and on the other hand the complete implementation including any construction services, IT services and further services (such as support and training). The contract is awarded as a staged contract: Upon the award of contract, solely stage 1 (drawing up of the concepts) is commissioned, whereas the implementation services (stage 2) as well as the granting of licences, technical support and training (stage 3) are tendered as options, on the calling-off of which the contracting authority decides within five months after acceptance of stage 1. The concept, the planning of the implementation and the implementation itself are to be designed freely by the contractor, but must meet certain minimum requirements based on the actual situation coupled with the available budget and the statutory provisions. General requirements: - The Externsteine and the entire surrounding area are subject to nature conservation, and all services to be conceptualised must be consistent with the requirements arising therefrom. The contractor must ensure that both the concept already and the complete implementation comply with all nature conservation law requirements. This also includes all necessary measures taken for the implementation of the concept. - The historical documents and data on the Externsteine are provided by the Landesverband Lippe and the Externsteine Conservation Association and are not to be compiled by the contractor, but are to be prepared didactically and scenographically, digitalised and compiled depending on the type of use. - This project is funded in part by a subsidy from the State of NRW and is therefore to be conceptualised and implemented in such a way that all funding law provisions are fully complied with. - A Progressive Web App or a mobile app for iOS and Android is to be conceptualised, programmed and made available for download in the common app stores, which contains natural history, geological and historical information on the Externsteine and depicts the area including paths and sights, and the app must also contain the link to the homepage so that current information can be accessed directly. Further content is to be conceptualised and implemented by the contractor. Further functions that allow visitors to experience the site actively must be present - a WhatsApp scavenger hunt is to be conceptualised as well - Every software must be compatible at least with ChromeOS and Windows 11 or higher, if available at the time of performance - every hardware must be compatible at least with ChromeOS, additional compatibility with Microsoft Windows 11 or higher, if available at the time of performance, is desirable. Information centre requirements: - Insertion of inspection openings everywhere where information technology is installed and/or will be installed - Replacement of obsolete hardware - Utilisation of the existing screen openings in the walls and the central X made of painted wood - No structural changes to the basic structure of the rooms - Preservation of the analogue stations in the display cases - Installation (indoor) including furnishing with software, licences and a moderation dashboard of a social wall; the moderation is taken over by the Landesverband Lippe - At least production and installation of a tactile relief of the Externsteine formation and the Descent from the Cross relief as a 3D print - Revision and modernisation as well as new creation of digital content including didactic aspects - Expansion of the use of the cinema - Digital content must be provided on physical data carriers (USB sticks, locally on a PC) in order to enable simple exchange and to be able to offer an integrated visitor experience even in the event of an internet outage; the file formats must be playable independently of the operating system - Excluded from this are contents whose existence is purely online (SocialWall, App) - Creation of barrier-free access to contents - Reliable and easily analysable visitor counter - Sign stating that the measure is subsidised according to the specification from the approval notice. Further specific requirements can be found in sections V and VI of the specification of services (Appendix B01). The project is financed in part from public subsidy funds. Binding under funding law are a total budget of 620.000 EUR (thereof 372.000 EUR subsidised, distributed across financial years 2026 and 2027) as well as a cost breakdown of 255.000 EUR furnishings/scenography, 25.000 EUR construction costs and 340.000 EUR technology costs. All services are to be rendered by the end of calendar year 2027. The basis of the contract is an EVB-IT cloud contract and an EVB-IT system contract.
sig_dc7d4b0214ccaf561bc6.title: LVL Externsteine

sig_dcc46098575b55940870.description: Supply of thermal orthophotos for the area of Region Hannover 1. Background The Region Hannover has set itself the ambitious goal of being climate-neutral by the year 2035. The energy-efficient refurbishment of the building stock is a central component for achieving this goal. In particular, improving the thermal insulation of buildings offers considerable potential for reducing CO2 emissions and increasing energy efficiency. In order to raise awareness among owners of residential and non-residential buildings regarding potential heat losses and refurbishment needs, a comprehensive thermal imaging map is to be created. The aim is to create a low-threshold information basis through a visually prepared presentation of thermal radiation data. The interactive online map should make it possible to classify one's own building stock in a regional context and initiate further steps if necessary. By linking with the advisory services of the climate protection agency Region Hannover (KSA) as well as existing funding programmes, the project is intended to trigger concrete refurbishment measures. 2. Contents and procedure The subject of the contract is the supply of thermographic digital orthophotos (DOP), i.e., distortion-free and georeferenced thermography recordings, for the area of Region Hannover. The contractor's delivery service includes carrying out the flight including preparation as well as the transmission of the processed data.
sig_dcc46098575b55940870.title: Supply of thermal orthophotos for the area of Region Hannover

sig_dddffdfb7fbbaa3d2f49.description: DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCUREMENT AND MARKET DIALOGUE The subject of the planned procurement is the acquisition of expert services for the establishment, development and operation of a centralized AI and Data Factory service (hereinafter the “AI & Data Factory”). The AI and Data Factory will support the Contracting Entity in developing, deploying, maintaining and continuously improving data, artificial intelligence, machine learning and analytics solutions and capabilities throughout their lifecycle. The AI and Data Factory service may include, but is not limited to, the following services: Decision Intelligence and Data Platform services Design, development, testing, deployment and continuous lifecycle management of Decision Intelligence solutions, including business intelligence, data science, machine learning, deep learning, generative AI and agentic AI, as well as related data platform capabilities. The services may include, for example: - design and implementation of data, business intelligence, advanced analytics, machine-learning and AI solutions; - continuous development, maintenance, monitoring and lifecycle management of Decision Intelligence solutions; - continuous validation and quality assurance, including model behaviour, outputs, end-result quality, data quality and data usage; - development, deployment and operation of AI and AI agent governance practices; - development, operation and continuous improvement of data platforms; and - other AI-, data-, analytics- and technology-related expert and consulting services supporting the objectives of the procurement. Data Governance and Management services Data governance and data management services may be provided as part of projects, continuous development activities and ongoing data management operations. The services may include, for example: - external data sourcing, data content development, data validation and data migration; - continuous data quality monitoring and improvement; and - development, implementation and follow-up of master data management processes for agreed data domains. The services are expected to be delivered in close collaboration with the Contracting Entity’s internal experts and other suppliers. The preliminary allocation of responsibilities between the Contracting Entity and the Supplier or Suppliers will be further specified based on the procurement preparation and market dialogue. The Contracting Entity intends to select 3 - 5 or more Suppliers. The final procurement and service delivery model, including the number of Suppliers and the allocation of responsibilities, will be determined during the preparation of the procurement. OBJECTIVES OF THE MARKET DIALOGUE The Contracting Authority seeks market input on the planned scope of the procurement, service model, preliminary service descriptions, procurement structure, competence requirements, commercial models and other elements relevant to the successful establishment and operation of the AI Factory. Suppliers are encouraged not only to comment on the Contracting Authority's preliminary proposals, but also to challenge the proposed approaches and suggest alternative, innovative or more effective solutions and operating models based on their experience, market practices and emerging AI capabilities. The Contracting Authority particularly welcomes ideas that may improve the scope, structure, flexibility, scalability, commercial model or long-term effectiveness of the procurement. The purpose of the market dialogue is to utilize market expertise in developing the procurement and to ensure that the final approach is feasible, proportionate, future-proof and aligned with market capabilities, while enabling innovation and the effective adoption of evolving AI technologies, services and operating models. PRELIMINARY TIMETABLE - Market dialogue: H2/2026 - Publication of the Invitation to Tender: Q1/2026 - Evaluation of tenders: H1/2027 - Procurement decision: H1/2027 - Contract commencement: H1/2027 ADDITIONAL INFORMATION This notice is a Prior Information Notice. It is not a contract notice or a call for tenders. The Prior Information Notice includes an invitation to participate in a market dialogue. All interested suppliers are invited to participate in technical discussions with the Contracting Entity concerning the planned procurement. The purpose of the dialogue is to discuss the procurement at a general level and to obtain market feedback on the proposed scope and definition of the procurement. Suppliers interested in participating in the market dialogue are requested to submit their expression of interest by email to tommi.aarnio@vr.fi no later than 28 September 2026 at 12:00 noon (Finnish time). Participation in the market dialogue does not oblige the Contracting Entity to proceed with the procurement, nor does it oblige suppliers to participate in any subsequent tendering procedure. Interested suppliers will be provided with preliminary procurement materials and/or questions for review and comments. The Contracting Entity may organize written consultation rounds, joint market dialogue sessions and, where considered appropriate, bilateral meetings with selected suppliers. The Contracting Entity reserves the right to amend the scope, content, procurement model, timetable and market dialogue process during the preparation of the procurement. No compensation will be paid to suppliers for participating in the market dialogue or for providing comments.
sig_dddffdfb7fbbaa3d2f49.title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: AI & Data Factory - Expert Services for AI and Data Development, Governance and Continuous Operations

sig_dde1696066b8d991bfd1.description: The objective is to manage user identities, roles, and permissions centrally, in an automated and audit-proof manner in the future. The scope of services includes the provision of the IAM software, complete implementation and integration into the existing IT infrastructure, the migration of existing data, comprehensive testing, and ongoing German-language support. The solution must be operated entirely within the ALDB infrastructure. The licences are to be provided for a minimum term of two years, with a maximum of four years. Functionally required are, in particular, joiner, mover, and leaver processes, role and permission management, access requests, approval workflows, identity governance, administration, reporting, audit logging, and interfaces to existing systems such as Active Directory, HR systems, databases, and Kubernetes environments. In addition, a secure backup and recovery concept, a minimum availability of 95 % per month, and regulated training and acceptance processes are provided for. Operational go-live is to take place following a successful test and acceptance phase, at the latest by 01.12.2026. An exit concept must be provided for the end of the contract. The project comprises the following service components: a) Provision of the IAM software solution (on-premise) The contractor must provide the offered Identity & Access Management (IAM) solution as an on-premise solution. This includes all software licences, including all modules and functionalities required to fulfil the functional, technical, and security-related requirements defined in this specification of services. Licencing must enable the management of the intended number of user identities, roles, permissions, target systems, and applications, as well as demand-driven scaling to support future expansions of ALDB's IT landscape. b) Consulting services, implementation, and integration The contractor is responsible for the complete planning, implementation, configuration, parameterisation, integration, commissioning, test support, and professional and technical guidance throughout the entire project duration. The scope of services includes, in particular, the integration of the IAM solution into ALDB's existing IT infrastructure, including the connection of all agreed source and target systems, Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, Kubernetes environments, and other business-critical applications. Furthermore, the organisational structure, the role and permission concept, identity lifecycle management, provisioning and de-provisioning processes, approval workflows, access requests, recertification processes, and audit and reporting functions are to be implemented and configured. All implementation and integration work must be carried out in such a way that ALDB's ongoing business operations are not impaired. c) Testing Following the award of the contract and prior to operational go-live, a test environment must be provided that largely corresponds to the subsequent productive environment. Comprehensive functional, technical, integrative, security-related, and professional acceptance tests must be carried out prior to go-live. Operational go-live may only take place after the successful completion of all tests and written approval by ALDB. d) Migration The contractor is responsible for the complete planning, execution, and documentation of the migration in coordination with the contracting authority. As part of the migration, all user identities, roles, permissions, organisational structures, configurations, and all data required for the operation of the IAM solution must be transferred completely, consistently, and without data loss into the new system. The migration must be carried out in such a way that interruptions to productive operations are reduced to a minimum and the integrity of all data is ensured at all times. e) Customer Support The IAM customer service to be provided by the contractor comprises technical support, operation, maintenance, and continuous further development of the implemented Identity & Access Management solution in accordance with ALDB's functional and technical requirements. The service meets KRITIS requirements and is German-language support. The scope of services includes, in particular, incident and problem management, error analysis and troubleshooting, software updates, hotfixes, patches, and security-related updates, as well as support for configuration changes, change requests, extensions, and the integration of additional source and target systems. Furthermore, the contractor supports ALDB in optimising existing identity and access management processes, further developing the role and permission concept, and implementing new functional and regulatory requirements.

sig_dde53e36b1b5ef4db120.description: Gol municipality plans, on behalf of the municipalities in Hallingdal, to carry out a market survey on general documentation management in the region. 1.1.1 Background and purpose of the market survey The six municipalities in Hallingdal have started a preliminary study to look at a more comprehensive and future orientated documentation management, at the same time that we must continually deal with archival documentation in new trade systems. Our ongoing procurement of a new electronic patient journal (EPJ) has clarified the need for a total assessment of how archival documentation is handled across trade systems. The current systems are fragmented, with many archive cores and complex set-ups, and present challenges, among other things, for structure, work flow, quality and resource use. The six municipalities have joint ICT operations and cooperate on digitalisation projects and procurements of new digital systems with the accompanying joint contract management. In order to gain insight that can enable us to make good road choices further, we would like to carry out a market survey with potential suppliers. The main focus is the safeguarding of archival information generated in trade systems in accordance with laws and regulations, and it is especially important for us to see this in the light of changed laws, regulations and standards in the archive area, new technology and possibilities for a more comprehensive approach further.
sig_dde53e36b1b5ef4db120.title: Market Survey/RFI - Archive Core

sig_dde965056278242d7989.description: The KVB intends to replace its existing SAP HCM landscape, which is also used for the group company KSG, by way of a carve-out and to transform it to SAP SuccessFactors as a full cloud solution. The contract covers the preparation, implementation, and operational phases, in particular conception and preparation of the requirements specification, implementation, configuration and customising, data migration, integration and interface adaptation, testing, training, project management, change management support, go-live and hypercare, as well as subsequent support during productive operation. In particular, Employee Central, Employee Central Payroll, Time Tracking, Learning, Onboarding, and WalkMe Premium for SuccessFactors are to be introduced. SAP S/4HANA, SAP Integration Suite, and SAP BW on HANA are to be included in particular. The required SuccessFactors licences are already available and are not the subject of the contract. In addition, an optional quota of up to 1.000 person-days is provided for supplementary services. Full productive operation is scheduled for no later than 01.06.2028. Details regarding the scope of services and binding requirements can be found in the service description and the other tender documents. The following binding minimum requirements or knock-out criteria apply to the tender phase: 1. The personnel deployed for the provision of services must possess sound to long-standing, extensive, and in-depth experience and knowledge regarding SAP HCM and SuccessFactors. The bidder must guarantee this in its tender. 2. The bidder must guarantee that the provision of services complies with the current state of the art and recognised technical rules as well as the principle of sensible, appropriate, and economical use, also with regard to further costs such as, in particular, operating costs. In justified cases of doubt, compliance with these requirements must be proven at the contractor's expense. 3. The project language is German. All documentation, minutes, reports, planning, and training materials must be written entirely in German. Meetings, workshops, and training sessions must be conducted in German. The specialist personnel deployed must have a fluent command of the German language in both speech and writing. If German is not the native language, at least a German language diploma of level C1 according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages is required. 4. All of the bidder's employees, including external subcontractors and freelancers, must comply with the provisions of the General Data Protection Regulation. The bidder may only deploy persons for whom a written declaration of consent to comply with the General Data Protection Regulation is available. 5. The offered solution must in particular meet the requirements of the General Data Protection Regulation, the Federal Data Protection Act, the principles for the proper keeping and storage of books, records, and documents in electronic form, and for data access, as well as other statutory retention and documentation obligations. 6. Completed personnel-related processes, data sets, documents, and records may only be deleted or archived after the expiry of the respective applicable statutory or professional retention periods. The corresponding process must be designed in a legally compliant and audit-proof manner and documented by means of procedural documentation. Failure to meet any of these minimum requirements will lead to the exclusion of the tender. The individual and sub-criteria, their weighting, the evaluation method including the linking of price and performance, the scoring scale, any minimum scores, as well as the information and evidence to be submitted will be provided uniformly to the selected applicants with the invitation to submit the indicative initial tender. They will specify the aforementioned award framework.

sig_dec3d929cc52ef9a1f14.description: Already in 2008 the Klinikum Altmühlfranken in Weißenburg was extended by a specialist medical centre. Now the hospital is to be comprehensively refurbished and extended in two construction phases – due to the age of the building and deficits in the space available and functionality. Part of this application for construction and equipment planning is the 1. construction phase BA1 and here the two sub-construction phases BA1A and BA1E. BA1 – 1. construction phase. In the first construction phase, the existing functional wing is replaced by a new building (BA1A) and subsequently refurbished or converted for subsequent uses (BA1B). In addition, the existing entrance hall is extended and renewed (BA1E). BA1A - New building: The new building in the south-east of the property is planned as a compact structure with an ideal floor plan organisation and direct connection to the main entrance. All highly installed core functions of the hospital are concentrated and accommodated in the new building: - Basement: CSSD, laboratory, changing rooms, archive, laundry exchange point, services - Ground floor: Central emergency admission / central accident and emergency with new patient transport access and outpatient entrance, radiology, endoscopy, functional diagnostics, obstetrics - 1.upper floor: Operating theatre department with same-day surgery, intensive care medicine, on-call service - 2.upper floor: Services. The floor plan provides for a centrally located public access axis in an east-west orientation, to which the individual functional areas and vertical access with lift core are attached. On the 1.upper floor, an inner courtyard is also formed, which ensures the lighting of the respective departments. Optimum processes of hospital operation are achieved in this custom-built new building, and the primary functional deficits of the existing building are eliminated. Due to the self-sufficient construction of the new functional wing BA1A, ongoing operations in the existing building can be continued without impairment. BA1E - New building / refurbishment of entrance hall: Through the new building and its connection to the existing building, a new entrance situation and thus a new forward-looking urban planning appearance of the hospital is created at the same time. For this purpose, the existing entrance hall at entrance level is extended/straightened, thus creating a clear, unambiguous access. The entrance hall at the central location of the hospital is gutted and general functions are accommodated here: - Ground floor: Service facilities with reception/mailroom, pastoral care and social service area - Upper floors: Access with lounge areas. During this refurbishment, a provisional main entrance can be located from the north at the transition to the new building. BA1B - Refurbishment of existing building, outlook (not part of this BAP): After relocation of the core functions of the hospital into the newly constructed building BA1A, the original functional wing is converted accordingly and the following functions are located here: - Basement: Supply/disposal, storage, house and transport service, maintenance/repair, waste disposal, pharmaceuticals, services - Ground floor: Physical therapy, medical service, on-call service, catering with visitor/staff cafeteria with outdoor area - 1.upper floor: Medical service, administration - 2.upper floor: Prayer room, services. As part of the gutting, as a major structural intervention, an inner courtyard is formed on the 1.upper floor for the purpose of lighting the adjacent functions. The entire refurbishment can be carried out in one go, only 4 / 7 the existing catering in the 1.basement initially remains and is dismantled and converted accordingly after completion of the new catering on the ground floor. BA2 - 2. construction phase, outlook (not part of this BAP): In the second construction phase, nursing care is then to be modernised at Klinikum Altmühlfranken Weißenburg. This results in two possibilities: - Refurbishment and extension of the existing nursing wards - New nursing care buildings next to the newly constructed functional wing BA1A, which allows an ideal connection to new nursing blocks in its positioning and floor plan layout. Data-image-video management system consisting of built-in, display monitors and audio system as well as maintenance services
sig_dec3d929cc52ef9a1f14.title: Extension and refurbishment of Klinikum Altmühlfranken Weißenburg 1. BA (sub-construction section 1a)

sig_ded3cad650ed57c711e0.description: Background Troms County (TFK) manages buildings of 218,000 m2, comprising i.a. schools, sports facilities, dental clinics, workplaces and other county buildings. The cleaning services are carried out by approx. 130 cleaners organised by teams, with a focus on flexible work forms, efficient use of resources and quality in the service delivery. The County municipality needs a more uniform, digital and documentable follow-up of cleaning across buildings, rooms and areas. The current systems do not provide sufficient support for registration and follow-up of work performed, deviations and quality measurements. Therefore there is a need for a system that makes it easy for cleaners to register work and register conditions that affect cleaning, for example rooms that cannot be cleaned, deviations or a lack of periodic cleaning. At the same time, the county needs a better overview and management information. Managers should be able to follow the status per building, area and room, identify areas that have not been cleaned and get a better basis for planning capacity, resource use and absence management. The cleaning quality shall be measured and documented in accordance with NS-INSTA 800. TFK would like systems that provide good support for quality follow-up, reporting and analysis, which contribute to increased user friendliness, better decision making and more efficient operation. The procurement is being made to establish a future orientated digital system that provides a better overview, more uniform practice, better documentation and more efficient management of deviations, quality follow-up and resource planning. Description of the assignment The assignment includes the delivery, establishment, operation and support of a digital cleaning system for Troms County. The system shall provide an overview of cleaning per building, room and area and it can be used by cleaners, substitutes, managers, administrators and operations managers where the work is carried out. The system shall support planning, implementation, documentation and follow-up of the cleaning services. The system shall, among other things: Give easy registration of completed cleaning, status and deviations. Support registration and follow-up of periodic cleaning. Give an overview of rooms and areas that have not been cleaned or where deviations are registered. Support quality measurements and documentation in accordance with NS-INSTA 800. Offer reports and management information that supports follow-up, documentation, analysis and resource planning. Support both short term and long term planning of assignments and resources. Be able to integrate with existing and future MOM systems, as well as facilitate future integrations with other support systems, including possibilities for future use of sensor technology, such as dispensers, waste handling, machines and robots. The delivery shall include the necessary establishment and configuration of the building and room structure, user roles and access management, as well as training, user support and administrative assistance in connection with the introduction and use of the system. TFK would like a user friendly and visually oriented system that facilitates efficient operation, good quality control and future development of the cleaning services. Further requirements for functionality, technical conditions, security, privacy, integrations and service level are stated in the requirement specification.
sig_ded3cad650ed57c711e0.title: Digital system for registering cleaning and deviations.

sig_df4e64e9abf385290883.description: Rijkswaterstaat (RWS) has started replacing current traffic signal controllers (TSCs) with intelligent traffic signal controllers (iTSCs). The reason for this is that the iTSC is the new standard and the iTSC facilitates nationally specific target groups, such as the prioritisation of emergency services (including road inspectors), logistics and cyclists. In recent years, in a first tranche, RWS has replaced or converted 19 TSCs into iTSCs. Experience with these first iTSCs shows that they can be of added value in achieving policy objectives aimed at optimising traffic flow and prioritising specific target groups as described above. The contract concerns the supply, implementation and management of C-ITS (Cooperative Intelligent Transportation Systems) applications for iTSCs (intelligent traffic signal controllers). For further information, see the Descriptive Document. see the Descriptive Document. This is a C-ITS application based on CCOL that is hosted locally, in which policy objectives are translated into the control logic by setting parameters, switches and (time) settings. The C-ITS application from this lot is Ivera-oriented. Rijkswaterstaat can largely manage parameters itself via the TSC management centre (currently MobiMaestro). As a result, fewer traffic engineering services are requested for this type of application. This C-ITS application is most similar to the applications used in conventional TSCs, supplemented by the use cases for the iTSC. A maximum of one supplier will be selected for this lot. For further information, see the Descriptive Document. see the Descriptive Document.; This is a C-ITS application hosted locally or in the cloud, in which policy objectives can be configured in the C-ITS application at intersection or network level. The C-ITS application optimises on the basis of the configured policy objectives. For its operation, (traffic engineering) services are requested in this call for tender. How the configuration and optimisation are carried out is the responsibility of the Contractor. A maximum of one supplier will be selected for this lot. see further the Descriptive Document See descriptive document

sig_e01826a8e1aa506810aa.description: Background and purpose Arendal is located in the central part of Sørlandet. The municipality has approx. 46,000 inhabitants. Arendal municipality has a decentralised school structure with 16 municipal primary and secondary schools, organised as independent entities with separate rectors and management groups. The schools include both combined 1st - 10th schools and pure primary schools (1st - 7th years), as well as a resource centre with tenders across the stages. The municipality has a total of approx. 5,000 pupils in the primary and lower secondary schools. Arendal municipality is in an ongoing change of the school structure. Two primary schools (1st – 7th years) and the secondary school for one school have been decided to be folded. The changes are planned to be implemented from 01.01.2027. The overall responsibility for the school area is at the school office, which follows up on joint priorities, quality work and regulations, and acts as a link between the political level and the schools. The cooperation between the school office and the schools will take place, among other things, through fixed meeting points and joint development work, at the same time that each school adapts the work to local needs. The adult education is organised as a part of the municipality ́s training and is also a user of relevant digital services. Arendal municipality needs a joint system for the administration, distribution and access management of digital teaching aids in primary and secondary schools. The municipality has used a system for this purpose over time and has developed good experience with procurement, licence management and access management in this area. The procurement will be carried out as a result of the expiry of the existing agreement and shall ensure the continuation and further development of this work. Information on the procurement and process is in the document Konkurransegrunnlag_Digital Platform for schools. Scope The estimated annual scope is challenging to estimate. This is connected with the complexity, changes in the school structure and a market with different actors. We estimate that the annual turnover will be NOK 3.0 million excluding VAT, which over 8 years will be NOK 24 million excluding VAT. The contract will have a valid amount of NOK 30 million excluding VAT during the contract period. The estimated scope is based on experiences with the current supplier, market dialogue and indicative prices in the market. The estimated scope is not binding for the contracting authority. The following is not included in this procurement: - Learning platform (LMS) and educational follow-up. - functionality connected to artificial intelligence (KI) - other school administrative systems. The procurement is for the administration and distribution of digital teaching aids and a learning tool. Handling printed teaching aids is not included. The procurement does not include discipline specific teaching aids or individual applications. Reservations All conditions that the tenderer has for the tender shall be stated in the point conditions in the requirement specification document. Alternative tenders Alternative tenders cannot be submitted. Documents Please see the attached documents. Note that the tenderer shall fill in information in the attached documents.
sig_e01826a8e1aa506810aa.title: Platform for the administration and distribution of digital teaching aids and learning tools.

sig_e09cb2aa998d64d69f62.description: Ards and North Down Borough Council is currently preparing to initiate a procurement process to appoint an Operating Partner for a Creative Innovation Hub in Holywood, Co.Down. The Holywood Innovation Hub is a project funded through investment from the Belfast Region City Deal (BRCD) and Ards and North Down Borough Council. It will focus on micro and small businesses within the digital, creative and screen industries: providing facilities and a secure environment to meet specific security, connectivity and technical needs. The proposed hub is intended to provide accommodation for the creative technology sector, specifically for start-up and smaller firms seeking to grow within the sector. It would also seek to provide accommodation for larger established 'anchor' tenants and potentially act as a short-term flexible base for FDI projects supported by NI Screen. The proposed hub is also intended to create an ecosystem within the creative technology sector: improving skills and employability across Ards and North Down and the overall Belfast Region City Deal (BRCD) region. A primary reason for market failure in this sector is stated as a lack of suitable accommodation. This project will address this situation, supporting the growth of firms in the digital creative sector beyond the initial 'work from home' phase. The capital funding requirement for the proposal is £8,921,200 from the BRCD, with a further contribution of £1.1m from Ards and North Down Borough Council (ANDBC), further funding is required from the private sector to unlock this funding. ANDBC intends to appoint an operator for the Innovation Hub at an early stage of project development. The operator will assume management responsibilities and associated risks as set out in the final contractual structure. The operator will be appointed prior to the procurement of the Integrated Consultancy Team (ICT) responsible for the design of the Innovation Hub, enabling operational requirements and commercial considerations to be incorporated into the design and helping to maximise the hub's long-term economic performance. Prior to initiating the procurement, the Council is undertaking an Expression of Interest (EoI) and Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) Exercise . This EoI/PME exercise is being conducted pursuant to section 16 of the Procurement Act 2023 for the purposes of: (a) developing the Council's requirements and approach to the procurement; (b) designing conditions of participation and award criteria; (c) preparing the tender notice and associated tender documents; and (d) identifying suppliers capable of performing the proposed contract. The pre-market engagement is intended to facilitate high-level conversations to identify potential interested suppliers and capabilities to inform the Council's procurement approach. A summary of the opportunity is detailed in the brochure and questionnaire documents that can be accessed via the CfT documents area (Resource ID 6717503) on the eTendersNI platform (https://etendersni.gov.uk).
sig_e09cb2aa998d64d69f62.title: ANDBC Preliminary Market Engagement Exercise - Appointment of an Operating Partner for a Creative Innovation Hub in Holywood, Co.Down
