Lot 1: . The product that will be procured will need to cover the following. PC Booking The system must support booking of public PCs. PC bookings must be configurable by location to reflect site‐specific arrangements. Self‐Service and Staff‐Assisted Booking Members of the public must be able to make PC bookings independently. Staff must be able to create or manage PC bookings on behalf of members of the public. Ability for patrons to book PCs in advance (online, kiosk, staff-assisted). Walk-up access with immediate log-on if PCs are available. Integration with Printing Services The solution must integrate with the existing printing system. It must provide print release functionality and support payments for printing. Library Management System Integration The solution must link to the Spydus Library Management System using LCF protocol for providing borrower authentication. Authentication must ensure only eligible borrowers can access PCs and services. Browsing History Reporting The system must provide reporting on user browsing session history to meet MAPPA agreement requirements. Borrower Type Management & Internet Restrictions The system must manage borrower types to enforce restrictions on internet browsing sessions. Restrictions must be configurable by borrower type or age ranges. Reporting & Analytics The system must provide a variety of statistical reports, including usage, bookings, printing, and browsing session activity. Reports must support operational monitoring and compliance requirements. Export options (Excel, CSV, BI tools). Security & Compliance GDPR-compliant handling of personal data. Role-based access control for staff and administrators. Audit trails and logging of user activity. Accessibility & Usability Compliance with WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards. Simple, intuitive user interface for both patrons and staff. Technical Requirements Ability to manage and update programs, shortcuts (internet etc) and windows updates / patches centrally / remotely. Ability for Users to access USB memory Sticks on Public Access PCs Peripherals - System must work with standard peripherals e.g. scanners / headsets Nice to have - Reimage from local drive partition if local PCs. If cloud managed then this would already be in solution but PCs on site would likely become Cloud Managed and allow remote rebuild.. sig_e24c76052c5125d06fac.description: Society relies on chemical processes to turn raw materials into useful products. The Chemical Process Systems (CPS) program invests in fundamental research on chemical and biochemical processes to make them more efficient, sustainable, and resilient. New CPS technologies for manufacturing, biotechnology, critical minerals, energy, food, and other national priorities will help make the U.S. more competitive and secure. Research supported by the CPS program covers the full breadth of chemical and biochemical process innovation. It spans reaction engineering and molecular thermodynamics; reactor design; catalysis; electrochemical systems; separations; and process design. The program encourages proposals that connect the molecular scale to process and plant scales. The CPS program explores active-site structure and function, reaction mechanisms, in situ and operando characterization, durability, and device-level integration. Microreactors, membrane and catalytic reactors, atmospheric plasmas, and other novel configurations are of interest. The program supports research in catalysis and electrochemical systems to produce, use, and store energy, to reduce waste, to process polymers, and to synthesize fuels and chemicals. This includes process and materials innovation to support the nuclear fuel cycle. The CPS program also targets chemical and biological separations that are efficient and scalable. Research includes the design of membranes, sorbents, and specialized interfaces. Advances can be used in gas separations, the recovery of critical minerals, bioprocessing, and protein and water purification. The program supports research in process design and optimization that uses tools such as artificial intelligence, machine learning, and uncertainty quantification. CPS research also explores quantum information science and engineering; quantum simulation and sensing, for example, may accelerate the discovery of materials and improve process models. Partnerships: To speed discovery and innovation, NSF partners with federal agencies, industry, international groups, and others. Current opportunities are at NSF ENG Partnerships.
sig_e24c76052c5125d06fac.title: Chemical Process Systems (CPS)

sig_e441f9e2437814408f88.description: The tender procedure is carried out by the contracting authorities as a joint procurement procedure, cf. section 123, subsection 5. The tender procedure is covered by the Danish Public Procurement Act (Act No. 1564 of 15 December 2015 as amended), which implements the Public Procurement Directive (Directive 2014/24/EU). The tender procedure concerns the procurement of diabetes technology by Region Midtjylland, Region Syddanmark, Region Nordjylland and Region Østdanmark (current Region Sjælland and Region Hovedstaden), divided into two subcontracts concerning respectively (1) AID insulin pump systems and (2) continuous glucose monitoring systems (CGM). The tender also covers the system components, accessories and consumables that are necessary or relevant for putting the offered systems into operation and using them as intended. As an integral part of the delivery, the suppliers must also make the associated digital solutions available, including apps and patient and clinician platforms, and provide training for patients and healthcare professionals as well as technical support for patients. The products covered are set out in Contract Appendix 3, while the requirements for the products and associated services are set out in the Contract and the Requirements Specification, cf. Contract Appendix 2. The contract put out to tender, including subcontracts (1) and (2), are framework agreements in accordance with section 24, no. 30 of the Public Procurement Act. Subcontract 1 and Subcontract 2 are separate framework agreements. In connection with the conclusion of the contract, separate contracts and contract appendices will be drawn up (except for contract appendix 5, which is already included in the tender documents in one copy for each participating region) for each of the other participating regions. This means that each region concludes separate contracts/framework agreements with the winning tenderers. The subcontract concerns the procurement of AID insulin pumps in the form of either insulin pumps for infusion sets or patch pumps. The subcontract also covers the system components, accessories and consumables that are necessary or relevant for putting the offered AID insulin pump system into operation and using it as intended, including, depending on the offered system, for example pods, pump bases, PDM/control units, infusion sets and reservoirs. As an integral part of the delivery, the supplier must make associated digital solutions available, including apps and patient and clinician platforms, and provide training in the use of the offered products as well as technical support for patients. The detailed scope of the subcontract appears from the tender documents, including Contract Appendix 2 and Contract Appendix 3.; The subcontract concerns the procurement of continuous sensor-based glucose monitoring systems (CGM). The subcontract covers sensors, receivers and other system components, accessories and consumables that are necessary or relevant for putting the offered CGM system into operation and using it as intended, including, for example, senders/transmitters. As an integral part of the delivery, the supplier must make associated digital solutions available, including apps and patient and clinician platforms, and provide training in the use of the offered products as well as technical support for patients. The detailed scope of the subcontract appears from the tender documents, including Contract Appendix 2 and Contract Appendix 3. As an integral part of the delivery, the supplier must make associated digital solutions available, including apps and patient and clinician platforms, and provide training in the use of the offered products as well as technical support for patients. The detailed scope of the subcontract appears from the tender documents, including Contract Appendix 2 and Contract Appendix 3.

sig_e443bf5a7bbda61409ba.description: The Dresdner Verkehrsbetriebe AG (DVB) are conducting market consultation on AI-supported solutions for the control centre in the event of disruptions as well as for the further development of their data architecture. The aim is to get to know available solutions, technological approaches and operating models to support spontaneous line closures and comparable operational restrictions. The focus is on the introduction of an AI-supported evaluation tool for the analysis of dispatch measures and detours as well as the potential use of a data warehouse or lakehouse for the use of historical and analytical data. In addition, suitable integration approaches, data sources and operating models (cloud, on-premises or hybrid) are to be evaluated. Lot LOT-0001: Market consultation in accordance with § 26 SektVO for the intended procurement of an AI evaluation tool and data warehouse/lakehouse. The aim of the market consultation is to draw up well-founded procurement documents through careful planning and to create a reliable calculation basis. Requirements of the specification sheet are to be refined on the basis of the market consultation results.
sig_e443bf5a7bbda61409ba.title: Market exploration pursuant to § 26 SektVO regarding the intended procurement of an AI evaluation tool and data warehouse/lakehouse

sig_e4464159e008dbabdcbb.description: Provision, implementation, operation and maintenance of the complete technical infrastructure for the EUDI Wallet Support Organisation. Covers all systems from the self-service portal and ticket management to telephony, knowledge base and identity management. The subject of this tender is the award of services for the technical infrastructure of the EUDI Wallet Support Organisation (EWSO), known as tooling. The contractor shall implement, configure and commission: the ticket and CRM system, the knowledge base and FAQ portal, the in-app bot (or compatibility with the client's internal app bot solution), the telephony and IVR infrastructure, the connection and compatibility with the B2B portal: EUDI Hub, the IAM system, the central event log system and the redaction system. The contractor shall accompany the closed beta phase (Q4 2026) and the go-live phase (Q1 2027) with hypercare support and, following an orderly knowledge transfer, hand over operational system sovereignty to the client's internal team. The services comprise in particular EU-compliant infrastructure ((ISO 27001), no US CLOUD Act exposure), WCAG 21 compliance of all user front ends, a mandatory external penetration test prior to go-live as well as complete system documentation and training of the internal team.
sig_e4464159e008dbabdcbb.title: EUDI Wallet Support Organisation Technical Infrastructure of the EUDI Wallet Support Organisation (EWSO) - "Tooling"

sig_e4495dc4a5fa0d21753a.description: As part of the re-tendering process for TenneT’s Content Collaboration Platform, Lot 2 encompasses a multi-vendor framework agreement focused on the integration, implementation, configuration, migration, and support of platform functionalities tailored to TenneT’s infrastructure project needs. The present tender focuses primarily on TenneT’s German operations. As beneficiaries under the SaaS Agreement, Dutch TenneT operations may optionally draw from the services that are subject hereof. With the re-tendering of the current Content Collaboration Platform, TenneT is aiming to continue achieving a single source of information for all documents generated in infrastructure projects and managing the supplier collaboration (external collaboration) regarding the exchange and management of documents and additional data. The targeted system is facilitating and capturing the complete project lifecycle in addition to providing auditable documentation and information throughout the organization. The tender procedure is divided into two lots, which will be tendered in sequence in two different tenders: Tender 1 [Lot 1] "CDE - Collaboration-Platform for Document and Data Exchange": includes the platform provisioning, development, deployment (Implementation), initial customization and configuration, platform interfaces as well as maintenance and support of the platform and – as a proof of concept and for purposes of a successful transition – the migration of TenneT metadata as well as existing construction projects from the current to the new platform. This tender has been completed. The awarded solution is provided by ThinkProject. Tender 2 [Lot 2]: "CDE – Multi-Contractor Integration": includes intergration and implementation services associated with the platform and comprises subsequent configuration, customization and consulting services in relation to the Content Collaboration Platform. The Lot 1 Provider must always collaborate pro-actively and in a constructive manner with any Lot 2 Contractor(s), e.g. providing access, support and knowledge transfer regarding the platform and implementing technically necessary changes within Lot 1 where mutually agreed with or commissioned by TenneT. Lot 2 will be tendered subsequent to the award of Lot 1. Performance Scope Lot 2 The Lot 2 providers selected during the selection phase must be qualified for the following service areas within the framework of the mini competitions and be able to obtain contracts in these areas: Business Support for CDE Initiatives and Projects The contractor shall provide advisory and operational support for departments and project teams in the context of CDE utilization, in particular: Advising on methodological and operational use of CDE platforms in project environments Supporting data migration processes (e.g., from legacy systems) Assisting with platform configuration and workflow optimization Developing and maintaining structured knowledge management tools (e.g., CDE user guides, training materials, FAQs) Facilitating workshops to gather and refine user requirements Design, Development, and Implementation of Non-Standard Changes This service domain includes support in extending the functional scope of the CDE platform beyond its standard features: Designing and specifying customized solutions (e.g., plug-ins, tailored workflows) Developing enhancements, interfaces, and automation features Supporting innovation initiatives, e.g., through prototyping of new digital tools Providing comprehensive technical and user documentation Performing quality assurance and testing of developed components Integration support for non-standard changes The contractor will provide technical and conceptual support for integrating enhancements into the existing CDE ecosystem: Designing and executing system integration concepts (e.g., CDE ↔ third-party systems) Developing and maintaining interfaces (e.g., REST, SOAP, file-based) Conducting system, integration, and regression testing Monitoring and issue resolution during and after go-live Preparing technical operations documentation (e.g., monitoring and handover guides) Project execution The contractor shall support the delivery of CDE-related (sub-)projects, including: Providing project management services (e.g., project office, timeline planning, reporting, risk management) Conducting requirement analysis and scope definition with business stakeholders Coordinating internal and external implementation partners Reporting to project leadership or steering committees Supporting change and rollout management measures For more details please see "L2 - C11 - Summary of Requirements" and "L2 – N01 – Annex 01 – Service Description" (will be sent after signing the NDA). Both tenders/lots are evaluated and awarded independently of each other. This publication refers only to Tender 2 [Lot 2]. Procedural note A detailed service description and other documents relevant to the procedure will be provided after signing an NDA. You will find the NDA in question 1.15. Please send it to us signed via the Mercell messaging function. The tender is being conducted in accordance with SektVO in a negotiated procedure with competitive participation.

sig_e4c9e6e9a8c3276ad3b3.buyer_name: Heidelberg University Hospital Public Law Corporation
sig_e4c9e6e9a8c3276ad3b3.description: Dear Sir or Madam, Heidelberg University Hospital (UKHD) currently uses a self-developed ABAP-based add-on called BISI for electronic demand notification. As part of the SAP S/4 migration, this demand notification system is to be replaced by a long-term future-proof and modern solution. From a prospective perspective, the demand notification system is intended to support the entire Heidelberg-Mannheim hospital network with all subsidiaries and holdings. UKHD manages 2589 beds. With 87.441 inpatient patients and 1.275.241 outpatient treatment cases, it is the largest employer in the region. 14544 employees from 133 nations are employed at UKHD. The Faculty of Medicine trains 4.750 students. The Corporate Purchasing and Logistics Management division and the pharmacy supply the entire UKHD corporate group including subsidiaries and holdings and also supply external hospitals in the surrounding area. The newly procured tool for demand requests must be intuitive and easy for end users to operate and be based on the look and feel of modern, future-proof, efficient request platforms. This requires that end customers can record and request any demands during demand requests regardless of the product group, article group, purchasing organisation or financing type in the sense of a mixed shopping basket. The tool takes over the routing of requirements into the correct demand channels and controls the follow-on documents. The tool to be procured must be able to be connected to both SAP ECC and S/4 HANA. In this market exploration, UKHD therefore wishes to examine what options the relevant market currently offers for this contract subject, what empirical values can be contributed and what price range these services fall within.
sig_e4c9e6e9a8c3276ad3b3.title: Market exploration regarding a demand notification tool for Heidelberg University Hospital

sig_e5740702950e74e82984.description: RVK is a modern transport company that has been under municipal ownership since 1996. The company was formed in 1976 from a merger of the railway and postal bus services. The transport area extends across the Rheinisch-Bergischer district, the left-bank Rhein-Sieg district, the Euskirchen district and the cities of Cologne, Bonn, Leverkusen, Hürth, Brühl and Wesseling. RVK thus connects urban conurbations with sparsely populated, more rural areas. With capacity, competence and many years of experience, RVK ensures that people in the region are on the move reliably and safely – and in an environmentally friendly, sustainable and innovative way. The RVK bus fleet comprises over 600 vehicles, some of which are operated by the company itself and some of which operate on behalf of RVK. The transport network comprises 132 lines with a total length of 2.595 km. In addition, 58 lines are operated by RVK for other transport companies. In total, RVK provides a mileage of approx. 22,6 million km with approx. 23 million passengers annually. Most of the RVK buses are already equipped with TFT interior displays. However, as not all buses have TFT monitors, RVK is procuring at least 100 additional 29 inch TFT interior displays (and up to a total of 350 TFT interior displays) for use in public transport vehicles via a framework agreement. sig_e5c57127e832fb59b09c.description: The object of the contract is the procurement of Services for the preparation of technical-economic documentation, DALI phase, for the investment objective "Studies, documentation for street works - Reconfiguration, rehabilitation and modernisation of the intersection of Chitiliei Road with Bucureștii Noi Boulevard, reconfiguration, rehabilitation and modernisation of Bucureștii Noi (segment Timișului Street - Constanța Bridge), reconfiguration, rehabilitation and modernisation of Griviței Road (segment Constanța Bridge - Carpați Street), reconstruction of Constanța bridge and the creation of an intermodal node", according to the specifications in the tender specifications. The deadline by which any interested economic operator has the right to request clarifications or additional information regarding the award documentation is a maximum of 20 days before the deadline for submission of tenders. The contracting authority will respond clearly and completely to all requests for clarification/additional information on the 11 day before the deadline for submission of tenders. The contracting authority mentions that it will respond to requests for clarification addressed by economic operators by the deadline established in the Contract Notice. Any request for clarification must be transmitted in SEAP (http://sicap-prod.e-licitatie.ro/pub). The programme for the modernisation and rehabilitation of major urban thoroughfares is part of a broader programme to remedy existing deficiencies in urban traffic. The lack of efficient connections between areas of the Municipality of Bucharest affects car traffic, pedestrian traffic and public transport, creating large losses of time and additional fuel consumption. To streamline heavy traffic in the north of the Capital, it is necessary to modernise the infrastructure in this area, ensuring increased safety and comfort conditions. Due to severe degradation, low travel speeds lead to increased CO2 emissions and hinder access for Police, Ambulance and Fire Brigade crews. Implementing the investment in the area of the intersection of Chitilei Road with Bucureștii Noi Boulevard and Griviței Road, together with the reconstruction of the Constanța Bridge and the creation of an intermodal node, will improve access to public services and reduce travel times, increasing the quality of life for residents and people in transit. The duration of the provision of services is 180 calendar days.

sig_e5d13788d4743ecf509c.description: In the current model, the technical implementation of communal services is integrated into the IT organisation established by the State of Fribourg. In particular, SITel ensures contracting with technical service providers and the management of IT developments, in collaboration with the DIGI-FR team, which carries the business needs and ensures functional responsibility for communal services. With the coming to an end of the DIGI-FR program 2023–2026 and the evolution of the legal framework relating to e-government, this model is bound to evolve. From 2027, the municipalities, through the entity responsible for representing them, will take over responsibility for the development, operation and maintenance of their services on the Fribourg virtual counter. They will thus have the capacity to directly commission the necessary service providers and manage the end-to-end technical implementation of their services. This call for tenders aims to establish the capacities required for the development and maintenance of communal services in this new model. The public procurement aims to establish a contractual framework which will subsequently allow the ACF, according to its needs and on the basis of a predefined service catalogue, to award its contracts to referenced partners via single consultations (mini-tenders) in a simplified and competitive procedure.
sig_e5d13788d4743ecf509c.title: Framework contract for e-government DIGI-FR

sig_e5d463b07d7476d5424b.description: New establishment of a digital alerting system in the POCSAG standard (2m band) for non-police emergency response in the Landkreis Emmendingen to replace the analogue 5-tone alerting. The subject of the procurement is the supply, installation and commissioning of a area-wide digital alerting system complying with the POCSAG standard in the 2m band for emergency services organisations in the Landkreis Emmendingen, including migration from the existing analogue 5-tone alerting, the supply of end-user devices as well as maintenance and service provisions. The procurement procedure in question comprises the establishment of 37 digital alerting repeater sites within the district area including antenna and lightning protection technology as well as the electrotechnical upgrading of the structures for these sites. Furthermore, a total of four digital alerters (two fixed installations and two mobile emergency alerters) as well as network and IT technology for the central system technology will be installed at the site of the Integrated Control Centre Emmendingen. The contract is divided into four lots. Lot 1 comprises the digital alerting system technology, in particular the supply, assembly, commissioning and configuration of the digital alerting repeaters and digital alerters with subsequent services on the basis of an EVB-IT service contract with a fixed term of 24 months. Lot 2 includes antenna technology and mast construction, meaning in particular the supply and assembly of antenna masts and lightning protection as well as earthing components. Lot 3 describes the necessary electrical work. Lot 4 comprises the procurement of end-user devices using a shopping-basket principle with call-offs by the respective authorised municipalities or relief organisations. Supply, installation, and commissioning of the central and decentralised system technology of the digital alerting system (including digital alerters, digital alerting repeaters, switches, software), including system integration, tests, training as well as the conclusion of an EVB-IT service contract limited to the first 24 months.; Supply, assembly and commissioning of antenna systems (2m, GPS, LTE), antenna carriers and mast structures including lightning protection and earthing measures and structural analyses, as well as coordination with property owners.; Execution of all electrical connection and installation work at transmitter and technical sites, including power supply as well as documentation in accordance with DIN VDE 0100-600.; Supply, installation, configuration and commissioning of end-user devices for receiving the alarm messages transmitted via the components of lot 1 and of components for remote programming of these end-user devices (server-client structure) and central components for implementing a call-back functionality from and additional alarm information to the end-user devices via the mobile communications network. The procurement of the end-user devices takes place via a framework agreement according to the shopping-basket principle with call-offs by the authorised municipalities and relief organisations.
sig_e5d463b07d7476d5424b.title: Tender for Digital Alerting (Hardware & Installation)

sig_e65b3b1c01dca77388d9.description: Our ambition is to implement a workwear solution that is accessible, and inclusive for all colleagues, incorporating maternity options, religious considerations, gender-appropriate fits, and consistent sizing standards. Lot 1: . Our vision is to create a fully branded, inclusive, and functional workwear and PPE solution that unites every colleague across our organisation reflecting who we are, what we stand for, and the pride we take in serving our communities. We will deliver a modern, high‐quality uniform range designed from the ground up to support the unique needs of our operational, maritime, port, and shore‐based teams. Rooted in the heritage of Caledonian MacBrayne and our communities, our workwear will combine safety, comfort, durability, and unmistakable brand identity in every garment. Our ambition is to implement a workwear solution that is accessible, and inclusive for all colleagues, incorporating maternity options, religious considerations, gender-appropriate fits, and consistent sizing standards. Through clear uniform standards, easy maintenance guidance, and from warehouse to home/work distribution processes, we will set and uphold a new standard for how our brand is worn and represented. Powered by digital self-service ordering tools, our workwear transformation will enhance operational efficiency, improve stock management, and allow us to scale sustainably. Cross-functional collaboration at the early stages will ensure that every voice is heard and every role is understood, creating a sense of ownership, pride, and confidence in the final solution. By learning from industry-leading transformations and working with expert partners, we will introduce a workwear range that not only serves practical needs but also strengthens culture, improves staff experience, and supports our organisation’s evolution. This is more than new uniform, it's an opportunity to reinforce our brand, celebrate our heritage, empower our people, and deliver a workwear experience that is fit for the future.

sig_e76cad13ba556c235e05.description: ITZBund requires services in the area of software lifecycle management (SLM) for software development and project management solutions in use. The aim of this tender is to conclude a framework agreement to ensure the operation as well as the maintenance and (further) development of the existing Cloud software development and project management platform and associated specialist applications of ITZBund. In addition, sovereignty is to be strengthened through the expansion of open source tools to be procured. ITZBund understands open source to be software whose source code is freely available. In principle, everyone is permitted to use, analyse, modify and pass on this software free of charge and without restriction in terms of content regarding the object and source code. Specifications of the respective relevant open source licence, in particular regarding licence texts, copyright notices or copyleft effects, remain unaffected. The services advertised encompass services along the entire software lifecycle, in particular operational services, maintenance and support services, support services in connection with releases and rollouts as well as demand-oriented new developments and further developments of existing software and software-related tools. The contracting authority, who can commission services commissioned by its customers, is authorised to call off services. The operation of the procured software products generally takes place within ITZBund; exceptions in special individual cases permit operation at customers of the contracting authority with their own licensing. The services mentioned at the outset are advertised in five lots: - Lot 1: Ensuring the maintenance and (further) development of the deployed Cloud software development and project management platform - Lot 2: Ensuring the operation and automated rollout of releases of the deployed Cloud software development and project management platform - Lot 3: Provision of Sonatype software products - Lot 4: Provision of an open source issue tracker including in particular training, support, further development and migration services - Lot 5: Provision of an open source wiki including in particular training, support, further development and migration services This specification of services considers the subject matter of Lot 5: The subject matter of this lot is the provision of an open source wiki including associated training, support, further development and migration services. Lot LOT-0000: Provision of an open source wiki including in particular training, support, further development and migration services. For the total contract period of 4 years, an upper limit of 1.450 instances and 162.608 person-hours (ph) or 20.326 person-days (pd) results for the estimated calculatory costs.
sig_e76cad13ba556c235e05.title: Provision of an open source wiki including, in particular, training, support, further development and migration services

sig_e778d4c4281ef3fef99c.description: The National Library of Medicine (NLM) seeks applications for research projects that drive groundbreaking innovation and advanced development in the fields of bioinformatics, translational bioinformatics, and computational biology. The primary goal of this initiative is to support the creation and implementation of cutting-edge methods, tools, and approaches that can transform the landscape of biomedical data science. This NOFO aims to address the growing need to leverage transformative technologies — such as artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, and large-scale computational platforms — to extract actionable knowledge from vast, diverse, and complex biological datasets. By enabling more effective interpretation and integration of multi-dimensional biological and biomedical data, this research will ultimately contribute to improving individual and population health outcomes.

sig_e7d5d6310a2da1c26cbb.description: GENERAL This document is not a procurement announcement, not an Call for tenders, nor will its publication start a Tender Procurement Process. The purpose of this Pre-market consultation notice is to identify potential suppliers operating in the market and their offerings. Responding or not responding to this Pre-market consultation notice does not prevent participation in a possible future tender. This Pre-market consultation notice does not obligate the contracting authority to carry out an actual procurement procedure. All information presented in this Pre-market consultation notice is preliminary and indicative. Laurea University of Applied Sciences operates in five locations in the Uusimaa region in Finland. Laurea offers both bachelor’s and master’s degree studies but also open university studies, specialisation education and continuing education. The fields of study are Business Management, Information technology, Service business, Social Services, Nursing, Health Care and Hospitality Management. Laurea has approximately 9,900-degree students and approximately 13,000 Open UAS students per year as well as about 670 employees. PRELIMINARY SCOPE OF THE PROCUREMENT The scope of the procurement is a Software as a Service (SaaS) online exam proctoring system for Laurea UAS. The system must integrate with Laurea's learning platform (Canvas) and provide video and audio-based proctoring recorded and stored by the system. The procurement does not include a personal live monitoring service by the supplier or the use of artificial intelligence to monitor/check and identify suspected fraud. The procurement includes the deployment of the software service and support and maintenance services separately for each higher education institution. MARKET DIALOGUE The contracting authority reserves the right to engage in market dialogue with the responding companies regarding the planned procurement and the tender documents. In addition, the contracting authority reserves the right to conduct the potential market dialogue either in the form of written comments on the draft tender documents or through one-on-one meetings (via Teams or in person). The possibility to comment on the draft tender documents is preliminary planned to be arranged once before the publication of the final Call for tenders, regardless of the format. Any potential market dialogue will be conducted in English, and all related materials will be provided only in English. No compensation will be paid for participation in the market dialogue. Hansel Oy will act in a consultative role in the procurement process. REGISTRATION FOR THE MARKET DIALOGUE Potential service providers interested in participating in the dialogue are kindly asked to register via email as soon as possible and at the latest by 6 February 2026. Send the name and contact details of the interested service provider to maritta.riskila@laurea.fi. Use a reference "TD for an Online exam proctoring system" and the company name as the subject of the email. The service providers may register in Finnish or English.
sig_e7d5d6310a2da1c26cbb.title: Online exam proctoring system

sig_e7e767c9b6181b349fa2.description: The National Institute on Aging (NIA) intends to publish a Notice of Funding Opportunity (NOFO) that builds upon its investment in data-driven approaches for the purpose of defining molecular mechanisms of resilience in the presence of various types of Alzheimer's disease (AD) and AD-related dementias (ADRD) risk. The goal of this NOFO is to build a robust program that integrates epidemiologic, genomic, and mechanistic research through the use of data driven, systems-based approaches (including the use of artificial intelligence and/or machine learning methods) to discover the molecular/cellular determinants of resilience to AD/ADRD risk across representative populations. The initiative will support the generation of high-dimensional molecular data from brain and peripheral tissues, including longitudinal data, to enable dynamic modeling of resilience mechanisms and to discover molecular predictors of resilience. Applications are not being solicited at this time. Notice is being provided to allow potential applicants sufficient time to develop meaningful collaborations and responsive projects. This NOFO intends to utilize the U01 activity code. Investigators with expertise and insights into this area of aging research are encouraged to begin to consider applying for this new NOFO.
sig_e7e767c9b6181b349fa2.title: Interdisciplinary Research to Understand the Complex Biology of Resilience to Alzheimer’s and Related Dementias Disease Risk

sig_e7ece7826066941a8bf4.description: DESCRIPTION OF THE PROCUREMENT VR-Group Plc (“VR” or the “Contracting Entity”) is procuring a modern, SaaS-based HR solution to replace its current HRM systems in Finland and Sweden. The solution must provide a secure, reliable, and scalable platform for more than 10 000 employees globally, support country-specific requirements, and enable expansion into additional countries if needed, without major customization. VR is seeking a robust, scalable, and future-ready HR solution delivered as a single, integrated product. The solution will serve as VR’s central employment management platform and provide a reliable, secure, and consistent source of personnel and employment information throughout the employee lifecycle. The solution must enable VR to standardize and streamline core HR processes, reduce fragmented systems and manual work, improve data quality, and support efficient collaboration between HR, payroll, managers, employees, and other relevant stakeholders. The scope of this procurement is limited to the acquisition of the technology, including the HR SaaS solution and the necessary user licences. The implementation of the solution and the related support and maintenance services will be subject to a separate procurement procedure to be conducted after the technology provider has been selected. Thus, the selected HR technology must have a strong partner ecosystem in Finland and Sweden to enable competitive procurement. The new SaaS-based HR solution must include secure, enterprise-grade AI capabilities with appropriate governance and human oversight. The provider must also demonstrate continuous and substantial annual investment in product development. OBJECTIVES OF THE MARKET DIALOGUE VR is conducting a market dialogue to obtain specific, substantiated, and commercially relevant input on the planned procurement scope, requirements and delivery model. VR also seeks verifiable evidence of the solution’s impact on employee experience and customer satisfaction, supported by clearly defined metrics, comparable customer results, and independent research or third-party assessments. Participants must provide concrete, evidence-based responses and clearly distinguish between: - Standard, generally available product capabilities - Configurable functionality - AI capabilities currently in production - AI capabilities planned on the committed product roadmap - Partner-delivered services - Functionality requiring customization The purpose is to ensure that the procurement reflects proven market capabilities, supports VR’s strategic objectives, and enables genuine and effective competition. VR may use the results to refine the procurement scope, mandatory requirements, evaluation criteria, contractual framework, and subsequent tendering process. PRELIMINARY SCHEDULE - Market dialogue in September-October 2026 - Publication of the invitation to tender in November-December 2026 - Evaluation of the tenders and contract award in December 2026 - February 2027 - Contract period starts in November 2027 ADDITIONAL INFORMATION This notice is a request for information. It is not a contract notice or a call for tenders. The request for information includes an invitation to participate in a market dialogue. All interested suppliers are invited to participate in technical discussions with the Contracting Entity concerning the planned procurement. The purpose of the dialogue is to discuss the procurement at a general level and to obtain market feedback on the proposed scope and definition of the procurement. Discussion are held mainly as a written market dialogue rounds. Interested suppliers will be provided with preliminary procurement materials and/or questions for review and comments. The Contracting Entity may organize also joint market dialogue sessions and individual meetings with interested suppliers. Suppliers interested in participating in the market dialogue are requested to submit their expression of interest via the link:https://forms.cloud.microsoft/e/ZSEbHcb4b6 no later than 30th of September 2026 at 12:00 noon (Finnish time). Participation in the market dialogue does not oblige the Contracting Entity to proceed with the procurement, nor does it oblige suppliers to participate in any subsequent tendering procedure. Non-participation in the market dialogue does not prohibit supplier to submit a tender in the subsequent tendering procedure. The Contracting Entity reserves the right to amend the scope, content, procurement model, schedule and market dialogue process during the preparation of the procurement. No compensation will be paid to suppliers for participating in the market dialogue or for providing comments.
sig_e7ece7826066941a8bf4.title: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: HR Solution as a global Cloud solution for VR Group

In addition to good delivery reliability, the contract suppliers must have the ability, competence and resources to handle demanding and varied assignments within each area of expertise for the expert services. A framework arrangement will be formed from the procurement. The assignments covered by the procurement vary according to the current need. The procurement is divided into six areas as follows: • Area 1: Expert services for public procurements (goods and services) • Area 2: Expert services for public procurements (ICT procurements) • Area 3: Expert services for public procurements (construction) • Area 4: Expert services for public procurements (social and health services and other special service procurements) • Area 5: Expert services for public procurements (innovative procurements and procurement development) • Area 6: Legal services related to public procurements. For each area, 4 suppliers will be selected, unless there are fewer suppliers that meet the requirements. A separate priority order will be formed for each area. The maximum value of the procurement is 10,5 million euros (VAT 0 %). The estimated value includes the entire contract period, i.e. four (4) years, and it is estimated to be divided by area as follows: area 1: 2,8 million €, area 2: 2,65 million €, area 3: 1,65 million €, area 4: 700 000 €, area 5: 1 million €, area 6: 1,7 million €. The services of the area include goods and service procurements. There are separate areas for ICT procurements, construction-related procurements, social and health services and other special services, as well as innovative procurements. Assignments may include carrying out the entire procurement process or individual tasks related to the procurement process, participating in or leading working groups consisting of the contracting authority's experts and stakeholder representatives, and other expert tasks related to procurements. The area emphasises knowledge of the special features of ICT procurements and markets, their contract and pricing models, and other commercial aspects related to ICT procurements. Assignments may include carrying out the entire procurement process or individual tasks related to the procurement process, participating in or leading working groups consisting of the contracting authority's experts and stakeholder representatives, and other expert tasks related to procurements. The subject of the procurement is defined in more detail in this invitation to tender and its appendices.; The services of the area include construction-related procurements. The area emphasises special expertise related to construction projects, contract forms, YSE terms and conditions, and construction contract law. Assignments may include carrying out the entire procurement process or individual tasks related to the procurement process, participating in or leading working groups consisting of the contracting authority's experts and stakeholder representatives, and other expert tasks related to procurements. The subject of the procurement is defined in more detail in this invitation to tender and its appendices.; The services of the area include procurements according to social and health services and other special services, which belong to the procurements according to Appendix E of the Procurement Act. Assignments may include carrying out the entire procurement process or individual tasks related to the procurement process, participating in or leading working groups consisting of the contracting authority's experts and stakeholder representatives, and other expert tasks related to procurements. The subject of the procurement is defined in more detail in this invitation to tender and its appendices.; The services of the area include, in particular, innovative public procurements. By innovative procurements, we mean the procurement of a new or significantly improved product or service that aims to improve productivity, quality, sustainability and effectiveness. The area emphasises: - development of result- and effectiveness-based procurements and development/modelling of the earnings logic for related procurements, - definition of effectiveness targets and monitored impacts, as well as preparation of a measurement system. Assignments may include carrying out the entire procurement process or individual tasks related to the procurement process, participating in or leading working groups consisting of the contracting authority's experts and stakeholder representatives, and other expert tasks related to procurements. The subject of the procurement is defined in more detail in this invitation to tender and its appendices.; The services of the area do not include carrying out the entire procurement process, but the service focuses on legal advice related to public procurements and representation in courts regarding the Procurement Act (the Procurement Act refers to procurements falling within the scope of the Procurement Act and the Act on Public Procurement and Concession Contracts in the Utilities Sector; acts 1397/2016, 1398/2016). The contract comprises the analysis of the current assessment practice, the adaptation of the multidisciplinary ICF assessment form to the needs and context of DG HAN, its pilot implementation, as well as — as mandatory options — the preparation of digital implementation and change management, and finally the evaluation of the new instrument and recommendations regarding it. The services are described in more detail in point 8 and in Part B (technical specifications) of this special procurement documents.

sig_e93a745e6866864fb43d.description: This Request for Information seeks market input on modern Student Information Systems (SIS) for compulsory education in the City of Reykjavík. The Organization is interested in solutions that support student administration, school organization, attendance, assessment, communication, reporting, integrations, data management, security, privacy, accessibility and usability. sig_e943135f233a03f9eb30.description: The Commission is seeking to appoint a suitably qualified service provider for the design, management and delivery of a Shared Island Media Fund Talent Development and Content Development Initiative for Audiovisual Content. The successful Tenderer will be required to design, manage and deliver a structured programme of talent development and content development activities that strengthen professional capability within the audiovisual sector, facilitate collaboration between practitioners across the island of Ireland and support the development of high-quality audiovisual projects aligned with the objectives of the Shared Island Media Fund. The services to be provided include, but are not limited to: • designing and delivering a structured programme of workshops, masterclasses, mentoring, networking events and audiovisual content development activities; • developing and implementing a fair, open and transparent recruitment and selection process for programme participants; • facilitating collaboration between audiovisual practitioners from across the island of Ireland, including participants from different jurisdictions, backgrounds and communities; • providing experienced facilitators, mentors and industry specialists to support participant learning and project development; • supporting participants in the development of audiovisual projects that demonstrate potential to progress to production and reflect the objectives of the Shared Island Media Fund; • managing all aspects of programme delivery, stakeholder engagement, administration and communications; • monitoring programme delivery and performance against agreed milestones; and • providing progress reports, financial reporting and a final programme evaluation report in accordance with the requirements set out in Appendix 1 – Specification of Services.
sig_e943135f233a03f9eb30.title: Request for Tender for the Provision of a Shared Island Media Fund Talent Development and Content Development Initiative for Audiovisual Content

sig_e9507d2c77fcbafaa474.description: Essex County Council (ECC) is seeking information from suppliers who can provide an existing, fully developed, cloud based DBS processing platform to support its HR Shared Services Team. The team delivers recruitment and vetting services for ECC and external public sector customers. ECC is an established DBS Registered Body, Umbrella Organisation, & a Responsible Organisation and will continue operating in these capacities throughout the contract. All DBS applications must be submitted under ECC's Registered Body identity, with counter signatory duties remaining with ECC. The supplier will act solely as a processor and platform provider. The platform must support Basic, Standard and Enhanced DBS checks, provide comprehensive reporting to support invoicing and financial processes, offer customer self service capability, and operate with minimal impact on ECC's infrastructure. Suppliers must demonstrate appropriate business continuity arrangements (excluding any DBS initiated eBulk suspension) and provide training and knowledge transfer at mobilisation to enable ECC to train system users. ECC's current contract ends on 30 September 2026, and this early market engagement is being undertaken in preparation for that expiry. We aim to understand market capability, implementation timescales, indicative costs, and interest ahead of issuing our formal Request for Quotation (RFQ). We are keen to identify suppliers who wish to be included in the RFQ process. We look forward to hearing from interested suppliers as part of this early engagement exercise.
sig_e9507d2c77fcbafaa474.title: Cloud Based DBS Processing Platform

Part 1) - Procurement of technologies for server rooms The subject matter of this part of the public contract is the comprehensive supply, expert implementation and subsequent commissioning of a complete technological solution for the expansion and supplementation of the existing data centre infrastructure, both physically and technologically. Specifically, this involves the installation and integration of physical infrastructure elements, a modern air conditioning system, an uninterruptible power supply, a CCTV system for monitoring and security purposes, fire safety systems and the establishment of an optical connection with a dedicated backup server room, which will ensure high availability and operational continuity. Part 2) – Procurement of network technologies The subject matter of this part of the public contract is the supply, implementation and commissioning of a comprehensive solution to increase LAN access security and modernise the backbone and access network infrastructure. This includes the replacement of active components in both the access and backbone layers, the deployment of a network access control (NAC) system with support for IEEE 802.1X and the supply of central switch management in the form of on-premises or cloud management. New switches (2 backbone switches and 7 access switches) will be deployed within the access layer to ensure secure connection of end devices using authentication and authorisation based on IEEE 802.1X. This part forms the basic communication and authentication layer of the infrastructure and is designed in direct succession to the security, monitoring and logging systems specified in the technical specification - part 3, with which it must be fully interoperable at the level of access control, security events, logging and automated response. The aim is to expand the computing and storage capacity of the hospital infrastructure with an emphasis on high performance, redundancy, scalability, advanced management and security features, including support for virtualisation, high availability and data services. Furthermore, the supply, implementation and commissioning of a comprehensive solution for the security of the organisation's perimeter, security policy management and cyber threat detection. This includes the deployment of a high-availability firewall cluster, a central security event management system and training of responsible personnel. sig_e9c92664fd86afcef37d.buyer_name: Jyväskylä University of Applied Sciences Ltd.
sig_e9c92664fd86afcef37d.description: NOTE! THIS IS NOT A CONTRACT NOTICE OR A CALL FOR TENDERS BUT A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION FOR MARKET RESEARCH AND TECHNICAL DIALOGUE: Simulation system Subject and purpose of the request for information: The purpose of the request for information is to survey solutions available on the market and, in particular, companies that have the capability to design and implement a large-scale simulation system for the Contracting Authority's needs. The request for information is used to gather information for procurement planning. The Hippos area being built in Jyväskylä offers an international-level complex for physical activity, hobbies and sport. The area strengthens Jyväskylä's position as a centre for physical activity, elite sports, research and education. The Hippos Centre consists of four entities: Sports Centre, Competence Centre, Ice Sports Centre and the HipposPark car park. The Welfare Unit of Jyväskylä University of Applied Sciences is relocating to the 5 and 6 floors of the Competence Centre. Construction will begin in January 2026 and will be completed in late 2027. The commissioning of the premises is planned for August 2027. The subject of the procurement is a simulation system (AV system), which covers the simulation premises and learning premises on two floors as well as control rooms from which simulation situations and connections to various teaching premises are controlled. The simulation system is used to create simulation exercises resembling genuine interaction and customer situations for teaching purposes. The system enables the recording, saving and real-time control of situations. The objective of the request for information is to obtain information so that the planned procurement can be implemented as purposefully as possible. Responding to the request for information is not a prerequisite for participation in the subsequent procurement procedure and does not affect the tenderer's position in the procurement procedure. The matters presented in the request for information are preliminary and may change as the procurement preparations progress. This notice is a market survey used in the preparation of the procurement by Jyväskylä University of Applied Sciences. The contracting authority requests potential suppliers to respond through this request for information and to participate in one-to-one market dialogues. Participation is voluntary and no remuneration is paid for participating. The responses given and discussions held will be treated with complete confidentiality.
sig_e9c92664fd86afcef37d.title: Jamk - Simulation system request for information

sig_e9e86b4dc1a5aa7b8af5.description: In this context, all building files of department 6-63 - Building Inspection are to be digitised and imported into the existing DMS (enaio from the company Optimal Systems). Department 6-63 - Building Inspection expects both space savings and media-break-free case processing as a result. Lot LOT-0001: Scanning services for the digitisation of the building file archive of department 6-63 - Building Inspection. Key data These are approx. 970 linear metres of building files which are to be digitised in a legally compliant manner and in compliance with data protection regulations with security class "Normal" in accordance with TR-RESISCAN and subsequently imported into the DMS (enaio) of the company Optimal Systems. The importing into the DMS is carried out by the contracting authority. All building files are to be processed within 3 years (i.e. approx. 27 linear metres per month). Assumptions (estimated values/extrapolation): - per linear metre approx. 1.500 - 2000 sheets - 50% of the sheets are double-sided, i.e. 3.000 pages per linear metre - 27 linear metres of files per month * 3.000 pages per linear metre = 81.000 pages per month - The file volume per file amounts on average to 100 to 200 sheets of vouchers and drawings up to format DIN A3 as well as additionally about 5 to 10 large-format drawings or plans. The complete process steps from collection/recording, file preparation, scanning, indexing to the return of original documents etc. to the contracting authority are the responsibility of the service provider.
sig_e9e86b4dc1a5aa7b8af5.title: Scanning services for the digitisation of the building file archive of department 6-63 - Building Inspection

sig_ea514f98d47fe9c1a57a.description:
The subject of the contract is the provision of service support for an economic information system. The support will include the following parts: 1. Microsoft Dynamics NAV (hereinafter “MD NAV”) updates within the Microsoft Enhancement Plan. 2. Service and updates for the economic information system, including all its add-ons. Helpdesk service provided via a web portal and development and support service according to the Contracting Authority's requirements. The Contracting Authority has a valid MS BREP "Business Ready Enhancement Plan" (hereinafter “maintenance”) for MD NAV Acct number: 6100645 valid until 29.10.2026. The Contractor shall conclude a contract with the Contracting Authority for the further continuation of maintenance – Microsoft Enhancement Plan for a fixed term until 29.10.2029 inclusive. The provision of the maintenance service shall include the right to use all higher versions, entitlement to service packs and updates, entitlement to support and a guarantee of compatibility with other Microsoft products released by Microsoft for use in the Czech Republic for Microsoft Dynamics NAV. The Contracting Authority requires that the price of this service be fixed for the entire duration of the contract. The contract will be concluded for a fixed term of 3 years from the date it becomes effective. The Contracting Authority requires the commencement of performance under the contract from 30. 10. 2026. Provided that the contractor commences performance according to the Contracting Authority's requirement by 30. 10. 2026, the contract will be concluded for a fixed term until 29.10.2029 inclusive. In the event that the contract becomes effective after 30. 10. 2026, the contractor shall commence the provision of performance under the contract on the date the contract becomes effective, with performance being provided for a period of 3 years. All software solutions (within part 1) will be supplied and implemented in the On-Premise version.; and: Updates to extension modules The Contracting Authority uses extension modules supplied by Konica Minolta IT Solutions Czech a.s. The service includes: - provision of an unlimited right to use all new released versions and updates of these modules for the duration of the contractual relationship. - ensuring such updates and modifications to the EIS that allow for the processing of financial, asset and other necessary data in the EIS in accordance with the legislative requirements of the Czech Republic that are binding on the Contracting Authority. The contractor shall carry out the necessary updates and modifications to the EIS in sufficient time so that they are implemented without serious acceptance reservations no later than 10 working days before the date on which the relevant legislative requirements enter into force and become binding on the Contracting Authority. In the event that the period between the publication of a legal regulation and the date of its entry into force is less than 30 days, and the contractor is unable to ensure the update and modification in advance, the deadline for delivery of the update shall be 30 days from the publication of this regulation. The contractor guarantees the flawless functionality of the reflected changes and simultaneously guarantees the flawless functionality of other system modules that were not affected by the changes made. In the event of identified defects and errors, the contractor undertakes to remove the discrepancies under the conditions stated in point b: Helpdesk Service. The contractor is obliged, when performing the public contract, to take such measures and act in such a way as to prevent the occurrence of damage. If the contractor causes damage to the Contracting Authority or other entities, the contractor is obliged to remove the damage without undue delay and, if this is not possible, to compensate for it financially. All costs associated with this shall be borne by the contractor. The choice of the method of compensation for damage belongs to the Contracting Authority if it is affected by the damage. The service does not include: - provision of an unlimited right to use all new released versions of the Travel Orders module and updates to the Travel Orders module for the duration of the contractual relationship. b: Helpdesk Service The service consists of resolving service requests, complaints about products and services supplied as part of previous performance reported using the web portal. The web portal for reporting service requests must be available 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. The service response to service requests must be ensured according to the priorities listed below. In the event of technical difficulties, there must be an option to submit a request via email or telephone. The following priorities are set for submitting service requests: 1. Emergency – The EIS is unusable in its basic functions. This state may threaten the operational activity of the Contracting Authority or its obligations arising from the law within a time horizon of five working days. 2. High – Some EIS functions work in a limited manner, but this limitation cannot be considered as one that could threaten the operational activity of the Contracting Authority or its obligations arising from the law within a time horizon of two weeks. 3. Standard – There is no danger of direct threat to the operational activity of the Contracting Authority. The contractor shall contractually undertake to commence the resolution of a service request with a given priority and resolve it as follows: 1. Emergency – within 5 hours of reporting, the contractor shall inform the Contracting Authority of the receipt of the request with an expected resolution date as soon as possible, no later than 24 hours from the notification of the service request. The contractor shall ensure the resolution of the request even during non-working days (i.e. Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays). 2. High – within 24 hours of reporting, the contractor shall inform the Contracting Authority of the receipt of the request, commence resolution no later than the next working day, and resolve within 5 working days from the notification of the operational problem 3. Standard – within 48 hours of reporting, the contractor shall inform the Contracting Authority of the receipt of the request, commence resolution no later than within 1 week, and resolve within 2 weeks from the notification of the operational problem. Resolution of a request means: - resolution of the reported (recorded) request or - provision of another acceptable solution or - proposal of an acceptable alternative solution or - provision of instructions for an alternative solution, which, however, does not have to be accepted by the Contracting Authority as a sufficient solution - forwarding the problem for resolution to a third party (e.g. Microsoft, HW supplier, etc.) in the event of a problem caused by the incorrect behaviour of a component supplied or supported by a third party c: Development and support service according to the Contracting Authority's requirements and ensuring compliance with legislation The service consists of drawing on a guaranteed range of hours at a set hourly rate excluding VAT.

The minimum required guaranteed range is set at 10 hours per month. The basis for invoicing will be the hours actually realised and not the guaranteed capacity. The contractor must guarantee the availability of the above-mentioned service in the range of at least 10 hours per month (with the understanding that this indicative range is also set for the purposes of evaluating tenders). However, the Contracting Authority will draw according to its current needs and does not have to use up all the guaranteed hours. At the same time, it may also exceed the number of hours. The contractor will invoice the service based on the actual number of hours consumed, based on the set hourly rate. Requests are submitted via the web portal, where all communication takes place – proposal of the request solution, schedule, determination of labour intensity, price and ordering, or rejection. At the same time, the web portal will send confirmation emails to selected email addresses of the Contracting Authority regarding the entry and status of the request resolution upon every saved change. In the event of technical difficulties, there is an option to submit a request via email or telephone. The service can also be used for consultation visits by a contractor's employee with the aim of providing expert consultations for resolving requests at the Contracting Authority's workplace. It can also be used for the implementation of new versions of updates, upgrades or builds of Microsoft Dynamics NAV application equipment and extension modules with regard to legislative changes. All software solutions (within part 2 of the public contract) will be supplied and implemented in the on-premises version.

sig_ea971947a93b5580d449.description: MARKET CONSULTATION The subject of the market consultation is the procurement of a maintenance operations management system for the tracks of Väylävirasto. BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES The most central task of the operations management system is to support day-to-day maintenance management by offering various functionalities for equipment and work management ranging from work planning to work reporting, as well as enabling various tracking functions, for example with regard to accumulated work and costs. Another key factor for the system is to support information-driven management, i.e., to provide, inter alia, up-to-date information on maintenance activities carried out on assets and the resulting costs, as well as potential consequential effects over the entire lifecycle of the equipment. The system's functionalities should offer the target organisation the opportunity to implement maintenance operations characteristic of its operations in a process-driven manner, such that the system supports the execution of the process at different stages of the process, in accordance with the functionalities required of it. The efficient implementation of maintenance processes, ensuring both personnel and information security, requires strong support from the operations management system with which operations are managed and monitored. The operations management system should provide an open interface for the target organisation to monitor and manage maintenance operations between different stakeholders, such as in situations where maintenance is procured either partially or entirely as a service. In addition to the primary functionalities of maintenance management, the operations management system should cover a wide range of various functionalities supporting operations. The functionalities of the system can be roughly classified as follows: - Equipment management - Work management - Reports and analysis - Mobile application - User management - Cost tracking - Contract management - Inventory management - Procurement The task of the operations management system is to act in connection with day-to-day maintenance management as part of the broader system architecture of Väylävirasto. For this reason, various integrations with other operational and administrative systems of Väylävirasto will also be necessary. PRELIMINARY SCHEDULE The contracting authority's target schedule for carrying out the market consultation and procurement is: - Market consultation, technical dialogue (commenting on material) September-October 2025 - Market consultation, bilateral negotiations (approx. 3-6 companies) October-early November 2025 - Year 2026 ----- ADDITIONAL INFORMATION ON THE NOTICE This notice is a prior information notice. This notice does not request tenders. The prior information notice is accompanied by an invitation to a market consultation, whereby all suppliers interested in the procurement have the opportunity to engage in a technical dialogue concerning the procurement with Väylävirasto. The purpose of the technical dialogue is to discuss the subject matter of the procurement and its definition at a general level. The technical dialogue does not bind Väylävirasto to carry out the procurement. Nor does the technical dialogue bind the supplier to participate in a potential tendering procedure, nor does it prevent participation if the supplier has not participated in the dialogue. TECHNICAL DIALOGUE AND BILATERAL DISCUSSIONS The market consultation is organised in two phases: 1. As a technical dialogue, where potential suppliers are asked to familiarise themselves with the service description and requirement specification and to answer the contracting authority's preliminary questions (carried out in September-October by email in accordance with registrations) 2. As bilateral discussions, where the contracting authority invites 3-6 suppliers to discussions. The contracting authority will send invitations to the discussions to the selected suppliers as soon as possible. The discussions will take place during October-November 2025 (the following times are preliminarily reserved, participants are requested to reserve the times in their calendars where possible): - Mon 27.10 at 9.30-11 - Mon 27.10 at 14-15.30 - Wed 29.10 at 14.30-16 - Fri 31.10 at 12-13.30 - Mon 3.11 at 14-15.30 - Wed 5.11 at 12-13.30 The times will be confirmed to the suppliers selected for the bilateral negotiations approximately two weeks before the time. In addition to the above, the contracting authority reserves the right for a later scheduled commenting period on draft versions of the final tender documentation and for answering the contracting authority's new questions related to the subject matter of the procurement. INSTRUCTIONS FOR REGISTRATION The supplier must notify its interest in participating in the market consultation by 20.10.2025 at 12.00 by sending a message to tommi.aarnio@vayla.fi and virpi.kukkonen@vayla.fi with the subject heading: "Ratojen kunnossapidon toiminnanohjausjärjestelmä - markkinavuoropuhelu". The supplier is requested to provide the following information in the message: - name, email address and telephone number of the supplier's contact person - a brief description of the supplier (e.g., the company's line of business and main services) - a brief description of the solution offered by the supplier for the procurement subject to the market consultation - information on whether the solution is an already existing solution or a concept under development - the supplier's previous deliveries and references (corresponding to the subject matter of the procurement) The descriptions presented in this prior information notice and the estimated publication date of the contract notice, as well as the dialogue draft materials to be provided later, are preliminary and indicative procurement information. Participating companies will not be paid compensation for responding or participating.
