sig_f0e24f0a815eeb1b6a10.description: HUS requests your tender for a software service that manages HUS Pharmacy's enterprise resource planning, covering the operational areas described in the appendices. Processes and data concerning HUS Pharmacy's medication management will be configured into the software service to be procured. The software service must integrate with the systems used by HUS in its other enterprise resource planning (e.g. Oracle Fusion Cloud). The appendices to the call for tender (appendix 0 and appendices 1: Description of current operations) describe the scope of current operations through verbal descriptions by operational area. The purpose of the descriptions is to familiarise the tenderer with HUS Pharmacy's current operations. The appendices (appendices 2: Description of target state) describe the requirements set for the subject of the procurement by operational area using various process descriptions and listed requirements. The purpose of this is to express to tenderers the minimum requirements set for enterprise resource planning. In addition, objectives for developing current operations are described. Our intention is to replace the current system with a software service (SaaS) that enables process development and guarantees a qualitatively stable operation. HUS is seeking a SaaS-based software service, which must be based on software that is already in production use and ready-made, and a solution configured from it for the contracting authority. The project schedule is planned such that the software service will be implemented during the year 2028. The project will be initiated with a definition phase, in which the made descriptions are refined against the software service offered by the winning tenderer, thereby ensuring that the software service in question meets the set requirements and offers a clear development path. In this definition phase, the implementation project plan is also refined to such a level that the parties can commit to the execution of the project. The definition phase is invoiced on a time basis, for a maximum of 50 000 euros and for a duration of no more than four months. The appendix Description of the implementation project explains in more detail what must be produced during the definition phase. After the definition phase, both parties have the option, if they so wish, to withdraw from the project. Following the definition phase, the contracting authority and the tenderer will negotiate the target workload and price for the project in the manner presented in the call for tender. Other appendices to the call for tender describe requirements related to the implementation phase, ongoing services, and information security. The software service must be capable of being integrated in a conventional manner into various administrative systems. The interfaces of the software service are presented in the appendix "Integrations". Oracle FINA interfaces are individually described in more detail in appendix 2.9.3. The appendix "Draft Agreement" covers operations during both the implementation phase and ongoing services. The appendix "Price Form" describes the calculation of the comparative price of tenders and the procedures for establishing the target price.
sig_f0e24f0a815eeb1b6a10.title: e-Forms 2023 / EU / HUS 486-2023 Pharmacy enterprise resource planning system as a software service

sig_f171b70efb97b0b9eef4.description: The aim of this project is to provide tools in the form of a guideline and a tool for public administration, industry, and security research that make it possible to increase the resilience of cloud applications in particular against microarchitectural attacks such as Spectre and Meltdown and newer variants. The focus is to be on defensive programming countermeasures at the application level. In this way, the security of the software used is to be made more independent of the cloud provider's countermeasures. To reach as large a target group as possible, the results are to be written in English. The guideline is to describe concrete, practical, and easily applicable measures, and the developed tool is to automatically identify vulnerabilities and mitigate them if necessary. Supply of a forest fire location system divided into two parts. Part No. 1 - Supply, installation and commissioning of a forest fire monitoring system based on long-range fire-fighting cameras together with software for automatic smoke detection. Part No. 2 - Supply, installation and commissioning of a complete unmanned aerial vehicle system with an automatic docking station for fire monitoring of forest areas. A detailed description can be found in the relevant parts of the contract. The subject of the contract consists of sets of equipment together with installation and commissioning, the task of which will be to enable automatic detection and location of forest fires, including long-range fire-fighting cameras mounted on observation towers together with necessary accessories and the equipment of the Inspectorate's Alarm and Dispatch Point (ADP). The purpose of the system will be to carry out continuous fire monitoring of forest areas. Fire-fighting cameras mounted on observation towers are to work with the supplied software for automatic fire detection, which is intended to increase the effectiveness of monitoring in the given area. The image from the cameras must be sent to the ADP via a radio link in the unlicensed band, supplied and installed under this contract. The transmission system must be designed in a way that enables the future change of the transmission medium from radio to fibre-optic without the need to replace cameras, software and active network devices, with the exception of terminal devices used for connecting the fibre optic.. The Baczków and Hysne towers should be retrofitted with an Off-Grid power supply installation, and the ADP with a UPS emergency power supply system. The power supply must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62040-5-3:2017-05 (UPS systems) or equivalent. The installation must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62446-1:2016-08 (Photovoltaic installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62446-1:2016-08/A1:2019-01 (Testing of PV installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62109-2:2011 (Inverter safety) or equivalent and PN-EN IEC 62619:2023-02 (Lithium battery safety) or equivalent. The contract includes: - dismantling of the existing fire monitoring system, - supply and installation of 3 cameras for observing forest areas on the Baczków, Hysne and Dąbrowa fire-fighting towers, - supply and installation of sprinklers together with a fluid tank for the mounted cameras, - supply and installation of an off-grid power supply on the Baczków and Hysne towers. The installation must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62548 (Photovoltaic installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62446 (Testing of PV installations) or equivalent, PN-EN 62109 (Inverter safety) or equivalent and PN-EN IEC 62619 (Lithium battery safety) or equivalent. - supply and installation of an alarm system and anti-burglary cameras on the fire-fighting towers, - supply and installation of radio links establishing connections: ● Baczków tower – Hysne tower in the 5 GHz band, ● Hysne tower – Dąbrowa tower in the 5 GHz band, ● Dąbrowa tower – Church in the 60 GHZ band with a backup 5 GHz, ● Church – Inspectorate building in the 60 GHZ band with a backup 5 GHz, ● Baczków tower – Dąbrowa tower in the 5 GHz band (redundant connection), - supply and installation of devices to provide backup communication 5G/LTE, - supply and installation of ADP equipment: ● supply and installation of 3 televisions for observing images from fire-fighting cameras, ● supply and installation of a computer with two monitors, ● supply and installation of a control console, ● supply and installation of a UPS emergency power supply. The power supply must meet the requirements of PN-EN 62040 (UPS systems) or equivalent. - supply, installation and commissioning of an automatic smoke detection system, - training on system operation. The Contractor is obliged to execute a complete work from the point of view of the purpose it is to serve. The Contracting Authority permits the installation of additional devices not included in the specification if they are necessary to achieve the required functionalities. Other information can be found in the procurement documents - Appendix No. 2 to the ToR; Supply, installation and commissioning of a complete unmanned aerial vehicle system with an automatic docking station for fire monitoring of forest areas - equipment under the FEnIKS project entitled: Comprehensive project for the adaptation of forests and forestry to climate change - prevention, counteracting and limiting the effects of threats related to forest fires (FIRE 2). 1. Subject of the contract 1.1. The subject of the contract is the supply of one complete, factory-new and unused UAS system comprising an unmanned aerial vehicle, an automatic docking station, a multi-sensor observation head, a control device, software, accessories, installation, configuration, commissioning, training and warranty service. 1.2. The system will be intended primarily for: automatic and ad-hoc patrols of forest areas during the fire hazard period; remote verification of smoke or fire alarms, including alarms transmitted by the alarm and dispatch point, camera system or rescue services; locating heat sources and determining their coordinates; live transmission in the visible and thermal imaging band; monitoring fire development, access roads, endangered objects and control after extinguishing a fire. 1.3. The subject of the contract has been described through functional requirements and minimum performance parameters. The Contracting Authority does not require a product of a specific brand or a single manufacturer's solution. However, all elements must form one compatible system, for the correct operation of which the Contractor is responsible. 2. Basis and rules for describing the subject of the contract. The description was drawn up taking into account in particular Article 16, Article 99, Article 101 and Article 105–107 of the Act of 11 September 2019 on Public Procurement Law (unified text: Journal of Laws of 2026, item 793 as amended). References to standards are to be understood as references to the indicated standard or an equivalent standard.

• Each indicated parameter is a minimum parameter, unless expressly stated otherwise. • Structurally different technical solutions are permitted if they ensure at least the same functionality, level of security and performance parameters. • If meeting a requirement requires an additional module, licence, modem, antenna, service or accessory, this element must be included in the tender and price. • All costs necessary to use the full functionality of the system for the period indicated in the OPZ must be itemised in the price form. Other information can be found in the procurement documents - Appendix No. 2 to the ToR

sig_f190c6d0543acc5586a5.description: The European Green Deal is the roadmap for making the EU’s economy sustainable. It is a set of policy initiatives with the overarching aim of making Europe climate neutral by 2050. The "Economics of Climate Change, Energy and Transport" Unit (JRC.C.6) of the Joint Research Centre supports the European Commission’s European Green Deal by performing economics-based research in several areas related to energy and climate change. This work includes the development of a reference toolset of economic models and the completion of associated research activities to improve the models' reliability and robustness. The JRC.C.6 Unit is based in Seville, Spain. JRC.C.6 is seeking to strengthen its socio-economic research and modelling capabilities by expanding its coverage of modelling areas and by updating and improving its existing models and toolsets. The unit JRC.C.6 maintains, develops and applies a number of quantitative tools to analyse the impact of different policies on the energy demand and supply sectors, as well as tools for macro-economic modelling. This toolset comprises the EU and global partial equilibrium models POTEnCIA and POLES including their corresponding databases (notably JRC-IDEES), and the global general equilibrium model JRC-GEM-E3. All these tools are able to provide model output in terms of CO2 emissions. The comprehensive modelling of climate change mitigation scenarios requires additional information as regards non-CO2 greenhouse gas emissions as well as on emissions and sinks related to land use, land use change and forestry offsets (LULUCF). Besides, climate action can have important co[1]benefits in terms of reduced emissions of air pollutants and of improved air quality. This Framework Contract aims at supporting the operation of the abovementioned set of models by providing the JRC with data, methods and results relevant for the analysis of non-CO2 greenhouse gas emissions, emissions of air pollutants (including air quality impacts), and LULUCF offsets.
sig_f190c6d0543acc5586a5.title: Provision of services to support economic modelling of climate change and energy policies: Modelling of non-CO2 greenhouse gases, air pollutants, and LULUCF offsets

sig_f1a6632c8b8048d5313d.description: The aims of the project are to produce an evaluation of the SLC’s rural land market reporting to generate insights and improvements for future reporting. The evaluation will focus on several elements: 1) Impact – this objective is to understand the use of the report and its effects, outcomes and the extent to which reporting is effective in informing policy and decision making. There is a comparative element for this. 2) Process – understanding the effectiveness of the current approach, how the reporting process is working, assessing potential improvements to the methodology, and considering expansion of the coverage of reporting to other areas. 3) Economic Value – understanding value for money and costing the tangible benefits of the reports compared to the costs. What are the wider economic benefits to participants, public finances and society? 4) Analysis and Recommendations – the above steps inform the analysis and evaluation to understand to what extent and degree of progress towards the reporting aims are being made, and any recommendations for improvements. The report should, where appropriate, include advice for the SLC for future land market reports. Lot 1: . sig_f1cdfe45e91beb444607.description: Dundee City Council intends to procure a construction consultant resource and project management system to improve the planning, allocation and monitoring of architectural, engineering and specialist consultancy resources across its capital and housing programmes. The information gathered will assist the Council in developing its procurement strategy, refining its requirements and determining the most appropriate route to market. As part of this exercise, the Council intends to invite selected suppliers to participate in product demonstrations, currently anticipated to take place during early October 2026 (please note, these dates are indicative only). These demonstrations will provide an opportunity for the Council to gain a greater understanding of available solutions, functionality, implementation approaches and delivery models. Suppliers wishing to be considered for participation in the demonstration stage are requested to complete and return the attached questionnaire. The information provided will be used solely for market engagement purposes and to assist the Council in identifying suppliers whose solutions appear capable of meeting the Council's requirements. Completed questionnaires should be submitted by 12 Noon on 25 September 2026 to trina.forbes@dundeecity.gov.uk. Suppliers who do not submit a completed questionnaire will not be considered for participation in the demonstration stage. The Council reserves the right to limit the number of demonstrations undertaken and participation in this market engagement exercise will not confer any advantage or disadvantage in any subsequent procurement process. Additional information: This PIN is issued for market engagement purposes only and will not be used to evaluate, select or exclude suppliers in any future procurement process. Information received will help Dundee City Council understand the market, develop its requirements and determine the most appropriate procurement approach. Participation is voluntary and does not commit the Council to proceed.

Failure to meet the above requirement shall result in the rejection of the tender pursuant to Article 226 paragraph 1 point 17 or point 19 of the Public Procurement Law respectively. In the event of the publication of a recommendation or a decision covering an ICT element used for the execution of the contract, the contractor shall immediately inform the contracting authority thereof and present a method for ensuring the continued compliance of the performance of the contract with legal provisions and the procurement documents. The subject of the contract is: a) execution of the modernisation of the permanent exhibition of the Toruń History Museum in the Esken House according to the design constituting attachment no. 1 to the SWZ and the description of the subject of the contract constituting attachment no. 2. b) execution of a temporary panel exhibition in cooperation with a foreign partner – within the scope of preparing the design of a maximum of 20 panels and their print on PVC 5 mm, dimensions 131 x 120 cm (portrait), secured with UV foil – the panels will be mounted by the Contracting Authority in its existing frame in the area of the Old Town Hall. sig_f1ff1a84db1ec5d89195.description: This is not a prior information notice, call for tenders, procurement notice or invitation to negotiate, nor does the publication of the notice initiate a competitive tendering procedure. A possible procurement notice and call for tenders will be published later. The request for information does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement. This request for information surveys the market and obtains information regarding the procurement when planning the procurement of the Helsinki City artificial intelligence management system. The objective of this request for information is to obtain information on solutions, capabilities and alternative implementation methods available on the market before the actual potential tendering process. Helsingin kaupunki is preparing a procurement for an artificial intelligence management system, the purpose of which is to enable the management and documentation of obligations in accordance with the EU Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act) and to support the lifecycle management of all the city's artificial intelligence systems. The artificial intelligence management system enables the management, demonstration and reporting of the obligations of the provider and deployer of the EU Artificial Intelligence Act with regard to high-risk artificial intelligence systems, and supports the management of all the city's artificial intelligence systems, the identification and management of artificial intelligence risks, and communication about artificial intelligence. The artificial intelligence management system will produce information for the city's management, artificial intelligence developers, and the city's services and websites utilizing artificial intelligence. The system will act as a central tool in identifying and managing risks, documentation, preparing communications and supporting deployment processes. Further information on the subject matter of the procurement is described in the appendix "Description of the subject matter of the procurement". The contracting authority will deliver potentially preliminary tender documents for commenting later. The information collected through the request for information and market dialogue will remain confidential and will be used solely for procurement planning. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION The contracting authority is not bound by the information stated in this notice or its appendices, but as the preparation progresses, the subject matter and requirements of the procurement may change. The responses given in the request for information are not binding on the supplier. Responding to the request for information is not a prerequisite for participation in any subsequent procurement that may be organized. Responding or failing to respond to the request for information does not affect a potential supplier's position in the actual tendering process. No compensation is paid for responding to the request for information or participating in the market dialogue. Preliminarily, the call for tenders is planned to be published during June 2026.

sig_f39e1119fdcfe02fd7c1.description: Short Description This Notice signals BIST's intention to go to market for the provision of Data Pipelines, Analytics and Visualisation (DPAV) services in support of the National Digital Twin Programme (NDTP) and is for Market Engagement purposes only. The National Digital Twin Programme is a BIST led programme developing trusted, secure and reusable digital twin capabilities across government and wider public sector partners. The programme develops open source technologies, interoperability mechanisms, data sharing capabilities and application-layer services to support improved decision-making through data and digital technologies. Description of the Scope NDTP is seeking to engage with suppliers capable of providing specialist Data Pipelines, Analytics and Visualisation (DPAV) services. The requirement will support the design, development, testing, deployment and continuous improvement of data-driven applications, analytics products, visualisation tools and supporting data pipelines across the NDTP portfolio. The scope may include the development of new applications and analytical capabilities, enhancement and extension of existing NDTP applications, creation of data ingestion and transformation pipelines, integration with nodes, node nets, APIs and data services, and the delivery of user-facing dashboards, maps, visualisations, analytical tools and decision-support capabilities. Suppliers may also be required to support geospatial analysis, scenario modelling, application deployment, technical documentation and transition to operational environments. The successful supplier will be expected to work within NDTP's open source delivery model, contributing code and associated artefacts through NDTP GitHub environments and supporting collaboration with government departments, public sector organisations, technical partners and other suppliers. To aid BIST in developing the specification, we are interested in furthering our understanding of the market and available capabilities. In particular, we would like to hear from suppliers with experience in application development, data engineering, analytics, visualisation, open source delivery, cloud-native technologies and integration of complex data services. Additional information: Additional Information Please note that should we proceed to market we will use the Government Commercial Agency (GCA) Spark DPS RM6094 to undertake this procurement. Only suppliers who are registered on the Spark DPS will be eligible to participate. If this opportunity is of interest, suppliers are strongly encouraged to register as soon as possible, as applications to join the DPS are assessed independently by GCA and processing times may vary. BIST intends to undertake the initial Spark DPS supplier filtering exercise during the week commencing 24th August. Suppliers wishing to be considered for this opportunity should ensure they are successfully registered on the Spark DPS and that their category selections align with the filters set out in Annex A before this date. Following the filtering exercise, BIST will issue a capability assessment questionnaire to the shortlisted suppliers. Completion of the capability assessment will be a mandatory requirement in order to be considered for invitation to tender. It is anticipated that the ITT will be published in September 2026. The contract is expected to have a value of up to £10.5 million and run until October 2029, with the option to extend for up to one additional year. This advance notice is intended to provide suppliers with sufficient time to complete Spark DPS registration and review their selected categories before the procurement is launched. Details can be found at https://www.gca.gov.uk/agreements/RM6094. Any queries relating to registering on the Spark DPS should be directed to GCA as BIST does not have any control over the process or requirements. Annex A - Spark DPS Filters Delivery Method AI & Automation Natural Language Processing Predicted Analytics Prescriptive Analysis Engineering / Materials Science Spatial Computing Data Data Presentation Location UK Security Above Official
sig_f39e1119fdcfe02fd7c1.title: Provision National Digital Twins Programme - Data Pipelines, Analytics and Visualisation PIN

sig_f3a68edde8703acddc60.description: This Challenge presents an exciting opportunity to make a positive difference in protecting children in Scotland from harm, an area of the highest priority for the Scottish Cabinet and partners. Scotland’s child protection system relies on Inter-Agency Referral Discussions (IRDs) to make timely safeguarding decisions for children (over 17,000 IRDs took place during 2024-25). IRDs are effective and work well as a process, however they are currently supported by fragmented IT systems, manual processes and localised records. This results in duplication, delays, and barriers to information sharing across agencies and local authorities. These inefficiencies increase administrative burden, reducing time available for direct support to children and families. The Scottish Government, Police Scotland and the National Social Work Agency (TBC) are seeking innovative solutions that will enable secure streamlined multi-agency information sharing for the existing IRD process, as well as providing real-time local and national data to improve child protection outcomes across Scotland.
sig_f3a68edde8703acddc60.title: CivTech 12.5 - How can technology support multi agency processes for the protection of children in Scotland?

sig_f3a77ce61c4837cba610.description: Oslo municipality would like to map whether there are market participants who have systems that can or are able to meet the municipality's needs, which are summarised below and described in the attached document. sig_f3b8c5e60f281ca93dcc.description: The purpose of this above-threshold Public contract for services awarded in an open procedure pursuant to Section 56 et seq. of the Public Procurement Act is the conclusion of (i) a contract for the implementation of an application / applications focused on supporting financial risk management for the needs of Risk Tools, HBK System – Rating Calculator (“HBK System – Rating Calculator”; “Implementation Contract”) and (ii) a subsequent contract for the maintenance, support and development of the HBK System – Rating Calculator (“Service Contract”; the Implementation Contract and the Service Contract collectively the “Contracts” or “Contractual Documentation”). The subject of the Public contract is the supply and implementation of a new application or applications focused on supporting risk management tools, and the provision of related services, specifically: - supply and implementation of the HBK System – Rating Calculator; - development of Rating models according to the Contracting Authority's requirements; - independent validation of the developed Rating models; - services leading to the successful implementation of the HBK System – Rating Calculator in the Contracting Authority's environment; - provision of long-term support and maintenance and minor development for a period of 10 years from the implementation of the HBK System – Rating Calculator. Based on the Contracts, the subject of the Public contract will be realised with one supplier, whose tender will be evaluated as the most economically advantageous based on the evaluation of tenders. Rating calculator A rating calculator is a technological solution, i.e. a system / application or functional component that uses a Rating model to systematically evaluate entities. Rating model A rating model is a systematic tool used to evaluate a client's creditworthiness. The goal of the Public contract implementation is the simplification of processes, the use of modern technologies and approaches, and the flexibility of the HBK System – Rating Calculator fulfilling the Contracting Authority's premises. The Contracting Authority points out that through this Public contract it is seeking a supplier that will provide it with a complete solution, i.e. it will both supply and implement the HBK System – Rating Calculator (and ensure its support and maintenance), and create individual Rating models according to the Contracting Authority's requirements and ensure their independent validation. Rating models will be newly created in the HBK System – Rating Calculator with limited use of the Bank's historical client data. The Contracting Authority does not possess the know-how for the creation and implementation of Rating models and the selected supplier therefore cannot expect above-standard cooperation from the Contracting Authority in this area. The Contracting Authority is able to provide the selected supplier with a limited range of data, but is not able to provide the scope of data on which it would be possible to calibrate a Rating model. The subject of the Public contract is the supply, implementation, maintenance, development and support of the HBK System – Rating Calculator (including the development and validation of Rating models), the detailed specification and components of which are set out in detail in the annexes to the Contracts. The performance will be divided into two Contracts, i.e. into (i) the Implementation Contract and (ii) the Service Contract. Based on the Service Contract, the service, maintenance, support and minor development of the System will take place. A closer specification of the subject of the Public contract is regulated in other parts of the Tender documentation, especially in the binding drafts of the Contractual Documentation – Annex No. 6 and 7 of the Tender documentation, and the Technical specification of the Public contract – Annex No. 8. For more, see the TD.
sig_f3b8c5e60f281ca93dcc.title: HBK System – Rating calculator

sig_f407665173fc522d220b.description: Ballerup Kommune wishes to purchase a system that can handle the municipal salary negotiation process for all stakeholders. In a municipality, salary negotiations take place with the involvement of both employees, managers, and trade unions and employee representatives, which makes the task complex. The salary negotiation process involves data from several systems and many different stakeholders: HR, managers both centrally and locally, employee representatives and trade unions, as well as all employees in Ballerup Kommune. Today, the task is handled through manual updating and circulation of Excel sheets with a high risk of errors and GDPR breaches. The purpose of the purchase is to ensure a quality boost of data in salary negotiations, make it more person-independent and transparent for the stakeholders. There is also a desire to reduce the time spent by HR, employee representatives and managers in connection with the salary negotiation process. Ballerup Kommune has prepared a requirements specification and would like to invite suppliers to a market dialogue based on this requirements specification and, naturally, a demonstration of the supplier's solution. It is important to note that a development project is not desired, but rather a standard solution that supports our requirements. The market dialogue will be held at the following times: d. 6. October 2025 10.00-15.30 d. 7. October 2025 12.00- 15.30 d. 9. October 2025 11.30- 15.30 2 hours are allocated per supplier. Suppliers who may be interested in participating in a market dialogue are requested to show their interest by writing to Ballerup Kommune via Mercell no later than 1. October 2025, stating which date and time among the three possible ones above. Ballerup Kommune reserves the right to reject any interested companies if there are too many interested parties or if the company has a solution that is currently only on the drawing board.
sig_f407665173fc522d220b.title: Invitation to market dialogue regarding intended procurement of salary negotiation system

sig_f42dfbd119f70092f405.description: INTRODUCTION Mid Ulster District Council is preparing a procurement for the renewal, supply, management and optimisation of its Microsoft enterprise licensing, associated CSP services and specialist Microsoft expertise. This pre-market engagement exercise will help the Council understand available market models, risks, pricing approaches, support arrangements and proportionate requirements before any formal procurement is issued. PURPOSE AND OBJECTIVES OF THIS PRE-MARKET ENGAGEMENT EXERCISE The objectives are to confirm market interest, test the most suitable agreement route and service model, identify risks or dependencies, understand pricing and governance options, and inform the Council's procurement strategy. This is not a procurement process and responses will not be evaluated as part of any future tender. BACKGROUND INFORMATION The Council's Microsoft estate includes Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365, Teams, Power Platform, Azure, server licensing and associated Software Assurance requirements. Market input is sought on CSP, Enterprise Agreement or other Microsoft agreement routes, billing options, licence optimisation, tenant support, adoption, security and compliance support, escalation and access to qualified Microsoft expertise. STATEMENT OF REQUIREMENTS MUDC wishes to establish a contract with a suitably experienced Microsoft CSP partner to provide: • licensing renewal, supply and management through CSP, Enterprise Agreement or another suitable route; • licence optimisation, proof of licence, inventory records, renewal tracking and compliance reporting; • Microsoft 365, Azure, Dynamics 365, Teams, Power Platform, security, compliance, identity, endpoint and server licensing expertise; • support for billing, subscription changes, incidents, Microsoft escalation, account governance and roadmap advice; The Council also wishes to understand transparent pricing structures, including margins, discounts, billing models, separate professional services rates and how best to separate user subscriptions, device subscriptions, Azure consumption, server licensing, trial/free SKUs and advisory services. Responses should assist the Council in considering proportionate partner status, accreditations, insurance, service capability, support model and future evaluation balance between price, quality and added value. 5.0 PRE-MARKET ENGAGEMENT APPROACH INDICATIVE PROCUREMENT TIMEFRAME 7.0 Indicative milestones: PME published 10th September 2026 ; responses due via eTendersNI by 3.00 pm on 24th September 2026; procurement launch October , contract award December ; licensing renewal / contract commencement 31st January 2027. Lot 1: .

sig_f47670163e5812efefba.description: The Initiative D21 e.V. ("contracting authority") is a non-partisan, non-profit network of business, politics, science and civil society that campaigns for the promotion of digital transformation in Germany. Through studies, recommendations for action and dialogue formats, it supports the development of a high-performing, inclusive and future-oriented digital society. The subject of the tender is the execution, evaluation and documentation of two population-representative surveys within the scope of the project "The digital society - understanding, shaping, strengthening. Mechanisms, levers and success conditions of digital transformation (DiGeVe)" for the Initiative D21. Based on the collected and evaluated data, two publications are to be produced in the years 2027 and 2029. The project is funded by monies from the Federal Ministry of Education, Family, Senior Citizens, Women and Youth. The Initiative D21 is a leading non-profit civil society actor and the largest non-partisan network for the digital society in Germany. With around 140 member organisations from business, science, politics and civil society, the association, as an independent platform, combines social benefit with technological innovation. The association regularly publishes evidence-based studies, such as the D21 Digital Index and the eGovernment MONITOR. These studies provide a sound data basis for a digital transformation that both promotes equal opportunities and social progress and secures economic and state future viability. The studies are published on the association's website. The contractor (hereinafter referred to as the contractor) must carry out two large-scale quantitative primary surveys. To this end, the development and programming of the survey design, including the programming of questionnaires, are to be provided by the contractor (see chapter 2.1 of the specification of services). The contractor must regularly coordinate with the contracting authority (hereinafter referred to as the CA) regarding the content development and design of the questionnaires. The contractor must operatively carry out these data collections (see chapter 2.2 of the specification of services). Operational execution includes at least sampling as well as field management via the weighting and delivery of the quality-assured raw dataset. The data determined as a result of the data collection are to be prepared and statistically evaluated in two runs (see chapter 2.3 of the specification of services). In doing so, the contractor is to design complex statistical analyses and coordinate them jointly with the CA. Subsequently, the statistical analyses are to be carried out. The CA reserves the right to perform quality assurance on the results of the statistical analyses. The substantive interpretation of the results remains with the CA. The contractor must continuously cooperate with the CA (see chapter 2.4 of the specification of services). For further details, see the procurement documents.
sig_f47670163e5812efefba.title: Main study DiGeVe - Data collection & evaluation

sig_f559dbdaeb69de5ac52b.description: This Invitation to Tender (ITT) is issued by NHS Wales Shared Services Partnership Procurement Services (hosted by Velindre University NHS Trust) ("NWSSP") on behalf of Hywel Dda University Health Board ("HDUHB"), which will act as the lead contracting authority and enter into the resulting agreement. Hywel Dda University Health Board, acting on behalf of Betsi Cadwaladr University Health Board, Cwm Taf Morgannwg University Health Board and Swansea Bay University Health Board, is seeking to procure a modern Community Information System to replace the existing Wales Community Care Information System (WCCIS), which is approaching end of life. The procurement presents a significant opportunity to deliver a strategic digital care record solution supporting integrated health, community, mental health and social care services across Wales. The Authority is seeking a cloud-ready, secure, resilient and highly interoperable platform capable of supporting a shared digital care record, mobile working, multidisciplinary care planning, advanced reporting, and seamless integration with national and local health and care systems. Suppliers will be expected to demonstrate strong implementation and data migration capability, alignment with NHS Wales Digital Architecture principles, robust cyber security and information governance arrangements, and a commitment to innovation, service transformation and long-term scalability. The solution will support a broad range of community services, including Health Visiting, School Nursing, Children's Community Nursing, Safeguarding and Community Nursing services, with the potential for future expansion. The resulting contract will play a key role in enabling person-centred, digitally enabled integrated care, improving information sharing, reducing administrative burden and supporting better outcomes for citizens across Wales. sig_f64fbd7b1b6867fc525b.description: The City of Helsinki's Culture and Leisure Division is developing data-driven management and, in connection with this, visitor counting for its locations and related solutions. Visitor data is one of the most important key performance indicators for operations: visitor data is used, among other things, for resource allocation, operational planning and development, and for assessing the impact of operations. The goal of the visitor counting service is to collect comparable and accurate visitor data from the division's locations as automatically as possible for analysis and reporting needs. The SaaS (Software as a Service) provided by the supplier includes at least: • production of visitor data from the counting target according to the needs defined by the division • transmission of visitor data by providing an interface (interface service) for transferring data to the division's data warehouse • transmission of visitor data by providing a user interface (user interface service) for viewing the data • collection of visitor data from devices, as well as monitoring and reporting of data accuracy and coverage (incl. verification counts for measurement at defined intervals) • devices used for visitor data collection as a lifecycle service (HaaS service, Hardware as a Service): - installation, commissioning, maintenance, servicing, functionality testing and calibration of devices - monitoring of device operation - removal and recycling of device installations. The contracting authority is currently surveying the procurement of a new data platform and will put it out to tender in approximately late 2026. By submitting a tender, the tenderer undertakes to assist with integrations and to provide an interface from the visitor counting service to the data platform. The estimated total value of the procurement excluding VAT is 1 680 000,00 euros. The estimated value includes the actual contract period of two (2) years and, in addition, one (1) two-year (2) option period. The procurement is divided into three (3) different lots: - lot 1: indoor locations - lot 2: outdoor locations - lot 3: multi-purpose outdoor locations. The tenderer may submit a tender for as many lots as they wish. Tenderers will be selected for the framework agreement based on the most economically advantageous tender. Qualitative requirements (quality criteria) have been set as minimum requirements for the devices and services to be procured, which the offered devices and services must meet. In addition, the price comparison will compare the maximum prices per lot (hereinafter ceiling price) from cheapest to most expensive. The supplier provides a ceiling price according to the most demanding example location of the lot defined by the contracting authority. Based on the tender competition, a framework agreement will be concluded for the subject of the procurement, to which five (5) contract suppliers who have submitted the lowest ceiling price per lot will be selected, unless there are fewer tenderers meeting the requirements. The suppliers selected for the framework agreement do not have exclusive rights to the procurements covered by the framework agreement, but the contracting authority has the right to procure the same subject of procurement also from outside this framework agreement. The contracting authority also does not commit to specific procurement volumes during the framework agreement. A more detailed description of the subject of the procurement is described in this invitation to tender and its appendices. The locations in the lot have one or more entrances to the site. There is a need for location-specific breakdown of visitor data for different indoor locations. Such locations include, for example, libraries, youth centres, cultural centres and sports halls. A more detailed description of the service and the minimum requirements are presented in the Description of the subject of the procurement, Requirement Specification, Service Levels appendix and other appendices of the invitation to tender attached to the invitation to tender. The contracting authority estimates that 80 such locations will be put out to tender during the framework agreement period. The amount is an estimate and does not bind the contracting authority.; The locations in the lot have one or more restricted or unrestricted entrances. There is a need for location-specific breakdown of visitor data for different outdoor locations. Such locations include, for example, fenced tennis courts, skate parks, events in urban space, beaches, outdoor islands and trails. A more detailed description of the service and the minimum requirements are presented in the Description of the subject of the procurement, Requirement Specification, Service Levels appendix and other appendices of the invitation to tender attached to the invitation to tender. The contracting authority estimates that 82 such locations will be put out to tender during the framework agreement period. The amount is an estimate and does not bind the contracting authority.; The locations in the lot have several restricted or unrestricted entrances to the space and it includes several service points or spaces. Breakdown of visitor data is essential. Such locations include, for example, sports parks. A more detailed description of the service and the minimum requirements are presented in the Description of the subject of the procurement, Requirement Specification, Service Levels appendix and other appendices of the invitation to tender attached to the invitation to tender. The contracting authority estimates that 38 such locations will be put out to tender during the framework agreement period. The amount is an estimate and does not bind the contracting authority.
sig_f64fbd7b1b6867fc525b.title: Procurement of visitor counting as a comprehensive service, framework agreement 2026-2028 (2028-2030)

sig_f65cb197fb4b014a93db.description: 1 INTRODUCTION We kindly ask you to submit your response to this Request for Information concerning the planning of the procurement for a questionnaire and event management system. We greatly appreciate all responses received, and each of them will be taken into account in the preparation of any potential tendering process. With this Request for Information, we aim to map supplier offerings regarding systems that support and provide a smooth and appropriate user experience for the end user. More detailed information on the subject of the procurement can be found in appendix 1 "Request for Information Questions" of this Request for Information. The end user of the procurement is Istekki and its owner-customers. At the same time, we aim to familiarise ourselves with the market situation, products potentially related to the use of the system, and contractual and commercial terms, such as pricing. 2 ORGANISING MARKET DIALOGUE Based on the responses to the Request for Information, market dialogue sessions will be organised where suppliers can present their own services, products and options for implementing the subject of the procurement. Based on the responses to this Request for Information, Istekki will select an estimated approximately 3–5 tenderers for the market dialogue. Any market dialogue sessions will be organised at a time specified by 24.3.2025 the contracting authority. If market dialogue sessions are organised, they will be conducted in the Finnish language. Istekki will provide the companies selected for the sessions with more detailed schedules and a Teams meeting link at a later date. Additional information questions may also be posed to suppliers. Please note that the information, descriptions and estimates of the publication date of the actual tendering process presented in this Request for Information are preliminary and indicative. Final schedules will be refined as the preparation progresses. 3 RESPONDING TO THE REQUEST FOR INFORMATION We kindly ask you to submit your response by email to hankinnat@istekki.fi no later than 18.3.2026 at 12.00. The Request for Information is to be answered using the form "Request for Information Questions" attached to this Request for Information (appendix 1). Send the completed form to the specified email address by the deadline. All responses received to the Request for Information will be taken into account in the preparation of the invitation to tender, and they form an important part of understanding the overall picture. It is worth noting that this Request for Information does not oblige Istekki Oy to carry out the procurement in the manner presented in this document or its appendices. A potential tendering process may also be left unorganised. No separate compensation will be paid for responding to the Request for Information or participating in any presentation sessions. We would like to emphasise once again that this is a Request for Information, not a prior information notice, contract notice or invitation to tender. The purpose of the Request for Information is to familiarise with the market situation and gather information related to the subject of the procurement to support the planning of the future tendering process. Responding to the Request for Information is voluntary and is not a prerequisite for participating in a potential tendering process, nor does it bind Istekki to publish a tendering process. At the same time, we greatly appreciate the information provided by suppliers, as it helps us build the future tendering process into as functional and clear a whole as possible.

sig_f69f67ab6ecf615e9e4d.description: The Contractor shall provide Think Trends Software as an Agentic AI and Document Intelligence solution capable of processing structured, semi-structured, and unstructured adverse event documents, including scanned PDFs, handwritten or machine-generated forms, narratives, attachments, medical records, product complaints, lab reports, follow-up submissions, and case correspondence. The solution shall support end-to-end adverse event document processing through the following capabilities: A. Agentic Document Intake and Classification Think Trends Software AI agents shall automatically receive, classify, and route adverse event documents by submission type, FDA Center, product category, source, urgency, and case-processing requirements. The intake agent shall identify whether a document relates to drugs, biologics, devices, veterinary products, tobacco products, combination products, or other FDA-regulated products. Key capabilities include: • Automated ingestion of scanned PDFs, forms, emails, images, attachments, and electronic documents. • Classification of documents by Center-specific workflow, product type, and reporting pathway. • Detection of new cases, follow-up cases, duplicate submissions, incomplete submissions, and supporting attachments. • Intelligent routing to appropriate review queues, case-processing teams, or downstream systems. B. Agentic OCR and Intelligent Data Extraction Think Trends Software Agentic OCR shall combine optical character recognition, computer vision, natural language processing, large language models, and rule-based validation agents to extract key adverse event data elements from complex documents. The platform shall extract and structure critical case information, including: • Reporter, patient, animal, subject, or consumer information. • Product information, including drug, biologic, device, tobacco, or veterinary product details. • Adverse event terms, symptoms, outcomes, seriousness, and event narratives. • Dates, timelines, exposure details, dose, route, duration, lot numbers, manufacturer information, and product identifiers. • Medical history, concomitant products, lab results, device problem codes, clinical narratives, and follow-up information. • Center-specific data elements required for CVM-Drugs and CVM-Food, CDRH, CTP, CDER, CBER and HFP. C. Center-Specific Adverse Event Processing Agents The Contractor shall configure specialized AI agents within Think Trends Software to support unique regulatory and operational needs across FDA Centers. Each agent shall apply Center-specific data models, validation logic, terminology, business rules, and review workflows. Examples include: • CVM Agent: Processes veterinary adverse event reports, animal species, breed, weight, product exposure, dosage, outcome, and veterinarian/reporter information. • CDRH Agent: Processes device-related adverse events, device identifiers, manufacturer information, malfunction details, patient impact, and device problem descriptions. • CTP Agent: Processes tobacco product adverse experiences, product use patterns, health effects, consumer narratives, and product category information. • HFP Agent: Processes HFP-specific adverse event reporting requirements and associated workflows. • CDER Agent: Process drug product adverse experiences, product use patterns, health effects, consumer narratives, and product category information. • CBER Agent: Processes biologics product adverse experiences, product use patterns, health effects, consumer narratives, and product category information. D. Case Validation, Quality Control, and Human-in-the-Loop Review Think Trends Software shall incorporate validation agents to compare extracted data against business rules, required fields, confidence thresholds, terminology standards, and case-processing logic. Records that meet defined thresholds may proceed automatically, while exceptions shall be routed for human review. Key quality-control features include: • Confidence scoring at field, document, and case levels. • Source traceability to page, section, table, and line references. • Automated flagging of missing, inconsistent, conflicting, or low-confidence data. • Human-in-the-loop review screens for case processors and safety reviewers. • Reviewer acceptance, correction, override, and approval workflows. • Full audit trail of AI extraction, human edits, and final approved values. E. Data Standardization and Regulatory Output Generation Think Trends Software shall transform extracted adverse event information into structured formats required for case management, analytics, and downstream regulatory processing. The platform shall support configurable mappings to FDA data standards, Center-specific systems, XML structures, APIs, and reporting formats. Capabilities include: • Normalization of adverse event terms, product names, dates, identifiers, and narrative fields. • Mapping to Center-specific safety data models and controlled terminology. • Generation of structured case records for downstream review and processing. • API-based integration with FDA systems, case-processing platforms, data lakes, document repositories, and workflow tools. • Export to XML, JSON, CSV, database tables, or other required formats. F. Agentic Workflow Automation and Triage Think Trends Software shall automate repetitive case-processing steps while maintaining reviewer control for regulatory decisions. The system shall support configurable AI agents capable of executing multi-step workflows, requesting missing information, summarizing case narratives, identifying seriousness indicators, detecting duplicates, and prioritizing work queues. Workflow automation shall include: • Case prioritization based on seriousness, product risk, event severity, due dates, and Center-defined rules. • Automated summarization of long adverse event narratives and supporting attachments. • Duplicate and follow-up detection across submissions. • Exception handling and escalation workflows. • Generation of reviewer-ready case summaries. • Dashboard visibility into case volumes, processing status, aging, backlog, error rates, and productivity metrics. G. AI-Enabled Redaction for FOIA Compliance ThinkTrends will provide AI-powered redaction capabilities to support FDA's obligations under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA). The platform will automatically identify and redact personally identifiable information (PII), protected health information (PHI), commercially confidential data, law-enforcement-sensitive content, and other exemption-covered materials from adverse event documents prior to public release or response to FOIA requests. Key capabilities include: • Automated detection and redaction of PII and PHI, including patient names, addresses, dates of birth, medical record numbers, Social Security numbers, and other personal identifiers. • Identification and suppression of trade secrets, proprietary formulations, manufacturing processes, and commercially confidential submitter information protected under FOIA Exemption. • Detection of law-enforcement-sensitive and inter-agency deliberative content subject to FOIA Exemptions. • Configurable exemption profiles aligned to FDA FOIA policy, Center-specific guidance, and applicable federal regulations. • Confidence-scored redaction recommendations with source traceability, enabling FOIA reviewers to accept, modify, or override AI-proposed redactions. • Human-in-the-loop review workflow allowing FOIA analysts to validate, annotate, and finalize redacted documents before release. • Generation of redacted PDF and document versions with visible redaction markers, exemption codes, and reviewer audit annotations. • Full audit trail recording every AI-proposed redaction, reviewer decision, exemption code applied, and final release determination. • Support for bulk redaction processing across large FOIA request batches, including multi-document packages and rolling requests. • Integration with FDA FOIA tracking systems, document repositories, and case management workflows. 1.3 SALIENT FEATURES OF THINK TRENDS SOFTWARE Think Trends Software provides the following differentiating capabilities relevant to FDA adverse event reporting modernization: 1. Agentic OCR Beyond Traditional OCR: Think Trends Software does not merely convert images to text. It applies AI agents that read, interpret, validate, cross-check, and structure regulatory information from complex adverse event documents. 2. Center-Agnostic Core with Center-Specific Configuration: The platform provides a common document intelligence foundation while allowing FDA Centers such as CVM, CDRH, CTP, and HFP to configure unique workflows, data models, rules, and outputs. 3. End-to-End Adverse Event Case Automation: Think Trends Software supports intake, classification, extraction, validation, triage, routing, human review, data transformation, and downstream submission/output generation. 4. Human-in-the-Loop Regulatory Control: The system keeps FDA reviewers in control by allowing them to review, correct, approve, or override AI-generated outputs before final case acceptance. 5. Explainability and Source Traceability: Each extracted field can be traced back to the original source document, page, section, and text reference, supporting transparency, auditability, and reviewer confidence. 6. Confidence-Based Processing: Think Trends Software assigns confidence scores to extracted data and automatically routes low-confidence or inconsistent records for human review. 7. Multi-Document and Multi-Format Processing: Think Trends Software shall process scanned PDFs, structured forms, unstructured narratives, tables, handwritten content where feasible, images, attachments, correspondence, and supporting records. 8. Duplicate and Follow-Up Detection: AI agents shall compare incoming submissions against existing records to identify potential duplicates, follow-ups, related cases, and case-history updates. 9. Reviewer-Ready Case Summaries: Think Trends Software shall generate concise adverse event summaries, chronology, product-event relationships, missing-field lists, and review-ready case packages. 10. Secure FDA-Aligned Deployment: Think Trends Software shall be deployable in secure government cloud, FDA-managed, or approved hosting environments with role-based access, audit logs, encryption, and integration with enterprise identity management. 1.4 TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS Implementation of Think Trends Software for adverse event document processing is expected to deliver the following outcomes: • Reduction in manual data entry and repetitive case-processing tasks. • Faster adverse event intake, triage, and reviewer preparation. • Improved data quality through AI-assisted validation and standardization. • Greater consistency across FDA Centers while preserving Center-specific workflows. • Enhanced traceability, auditability, and regulatory transparency. • Improved ability to manage high-volume document backlogs and surge workloads. • Increased reviewer productivity through AI-generated summaries and exception-based review. • Scalable platform foundation for future FDA adverse event modernization initiatives. Please view the attached Request for Quote (RFQ) RFQ FDA-SOL-75F40126Q00384 document for additional information.

sig_f6fe09a24878199d77b7.description: Numera Palvelut Oy (hereinafter Numera or Contracting Authority) requests your tender for a joint procurement concerning Printing and information services (Multifunction devices and related services) in accordance with the call for tender documents. The procurement is not divided into lots; instead, a single supplier will be selected, with whom Numera will draw up mutual procurement contracts.: The competitive tendering is conducted via an open procedure. The selection criterion used for the competitive tendering is the most economically advantageous tender, and the comparison criterion is [the best price-quality ratio]. Detailed information on scoring and comparison criteria is presented in the section Criteria for the subject of the procurement of the call for tender. If several tenderers achieve the exact same score with their tender, the Contracting Authority will draw lots to determine the winner. Drawing lots is an accepted method in procurement law case law. Parallel tenders and alternative tenders are not accepted. The procurement contract shall be valid for a fixed term of two (2) years. Thereafter, the contract shall continue until further notice. Numera's customer communities using the joint procurement and potentially joining it during the contract period are stated in appendix one (1) of the draft agreement. The procurement contract shall enter into force once the procurement decision has become legally binding or the Market Court has granted an enforcement permit for the procurement decision, and both contracting parties have signed a written procurement contract. The notice period for terminating the contract is six (6) months for both contracting parties. A customer participating in the contract may terminate the contract in respect of itself with a notice period of 6 months. By submitting a tender, the tenderer undertakes to comply with all conditions in the call for tender documents and any additional information provided during the procurement procedure. The Contracting Authority has the right to verify the information provided by the tenderer in its tender documents before making the procurement decision. If the information provided is incorrect, the tenderer may be excluded from the procurement procedure. The main subject of the procurement is multifunction devices for uniform use (emphasising A4-sized devices) for printing and scanning, document workflow management, and support and additional services related to the aforementioned devices and their services (e.g. secure printing, management solutions, toner and supply solutions, ordering system, etc.). The focus of the procurement is on cost-effective devices supporting A4 printing, X-archive scanning (healthcare XDS solutions) individual devices agreed on a case-by-case basis, taking GDPR into account in operations, support and maintenance services, and other additional printing services in accordance with the documents. This procurement does not include the procurement of printing paper, printing work, or printing services (e.g. digital and offset printing). It is possible to expand the procurement during the negotiation procedure as an option regarding printers connected to workstations via USB. Numera decides on the implementation of the option. In questions and problem situations related to the use of the tendering service, the tenderer must contact the service provider's (Cloudia Oy / Tarjouspalvelu.fi) Helpdesk: tel. 020 766 1075, tuki@cloudia.fi.

sig_f75214932dc650000c29.description: The tender process comprises a contract for the contracting authority's procurement of the supply, implementation, operation, maintenance and support of an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system. The procurement of an enterprise resource planning system is part of the contracting authority's new strategy to create a greater degree of uniformity in the IT area across the contracting authority's organisation with a view to realising both financial and quality benefits. "Uniformity" does not mean that all units in the organisation must use identical solutions, but that IT decisions are made on the basis of common principles, procedures and guidelines. In this way, coherence, standardisation where possible, and flexibility where necessary are ensured. The purpose of procuring a new ERP system is thus to achieve a higher degree of standardisation and harmonisation of processes across the organisation. This is intended to ensure simpler workflows, reduced complexity and more cost-effective operation. The contracting authority wishes the new ERP system to offer modern technological capabilities, including support for machine learning (ML), artificial intelligence (AI) and other tools that can contribute to increased automation and decision support. Likewise, easy access to new functionality via ongoing upgrades is a central requirement, so that the organisation can quickly exploit new opportunities without extensive customisation. The ERP system must function as the central core of the organisation's transaction layer, where all significant data and processes are collected and handled. This is intended to ensure data consistency, transparency and support an integrated ecosystem of surrounding applications. The annual value of the contract is estimated at three (3) million DKK excl. VAT. In addition, there is a one-off implementation with an expected cost of three (3) million DKK excl. VAT. The duration of the contract is set at 10 years, which gives a total estimated contract value of 33 million DKK excl. VAT. The total volume is indicative only and based on historical data and can therefore not be considered a guarantee of future turnover.
sig_f75214932dc650000c29.title: Competitive procedure with negotiation regarding a contract for the supply, implementation, operation, maintenance and support of an enterprise resource planning (ERP) system for Kredsløb A/S

Market exploration - voluntary prior information - No contract notice The Deutsche Bundesbank intends to obtain information on services for an IT maintenance contract for the research information system "Research Hub" as part of a market exploration in accordance with Section 28 of the Public Procurement Ordinance (VgV). The subject of this market exploration is to gain knowledge about IT services available on the market for the maintenance and further development of the web-based research information system "Research Hub" regarding the takeover of the existing codebase, for ongoing maintenance, security and dependency updates, and technical support (excluding hosting). Interested providers can contact the email address "research-hub@bundesbank.de" by 14.10.2026 with a brief description of their services and their suitability for fulfilling the stated requirements, stating the subject "Markterkundung - IT-Dienstleistungen Research-Hub", in order to participate in this market exploration. The Deutsche Bundesbank reserves the right to use the results of the market exploration for the preparation of a procurement procedure. Market Exploration - Voluntary pre-notice - No Contract Notice The Deutsche Bundesbank intends to gather information, as part of a market exploration pursuant to Section 28 of the Regulation on the Award of Public Contracts (VgV), regarding services for an IT maintenance contract for the research information system "Research Hub." The purpose of this market exploration is to gather information on IT services available on the market for the maintenance and further development of the web-based research information system "Research Hub," specifically regarding the adoption of the existing codebase, ongoing maintenance, security and dependency updates, and technical support (excluding hosting). Interested providers may participate in this market exploration by sending a brief description of their services and their suitability for meeting the stated requirements-with the subject line "Market Exploration - IT Services Research Hub" - to the email address "research-hub@bundesbank.de" by October 14, 2026. The Deutsche Bundesbank reserves the right to use the results of the market exploration to prepare a procurement process. Lot PAR-0001: Market exploration in accordance with Section 28 VgV for an IT maintenance contract for the research information system "Research Hub" - Market Exploration Section 28 VgV for an IT Maintenance Contract for the "Research Hub". This market exploration serves exclusively for information gathering and the preparation of a potential procurement procedure. It does not constitute a call for tenders or prior information within the meaning of procurement law. A procurement procedure will be initiated at a later date if necessary. The web-based research information system "Research Hub" supports, among other things, the management and processing of research projects, publications and associated workflows. The aim of the market exploration is to gain a general overview of the market as well as potentially suitable service providers and their service profiles. The focus is in particular on experience with the takeover, support and further development of existing software systems as well as with comparable applications in the scientific or public environment. At the present time, neither concrete service requirements nor a specific contract model have been defined. The subject of a possible later commission could - depending on further findings and the concrete demand situation - in particular be support services in connection with the ongoing operation, technical support, maintenance and further development of the system. A possible later tender may include content that deviates from or goes beyond this. In this early phase, the Bundesbank would particularly like to know: - whether there is a fundamental interest in potential support in this environment; - what general experience the company has with comparable web-based software systems; - in which areas of software development, system support or technical consulting there are special competencies; - whether there is experience with science-related applications, publication processes, repositories or comparable technical systems; - how the takeover and further support of an existing software solution could be structured in principle; - whether there is a fundamental interest in a non-binding information meeting. sig_f76d0c844dda42681c86.description: We invite forward leaning tenderers to register for our market dialogue for a future procurement of a tender implementation tool (KGV), with the accompanying options, the County Municipalities would like a modern and user friendly tool that helps both the contracting authority and the tenderer with implementation competitions in a flexible way. Simple process and user support should be available by phone and email. The tool shall contribute to increased efficiency in the procurement work and reduce complexity, so that several parts of the entities can use the tool in line with the organisations' maturity. The contracting authorities are looking for a tool that offers efficient work flow and automated processes. The use ought to contribute to reduced the organisation's use of resources in procurement processes and contract follow-up and that the company can more easily comply with the regulations. The contracting authorities want a robust, modern and cloud based system that uses new technology to enable efficient data processing, automation of work processes and seamless integration with the existing infrastructure in the counties. The solution is expected to be maintained, upgraded and developed to support legislative changes, adopt new technology, improve the user experience, and provide continual value during the contract period. It is important that the procured system is developed in line with the market and contributes to strengthening the digitalisation work for the procurement discipline. The system shall assist with the transition to data driven everyday life for procurement consultants. In the future, it may be necessary to integrate artificial intelligence into your infrastructure, such as with Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Azure, to improve employee efficiency and provide access to verified information from trusted data sources, while maintaining security and data quality. The contracting authority wants a tool that, in the long term, can connect artificial intelligence to data in KGV/KAV and other parts of the system, so that employees can reliable information through interaction with artificial intelligence, independent of client. The main goals are: Streamlining of the procurement work, repaired complexity in the processes. Automation and improved work flow. Better compliance with the rules. Support for digitalisation and transition to data driven processes. Future integration of artificial intelligence, especially with Microsoft 365 and Azure.Need for integration with archive system FINT (Joint County InTegraions)What is GOOD? FINT Arkiv – Novari IKSFINT is a common digital platform that is used by Norwegian counties to standardise and make information available through open APIs. This contributes to increased efficiency, better data quality and reduced costs by enabling real time reuse of data. FINT Arkiv-integration shall be used by county entities included in this competition. Other affiliated entities may require integration in other ways, adapted to their system landscape. As the Contracting Authority consists of several entities, different archive systems are currently used. With FINT Arkiv, however, the underlying archive system does not function as the interface for the integration - FINT provides a common interface regardless of which archive system is used. Fint Arkiv is used by all of the counties in the country, byantikvaren and Bymiljøetaten in Oslo kommune as well as Sametinget.With FINT Arkiv the counties get an API with a joint information model for standardised exchange of archive information. The counties that currently participate in this competition use three different archive systems: Tieto Evry - Public 360Sikri - ElementsAcos - WebSak+Overall Requirement - Integration friendly and data driven system The contracting authority shall use systems with open and documented APIs that enable safe and efficient integration. With limited internal resources for development, the contracting authority needs assistance to extract more value from the existing data. The tenderer shall develop integrations that are easy to implement, maintain and reuse - and that can be shared with other public entities when relevant. The system shall be based on open standards and it shall provide sufficient documentation for both technical and functional understanding. The Contracting Authority strives to procure systems that shall offer an open and documented API with sufficient functionality for safe and efficient integration with other systems and data sources. The API shall support standardised protocols and formats and be available for integration without a need for comprehensive adaptations. The integrations shall be designed with modular architecture that enables reuse and sharing with other public entities. All the necessary documentation connected to the API, data flow and process design shall be provided and suitable for both technical and functional understanding. The tenderer shall assist in implementing value from existing data and contribute to a more data driven and coherent public sector.

sig_f79e77664b464d5e454a.description: The far-reaching impact and rate of innovation in the computer and information science and engineering fields has been remarkable, generating economic prosperity and enhancing the quality of life for people throughout the world. More than a decade ago, the National Science Foundation’s (NSF) Directorate for Computer and Information Science and Engineering (CISE) established the Expeditions in Computing (Expeditions) program to build on past successes and provide the CISE research and education community with the opportunity to pursue ambitious, fundamental research agendas that promise to define the future of computing and information. In planning Expeditions projects, investigators are strongly encouraged to come together within or across departments or institutions to combine their creative talents in the identification of compelling, transformative research agendas that look ahead by at least a decade and promise disruptive innovations in computer and information science and engineering for many years to come. Now funded at levels up to $15,000,000 for seven years, Expeditions projects represent some of the largest single investments currently made by the CISE directorate. Together with the Science and Technology Centers and the National Artificial Intelligence Research Institutes that CISE supports, Expeditions projects form the centerpiece of the directorate's center-scale award portfolio. With awards funded at levels that promote the formation of large research teams, CISE recognizes that concurrent research advances in multiple fields or sub-fields are often necessary to stimulate deep and enduring outcomes. The awards made in this program will complement research areas supported by other CISE programs, which target particular computer and information science and engineering fields. Additionally, CISE offers Innovation Transition (InTrans) awards for teams nearing the end of their Expeditions as well as Secure and Trustworthy Cyberspace (SaTC) and Cyber-Physical Systems (CPS) Frontier projects. The goal of InTransis to continue the long-term vision and objectives of CISE’s center-scale projects. Through InTrans awards, CISE will provide limited funds to match industry support.
