sig_f7b493df20383bf0b66e.description: The procedure is organised with a view to concluding a forest management services contract for the area of 22.550,91 ha, the management plan of the Viseu Forestry Office within the Maramureș Forestry Directorate expiring on 31.12.2027, it being necessary to initiate the procurement procedure in good time to comply with legal deadlines. The services involve the development of the forest management plan and, where appropriate, the additional study for modifying the provisions of the forest management plan, a product of the management activity with technical-organisational content, ecologically grounded, through which the works necessary to be executed in a production unit are established for a period of time, with the aim of bringing and, subsequently, maintaining the structural characteristics of the stands and the forest as a whole at the values corresponding to the optimal structural model, defined in accordance with the ecological, social and economic objectives pursued through sustainable management. According to the provisions of Art. 63 para. (11) of Law no. 331/2024 on the Forestry Code, as subsequently amended and supplemented, it is necessary for the development of forest management plans to be carried out through public procurement procedures. The management of the state-owned public forest fund constitutes a priority obligation of the forest fund administrators. The method of managing the state-owned public forest fund is regulated by forest management plans. Forest management plans and their amendments are approved by order of the head of the Authority. In the case of state-owned public land, the management plans provide data and information necessary for their registration/updating in the centralised inventory of goods in the state's public domain and for registration in the integrated cadastre and land register system. Requests for clarification formulated by tenderers during the advertising period of the contract notice may be made with a deadline of at most 18 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. The contracting authority will respond to all requests for clarification formulated in compliance with the above deadline, once, in a consolidated manner, 11 days before the deadline for the submission of tenders. Forest management plan development services for the state-owned public forest fund managed by the Maramureș Forestry Directorate – Viseu Forestry Office, field phase 2027, for the area of 22.550,91 ha. The services include preparatory work, field data collection, data processing and drafting of the forest management plan, development of the GIS database and management maps, preparation of the necessary environmental documentation, obtaining the regulatory act issued by the competent authority for environmental protection, supporting the documentation within the Technical Commission for Forestry Approval (CTAS) and obtaining the order for the approval of the forest management plan.

sig_f80455249704c571f3c1.description: Keravan kaupunki requests tenders for a maintenance log and facility management system. Keravan kaupunki owns and manages an extensive property portfolio, which includes, among others: - schools - day-care centres - sports facilities - office buildings - other buildings used by the city. Managing the properties requires the coordination of several different data points and processes, such as: - maintenance and servicing tasks - energy consumption - water consumption - environmental conditions - alarms and deviations - reporting and analytics. In the current operating environment, this information is managed in several different systems as well as through partially manual processes. The fragmentation of information makes it difficult to form an overall picture of the state of the properties and slows down decision-making. In addition, the maintenance of properties increasingly emphasises the need to: - improve energy efficiency - identify deviations quickly - move towards predictive maintenance - utilise data to support decision-making. For this reason, Keravan kaupunki is procuring a centralised system that combines operational and analytical data related to properties into a single service.
sig_f80455249704c571f3c1.title: Procurement of a maintenance log and facility management system for the City of Kerava

sig_f84f33b219fc3a9f720d.description: The BMWE intends to tender a contract for the "FRAUEN unternehmen" (WOMEN in business) office. The office is to develop the content of the new priorities specified by the BMWE and develop new measures to sensitise girls and women to professional self-employment together with the "role model entrepreneurs" (VUs). In order to prevent or counteract social conditioning and to promote a cliché-free choice of career, the intention is to increasingly address general education schools in addition to vocational schools and universities. It is in the interest of the contracting authority (CA) to cooperate with other programmes/projects funded by the BMWE, such as the SCHULEWIRTSCHAFT-PREIS or the BMWE initiative group "Gründung in school" (Founding in school), and, where sensible and possible, to develop proposals for cooperation in order to exploit potential synergies. Furthermore, the "FRAUEN unternehmen" initiative is also a measure from the joint action plan "More female entrepreneurs for the SME sector". As part of the action plan, the office also participates actively as a member of the network. Through suitable measures, the topic of "female entrepreneurship" is to be placed more strongly in the public eye. To this end, a greater reach in social media is also to be achieved. Furthermore, a targeted expansion of the circle of active VUs is expected, in particular to include female entrepreneurs from the fields of skilled crafts, STEM, AI and digitalisation, from the East German federal states and rural areas, as well as those female entrepreneurs who have themselves taken over a business. The core tasks of the contract include, in particular, the provision of personnel, basic equipment for carrying out network coordination and project management, travel activities, and internal and external communication, including the annual preparation of a media concept (details in the respective work package). The following services are to be taken into account: - AP 1: Central contact point for VUs and all those interested in the initiative - AP 2: Matching of VUs with the target group - AP 3: Development and expansion of the external network/addressing multipliers and network partners - AP 4: External communication – strengthening the general visibility of the "FRAUEN unternehmen" initiative as well as the commitment of the VUs within the framework of the initiative - AP 5: Internal communication – strengthening the internal network of VUs and supporting the exchange of experience among VUs - AP 6: Monitoring, evaluation of the initiative and preparation of results - AP 7: Targeted expansion of the circle of VUs Lot LOT-0000: Office of the BMWE initiative "FRAUEN unternehmen". sig_f8a1fe8a7d4f75e336ab.description:
The subject of the contract concerns the provision of maintenance and technical support services for the IPTO GIS System (hereinafter the "Company") for the years 2027 & 2028, and includes the following: 1.1 Maintenance and support of Smallworld software from the manufacturer General Electric, with which the system was developed, and specifically of: • 26 run-time licences for the Smallworld Core Spatial Technology product, • 4 licences for the Smallworld WebMapServer SOM product, of the Smallworld GeoSpatial Server (GSS) product, • 16 licences for the Smallworld AddOn for Google Maps product • 4 Professional licences for the Smallworld GeoSpatial Analysis product • 80 Lite licences for the Smallworld GeoSpatial Analysis product. This maintenance and support includes: • The provision to the Company of new versions of Smallworld products made available by their developer, GE Energy. New versions may arise due to improvements or the elimination of errors and malfunctions in the software, as well as due to the integration of new features that allow the software to operate in a new environment (operating system, network, etc.). Also, new versions may arise due to the integration of new capabilities or due to monitoring technological developments in both computer hardware and peripherals, and in software (operating systems or other products with which the Smallworld software interacts). New versions also include supplements made available to correct errors in the current version at any given time. New versions are provided in the form of an installation programme, stored in electronic format within one month of the announcement of their release by the developer. • The provision to the Company of detailed manuals for the presentation, analysis and instructions for use of the new features incorporated into the new versions. These manuals accompany the new versions and are provided in electronic format. • The restoration of any anomaly that may occur in the Smallworld software or other software on the computers on which it is used, provided that the anomaly is due to weaknesses in the Smallworld products that appeared during their proper use and not due to misuse of the software, the operating system or the computer. To restore the aforementioned anomalies, the contractor may, at its discretion, either provide the necessary instructions by telephone, email or fax to Company personnel, or make an on-site visit, without additional compensation or remuneration. The contractor undertakes to address every aforementioned anomaly with the aim of resolving it within two working days. • The provision of advice by telephone or via email or fax, firstly for the installation of new versions and any intervention necessary for this purpose, and secondly for addressing critical points and/or malfunctions related to the Smallworld software, whenever they arise. Support is provided during working hours. 1.2 Maintenance and support of specialised applications for IPTO that have been developed, as well as their supporting sub-applications which concern: 1.2.1 Basic Modules  Transmission Lines Application  Substations Application which includes the digitisation of Single-Line Diagrams  Operational Diagram Application which depicts the electrical topology of the equipment,  Fibre Optic Network Application  Real Estate buildings and land plots Application 1.2.2 Supporting sub-applications of the basic Modules • Isolation limits calculation application (dynamic determination-calculation) • Environmental Licensing application for Substation and Transmission Line projects • Application for issuing Isolation Requests (Emergency and Scheduled) for parts of the System to the National Energy Control Centre • Installed equipment report application • Circuit outage and performance indicator calculation application • Geospatial visualisation of the entire IPTO fibre optic network, in combination with the Transmission System as well as the ability to record the relevant technical characteristics • Analysis of fibre optics into optical circuits, including the geographic visualisation function per circuit • Recording and geospatial visualisation of associated equipment (optical connectors, ODF, ODS) • Function for detecting available and unavailable optical circuits as well as the carrier using them. 1.3 Application for the interoperability of the GIS with the SAP EAM The maintenance and support includes in detail: • The upgrading of these applications whenever a new version of Smallworld products is made available. The upgrade includes the modification of the applications so that they are compatible with the new version of Smallworld products at any given time, while simultaneously incorporating all the capabilities of the applications and all the additional capabilities of the new version of the Smallworld products. • The possibility of parallel installation and use of the applications based on both the previous version of the Smallworld products at any given time and the new version of it at any given time, until IPTO S.A. decides to transition from the previous to the new version. • The restoration of any anomaly that occurred in the applications or other software of the computers on which they are used, provided that the anomaly is due to weaknesses in the applications that appeared during their proper use and not due to misuse of the applications, the operating system or the computer. • The obligation of the contractor to respond within one week to any request from the company for the provision of the works. 1.4 Provision of software development services The provision of 40 man-days (MD) of software development work is required, such as improvements, modifications and extensions of the system's applications.

sig_f8ae74998e3e5212bd22.description: The subject of the contract is the upgrade and expansion of the multi-channel citizen information and service system 1555, which has been operated by 1/10/2022 as a single service hub for citizens and businesses regarding matters falling within the remit of the Ministry of Labour and Social Security and its supervised bodies. As part of the upgrade, the digital architecture and software subsystems, such as the web portal, knowledge base, artificial intelligence solutions and ticketing, are being enhanced so that 1555 can gradually transition from a predominantly voice-centric model to a balanced service model, where more complex and sensitive cases remain with human service through the reinforcement of specialised representatives, while simpler cases are closed via self-service services and automation. Specifically, the use of AI solutions is provided for both citizens and representatives, such as IVRs and AI agents for intent recognition and routing to digital solutions or appropriate specialised representatives, agent assist tools that retrieve content from the knowledge base to reduce errors and handling time, as well as analytics to understand requests and better plan staffing. At the same time, interoperability at the infrastructure or service level with the Citizen Request Management System (CC ticketing) and the utilisation of data from ticketing and the knowledge base are being enhanced, with provision for continuous improvement through feedback and conversation analysis. The operation of specialised consultants will be expanded and enhanced so that citizens have even greater access to personalised information. Digital systems will be further upgraded and new ones introduced with the aim of enhancing service delivery. A team of experts will be able to carry out targeted studies on specific subject matters of the serviced bodies, and surveys may also be conducted to further strengthen the bodies through the project. The development and management of the project are organised into work packages as follows: I. Public communication and service structure II. Technical Infrastructures III. Satisfaction surveys and Quality Assurance IV. Strengthening of bodies on specific subject matters – special surveys V. Project management VI. Service training Upgrade and expansion of a multi-channel citizen service system 1555

Lot 1: . The Council requires a hub where users can access the system and have the ability to find any needed legislation or regulation to help ensure that whatever project they are working on is compliant with government law and standards. A portal is currently used for this requirement that has 2 parts. The first part is the Construction Information Service legislation and technical information management solution. This service ensures that Fife Council will have access to the correct, current and complaint business critical information year-round. This service provides the Council access to 27,000 full-text PDFs with the ability to save, view, print, download, copy and paste any of these documents. There are over 350 publishers that add documents to this service. Fife Council require something equal in quality and quantity to this. The second part of the portal is Occupational Health & Safety Information Service. This single source library holds more than 90,000 documents from more than 400 publishers. The focus of this service is Health, Safety, Environmental and Fire. This service relates to risk management, hazardous substances and operations, control principles, movement of people and vehicles. Fife Council also require something that is equal in quality and quantity to this part of the portal. Overall, the current solution allows access to over 2.3 million industry standards, over 10 thousand engineering manuals, handbooks, reference books, over 76 million technical articles, journals and books, over 107 million patents, patent applications, unity models and abstracts and over 39 million industry-to-industry reference links across all hosted content

sig_f956a0a97d268a0369e2.description: The Technische Universität Darmstadt is among the leading technical universities in Germany and is characterised by innovative research and an international orientation. The university is structured into 13 departments and over 120 institutes. This structure is supplemented by eight directorates, which handle central administrative tasks such as student services, financial and personnel affairs, construction management and international affairs, thereby ensuring the smooth operation of the university. In total, the TU Darmstadt comprises around 24.300 students and about 5.200 employees. A special role is played here by Directorates IV (Real Estate Management) and V (Construction Management and Technical Operations), which are responsible for the administration and management of a total of 210 buildings on the campus. In the course of these demanding tasks, the directorates have relied on SAP ERP software with various modules since 2000. Since 2004, the SAP RE-FX (Real Estate Management) and SAP PM (Plant Maintenance) modules have been used in the aforementioned areas. For construction management, 2019 SAP PS (Project System) including the construction add-on from PROMOS was implemented. Currently, however, many internal processes in the field of building management and maintenance are mapped outside of SAP, as only a small part of the technical requirements can be implemented in SAP. Digital plan data (CAD) and digital spatial data (SAP RE-FX spatial database) are not linked. Data is reconciled manually. Documents are only partially available in digitised form, without reference to other systems. The diverse tasks and processes of the directorates are to be supported in future step-by-step by a uniform solution in the form of a CAFM system. The professional support requirement primarily consists of creating a uniform database in order to better link and evaluate information. Further requirements arise from the specialist tasks with regard to property and facility management and facility operations.
sig_f956a0a97d268a0369e2.title: IMMO4TU

sig_f997918e53159440ef8c.description: The subject of the procurement is the nurse call, fall detection, and movement monitoring systems to be introduced in Helsingin kaupungin sosiaali-, terveys- ja pelastustoimiala. Nurse call systems are used in the social, health, and rescue sectors in hospitals, senior centres, care homes, enhanced assisted living units, health centre inpatient wards, rehabilitation units, and other operating environments requiring round-the-clock care and supervision. In addition, the systems are utilised in home care support services and special units where clients may have a sudden need for assistance that requires a response. Nurse call systems are a core part of daily care and nursing work, as well as client and patient safety. They ensure that requests for assistance are forwarded without delay to the right personnel and that nursing staff are able to prioritise their tasks according to the urgency of the situation. At the same time, they support the occupational safety of staff, for example in threatening and hazardous situations, and enable the monitoring, reporting, and development of operations. The importance of nurse call systems is particularly emphasized in situations where clients' functional capacity is impaired, memory disorders are common, or the need for care is continuous. In such cases, the system's operational reliability, ease of use, and integration with other systems are not merely technical features, but factors that directly affect the quality and safety of care. The objective of the procurement is to ensure that the solutions in use meet current and future needs. This requires the systems to be scalable, compatible with other technologies, and capable of adapting to various care environments without complicating the use of the systems. At the same time, it is ensured that the solutions to be procured fulfil obligations regarding data protection, information security, and official requirements. Overall, nurse call systems are a critical part of the functionality of the service system, and their procurement must be carried out in a way that long-term supports the quality, safety, and cost-efficiency of services. The aim of the tendering procedure for the framework arrangement is to find up to five suppliers capable of delivering a nurse call system to the sector's sites that can handle traditional nurse calls (a client/patient can call a nurse to the room) and additionally utilise new technology that allows the system to proactively alert a nurse to the client's/patient's location in connection with risk situations (e.g., getting out of a bed, falling). The new technology aims to improve client/patient safety within the limits defined by law. A nurse call system is required in all new and renovated hospitals, senior centres, etc. In addition, the social, health, and rescue sector has several sites where a nurse call system was procured in the past but has become obsolete, and for which the supplier no longer provides maintenance and support. These obsolete systems must be replaced with new ones. The solutions that are the subject of the procurement will primarily be acquired as a comprehensive service provided by the suppliers selected for the framework arrangement. The subject of the procurement is described in more detail in the appendices of this call for tenders.
sig_f997918e53159440ef8c.title: Nurse call systems

sig_fa36135e9c87227e1d5d.description: This is not a contract notice or a call for tenders, but a request for information, through which the South Karelia Wellbeing Services County invites system suppliers to register for a potential procurement. This is a request for information/market dialogue, through which Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue is surveying potential system suppliers for a shift planning and working time management system. The wellbeing services county is responsible for social and healthcare and rescue services. It is the largest employer in the region, employing approximately 5 500 professionals from various fields. The vision is to be a pioneering community, which is why the wellbeing services county has accessible services, the healthiest population in Finland, and the happiest employees. Strategic priorities include impactful services that meet people's needs, as well as a skilled and motivated frontline team. The goal is, among other things, that all services are clearly guided by indicators derived from operational impact and that operations are organised in an economically sustainable manner. The personnel programme of Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue is based directly on the main strategy guiding the organisation, where one of the key priorities is investing in personnel. Well-being personnel do the right things in the right way and serve their customers in the best possible way. Realising these requires efficient, secure, and user-friendly solutions. The shift planning system plays a central role in supporting the smoothness of everyday operations, the well-being of personnel at work, and cost-efficiency. The market dialogue is open to all suppliers that can offer comprehensive solutions falling within the scope of this solution package. The information obtained can be used to assess what kind of solutions are on the market, what benefits they produce, and how they suit the needs of the wellbeing services county. Through the market dialogue, the wellbeing services county aims to: 1. Understand system functionalities and key use cases 2. Clarify integration possibilities with existing systems and platforms 3. Obtain an overview of pricing models and cost structures (no individual tenders) 4. Survey delivery and service models 5. Obtain concrete examples and demos from suppliers, which can be used to illustrate the suitability of the solutions for the needs of the wellbeing services county. The focus of the dialogue is on solutions that are already in production or available on the market. Suppliers are requested to present systems and services that are available and where key functionalities are already implemented. Presentations of solutions under development or only at the concept level are not desired in this context. Registration for the market dialogue is made by the service provider's response regarding the system on offer. Marketing videos are not accepted as responses. The response must indicate the following: - What ready-made solutions and services they offer - In what kind of environments the solutions have been implemented (example descriptions, not mandatory references) - Key features of the solution that they wish to present in the market dialogue. All participants are offered equal opportunities to receive information about the market dialogue. The dialogue does not bind Etelä-Karjalan hyvinvointialue to initiate a procurement, and no procurement decisions will be made based on it. If the contracting authority considers it necessary, the possibility of holding individual meetings is reserved. The market dialogue will focus particularly on how the solutions can support the key operations of the wellbeing services county. These are not procurement requirements, but subject areas intended as a basis for discussion and illustration: - Usability - Mobile use of the system - Technical features - The system as a support for well-being at work - Personnel and competence - Data-driven management and reporting - Implementation, training, and change management - Continuous service and development - Pricing and lifecycle services. Participating suppliers are requested to provide presentations on different use cases. Participating suppliers have the opportunity to illustrate their solutions through demos or practical example situations. The wellbeing services county will provide questions and use case examples in advance, which will guide the discussion and ensure that the presentations of different suppliers can be compared equally. The market dialogue will be carried out as supplier-specific meetings via remote connection (Teams). The duration of an individual meeting is approximately 120–150 minutes. The supplier has the opportunity to present their solution and its key features. The wellbeing services county will also present pre-defined questions that support the equality and comparability of the discussion. Meetings will be held on the following days: 15.9., 18.9., 23.9. and 28.9.2026. The exact time will be agreed upon with the registered suppliers based on the order of registration and the coordination of schedules. The language of any presentations/meetings is Finnish. sig_fb4decc69f3feb81eee2.description: The automated diagnostics solution must encompass key functionalities and ensure the following business outcomes: 1. ensure automated procedures for retrieving data on the type and content of informative elements of all monitored infrastructure parts of the business IT system using standard and advanced integration methods, with the aim of reading the current state, including at a minimum: - detailed physical infrastructure parameters (e.g. manufacturer, hardware version, etc.), - detailed logical infrastructure parameters (e.g. software version, number of the last applied patch, IP addresses, etc.) 2. reconciliation of data retrieved by automated procedures, the solution should enable this by updating documented records with the latest data, while simultaneously retaining unchanged data, regardless of whether they belong to physical or logical entities, with the aim of full lifecycle tracking of physical and logical elements of the entire IT system 3. ensure continuous collection of configurations of all available IT system elements, while tracking their program codes, versions and differences between versions, while recording information on configuration changes and commands executed on system elements (hardware and virtual), with the possibility of re-retrieving infrastructure data and reconciliation when recording new configurations 4. enable dynamic management of system documentation, documenting changes and enabling automated documentation of IP addresses as part of the process of retrieving system logical infrastructure parameters. The subject solution needs to be viewed within the framework of expanding the scope of the existing system for overarching monitoring and management of ICT infrastructure, in order to consolidate the number of individual management systems and utilise the possibilities of combining the functionalities of the subject solution and the existing system. The subject solution needs to be implemented and highly integrated within the existing IT environment, in order to ensure the highest level of information security, by disabling any influence of external elements on the operation of the system. A detailed description of the subject of procurement is located in the document Description of the subject of procurement.
sig_fb4decc69f3feb81eee2.title: Automated diagnostics solution

The initial priority will be to maintain continuity and stabilise these business-critical services as they transition away from the existing National IT Contract, while establishing a strong foundation for subsequent improvement and modernisation. Lot 1: . PSD Scotland intends to procure a Service Integration and Management contract for selected national digital services supporting clinical, operational and administrative functions across NHS Scotland. The procurement will establish replacement arrangements for services currently delivered under the National IT Contract, which is due to expire on 31 March 2028. The principal objective is to maintain uninterrupted delivery of these business-critical services throughout transition and thereafter. The anticipated scope includes services and applications supporting Primary and Community Care, National Screening and Child Health, together with other services confirmed in the procurement documents. Depending on the requirements of each service, the contract may include application support, maintenance and development, as well as the associated infrastructure, platform, integrations and data services. IT Service Management capabilities are also required for end-to-end operation. The detailed application scope, service boundaries and allocation of responsibilities will be defined in the tender documentation. The successful supplier will act as the prime contractor, providing a single point of accountability for the contract. The supplier will be expected to coordinate its subcontractors and work effectively with the Authority’s retained teams and other internal and external providers. Service continuity will take precedence during the initial transition, followed by stabilisation to address supportability, resilience, cyber security, regulatory compliance and technical-debt risks. Once services have been stabilised, the supplier will support proportionate and staged modernisation through software and infrastructure engineering practices. Intended outcomes include: -Secure, compliant and resilient services -Clear and measurable service performance -Visibility of costs and dependencies -Improved value for money The supplier will also be expected to support knowledge transfer, effective service ownership, data portability and robust exit arrangements, reducing long-term supplier dependency and preserving future competition. The Authority will retain accountability for strategic direction, governance, business outcomes and service ownership throughout the contract.

INVITATION TO MARKET DIALOGUE The purpose of this market dialogue is to survey the operators in the market and to collect comments from suppliers. The aim is to obtain comprehensive information to support the implementation of a potential future procurement. The subject and content of the procurement will be specified and defined in the final published call for tenders. With this invitation, we request tenderers interested in the procurement to register and participate in the dialogue concerning the procurement. The dialogue seeks information on the tenderers operating in the market and the features of the services offered in relation to the contracting authority's needs. The aim is to obtain feedback and potential development suggestions for the call for tenders package currently under preparation. Market dialogue The market dialogue sessions will be held according to the preliminary schedule between Tue 22.9.2026 at 12-14 via remote connection as a Teams meeting. The discussion sessions will be organised with a maximum of three (3) suppliers. If there are more than three (3) companies registered for the market dialogue, the contracting authority will select the most suitable suppliers for the dialogue based on its own criteria. The purpose of the market dialogue is to inform the market about the upcoming procurement, survey the market situation, enable the submission of comments on the future procurement, and obtain information concerning the procurement so that the actual tendering process can be carried out in the most appropriate manner. In the market dialogue session, the purpose and objectives of the future procurement will be presented, as well as the procurement process in general with its schedule (non-binding). The contracting authority reserves the right to provide the registered participants with preliminary questions and a draft of the tender documents before the session. These materials will be reviewed together during the session. Suppliers are requested to prepare for the session with a presentation of no more than 10 minutes, introducing the company's operations, key areas of expertise, and services relevant to the procurement. During the session, suppliers will also have the opportunity to ask questions and make suggestions regarding the procurement. The market dialogue will be conducted in Finnish. No compensation will be paid for participating in the dialogue, and the contracting authority will not reimburse any costs incurred from participating in the market dialogue. REGISTRATION All interested operators in the field are requested to register for the market dialogue no later than 15.9.2026 at 11.00 at the address https://kaarina.toimittajapalvelu.fi/ Further information regarding registration: hankinnat@kaarina.fi ADDITIONAL INFORMATION ON THE NOTICE This notice is an invitation to a market dialogue. This notice does not request tenders. This notice does not oblige the contracting authority to carry out the actual procurement, and the contracting authority does not commit to making any procurements in accordance with this notice. The information provided about the procurement or the procurement procedure is not binding on the contracting authority in any potential subsequent procurement procedure. Refraining from participating in this market dialogue does not prevent participation in a potential call for tenders, and participation in the dialogue does not affect the tenderer's position in the actual call for tenders. The information that emerges during the market dialogue will remain strictly confidential and will be used solely for the development and planning of the potential procurement. However, the contracting authority is not obliged to take into account the responses received during the market dialogue when drafting the call for tenders.

INTRODUCTION & SYNOPSIS This announcement is a formal Request for Prototype Proposal (RPP) issued by the Mission & Installation Contracting Command (MICC) – Fort Campbell on behalf of the Directorate of Public Works (DPW) at Fort Campbell, Kentucky. The Government is seeking competitive prototype proposals to design, integrate, and execute a modernized facility management solution across 58 unaccompanied housing (barracks) facilities. The prototype will integrate an advanced, secure Enterprise Asset Management (EAM) software platform with cross-trained physical maintenance execution to streamline work order triage, optimize Between Occupancy Maintenance (BOM), and execute proactive Preventative Maintenance Orders (PMO). Authority: 10 U.S.C. § 4022, Other Transaction Authority (OTA) for Prototype Projects. Agreement Type: The Government intends to award a single Other Transaction (OT) agreement. Follow-on Production / Sustainment: Offerors are advised that in accordance with 10 U.S.C. § 4022(f), successful completion of this prototype project may result in the award of a non-competitive, follow-on production/sustainment agreement or contract without further competition. 2. BACKGROUND Fort Campbell DPW is responsible for maintaining unaccompanied housing infrastructure that directly impacts Soldier readiness and Quality of Life (QoL). The current operating model relies heavily on manual administrative workflows, disparate tracking mechanisms, and reactive maintenance practices, leading to extended vacancy timelines during unit rotations, misdiagnosed service dispatches, and increased facility wear. This prototype project seeks to validate a modernized operational model that combines commercial best practices with enterprise Army platforms (including integration with ArMA, GFEBS, and the forthcoming enterprise IBM Maximo migration). Key modernization elements include QR-code-enabled request intake, automated work order routing, decentralized parts staging solutions (e.g., smart lockers), and dual-track maintenance (physical inspections for legacy systems and sensor-based monitoring for modern equipment). 3. ELIGIBILITY This RPP is open to all responsible business entities. In accordance with 10 U.S.C. § 4022(d)(1), an award may only be made if at least one of the following conditions is met: At least one nontraditional defense contractor or small business participates to a significant extent in the prototype project; OR All significant participants in the transaction other than the Federal Government are small businesses or nontraditional defense contractors; OR At least one-third (1/3) of the total cost of the prototype project is to be paid out of funds provided by sources other than the Federal Government (cost share); OR The Senior Procurement Executive provides written approval for exceptional circumstances. 4. PROPOSAL SUBMISSION & KEY DATES Proposal Instructions: Interested Offerors shall submit a comprehensive proposal package consisting of: Technical Approach (addressing EAM integration, physical maintenance, and predictive monitoring) Integrated Logistics & Sustainability Plan (addressing supply chain, SOPs, and knowledge transfer) Management, Programmatic, & Lifecycle Approach (Integrated Master Schedule, risk management, and scaling) Cost / Price Proposal Performance Work Statement (PWS) (directly derived from Attachment 001, Statement of Objectives) Key Dates: Questions Due Date: Sep 16, 2026, at 11:00 AM Central Time (CT) Site Visit Date: Sep 17, 2026, at 10:00 AM CT Proposal Due Date: Sep 25, 2026, at 11:00 AM Central Time (CT) Submission Instructions: Method: All questions and proposals must be submitted electronically via email. Email Address: evan.m.rea.civ@army.mil 5. GOVERNMENT POINTS OF CONTACT (POCs) Agreements Officer (AO): Eric C. Boston (eric.c.boston.civ@army.mil) Agreements Specialist / Contract Specialist: Evan M. sig_fd0de47cb33be66edd6d.description: The activities proposed within the project address the needs identified at the level of the ANAP regarding the strengthening of administrative capacity, the reduction of bureaucracy and the digitalisation of professional skills development processes in the field of public procurement. The project contributes to the establishment and operationalisation of integrated digital tools, which will support standardised skills management and the continuous professional development of staff in the central public administration. In order to achieve these objectives, the project will develop and implement an integrated e-learning platform that will include: - a tool for assessing existing skills in the field of public procurement for the target group; - a tool for identifying and analysing professional training needs; - personalised analyses of training needs for each category of user; - professional training programmes in the field of public procurement, with an emphasis on the strategic role of this function, adapted to different categories of staff; - educational materials and learning resources integrated into the platform; - a system for assessing and certifying acquired skills; - coaching and mentoring programmes for professional skills development and knowledge transfer. The implementation of the integrated platform will lead to: - increased access for staff to continuous training and flexible learning opportunities; standardisation of the processes for assessing, training and certifying skills in the field of public procurement; - improvement in the quality and efficiency of professional training activities; - reduction of administrative costs and bureaucratic burdens associated with managing training processes; - development of an organisational culture oriented towards continuous learning and performance; - increase in the level of competence of staff involved in managing public procurement; - strengthening of the institutional capacity of the ANAP and beneficiary entities to efficiently implement public policies in the field of public procurement. The number of days before the deadline for the submission of tenders by which clarifications may be requested is 20 days. The contracting authority will respond clearly and completely to all requests for clarification on the 11-th day before the deadline for the submission of tenders. The duration of the implementation of the contract is from the date of its signing by both parties until the completion of the project implementation, by 31.03.2029, with the possibility of extension under the conditions of a change in the duration of the financing contract. THE DURATION OF THE EXECUTION OF THE CONTRACT SERVICES is 3 months, from the date of signing of the contract by both parties. The activities proposed within the project address the needs identified at the level of the ANAP regarding the strengthening of administrative capacity, the reduction of bureaucracy and the digitalisation of professional skills development processes in the field of public procurement. The project contributes to the establishment and operationalisation of integrated digital tools, which will support standardised skills management and the continuous professional development of staff in the central public administration.

sig_fde596abed61f68cf813.description: The existing building was constructed 1911 in solid construction with a hipped roof. The last general refurbishment was carried out in 1986, alongside smaller refurbishment measures in recent years. The site has a gradient from east to west. The playground located to the south of the existing building is available as the construction site for the extension of the Erich Kästner School. The new "glass joint" or intermediate building connects the existing school with the planned extension and provides a new second structural escape route including a lift for barrier-free access. The new four-storey school building was designed in solid construction with a punched window façade. Structurally, each storey contains up to 3 classrooms, depending on the requirements of the room schedule, which are separated by a group room. In the north-east of the extension, directly next to the new stairwell, there is a ancillary room zone spanning all floors, which contains sanitary, storage and technical rooms. sig_fded948ea627b084551a.description: The U.S. National Science Foundation Directorate for Engineering (NSF ENG) supports foundational research for electrical, communications and computing systems through the following programs: The Electronic, Photonic, Magnetic, and Quantum Devices (EPMQD) program supports foundational engineering research on novel classical and quantum devices, exploring matter’s electronic, photonic, and magnetic properties to enable new applications. The Circuits and Systems for Communications and Sensing (CSCS) program supports foundational engineering research on classical and quantum aspects of advanced components, systems, and signal processing for communications and sensing. The Energy, Power, Control, and Learning (EPCL) program supports foundational research on systems and control, learning, optimization, artificial intelligence, and networked multi-agent systems, and their applications, with emphasis on power and energy systems. NSF ENG anticipates a portfolio of ENG: Electrical, Communications, and Computing Systems (ECCS) awards with a range of budgets and durations. Estimated program budget, number of awards, and average award size/duration are subject to the availability of funds. NSF ENG is particularly interested in intellectually ambitious and potentially transformative foundational research. Proposals need not promise a near-term product, deployment, or commercial outcome, nor need they address later-stage development to be competitive.

Step 2 — Formal Proposal Due Date & Time: Formal technical and cost proposals will be requested solely from offerors whose submitted white papers are evaluated as successfully meeting the operational and research needs of the Air Force. Late Receipt Provisions: White paper and proposal receipts after the specified cutoff date and time shall be governed strictly by the provisions of FAR 52.215-1(c)(3). 1.2 Instrument Types and Contracting Guidance The Air Force reserves the right to award the contractual instrument best suited to the nature of the research proposed. Accordingly, the Government may award any appropriate contract type under the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), Other Transaction (OT) for Prototype authority, Grant, Cooperative Agreement, OT for Research, or an applicable technology transfer mechanism. Awards under this BAA are generally anticipated to be cost-reimbursement. Offerors are specifically advised that cost-reimbursement contracts require an accounting system determined adequate by the Government for tracking allocable contract costs. 1.3 Communications & Contracting Points of Contact Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is strongly encouraged prior to proposal submission. Technical discussions shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to fund or award any proposed effort. Only warranted Contracting Officers possess the legal authority to commit the Government. Inquiries regarding this solicitation should be directed to the Contracting POCs: Primary Contracting Officer: Eric Moss — eric.moss.3@us.af.mil Alternate Contracting Officer: Joseph Spear — joseph.spear.1@us.af.mil 2. Section I — Program Description & Strategic Objectives The Department of the Air Force (DAF) has identified critical operational gaps in the enterprise databases, analytical methods, and predictive tools regularly employed for weapon system cost estimating and analysis. DAF is actively committed to modernizing the efficiency, fidelity, and throughput of its cost estimating capabilities. This requirement invests in strengthening, accelerating, and elevating cost data and analytic capabilities using modern data science and cloud engineering technologies to enable faster, higher-quality, and higher-volume analytic decision support across the DAF cost community. The CEMDAR research initiative executes four fundamental architectural shifts across enterprise cost operations: Platform Modernization: Transitioning from legacy desktop-based analytical tools to secure enterprise cloud platforms (e.g., DAF Data Fabric, VAULT, Envision). Relational Data Integration: Moving from isolated, commodity-specific datasets to integrated, relational architectures linking programmatic, technical, cost, and schedule parameters. Pipeline Automation: Replacing static spreadsheets and recurring manual reporting with dynamic, automated data engineering pipelines. Scalable Predictive Modeling: Advancing from low-volume static cost modeling to highly scalable data collection, curation, machine learning, and empirical analytics. 2.1 Strategic Research Objectives Elevating Data Fidelity: Improving the verifiable quality, authenticity, granularity, and volume of empirical data collected and accessible to DAF cost analysts. Relational Enterprise Databases: Engineering centralized, enterprise-level relational cost, schedule, and technical databases adhering to rigorous data science principles and MIL-STD-881 standards. Analytical Workflow Optimization: Constructing capabilities and streamlined workflows that empower analysts to rapidly synthesize large-scale multi-commodity datasets. Predictive Modeling & Decision Support: Establishing authoritative enterprise datasets and generating dynamic Cost Estimating Relationships (CERs), Schedule Estimating Relationships (SERs), Technical Estimating Relationships (TERs), benchmark metrics, interactive dashboards, and cloud-native cost models. The overarching vision is not only to elevate the timeliness and accuracy of program Life-Cycle Cost Estimates (LCCEs) for budgeting, programming, and acquisition milestone decisions, but also to build an agile capability for rapid high-level force design, alternative architecture trades, and component-level engineering trade-off evaluations. 3. Section II — Technical Description & Core Competencies The Department of the Air Force Cost Analysis Agency (AFCAA) is soliciting white papers (and subsequently formal technical and cost proposals from qualified respondents) addressing innovative synchronization of research related to technical, cost and schedule for DoW/DAF programs across the following five Core Competencies. Submitted white papers must move beyond generic capability statements and clearly articulate the offeror's specific technical approach, proposed system architectures and analytical methodologies. Offerors should include concrete examples of relevant past work, demonstrating proven experience in designing data pipelines, executing predictive cost modeling, and conducting targeted cost specific research within defense or similarly regulated enterprise environments. To ensure holistic technical execution, white papers must also address the following staffing and expertise qualifications: Key Personnel Competencies & Experience: Offerors must explicitly summarize the core technical competencies, relevant project experience, and security clearance/access readiness of proposed Key Personnel—specifically the Contractor Program Manager (PM), the Chief Cost Data Scientist (governing Task 2 Level 1 architectural decisions and CADOM pipelines), and any designated Technical / Data Science Task Leads—substantiating the leadership team's qualification to direct contract activities from Day 1. On-Demand Cost & Commodity Subject Matter Experts (SMEs): Offerors must demonstrate an established, agile capability to deploy specialized Cost and Technical Domain SMEs on an as-required basis. These experts must possess deep commodity and engineering expertise to support targeted cost studies, schedule analyses, and novel data pipeline mapping across diverse defense domains—including Aircraft, Space and Launch Systems, Missiles and Munitions, C4ISR, Cyber and Software Systems, and Operations and Support (O&S) Sustainment. 3.1 Core Competency 1: Enterprise Data Governance, Access, and Research Lifecycle Planning (envisioned PWS Tasks 1 & 2) Task 1 — Data Access Permissions, Proprietary Information Protection, and OCI Governance: Establishes the administrative, legal, and multi-tier security foundation required to ingest proprietary defense data. Offerors must structure and manage Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs) across AFCAA, OSD CAPE (for the Cost Assessment Data Enterprise [CADE] repository), Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs), and prime/subcontractor tiers. Because weapon system cost repositories contain business-sensitive Proprietary Information (PROPIN), tasks require rigorous OEM engagement protocols, proactive OCI screening, and monitoring to eliminate conflicts resulting from corporate reorganizations or contractor commercial affiliations. Task 2 — Integrated Research Planning, POA&M Execution, and Agile Governance: This area establishes a centralized, contractor-maintained Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M) serving as the operational roadmap governing all contract activities. The integrated POA&M must establish element-level execution schedules, critical path milestones, risk mitigation triggers, and formal go/no-go evaluation gates integrating all technical efforts: foundational data governance and ingestion, automated Medallion pipeline curation (Task 3), empirical studies and predictive model building (Task 4), acquisition database modernization (Task 5), and surge research directives. To ensure seamless technical integration without compromising Government oversight, offerors must establish a disciplined governance framework that strictly delineates contractor operational management from inherently governmental authority: Contractor Operational Governance: Led by the Chief Cost Data Scientist and Contractor PM, the contractor manages internal agile execution, sprint velocity, data quality gates, and Level 1 Architectural Decisions (internal pipeline scripting, routine algorithms, and code refactoring). The contractor must maintain an Integration and Dependency Matrix linking Task 4 analytical use cases directly to underlying Task 3 data pipelines. Government Technical Oversight: The Government retains all approval and baseline acceptance authority. The AFCAA Technical Lead / COR approves Level 2 Decisions (changes to enterprise data schemas, cloud infrastructure, or CADOM standards), while Level 3 Decisions (cross-agency data sharing and multi-service standards) require stakeholder consensus (AFCAA, OSD CAPE, and Service Cost Centers). 3.2 Core Competency 2: Automated Data Pipeline Engineering & Enterprise Architecture (envisioned PWS Task 3) Cost Analysis Data Operating Model (CADOM) & Medallion Pipeline Architecture: Focuses on architecting, testing, and operationalizing scalable ETL/ELT pipelines unifying disparate programmatic, technical, cost, and schedule data streams into an enterprise CADOM schema. Utilizing modern technologies (Apache Spark, Databricks, Python, SQL, cloud data warehouses), pipelines implement a multi-stage medallion architecture: Bronze (raw ingestion), Silver (cleansed, schema-validated, normalized records), and Gold (curated, high-performance analytical views). Work mandates automated quality gates, comprehensive error-handling and telemetry logging, and full audit lineage tracing Gold metrics back to source records. Target feeds include Cost and Software Data Reporting (CSDR/FlexFile), Selected Acquisition Reports (SAR/MSAR), Earned Value Management (EVM/IPMDAR), Air Force Total Ownership Cost (AFTOC), and defense budget exhibits. Enterprise Metadata Schema, Data Lineage, and Catalog Services: Maintains and enriches centralized metadata models, embedding automated tagging routines during ingestion to tag program identifiers, commodity domains, and MIL-STD-881 Work Breakdown Structures (WBS). Develops searchable data catalog services (e.g., Unity Catalog, Foundry), implements Data Fidelity Scorecards measuring authenticity and normalization readiness, and enforces granular role-based access control (RBAC) and attribute-based access control (ABAC) across proprietary and classified boundaries. Enterprise Analytical Applications & AI/ML Data Infrastructure: Builds cross-cutting analytic applications and ML pipelines, such as cross-commodity benchmarking engines, automated NLP-driven WBS mapping from historical CSDR submissions, and Silver-layer anomaly detection routines. Manages version-controlled infrastructure-as-code and reproducible deployment scripts inside government-controlled Git repositories. 3.3 Core Competency 3: Data-Driven Analytics, Predictive Modeling, and Application Deployment (envisioned PWS Task 4) This technical area encompasses research, predictive modeling, and application deployment executed through approved subtasks in the POA&M. Depending on operational objectives, subtasks will combine data analysis, dynamic model development, custom tool engineering, and targeted empirical studies: Dynamic Analysis, Predictive Modeling & Empirical Studies: Applies regression, econometrics, machine learning, and Bayesian methods to develop dynamic models, empirical CERs, SERs, TERs, and cost growth benchmarks. Research covers core weapon system commodities—Aircraft (Fixed/Rotary/Unmanned), Space & Launch, Missiles, Cyber/Software, and Operations & Support (O&S) sustainment. Focus areas include, for example, expenditure time-phasing, flight test benchmarks, commercial space cost adjustments, agile software metrics, and AI-generated code productivity/defects. Custom Analytical Applications & CADOM Deployment: Designs, packages, and deploys user-facing tools, calculation workbooks, and interactive dashboards connected directly to CADOM pipelines. Automates repetitive estimating workflows (e.g., inflation/escalation, price normalization, trade-off analysis). In alignment with the Integration and Dependency Matrix, models and containerized applications must comply with CADOM standards and include reproducible code and technical documentation. 3.4 Core Competency 4: Specialized Acquisition Databases and Statutory Cost Reporting Administration (envisioned PWS Task 5) Task 5 (Option CLIN) — AFCAA Contracts Database (KDB) Modernization and Analysis: Modernizes and hosts the enterprise AFCAA Contracts Database within cloud platforms (e.g., VAULT). Fuses procurement data from SAM.gov, FPDS, EDA, and USA Spending with internal metadata models (CSDR, SAR, EVM). Constructs BI pipelines, refines contract growth classification buckets, conducts Engineering Change Order (ECO) analyses to isolate cost drivers, issues quarterly database releases to CADE users, and delivers hybrid user training. 3.5 Core Competency 5: Mission Augmentation and Surge Analytical Capabilities (envisioned PWS Task 6) Task 6 (Option CLIN) — RDT&E Surge Research and Rapid Prototyping Support: Pre-negotiated surge mechanism to rapidly deploy specialized cost estimators, data scientists, machine learning engineers, and technical SMEs for high-priority emergent research, algorithm development, and novel methodology prototyping requiring RDT&E funding. 4. Section III — Contractual, Security, and Administrative Requirements Within Scope Modifications: Due to the inherent uncertainty of research and development efforts, awards resulting from this announcement may be modified during performance to execute within-scope adjustments, including modifications to increase contract ceiling. 4.1 Period of Performance and Deliverable Schedule The anticipated period of performance spans 12 to 60 months for the technical effort, tailored to individual award determinations. Hardware and specialized software items shall be determined per contract award. Deliverable Category Contractual Requirement Governing Standard / Delivery Frequency Period of Performance 12 to 60 months total duration Tailored to contract award and CLIN structure Data Items (CDRLs) Research reports, POA&Ms, schemas Specified in resultant Contract Work Statement Software / Codebase Data pipelines, containerized tools Delivered to government repositories; Open/Gov Rights Quarterly Releases AFCAA KDB and CADOM deployments Quarterly release cycles into VAULT/CADE environments 4.2 Security, OPSEC, and Export Control Compliance Facility & Personnel Clearance: Program classification requirements span up to and including Top Secret (refer to RFP DD Form 254). Offerors must maintain an active Facility Clearance and ensure current Cognizant Security Office records are registered with DCSA (www.dcsa.mil). All proposed Key Personnel must hold and maintain an active SECRET security clearance at contract award, and offerors must demonstrate that they have immediate access to personnel that possess the access capability to utilize TOP SECRET / SCI clearances and facilities as required for classified studies and task directives. All non-key contractor and subcontractor personnel assigned to this contract must possess, at a minimum, a favorably completed and adjudicated Tier 2 (T2) background investigation (or higher) on Day 1 of contract performance to support Moderate-Risk Public Trust (MRPT) and Common Access Card (CAC) / system access requirements. ). TS/SCI work is anticipated to be a small fraction of the overall work in year 1 but could vary each year as requirements evolve. Operations Security (OPSEC): Contractors and subcontractors must implement Industrial Security, Information Security, Personnel Security, and OPSEC measures to protect critical program data from adversary exploitation and export breaches. Export Control & ITAR: Technical information generated or utilized may be subject to ITAR (22 CFR 120-131) and EAR (15 CFR 710-774). Where applicable, a Certified DD Form 2345 (Militarily Critical Technical Data Agreement) must accompany formal proposals. DFARS 252.225-7048 applies to all resulting awards. Contractor Performance Assessment (CPARS): Interim annual evaluations and a final evaluation will be conducted. Contractors are provided 14 calendar days to review and submit rebuttals before final determinations by the authority one level above the Contracting Officer. 4.3 Logistics, Base Support, and Intellectual Property Rights Government-Furnished Property (GFP) / Equipment (GFE): In accordance with Section VI of the PWS, the Government will furnish standard encrypted laptops, required application software licenses, and cloud platform tenant environments (e.g., DAF VAULT / Data Fabric) for authorized contractor personnel performing work under resulting awards. Provisioning will occur within 10–15 business days following security badge issuance. No additional GFP/GFE is anticipated; any extra equipment requested in an offeror's proposal must be pre-approved by the Contracting Officer. Primary contract performance will occur at contractor facilities. However, the Government will provide on-site base access, workspace, and local network connectivity for contractor personnel designated to work on-site or attend recurring program reviews at government locations in the National Capital Region (NCR), and other AFCAA Operating locations as necessary. 4.4 Data Rights and Commercial Software Licensing The Government desires the following data rights determinations: Noncommercial Technical Data: Unlimited Rights. Noncommercial Computer Software (NCS) & Documentation: Unlimited Rights. Commercial Computer Software: Customary Commercial License consistent with Federal procurement statutes. Final data rights will be determined during contract negotiations in accordance with RFO and R-DFARs. Third-party commercial and noncommercial software not reasonably identifiable at proposal submission must be formally approved by the Contracting Officer or Contracting Officer’s Representative (COR) prior to incorporation. Software licenses transferred to the Government must not disclaim all warranties via ‘as is’ provisions, must permit use across Air Force and support contractor facilities, and must allow code embedding/derivative works. Licensors must agree to incorporate standard federal preemption terms nullifying any provisions inconsistent with Federal law. 5. Section IV — Proposal Preparation and Evaluation Review This solicitation executes a Two-Step selection process. White papers and proposals must adhere strictly to the guidelines outlined below. The Government reserves the right to review white papers and fund some, all, or none of the proposals received. ONLY WHITE PAPERS ARE BEING SOLICIATED AT THIS TIME. 5.1 Eligibility Information Eligible Offeror: This is a 100% Small Business Set-aside. Cost Sharing or Matching: Cost Sharing is not required. Government Agencies: If a Government agency is interested in performing work, contact the Contracting Officer identified in the BAA. If those discussions result in a mutual interest to pursue your agency's participation, the effort will be pursued independent of this announcement. Other: Foreign Participation: SAF/FM is authorized to exclude all foreign participation at the prime contractor level for the subject procurement. Foreign participation will be addressed for each white paper that have the potential to best meet the Air Force’s needs based on the white paper evaluation information in Section V. Notice to Foreign-Owned Firms: Such firms are asked to immediately notify the Contracting Officer before deciding to respond to this announcement. Foreign contractors should be aware that restrictions might apply which could preclude their participation in this acquisition. There are no limits on the number of white papers/proposals an offeror may submit. You may be ineligible for award if all requirements of this solicitation are not met on the white paper (and later proposal) due date as identified above. 5.2 Step 1: White Paper Submission Format White papers must be structured into four distinct, concise sections. Total of all sections combined should be no more than 30 pages: Offerors must format white paper submissions in accordance with the standard guidelines below. Requirements are kept intentionally streamlined to minimize proposal preparation burden while ensuring equitable technical evaluation. Page Format & Margins: All pages must be formatted for standard 8.5" x 11" paper with a minimum of one-inch (1.0") margins on all four borders. Page orientation must be portrait. Typography & Line Spacing: Narrative text must be single-spaced using Times New Roman (minimum 12-point), Arial (minimum 10-point), or Calibri (minimum 11-point). Text within tables, figures, charts, and diagrams may be reduced to a minimum of 8-point font, provided all content remains legible at 100% zoom. Electronic File Formats: White papers must be submitted electronically via email as a single, searchable Adobe Portable Document Format (pdf) file. The Cost Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM) may also include an optional, unlocked Microsoft Excel (.xlsx) workbook showing active formulas and calculations. Do not submit .zip compressed archives or password-protected files. Header/Footer Information: Headers and footers may fall within margin boundaries and must include the BAA number (FA7014-26-S-CS02), company name, CAGE code, and sequential page numbering ("Page X of Y"). Page Limitations: Pages shall be numbered starting with the cover page being Page 1, and the last page being no greater than Page 30. The Government may remove and not evaluate any pages that exceed the established limitations. Section A — Administrative & Corporate Metadata: BAA Number, Title of Research Effort, Company Name, Business Size, CAGE code, DUNS/UEI number, and Company Technical & Contracting POCs (with direct telephone numbers and email addresses). Section B — Technical Approach & Capability Summary: Statement of task objectives; detailed technical methodology demonstrating alignment with Core Competencies 1 through 5; concrete examples of past work demonstrating automated pipeline engineering and predictive cost modeling; and a concise staffing summary detailing: The qualifications, core competencies, relevant experience, and clearance status of proposed Key Personnel; and The offeror's established approach for providing on-demand Cost and Commodity Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) across weapon system domains as task assignments require. Section C — Cost & Rough Order of Magnitude (ROM): Comprehensive ROM cost estimate reflecting labor, data infrastructure, and travel necessary to execute the proposed research. Section D — Associate Contractor Agreements (ACAs): Identification of anticipated ACA frameworks required to exchange proprietary technical data, software code, and research assets among multiple defense contractors. 5.3 Step 1: White Paper Review Criteria MANDATORY EVALUATION GATE: Only white papers submitted by respondents possessing an active and verifiable Facility Security Clearance (FCL) at the TOP SECRET level (issued and recorded in the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency [DCSA] National Industrial Security System [NISS] at the time of white paper submission will be reviewed by the Government. Submissions lacking verification of an active Top Secret FCL at the time of submission will be rejected without consideration. Teaming Arrangements and Joint Ventures: In any contractor teaming arrangement or Joint Venture (JV), the Prime Contractor must independently hold an active Secret FCL at submission. Cleared entities within the proposed teaming arrangement possessing the requisite FCL must perform at least fifty percent (50%) of the direct labor/technical effort. A cleared subcontractor may not on its own fulfill this requirement on behalf of an uncleared prime contractor. Day-1 Vetting Readiness Attestation: Offerors must certify in Section A of their white paper that: All proposed Key Personnel hold active SECRET security clearances at contract award; All labor planned for Day-1 contract performance possesses, at a minimum, a favorably completed and adjudicated Tier 2 (T2) background investigation (or higher); and The offeror possesses verified access capability to deploy appropriately cleared TOP SECRET / SCI analysts as required for classified projects and studies (e.g., representative efforts identified in PWS Appendix A or subsequent POA&M task directives). Technical Relevance: Is the proposed technical approach rigorously consistent with the research domains and technologies listed in this BAA? Government Interest: Does the proposed technical methodology address urgent analytical gaps and provide high-value decision support to SAF/FM and AFCAA? Fiscal Viability: Is appropriate research and operational funding available to support the proposed scope and period of performance? 5.4 Step 2: Full Proposal Preparation & Evaluation Offerors receiving favorable white paper evaluations will receive an official Request for Proposal (RFP) detailing Step 2 technical and cost submission instructions, review criteria, and formal deliverable requirements. Offerors will be notified regarding recommendation for full proposal submission on or about 30 calendar days following white paper receipt. 5.5 Statutory and Administrative Disclosures Acquisition of Commercial Items: The Government is not utilizing FAR Part 12 policies for this solicitation. Interested firms may submit commercial capability statements within 15 calendar days of notice issuance. Support Contractor Participation: Government employees will conduct all evaluations. Commercial contractor personnel providing administrative support to AFDW/PK are bound by non-disclosure agreements protecting proprietary data. Debriefing & Feedback Sessions: Offerors may request a debriefing session consistent with governing BAA and FAR acquisition procedures. Responsibility Matters (FAR 52.209-9): Applies to awards exceeding $600,000 where affirmative responsibility matters are checked under FAR 52.209-7. Proposal Adequacy Checklist: Pursuant to DFARS 215.408, proposals requiring certified cost or pricing data must include the completed DFARS 252.215-7009 Proposal Adequacy Checklist.
